When Mr Korbes came home, he went to the fireplace to make a fire; but

the cat threw all the ashes in his eyes: so he ran to the kitchen to

wash himself; but there the duck splashed all the water in his face; and

when he tried to wipe himself, the egg broke to pieces in the towel all

over his face and eyes. Then he was very angry, and went without his

supper to bed; but when he laid his head on the pillow, the pin ran into

his cheek: at this he became quite furious, and, jumping up, would have

run out of the house; but when he came to the door, the millstone fell

down on his head, and killed him on the spot.

3. HOW PARTLET DIED AND WAS BURIED, AND HOW CHANTICLEER DIED OF GRIEF

Another day Chanticleer and Partlet agreed to go again to the mountains

to eat nuts; and it was settled that all the nuts which they found

should be shared equally between them. Now Partlet found a very large

nut; but she said nothing about it to Chanticleer, and kept it all to

herself: however, it was so big that she could not swallow it, and it

stuck in her throat. Then she was in a great fright, and cried out to

Chanticleer, 'Pray run as fast as you can, and fetch me some water, or I

shall be choked.' Chanticleer ran as fast as he could to the river, and

said, 'River, give me some water, for Partlet lies in the mountain, and

will be choked by a great nut.' The river said, 'Run first to the bride,

and ask her for a silken cord to draw up the water.' Chanticleer ran to

the bride, and said, 'Bride, you must give me a silken cord, for then

the river will give me water, and the water I will carry to Partlet, who

lies on the mountain, and will be choked by a great nut.' But the bride

said, 'Run first, and bring me my garland that is hanging on a willow

in the garden.' Then Chanticleer ran to the garden, and took the garland

from the bough where it hung, and brought it to the bride; and then

the bride gave him the silken cord, and he took the silken cord to

the river, and the river gave him water, and he carried the water to

Partlet; but in the meantime she was choked by the great nut, and lay

quite dead, and never moved any more.

Then Chanticleer was very sorry, and cried bitterly; and all the beasts

came and wept with him over poor Partlet. And six mice built a little

hearse to carry her to her grave; and when it was ready they harnessed

themselves before it, and Chanticleer drove them. On the way they

met the fox. 'Where are you going, Chanticleer?' said he. 'To bury my

Partlet,' said the other. 'May I go with you?' said the fox. 'Yes; but

you must get up behind, or my horses will not be able to draw you.' Then

the fox got up behind; and presently the wolf, the bear, the goat, and

all the beasts of the wood, came and climbed upon the hearse.

So on they went till they came to a rapid stream. 'How shall we get

over?' said Chanticleer. Then said a straw, 'I will lay myself across,

and you may pass over upon me.' But as the mice were going over, the

straw slipped away and fell into the water, and the six mice all fell in

and were drowned. What was to be done? Then a large log of wood came

and said, 'I am big enough; I will lay myself across the stream, and you

shall pass over upon me.' So he laid himself down; but they managed

so clumsily, that the log of wood fell in and was carried away by the

stream. Then a stone, who saw what had happened, came up and kindly

offered to help poor Chanticleer by laying himself across the stream;

and this time he got safely to the other side with the hearse, and

managed to get Partlet out of it; but the fox and the other mourners,

who were sitting behind, were too heavy, and fell back into the water

and were all carried away by the stream and drowned.

Thus Chanticleer was left alone with his dead Partlet; and having dug

a grave for her, he laid her in it, and made a little hillock over her.

Then he sat down by the grave, and wept and mourned, till at last he

died too; and so all were dead.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved eating candy. Every Wednesday, he would go to the store to buy some candy. But one Wednesday, the store had no candy left. Timmy was sad and cried.

LITTLE RED-CAP [LITTLE RED RIDING HOOD]

Once upon a time there was a dear little girl who was loved by everyone

who looked at her, but most of all by her grandmother, and there was

nothing that she would not have given to the child. Once she gave her a

little cap of red velvet, which suited her so well that she would never

wear anything else; so she was always called 'Little Red-Cap.'

One day her mother said to her: 'Come, Little Red-Cap, here is a piece

of cake and a bottle of wine; take them to your grandmother, she is ill

and weak, and they will do her good. Set out before it gets hot, and

when you are going, walk nicely and quietly and do not run off the path,

or you may fall and break the bottle, and then your grandmother will

get nothing; and when you go into her room, don't forget to say, "Good

morning", and don't peep into every corner before you do it.'

'I will take great care,' said Little Red-Cap to her mother, and gave

her hand on it.

The grandmother lived out in the wood, half a league from the village,

and just as Little Red-Cap entered the wood, a wolf met her. Red-Cap

did not know what a wicked creature he was, and was not at all afraid of

him.

'Good day, Little Red-Cap,' said he.

'Thank you kindly, wolf.'

'Whither away so early, Little Red-Cap?'

'To my grandmother's.'

'What have you got in your apron?'

'Cake and wine; yesterday was baking-day, so poor sick grandmother is to

have something good, to make her stronger.'

'Where does your grandmother live, Little Red-Cap?'

'A good quarter of a league farther on in the wood; her house stands

under the three large oak-trees, the nut-trees are just below; you

surely must know it,' replied Little Red-Cap.

The wolf thought to himself: 'What a tender young creature! what a nice

plump mouthful--she will be better to eat than the old woman. I must

act craftily, so as to catch both.' So he walked for a short time by

the side of Little Red-Cap, and then he said: 'See, Little Red-Cap, how

pretty the flowers are about here--why do you not look round? I believe,

too, that you do not hear how sweetly the little birds are singing; you

walk gravely along as if you were going to school, while everything else

out here in the wood is merry.'

Little Red-Cap raised her eyes, and when she saw the sunbeams dancing

here and there through the trees, and pretty flowers growing everywhere,

she thought: 'Suppose I take grandmother a fresh nosegay; that would

please her too. It is so early in the day that I shall still get there

in good time'; and so she ran from the path into the wood to look for

flowers. And whenever she had picked one, she fancied that she saw a

still prettier one farther on, and ran after it, and so got deeper and

deeper into the wood.

Meanwhile the wolf ran straight to the grandmother's house and knocked

at the door.

'Who is there?'

'Little Red-Cap,' replied the wolf. 'She is bringing cake and wine; open

the door.'

'Lift the latch,' called out the grandmother, 'I am too weak, and cannot

get up.'

The wolf lifted the latch, the door sprang open, and without saying a

word he went straight to the grandmother's bed, and devoured her. Then

he put on her clothes, dressed himself in her cap laid himself in bed

and drew the curtains.

Little Red-Cap, however, had been running about picking flowers,

and when she had gathered so many that she could carry no more, she

remembered her grandmother, and set out on the way to her.

She was surprised to find the cottage-door standing open, and when she

went into the room, she had such a strange feeling that she said to

herself: 'Oh dear! how uneasy I feel today, and at other times I like

being with grandmother so much.' She called out: 'Good morning,' but

received no answer; so she went to the bed and drew back the curtains.

There lay her grandmother with her cap pulled far over her face, and

looking very strange.

'Oh! grandmother,' she said, 'what big ears you have!'

'The better to hear you with, my child,' was the reply.

'But, grandmother, what big eyes you have!' she said.

'The better to see you with, my dear.'

'But, grandmother, what large hands you have!'

'The better to hug you with.'

'Oh! but, grandmother, what a terrible big mouth you have!'

'The better to eat you with!'

And scarcely had the wolf said this, than with one bound he was out of

bed and swallowed up Red-Cap.

When the wolf had appeased his appetite, he lay down again in the bed,

fell asleep and began to snore very loud. The huntsman was just passing

the house, and thought to himself: 'How the old woman is snoring! I must

just see if she wants anything.' So he went into the room, and when he

came to the bed, he saw that the wolf was lying in it. 'Do I find you

here, you old sinner!' said he. 'I have long sought you!' Then just as

he was going to fire at him, it occurred to him that the wolf might have

devoured the grandmother, and that she might still be saved, so he did

not fire, but took a pair of scissors, and began to cut open the stomach

of the sleeping wolf. When he had made two snips, he saw the little

Red-Cap shining, and then he made two snips more, and the little girl

sprang out, crying: 'Ah, how frightened I have been! How dark it was

inside the wolf'; and after that the aged grandmother came out alive

also, but scarcely able to breathe. Red-Cap, however, quickly fetched

great stones with which they filled the wolf's belly, and when he awoke,

he wanted to run away, but the stones were so heavy that he collapsed at

once, and fell dead.

Then all three were delighted. The huntsman drew off the wolf's skin and

went home with it; the grandmother ate the cake and drank the wine which

Red-Cap had brought, and revived, but Red-Cap thought to herself: 'As

long as I live, I will never by myself leave the path, to run into the

wood, when my mother has forbidden me to do so.'

It also related that once when Red-Cap was again taking cakes to the old

grandmother, another wolf spoke to her, and tried to entice her from the

path. Red-Cap, however, was on her guard, and went straight forward on

her way, and told her grandmother that she had met the wolf, and that he

had said 'good morning' to her, but with such a wicked look in his eyes,

that if they had not been on the public road she was certain he would

have eaten her up. 'Well,' said the grandmother, 'we will shut the door,

that he may not come in.' Soon afterwards the wolf knocked, and cried:

'Open the door, grandmother, I am Little Red-Cap, and am bringing you

some cakes.' But they did not speak, or open the door, so the grey-beard

stole twice or thrice round the house, and at last jumped on the roof,

intending to wait until Red-Cap went home in the evening, and then to

steal after her and devour her in the darkness. But the grandmother

saw what was in his thoughts. In front of the house was a great stone

trough, so she said to the child: 'Take the pail, Red-Cap; I made some

sausages yesterday, so carry the water in which I boiled them to the

trough.' Red-Cap carried until the great trough was quite full. Then the

smell of the sausages reached the wolf, and he sniffed and peeped down,

and at last stretched out his neck so far that he could no longer keep

his footing and began to slip, and slipped down from the roof straight

into the great trough, and was drowned. But Red-Cap went joyously home,

and no one ever did anything to harm her again.

Once upon a time, there was an old tree in the middle of the forest. "What is this old thing?" asked a curious 3 year old girl, as she reached out to touch it.

Suddenly, the old tree began to move. The little girl was so frightened that she backed away. But the tree was very kind and called to her, "Come closer! I won't hurt you." The little girl hesitantly stepped closer to the tree.

The tree then revealed a hidden door that no one in the forest had ever seen before. The tree said, "If you open this door, you will find something special. It may take courage, but if you try, who knows what wonders you will find."

The little girl was unsure at first, but then she bravely opened the door. Inside, she found an entire world filled with amazing things to explore. She spent the entire day exploring and playing.

This teaches us that no matter how uncomfortable something may seem at first, if we just have courage and believe in ourselves, we can find wonderful and hidden treasures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was very hungry. Her tummy felt funny and all she wanted was something yummy. So she went outside to look for something to eat.

As she walked, the sky grew dark and a storm began. Big rain drops started to fall and thunder clapped in the sky. Amy was scared and started to cry.

But then, she heard a voice from behind, saying "Amy, don't worry". When she looked back, she saw her Mommy. Her Mommy opened her umbrella and said, "Come here, I will squeeze you tight".

Amy felt much better when her Mommy held her. She knew she felt safe and loved in her Mommy's arms.

From that day on, Amy learned that when times were tough and the storm was scary, all she had to do was squeeze her Mommy and she would feel safe. This taught her that love was one of the most important things in life.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named John. He was very gifted, and had lots of toys. One day, he spotted a big ship sailing near his house. He was so excited to get on board!

John asked his mom if he could go on the ship, but she said no. "It's too dangerous, sweetheart," she said. So, John made a plan to steal the ship and sail away.

He packed a bag of food and some clothes and sneaked onto the ship. As he was sailing away, John shouted, "I'm taking this ship on a journey!"

Suddenly, he saw the ship's captain, who yelled, "Oh no! You can't take this ship!" John was very scared and he started to cry.

The captain was very kind and said, "It's ok. I understand why you wanted to steal the ship. You can stay on board and help me sail this ship!"

John was really happy and agreed to stay. From then on, he and the captain started having many great adventures together!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to go camping with his family. They would set up a tent and roast marshmallows over the fire. Timmy was very loyal to his family and always helped them.

One day, Timmy and his family went camping in the forest. They set up their tent and started a fire. Timmy helped his family gather wood for the fire. When it was time to sleep, Timmy went inside the tent. But he forgot to zip it up!

During the night, a big bear came and smelled the food. The bear went inside the tent and ate all the food. Timmy woke up and saw the bear. He was scared and ran away. The bear chased him and Timmy got lost in the forest. Timmy was sad and scared. He wished he had thanked his family for taking care of him.

Kate was a little girl who liked to dress up. She had a lot of fancy clothes and really liked picking out the perfect outfit of the day. One day she and her family went out to take a special picture at a park.

Her mom asked Kate to dress in her favorite clothes. Kate took out her best dress and put it on. She was very proud of how she looked.

When they got to the park, they set up a big camera. They placed Kate in front and took her picture. Kate posed like she was a movie star.

After the picture was taken, everyone was very proud of how well Kate looked. She was so proud too. They all felt very happy to have this special picture. It was a picture to remember!

Andy was so excited for his first day of school. He put on his backpack and skipped all the way to the classroom. As he walked into the classroom, he heard the teacher say "Welcome! Let's start with a safe game of bounce."

Andy was so excited, he couldn't wait to try. He ran up to the middle of the room and said to the teacher, "Let me try first!"

The teacher smiled and said, "Okay then, Andy. Bounce the ball all the way around the room!"

Andy excitedly started bouncing the ball. He bounced it around all the tables and chairs in the classroom. He bounced it through the door and back around again. Andy felt very safe, even though he was bouncing alone.

When he was done, the teacher smiled and said, "Well done, Andy! You can keep bouncing around the classroom whenever it's safe to play!"

Andy smiled and bounced his way back to his seat. He couldn't wait to come back to school tomorrow!

Once there was a girl named Lisa. She was walking in the park and carrying her purple purse. Suddenly, a strange man ran past and grabbed it! Lisa was very confused.

"Help!" she screamed. But no one could help. The man ran away with Lisa's purse.

Lisa stood there, afraid and confused. She couldn't remember what she should do next. Then she saw the policeman and ran over to him. She told him all about the man who had taken her purse.

The policeman said, "Don't worry, little girl. I'm sure we'll find it soon."

But unfortunately, the policeman couldn't find the purse and the man was never caught. Lisa was feeling very sad and confused. She walked home empty-handed that day, remembering how frightened she had been.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emma. She was only 3 years old and she was very curious. She was always asking questions and searching for answers.

One day, Emma was playing in the garden near her house when she saw a deep hole in the ground. She was so excited that she ran inside straight away to ask her mum a question. "What is this deep hole?" she said.

Mum smiled and said, "Maybe let's go and search for the answer together."

Emma was so excited to find out the answer. She helped her mum search the hole and eventually they found a shiny key.

"Let's keep it safe," said mum. Emma wondered where it might open.

The next day, mum and Emma set off to the old castle near their house. When they arrived, they saw that the door was locked with a keyhole. Emma immediately knew what it was for!

She used the key her and mum had found the day before and the door opened. Inside, they found the biggest treasure chest they had ever seen. Emma was so amazed and happy.

"Thank you for your deep searching, Emma," said mum. Emma couldn't believe what they had found.

Once upon a time, there were two birds. They were friends, but they were different. One bird was blue and the other was red. They liked to play together on a branch. One day, the blue bird saw a shiny rock on the ground. The blue bird wanted the rock, but the red bird saw it too. The blue bird thought, "I will take the rock when the red bird is not looking."

But the red bird saw what the blue bird was doing. The red bird whispered, "That is not nice. Friends share things." The blue bird felt bad and gave the rock to the red bird. From that day on, the blue bird learned that it is better to share with friends than to keep things for yourself.

Once there was a boy named Tim. He liked to play with his big toy box. One day, Tim opened up his toy box and saw something funny; a metal. It was shiny and smooth, but it was too big to play with.

So Tim had an idea. He grabbed the metal and started to fold it. He folded it a few times this way and that way, until it was as small as a toy car. He smiled, because now he had something fun to play with.

Tim imagined that the folded metal was now a toy car and it could drive around his room. He was so busy playing with his new toy car that he forgot all about the big metal. Tim played until he was very tired and then he put his toy car back into the toy box and went to get a drink of water.

The next day, Tim opened his toy box and was so excited to see the folded metal was still there. He had lots of fun playing with it for the rest of the day. The metal had become his favorite toy!

Henry was a brave little boy. He was only three, but he wasn't scared of many things. One day his mommy wanted him to go with her to the store. He was a bit frightened when he saw the store. It was a big, tall building.

Mommy said they were going to buy some powder. Henry asked what powder it was. Mommy said it was special powder that could help him when he was feeling sick.

Henry leaned into his mommy's side. He was still a bit frightened. They entered the store and Mommy went to get the powder. He waited for her next to the cash register and leaned against the wall. The cashier was nice and smiled at him.

Mommy came back carrying a big bag of powder. Henry felt his fears melting away. Mommy put her arm around him and hugged him tight. She said it was time to go home.

Henry leaned against his mommy's side as they walked out of the store. He was still a bit scared but he was also feeling brave and safe. He couldn't wait to get back to his cozy bed.

Jill and Jack were playing outside in their backyard when they heard a loud thunder. Scared of the noise Jill started to cry. Jack looked up into the sky and saw tiny white fluffy clouds. He knew they were only having a mild storm.

He looked at Jill and said, "Don't be scared Jill, it's only thunder. See the clouds? They aren't dark and scary, look how mild they are."

Jill looked up at the clouds and said, "Yeah they are mild, but what if it gets worse?" She was still scared of the noise.

Jack looked around the backyard and noticed a large tree nearby. He smiled and held out his hand. "Come on, let's run under the tree. That way when the thunder comes, it won't scare you anymore!"

Jill grabbed his hand and laughed. Together they ran and hid under the tree. They smiled as the mild thunder came and went.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Pippin. Pippin loved to perform tricks for his friends. He would jump high and run fast, making everyone happy. Pippin was a very good dog.

One day, Pippin saw a big ball near a pass. It was a very pretty ball. Pippin wanted to play with the ball, but it was on the other side of the pass. Pippin was a very persistent dog, so he did not give up. He tried to find a way to get the ball.

Pippin thought and thought. He tried to jump over the pass, but it was too big. He tried to go around the pass, but it was too long. Finally, Pippin had an idea. He would perform his best trick and dig a hole under the pass. Pippin dug and dug until he made a tunnel. He crawled through the tunnel and got the pretty ball. Pippin was very happy, and his friends were proud of him.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim was a selfish boy. He did not like to share his things with others. One day, his mom brought home a big bag of vegetables. She wanted to explain to Tim why it was important to share.

"Tim," said Mom, "we need to share these vegetables with our neighbors. It is not good to be selfish." Tim did not want to share the vegetables. He wanted to keep them all for himself. But Mom told him, "If you share, you will make others happy."

Tim thought about it and then said, "No, I don't want to share." So, he took the vegetables and hid them in his room. The neighbors were sad because they had no food to eat. They knocked on Tim's door and asked if he had any food to share. Tim did not want to share, so he said no.

That night, Tim ate all the vegetables by himself. He felt very full and sick. He wished he had listened to his mom and shared with the neighbors. But now, it was too late. The vegetables were gone, and Tim felt very bad.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous cactus. Its spikes were as sharp as thorns, and it's green body reached far into the sky.

One day, a three year old came across the cactus. She was walking in the desert and noticed how big it was. She got close to the enormous cactus and called out to her mom, asking to pick it.

Her mom quickly told her to keep away. She said, "No no. You can't miss that cactus."

But the three year old was very stubborn and she ignored her mom and reached out for the cactus. As soon as she touched it, she was hurt by the sharp spikes.

She began to cry loudly and felt a lot of pain. Her mom quickly came to help her. The three year old felt very sad and she had to go to the doctor.

Sadly, the three year old had to miss playing outdoors and visit the doctor often, because of the enormous cactus.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a girl named Amy. She loved to eat delicious apples from her tree. One day, she saw a big, red apple at the top of the tree.

She asked her friend Tom, who was tall, if she could borrow his ladder. Tom said yes, and they put the ladder by the tree. Amy climbed up and picked the big, red apple. She was very happy.

Later, Amy went to see her tutor, Mr. Owl. She shared the apple with him. Mr. Owl said it was the most delicious apple he had ever eaten. They both laughed and had a great day.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to play with her toys, but today was different. She was outside with her parents and there were a lot of people around. They were all wealthy people and were talking about something strange.

Lucy listened carefully, but the words were all strange to her. She then noticed one wealthy man pointing to his toes. She wondered why and asked her dad, "What's he pointing at?"

Her dad laughed and smiled, "That man is showing off his money! He's wealthy and he wants everyone to know."

This made little Lucy excited. She wished she had money too. She wanted to show off her wealth like the man.

But then her dad said something that made her sad. He said, "It's just playing pretend. You don't need money to have fun!"

So Lucy put away her dreams of being wealthy and went back to playing with her toys. But secretly she still hoped one day she could show off her own wealth too!

Cindy was a three year old girl who loved playing in the garden. One day she ran out of the house and opened the gate. She was so excited to explore, and started looking around.

Suddenly, Cindy noticed a wheat field. She thought it looked like a magical place, so she ran inside. She gasped as she saw a big, beautiful sunflower.

"I wish I could freeze this moment forever," she said aloud.

Just then, Cindy heard a voice. "No, that's not easy. It takes a lot of work to grow wheat," the voice said.

Cindy turned and saw a farmer standing in the field. She didn't understand what the farmer meant, so she just smiled and said, "I still wish I could freeze this moment."

The farmer looked at Cindy kindly and with a twinkle in his eye, said, "Perhaps you can, but it takes effort. You need to plant the wheat, water it and look after it. With some work, you'll be able to enjoy this moment for a long time."

So Cindy started to work on the field, and soon she was able to enjoy the beautiful wheat field she'd discovered. She felt proud of her efforts and happy that she'd been able to freeze a moment in time that she could enjoy for a very long time.

Once upon a time, there was a dinosaur. He was very big and he was very kind. He was a compassionate dinosaur.

One day, he saw a little girl. She looked sad and he wanted to help her. He asked her why she was so sad.

The little girl started to cry. She told him that she had lost her favourite bird. The dinosaur said he was sorry and asked her if there was anything he could do to help.

The little girl thought for a moment, then she had an idea. She mentioned that maybe they could look together. The dinosaur said that sounded like a good idea and they set off on their search.

After a while, they found the little girl's bird! The little girl was so happy and thanked the kind dinosaur. Then they both went on their way.

The dinosaur was very happy that he had been able to help. He felt proud and was reminded that it is important to be compassionate.

Molly and Brad were in love. They decided to marry each other. Brad bought Molly a pretty bathrobe for their wedding. Molly was so happy and said, "this looks so organized!"

They got married in a big church with all their family and friends. It was a beautiful day and Molly and Brad looked so happy together.

At the reception, everyone clapped and cheered for them. Molly wore her bathrobe and Brad wore a nice suit. They had fun with their friends and family and ate lots of tasty cake.

At the end of the night, Molly and Brad hugged each other and kissed. They were so happy to be married and they couldn't wait to start their new life together.

Once upon a time, there were two good friends, Ben and Sam. They loved to be together and often joined their two hands to make a frame. Ben and Sam felt the frame was very delicate, and only wanted to use it for special things.

One day, the friends decided to join the frame around a pretty flower in their garden. The flower looked beautiful inside the delicate frame and the friends decided to pick it and show it to everyone in the neighborhood.

Ben and Sam walked through the town holding the framed flower, and everyone they saw said it was the most beautiful flower they had ever seen. Pretty soon, the whole town was filled with framed flowers, and everyone was joining hands to create their own delicate frames. Ben and Sam smiled at each other, proud of what they had done.

Bob was a little boy. He had a sleepy shirt. He liked to wear it. One day, Bob wanted to try something different. He wanted to enter the forest. So he put on his shirt and entered.

When Bob entered the forest, he saw a lot of birds and butterflies. He felt so happy and excited. He ran around and played with the animals. He felt so happy and carefree.

After a while, Bob started to get very sleepy. He lay down on the grass and closed his eyes. He fell asleep with the birds singing in the background.

Bob had a nice sleep. When he woke up, he felt better and refreshed. He put on his sleepy shirt and walked back home. He had a wonderful time in the forest.

Once there was a grumpy school teacher called Mrs. Johnson. She was always so cross and never wanted to laugh or play.

On the wall of Mrs. Johnson's classroom was a big blackboard with chalk stuck to it. Every day the children in the classroom would come in and learn something new.

One day, Mrs. Johnson was feeling very grumpy and cross as usual. She was shouting and scolding the children and they all started to get very scared.

Suddenly, an angel flew into the classroom! The angel had a bright light around her and she said to Mrs. Johnson:

"It's time to heal your heart. Start by being kind to the children in your classroom."

Mrs. Johnson started to feel a warmth in her heart. She smiled at the children, hugged them and played games with them. Everyone was so happy.

At the end of the day, Mrs. Johnson felt much better and everyone thanked the angel for helping her to heal. The angel smiled and flew off into the bright blue sky.

Joey loved playing with his friend Penny. Today they decided to take a walk around the park. Joey looked around and noticed the fog was getting closer. But he wasn't scared, because he knew his friend was dependable.

So together they began to walk. As they went around the lake, Joey suddenly heard a sound. He stopped and asked Penny, "What was that?"
"It's a whistle," answered Penny. "Let's follow it."

They began to follow the whistle, until it led them to a wooden bridge. They looked around and saw an old man who was smiling and whistling. He said, "Hello my children. Are you ready for an adventure?"
Joey and Penny smiled and eagerly said, "Yes!"

The old man then took them on a magical journey through the fog. They saw all sorts of wonderful things. The old man said goodbye to Joey and Penny and wished them well.

Joey and Penny thanked the old man, and said goodbye. As they walked back home, Joey whispered to Penny, "Thank you for being so dependable today."
"You're welcome," Penny smiled.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went to the park with his mommy. Timmy loved going down the slide, but today there was a big problem. The slide was too short! Timmy was sad because he wanted to slide more.

Timmy's mommy saw him looking sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy said, "Slide too short. Want more slide." His mommy had an idea! She took a tube and added it to the slide. Now the slide was longer! Timmy was happy and said, "Mommy, you fixed it! Thank you!"

Timmy slid down the slide again and again, but after a while, he started feeling dizzy. He told his mommy, "Mommy, dizzy!" His mommy said, "Okay, let's take a break and get some ice cream." Timmy smiled and said, "Yay, ice cream!"

Once there was a little girl named Becky who loved to play outside. All of her favorite things to do were running, jumping and playing hide-and-seek.

One day, when Becky was playing outside, it started to get really cold. The air was so still, it felt like it was frozen. Suddenly, all the leaves on the trees stopped moving and everything around Becky was quiet. She had never seen anything like it!

Becky was so curious that she started to move really slowly, hoping not to make a sound. She crept to the edge of the garden and spotted a door, it looked like it was the exit! She slowly opened the door, it was icy cold. Inside, there was a room filled with spoiled food. Becky couldn't believe her eyes!

When the door shut behind her, Becky realized that she was in trouble. She tried to open the door three times but nothing happened. She was frozen in the room, unable to escape!

Fortunately, Becky's mom and dad soon realized that she was missing. They quickly followed her trail and found her inside the cold room. Once she was free from the exit, Becky hugged her mom and dad and thanked them for finding her!

Once upon a time, two friends, Jack and Lily, were walking in the park. Lily noticed an old bookcase in the park and wanted to take a closer look.

Lily: "Look Jack, there's a bookcase!"

Jack: "Oh wow! I wonder what's inside?"

Lily: "Let's go see!"

The two friends ran over to the bookcase, and inside they found a jar of honey.

Jack: "Oh wow! Let's taste it!"

Lily: "Yes! Taste it and see if it's yummy."

Jack and Lily tasted the honey. It was so sweet and delicious.

Jack: "This is very important! We should keep it safe."

Lily: "Yes! We can put it in our bookcase at home."

And so that's what Jack and Lily did. They put the jar of honey in the bookcase in their house and kept it safe. They never forgot the important and tasty honey.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved watching movies with his family. One day, they started watching a movie about a princess and a dragon. Timmy was so excited to watch it!

But then, his little sister Sally started to cry. "I want to watch a different movie!" she said, feeling jealous of the attention Timmy was getting.

Timmy's mom said, "Don't worry Sally, we can start a new movie after this one is finished." And so, they all watched the princess and the dragon together, and Sally was happy again. The end.

Ben and Jen are twins. They live in a hut with their mom and dad. They have a dog, a cat and a hen. The dog is big and brown. The cat is small and black. The hen is white and lays eggs.

Every morning, Ben and Jen help their mom and dad. They feed the dog, the cat and the hen. They give them water and food. The dog likes bones. The cat likes milk. The hen likes corn. They are happy animals.

But one day, Ben and Jen are lazy. They do not want to feed the dog, the cat and the hen. They want to play with their toys. They say to their mom and dad, "We are tired. We do not want to feed the animals. You do it."

Their mom and dad are not happy. They say to Ben and Jen, "You are not tired. You are lazy. You have to feed the animals. They are hungry and thirsty. They need you. If you do not feed them, they will be sad and sick."

Ben and Jen feel bad. They do not want to make the animals sad and sick. They say to their mom and dad, "We are sorry. We will feed the animals. We love them." They go to the hut and get the water and food. They feed the dog, the cat and the hen. They pet them and talk to them. The animals are happy and healthy. Ben and Jen are happy and proud. They are not lazy. They are good twins.

Once upon a time there was a little duck called Tom. Tom wanted to have an adventure and explore the world outside his pond. One day, Tom made an organized plan - he wanted to build a sail and go for a travel. He gathered all the materials he needed and soon he had the most beautiful sail ever made.

Tom was so excited that he couldn't wait to leave. He sailed far away and didn't look back.

As he sailed, he saw many interesting creatures and exciting locations. He felt so safe and protected travelling by sea.

After a few days, a terrible storm hit the ocean and Tom's sail was no longer safe. He tried to protect it with all his might but it was no match for the storm.

The sail broke to pieces and Tom was thrown into the sea. He tried to swim back to the shore but he was too exhausted and eventually sunk under the water and was never seen again.

Mama was tired. She had been washing dishes by hand all day and her hands were getting sore. She wanted to find a better way to do it. Then one day, she saw a big blue box in the store. It was a dishwasher! She bought it and brought it home.

Mama was so excited. She put a bunch of dishes in it, filled it with soapy water, then pushed a button. The dishwasher started to hum and make bubbles. Mama smiled.

When the dishwasher was done, the dishes were very clean and dry. Mama had to put them away. She was so happy. No more washing dishes by hand! From now on, Mama would use the dishwasher to keep her dishes clean and dry.

One day, Joe was very troubled. He wanted to fix something but he didn't know what. He walked around, looking for something to do, when he saw an old, rusty motorcycle. He knew right away what he wanted to do - decorate it! He got some paint, glue and some sparkles and set to work. He painted the bike different colors and added some sparkles to make it even more special. When he was done, Joe was so proud of his work. Everyone in the town would stop and admire Joe's beautiful, decorated motorcycle. Joe was no longer troubled. He was so happy and excited to show off his work.

Once upon a time there was a yacht. It floated in the deep blue sea. The yacht was big and white and shiny. The people who lived in the yacht were happy.

One day, the people on the yacht wanted to add something special. They asked a friendly fish. The fish gave them a disgusting old shell. The people laughed but they decided to add it to the yacht.

The people decorated the shell with shiny pain and blue ribbons. It looked lovely. The people added it to the yacht and the yacht looked even better! Everyone on the yacht was so happy.

Bobro was very sad. He had no friends and wanted someone to play with him. He sat alone in the park eating his pizza. Suddenly, he heard a voice.

"Hey Bobro, I'm Sonny. I'm new here and I don't know anyone. Can I be your friend?" asked Sonny.

Bobro was so excited. Suddenly, he had a daring idea.

"Let's play a game!" he said, smiling. "I dare you to jump rope for 3 minutes straight."

Sonny happily accepted the challenge and the two of them jumped rope together for a few minutes. After they finished, Bobro was even happier. He was no longer sad, and he had finally made a new friend.

The sun was shining warmly and Ben was playing in the backyard. He liked to jump around and feel the soft grass tickle his toes. He heard a funny noise coming from behind the old tree and he ran to investigate.
Ben then saw a small fluffy bunny hopping around, it was sooo cute! He wanted to pick it up, but was scared to scare it away. But then he saw the bunny looking straight at him. Ben smiled and asked the bunny;
"Hi little one, can I play with you?"
Suddenly the bunny hopped away and revealed a hidden hole. Ben ran up to it and peered inside. It was so dark and he couldn't see anything. He called out to the bunny;
"Hello? can you come out? I won't hurt you!"
He looked around the backyard trying to find the bunny, but it was nowhere to be seen. He couldn't believe it. He thought the bunny was his new friend! Suddenly he heard a whisper coming from the hole,
"Come back tomorrow, I'll be waiting for you".
Ben was so excited; he was finally going to have a friend! He knew he wouldn't forget and he would be back the next day for sure.

Once there was a bear who loved spicy food. He always used to pick the spiciest of all the food in the village. One day, he was making his usual rounds at the village market when he saw his friend, the rabbit. The bear waved and the rabbit bowed in response.

The bear asked the rabbit what he had in his basket and the rabbit replied, "I'm bringing yummy carrot cake to my grandmother. It's her favourite."

The bear immediately started drooling. He asked the rabbit if he could have some and the rabbit said, "Sure, but it's really spicy. Are you sure you can take such a pain?"

The bear was too excited to wait. He eagerly took the carrot cake and bit into it. Alas! The bear had never tasted such a spicy food before. Suddenly his mouth was on fire and he yelped in pain.

The bear learnt a lesson that day: when it comes to food, not everything that tastes fancy is necessarily best for you.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red truck. They pretended the truck could take them to different places, like the park, the zoo, or the moon.

One day, their mom said they could have dessert after dinner, but only if they were helpful and cleaned their room. Lily and Ben agreed, and ran to their room. They started to put their toys in a big box, but then they saw the red truck.

"Let's play with the truck first," Ben said. "We can clean later."

"No, we have to be helpful," Lily said. "Mom will be happy if we clean now, and then we can have dessert."

"But I want to play with the truck," Ben said. "It's so fun. I believe it can fly."

Lily thought for a moment. She liked the truck too, but she also wanted dessert. She had an idea.

"OK, let's play with the truck, but only for a little bit," she said. "And then we can use the truck to help us clean. We can put the toys in the truck, and drive them to the box. It will be faster and more fun."

Ben liked the idea. He smiled and nodded.

"OK, let's do that," he said. "The truck is helpful too."

They played with the truck for a little bit, and then they used it to help them clean. They drove the truck around the room, and picked up the toys. They made vroom and beep sounds, and pretended they were on a mission.

Soon, their room was clean, and their mom came to check on them.

"Wow, you did a great job," she said. "You were very helpful. I'm proud of you. Now you can have dessert."

Lily and Ben were happy. They thanked their mom, and followed her to the kitchen. They saw a big cake with chocolate and sprinkles.

"Wow, that looks yummy," Lily said.

"Yes, it does," Ben said. "Can we have a big piece?"

"Sure, you can," their mom said. "You earned it. You were very helpful."

Lily and Ben smiled. They ate their cake, and shared some with the truck. They believed the truck was happy too.

Jack was happy to be at the beach. He had been looking forward to it all day. He saw lots of people jumping in the water and surfing on their boards. Everyone was having a lot of fun.

He climbed onto a board himself and started paddling. His eyes lit up when he saw how far the waves were taking him. He felt like he had wings on the board.

After some time, the people around cheered and applauded when Jack stood up on the board. He was so happy and proud of himself. A few minutes later, he tried again, but failed. He felt ashamed and started crying.

His Dad noticed and came to his side. He hugged Jack and wiped away his tears. â€œI think you're a natural surfer,â€ Dad said encouragingly. â€œDon't be ashamed, you just need more practice. You did really great! I'm really proud of you.â€

Once upon a time, there was a red rhinoceros. He was a big, strong rhinoceros. Every day he would run around and play in the grass.

The rhinoceros was sad because the boy was scared. He decided to bring the boy some flowers, so that the boy would understand that the rhinoceros was friendly.

The boy was surprised to see all the beautiful flowers. He smiled and hugged the rhinoceros. He finally understood that the rhinoceros was his friend, and they played and laughed together.

Mama and baby were in the car. They were going to the grocery. Mama was tired, but baby was excited. They drove to the grocery and Mama got out of the car with baby. They went into the grocery and baby saw lots of fun things.

Mama and baby walked around the store and picked out some food. Baby wanted lots of treats, but Mama said no. Mama and baby finished shopping and they went back to the car.

They drove home and Mama put away the groceries. Baby was tired from all the fun at the grocery, so Mama put him in bed. Mama tucked him in and kissed him goodnight. Baby fell asleep and Mama finished cleaning up the kitchen.

Once there was a little girl called Amy. She was very curious and loved exploring. One day she asked her mummy, "What's a stadium?"

Amy had a wonderful time and she will never forget her first visit to the stadium.

Once there was an angry monkey. He was so angry that he started to scatter things everywhere. He scattered all of his toys, his pillow and even the food. He threw it all around the room.

Then he heard a voice. He turned to see a little girl, no more than three years old, standing there. When she saw the mess the monkey had made, she started to cry.

"Why is the monkey so angry?" she asked between sobs.

The monkey hung his head. "I don't know," he said sadly. "I just feel so sad."

The little girl reached out her hand, and the monkey let her stroke his fur. Then the girl said something wonderful. "I know how to help!"

The little girl ran out of the room and came back a few minutes later with a handful of flowers. She scattered the flowers all around the monkey, while singing a soft wordless song. All around them the flowers bloomed and the room filled with a sweet fragrance.

The monkey smiled softly and felt much better. He was no longer angry and he was no longer dead inside. All thanks to the little girl and her magical flowers.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park. He would run around and pick up sticks and rocks. One day, Timmy saw a big pile of grass. He decided to throw the grass up in the air and watch it fall down.

As Timmy was playing, he saw a man walking towards him. The man looked sad and tired. Timmy's mom always told him to be kind to others, so Timmy went up to the man and said hello. The man smiled and thanked Timmy for being friendly.

Timmy felt grateful that he could make someone happy just by saying hello. He remembered the pile of grass he had thrown earlier and had an idea. He asked the man if he wanted to play with him and throw the grass up in the air. The man's face lit up and he said yes.

Timmy and the man played together for a while and had a lot of fun. As the man was leaving, he thanked Timmy again for being so kind. Timmy felt happy that he could make a new friend and was grateful for the fun they had playing together.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a hidden kite in his room. He was very happy and wanted to play with it. He ran to his mom to show her the kite. "Mom, look! I found a kite!" he said.

His mom tried to explain to him that it was not a good day to fly the kite. The wind was too strong and it could be dangerous. But Tim did not listen to her. He wanted to fly the kite anyway. "Please, Mom, let me play with the kite!" he begged.

So, Tim took the kite outside and started to play with it. The wind was very strong, and it pulled the kite high into the sky. Tim was very happy, but he did not know how to control the kite. Suddenly, the wind pulled the kite away from him. He tried to catch it, but it was too late.

"Mom, help! My kite is gone!" Tim cried. His mom came outside and saw the kite flying away. She was sad for Tim, but she knew this would happen. "I tried to explain, Tim. The wind was too strong," she said.

Tim was very sad and upset. He had lost his hidden kite. He wished he had listened to his mom. Now, he had nothing to play with and the day had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bee named Buzzy. Buzzy loved to fly around and explore the world. He flew above a river and saw something very interesting. It was an oxygen tank, split in two!

Buzzy flew around the tank, confused. He had never seen anything like it before. Buzzy wanted to get closer, so he carefully flew inside the oxygen tank. It was dark, but he could still see water everywhere around him.

He decided it was time to find out where the split had happened. He flew up to the top of the oxygen tank and saw that it was very broken. There was a big crack in the middle. That must have been what caused the tank to split.

Buzzy flew out of the tank and went back to his friends. He told them all about his amazing discovery. They were very impressed! From that day on, they all paid more attention to the world around them.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jack and Lucy. They were very happy, until one day, Jack said that he was going to marry someone and he couldn't tell Lucy who it was. Lucy was sad and asked Jack to tell her. He said that the language was too weird for her to understand.

Lucy didn't understand why she couldn't know and started to cry. Jack noticed and sat next to her. He said, "Don't worry, Lucy. I think you'll be pleased when I marry. It'll be like a happy surprise."

Lucy sniffed and asked Jack, "Will it make you happy?"

"Yes, of course," said Jack with a smile. "I'm going to marry my love and that's what makes me happy."

Lucy was surprised but happy. She hugged Jack and said, "That's the best surprise ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a shy little bird named Tweety. One day, he went for a walk around the park. As he was walking, he slipped on a banana peel and fell to the ground. He tried to fly away, but he hurt his wing. Upset, he started to cry.

A kindly veterinarian saw him and took him in. She said to him, "Don't worry little Tweety, I can help." Tweety, still feeling shy, just nodded.

The veterinarian said, "I'll have to take care of your wing for a few days so that you can fly again. Can you come back tomorrow?" Tweety nodded and the veterinarian smiled.

The next day, Tweety came back. He was feeling much better and flew around the park again. He never slipped again and was happy he had been able to find help!

Once upon a time, there was a little bee. The bee was very filthy. It did not like to be clean. The bee had many friends, but they did not like how dirty it was.

One day, the bee went to play with its friends. The friends said, "We hate how filthy you are! We don't want to play with you." The bee felt very sad but did not want to be clean.

The bee went to find new friends. It found a big spider. The spider said, "I like how filthy you are. We can be friends." The bee was happy to have a new friend. But the spider was not a good friend. It wanted to eat the bee.

In the end, the spider ate the bee. The bee's old friends were sad. They wished they had been kinder to the filthy bee.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Karen. She was three years old and loved to play. Karen loved to kick the ball around in her garden.

One day, Karen kicked the ball very high. It went right over the fence and into the neighbour's garden! Karen hopped over the fence to get it back.

When she got to the other garden, Karen found a brilliant prize! It was shiny and sparkly, and even had her name written on it.

Karen was so excited; she had found a special prize. She quickly grabbed the prize and ran back to her garden. Karen was so happy, she started to kick the ball around again!

The sun was shining and little Tommy was full of energy. He was running around the garden and laughing with delight. His mommy was following him closely, watching him with love.

Suddenly, Tommy heard a strange noise - the sound of a motor! He walked towards it and saw it coming from his neighbor's car. He was so excited and started jumping around the car, saying "motor, motor!".

His mommy came up and said, smiling, "That's right, Tommy. That's a motor. It helps us move around."

Tommy kept jumping and watching the motor with fascination. He said in his little, helpless voice, "Mommy, can I keep the motor? Please, Mommy?"

Mommy looked at Tommy, her heart filled with love. She said, "No, Tommy, we can't keep the motor. But you can enjoy watching it!"

Tommy smiled, happy that he could still watch the motor from his garden. He ran around again, and the motor kept running, helping people get around.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside and explore. One day, Timmy went on an adventure to find a treasure. He looked high and low, but he couldn't find anything.

As he was walking, he saw a big pot with steam coming out of it. He went closer and saw an old lady cooking soup. The old lady saw Timmy and invited him to have some soup. Timmy was hesitant at first because the soup looked ugly, but he decided to try it anyway.

To his surprise, the soup tasted delicious! Timmy realized that sometimes things that look ugly on the outside can be beautiful on the inside. He thanked the old lady and continued his adventure, feeling happy and grateful for the lesson he learned.

Once upon a time there was a bad jungle. No one wanted to go near it, because it was so bad. But one day a little girl decided to go in and explore. She saw a lot of wild animals she had never seen before. She was a bit scared, but she kept going.

She eventually found a baby monkey in the jungle. It was so small and scared, so the girl decided to feed it. She picked some fruit from the jungle and the monkey happily ate it all up.

The monkey became her friend, and every day she would feed it and play with it. The jungle didn't seem so bad after all now that she had a new friend.

They stayed together in the jungle for a long time. The girl stopped being scared of the bad jungle and found lots of other animals she could feed and play with.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a parade. Everyone was wearing comfortable clothes and were happy. They all had something to attach to their outfit. Some had balloons, others had ribbons, and some had flags. Everyone was having a great time.

They all went away feeling very happy, knowing that they had been part of a great parade. And from now on, each time they saw a parade, they would remember how wonderful and comfortable it was.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Joe and Sam. Joe had a quiz and was very excited to take it. He wanted Sam to take it too, but Sam was a bit impatient.

Once upon a time, a little girl went to find a cave. She knew the cave was very far away and the path was difficult. She kept walking until she got to the cave. Once she arrived, she noticed something was attached to the cave. She looked closer and saw a pink flower! She thought it was the most beautiful thing she had ever seen. She decided to attach her own flower to the cave. She was very proud of her work. From that day forward, she wanted to go back to the cave every day. The cave became a special place to her.

John loves watching pigeons. He watched from his bedroom window as they fluttered and hopped around in the garden. Today they were especially calm, which made John even more excited.

He ran downstairs to the garden and saw lots of them. He pointed at a nearby pigeon and smiled. The pigeon turned its head to look at him. John leaned in closer, but it flew away and joined the others.

John followed the pigeons, pointing at them as they flew and hopped. He was so happy to watch them move around, he didn't even notice when his mother called him in for dinner.

After dinner, John ran back to the garden, but the pigeons were no longer there. He was sad - but he knew he can see them again tomorrow. He smiled, waved goodbye and went back inside.

One day, a big rain came. It made the ground very wet. A little boy named Tim went outside to play. He saw a small bird who was sad.

"Why are you sad?" Tim asked the bird.

"My nest is wet, and I can't keep my eggs warm," the bird said.

Tim wanted to help the bird. He found a dry spot under a big tree. He helped the bird move her nest there. The bird was happy.

"Thank you, Tim," said the bird. "Now I can keep my eggs warm."

From that day on, Tim and the bird were good friends. They played together every day, even when the ground was wet.

Maia and Mom were walking down the street, admiring the tidy gardens. Maia saw a butterfly flitting from one bush to the next.

"Mom," she said, pointing, "look, pretty!"

Mom smiled at her. "Yes indeed. It is beautiful, isn't it ?"

Maia nodded and asked, "Will you carry me?"

Mom picked her up and put her on her shoulder. Maia giggled and asked, "Where are we going?"

"To the park, silly!" Mom said, tickling her.

But when they got to the park, Maia wasn't sure what to do. She looked around and asked, "What can I play with, Mom ?"

Mom pointed to a slide, a swing, and a jungle gym. "There's lots of fun things here! Why don't you start by tidying up your toys when you're done?"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who wanted a new toy. He asked his parents if they would buy him the toy, but they said no. He was very sad.

The little boy thought of an idea. He saw a wide river and wondered if he could trade with someone on the other side. He found a boat, and paddled across the river.

When he reached the other side, he saw a man. The man said he would give the little boy the toy if the little boy gave him a hug.

The little boy was scared and asked the man if he could forgive him, but the man said no. Instead, he took all of the little boy's toys, and sailed away in the boat.

The little boy was very sad and cried all the way home. He never got the new toy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read the newspaper every morning with her daddy. One day, Lily's daddy couldn't find the newspaper. He looked everywhere but it was nowhere to be found.

Lily asked, "Daddy, where is the newspaper?"

"I don't know, Lily. I can't find it," replied her daddy.

Lily said, "Let's organize the room and maybe we can find it." So they organized the room and found the newspaper under a pile of clothes. Daddy was happy and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are so helpful." They read the newspaper together and enjoyed a mild morning.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved trips. She woke up one morning and asked her mom, "Can we go on a trip today?" Her Mom smiled and said, "Yes, let's go!"

The little girl got dressed quickly and they went outside. The sun was bright and the sky was a beautiful color.

The mom and the little girl walked to the park and went to the pond. The little girl became very excited and wanted to stir the pond. She grabbed the stick and stirred the water.

The pond became a colorful whirlpool of fun. The little girl was so happy that she danced around with joy. Inside the whirlpool, she found colorful fish, rocks, and some small treasure.

The mom and the little girl had a wonderful trip and returned home with lots of beautiful memories.

Once upon a time, there was a race between two animals, a rabbit and a turtle. The rabbit was very fast and the turtle was very slow. The rabbit liked to win and be the best. He was very competitive.

The turtle said, "I may be slow, but I will try my best." The race started and the rabbit ran very fast. The turtle was very slow and the rabbit was very far ahead. The rabbit thought he was going to win.

But, the rabbit got tired and took a nap. The turtle kept going and going. The turtle finally passed the rabbit and won the race! The turtle gained a lot by not giving up and trying his best. The moral of the story is to never give up and always try your best.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He was playing in his backyard when he found a magic wand. He picked it up and said, "Wow, this is magic!"

Suddenly, a fairy appeared and said, "I am the fairy of the magic wand. You can make anything happen by pulling the wand."

Timmy was so excited and he pulled the wand. The fairy then turned his ordinary toy car into a real car. Timmy was amazed and said, "This is so cool! Thank you, fairy!" The fairy smiled and said, "You're welcome, Timmy. Just remember, with great power comes great responsibility." And with that, the fairy disappeared. Timmy played with his new car and promised to use the magic wand wisely.

One day, a silly cat named Tom found a hoop in the yard. He wanted to play with it, but it was too big. Tom thought very hard about how to make the hoop smaller.

Tom had an idea. He would stretch the hoop to make it smaller. He put his paws on the hoop and pulled as hard as he could. The hoop started to stretch! It got smaller and smaller.

Now, the hoop was just the right size for Tom to play with. He jumped through the hoop and chased it around the yard. Tom had so much fun playing with his new toy. And that is the story of the silly cat and the hoop.

One day, a ball went for a roll in the park. The ball was red and liked to roll very fast. The ball rolled down a big hill and bumped into a poor cat. The cat was sad because it hurt.

"Ouch!" said the cat, "Why did you roll into me?" The ball felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, cat. I did not see you. Can I help you feel better?" The cat nodded and they went to find a nurse.

They found a nurse near a big tree. The nurse was kind and helped the poor cat. She put a band on the cat's leg. The cat felt better and thanked the nurse. The ball and the cat became friends and played together in the park.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy cup who lived in an enormous castle. Every day the cup would march through the castle's grand hallways, admiring its beauty.

One day, the cup was strolling through the corridors when it ran into a tiny mouse. The cup stopped and asked the mouse, "What are you doing here?" The mouse replied, "I am looking for food. I haven't eaten anything in days!"

The cup felt sorry for the mouse and decided to help. It marched to the castle kitchen and brought back a cup filled with cheese. The mouse was thrilled and thanked the cup for its help.

The cup smiled and said, "You're welcome! It's so important to help those who are less fortunate than us." The mouse nodded in agreement and happily scurried off to enjoy its meal.

From then on, the wealthy cup was known as the most generous in the castle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to explore. She was very curious and excited to find out what she would discover.

One day, she found a box with a colorful mask inside. She was amazed by its shiny colors and wanted to take it home. She held the mask close to her chest and the box too.

The girl was about to lift the box when she heard a noise coming from the corner of the room. She looked over and saw a smiling cat wearing the same mask she had found. The girl was so excited and wanted to give it try.

The girl immediately put on the mask and skipped over to the cat. The cat seemed happy to see her wearing the same colorful mask.

The girl lifted the box and brought it back home. She showed her mom and dad the mask, and they were both happy to see it.

The little girl and the cat wore the colorful masks in many adventures to come. The masks were always a reminder to the little girl of how much fun it is to explore and make new discoveries.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Susie. She was very scared of the dark. One night when Susie's parents were out, Susie heard a noise coming from the kitchen. She was too scared to check what it was so she just stayed in her bedroom.

Suddenly there was a bright light coming from the kitchen. Susie was scared but she also wanted to know what it was. She tiptoed towards the kitchen door and whispered: "Hello?"

The light was coming from the fridge and it had started to shine! Susie felt relieved but then she noticed something strange. The fridge was covered with a big, dark and spooky shadow! Susie was so scared she started screaming and ran away back to her bedroom. She never went back to the kitchen again.

Once there was a little girl named Mary. She was embarrassed when she saw a hive in the nearby field. It was a huge hive and it was filled with bees!

But the bees were not angry. They were quite mild and didn't even buzz around. Even though she was scared, Mary felt that she had to go see it.

So she went to the bee hive and looked inside. It was full of little wax cells, filled with honey! Mary was amazed and she smiled. She was no longer scared, she was happy to have discovered this hive.

But then, something embarrassing happened. Mary accidentally knocked over the hive! All the honey and wax spilled out, making a giant sticky mess.

Mary quickly ran away from the hive, embarrassed that she had made such a big mess. But she would never forget the mild and friendly bees in the hive.

She saw Tom and Mia playing with a doll. She called them and said, "Look at my veil! Isn't it wonderful?" Tom and Mia looked at her and nodded. They said, "Yes, it is very wonderful. Can we see it?" Lily said, "No, it is mine. You can't touch it." She hugged her sack and her veil and ran away.
