Joe stepped back and looked at his masterpiece. He smiled as the colours twirled around in the mix. His dad saw him and asked â€œWhat are you doing, Joe?â€

Joe proudly held up the handle. â€œLook Dad! I made the night sky even more colourful. Now the stars are really shining!â€

His dad smiled and gave Joe a hug. He said â€œThat looks great! Now the dark night sky is even more beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a little goat named Sammy. Sammy was a very happy goat who loved to play in the fields all day long. But one day, Sammy was feeling worried. He didn't know why, but he just felt something wasn't right.

So Sammy went to his friend, the farmer, and asked him, "What's wrong? Why do I feel so worried?" The farmer just shrugged and said, "I don't know, Sammy. Maybe something bad is going to happen. Let's keep a look out."

So Sammy kept an eye out all day, looking for anything suspicious. He saw some birds flying and some animals scurrying around, but nothing out of the ordinary.

Finally, the farmer came out and said, "Well, Sammy, I think everything is okay. Let's go out and have some fun."

So they played in the fields all day, and Sammy forgot all about his worries. He had a great time, and knew that all was right in the world.

Lily was very happy. Today was her birthday. She had a big cake with candles and a lovely dress with flowers. She wanted to share her cake with her friends. She asked her mom if she could invite them to her house.

Mom said yes, but she had a surprise for Lily. She said Lily would meet someone new and get a special present. Lily was curious. Who could it be? What could it be? She hoped it was something fun and nice.

Mom took Lily to the car and drove to a big place with many animals. Lily loved animals. She saw dogs, cats, birds, rabbits, and more. She wanted to pet them all. Mom said they were here to adopt one of them. Lily was very excited. She could have a new friend!

Mom took Lily to a room where a lady was waiting. The lady smiled and said hello. She had a box in her hands. She said it was for Lily. She opened the box and Lily saw a small, fluffy, white kitten. The kitten looked at Lily with big, blue eyes and meowed softly. Lily gasped. She loved the kitten. She reached out and touched its fur. It was soft and warm. The kitten licked her hand and purred.

Lily hugged the kitten and thanked the lady. She thanked her mom too. She said it was the best present ever. She named the kitten Snowy. She said Snowy was her new best friend. She was very happy. She couldn't wait to show Snowy to her other friends and share her cake with them. She knew they would love Snowy too. It was a lovely birthday.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Carl. He was very hungry and wanted something to eat. He looked around the house and saw a big envelope on the table. He thought maybe the envelope had something special inside, so he opened it up.

What he found inside was a measuring tape. He was so excited and smiled with joy. He grabbed the measuring tape and ran around the house, measuring everything. He measured the table, the chairs, even his bed!

Suddenly, Carl's mom came in and saw what he was doing. She smiled at him and said, "It looks like you're measuring everything. What are you measuring for?"

Carl said, "I'm measuring to find something to eat! I'm so hungry!"

His mom laughed and said, "Well, why don't you come into the kitchen with me and we can look for something tasty."

And so, Carl and his mom went into the kitchen and found all sorts of delicious snacks! Carl was so happy and he never forgot the envelope that contained the measuring tape.

Once there was a very special little girl named Lisa. She had a unique drawer in her room that was filled with fun surprises.

One day, Lisa was looking through the drawer and came across an old torn piece of paper. She pulled it out and was excited to see a drawing on it.

She used her crayons and coloured in the lines of the drawing, adding her own unique touches. When she was finished, she hugged the drawing and put it back in the drawer.

The next day, she had a surprise for her family. She took out the drawing and handed it to her mom. Mom was so surprised to see the beautiful drawing.

Lisa had brought a unique tear to the drawing and it was now a one-of-a-kind work of art! Everyone was so proud of Lisa, and they all agreed that her drawing was the best one in the drawer, and the most unique one of all.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Amy and Jack. They liked to play together in the old gym.

One day, Amy asked Jack, "Do you want to go play at the gym?"

Jack said, "Yes! Let's go!"

So they quickly grabbed their things and went to the old gym. Once they got there, they ran around and played many different games. They played tag, hide-and-seek, and even a game of catch.

After a few hours of playing, Amy said, "Let's go home now, I'm getting tired."

Jack replied, "Okay, let's go home together."

So they said goodbye and went their separate ways. They had a great time playing together at the old gym and they knew they would be back soon to play again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, yellow squash. The squash lived in a garden with many other plants. One day, a foolish bird came to the garden. The bird saw the squash and thought it was a big, yellow ball.

The bird said, "Hello, ball! Can you teach me how to fly?" The squash did not say anything because it was a squash, not a ball. The bird tried to fly with the squash, but it was too heavy. The bird fell down and felt sad.

A wise old owl saw the bird and the squash. The owl said, "Silly bird, that is not a ball. That is a squash!" The bird felt foolish, but the owl helped the bird learn how to fly. The bird thanked the owl and they became friends. The squash stayed in the garden, happy to be a squash and not a ball.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jessie. She was three years old and loved to paint. She had all sorts of colors, but her favorite was pink.

One day, she took her paintbrush and some pink paint, ran to a beautiful open field and started to paint. She painted swirls and shapes in the sky, making them look graceful and pretty.

Suddenly, she heard a voice behind her. It was her mom! She said, "What are you doing, Jessie?"
Jessie replied, "I'm painting in the sky! It's so fun!"

Her mom smiled and said, "It looks lovely! You are so graceful at painting."

Jessie beamed with joy, and finished her painting. With the pink paint, she had managed to make something so beautiful that it even made her mom smile.

Once upon a time, there was a queen. She was a very nice queen. She had a big, pretty castle. The queen had a lot of work to do every day. But today, she wanted to relax.

The queen went to the park to relax. She sat on a soft, green grass. The queen saw a bug. The bug was disgusting. The queen did not like the disgusting bug.

The queen went back to her castle. She was happy to be away from the disgusting bug. Now, the queen could relax in her big, pretty castle. The queen smiled and had a good day.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe. Joe loved baseball. One day he wanted to play with his friends in the park. He went outside wearing a big hat and hunkered down to find his baseball. As Joe scooted around, he heard a loud noise. It was a sneeze. Joe looked up and saw an empty playground. He wondered who had made the noise. He decided to keep looking for his baseball and soon found it near the slide. He was excited and was about to pick it up when he heard the sneeze again. He looked around and saw a kitten by the swings. Joe was happy. He picked up the baseball and played with the kitten all day. They had so much fun and even made up games together. Joe was so happy the playground wasn't empty anymore and that he'd found a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy garage owner called John. John had lots of money and was very proud of it.

One day, a young boy and his father knocked on John's door. They asked if they could have shelter in the garage and John said no. He was not willing to accept them, even though they were poor.

The boy's father spoke up and said, "Please, my son is only three years old and it's getting late. We just need a place to sleep for the night, just until the morning."

But John refused to accept them and said, "I am wealthy and have a nice garage. Not just anyone can stay here!"

The father and son left feeling sad and scared. They walked on into the night not knowing where they could go.

The bad ending is that John never accepted the father and son, and they were out in the cold until the morning.

One day, a small boy called Sam found a kite in the park. He was so happy to see it! He ran to get it and started to fly it.

Suddenly, an old man came over and told him, "Stop! You're disturbing me!" Sam was so scared.

The old man had a very gentle voice. He said, "This kite belongs to me. I lost it a long time ago." Sam was sorry to hear this and apologised to the old man.

The old man was very compassionate. He said, "I'm happy that you found it. Do you want to keep the kite? You can fly it whenever you want".

Sam was overjoyed that the old man was so kind. He thanked him a hundred times and flew away with the kite. He had a wonderful time in the park, flying his kite with a compassionate old man.

Once, there was a little girl named Ella. She was very excited, because today was a very special day.

Ella grabbed her toys and her backpack. Then, she stepped out of her house and started walking.

Ella followed the pathway until she reached a big, red stove in the middle of the forest. It was very unique! Ella looked around and saw nobody.

Ella stepped closer to the stove and asked, "Who are you?".

Suddenly, out of nowhere, Ella heard a voice. It was coming from the stove. It said, "I'm a magical stove! I can grant you three wishes!".

Ella was baffled. But she was also excited about her wishes. She thought for a short moment and made her wishes.

The magical stove granted all of Ella's wishes in an instant. Ella was so happy. She thanked the magical stove and stepped back, returning to her home.

From that moment on, Ella was sure that her wishes would come true. She knew that she had met something very unique that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was not feeling well, so his mom gave him a pill to help him feel better. Tim looked at the pill and thought it was too big for him. He did not want to take it.

Tim's friend, Sam, came to visit. Sam saw the pill and asked, "Why did you not take the pill, Tim?" Tim said, "It is too big, and I am scared." Sam was not selfish and wanted to help. "Let me pass it to you, and I will help you take it," Sam said.

With Sam's help, Tim took the pill. Soon, Tim felt much better. He was happy that Sam was not selfish and helped him. They played together all day and had lots of fun. Tim learned that it is good to have friends who help when you need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She was troubled, because she didn't have anyone to play with. Then one day, she saw a purse! Inside was a note with a surprise; it was an invite!

It was from her friend, Bob. He wanted her to come over and play. Anna was so happy! She put on her shoes and raced outside.

When she got to Bob's house, there were all sorts of toys. They laughed and played for hours. They invited some of their other friends and had a huge party. Everyone had so much fun playing together!

Anna was no longer troubled. She was so glad Bob had invited her over. They became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big farm. On the farm, there was a large chicken. The chicken was very happy and liked to walk around the farm all day. One day, a little girl came to visit the farm with her family. She noticed the large chicken and thought it was very funny. She wanted to play with the chicken, so she went closer to it. The chicken was not scared and let the little girl pet it. They became friends and played together all day. The little girl was very happy to have met such a nice chicken on the farm.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She lived with her mom and dad in a big, white house.

One day Lily's mom told Lily that it was time to wash the chair. Lily didn't want to wash the chair, so she started to pout.

"Come on, Lily," her mom said in a gentle voice. "It won't take long and it will be a graceful job once it's done."

Lily grumbled a bit more but then she eventually got to work. She got the wet cloth and started to rub it on the chair. Then, she got another cloth and started to dry the chair.

By the end of it, the chair looked so beautiful! Lily smiled and was filled with pride.

"Now that is a graceful job!" her mom said as she beamed.

Lily was so proud of herself and she couldn't wait to show everyone the beautiful chair.

Once upon a time, there was a pink balloon. It loved to fly around in the sky, but it was lonely. One day, it went to a park to meet some new friends.

The first thing it saw was a boy playing with a ball. He noticed the balloon and asked if it wanted to play. The balloon was excited and said yes!

They started to play and the balloon was having lots of fun. But then the balloon bumped the ball too hard and the boy started to complain. He said the balloon was too rough and not being careful.

The balloon felt sad and started to cry. But the boy said he was sorry and gave it a hug. He said it was okay and told the balloon to try again.

So the balloon flew around the park, slowly and carefully. And the balloon stayed friends with the boy for many years afterwards. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around outside. But one day, her mom told her she had to study for a test at school. Lily didn't want to study because it wasn't easy for her.

Instead, she decided to play with her toys and forgot all about studying. The next day, she went to school and took the test. But she didn't do well because she didn't study. Her teacher was disappointed and gave her a mop to clean the classroom as a punishment.

Lily realized that studying was important and promised to do better next time. She cleaned the classroom with the mop and thought about how she could make studying easier for herself. From then on, she made sure to study every day and never forgot the importance of it.

Once upon a time, there was a funny little mouse called Sam. Sam had the most creative ideas, but no one paid much attention to them.

One day, Sam decided to do something about it. He grabbed a big box and started to squeeze it with all his might. His tiny little paws managed to create the most amazing sound.

A nearby pigeon heard the sound and was so surprised that it asked, "What was that sound?"

Sam grinned and replied, "It's my creative idea! I'm using the box to make music!"

The pigeon was so impressed that soon all the animals started to join in. Soon, the forest was full of funny little animals squeezing boxes, creating the most wonderful music.

Everyone had a wonderful time and Sam finally felt appreciated for his creative talent.

Once upon a time there was a bear named Bob. Bob loved the woods and enjoyed spending his days there. One day he was walking through the woods when he smelt something spicy. He followed the aroma until he came to a clearing where he found a small fire with a pot of something cooking on top.

Bob went over to have a closer look and said, "What's that?"
Bob heard a voice coming from the pot, "I'm stew! Come and enjoy some, it's very yummy!"

Bob was surprised and said, "Wow, stew!" He couldn't believe it was talking. So he decided to give it a try. Bob tasted the stew and it was so spicy and delicious that he could not help but enjoy it.

He thanked the stew for the delicious meal and said goodbye as he walked away, happy and full from his spicy adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet little girl called Rachel. She liked to spin around in circles very fast. Rachel liked to spin around when she was learning to walk.

One day, Rachel was spinning around in the living room. She spun around the furniture and around and around it went. She was so happy that she could spin around the furniture without falling down.

When Rachel finally stopped spinning, she was so dizzy. She sat down on the furniture and felt dizzy for a few moments. After a while, Rachel felt better and wanted to spin some more.

Rachel and the furniture spun around in circles until she was too tired to spin anymore. Rachel laughed and gave the furniture a big hug as she said goodbye.

Rachel went to bed with a smile on her face, feeling so sweet and happy from spinning around the furniture.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little boy named Tim. He loved to play and run around. One day, Tim saw a tall pole in the park. He thought it would be fun to climb it.

As Tim climbed the pole, he got scared. He was very high up and didn't know how to get down. Tim started to weep. His tears fell down like rain. He called for his mom to help him.

Tim's mom heard him weep and came running. She told him not to worry and to hold on tight. She called a big, strong man to help. The man helped Tim get down from the pole. Tim hugged his mom and said sorry for being naughty. From that day on, Tim never climbed poles again.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lola who loved to play. She had lots of toys and furniture in her room. Lola liked to keep everything organized so she could find all of her things.

Lola flew all around the room and then stopped at the bed. She shouted "dive" and jumped so high, she nearly touched the ceiling. Afterwards, she was so tired, she fell fast asleep.

The next morning when Lola woke up, she couldn't believe what she saw. The furniture was all neatly organized! Maybe her superhero powers worked!

Once upon a time, there was a little chicken. The chicken was very high. It stood on top of a hill and could see the whole wide world.

The chicken was so happy. He clucked and smiled, dancing around the hilltop. One day, the chicken decided to explore. He pecked the ground and hopped around.

Soon, the chicken noticed something new on the ground - it was a worm! The little chicken picked up the worm and proudly showed it off to all his friends. Everyone clucked in delight.

The chicken stood tall, feeling so proud of his discovery. He knew that he could still explore the world, but he chose to stay high on the hill. He looked out into the horizon, and he was happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. She was only three years old and loved to play all day.

Danny was in a hurry. He wanted to get to the park quickly and he ran as fast as he could. His mama said they would be late if he didn't hurry up.

Once there was a pink shape. It was a nice shape and it kept growing. Every day the shape increased.

One day, a boy saw the shape and tried to touch it. The shape got angry and said, "Don't touch me!" The boy was scared and ran.

The boy told his mom what had happened. His mom said, "Maybe you should have been more friendly. Even though the shape was scary, it didn't mean you had to be scared too."

The next day, the shape had increased even more. The boy was curious, so he decided to try again. This time, he said, "Hi. I'm very sorry for being scared yesterday. Can I look at you?"

But before the shape could reply, it started to grow bigger and bigger until it was too big for the boy to handle. He ran away, scared.

Moral: Be friendly even to those who appear scary.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was three years old and very excited. She wanted to bring something special to school to show her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a special toy called a microscope. He loved to sit and look through it to see things up close.

Lily started to feel worried. She didn't know where her ball was, and she wanted to play with it. She decided to ask her friends if they had seen it. Her friends said they hadn't seen it, but Lily saw a thief running away with her ball!

Lily knew she had to choose what to do next. She could cry and be sad, or she could be brave and tell her parents. Lily chose to be brave and told her parents what happened. Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lily who loved to explore the jungle. One day, she met a crocodile who was very big and green. Lily was scared at first, but the crocodile was friendly and they became friends.

"I like your shiny scales," said Lily.

"Thank you, I like your pretty dress," replied the crocodile.

As they walked together, the crocodile told Lily about his life in the river. He explained how he used to be small but he had become big and strong over time.

Lily was amazed by the crocodile's story and they continued to explore the jungle together, enjoying each other's company. From that day on, they were the best of friends and went on many adventures together.

Anna liked to sign songs with her hands. She learned sign from her friend Mia, who could not hear. Anna and Mia played together at school and taught each other new signs.

One day, Anna wanted to sign a song for her mom. She looked for her book of songs on the shelf in her room. But she could not find it. She saw that her brother Ben had taken it. He was reading it on his bed.

"Ben, give me my book!" Anna said. "I need it to sign a song for mom."

"No, I want to read it," Ben said. "It has nice pictures and words."

"Please, Ben, it is my book. You are naughty to take it," Anna said. She tried to grab the book from Ben, but he held it tight.

They pulled and pushed the book until it ripped. They both gasped and looked at the torn pages. They felt sad and sorry.

"Mom will be mad at us," Ben said.

"I know. We were both naughty," Anna said. "Let's say sorry to mom and to each other. And let's fix the book with tape."

They hugged and said sorry. Then they went to find mom and told her what happened. Mom was not happy, but she was glad they were honest and kind. She helped them tape the book and hugged them.

"Can you still sign a song for me, Anna?" mom asked.

"Yes, mom. I remember some signs. And Ben can help me," Anna said.

They signed a song together for mom. It was a song about saying sorry and being friends. Mom smiled and clapped. She was proud of them.

Tim and Sam were two squirrels who liked to play in the park. They had a big tree where they stored their nuts for winter. One day, they decided to organize their nuts by size and color. They made piles of big nuts, small nuts, brown nuts, and green nuts.

"Look, Tim, we have so many nuts!" Sam said. "We are very smart and hard-working."

"Yes, we are, Sam. And we are very lucky, too. No one can take our nuts away from us," Tim said.

But they did not see that a naughty crow was watching them from another tree. The crow was hungry and greedy. He wanted to eat their nuts. He waited until Tim and Sam went to look for more nuts. Then he flew down and started to peck at their piles.

"Yum, yum, these nuts are delicious!" the crow said. "I will eat them all and leave nothing for the squirrels."

But Tim and Sam came back soon. They saw the crow eating their nuts. They were very angry and sad.

"Hey, you, stop that!" Tim shouted. "Those are our nuts! We worked hard to find them and organize them!"

"Too bad, squirrels. I am bigger and stronger than you. I can eat whatever I want," the crow said. He laughed and pecked at another nut.

Tim and Sam did not know what to do. They were too small to fight the crow. They needed help. They looked around and saw their friends, the rabbits, the mice, and the birds. They called them and told them what happened.

"Help us, please! The naughty crow is stealing our nuts!" Tim and Sam said.

Their friends were kind and brave. They came to help them. They made a loud noise and scared the crow away. They helped Tim and Sam pick up their nuts and put them back in their tree.

"Thank you, friends. You are very good and helpful," Tim and Sam said.

"You are welcome, squirrels. We are happy to help you. We are all friends in the park," their friends said.

Tim and Sam learned a lesson. They learned that it is good to organize their nuts, but it is also good to share them with their friends. They learned that being greedy and selfish is naughty and wrong. They learned that being kind and generous is good and right. They learned that friends are more important than nuts.

THE VALIANT LITTLE TAILOR

One summer's morning a little tailor was sitting on his table by the

window; he was in good spirits, and sewed with all his might. Then came

a peasant woman down the street crying: 'Good jams, cheap! Good jams,

cheap!' This rang pleasantly in the tailor's ears; he stretched his

delicate head out of the window, and called: 'Come up here, dear woman;

here you will get rid of your goods.' The woman came up the three steps

to the tailor with her heavy basket, and he made her unpack all the pots

for him. He inspected each one, lifted it up, put his nose to it, and

at length said: 'The jam seems to me to be good, so weigh me out four

ounces, dear woman, and if it is a quarter of a pound that is of no

consequence.' The woman who had hoped to find a good sale, gave him

what he desired, but went away quite angry and grumbling. 'Now, this jam

shall be blessed by God,' cried the little tailor, 'and give me health

and strength'; so he brought the bread out of the cupboard, cut himself

a piece right across the loaf and spread the jam over it. 'This won't

taste bitter,' said he, 'but I will just finish the jacket before I

take a bite.' He laid the bread near him, sewed on, and in his joy, made

bigger and bigger stitches. In the meantime the smell of the sweet jam

rose to where the flies were sitting in great numbers, and they were

attracted and descended on it in hosts. 'Hi! who invited you?' said the

little tailor, and drove the unbidden guests away. The flies, however,

who understood no German, would not be turned away, but came back

again in ever-increasing companies. The little tailor at last lost all

patience, and drew a piece of cloth from the hole under his work-table,

and saying: 'Wait, and I will give it to you,' struck it mercilessly on

them. When he drew it away and counted, there lay before him no fewer

than seven, dead and with legs stretched out. 'Are you a fellow of that

sort?' said he, and could not help admiring his own bravery. 'The whole

town shall know of this!' And the little tailor hastened to cut himself

a girdle, stitched it, and embroidered on it in large letters: 'Seven at

one stroke!' 'What, the town!' he continued, 'the whole world shall hear

of it!' and his heart wagged with joy like a lamb's tail. The tailor

put on the girdle, and resolved to go forth into the world, because he

thought his workshop was too small for his valour. Before he went away,

he sought about in the house to see if there was anything which he could

take with him; however, he found nothing but an old cheese, and that

he put in his pocket. In front of the door he observed a bird which

had caught itself in the thicket. It had to go into his pocket with the

cheese. Now he took to the road boldly, and as he was light and nimble,

he felt no fatigue. The road led him up a mountain, and when he had

reached the highest point of it, there sat a powerful giant looking

peacefully about him. The little tailor went bravely up, spoke to him,

and said: 'Good day, comrade, so you are sitting there overlooking the

wide-spread world! I am just on my way thither, and want to try my luck.

Have you any inclination to go with me?' The giant looked contemptuously

at the tailor, and said: 'You ragamuffin! You miserable creature!'

'Oh, indeed?' answered the little tailor, and unbuttoned his coat, and

showed the giant the girdle, 'there may you read what kind of a man I

am!' The giant read: 'Seven at one stroke,' and thought that they had

been men whom the tailor had killed, and began to feel a little respect

for the tiny fellow. Nevertheless, he wished to try him first, and took

a stone in his hand and squeezed it together so that water dropped out

of it. 'Do that likewise,' said the giant, 'if you have strength.' 'Is

that all?' said the tailor, 'that is child's play with us!' and put his

hand into his pocket, brought out the soft cheese, and pressed it until

the liquid ran out of it. 'Faith,' said he, 'that was a little better,

wasn't it?' The giant did not know what to say, and could not believe it

of the little man. Then the giant picked up a stone and threw it so high

that the eye could scarcely follow it. 'Now, little mite of a man, do

that likewise,' 'Well thrown,' said the tailor, 'but after all the stone

came down to earth again; I will throw you one which shall never come

back at all,' and he put his hand into his pocket, took out the bird,

and threw it into the air. The bird, delighted with its liberty,

rose, flew away and did not come back. 'How does that shot please you,

comrade?' asked the tailor. 'You can certainly throw,' said the giant,

'but now we will see if you are able to carry anything properly.' He

took the little tailor to a mighty oak tree which lay there felled on

the ground, and said: 'If you are strong enough, help me to carry the

tree out of the forest.' 'Readily,' answered the little man; 'take you

the trunk on your shoulders, and I will raise up the branches and twigs;

after all, they are the heaviest.' The giant took the trunk on his

shoulder, but the tailor seated himself on a branch, and the giant, who

could not look round, had to carry away the whole tree, and the little

tailor into the bargain: he behind, was quite merry and happy, and

whistled the song: 'Three tailors rode forth from the gate,' as if

carrying the tree were child's play. The giant, after he had dragged the

heavy burden part of the way, could go no further, and cried: 'Hark

you, I shall have to let the tree fall!' The tailor sprang nimbly down,

seized the tree with both arms as if he had been carrying it, and said

to the giant: 'You are such a great fellow, and yet cannot even carry

the tree!'

They went on together, and as they passed a cherry-tree, the giant laid

hold of the top of the tree where the ripest fruit was hanging, bent it

down, gave it into the tailor's hand, and bade him eat. But the little

tailor was much too weak to hold the tree, and when the giant let it go,

it sprang back again, and the tailor was tossed into the air with it.

When he had fallen down again without injury, the giant said: 'What is

this? Have you not strength enough to hold the weak twig?' 'There is no

lack of strength,' answered the little tailor. 'Do you think that could

be anything to a man who has struck down seven at one blow? I leapt over

the tree because the huntsmen are shooting down there in the thicket.

Jump as I did, if you can do it.' The giant made the attempt but he

could not get over the tree, and remained hanging in the branches, so

that in this also the tailor kept the upper hand.

The giant said: 'If you are such a valiant fellow, come with me into our

cavern and spend the night with us.' The little tailor was willing, and

followed him. When they went into the cave, other giants were sitting

there by the fire, and each of them had a roasted sheep in his hand and

was eating it. The little tailor looked round and thought: 'It is much

more spacious here than in my workshop.' The giant showed him a bed, and

said he was to lie down in it and sleep. The bed, however, was too

big for the little tailor; he did not lie down in it, but crept into

a corner. When it was midnight, and the giant thought that the little

tailor was lying in a sound sleep, he got up, took a great iron bar,

cut through the bed with one blow, and thought he had finished off the

grasshopper for good. With the earliest dawn the giants went into the

forest, and had quite forgotten the little tailor, when all at once he

walked up to them quite merrily and boldly. The giants were terrified,

they were afraid that he would strike them all dead, and ran away in a

great hurry.

The little tailor went onwards, always following his own pointed nose.

After he had walked for a long time, he came to the courtyard of a royal

palace, and as he felt weary, he lay down on the grass and fell asleep.

Whilst he lay there, the people came and inspected him on all sides, and

read on his girdle: 'Seven at one stroke.' 'Ah!' said they, 'what does

the great warrior want here in the midst of peace? He must be a mighty

lord.' They went and announced him to the king, and gave it as their

opinion that if war should break out, this would be a weighty and useful

man who ought on no account to be allowed to depart. The counsel pleased

the king, and he sent one of his courtiers to the little tailor to offer

him military service when he awoke. The ambassador remained standing by

the sleeper, waited until he stretched his limbs and opened his eyes,

and then conveyed to him this proposal. 'For this very reason have

I come here,' the tailor replied, 'I am ready to enter the king's

service.' He was therefore honourably received, and a special dwelling

was assigned him.

The soldiers, however, were set against the little tailor, and wished

him a thousand miles away. 'What is to be the end of this?' they said

among themselves. 'If we quarrel with him, and he strikes about him,

seven of us will fall at every blow; not one of us can stand against

him.' They came therefore to a decision, betook themselves in a body to

the king, and begged for their dismissal. 'We are not prepared,' said

they, 'to stay with a man who kills seven at one stroke.' The king was

sorry that for the sake of one he should lose all his faithful servants,

wished that he had never set eyes on the tailor, and would willingly

have been rid of him again. But he did not venture to give him his

dismissal, for he dreaded lest he should strike him and all his people

dead, and place himself on the royal throne. He thought about it for a

long time, and at last found good counsel. He sent to the little tailor

and caused him to be informed that as he was a great warrior, he had one

request to make to him. In a forest of his country lived two giants,

who caused great mischief with their robbing, murdering, ravaging,

and burning, and no one could approach them without putting himself in

danger of death. If the tailor conquered and killed these two giants, he

would give him his only daughter to wife, and half of his kingdom as a

dowry, likewise one hundred horsemen should go with him to assist him.

'That would indeed be a fine thing for a man like me!' thought the

little tailor. 'One is not offered a beautiful princess and half a

kingdom every day of one's life!' 'Oh, yes,' he replied, 'I will soon

subdue the giants, and do not require the help of the hundred horsemen

to do it; he who can hit seven with one blow has no need to be afraid of

two.'

The little tailor went forth, and the hundred horsemen followed him.

When he came to the outskirts of the forest, he said to his followers:

'Just stay waiting here, I alone will soon finish off the giants.' Then

he bounded into the forest and looked about right and left. After a

while he perceived both giants. They lay sleeping under a tree, and

snored so that the branches waved up and down. The little tailor, not

idle, gathered two pocketsful of stones, and with these climbed up the

tree. When he was halfway up, he slipped down by a branch, until he sat

just above the sleepers, and then let one stone after another fall on

the breast of one of the giants. For a long time the giant felt nothing,

but at last he awoke, pushed his comrade, and said: 'Why are you

knocking me?' 'You must be dreaming,' said the other, 'I am not knocking

you.' They laid themselves down to sleep again, and then the tailor

threw a stone down on the second. 'What is the meaning of this?' cried

the other 'Why are you pelting me?' 'I am not pelting you,' answered

the first, growling. They disputed about it for a time, but as they were

weary they let the matter rest, and their eyes closed once more. The

little tailor began his game again, picked out the biggest stone, and

threw it with all his might on the breast of the first giant. 'That

is too bad!' cried he, and sprang up like a madman, and pushed his

companion against the tree until it shook. The other paid him back in

the same coin, and they got into such a rage that they tore up trees and

belaboured each other so long, that at last they both fell down dead on

the ground at the same time. Then the little tailor leapt down. 'It is

a lucky thing,' said he, 'that they did not tear up the tree on which

I was sitting, or I should have had to sprint on to another like a

squirrel; but we tailors are nimble.' He drew out his sword and gave

each of them a couple of thrusts in the breast, and then went out to the

horsemen and said: 'The work is done; I have finished both of them

off, but it was hard work! They tore up trees in their sore need, and

defended themselves with them, but all that is to no purpose when a man

like myself comes, who can kill seven at one blow.' 'But are you not

wounded?' asked the horsemen. 'You need not concern yourself about

that,' answered the tailor, 'they have not bent one hair of mine.' The

horsemen would not believe him, and rode into the forest; there they

found the giants swimming in their blood, and all round about lay the

torn-up trees.

The little tailor demanded of the king the promised reward; he, however,

repented of his promise, and again bethought himself how he could get

rid of the hero. 'Before you receive my daughter, and the half of my

kingdom,' said he to him, 'you must perform one more heroic deed. In

the forest roams a unicorn which does great harm, and you must catch

it first.' 'I fear one unicorn still less than two giants. Seven at one

blow, is my kind of affair.' He took a rope and an axe with him, went

forth into the forest, and again bade those who were sent with him to

wait outside. He had not long to seek. The unicorn soon came towards

him, and rushed directly on the tailor, as if it would gore him with its

horn without more ado. 'Softly, softly; it can't be done as quickly as

that,' said he, and stood still and waited until the animal was quite

close, and then sprang nimbly behind the tree. The unicorn ran against

the tree with all its strength, and stuck its horn so fast in the trunk

that it had not the strength enough to draw it out again, and thus it

was caught. 'Now, I have got the bird,' said the tailor, and came out

from behind the tree and put the rope round its neck, and then with his

axe he hewed the horn out of the tree, and when all was ready he led the

beast away and took it to the king.

The king still would not give him the promised reward, and made a third

demand. Before the wedding the tailor was to catch him a wild boar that

made great havoc in the forest, and the huntsmen should give him their

help. 'Willingly,' said the tailor, 'that is child's play!' He did not

take the huntsmen with him into the forest, and they were well pleased

that he did not, for the wild boar had several times received them in

such a manner that they had no inclination to lie in wait for him. When

the boar perceived the tailor, it ran on him with foaming mouth and

whetted tusks, and was about to throw him to the ground, but the hero

fled and sprang into a chapel which was near and up to the window at

once, and in one bound out again. The boar ran after him, but the tailor

ran round outside and shut the door behind it, and then the raging

beast, which was much too heavy and awkward to leap out of the window,

was caught. The little tailor called the huntsmen thither that they

might see the prisoner with their own eyes. The hero, however, went to

the king, who was now, whether he liked it or not, obliged to keep his

promise, and gave his daughter and the half of his kingdom. Had he known

that it was no warlike hero, but a little tailor who was standing before

him, it would have gone to his heart still more than it did. The wedding

was held with great magnificence and small joy, and out of a tailor a

king was made.

After some time the young queen heard her husband say in his dreams at

night: 'Boy, make me the doublet, and patch the pantaloons, or else I

will rap the yard-measure over your ears.' Then she discovered in what

state of life the young lord had been born, and next morning complained

of her wrongs to her father, and begged him to help her to get rid of

her husband, who was nothing else but a tailor. The king comforted her

and said: 'Leave your bedroom door open this night, and my servants

shall stand outside, and when he has fallen asleep shall go in, bind

him, and take him on board a ship which shall carry him into the wide

world.' The woman was satisfied with this; but the king's armour-bearer,

who had heard all, was friendly with the young lord, and informed him of

the whole plot. 'I'll put a screw into that business,' said the little

tailor. At night he went to bed with his wife at the usual time, and

when she thought that he had fallen asleep, she got up, opened the door,

and then lay down again. The little tailor, who was only pretending to

be asleep, began to cry out in a clear voice: 'Boy, make me the doublet

and patch me the pantaloons, or I will rap the yard-measure over your

ears. I smote seven at one blow. I killed two giants, I brought away one

unicorn, and caught a wild boar, and am I to fear those who are standing

outside the room.' When these men heard the tailor speaking thus, they

were overcome by a great dread, and ran as if the wild huntsman were

behind them, and none of them would venture anything further against

him. So the little tailor was and remained a king to the end of his

life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick vegetables from her garden. One day, she found a strange vegetable that she had never seen before. She called her mommy to come and examine it with her.

"Mommy, look at this vegetable! It's so funny-looking," said Lily.

Her mommy came over and examined the vegetable closely. "Hmm, I'm not sure what kind of vegetable this is," said her mommy.

Later that night, Lily felt very sleepy and went to bed early. But she couldn't sleep because she kept thinking about the strange vegetable. She got out of bed and went to the kitchen to examine it again.

Suddenly, the vegetable started moving and growing bigger and bigger! It turned into a monster and scared Lily so much that she ran back to her bedroom and hid under the covers.

From that day on, Lily never went near her garden again. She learned that some vegetables can be very dangerous and scary.

Once upon a time there was a fish who wanted to climb a mountain. He was a brave little fish, but the mountain was very high and it look heavy to climb. He asked his friend the bird to help him, "Please help me to climb, my friend?"

The bird said, "It is too heavy for you. I can help you find a better way, let's think together." The bird and the little fish thought and thought until they finally came with a plan.

The fish and the bird decided to go to the sea together. When they got there, the fish swam up and slowly, slowly made his way up the mountain by swimming and jumping. The bird flew ahead to the top and shouted and waved.

The little fish made it! He was so proud and grateful for his friend's help and shouted, "You are the best, my friend!"

The fish enjoyed the beautiful view from the top and after a while, started to make his way down again, back to the sea.

So, with the help of a friend and a lot of courage, the fish was able to climb the heavy mountain.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Nora and she was three years old. Nora loved to explore the world around her.

On one of her adventures, Nora found a big purple box with a strange label that said 'measure lumber'. She was very curious, so she opened the box. Inside were all kinds of purple measuring tools. There were rulers and measuring tapes.

Nora took out a ruler and held it up. It was longer than she was tall! She measured a piece of lumber with it, to see how long it was.

Nora was so excited about her discoveries. She spent the day measuring all sorts of different kinds of lumber with her purple ruler. By the end of the day, she was very happy and very tired.

Nora had a lot of fun measuring lumber with her purple ruler. And she learned that measuring can be a lot of fun, too!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named George. He was excited to have a special day with his family.

They all went to the museum to see the skeletons. George was so excited when he saw all the bones!

George rubbed his hands on the bones. They felt so smooth and shiny. He rubbed the rib bones, the tail bone and the head bone.

He was having so much fun! He couldn't believe the skeleton felt so nice to touch. His family laughed at George and they were happy to see him so excited.

The day ended, and they all got ready to go home. George hugged the skeleton before they left and waved goodbye. He was so happy to have gotten to rub the skeleton.

Ben and his dad walked through the swamp. Everywhere there were logs lying around. Dad was looking for a perfect log to take home.

"Where's the perfect log?", Dad asked Ben.

Ben looked around. Everywhere was wet and somebody had put lots of logs there.

Dad became impatient. "Maybe if we struggle to find the log it will help," Dad said.

Ben started feeling around the logs and pushing them to see which was the perfect log for Dad. At last, Ben found the perfect log and gave it to Dad.

Dad was so happy. He thanked Ben for his help. Together they took the log home.

Once upon a time there was an adorable little boy named Bob. Bob had a very special eraser because it was so cuddly and soft. Every day, Bob would take his eraser with him everywhere he went.

One day, Bob was feeling sad and lonely. He didn't know why he felt like this, but it made him very sad. He was so sad that he hugged his eraser very tight and started to cry.

All of a sudden, a kind voice said, "It's alright, everything will be ok". Bob looked up and he saw a big, friendly smile coming from someone he had never seen before. It was his mom! Bob ran to her and she hugged him tight and rubbed his back. This made Bob feel very safe and he was comforted.

Bob was so happy that his mom was there with him. He knew that when she was around, everything would be ok. They hugged and cuddled for a long time and soon Bob stopped feeling sad. His eraser cuddled up by his side, and Bob knew it was his little friend taking care of him.

Once upon a time there was a clown called Jack. He was an incredible clown and loved to make children laugh. He went to many places to do his shows.

On one of his shows, he met a little girl called Dolly. She was really excited to see him and asked if he can provide her some fun. Jack agreed and proceeded to put on an amazing show for her.

When it was finally the end of the show, Dolly thanked him for the incredible performance. Jack was feeling really proud of himself and said to Dolly, "I'm glad you liked my show! Was it fun?"

Dolly smiled widely and excitedly replied, "Yes! It was amazing!" But before she could say anything else, a thunder lit up the sky.

The sky suddenly turned dark and a heavy rain started pouring. Dolly's parents called for her and she had to leave. Unfortunately, Jack never got to say goodbye and Dolly never found out about his incredible show again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice-cream more than anything in the world. Every day, she asked her mom for ice-cream, but her mom said no because it was too close to dinner time.

One day, Lily's mom took her to the park to play. Lily saw an ice-cream truck and got very nervous. She wanted ice-cream, but she knew her mom would say no.

Lily's mom saw how nervous she was and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her about the ice-cream truck and how much she wanted some. Her mom said they could get some, but only if they ate their dinner first. This prevented Lily from being sad and made her very happy. She enjoyed her ice-cream with a big smile on her face.

Anna likes to help her mom in the kitchen. She puts on a pink apron and a big smile. She wants to make a cake for dad's birthday. Mom gives her a bowl and a spoon. She says, "Mix the flour, the sugar, and the eggs."

Anna tries to mix, but she is clumsy. She spills some flour on the floor. She drops some sugar on the table. She breaks an egg on her apron. She says, "Oops! Sorry, mom!"

Mom laughs and hugs her. She says, "It's okay, Anna. You are learning. Let me help you." She wipes the mess and adds some butter and milk. She pours the batter into a pan and puts it in the oven. She says, "Now we wait for the cake to bake."

Anna waits and smells the cake. It smells yummy. She says, "Can I eat some, mom?" Mom says, "Not yet, Anna. We have to wait for dad to come home. Then we can surprise him with the cake and sing happy birthday."

Anna nods and smiles. She loves her mom and dad. She loves to help in the kitchen. She loves to eat cake. She thinks, "Maybe next time I will be less clumsy."

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to play. She wanted to join all the big kids in their favorite game. The game was to shoot arrows at a target and try to hit it.

The little girl wanted to join in, but she didn't have an arrow. Everyone else was very competitive and she was scared they would not let her play.

The little girl was sad until she saw a stick in the grass and picked it up. She brought it to the target and set it up.

The little girl took a deep breath and then reached into the grass to pick up three stones. She closed her eyes and threw the stones one by one.

The stones flew through the air and struck the stick. The little girl was so surprised when she opened her eyes, her arrow had hit the target!

The big kids cheered and the little girl was so happy she could take part in the game. From then on, the little girl learned to shoot arrows and was the most competitive of all.

Timmy was very excited. His mum and dad had bought him a special bell for his bedroom. It was a big brass bell with a long, shiny handle. Whenever Timmy wanted to call his mum or dad, he just had to ring the bell.

One day, his mum said, "It's time for your exam!" Timmy's eyes grew wide. He was a bit scared. He wasn't sure what an exam was.

"But why?" he asked.

His mum smiled. "It's just for fun," she said. "It's a silly game that we can play."

Timmy looked at his mum and dad with big, hopeful eyes.

"It's okay," his dad said. "You can ring the bell if you get stuck or need help. When you're finished, we'll all ring the bell together. Isn't that a good idea?"

Timmy nodded. He took a deep breath and started the exam. He was worried at first, but soon he was having fun. Whenever he got stuck, he'd ring the bell and get help from mum or dad.

When he finished the exam, he and his parents rang the bell together. It was the best exam that Timmy had ever taken!

One day Harper was feeling very playful. She was wearing a big pink dress and wanted to have some fun. She asked her mom if they could bake a cake together.

"Yes we can Harper!" her mom said. They gathered all the ingredients for the cake and began to mix them together. When the cake batter was finished, Harper scooped into bowls and added a few drops of ink to make it colorful.

Harper's mom put the bowls of cake into the oven. Harper was very excited to taste the delicious cake. After one hour of baking, Harper's mom took the cake out of the oven. The cake looked amazing and smelled delicious.

Harper and her mom had a fun time eating the cake with their hands. Harper was so excited that her cake turned out so well. The cake was very delicious and they laughed while they ate it. They had lots of fun baking together.

Jen and Ben had a dog named Spot. Spot was unique. He had black and white spots all over his fur. He liked to run and play and chase balls. Jen and Ben loved Spot very much.

One day, Jen and Ben wanted to take Spot to the park. They had a new leash for him. It was red and shiny and had a bell on it. Jen and Ben thought it was very pretty. They hoped Spot would like it too.

They put the leash on Spot and went outside. Spot was excited. He saw a lot of things to sniff and explore. He pulled on the leash and made the bell ring. Jen and Ben laughed and followed him.

But when they got to the park, they saw a problem. There was a big sign that said: "No dogs allowed". Jen and Ben were sad. They wanted to play with Spot in the park. They looked around and saw a lot of people and children and bikes and swings. They did not see any other dogs.

They wondered what to do. They did not want to break the rule. They did not want to make Spot unhappy. They did not want to go back home. They wished they could find a place where Spot could fit in.

Then they saw it. Across the street, there was a pet store. It had a big window with a lot of animals inside. There were cats and birds and fish and hamsters and rabbits. And there were also dogs. They were all different sizes and colors and shapes. They looked happy and friendly.

Jen and Ben had an idea. They asked their mom if they could go to the pet store. Their mom said yes. They crossed the street and went inside. They took Spot with them. They showed him the other animals. They let him sniff and greet and play with the other dogs. They saw that Spot was unique, but he was not alone. He fit in with the other dogs. He made new friends.

Jen and Ben were happy. They found a place where Spot could fit in. They also liked the other animals. They asked their mom if they could come back again. Their mom said yes. They thanked the pet store owner and left. They still had the red and shiny leash with the bell on it. They still thought it was very pretty. They still hoped Spot would like it too. They decided to keep it for another day. A day when they could find a park where dogs were allowed. A park where Spot could run and play and chase balls. A park where Spot could be unique and happy.

Once upon a time, in a small house, lived an old man with a cane. He had a big cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was not a good cat. He did terrible things. He broke cups and knocked over plants.

One day, Fluffy and a little bird had a quarrel. "You are a bad cat!" said the little bird. "No, I am not!" said Fluffy. They were very loud.

The old man heard the quarrel and came outside. He saw the mess Fluffy made. "Fluffy, you must be good," said the old man. Fluffy felt sad and said, "I will be good." From that day on, Fluffy was a good cat and never had a quarrel again.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who planted some seeds in the soil, hoping for a good crop. But the sun was too hot and the soil was too dry, so the farmer's crop was not very good.

The farmer was sad and didn't know what to do, so he made a fake seed. He hoped that it would help his crop to grow, but it didn't work. In the end all the seeds he planted turned out to be fake and the crop was ruined.

The farmer was very sad and knew that he had made a mistake by planting fake seeds. He wished he had planted real ones in the soil, but it was too late now.

The farmer had to accept that there were no crops and he hoped he would never make the same mistake again.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She went to the store with her mom. Sarah's mom said, "Sarah, you can choose something for yourself." Sarah saw a pin that caught her eye. It had a spicy red color and looked magical.

Sarah said to her mom, "Can I please have the spicy pin?" Her mom said, "Yes, of course you can have the pin."

Sarah happily took the pin and put it in her pocket. She liked the pin because it was so spicy and made her feel special. She wanted to show her friends the pin, so she put it on her shirt.

Sarah loved her spicy pin and looked happy every time she saw it. She was proud that she chose something special all by herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up and pretend to be different things. One day, she found a mask in her toy box. It was a big, scary monster mask. Lily put it on and looked in the mirror. She thought she looked very cool.

Lily's mom came in the room and saw her wearing the mask. "Lily, take off that mask right now! It's too scary!" she said. Lily didn't want to take it off. She thought it was fun to pretend to be a monster.

But then Lily's little brother came into the room. He saw Lily wearing the mask and started crying. Lily realized that her brother was scared of the mask. She took it off and said, "I'm sorry. I didn't think it would scare you. I'll be more alert next time." From then on, Lily was more careful about what masks she wore around her brother.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah who loved plants. She planted lots of them in the garden and took time to care for them every day.

One night, a dark storm came and all the plants got wet from the rain. When morning came, Sarah looked in the garden and saw that a dark plant was missing. She gasped and asked her mom,
"Mommy, why is one of my plants gone?"
Her mom said sadly,
"Oh sweetie, sometimes things get lost during a storm. You will have to learn to accept that you lost it."

Sarah was very sad. She realised that if she had taken better care of her plants, maybe some of her plants would not have been lost.

The moral of the story is: When it comes to taking care of special things, it is important to protect and watch over them, so they don't get lost in bad storms.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the farm. They see many animals in the farm. They see cows, pigs, sheep and chickens.

One day, they want to feed the chickens. They ask the farmer for some corn. The farmer gives them a bucket of corn. He says, "Be careful with the chickens. They are healthy and strong. They can peck you if you are not nice to them."

Lily and Ben take the bucket of corn and go to the chicken coop. They see many chickens. Some are white, some are brown, some are black. They are noisy and busy. They cluck and flap their wings.

Lily and Ben wave to the chickens. They say, "Hello, chickens! We have some corn for you. Do you want some?" They throw some corn on the ground. The chickens run to the corn. They peck and scratch and eat. They are happy and full.

Lily and Ben smile and watch the chickens. They say, "You are good chickens. You give us eggs and meat. You are healthy and strong. We like you." They wave to the chickens again. They say, "Bye, chickens! See you next time!" They take the bucket and go back to the farmer. They thank him for the corn. They say, "We had fun with the chickens. They are nice to us." The farmer smiles and says, "You are welcome. You are good kids. You are nice to the chickens."

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who lived in an enormous forest. One day, the bear felt sick and didn't feel well. He knew he needed medicine, but he didn't know where to find it. The bear asked his friends, but they didn't know where to find medicine either.

The bear searched and searched, but he couldn't find any medicine. He felt sicker and sicker. Eventually, the bear became so sick that he couldn't move. Sadly, the bear passed away because he didn't get the medicine he needed. The forest became very quiet without the bear's roar.

John and Mommy were at the restaurant. John looked around and saw that there were so many big, colourful things to pick from. He was so excited. He pointed to a huge bowl of ice cream.

"I want that Mommy!" said John.

Mommy smiled and said, "Ok, we can order that John!"

John clapped his hands together. He couldn't wait! Mommy ordered a huge bowl of ice cream for John and it arrived shortly.

John dug in with a giant spoon. He smiled a huge smile as he ate his delicious, creamy treat. His face was covered in a white, sticky mess but he didn't care.

Mommy laughed and said, "John, you are a mess!"

John giggled as he ate his huge bowl of ice cream.

Once upon a time there was a heavy raft. It belonged to a family who all wanted to go on a fun, riverside journey.

The father lifted the heavy raft and put it in the river. Then he, his wife and the two children, clambered inside. They were all so excited for the fun ahead.

The family started their journey, but suddenly it started raining heavily. The rain was so strong, it made the raft sway from side to side. The father told them all to get off, so they jumped into the water with their life jackets on.

But after a while they all had to surrender. The heavy raft was starting to drift away and they could not get back on it. The waves were too high and the family were too exhausted.

So they waved goodbye as the heavy raft slowly drifted off, and they all hoped to see it again soon. Then they decided to walk home together, clingin to their life jackets.

And they all lived happily ever after. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a round, soft rug. He loved to play on it. One day he wanted to do something different. He decided to number the rug. So, the boy got his markers and carefully he started to number each side of the rug. The boy was slow and precise. He must make sure that the numbers were neat and even. Finally, the number rug was complete and the boy was very happy. Every day he wakes up, jumps onto the rug and counts the numbers. It was so much fun to sit and relax on his special number rug!

Once there was a boy and he was thirsty so he got a cup. He wanted to shut the cup though and it was very hard, so he asked his mom for help. His mom said it would be easy and showed him how to shut it. He tried it again and was able to shut the cup all by himself. He was very happy and smiled.

The boy filled up the cup with some juice and then went to play with his toys. He was so thirsty he quickly drank all the juice and finished his cup. After that, he shut it again and put the cup away.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jenny who had an uncle. Every day, Uncle would come over to play with Jenny.

One day, Uncle showed Jenny a fake smile. Jenny looked very confused.

"What are you using that for?" asked Jenny.

"I'm using it to make people laugh," said Uncle.

Jenny laughed and said, "That's silly!"

Uncle smiled and said, "You're right! That's why I like showing it to people."

From that day on, whenever Uncle visited, Jenny and Uncle would share a fake smile and giggle together. They both liked the way it made them feel.

Once there was a girl named Jane. Jane was three years old and she wanted to go on an adventure. She wanted to go to a magical place where everything was beautiful.

So one day, Jane decided to go. She put some makeup on and smiled as she looked in the mirror. She was ready to go.

Jane stepped outside and it was very rough. The wind was blowing and the clouds were everywhere. It seemed like an impossible journey, but Jane was determined.

She closed her eyes, took a deep breath and prayed. She asked for courage and strength. She prayed for help and protection.

Suddenly the sky cleared and Jane saw a rainbow in the sky. She knew that she had been heard. She smiled and knew that her adventure was about to begin.

Once upon a time there was a farmer who owned a bull. The bull was very special, but the farmer was a bit jealous. So, one day, the farmer decided to take the bull to wander around the farm.

The bull was very happy. He wandered around and ate some juicy grass. He was so content that he even stopped to have a nap in the sun. But then, he heard a noise. It was loud and made him jump.

It was the farmer. He was mad and was shouting. The farmer was jealous that the bull was so enjoying himself. He yelled at the bull to come back. The bull ran back to the farmer and the farmer put him on his farm.

But, the bull knew he was meant to wander and would often find ways to wander around the farm during the day. He was always happy when he did this and so the farmer was always jealous.

The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, a cat and a dog. They lived in a really beautiful neighbourhood with lots of trees and grass for them to play in. One day, the two friends went for a walk together. The cat and the dog were very excited because they had found a long cable. They decided to see how much it weighed.

The dog went first and tried to lift the cable. It was too heavy! The dog said, "This cable must be really heavy." The cat was very curious and wanted to try too, so it put its paws on the cable and tried to push it up. But the cable was too heavy for the cat too!

The cat said, "It must be really heavy because it doesn't feel regular." The two friends thought for a moment and then decided that the best thing to do was to ask a grown-up for help. So they went in search of one. In the end, a grown-up helped them find out that the cable weighed 164 pounds!

Sam and Ben were brothers who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide with a ladder and a tunnel. Sam wanted to go first, but Ben said he was too weak to climb the ladder.

"I'm not weak, you're weak!" Sam said. He ran to the ladder and started to climb. Ben followed him, but he was slower.

When Sam reached the top of the slide, he saw something shiny in the tunnel. He crawled inside and found a metal spike sticking out of the wall. He touched it and felt a sharp pain in his hand. He cried out and tried to pull his hand away, but the spike was stuck.

"Help! Help!" Sam shouted. Ben heard him and climbed into the tunnel. He saw Sam's hand bleeding and the spike holding it. He was scared, but he wanted to help his brother.

"Sam, don't move!" Ben said. He grabbed Sam's hand and gave it a hard shake. The spike came loose and Sam's hand was free. Sam hugged Ben and thanked him.

"Let's go home, Sam," Ben said. "We need to put a bandage on your hand."

"OK, Ben," Sam said. "You're not weak, you're brave."

They slid down the slide and ran to their mom, who was waiting for them. She saw their faces and knew something had happened.

"What's wrong, boys?" she asked.

"We'll tell you later, Mom," Ben said. "We just want to go home."

They held each other's hands and walked away from the park. They never played on that slide again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her dolls and stuffed animals. One day, she lost her favorite teddy bear. She searched and searched but couldn't find him anywhere. She felt miserable without him.

Lily's mom saw her frown and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her about her lost teddy bear. Her mom said, "Let's search for him together!" They looked in every room and under every bed, but still couldn't find him.

Just when they were about to give up, Lily's little brother came running in with the teddy bear in his hands. "I found him!" he exclaimed. Lily was so happy and hugged her brother tightly. "Thank you for helping me search," she said with a big smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Katie. She was three years old and very curious. One day, Katie asked her mom, "What can I do?" Her mom smiled and said, "You can help me clean up the junk in the backyard."

So, Katie put on her smock and went outside. She saw lots of junk that her mom wanted her to clean up. She was not sure how to start, but she was excited to try.

Then she saw an old bucket. She grabbed it and started to fill it with the junk. She worked hard and soon the bucket was full. She was very proud; she had completed her job!

She brought the bucket inside and her mom said, "Good job, Katie! Everything fits perfectly in here!" Katie smiled and knew that she had done a great job. She was so pleased with herself.

Molly and her family were sitting in the living room. Her mom and dad were on the couch and Molly was sitting on the floor. They were looking around the room, wondering what to do.

Then, Molly had an idea. She said, "Let's watch TV!" Everyone thought it was a good idea and so they decided to do it.

Molly's family looked around the room until they saw an old TV in the corner. It hadn't been used in a long time, but Molly's mom decided to plug it in and turn it on.

The TV made noises and lights came on. Molly was so excited and ran to the couch with her mom and dad. They all watched the show together and had a lot of fun.

At the end of the night, everyone said they had a great time. They thanked Molly for deciding to watch the old TV.

Sam was a curious boy who liked to examine everything he saw. One day, he found a big onion in the kitchen. He wondered what it was and how it smelled. He picked up the onion and peeled off the brown skin. He saw many white layers inside.

He wanted to know more, so he brought the onion to his nose and sniffed it. It smelled very strong and made his eyes water. He sneezed and rubbed his eyes. He felt a burning pain in his eyes and nose. He dropped the onion and cried.

His mom heard him and ran to the kitchen. She saw him holding his face and the onion on the floor. She knew what happened and felt sorry for him. She hugged him and took him to the sink. She washed his eyes and nose with water. She told him the onion was a food that made people cry. She said he should not examine it with his nose. She gave him a cookie and a kiss.

Sam learned his lesson and never examined an onion again. He still liked to be curious, but he was more careful. He asked his mom before he touched anything new. He did not want to cry or hurt himself again. He was a smart boy.

Once upon a time there was a big blackboard in a classroom. It was so big that it almost reached the ceiling! The teacher had been writing on the blackboard all morning when something amazing happened. The blackboard started to talk! The teacher was very surprised and told the students to mind the blackboard.

The students were very excited and listened carefully. The blackboard said, "I am here to teach you something very special. I will tell you all a story that will help you to understand things better". The students were all eager to learn what the blackboard had to say.

The blackboard started to tell a story about a small bird that had a very big heart. The bird wanted to help all the other birds in the forest and make them happy. The blackboard said, "Remember the bird and the big heart. Always put your own big heart first and help others".

At the end of the story, the teacher smiled and thanked the blackboard for the lesson. The students all said that they had learned something very important and thanked the blackboard too. The blackboard waved goodbye and disappeared.

From that day on, the students always remembered to mind their own big hearts and to help others. It was a lesson that they would never forget!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in nature. One day, while she was playing, she saw a butterfly with a broken wing.

Lily felt sad and wanted to help the butterfly. She went to her mom and said, "Mommy, can we help the butterfly with the broken wing?"

Her mom said, "Of course, we can. Let's cut some flowers and put them in a jar. Then we can put the butterfly in the jar with the flowers."

Lily was so happy and felt compassionate towards the butterfly. They put the jar outside in the sun, and soon the butterfly was able to fly away. Lily was so proud that she was able to help the butterfly and make it feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. One day, Sarah was with her mommy by the beach when she saw an orange engine. Sarah was so excited, she jumped and waved her hands.

Mommy said, "That looks amazing! Where did it come from?"
Sarah waved again and shouted, "Over there!"

Mommy smiled, "Let's go for a ride!"

So, Sarah and Mommy hopped onto the orange engine and the engine began to make a humming noise. Sarah was so excited, she couldn't help but wave her hand in the air.

Finally, they arrived at their destination. Sarah said, "Mommy! I had so much fun! Can we go on the orange engine again?"

Mommy nodded and said, "Maybe tomorrow, Sarah. It's time for bed now."

Sarah waved bye to the orange engine and made her way home with Mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a family of birds. They lived in a tree and had a view of the big, blue sky.

One day, the mama bird said to her four babies, â€œListen carefully! I want you to attach yourselves to the law!â€

The four little birds looked at each other with ignorant eyes, not understanding what she meant.

Mama bird went on, â€œThe law is something that everyone must obey. When you attach yourselves to it, no one will be able to hurt you.â€

The four little birds nodded in unison and chirped, â€œYes, Mama Bird!â€

Mama Bird smiled and said, â€œGood! Now you know the law and you can always keep it near your heart.â€
