Once upon a time, there was a wise owl who lived in a tree. Every Tuesday, the owl would fly to the river to catch fish for dinner. But one day, it started to rain and the owl got wet. So, the owl flew back to its tree to dry itself off.

The owl flapped its wings and shook its feathers to get dry. After a while, the sun came out and the owl felt warm again. It decided to wait until next Tuesday to catch fish. From then on, the owl always checked the weather before going out to catch fish.

"Look, mommy!" said Jerry as he gazed at the muffin in the bakery window. The muffin was a work of art - it was a swirl of different colors, and had a chocolate chip to top it off. Jerry was in awe.

"It's beautiful, isn't it?" said Mom. "Would you like to have one?"

Jerry nodded eagerly, and Mom bought him the muffin.

As he took his first bite, Jerry savored the sweet taste of the muffin. As he continued to gaze at it, he had an idea.

"Mommy," he said excitedly, "can we make creative muffins like this one at home?"

Mom smiled. "Yes, of course we can," she said. "We can make any kind of muffins you want!"

Jerry grinned, pleased that Mom was just as excited about making muffins as he was. He couldn't wait to get home and start making his imaginative creations.

THE WHITE SNAKE

A long time ago there lived a king who was famed for his wisdom through

all the land. Nothing was hidden from him, and it seemed as if news of

the most secret things was brought to him through the air. But he had a

strange custom; every day after dinner, when the table was cleared,

and no one else was present, a trusty servant had to bring him one more

dish. It was covered, however, and even the servant did not know what

was in it, neither did anyone know, for the king never took off the

cover to eat of it until he was quite alone.

This had gone on for a long time, when one day the servant, who took

away the dish, was overcome with such curiosity that he could not help

carrying the dish into his room. When he had carefully locked the door,

he lifted up the cover, and saw a white snake lying on the dish. But

when he saw it he could not deny himself the pleasure of tasting it,

so he cut of a little bit and put it into his mouth. No sooner had it

touched his tongue than he heard a strange whispering of little voices

outside his window. He went and listened, and then noticed that it was

the sparrows who were chattering together, and telling one another of

all kinds of things which they had seen in the fields and woods. Eating

the snake had given him power of understanding the language of animals.

Now it so happened that on this very day the queen lost her most

beautiful ring, and suspicion of having stolen it fell upon this trusty

servant, who was allowed to go everywhere. The king ordered the man to

be brought before him, and threatened with angry words that unless he

could before the morrow point out the thief, he himself should be looked

upon as guilty and executed. In vain he declared his innocence; he was

dismissed with no better answer.

In his trouble and fear he went down into the courtyard and took thought

how to help himself out of his trouble. Now some ducks were sitting

together quietly by a brook and taking their rest; and, whilst they

were making their feathers smooth with their bills, they were having a

confidential conversation together. The servant stood by and listened.

They were telling one another of all the places where they had been

waddling about all the morning, and what good food they had found; and

one said in a pitiful tone: 'Something lies heavy on my stomach; as

I was eating in haste I swallowed a ring which lay under the queen's

window.' The servant at once seized her by the neck, carried her to the

kitchen, and said to the cook: 'Here is a fine duck; pray, kill her.'

'Yes,' said the cook, and weighed her in his hand; 'she has spared

no trouble to fatten herself, and has been waiting to be roasted long

enough.' So he cut off her head, and as she was being dressed for the

spit, the queen's ring was found inside her.

The servant could now easily prove his innocence; and the king, to make

amends for the wrong, allowed him to ask a favour, and promised him

the best place in the court that he could wish for. The servant refused

everything, and only asked for a horse and some money for travelling, as

he had a mind to see the world and go about a little. When his request

was granted he set out on his way, and one day came to a pond, where he

saw three fishes caught in the reeds and gasping for water. Now, though

it is said that fishes are dumb, he heard them lamenting that they must

perish so miserably, and, as he had a kind heart, he got off his

horse and put the three prisoners back into the water. They leapt with

delight, put out their heads, and cried to him: 'We will remember you

and repay you for saving us!'

He rode on, and after a while it seemed to him that he heard a voice in

the sand at his feet. He listened, and heard an ant-king complain: 'Why

cannot folks, with their clumsy beasts, keep off our bodies? That stupid

horse, with his heavy hoofs, has been treading down my people without

mercy!' So he turned on to a side path and the ant-king cried out to

him: 'We will remember you--one good turn deserves another!'

The path led him into a wood, and there he saw two old ravens standing

by their nest, and throwing out their young ones. 'Out with you, you

idle, good-for-nothing creatures!' cried they; 'we cannot find food for

you any longer; you are big enough, and can provide for yourselves.'

But the poor young ravens lay upon the ground, flapping their wings, and

crying: 'Oh, what helpless chicks we are! We must shift for ourselves,

and yet we cannot fly! What can we do, but lie here and starve?' So the

good young fellow alighted and killed his horse with his sword, and gave

it to them for food. Then they came hopping up to it, satisfied their

hunger, and cried: 'We will remember you--one good turn deserves

another!'

And now he had to use his own legs, and when he had walked a long

way, he came to a large city. There was a great noise and crowd in

the streets, and a man rode up on horseback, crying aloud: 'The king's

daughter wants a husband; but whoever seeks her hand must perform a hard

task, and if he does not succeed he will forfeit his life.' Many had

already made the attempt, but in vain; nevertheless when the youth

saw the king's daughter he was so overcome by her great beauty that he

forgot all danger, went before the king, and declared himself a suitor.

So he was led out to the sea, and a gold ring was thrown into it, before

his eyes; then the king ordered him to fetch this ring up from the

bottom of the sea, and added: 'If you come up again without it you will

be thrown in again and again until you perish amid the waves.' All the

people grieved for the handsome youth; then they went away, leaving him

alone by the sea.

He stood on the shore and considered what he should do, when suddenly

he saw three fishes come swimming towards him, and they were the very

fishes whose lives he had saved. The one in the middle held a mussel in

its mouth, which it laid on the shore at the youth's feet, and when he

had taken it up and opened it, there lay the gold ring in the shell.

Full of joy he took it to the king and expected that he would grant him

the promised reward.

But when the proud princess perceived that he was not her equal in

birth, she scorned him, and required him first to perform another

task. She went down into the garden and strewed with her own hands ten

sacksful of millet-seed on the grass; then she said: 'Tomorrow morning

before sunrise these must be picked up, and not a single grain be

wanting.'

The youth sat down in the garden and considered how it might be possible

to perform this task, but he could think of nothing, and there he sat

sorrowfully awaiting the break of day, when he should be led to death.

But as soon as the first rays of the sun shone into the garden he saw

all the ten sacks standing side by side, quite full, and not a single

grain was missing. The ant-king had come in the night with thousands

and thousands of ants, and the grateful creatures had by great industry

picked up all the millet-seed and gathered them into the sacks.

Presently the king's daughter herself came down into the garden, and was

amazed to see that the young man had done the task she had given him.

But she could not yet conquer her proud heart, and said: 'Although he

has performed both the tasks, he shall not be my husband until he had

brought me an apple from the Tree of Life.' The youth did not know where

the Tree of Life stood, but he set out, and would have gone on for ever,

as long as his legs would carry him, though he had no hope of finding

it. After he had wandered through three kingdoms, he came one evening to

a wood, and lay down under a tree to sleep. But he heard a rustling in

the branches, and a golden apple fell into his hand. At the same time

three ravens flew down to him, perched themselves upon his knee, and

said: 'We are the three young ravens whom you saved from starving; when

we had grown big, and heard that you were seeking the Golden Apple,

we flew over the sea to the end of the world, where the Tree of Life

stands, and have brought you the apple.' The youth, full of joy, set out

homewards, and took the Golden Apple to the king's beautiful daughter,

who had now no more excuses left to make. They cut the Apple of Life in

two and ate it together; and then her heart became full of love for him,

and they lived in undisturbed happiness to a great age.

grieved them very much indeed. But one day as the queen was walking

by the side of the river, at the bottom of the garden, she saw a poor

little fish, that had thrown itself out of the water, and lay gasping

and nearly dead on the bank. Then the queen took pity on the little

fish, and threw it back again into the river; and before it swam away

it lifted its head out of the water and said, 'I know what your wish is,

and it shall be fulfilled, in return for your kindness to me--you will

soon have a daughter.' What the little fish had foretold soon came to

pass; and the queen had a little girl, so very beautiful that the king

could not cease looking on it for joy, and said he would hold a great

feast and make merry, and show the child to all the land. So he asked

his kinsmen, and nobles, and friends, and neighbours. But the queen

said, 'I will have the fairies also, that they might be kind and good

to our little daughter.' Now there were thirteen fairies in the kingdom;

but as the king and queen had only twelve golden dishes for them to eat

out of, they were forced to leave one of the fairies without asking her.

So twelve fairies came, each with a high red cap on her head, and red

shoes with high heels on her feet, and a long white wand in her hand:

and after the feast was over they gathered round in a ring and gave all

their best gifts to the little princess. One gave her goodness, another

beauty, another riches, and so on till she had all that was good in the

world.

Just as eleven of them had done blessing her, a great noise was heard in

the courtyard, and word was brought that the thirteenth fairy was

come, with a black cap on her head, and black shoes on her feet, and a

broomstick in her hand: and presently up she came into the dining-hall.

Now, as she had not been asked to the feast she was very angry, and

scolded the king and queen very much, and set to work to take her

revenge. So she cried out, 'The king's daughter shall, in her fifteenth

year, be wounded by a spindle, and fall down dead.' Then the twelfth of

the friendly fairies, who had not yet given her gift, came forward, and

said that the evil wish must be fulfilled, but that she could soften its

mischief; so her gift was, that the king's daughter, when the spindle

wounded her, should not really die, but should only fall asleep for a

hundred years.

However, the king hoped still to save his dear child altogether from

the threatened evil; so he ordered that all the spindles in the kingdom

should be bought up and burnt. But all the gifts of the first eleven

fairies were in the meantime fulfilled; for the princess was so

beautiful, and well behaved, and good, and wise, that everyone who knew

her loved her.

It happened that, on the very day she was fifteen years old, the king

and queen were not at home, and she was left alone in the palace. So she

roved about by herself, and looked at all the rooms and chambers, till

at last she came to an old tower, to which there was a narrow staircase

ending with a little door. In the door there was a golden key, and when

she turned it the door sprang open, and there sat an old lady spinning

away very busily. 'Why, how now, good mother,' said the princess; 'what

are you doing there?' 'Spinning,' said the old lady, and nodded her

head, humming a tune, while buzz! went the wheel. 'How prettily that

little thing turns round!' said the princess, and took the spindle

and began to try and spin. But scarcely had she touched it, before the

fairy's prophecy was fulfilled; the spindle wounded her, and she fell

down lifeless on the ground.

However, she was not dead, but had only fallen into a deep sleep; and

the king and the queen, who had just come home, and all their court,

fell asleep too; and the horses slept in the stables, and the dogs in

the court, the pigeons on the house-top, and the very flies slept upon

the walls. Even the fire on the hearth left off blazing, and went to

sleep; the jack stopped, and the spit that was turning about with a

goose upon it for the king's dinner stood still; and the cook, who was

at that moment pulling the kitchen-boy by the hair to give him a box

on the ear for something he had done amiss, let him go, and both fell

asleep; the butler, who was slyly tasting the ale, fell asleep with the

jug at his lips: and thus everything stood still, and slept soundly.

A large hedge of thorns soon grew round the palace, and every year it

became higher and thicker; till at last the old palace was surrounded

and hidden, so that not even the roof or the chimneys could be seen. But

there went a report through all the land of the beautiful sleeping Briar

Rose (for so the king's daughter was called): so that, from time to

time, several kings' sons came, and tried to break through the thicket

into the palace. This, however, none of them could ever do; for the

thorns and bushes laid hold of them, as it were with hands; and there

they stuck fast, and died wretchedly.

After many, many years there came a king's son into that land: and an

old man told him the story of the thicket of thorns; and how a beautiful

palace stood behind it, and how a wonderful princess, called Briar Rose,

lay in it asleep, with all her court. He told, too, how he had heard

from his grandfather that many, many princes had come, and had tried to

break through the thicket, but that they had all stuck fast in it, and

died. Then the young prince said, 'All this shall not frighten me; I

will go and see this Briar Rose.' The old man tried to hinder him, but

he was bent upon going.

Now that very day the hundred years were ended; and as the prince came

to the thicket he saw nothing but beautiful flowering shrubs, through

which he went with ease, and they shut in after him as thick as ever.

Then he came at last to the palace, and there in the court lay the dogs

asleep; and the horses were standing in the stables; and on the roof sat

the pigeons fast asleep, with their heads under their wings. And when he

came into the palace, the flies were sleeping on the walls; the spit

was standing still; the butler had the jug of ale at his lips, going

to drink a draught; the maid sat with a fowl in her lap ready to be

plucked; and the cook in the kitchen was still holding up her hand, as

if she was going to beat the boy.

Then he went on still farther, and all was so still that he could hear

every breath he drew; till at last he came to the old tower, and opened

the door of the little room in which Briar Rose was; and there she lay,

fast asleep on a couch by the window. She looked so beautiful that he

could not take his eyes off her, so he stooped down and gave her a kiss.

But the moment he kissed her she opened her eyes and awoke, and smiled

upon him; and they went out together; and soon the king and queen also

awoke, and all the court, and gazed on each other with great wonder.

And the horses shook themselves, and the dogs jumped up and barked; the

pigeons took their heads from under their wings, and looked about and

flew into the fields; the flies on the walls buzzed again; the fire in

the kitchen blazed up; round went the jack, and round went the spit,

with the goose for the king's dinner upon it; the butler finished his

draught of ale; the maid went on plucking the fowl; and the cook gave

the boy the box on his ear.

And then the prince and Briar Rose were married, and the wedding feast

was given; and they lived happily together all their lives long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Alice. She loved to go on adventures! Her favorite thing was to get her passport and check out different places around the world.

One day, Alice asked her mom if she could get her passport and go on an adventure. But her mom was feeling a bit grumpy and said no.
Alice was very unhappy and started to cry. "What did I do wrong?" she asked.

Alice's mom looked at her with a smile and said, "That's okay my darling. You can still have an adventure, just not with a passport. I can tell you a story about a far away place that would be fun for you to explore!"

Alice nodded her head and smiled. Soon, she was off exploring this magical world her mom had told her about. She had an amazing time, and realized that sometimes even without a passport you can still have a great adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a king who wore a large crown on his head. He loved to play with his toys and would often pause to take a break. One day, he lost his crown while playing and couldn't find it anywhere. He paused and looked all around his castle but still couldn't find it.

The king asked his friends to help him look for his crown. They searched high and low but still couldn't find it. The king started to feel sad because he loved his large crown so much. Just when he thought he would never find it, his dog came running up with the crown in his mouth. The king was so happy that he paused to give his dog a big hug. From then on, he made sure to always keep his crown safe while he played.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Max. Sam and Max liked to have fun together. One day they decided to prepare a jolly fire. Sam and Max found some sticks and small logs and laid them carefully in a pile. Max used a match to light the fire. Soon the small logs were burning brightly. The two friends loved to watch the flame dance around the wood.

Sam and Max were having so much fun that they decided to roast marshmallows. They put the marshmallows on sticks and held them over the fire. The marshmallows became all warm and gooey. The two friends ate the melted marshmallows and laughed. It was a jolly time for Sam and Max.

They enjoyed the fire until it got dark. Sam and Max tidied everything up and went home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Snowy. Snowy was very white and fluffy. One day, Snowy went to the forest to play with his friends. They played hide-and-seek, but Snowy couldn't find his friends. It was getting dark and Snowy was scared. Suddenly, he felt a pinch on his tail. It was his friend, the squirrel! They went home together and Snowy felt happy again. The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy who loved to wave. He waved to the sun, he waved to the birdies and he waved to his mommy and daddy. One day he wanted to be even better at waving. So, he went to the garden to practice.

The boy waved his arms all around. He waved them high and low. He waved them to the left and he waved them to the right. He became very competitive.

After a while he got tired. He reached up as high as he could and thenâ€¦ he fell down. There were lots of yummy leaves all around and he had a lot of fun. But then it became time to go home.

The boy said goodbye to the leaves and he waved again. He waved to the sky, the trees and his mommy and daddy. As he got ready to go home, he smiled because he knew he was the best waver in town.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play and laugh together. One day, they find a book of jokes. They want to read the jokes and make each other laugh.

Anna reads the first joke. She says, "What do you call a fish that wears a bow tie?" Ben thinks hard. He does not know. Anna says, "Sofishticated!" She laughs. Ben laughs too. He thinks the joke is funny.

Ben reads the next joke. He says, "Why did the chicken cross the road?" Anna thinks hard. She does not know. Ben says, "To get to the other slide!" He laughs. Anna does not laugh. She is confused. She says, "That is not a joke. That is silly. Chickens do not slide."

Ben says, "Yes, they do. Look at the picture." He shows Anna the picture in the book. It is a chicken on a slide. Anna says, "That is not a real chicken. That is a drawing. Drawings are not real."

Ben says, "But it is a joke. Jokes are not real. Jokes are funny." Anna says, "No, jokes are real. Jokes make sense. That joke does not make sense. That joke is bad."

Anna and Ben start to argue. They do not agree on what is a joke. They do not laugh anymore. They get angry and sad. They cry.

Mom hears them cry. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees the book of jokes. She says, "What is the matter, Anna and Ben? Why are you crying?"

Anna and Ben tell Mom about the jokes. They tell her why they are confused and upset. Mom listens. She says, "I understand. Jokes are tricky. Sometimes they are funny. Sometimes they are not. Sometimes they make sense. Sometimes they do not. It is okay to have different opinions. It is okay to not like a joke. But it is not okay to fight and cry. You are friends. You should be kind and respectful to each other. You should share and take turns. You should say sorry and forgive. You should have fun and learn together."

Anna and Ben nod. They say sorry to each other. They hug and make up. They wipe their tears. They smile. They decide to read more jokes. They hope to find some that they both like. They thank Mom for helping them. Mom says, "You are welcome. I love you both. Jokes are good. Jokes make you laugh. Laughter is good. Laughter makes you happy."

Bobby was out in the garden, gazing at the trees. The leaves danced in the warm breeze and the sun was shining brilliantly. He felt so small amongst the giant trees.

He looked up and saw a bird perched in the branches, singing joyfully. Bobby felt a strong desire to join the bird, but he was too helpless to even try. He sighed sadly.

Suddenly, his dad appeared beside him and gave him a hug. He said, "Don't feel helpless, Bobby. I promise I'll take you up there one day."

Bobby looked up at his dad with shining eyes. "Really?" he asked, still hopeful. His dad smiled and said with a gentle nod, "Yes, I promise."

Bobby smiled and hugged his dad tightly. He'd never felt so happy and excited. In that moment, he knew that his dad's promise was one that he could always rely on.

Once upon a time there was a small bunny called Alice. Alice liked to do things all by herself. She was very independent. One day Alice went to visit her friend. When she arrived there was a big fridge in the middle of the room. Alice had a great idea. She opened the fridge and found a big surprise. She saw yummy ice cream. She wanted to eat it all by herself, so she grabbed a bowl and the ice cream. She closed the fridge and enjoyed her ice cream. She remembered to always be independent.

The next day Alice and her friend were playing outside. Alice saw a fridge in the garden. She was so excited and rushed over. She opened it and saw something sparkly. It was a magic wand! Instinctively, Alice remembered what to do with the wand - make a wish. She closed the fridge and made her wish. She wished to always remember to be independent. In that moment, she felt so special.

Alice will never forget the magical moment when she found the magic wand in the fridge, and she will always remember to be independent.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lola. She was very curious about the world around her. One day, her mum and dad decided to get a tutor for Lola so she could learn about different things.

The tutor was called Mrs Smith and she was very kind and gentle. She arrived with lots of delicate books and paper. Mrs Smith helped Lola to sit down and started to explain everything.

At first, the pages looked like chicken scratches to Lola, but Mrs Smith said the words very clearly and slowly. She first explained about shapes, then letters and numbers. Lola listened carefully and soon became very good at understanding what Mrs Smith told her.

Mrs Smith was very pleased with Lola's progress and each time she came, she brought something new to explain. Lola learnt lots because of her tutor and she soon became very clever.

The End

One day, at the beach, Sam saw something strange. There was a mysterious row in the sand. The row seemed to be increasing, getting longer and longer.

Sam was curious and wanted to find out what it was. He touched the row and realized it was made up of tiny shells. Suddenly, a little crab emerged from the sand and waved its claws at Sam.

Sam was surprised and jumped back. He watched as the crab continued to increase the row of shells. Sam's mom smiled and told him that the crab was building its home.

Then, Sam and his mom watched together as the crab worked and the mysterious row of shells slowly increased in length. Sam smiled and knew he had found a new friend.

One hot day, Joe was outside playing in the sun. Suddenly, he heard something in the distance. Joe slowly crept to look, and he saw a cool monkey! Joe was very excited and ran over to the monkey. He said, "Hello, Monkey! My name is Joe. What are you doing?"

The monkey replied, "I'm washing in the river. It's a great way to stay cool in this heat!" Joe was curious and asked, "Can I wash too?" The monkey smiled and said, "Of course! Come join me!"

So Joe and the monkey washed in the river together. Joe was laughing and having such a great time that time flew by. Joe looked up and realized he had to go home, but he said goodbye and thanked the monkey for the cool adventure.

Anna was a very cheerful girl. She especially loved playing outside. One day, while Anna was playing in the garden, her mum came and called her inside.

Anna said, "Mum, why? I'm having so much fun!"

Mum smiled and said, "Anna, I need you to help me lift a blouse out of the cupboard. Will you come and help?"

Anna was very excited to help, so she followed her mum inside. Mum lifted the blouse from the cupboard and showed Anna.

"Now," said Mum, "Can you help me lift the blouse on my bed?"

Anna was eager to help, so she reached up and together with her mum, they lifted the blouse onto the bed.

When it was done, Anna said, "There!", feeling very proud of her work.

Mum smiled and said, "Well done, Anna. You did a great job."

Anna was very cheerful as she gave her mum a big hug. She was so glad she had helped.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and touch everything he saw. One day, Timmy's mommy had to go to work and she left him with his grandma.

Timmy's grandma was very rich and had a big house with lots of toys. Timmy was very happy and played with all the toys. He even touched the shiny things and the soft things.

After playing for a while, Timmy's grandma asked him to help her with some work. Timmy didn't like work, but he wanted to make his grandma happy, so he helped her. They worked together and finished all the work. Timmy was proud of himself for helping his grandma.

At the end of the day, Timmy's mommy came back from work and was very happy to see that Timmy had a good day with his grandma. Timmy told his mommy all about the toys he played with and the work he did with his grandma. His mommy was proud of him too. From that day on, Timmy loved to help his grandma with work and play with her toys.

John had his own paint. He was very excited and happy to show it to his mom. He said, "Mommy, I own paint!" His mom replied, "That's great John, let's paint together!" So, they opened the paint and John started to draw with it.

After a while, John finished his masterpiece and it looked so beautiful to him. He said to his mom, "Look mommy, I own tight paint!"

His mom was surprised and said, "Wow John, that's very impressive. Let's hang it up!" But, before they could hang the painting, John had an accident and the paint got smeared all over the place. His mom tried to console him but John was devastated and sad.

The bad ending had been foreshadowed ever since John opened his paint; his mom had warned him several times to be careful and not play around with the paint too much. But, inevitably, he went against his mother's advice and it cost him dearly in the end.

Once there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his camera and take pictures of everything. One day Timmy noticed something strange while he was taking pictures. He saw a big dog standing next to him. Timmy felt a bit scared, but the dog didn't do anything. He just stood there and watched Timmy.

Timmy's mom saw the dog and knew that the dog was there to protect Timmy. She smiled and said, "Don't be confused, Timmy. The dog is here to protect you!" Timmy was happy to hear that he was being protected.

So, every time Timmy took pictures, the dog would stay close by and keep him safe. Timmy wasn't afraid anymore because he knew that he was being protected. Timmy and the dog became best friends and Timmy felt safe whenever he had his camera with him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jake. Jake was an adventurous boy, who loved to explore new places. He wanted to store new things and trade with others.

One day, Jake decided to go on a trading mission. He brought along some of his treasures and he was super excited! He hopped on his bike and pedaled off, with a sense of determination.

When Jake reached the trade area, he saw lots of interesting things. He started trading and he was delighted when he got something special in return. He went home feeling very happy and proud.

Jake stored all of his new treasures in his closet, waiting to use them in his next big adventure!

One day, there were two friends named Abigail and Daniel. They decided they would march together in the park. So, they put on their coats and marched off. At first, everything was fun. They sang songs and marched along the sidewalk.

Suddenly, Abigail felt a sharp pain in her leg. She stopped and cried out. She was so angry. Daniel tried to help her, but she refused. She had to march on her own.

Abigail marched slowly, trying to ignore the pain. After a few moments, she felt a bit better. She and Daniel continued to march together, happily singing their favorite song. They had made it through their march, despite the pain.

Tim was an impatient little boy. He always wanted to do things quickly! One morning he woke up and asked his mom, "When will the sun rise?"

His mom said, "soon, sweetheart, soon. You have to be patient. But it's important to remember that sunrises are valuable. They give us a wonderful start to a new day. Doesn't that sound special?".

Tim thought about this for a moment and said, "yes, it does sound special. I think I can be patient now".

So they sat downstairs, snuggled up together on the sofa, and waited for the sunrise. When they saw it, they were both filled with wonder. What a beautiful and valuable sight it was!

Once there was a very smart bunny named Bun. He liked playing in the dark. One night, his mom told him it was bedtime, but Bun snuck out of bed. He grabbed his special toy, a little flashlight. He wanted to raise it up high and look around. He saw all kinds of things in the dark. He saw spiders and cats and he even saw a little mouse. Then he heard a noise. He was scared! He raiseed the flashlight up higher and saw it was his mom. She said "Bun, it's time to go to bed." Bun was so glad she was there. He raised the flashlight up to his face and smiled. And they both went back to bed.

THE DOG AND THE SPARROW

A shepherd's dog had a master who took no care of him, but often let him

suffer the greatest hunger. At last he could bear it no longer; so he

took to his heels, and off he ran in a very sad and sorrowful mood.

On the road he met a sparrow that said to him, 'Why are you so sad,

my friend?' 'Because,' said the dog, 'I am very very hungry, and have

nothing to eat.' 'If that be all,' answered the sparrow, 'come with me

into the next town, and I will soon find you plenty of food.' So on they

went together into the town: and as they passed by a butcher's shop,

the sparrow said to the dog, 'Stand there a little while till I peck you

down a piece of meat.' So the sparrow perched upon the shelf: and having

first looked carefully about her to see if anyone was watching her, she

pecked and scratched at a steak that lay upon the edge of the shelf,

till at last down it fell. Then the dog snapped it up, and scrambled

away with it into a corner, where he soon ate it all up. 'Well,' said

the sparrow, 'you shall have some more if you will; so come with me to

the next shop, and I will peck you down another steak.' When the dog had

eaten this too, the sparrow said to him, 'Well, my good friend, have you

had enough now?' 'I have had plenty of meat,' answered he, 'but I should

like to have a piece of bread to eat after it.' 'Come with me then,'

said the sparrow, 'and you shall soon have that too.' So she took him

to a baker's shop, and pecked at two rolls that lay in the window, till

they fell down: and as the dog still wished for more, she took him to

another shop and pecked down some more for him. When that was eaten, the

sparrow asked him whether he had had enough now. 'Yes,' said he; 'and

now let us take a walk a little way out of the town.' So they both went

out upon the high road; but as the weather was warm, they had not gone

far before the dog said, 'I am very much tired--I should like to take a

nap.' 'Very well,' answered the sparrow, 'do so, and in the meantime

I will perch upon that bush.' So the dog stretched himself out on the

road, and fell fast asleep. Whilst he slept, there came by a carter with

a cart drawn by three horses, and loaded with two casks of wine. The

sparrow, seeing that the carter did not turn out of the way, but would

go on in the track in which the dog lay, so as to drive over him, called

out, 'Stop! stop! Mr Carter, or it shall be the worse for you.' But the

carter, grumbling to himself, 'You make it the worse for me, indeed!

what can you do?' cracked his whip, and drove his cart over the poor

dog, so that the wheels crushed him to death. 'There,' cried the

sparrow, 'thou cruel villain, thou hast killed my friend the dog. Now

mind what I say. This deed of thine shall cost thee all thou art worth.'

'Do your worst, and welcome,' said the brute, 'what harm can you do me?'

and passed on. But the sparrow crept under the tilt of the cart, and

pecked at the bung of one of the casks till she loosened it; and then

all the wine ran out, without the carter seeing it. At last he looked

round, and saw that the cart was dripping, and the cask quite empty.

'What an unlucky wretch I am!' cried he. 'Not wretch enough yet!' said

the sparrow, as she alighted upon the head of one of the horses, and

pecked at him till he reared up and kicked. When the carter saw this,

he drew out his hatchet and aimed a blow at the sparrow, meaning to kill

her; but she flew away, and the blow fell upon the poor horse's head

with such force, that he fell down dead. 'Unlucky wretch that I am!'

cried he. 'Not wretch enough yet!' said the sparrow. And as the carter

went on with the other two horses, she again crept under the tilt of the

cart, and pecked out the bung of the second cask, so that all the wine

ran out. When the carter saw this, he again cried out, 'Miserable wretch

that I am!' But the sparrow answered, 'Not wretch enough yet!' and

perched on the head of the second horse, and pecked at him too. The

carter ran up and struck at her again with his hatchet; but away she

flew, and the blow fell upon the second horse and killed him on the

spot. 'Unlucky wretch that I am!' said he. 'Not wretch enough yet!' said

the sparrow; and perching upon the third horse, she began to peck him

too. The carter was mad with fury; and without looking about him, or

caring what he was about, struck again at the sparrow; but killed his

third horse as he done the other two. 'Alas! miserable wretch that I

am!' cried he. 'Not wretch enough yet!' answered the sparrow as she flew

away; 'now will I plague and punish thee at thy own house.' The

carter was forced at last to leave his cart behind him, and to go home

overflowing with rage and vexation. 'Alas!' said he to his wife, 'what

ill luck has befallen me!--my wine is all spilt, and my horses all three

dead.' 'Alas! husband,' replied she, 'and a wicked bird has come into

the house, and has brought with her all the birds in the world, I am

sure, and they have fallen upon our corn in the loft, and are eating it

up at such a rate!' Away ran the husband upstairs, and saw thousands of

birds sitting upon the floor eating up his corn, with the sparrow in the

midst of them. 'Unlucky wretch that I am!' cried the carter; for he saw

that the corn was almost all gone. 'Not wretch enough yet!' said the

sparrow; 'thy cruelty shall cost thee thy life yet!' and away she flew.

The carter seeing that he had thus lost all that he had, went down

into his kitchen; and was still not sorry for what he had done, but sat

himself angrily and sulkily in the chimney corner. But the sparrow sat

on the outside of the window, and cried 'Carter! thy cruelty shall cost

thee thy life!' With that he jumped up in a rage, seized his hatchet,

and threw it at the sparrow; but it missed her, and only broke the

window. The sparrow now hopped in, perched upon the window-seat, and

cried, 'Carter! it shall cost thee thy life!' Then he became mad and

blind with rage, and struck the window-seat with such force that he

cleft it in two: and as the sparrow flew from place to place, the carter

and his wife were so furious, that they broke all their furniture,

glasses, chairs, benches, the table, and at last the walls, without

touching the bird at all. In the end, however, they caught her: and the

wife said, 'Shall I kill her at once?' 'No,' cried he, 'that is letting

her off too easily: she shall die a much more cruel death; I will eat

her.' But the sparrow began to flutter about, and stretch out her neck

and cried, 'Carter! it shall cost thee thy life yet!' With that he

could wait no longer: so he gave his wife the hatchet, and cried, 'Wife,

strike at the bird and kill her in my hand.' And the wife struck; but

she missed her aim, and hit her husband on the head so that he fell down

dead, and the sparrow flew quietly home to her nest.

Once upon a time, there was a peaceful place. A little boy was walking through the peaceful place. He was looking for something. Suddenly he saw a lollipop! He got so excited. He walked over and began to poke the lollipop with his finger. He was curious to see what would happen. Suddenly, the lollipop started to spin around and around! He was so surprised. He wanted to play more with the lollipop, so he poked it again. Again, the lollipop started to spin. He had so much fun playing with the lollipop. Soon, his mom called him and he had to rush back home. But before he left, he gave the lollipop one last poke and then said goodbye. He went back home feeling happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big water bottle that she loved to carry with her everywhere. One day, she noticed that her water bottle was very heavy and she couldn't carry it anymore.

Lily went to her mom and said, "Mommy, my water bottle is too heavy. Can you help me carry it?"

Her mom replied, "Lily, you don't need to carry such a heavy water bottle. You can drink from a smaller one that is easier for you to carry."

Lily understood what her mom said and went to get a smaller water bottle. As she was pouring water into the new bottle, she noticed that her old water bottle had a leak. She told her mom about it and her mom said, "Lily, it's important to take care of our things. We need to fix the leak so we don't waste water."

Lily learned that it's important to take care of her things and to only carry what she needs.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl named Lily. She had a lot of energy and loved to explore the world around her.

One day, Lily was walking through the park and saw something very attractive. It was a shiny red car that was ready to zoom across the park. She had never seen a car like this before and wanted to ride in it.

Lily walked up to the car and said, "Hi! Can I have a ride?"

The car driver looked at her and said, "Sure! Hop in and I'll take you around the park."

Lily was so excited. She strapped herself in, and the car zoomed around the park. The wind blew in her face and the sun shone on her skin. Lily had never felt so happy.

When it was time to go home, Lily thanked the car driver and said, "That was fun!"

The car driver smiled and waved goodbye as the car zoomed away.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Sam. He was three years old, and he loved to explore.

One day, Sam went for a walk in the woods. He came to a lovely tunnel and he wanted to go inside. He searched and searched, but couldn't find an entrance.

Just then, a friendly rabbit hopped up to him.

"Hello!" said the rabbit. "Can I help you?"

Sam was very excited. "Yes please!" he said. "I want to go in this tunnel."

The rabbit smiled. "I know a way in!" it said cheerfully. "Follow me!"

The rabbit led Sam through the woods, until soon, the two of them were standing in front of a small door in the side of the tunnel.

Sam was delighted. He opened the door, and thanked the rabbit.

The rabbit waved goodbye, and Sam stepped inside the tunnel. He was amazed by what he found - there were all sorts of things to explore! So Sam spent the rest of the day searching around, and having a lovely time.

Sue and Mike were planning a picnic in the park. They wanted to have the best time ever! Sue and Mike packed snacks for their picnic. They brought lots of different snacks, but their favorite was the beans.

When they arrived in the park, they spread out their blanket and started to get ready for the picnic. Suddenly, Sue noticed something strange â€" there was a deaf rabbit in the middle of the park.

Sue was excited. She called out to Mike, "Let's give him some beans!" Mike nodded with a smile and together they took out an extra portion of beans and placed it near the rabbit.

The rabbit hopped around the beans and started to eat. Sue and Mike were delighted to see the rabbit enjoying their snack. They had a wonderful picnic and plan to visit the park again soon.

Once upon a time there was a young girl who lived in a tiny house with her parents. Every day she would play around her house, but what she liked the most was to go to the library. There was an amazing shelf that was so tall it almost touched the ceiling and it was filled with books!

One day the girl asked her mum if she could take one of the books home with her. Her mum said yes, but only if she picked the right one. The girl was so proud of herself when she found the perfect book for her. She carefully put it in her bag and went home with it.

Once the girl arrived home, her mum noticed the book in her bag. "What's this?" she said. The girl quickly told her mum all about the library and the shelf filled with books. She was so proud of her book! But her mum was not pleased; she said that she should never have taken the book without asking, and she had to return it immediately.

The girl was so happy when she got back to the library that she offered to put the book back on the shelf herself. As she did so, she realized that she had learned an important lesson. Taking things without asking was wrong, and she was proud to have done the right thing. From that day on, she always asked before she borrowed things.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and full of energy. She was always curious to know what was new and different in the world.

One day, her mommy took her to the park. It was filled with so many things to explore. She saw kids playing on the swings, dogs playing catch and birds flying through the sky.

The little girl began to wonder. She wondered what each thing knew and what it was like to have those amazing adventures.

So, her mommy took her to the top of a hill. She showed the little girl a new point. It was a point of knowledge. This was a place where the little girl could see a lot of things at once.

The little girl was so excited. She was intrigued by the new point and she wanted to know more. Her mommy told her that this was a place to learn and to become a part of the world.

From then on, the little girl had so many new adventures. She learned things from the point, and she felt that she knew more about the world. The little girl became smarter, happier and more excited every day.

Once upon a time, in a land far away, there was a big volcano. The volcano was very grumpy and would sometimes make a loud "boom" sound. People who lived near the volcano were scared and did not like the noise.

One day, a brave girl named Lily decided to help the people. She thought the volcano was grumpy because it was hungry. She knew that the volcano liked to eat sour fruits. So, Lily went to the market to buy some sour fruits. She did not have much money, but she wanted to help. She gave her money to the man at the market and said, "I want to pay for the sour fruits, please."

Lily took the sour fruits and climbed the big volcano. When she reached the top, she said, "Mr. Volcano, I brought you some sour fruits to eat. Please don't be grumpy anymore." The volcano ate the sour fruits and stopped making the loud "boom" sound. The people were very happy and thanked Lily for her help. From that day on, the volcano was not grumpy anymore, and everyone lived happily ever after.

Mama was explaining to her little one that the wind was blowing outside. She said it was very smooth. Her little one was curious and asked what that meant. Mama smiled and said that it felt very nice and gentle, like a warm hug. She then put her hands up and said, "Can you feel the wind? How smooth it is!" Her little one put her hands up and felt the wind and said, "It's tickly!" Mama laughed and said, "Yes, it is a bit tickly."

They both watched the leaves blowing in the wind, laughing as they did so. Mama explained that the wind was carrying the leaves, making them fly and swirl around. The little one was amazed, and asked Mama if she could do it too. Mama showed her how to put her arms out and spin around in the wind, just like the leaves. The little one did as Mama said and enjoyed feeling the wind on her face. She said it felt so smooth and soft!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who decided to go for a walk. He went down a path, and all of a sudden he found something. It was a pile of leaves! The little boy decided to sort them into different piles.

He sat down and started to sort the leaves. After a while he started to get really tired, but he kept on sorting. Suddenly, he thought he heard something coming down the path. He stopped sorting, and tried to listen carefully to see what it was.

It was a big, mean, wolf! The wolf was heading right for him! The little boy didn't know what to do, so he tried to build a little wall around himself with the leaves he had been sorting before. But that didn't stop the wolf!

The wolf ate the little boy up! That was the end of the little boy, and the leaves were left lying on the path.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy cat. Cat liked to find secrets. One day Cat heard a funny noise. Cat looked up to the sky and saw a big balloon. It had an exciting secret inside.

Cat said, â€œI want to know the secret inside!â€ Cat jumped at the balloon but it floated away. Cat followed the balloon through the sky.

Cat said, â€œWhat is the secret?â€

The balloon said, â€œI will disappear and you will never know the secret.â€ And with that, the balloon disappeared into the clouds.

Cat was sad the balloon was gone. But Cat kept looking for new secrets. And Cat was sure that one day Cat would find the secret of the mysterious disappearing balloon.

Jimmy was searching for something special to watch on tv. He wanted to find a good film. He asked his dad to help him find something available.

They looked and looked, but they couldn't find anything fun. Jimmy was starting to lose hope. Then suddenly, something caught his attention. It was a cartoon that was available!

Jimmy was so excited. He ran over to the tv and turned it on. There were lots of bright colors and fun sounds. He watched the whole movie and couldn't stop smiling.

When it finished, Jimmy searched for something else. He wanted to see what else was available. He watched several other films and was kept entertained the whole day.

Jimmy's dad was so happy to see his son enjoying himself. He was glad he was able to help him find the perfect film.

One day, a small girl went to the farm with her mom. She saw many animals like cows, pigs and chickens. Then, she saw a big field with small plants. Her mom told her that it was a field of oats. The girl saw that the oats were small and yellow. She picked one and saw that it was very light. She was happy to see the oats and wanted to take some home.

Once upon a time there lived a brave little mouse who liked to explore. One day the mouse decided to explore a big forest. As he made his way through the forest, he heard a whistle.

The mouse was scared but brave at the same time and so he followed the sound of the whistle. He soon found an elderly man with a big grey beard.

The mouse shouted 'Who are You?' but the man did not answer. The mouse asked again 'Why are you whistling?'

The old man smiled and said 'I'm just enjoying the nature.'

The mouse was so brave and curious, he dared to ask 'Can I join you?'

The old man grinned and said 'I'd love that.'

So the brave little mouse joined the elderly man in the forest, and they enjoyed the nature together. The end.

Rory was a very curious 3-year-old boy. One morning, he started watching his parents get ready for work. He noticed his mom was wearing big, black boots. He had never liked boots and he was fearful!

"Mommy," he asked, "why do you wear those big, black boots?"

His mom said, "I wear boots to keep my feet warm and dry."

Rory wasn't sure he believed her. He asked, "Can I try them on?"

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can. Let me help you get them on."

Rory was amazed! The boots were so big and they fit him perfectly! He started stomping around the living room, feeling brave and strong.

"The boots make me feel like I can do anything!" he shouted.

His mom laughed. "I guess they do, don't they!" she said.

Rory was so proud. He had learned that even the things he was fearful of could be wonderful, if he just gave them a try.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a big purple bike with a basket in front. One day, Lily wanted to ride her bike to the park. She put on her helmet and rode down the street.

When she got to the park, she saw a crazy clown. The clown had a big red nose and was juggling balls. Lily rode her bike over to watch the clown. The clown even gave her a purple balloon animal.

After watching the clown, Lily rode her bike to the swings. She swung back and forth, feeling the wind in her hair. She had so much fun riding her bike and playing at the park. When it was time to go home, she rode her bike back down the street, holding onto her purple balloon animal.

Tom likes to shine his shoes. He has black shoes that he wears to school. He wants them to look nice and smooth. He gets a newspaper from his dad and puts it on the floor. He gets a brush and some polish from his mom and starts to shine his shoes.

He rubs the polish on his shoes with the brush. He makes small circles with the brush. He sees the polish make his shoes shiny and smooth. He smiles and says, "Look, mom, look, dad, my shoes are shiny and smooth!"

His mom and dad look at his shoes and say, "Wow, Tom, your shoes are very shiny and smooth! You did a good job shining them. You are a good boy."

Tom feels happy and proud. He thanks his mom and dad for the polish and the brush. He picks up the newspaper and throws it in the trash. He puts on his shoes and says, "I'm ready for school. Bye, mom, bye, dad!"

He goes out the door and walks to the bus stop. He sees his friends and says, "Hi, friends, look at my shoes. They are shiny and smooth!"

His friends look at his shoes and say, "Wow, Tom, your shoes are very shiny and smooth! You have nice shoes. How did you shine them?"

Tom tells them about the newspaper, the brush and the polish. He says, "You can shine your shoes too. It is easy and fun. You just need a newspaper, a brush and some polish."

His friends say, "That sounds cool. We want to shine our shoes too. Can you show us how?"

Tom says, "Sure, I can show you how. Come to my house after school. We can shine our shoes together."

His friends say, "OK, that sounds fun. Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend."

Tom says, "You're welcome, friends. You are good friends too."

They get on the bus and go to school. They have a good day. They learn new things. They play and laugh. They are happy. They have shiny and smooth shoes.

Lily was sick. She had a bad cough and a sore throat. Mommy gave her some medicine, but Lily did not like it. It was bitter and yucky. She made a face and spit it out.

Mommy was upset. She said, "Lily, you need to take your medicine. It will make you feel better." She tried to give Lily the medicine again, but Lily turned her head and said, "No, no, no!"

Lily ran away from Mommy. She wanted to play with her toys. She did not want to take the medicine. She ran to her room, but she did not see the ball on the floor. She stepped on the ball and stumbled. She fell down and hurt her knee. She cried out loud.

Mommy heard Lily cry. She ran to her room and saw Lily on the floor. She picked her up and hugged her. She said, "Oh, Lily, are you okay? You have a boo-boo on your knee. Let me get a band-aid for you."

Lily stopped crying. She looked at Mommy and said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I was naughty. I did not take my medicine. Can I have it now?" Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, you can have your medicine now. I'm glad you changed your mind. It will make you feel better." She gave Lily the medicine and a glass of water. Lily drank it and made a face, but she did not spit it out.

Mommy kissed Lily and said, "Good girl, Lily. I love you. Now, let's go to bed. You need to rest and get well." Lily nodded and said, "I love you too, Mommy. Thank you for the medicine and the band-aid." Mommy tucked Lily in and turned off the light. Lily closed her eyes and fell asleep. She dreamed of happy things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress that fit her just right. One day, while playing outside, she fell and got a scrape on her knee. Her mommy came to her and wiped the blood away with a soft cloth. Then she gave her a kiss on the boo-boo to make it feel better. Lily was so happy to have such a loving mommy. From that day on, she made sure to be careful when playing outside.

Once upon a time there was a small girl. Her name was Sue. She was 3 years old.

One day Sue went for a walk in her garden and noticed something special. It was a delicate note that blew in on the wind. Sue felt excited. She wanted to read it and find out who the note was for.

So Sue picked up the note and opened it carefully. On the note was a large heart with a message inside. It said "Happy Birthday".

Sue felt happy. She put the note in her pocket and skipped back home. She smiled all day long as she thought of the special note.

That night, Sue put the note in an envelope and gave it to her mummy and daddy. She said "I found this note in the garden. It made me feel happy." They all smiled and hugged Sue.

The note reminded them all of how delicate and special life can be.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. He was a happy three year old. One day, Joe was looking at his calendar. He frowned. Something didn't smell right. It was smelly!

He asked his mom, "What that smell?"

"Honey, it's the trash!" His mom replied.

Joe frowned again. He was confused. He asked, "Why it smelly?"

His mom smiled. "It's time to take out the garbage. Come help me, Joe."

Joe shook his head. He was still confused but he followed his mom. Together they took out the smelly garbage and threw it out in the trash bin.

Joe's mom smiled. "See, that wasn't so hard. Now the smell is gone!"

Joe smiled and gave his mom a big hug. He was happy that the smelly trash was gone. And he learned an important lesson about taking out the garbage.

Once upon a time, there was a very fast onion named Gary. He was so fast, that he could even race the wind. He liked to brag about his speed to all of his friends.

One day, Gary decided to challenge the wind to a race. He wanted to prove that he was even faster than the wind. So, he zoomed off without a thought!

When Gary approached the wind his friends were worried. They shouted out to Gary to quit the race and come back, but Gary didn't listen. He wanted to prove that he was the fastest.

The wind started to pick up and Gary was struggling to keep up. Soon enough, he was too tired to keep up with the wind and Gary had to quit the race.

Poor Gary! All this excitement had been for nothing.

Despite his failure, Gary's friends assured him that he was still the fastest onion that they ever knew.

The moral of this story? It's important to remember your limits and to quit when things get too hard.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old. Her teachers said she was bossy, but she loved to play outside with her friends.

One day she decided to go exploring, and she saw something really exciting. There was an open door! She had never seen it before. She thought this must be a special door.

She slowly walked inside the room and was amazed. There were toys everywhere! She had never seen so many exciting things.

Then she realized something. This was her very own room. It was her special room filled with her own toys. It was even more amazing to her than the open door.

She had so much fun playing in her room. She showed it to all of her friends, and they all thought it was very cool. She was so proud that she was bossy enough to explore and find her own special room.

One day there was a clever radio. It sang lovely songs and made everyone happy. But then something strange happened. The radio began to split in two. It split and split until the pieces were very small. Everyone was so sad to see their clever radio fall apart. But then a very special thing happened. A man came and fixed the radio, and soon it was singing again. Everyone was so happy and cheered that their clever radio was back!

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to watch cartoons on TV. They sit on the couch and talk about the cartoons.

"Look, Sam, it's the dog and the cat!" Tim says. "They are funny. The dog is big and the cat is small."

"Yes, Tim, they are funny. The dog is silly and the cat is smart." Sam says. "They always chase each other and make noises."

They laugh and clap their hands. They watch the cartoons for a long time.

Then, Tim's mom comes in. She sees Tim and Sam on the couch. She sees the TV. She is not happy.

"Tim, Sam, you have watched enough cartoons. It's time to go outside and play." She says. "You need some sun and fresh air. You look pale."

Tim and Sam do not want to go outside. They want to watch more cartoons. They make sad faces.

"But mom, we like the cartoons. They are fun. Can we watch a little more?" Tim says.

"No, Tim, you can't. You have watched too much. You need to move and run and jump. That's good for you." She says. "Come on, put on your shoes and jackets. I'll take you to the park. You can play with other kids and have fun."

Tim and Sam sigh. They turn off the TV. They put on their shoes and jackets. They follow Tim's mom to the car. They hope they can watch more cartoons later.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey named Max. Max loved to eat bananas. One day, Max found a big banana but it was too big for him to eat.

Max asked his friend, a rabbit named Rosie, "Can you help me split this banana?"

Rosie tried to split the banana but it was too persistent. They both tried and tried but the banana wouldn't split.

Suddenly, Max had an idea. He climbed up a tree and dropped the banana from high up. The banana split into two pieces! Max and Rosie were so happy they could finally eat the banana together.

Once upon a time, there was an intelligent frog named Fred. Fred loved to hop all day long. He would hop in the green grass, hop in the cool water, and hop on the big rocks.

One day, Fred found a bottle of ink. The ink was blue and shiny. He thought it was very pretty. Fred wanted to hop with the ink, so he picked it up with his mouth.

Fred hopped and hopped with the ink. He hopped so much that the ink spilled everywhere! The grass, the water, and the rocks all had blue ink on them. Fred laughed and thought it was funny. Now, everything was blue and pretty just like the ink.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was very careless and liked to have fun. One day, she went outside and decided to jump in a big puddle. She splashed and made big waves around her. But, when she looked down, she noticed her hands were all muddy. She remembered her mom had said to mind the dirt, so she knew she had to clean her hands.

The girl went inside and her mom gave her some soap. She put it on her hands and started to rub them together. The soap foamed and she enjoyed feeling it tickle her palms. After she finished, she could see her hands were all clean and shiny again.

The girl was happy and didn't want to be careless again. Whenever she went outside and got her hands a bit dirty, she always made sure to mind the dirt and wash them with soap.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was sad and very miserable. She was so bored she couldn't find anything to do. Then she saw a bee buzzing in a flower.

The bee was buzzing around, but the little girl was too sad to follow it. Instead, she yawned and lay down in the sun.

After a while, the little girl began to feel better. She watched the bee and soon the boredom melted away. She smiled.

The bee helped the little girl to feel happy again. She thanked it for making her day better and waved goodbye as it flew away.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Tim. He was three years old and he liked to explore the world around him.

One day he was on a walk and he saw a cabin. He thought it looked so strange and it made him hurry to take a closer look.

When he got to the cabin, he was so surprised. It was terrible! It was full of cobwebs and the windows were broken. Tim was scared, but he was also curious to see what was inside. He decided to stay and take a look.

When he opened the door, he saw a big scary man. Tim was so scared that he ran away and he ran as fast as he could. He was so scared and he couldn't help but hurry home.

When Tim got home, he told his mom all about it. She was so glad that Tim was safe and that was the end of his terrible adventure!

Jim was a very curious three year old, who always asked lots of questions. His mum had alerted him to be careful not to touch the ashtray in the living room.

"Why not, mum," Jim asked.

"Because it's very hot," she answered.

Jim decided he would mail the ashtray to make sure it was safe. He carefully put it in a box, wrote an address on it and gave it to the postman.

The next day when he woke up, he was so excited. He ran to the mailbox, opened it and found a bigger box with a mild smell. Jim knew it must be the ashtray!

He brought it inside, showed it to his mum and hugged it. It was the best way he ever thought of to keep the ashtray safe.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy called Tom. He was very naughty and loved to have adventures. He often wanted to escape from his parents who chased him when he was naughty.

One day, he decided to try and escape them. He decided to make a fake plan. He wanted to spend the day roaming around in the park and running away from his parents. So, he pretended to go to bed but instead, he crept out of the house and ran to the park.

Tom spent the whole day playing and running around. He thought it was so much fun! He pretended to be an explorer and imagined he could escape from the park and explore the world.

Eventually, the evening came and Tom's parents had finally found him. Tom was quite sad to say goodbye to his pretend adventures but he was also glad to be back home. His parents gave him a hug and he knew that they would never let him escape again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in his backyard. One day, he found a colorful ball. He was so happy to have found it.

Timmy's mom called him inside for lunch. She made him a sandwich and gave him a glass of milk. "Mommy, can I bury my ball in the backyard?" Timmy asked.

His mom said, "Why do you want to bury your ball?"

Timmy replied, "I want to bury it so I can find it later and play with it again."

His mom smiled and said, "Okay, but make sure you remember where you bury it." So, Timmy went outside and buried his colorful ball in the backyard. He couldn't wait to dig it up and play with it again.

One day, a frog was hopping around a pond. It was a pretty frog, with bright green skin and a yellow belly. Suddenly, the frog heard a sound coming from the forest. The frog thought, "What is that noise?"

The frog hopped towards the forest. As he got closer, the frog started to worry. But he was curious and wanted to see what it was.

When he reached the edge of the forest, the frog saw a big, scary bear. The frog jumped in surprise and tried to run away. But the bear was too fast and caught the frog in its claws.

The bear growled and said, "I'm gonna eat you for dinner!"

The frog was so scared he couldn't move. After a few seconds, it was all over. The pretty frog was never seen again.

The story of the brave little frog, who ventured into the unknown despite his worries, ended with a bad ending. But it only goes to show that no matter how curious you are, sometimes things don't turn out the way you expect.

Once upon a time there was a boy with two buckets. One bucket was full of sand and the other was empty. He wanted to play a game with his friends and began to share the sand. He was happy and released it from the bucket into the air.

His friend was jealous because his bucket was empty. The boy said, "Don't be jealous! You can have some of my sand too!" He gave his friend a big scoop of sand, and their faces lit up with excitement.

The two boys enjoyed releasing the sand into the air and watching it sprinkle on them. They laughed and smiled as they took turns scooping and releasing the sand. The friends were joyous as they enjoyed their simple playtime.

"We better keep some sand to play with another day!" the boy said. So they put the rest of the sand back in the bucket and waved goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk outside and feel the ground beneath her feet. One day, she saw a big hill that was very high. She wanted to climb it and see what was at the top.

Lily started to walk up the hill, but it was very steep. She had to be careful not to fall down. As she got higher and higher, she could see more and more of the world around her. The trees looked very small and the houses looked like tiny toys.

Finally, Lily reached the top of the hill. She was so happy! She could see everything from up there. She felt like she was on top of the world. After a while, she started to walk back down the hill. She was tired but very proud of herself for climbing so high.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was walking in the park with her mommy. It was a rainy day and there were many puddles on the ground. Lily loved to jump in them and splash water everywhere. Suddenly, she saw a shiny penny in one of the puddles.

"Mommy, look! I found a penny!" Lily said, pointing at the puddle.

Her mommy smiled and said, "You're so lucky! Let's pick it up."

As they bent down to pick up the penny, a frog appeared out of nowhere and hopped into the puddle.

"Ribbit, ribbit!" the frog said.

Lily giggled and said, "Hi froggy! You're in my puddle!"

The frog hopped away and Lily and her mommy continued their walk, feeling happy and lucky to have found a penny and met a friendly frog.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she found a bird with a broken wing. Lily felt sad for the bird and wanted to help it. She took the bird home and gave it some water and seeds to eat.

Her nosy neighbor, Mrs. Brown, saw Lily taking care of the bird and asked what was going on. Lily told her about the bird's broken wing and how she was trying to help it. Mrs. Brown said that Lily was very kind and that she should be careful not to spoil the bird too much.

Lily didn't understand what Mrs. Brown meant by "spoil", but she knew that she wanted to help the bird. She decided to write a word on a piece of paper that said "get well soon" and put it next to the bird's cage. The bird chirped happily when it saw the word and Lily knew that she had done something good.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy orange. He just wanted to turn and be happy, but he could not figure out how. One day he saw a little boy who offered to help. The little boy was only three years old but was very wise. He said to the orange, "You have to turn yourself. Believe in yourself and you can do it!" The orange was happy and he tried to turn himself. He tried and tried, but he just couldn't find the strength. Then the little boy put the orange on the ground. He said, "Now, turn!" The orange was surprised when he suddenly spun and rolled away. He was so happy that he had turned himself. The orange thanked the little boy for showing him the way. He was no longer grumpy and was now free to spin and turn wherever he wanted.

Maddy was a poor little girl, who lived all by herself. She was very sad and lonely, so she would sit outside in the garden all alone. She was always looking for something to comfort her and make her feel better. One day, she saw something very special in the sky. It was a rainbow with all the colors of the world. Seeing the colors made Maddy feel so happy and comforted, as if someone was giving her a hug. From then on, Maddy tried to find something special and colorful every day to give her comfort. She would pick a flower, watch the birds fly, or just look at the sky and feel better. Maddy was so much happier now that she knew she was never alone.

Anna liked to play in the garden with her doll, Lily. She liked to pick daisies and make them into a necklace for Lily. She would tie the stems together with a knot and put the necklace around Lily's neck. She thought Lily looked very pretty with the daisies.

One day, it was raining and Anna could not go outside. She was miserable. She wanted to play with the daisies and Lily, but they were wet and muddy. She looked out of the window and saw the daisies drooping in the rain. She felt sad for them.

She asked her mom if she could go outside, but her mom said no. She said it was too cold and wet and Anna would catch a cold. She told Anna to play with her other toys in her room. Anna did not want to play with her other toys. She only wanted to play with the daisies and Lily.

She went to her room and sat on her bed. She hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. We can't play with the daisies today. They are wet and sad. Maybe tomorrow the sun will come out and we can play again."

She looked at Lily's necklace and saw that it was falling apart. The stems were breaking and the petals were falling off. She tried to tie them back together, but they were too wet and slippery. She cried and said, "Oh, Lily, your necklace is ruined. The daisies are ruined. Everything is ruined."

She lay down on her bed and closed her eyes. She wished the rain would stop and the daisies would grow back. She wished she could play in the garden with Lily and make her a new necklace. She wished she was not miserable.

One day, Mama and Mama's friend, Michelle, decided to go for a walk together. Mama was introducing Michelle to all of their neighbours.

Lila and Lulu stopped pulling. They looked at Molly. They felt sad. They had hurt their doll. They had hurt each other.

"I'm sorry, Lulu," Lila said. "I didn't mean to rip Molly's dress."

"I'm sorry, Lila," Lulu said. "I didn't mean to be mean to you."

They hugged each other. They hugged Molly. They said they loved each other. They loved Molly.

Once upon a time there was a patient sailor. He sailed around the world on a boat and saw all kinds of exciting things and animals.
One day, the sailor decided to bake some cookies and he got the ingredients ready. He mixed the dough and put it in the oven to bake.
The sailor waited patiently and when the cookies were done, he took them out of the oven and put them on a plate. The delicious smell made him smile and he took a bite of one of the cookies. It was so yummy that the sailor wanted to share them with his friends.
So he took them on his boat and went around the world to all of his friends. He shared the cookies with everyone and everyone was so happy.
The happy sailor was glad that he decided to bake!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to climb trees, but he was too short to reach the branches. One day, he found an axe in the shed and decided to use it to chop down a tree.

"Timmy, what are you doing with that axe?" asked his mom.

"I'm going to chop down a tree so I can climb it," Timmy replied politely.

His mom explained that chopping down trees was dangerous and that he could hurt himself. She suggested that he ask his dad for help instead.

Later that day, Timmy's dad helped him climb a tall tree in the backyard. Timmy was so happy that he thanked his dad politely. From that day on, Timmy never used the axe to chop down trees again.

The girl was surprised and looked all around. Then she spotted an animal up in a tree! It was a baby squirrel in a big nest. The squirrel had gotten stuck and couldn't get down.
