The girl smiled and was happy she had helped. She learned a valuable lesson that day - that if you help others, you can make them happy.

THE WATER OF LIFE

Long before you or I were born, there reigned, in a country a great way

off, a king who had three sons. This king once fell very ill--so ill

that nobody thought he could live. His sons were very much grieved

at their father's sickness; and as they were walking together very

mournfully in the garden of the palace, a little old man met them and

asked what was the matter. They told him that their father was very ill,

and that they were afraid nothing could save him. 'I know what would,'

said the little old man; 'it is the Water of Life. If he could have a

draught of it he would be well again; but it is very hard to get.' Then

the eldest son said, 'I will soon find it': and he went to the sick

king, and begged that he might go in search of the Water of Life, as

it was the only thing that could save him. 'No,' said the king. 'I had

rather die than place you in such great danger as you must meet with in

your journey.' But he begged so hard that the king let him go; and the

prince thought to himself, 'If I bring my father this water, he will

make me sole heir to his kingdom.'

Then he set out: and when he had gone on his way some time he came to a

deep valley, overhung with rocks and woods; and as he looked around, he

saw standing above him on one of the rocks a little ugly dwarf, with a

sugarloaf cap and a scarlet cloak; and the dwarf called to him and said,

'Prince, whither so fast?' 'What is that to thee, you ugly imp?' said

the prince haughtily, and rode on.

But the dwarf was enraged at his behaviour, and laid a fairy spell

of ill-luck upon him; so that as he rode on the mountain pass became

narrower and narrower, and at last the way was so straitened that he

could not go to step forward: and when he thought to have turned his

horse round and go back the way he came, he heard a loud laugh ringing

round him, and found that the path was closed behind him, so that he was

shut in all round. He next tried to get off his horse and make his way

on foot, but again the laugh rang in his ears, and he found himself

unable to move a step, and thus he was forced to abide spellbound.

Meantime the old king was lingering on in daily hope of his son's

return, till at last the second son said, 'Father, I will go in search

of the Water of Life.' For he thought to himself, 'My brother is surely

dead, and the kingdom will fall to me if I find the water.' The king was

at first very unwilling to let him go, but at last yielded to his wish.

So he set out and followed the same road which his brother had done,

and met with the same elf, who stopped him at the same spot in the

mountains, saying, as before, 'Prince, prince, whither so fast?' 'Mind

your own affairs, busybody!' said the prince scornfully, and rode on.

But the dwarf put the same spell upon him as he put on his elder

brother, and he, too, was at last obliged to take up his abode in the

heart of the mountains. Thus it is with proud silly people, who think

themselves above everyone else, and are too proud to ask or take advice.

When the second prince had thus been gone a long time, the youngest son

said he would go and search for the Water of Life, and trusted he should

soon be able to make his father well again. So he set out, and the dwarf

met him too at the same spot in the valley, among the mountains, and

said, 'Prince, whither so fast?' And the prince said, 'I am going in

search of the Water of Life, because my father is ill, and like to die:

can you help me? Pray be kind, and aid me if you can!' 'Do you know

where it is to be found?' asked the dwarf. 'No,' said the prince, 'I do

not. Pray tell me if you know.' 'Then as you have spoken to me kindly,

and are wise enough to seek for advice, I will tell you how and where to

go. The water you seek springs from a well in an enchanted castle; and,

that you may be able to reach it in safety, I will give you an iron wand

and two little loaves of bread; strike the iron door of the castle three

times with the wand, and it will open: two hungry lions will be lying

down inside gaping for their prey, but if you throw them the bread they

will let you pass; then hasten on to the well, and take some of the

Water of Life before the clock strikes twelve; for if you tarry longer

the door will shut upon you for ever.'

Then the prince thanked his little friend with the scarlet cloak for his

friendly aid, and took the wand and the bread, and went travelling on

and on, over sea and over land, till he came to his journey's end, and

found everything to be as the dwarf had told him. The door flew open at

the third stroke of the wand, and when the lions were quieted he went on

through the castle and came at length to a beautiful hall. Around it he

saw several knights sitting in a trance; then he pulled off their rings

and put them on his own fingers. In another room he saw on a table a

sword and a loaf of bread, which he also took. Further on he came to a

room where a beautiful young lady sat upon a couch; and she welcomed him

joyfully, and said, if he would set her free from the spell that bound

her, the kingdom should be his, if he would come back in a year and

marry her. Then she told him that the well that held the Water of Life

was in the palace gardens; and bade him make haste, and draw what he

wanted before the clock struck twelve.

He walked on; and as he walked through beautiful gardens he came to a

delightful shady spot in which stood a couch; and he thought to himself,

as he felt tired, that he would rest himself for a while, and gaze on

the lovely scenes around him. So he laid himself down, and sleep

fell upon him unawares, so that he did not wake up till the clock was

striking a quarter to twelve. Then he sprang from the couch dreadfully

frightened, ran to the well, filled a cup that was standing by him full

of water, and hastened to get away in time. Just as he was going out of

the iron door it struck twelve, and the door fell so quickly upon him

that it snapped off a piece of his heel.

When he found himself safe, he was overjoyed to think that he had got

the Water of Life; and as he was going on his way homewards, he passed

by the little dwarf, who, when he saw the sword and the loaf, said, 'You

have made a noble prize; with the sword you can at a blow slay whole

armies, and the bread will never fail you.' Then the prince thought

to himself, 'I cannot go home to my father without my brothers'; so he

said, 'My dear friend, cannot you tell me where my two brothers are, who

set out in search of the Water of Life before me, and never came back?'

'I have shut them up by a charm between two mountains,' said the dwarf,

'because they were proud and ill-behaved, and scorned to ask advice.'

The prince begged so hard for his brothers, that the dwarf at last set

them free, though unwillingly, saying, 'Beware of them, for they have

bad hearts.' Their brother, however, was greatly rejoiced to see them,

and told them all that had happened to him; how he had found the Water

of Life, and had taken a cup full of it; and how he had set a beautiful

princess free from a spell that bound her; and how she had engaged to

wait a whole year, and then to marry him, and to give him the kingdom.

Then they all three rode on together, and on their way home came to a

country that was laid waste by war and a dreadful famine, so that it was

feared all must die for want. But the prince gave the king of the land

the bread, and all his kingdom ate of it. And he lent the king the

wonderful sword, and he slew the enemy's army with it; and thus the

kingdom was once more in peace and plenty. In the same manner he

befriended two other countries through which they passed on their way.

When they came to the sea, they got into a ship and during their voyage

the two eldest said to themselves, 'Our brother has got the water which

we could not find, therefore our father will forsake us and give him the

kingdom, which is our right'; so they were full of envy and revenge, and

agreed together how they could ruin him. Then they waited till he was

fast asleep, and poured the Water of Life out of the cup, and took it

for themselves, giving him bitter sea-water instead.

When they came to their journey's end, the youngest son brought his cup

to the sick king, that he might drink and be healed. Scarcely, however,

had he tasted the bitter sea-water when he became worse even than he was

before; and then both the elder sons came in, and blamed the youngest

for what they had done; and said that he wanted to poison their father,

but that they had found the Water of Life, and had brought it with them.

He no sooner began to drink of what they brought him, than he felt his

sickness leave him, and was as strong and well as in his younger days.

Then they went to their brother, and laughed at him, and said, 'Well,

brother, you found the Water of Life, did you? You have had the trouble

and we shall have the reward. Pray, with all your cleverness, why did

not you manage to keep your eyes open? Next year one of us will take

away your beautiful princess, if you do not take care. You had better

say nothing about this to our father, for he does not believe a word you

say; and if you tell tales, you shall lose your life into the bargain:

but be quiet, and we will let you off.'

The old king was still very angry with his youngest son, and thought

that he really meant to have taken away his life; so he called his court

together, and asked what should be done, and all agreed that he ought to

be put to death. The prince knew nothing of what was going on, till one

day, when the king's chief huntsmen went a-hunting with him, and they

were alone in the wood together, the huntsman looked so sorrowful that

the prince said, 'My friend, what is the matter with you?' 'I cannot and

dare not tell you,' said he. But the prince begged very hard, and said,

'Only tell me what it is, and do not think I shall be angry, for I will

forgive you.' 'Alas!' said the huntsman; 'the king has ordered me to

shoot you.' The prince started at this, and said, 'Let me live, and I

will change dresses with you; you shall take my royal coat to show to my

father, and do you give me your shabby one.' 'With all my heart,' said

the huntsman; 'I am sure I shall be glad to save you, for I could not

have shot you.' Then he took the prince's coat, and gave him the shabby

one, and went away through the wood.

Some time after, three grand embassies came to the old king's court,

with rich gifts of gold and precious stones for his youngest son; now

all these were sent from the three kings to whom he had lent his sword

and loaf of bread, in order to rid them of their enemy and feed their

people. This touched the old king's heart, and he thought his son might

still be guiltless, and said to his court, 'O that my son were still

alive! how it grieves me that I had him killed!' 'He is still alive,'

said the huntsman; 'and I am glad that I had pity on him, but let him

go in peace, and brought home his royal coat.' At this the king was

overwhelmed with joy, and made it known throughout all his kingdom, that

if his son would come back to his court he would forgive him.

Meanwhile the princess was eagerly waiting till her deliverer should

come back; and had a road made leading up to her palace all of shining

gold; and told her courtiers that whoever came on horseback, and rode

straight up to the gate upon it, was her true lover; and that they must

let him in: but whoever rode on one side of it, they must be sure was

not the right one; and that they must send him away at once.

The time soon came, when the eldest brother thought that he would make

haste to go to the princess, and say that he was the one who had set

her free, and that he should have her for his wife, and the kingdom with

her. As he came before the palace and saw the golden road, he stopped to

look at it, and he thought to himself, 'It is a pity to ride upon this

beautiful road'; so he turned aside and rode on the right-hand side of

it. But when he came to the gate, the guards, who had seen the road

he took, said to him, he could not be what he said he was, and must go

about his business.

The second prince set out soon afterwards on the same errand; and when

he came to the golden road, and his horse had set one foot upon it,

he stopped to look at it, and thought it very beautiful, and said to

himself, 'What a pity it is that anything should tread here!' Then he

too turned aside and rode on the left side of it. But when he came to

the gate the guards said he was not the true prince, and that he too

must go away about his business; and away he went.

Now when the full year was come round, the third brother left the forest

in which he had lain hid for fear of his father's anger, and set out in

search of his betrothed bride. So he journeyed on, thinking of her all

the way, and rode so quickly that he did not even see what the road was

made of, but went with his horse straight over it; and as he came to the

gate it flew open, and the princess welcomed him with joy, and said

he was her deliverer, and should now be her husband and lord of the

kingdom. When the first joy at their meeting was over, the princess told

him she had heard of his father having forgiven him, and of his wish to

have him home again: so, before his wedding with the princess, he went

to visit his father, taking her with him. Then he told him everything;

how his brothers had cheated and robbed him, and yet that he had borne

all those wrongs for the love of his father. And the old king was very

angry, and wanted to punish his wicked sons; but they made their escape,

and got into a ship and sailed away over the wide sea, and where they

went to nobody knew and nobody cared.

And now the old king gathered together his court, and asked all his

kingdom to come and celebrate the wedding of his son and the princess.

And young and old, noble and squire, gentle and simple, came at once

on the summons; and among the rest came the friendly dwarf, with the

sugarloaf hat, and a new scarlet cloak.

And the wedding was held, and the merry bells run.

And all the good people they danced and they sung,

And feasted and frolick'd I can't tell how long.

Lily liked to watch the screen with her mom. The screen showed funny animals and people who made her laugh. Sometimes, her mom would tell her the names of the animals and what they were doing. Lily learned a lot from the screen. She was a very intelligent girl.

One day, Lily's dad came home early from work. He was tired and wanted to rest. He went to the bedroom and closed the door. Lily and her mom kept watching the screen in the living room. They did not make much noise, but they did not know that the screen was loud.

Lily's dad heard the screen from the bedroom. He could not sleep. He was angry. He got up and opened the door. He walked to the living room and saw Lily and her mom on the couch. He said in a loud voice, "Can you please turn off the screen? You are disturbing me. I need to sleep."

Lily and her mom were surprised. They did not mean to disturb Lily's dad. They felt sorry for him. They turned off the screen and said, "We are sorry, dad. We did not know you were sleeping. We will be quiet now."

Lily's dad felt bad for being rude. He said, "It's okay, I'm sorry too. I had a hard day at work. I love you both. How about we watch the screen together later, after I take a nap?"

Lily and her mom smiled. They said, "We love you too, dad. That sounds like a good idea. Have a nice nap."

Lily's dad went back to the bedroom and closed the door. He fell asleep quickly. Lily and her mom cuddled on the couch and waited for him to wake up. They were a happy family.

Mrs. Smith was walking down the road with her three year old daughter, Shannon. As the wind blew around them, Shannon grew chilly and started to shiver. Mrs. Smith grabbed her scarf from her coat pocket and wrapped it around her daughter tightly.

Shannon smiled, happy to have the warmth, and the two kept on walking. After a few moments, they arrived at their destination. It was a big field with lots of toys in organized sections. Shannon squealed with joy and ran forward, eager to start playing. Mrs. Smith followed closely behind her with a big smile!

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. They lived near a big river. The river was very pretty and had lots of fish in it. The family loved to go for walks by the river and watch the fish swim.

One day, the family went for a walk but they forgot to close the gate. Their dog saw the open gate and ran away. The family was very worried and looked for the dog everywhere.

After a while, the dog returned! He had been playing by the river and chasing the fish. The family was very happy to see him again. They hugged him and promised to always remember to close the gate. From then on, they never forgot to close it again.

Once upon a time there was a mighty puddle. It was so big and wet, it could not be ignored. One day, a 3 year old girl named Alice wanted to examine the puddle. She stood right in front of it, with her toes almost touching the edge.

"Look at this!" she said with a smile on her face.

Alice's mom walked over to her, "Don't get too close to the puddle, honey. What do you want to do with it?".

Alice grinned, "I wanna play in it! Can I?"

Mom shook her head, "No, not today. But you can examine it and see what it looks like."

Alice squatted down. She looked closely at the water, the dirt and all the tiny things floating in it. Up close, the puddle looked even mightier.

Alice stood up again and said, "It's so big and fun! Can I play in it next time?"

Mom smiled. "Maybe, if it's still here!"

Once upon a time, there lived a young boy named Jake. Jake had an incredible dream: he wanted to succeed at being the best bus driver in the world.

One day, Jake decided to make his dream come true. He got dressed, packed up his bag and hopped on the bus.

When Jake saw the bus, he became so excited! He had never seen a bus so big and shiny before. He smiled and said, "I'm going to do it! I'm going to be the best bus driver ever!"

He took the bus for a ride. It was incredible! He drove on roads and took curve with ease. He drove fast and slow. People around town started calling him the best bus driver in the world.

Finally, after a lot of hard work, Jake succeeded in being the best bus driver in the world! He was filled with joy and kept on driving the bus with a big smile on his face.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and blocks. One day, they hear a loud noise outside. They run to the window and see a big truck.

"Wow, look at that truck!" Tim says. "It has many colors and shapes on it."

"What is it doing?" Sam asks. "It is stopping at the park."

"Let's go see!" Tim says. He grabs his coat and hat. Sam does the same. They run to the door and open it. They see other kids running to the park too.

At the park, they see the truck open its back. Inside, there are many toys and books and balloons. A man comes out of the truck and smiles.

"Hello, kids!" he says. "This is a special event. We are giving away these things for free. You can choose one thing each. Have fun!"

Tim and Sam are very happy. They run to the truck and look at the things. They see cars and blocks and dolls and puzzles and more.

"This is so cool!" Tim says. "What do you want, Sam?"

"I want a car," Sam says. "A red one, like yours."

"I want a book," Tim says. "A book with animals, like this one."

They pick their things and say thank you to the man. They go back to their house and play with their new things. They are very happy. They think the truck is very cool. They hope it will come again.

Once upon a time there was a girl who went on a wild adventure. She had a weird rag with her and it was her best friend. One day, she went deep into the forest and came across a strange creature. The creature was so weird that the girl was scared. The creature said, "Will you feed me?"

The girl was unsure what to do. She thought about the rag she had with her. She slowly took the rag out of her pocket and offered it to the creature. To her surprise, the creature was so happy! It said, "Thank you for feeding me", before it disappeared back into the forest.

The girl was glad she had her rag with her. From then on, she always kept it with her on all of her adventures. She learned that it's better to be kind to creatures, no matter how weird they may look!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Zigzag. Zigzag loved to run and play in the park. One day, Zigzag saw a big twisty slide. He wanted to try it, so he ran up to the slide.

Zigzag twisted and turned as he went down the slide. He went so fast that he fell off at the end. He felt embarrassed because all his friends saw him fall. But his friends did not laugh at him. They ran to help Zigzag get up.

Zigzag's friends told him not to be embarrassed. They all tried the twisty slide, too. They all twisted and turned, just like Zigzag. They had so much fun playing together. And Zigzag learned that it's okay to make mistakes, as long as you have good friends by your side.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there was a gifted bird named Blue. Blue could sing very pretty songs. One day, Blue met a tall giraffe named Spot. Spot had a very long neck.

Blue said to Spot, "Can I sit on your long neck? I want to gain a better view of the forest." Spot nodded and let Blue sit on his neck. From up high, Blue saw a big red fruit on a tree. Blue knew it was a yummy fruit.

Blue thanked Spot and flew to get the fruit. Blue shared the yummy fruit with Spot. They became good friends and had many fun days in the big green forest.

Once upon a time there was a bird. He wanted to make a home. But he couldn't decide where it should go. He flew high, he flew far, he flew round and round in circles. He looked here, he looked there, but still he couldn't find the perfect place.

Suddenly he heard a sound. It was a baby bird. It was in a nest up near the top of a tall tree. The bird was troubled and alone. Feeling sad, the bird flew to the nest. He saw the baby bird, and he felt sorry. He wished he could take away the baby's troubles.

The big bird wanted to stay and help the baby bird, so he made a nest nearby. He was happy to be helping, but soon he started to regret it. Every day the nest needed more repairs, and it took a lot of time and effort.

But the bird was glad he had done it. Even though it was troublesome, he was glad he had helped the baby bird. Every day he would fly to the nest and make sure the baby was safe and sound. He was happy to take care of the baby bird, and he was thankful that he had offered his help when it was needed.

Lily liked to play with clay. She could make many things with clay. She could make balls, snakes, stars, and flowers. She liked to show her clay things to her mom and dad. They always said, "Good job, Lily!"

One day, Lily wanted to make a clay house. She had a big piece of clay. She rolled it and flattened it and cut it. She made four walls and a roof. She put them together with more clay. She made a door and a window. She was very happy with her clay house.

She wanted to show her clay house to her mom and dad. She picked it up carefully and walked to the living room. But on the way, she tripped on a toy. She fell down and dropped her clay house. It broke into many pieces. Lily was very upset. She cried and cried.

Her mom and dad heard her cry. They came to see what happened. They saw the broken clay house and the toy. They hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily. We're sorry your clay house broke. We know you worked hard on it. But you can make another one. You can succeed again. We love you, Lily."

Lily stopped crying. She looked at her mom and dad. She felt better. She said, "Thank you, mom and dad. I love you, too. I will make another clay house. And I will be careful with the toy." She smiled and hugged them back. She picked up the clay pieces and went back to her room. She was ready to try again.

Molly was looking for something to do. She zipped around the garden, getting dirtier and dirtier. Suddenly, she noticed a little bee. It was zooming above her head, buzzing loudly.

Molly chased the bee. She wanted to play with it. She ran faster and faster until all of a sudden she slipped on a big, muddy puddle. She lay there, gasping for breath, completely filthy.

The bee flew close to Molly's face and said, "Do not be sad, little one. Just have a little zip and you will be happy."

Molly laughed, stood up, and went back to zooming around the garden. She had lots of fun playing with her new little friend the bee.

The end.

Once upon a time there lived a shy little girl named Denise. Denise loved adventures and playing outside. One day Denise went to the beach and asked her mom if she could swim in the ocean. Her mom said to be careful, because there might be a hurricane coming.

Denise's mom was worried, but Denise wasn't scared. She felt like she could do anything. So Denise kept playing and swimming in the ocean.

After a while her mom noticed there was a storm coming. She yelled for Denise to come back and get out of the water. But Denise wanted to keep swimming. She wanted to prove that storms couldn't stop her.

Suddenly the scariness of the hurricane came closer and the waves were getting bigger and bigger. Denise was so frightened that she started to cry.

Her mom ran to Denise and said, "Honey, you were so brave, but you should always listen to me so you don't get hurt. You can be brave, but still be careful."

Denise hugged her mom and felt relieved. She had learned a very important lesson that day â€" you can be brave, but it's important to listen to the advice of others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around outside. One day, her mom asked her to clean her room upstairs.

Lily didn't want to clean her room. She wanted to play instead. But her mom told her it was important to keep her room tidy. Lily tried to resist, but her mom was firm.

Lily went upstairs and saw her messy room. She didn't want to clean it, but she knew she had to. So, she put on some music and started to tidy up. As she worked, she found her favorite stuffed animal and hugged it tightly. It was so comfortable in her arms.

When Lily was finished, she went downstairs to show her mom. "Look, Mommy! I cleaned my room!" she said proudly. Her mom smiled and gave her a big hug. "Good job, Lily! Your room looks great!"

Once upon a time, there was a big bird in the sky. The bird flapped its wings and flew all around. One day, it flew over a family. The family was very happy and they sang a song. The bird liked it so much that it flew past them again and again.

The family thought that the bird liked their song and they allowed the bird to listen. Every day, the bird flew by and listened to the family's song. Each time, the bird became happier.

One day, the family decided to no longer allow the big bird to listen. The bird was very sad and flew away.

The moral of the story is that it's important to share our joy with others. Allowing people to enjoy the good things we do can bring us and them a lot of happiness.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy whip. He liked to play with his whip every day. But sometimes, he felt helpless because he did not know how to use it well.

One day, Tim met a kind man. The man saw Tim with his whip and wanted to help him. He said, "I can teach you how to improve and use your whip better." Tim was happy and said, "Yes, please!"

The kind man showed Tim how to hold the whip and move it. Tim practiced and practiced. Soon, he was not helpless anymore. He knew how to use his whip very well. Tim was happy and thanked the kind man. And from that day on, Tim played with his whip and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride the bus to see new places. One day, Timmy got on the bus and saw a strange bag. He asked the bus driver, "What is in the bag?" The bus driver replied, "I don't know. It's unknown to me."

Timmy was curious about the bag, so he asked the bus driver if he could do something about it. The bus driver said yes, and Timmy went to check the bag. Inside the bag, Timmy found a toy car. He was so happy and showed it to the bus driver. The bus driver was happy too and said, "That's great! Now we know what was in the unknown bag."

From that day on, Timmy always looked for unknown things on the bus. He loved to do things to help the bus driver, like picking up trash or holding the door open for others. Timmy loved the bus and all the adventures it brought him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and singing songs. One day, she saw a trumpet in her toy box. She was so excited to try it out!

Lily picked up the trumpet and blew into it. It made a loud noise that made her giggle. Her mom heard the noise and came to see what was happening. "Wow, Lily! You're playing the trumpet!" her mom said.

Lily smiled and replied, "Yes, I'm trying to play it. It's so much fun!" Her mom was happy to see Lily so excited and they both danced to the music Lily made with her trumpet. From that day on, Lily played her trumpet every day and she became very good at it.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a little hut. In this hut, a man would sell incredible things. People from all over would come to see what he had.

One day, a little boy named Tim came to the hut. He wanted to buy something incredible for his mom's birthday. The man showed Tim many things, but Tim wanted something very special.

Finally, the man showed Tim a beautiful flower that would never die. Tim knew this was the perfect gift for his mom. He bought the flower and gave it to his mom. She loved it and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lily. She was very excited because today was her birthday. She ran outside to go play in the park.

As she walked, she noticed something sparkly in the grass. She bent down to take a look and saw a beautiful icy jewel! She was so surprised.

Lily picked up the jewel and admired its beauty. She ran back home to show her mom what she had found.

When her mom saw the jewel she said, â€œMy goodness! It looks like a very special gift. Let's keep it safe.â€

So Lily put the icy jewel in her drawer and she was very excited to show it to her friends.

The end.

Once, there was a farmer who had to make a long journey. To make sure he was ready for the adventure, he packed his bag. He put in food, clothes and more. He even packed a shovel - it was deep and heavy!

The farmer began his journey and walked a very long way. He crossed rivers, walked through a deep forest and climbed a mountain. Finally, he arrived at his destination.

The farmer was so happy he had packed all the things he needed. Without them, he wouldn't have been able to complete his journey! He looked deep into the horizon and grinned. His adventure had officially begun.

Mommy took me to a special hill. There were lots of rocks all around us. I could see the sun shining bright above us.

"Let's have a picnic!" she said.

We spread out a blanket and put out some food. It was yummy!

The sun was mild, so I asked Mommy if I could explore the hill. She said yes and I set off.

I found a huge rock that was the perfect size. I wanted to move it, but it was too heavy.

Then I remembered that my mommy had brought a blanket to cover the rock. So I ran to get it, and with Mommy's help, together we covered the rock so that it looked like a big furry animal.

I was so happy. We had created something special.
Mommy said, "Let's sit here and look at our work."

I smiled and said, "Yes! Let's cover more rocks!"

Ben and Lily were adventurous twins who liked to explore new places. One day, they found a big suitcase in the attic. It was old and dusty, but it had a shiny buckle on it.

"Let's open it and see what's inside!" Ben said.

"Okay, but be careful. It might be locked or have something scary in it." Lily said.

They tried to pull the buckle, but it was too hard. They pushed and twisted it, but it did not move.

"I don't understand. How do we open it?" Ben asked.

"Maybe we need a key or a code or something." Lily said.

They looked around the attic for clues, but they did not find anything. They were about to give up, when they heard a voice.

"Hello, children. Do you want to play a game?" The voice came from the suitcase.

Ben and Lily were surprised and curious. They went closer to the suitcase and saw a small speaker on it.

"Who are you? Where are you?" Ben asked.

"I am the suitcase. I have been waiting for someone to open me for a long time. I have many secrets and treasures inside, but you have to solve a riddle to unlock me." The voice said.

"A riddle? What is a riddle?" Lily asked.

"A riddle is a question that has a clever or funny answer. If you guess the answer, you can open the buckle. If you don't, you can try again later. Do you want to try?" The voice said.

Ben and Lily nodded. They liked games and puzzles. They wanted to see what was inside the suitcase.

"Okay, here is the riddle. Listen carefully. What has a face and two hands, but no arms or legs?" The voice said.

Ben and Lily thought hard. They looked at each other and whispered.

"Is it a clock?" Ben said.

"Or a watch?" Lily said.

They decided to say both answers, just in case.

"A clock or a watch!" They shouted together.

The voice laughed.

"Very good, children. You are smart and adventurous. You guessed the riddle. You can open the buckle now. Go ahead and see what I have for you." The voice said.

Ben and Lily were excited. They pulled the buckle again, and this time it opened. They lifted the lid of the suitcase and saw a lot of colorful things inside. There were books and toys and clothes and pictures and more.

"Wow, look at all this stuff!" Ben said.

"It's amazing! It's like a treasure chest!" Lily said.

They started to take out the things and play with them. They found a storybook about pirates and a teddy bear with a patch and a dress with sparkles and a camera with a flash and more.

They thanked the voice and the suitcase for the game and the gifts. They had a lot of fun and learned new things. They decided to keep the suitcase as their secret friend and visit it often. They were happy and adventurous twins.

Once upon a time there was a troubled boy. He didn't have any friends because he was always too sad and quiet.

One day the boy decided he needed to do something. So he took out his spoon and started digging and digging in the ground.

Then something strange happened. He dug right through the ground and ended up in a secret, underground world! This new world was filled with wonderful things he had never seen before and it made him very happy.

When he wanted to go home he used his spoon to make a hole in ground and climbed out. He had a smile on his face as he walked back to his house.

The boy never forgot his special adventure and he was no longer troubled. He had a secret all of his own that he could tell nobody about. And it made him feel better every time he thought about it. The end.

Once there was a bear named Larry. One day Larry wanted to go on an adventure, so he decided to jog. He was feeling very grateful because it was such a beautiful day! Larry jogged and jogged until he spotted something in the sky. It was a jet! He had never seen a jet before and he was very excited.

Larry waved to the jet as it flew over. The pilot of the jet could see him and smiled. The pilot waved back to Larry and flew away. Larry felt so grateful that he got to see the jet.

He kept jogging and visited all kinds of places. Everywhere he went, he had the most amazing adventures. Whenever he thought about the jet, he felt so grateful. He thanked the pilot for making his day so special.

Once upon a time, two siblings, Jimmy and Amanda, were playing in the park. Jimmy was loading a rock into a truck, while Amanda was running around and making the prettiest of flowers with a piece of paper. Suddenly, Jimmy noticed a big pile of smelly trash near the fence and he called his sister Amanda.

â€œAmanda! Look at this,â€ he shouted, pointing at the pile of trash, â€œit's disgusting!"

Amanda put her hand over her nose and said, â€œEeeew! What happened here? Let's clean this up!â€

Jimmy and Amanda got to work and, one by one, they loaded the trash into a big bin, keeping their knee close to the ground.

When the park was finally clean, both siblings felt great. They had worked together and taught each other the importance of taking care of the environment.

The moral of the story is that when you work together, getting rid of anything disgusting can be easy. So it's always better to have a friend or family by your side!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was walking down a path. She came across a surprise, a pretty, shiny jewel! The girl was so excited and asked, "What is it?"

The jewel started to move and spoke to the girl. It said, "I am a magical jewel and will grant you three wishes!"

The girl was amazed and asked, "Can I keep you?" The jewel revealed that it wanted to stay with the girl forever.

The girl embraced the jewel and said, "I wish we could be best friends forever!"

The jewel smiled and said, "Your wish is granted!" The girl was so happy that she now had a magical jewel friend who was always with her.

From that day on, the little girl and the jewel were always together. Everywhere the girl went, the pretty jewel went too. They were the best of friends forever!

Once upon a time, there lived two friends. They were very excited to have a dance party.

So, they went to a big house. It was an unusual house because it had lots of colorful decorations everywhere.

They put on their dancing shoes and began to dance. They twirled, jumped and spun around the house. They danced to the music that came out of the windows.

They didn't want it to end, but it was time to go home. So they said goodbye to the unusual house and left with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a rhinoceros named Rosie. Rosie loved to bounce up and down all day long. She would bounce on the soft grass and make her friends giggle.

One day, Rosie met a little bird who was sad. "Why are you sad, little bird?" Rosie asked. The bird said, "I tried to eat a spicy bug, but it was too hot for me." Rosie thought hard, then she had an idea. "Let's go find a sweet bug for you to eat instead!"

So, Rosie and the little bird went on a hunt for a sweet bug. They looked under leaves and on tree branches. Finally, they found a sweet bug for the little bird to eat. The bird was so happy and thanked Rosie.

From that day on, Rosie and the little bird became best friends. They learned that helping others can make you happy too. And Rosie kept on bouncing, making everyone in the forest laugh and smile.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and eat snacks. One day, they go to Lily's house after school. Lily's mom gives them tuna sandwiches and apple juice. They are happy and say thank you.

They take their sandwiches and juice to Lily's room. They see many toys on the floor. They see dolls, cars, blocks, and books. They want to play with everything. They forget about their sandwiches and juice. They leave them on the table.

They play for a long time. They make stories with the dolls and cars. They build towers with the blocks. They look at the pictures in the books. They have fun and laugh.

Then, they hear a noise. They turn around and see Lily's cat. The cat is on the table. The cat is eating their sandwiches and juice. The cat likes tuna. The cat does not like apple juice. The cat spills the juice on the floor.

Lily and Tom are surprised. They say, "Oh no! The cat ate our sandwiches and juice! We forgot to eat them! We were too busy playing!"

Lily's mom hears them. She comes to Lily's room. She sees the cat, the sandwiches, the juice, and the mess. She is not angry. She is kind. She says, "Don't worry, kids. It's okay. The cat was hungry too. I can make you more sandwiches and juice. But first, let's clean up the mess together."

Lily and Tom say, "Okay, mom. We are sorry. We will help you. And we will remember to eat our sandwiches and juice next time."

They clean up the mess with Lily's mom. They wash their hands. They eat their new sandwiches and juice. They are full and happy. They thank Lily's mom. They hug the cat. The cat purrs. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big dream. It was so big, it filled up a whole page! The dream was so amazing, it made everyone smile. They couldn't wait to make the dream come true.

The dream was so big and grand, it seemed impossible. But everyone worked hard and believed in the dream. Soon, it started to come true! Every day, it was getting bigger and better.

Finally, the dream was real! Everyone cheered and celebrated the big dream. It was the best day ever. They looked at the big page and smiled, knowing the dream was now real.

They had made their big dream come true.

There once was a very big zoo. In the zoo, there were many animals and birds. One day, two children, John and Jane, went to the zoo.

John was only three, but he was very brave. He followed Jane down a path and eventually they came to a big elephant. John was amazed.

Jane smiled at John and said, "Do you want to pet it?"

John nodded and with a trembling hand, he put his hand on the elephant's trunk. It was very soft and the elephant made a happy noise. John's face lit up with joy.

John and Jane continued their trip down the path. Everywhere John went, he was in awe of what he saw! At the end of their trip, the two of them had seen the biggest animals they had ever seen!

Once upon a time there was a group of chubby puppies. They were playing in the garden when one of them noticed something strange.

The puppy said "Wow! This flower is shrinking!"

The rest of the group came over to see and sure enough, the flower was getting smaller and smaller.

The puppies started to get scared. What could be causing the flower to shrink?

Suddenly, a wizard came out of the bushes and said "I'm using my shrinking potion. When I splash it on things, they shrink!"

The puppies were relieved and they started to laugh. They all thought the wizard was funny.

The wizard said "I'm glad you find it funny. Now, if you promise not to touch my potion again, I'll give you each a treat!"

The puppies cheered and promised. The wizard splashed his potion on the flower and it was back to its original size. Everyone was happy and the wizard gave each puppy a chubby treat for looking after the flower.

Sam and his aunt were playing hide and seek. Sam loved to play hide and seek with his aunt and would often try to hide in the same spot because he liked it so much.

Aunt: "Sam! Ready or not, here I come!"

Sam laughed and quickly scrambled to a regular spot, behind the big armchair. He hugged himself tightly and waited for his aunt to count to ten.

Aunt: "10! I'm coming to find you now, Sam!"

Sam giggled as he heard his aunt's voice, but he stayed really still. He wanted to win the game and be the first one to find her. Suddenly, he heard a noise and peered around the corner of the armchair. His aunt was looking under the bed!

Sam: "You found me!"

Aunt: "Yes! I found you, Sam!"

Sam smiled and hugged his aunt. He had won the game and was proud of himself. They hugged and laughed together, happy to be playing their regular game of hide and seek.

Nana and Grandpa were on a walk. Grandpa wanted to buy a gift for Nana from a special shop. But Nana disagreed. Grandpa thought the gifts from the shop were so charming that Nana would love them. But she still disagreed.

Grandpa asked Nana why she didn't like the shop. She said the prices were too high. Grandpa said the prices were really not that high and he asked her to just take a look at the shop.

But Nana said no. She said she thought it was better to buy gifts from another shop. Grandpa said, "But I think this shop has the best gifts in town!"

Nana smiled and said, "I know, but I still think the prices are too high. Maybe we can try another shop."

Grandpa thought for a moment and then said, "Ok, we can do that. Come on, let's go!"

And they went off in search of the perfect gift that they both agreed on.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally loved to explore, so she went on fun adventures every day.

One day, Sally was exploring a trail in the woods when she stopped in front of a big tree. At the base of the tree was an old metal box with a buckle. Sally was curious so she opened the buckle and looked inside the box.

Inside the box, Sally found something that looked harmless. She reached inside and grabbed it. It turned out to be a shiny tool that she could use to work.

Sally was very excited and couldn't wait to use the tool. She used it to build things and transform the world around her. She was very proud of the hard work she had done.

But Sally soon realized that wherever she had gotten the tool, it was not a harmless thing. In fact, it had been lying in wait for her, and now it was doing a different kind of work.

So Sally quickly put the tool back in the box with the buckle and hid it away under the tree. She knew that she needed to be careful when exploring, and she never wanted to come across the mysterious tool again.

Timmy was excited. He had a special surprise waiting for him at school today. His mom had told him he was going to see something "very fun" in his classroom.

When he arrived, Timmy saw that someone was in the room. He saw a big, gray box in the corner.

"Mom, who is that?" asked Timmy.

"That is a surprise for you, sweetheart," said his mom. "See what he is selling?"

Timmy looked closer at the box and saw that inside was a toy. He was so excited. The toy was gray, too!

"Can I buy it, mommy?" asked Timmy.

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course you can."

Timmy knew right away that his new gray toy was the best surprise ever. He couldn't wait to show it off to his friends in the classroom.

Once upon a time, there was a big garden. In the garden, there were many pretty flowers and yummy fruits. A graceful butterfly lived in the garden too. The butterfly liked to fly around and look at all the colors.

One day, a little boy came to the garden. He saw the butterfly and said, "Hi, butterfly! You are very pretty." The butterfly was happy and said, "Thank you, little boy! I like your garden."

The little boy wanted to play with the butterfly. He tried to grab it, but the butterfly was too fast. The butterfly said, "I am sorry, little boy. I cannot let you grab me. But we can still play in the garden together." The little boy was happy, and they played all day.

Mandy was feeling lucky. She was with her family and they were going to park their car. She watched as her mom and dad put coins in the parking meter. "We will be here for a few hours", said Mandy's mom.

Mandy started to explore the park. She saw some birds and butterflies flying around. She also noticed the mailman delivering the mail. "Good morning mailman!" said Mandy.

The mailman smiled and said, "Good morning Mandy. It's a lovely day to be in the park. You look very lucky!"

Mandy felt very lucky. She went on a few rides and played a few games with her family. As they left, Mandy was so happy she couldn't stop smiling. "I had such a lucky day at the park!" she said.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. One day, her mom asked her to go to the park and play. Lily was very happy and ran to the park.

At the park, Lily saw a wide tree. She went to the tree and saw a faucet. She turned the faucet and water came out. Lily was thirsty, so she drank some water. Then, she saw a little boy who was also thirsty. Lily said, "Hi, I am Lily. Let's be friends!" The little boy smiled and said, "Hi, I am Tom. Nice to meet you!" They both drank water and played together.

Lily and Tom played and had fun all day. They learned that it is good to share and help others. When they went home, they told their moms and dads about their new friend. Lily and Tom were happy because they learned that sharing and helping others makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big blackboard. It was very tall and perfect. Every day, the blackboard moved from one room to the other. Everyone was so excited to see the blackboard move.

One day, something special happened. A little 3 year old boy saw the blackboard and he was amazed. He loved the blackboard so much that he wanted to move it by himself. He grabbed the blackboard and started to move it away.

The little boy was so proud of himself because he could move the big blackboard. Everyone clapped and cheered for him. They were all so happy to see him do something so perfect.

The little boy couldn't believe that he did something so amazing! He promised himself that he would always remember how perfect it felt to move the blackboard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to play the piano. She had a little piano at home and she practiced every day. But she didn't like to listen to her mommy and daddy when they told her to practice more. She thought she was already good enough.

One day, there was a big piano competition in town. The little girl wanted to join, but her parents knew she wasn't ready yet. They told her she needed to improve her skills before she could join. But the little girl didn't listen and joined the competition anyway.

During the competition, the little girl played the piano, but she made many mistakes. She didn't win and felt very sad. Her parents told her that it was okay to lose, but she should have listened to them and practiced more. The little girl learned that it's important to listen to your parents and improve your skills before trying new things.

Once upon a time, there was a princess. She was very bossy and always told everyone what to do. One day, she decided she wanted to bake a cake. She told her helpers to get all the ingredients and mix them together. They followed her orders and baked the cake. When it was done, the princess tasted it and it was delicious! She shared it with all her friends and they all loved it. From then on, the princess wasn't as bossy and learned that everyone can work together to make something yummy. The end.

Molly and Mom went to were there were two big baskets. Mom said they were full of laundry. Mom combed Molly's hair and tied it back with a bow. Then Molly watched in amazement as Mom tied all the laundry up in big bundles.

Mom carried the bundles outside and tried to hang them on a line, but the wind was blowing too hard. Molly ran to help but it was too late - the laundry had fallen on the ground.

Molly felt hurt inside because she wanted to help, but she didn't know what else to do. But then Mom smiled, and showed her how to tie the laundry to the line with a knot. Molly worked hard, and soon all the laundry was tied up safely on the line.

Molly felt proud as she watched Mom fluff up the laundry on the line. Now it was ready for the wind to make it nice and clean.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went on a walk with her parent and they came across a big hill.

Lily said, "I want to climb the hill, but it looks too steep. What should I do?"

Her parent said, "I recommend that we take it slow and steady. We can hold hands and help each other up."

Lily thought that was a smart idea and they started to climb the hill together. As they reached the top, Lily felt proud of herself for making it all the way up with her smart parent by her side.

One day, Hannah was walking outside when she noticed it was getting very cold. She began to shiver and knew she needed to find warmth.

She noticed a jug of water nearby and decided to pick it up and bring it with her. The jug was cold to the touch and made her shiver even more.

As she walked, she saw a cozy-looking cottage with smoke coming out of the chimney. She knocked on the door and a friendly lady answered.

"Hello, are you cold?" the lady asked. Hannah nodded and handed her the cold jug.

The nice lady smiled and said, "Come in, my dear. Let me warm you up!"

Hannah was so happy that she got to go inside the warm cottage and stay warm. She said her thank yous and the lady said, "You're welcome, dear. Stay as long as you need to."

Hannah curled up in a chair and was cozy and warm for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sally. She was three years old and loved discovering new things.

One day, Sally went for a walk with her mom. As they walked, Sally spotted a magnet in a puddle. The magnet was wet. Sally wanted to pick it up but her mom said, "No Sally, it might scare you!"

But Sally was brave and she said, "I'm not scared! I want to pick it up!"

Her mom said, "I won't let you pick it up, it's a silly thing to do. It's safe to admire it from far away".

Sally thought for a moment and then agreed. So, Sally and her mom watched the magnet from afar and then carried on with their walk.

One day, a little duck named Tim went on an adventurous walk. He loved to splash in the water and play with his friends. The sun was shining and the sky was blue. Tim was very happy.

Tim splashed in a big puddle and laughed. His friends came to play too. They all splashed and had fun. After a while, they were tired and wanted to take a nap.

Tim and his friends found a nice, soft spot under a tree. They took a cozy nap together. When they woke up, they felt refreshed and ready for more splashing fun.

Once upon a time there was a big promise made to a three year old. She was promised a surprise if she weighed the same each day.

She was really excited and couldnâ€™t wait to see what her surprise was, so she weighed herself each morning.

One day, she jumped onto the scale and noticed that she weighed more than the day before. She was a little scared to look at her surprise and stepped off the scale.

Her mom was there to reassure her.

â€œItâ€™s ok, honeyâ€, she said. â€œIt doesnâ€™t matter if the numbers change a little. I promised you a surprise and I still want to give it to you.â€

The little girl smiled, stepped back onto the scale, and weighed herself. And when she finished, she got the surprise she had been waiting for - a big, delicious ice cream cone!

Once there was a brave girl named Jasmine. She was very competitive and loved to explore. One day she went for a walk in the woods. There she saw a very special mushroom. She had never seen an orange mushroom before.

Jasmine decided to protect the mushroom so that no one could take it away. She put a big rock on top of it to keep it safe. After that Jasmine looked around to make sure everything was alright.

Jasmine went back to the mushroom many times and she always watched over it to protect it. She even stayed up late to make sure no one disturbed the mushroom. She was determined to keep it safe.

Jasmine became friends with the mushroom and enjoyed playing around it. She was proud of her job to protect the mushroom. Eventually it was time to say goodbye to the mushroom and continue on her journey. Overall, Jasmine was happy that she could protect the mushroom.

Once upon a time there was a young boy who was very proud of his family. Every morning he would go down to the market to get a bag of rice for his family. He would go home, proud of himself for being able to get the rice for his family.

One day the boy went to the market, but the shopkeeper would not permit him to buy the rice. The shopkeeper said he was too young and could not buy it himself. The boy begged and pleaded with the shopkeeper, but he refused to let him buy the rice.

The boy was very sad and disappointed. He realized that being proud is not always enough, and that sometimes it is important to follow the rules, even if it is not what we want to do.

The boy went home that day, feeling less proud and not with the bag of rice he had set out for. He knew that he would have to try another way to get the rice for his family.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the park. They found a tasty pill on the ground. The cat wanted to eat it, but the dog wanted it too. They did not know what to do.

They sat down to discuss who should get the pill. The cat said, "I saw it first, so I should eat it." The dog said, "But I am bigger and need it more." They both wanted the pill very much.

Then, a big bird came down from the sky. The bird took the tasty pill away. The cat and the dog were sad. They learned that they should share things and not fight.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat spicy food, but her mommy always said it was too hot for her little tummy. One day, Lily and her mommy went to the train station to visit her grandma. They got on the train and found a seat.

Lily was excited to eat her favorite spicy chips on the train, but her mommy said no. "You know spicy food makes your tummy hurt," she said. "Let's wait until we get to grandma's house and settle in."

Lily was disappointed, but she listened to her mommy. As they rode the train, they saw a man with a big bag. Lily wondered what was inside. Suddenly, the man's bag fell and spilled all over the floor. It was full of spicy chips! The man was upset and didn't know what to do.

Lily remembered what her mommy said about settling in first, so she offered to help the man clean up his chips. He was grateful and even gave Lily a bag of her own to eat when they got to grandma's house. Lily was happy and her tummy didn't hurt because she waited to settle in before eating her spicy chips.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore his house and find new things to play with. One day, he found a knob on his bedroom door. He turned it and the door opened.

Timmy's mom saw him playing with the knob and said, "Timmy, be serious. You shouldn't play with the door knob. It's not a toy."

Timmy let go of the knob and said, "Okay, Mommy. I won't play with it anymore."

Later that day, Timmy's friend came over to play. Timmy showed him the knob on his door and said, "Look! This is the knob that opens my door. But my mommy said I can't play with it."

His friend said, "Let's play with something else. We can build a tower with these blocks."

Timmy agreed and they had fun building a tower together. From that day on, Timmy never played with the door knob again.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to sit under a big tree near his house. One day, while he was sitting, he saw a girl named Sue. Sue was very careful with her toys.

Tim and Sue became friends and decided to play together. They had many toys, like cars and dolls. They thought it would be fun to trade their toys with each other. Tim gave Sue a red car, and Sue gave Tim a pretty doll.

They played for hours, being careful not to break their new toys. They were so happy that they decided to trade toys every week. Tim and Sue learned that sharing and being careful with their things made them the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She liked pink. Pink was her favorite color. One day, the girl went to the park. She saw a butterfly. The butterfly was pink. The girl wanted to catch it, but her mom said, "mind the butterfly, it needs to fly." So the girl let the butterfly go. The end.

Once upon a time there lived a grumpy dragon named Fluffy. He lived in a cozy cave by the sea and never enjoyed company. One day, a small girl named Ashley stumbled into Fluffy's cave. Ashley was only three years old, but she had heard the stories of the dragon's magic powers.

"Please, dragon Fluffy," Ashley said, "Please show me your magic!"

Fluffy just ignored her. He kept on snoozing in the corner and refused to show Ashley his magic.

Ashley got really sad. She started to cry and begged Fluffy to show her his powers. But no matter what she said or did, the grumpy dragon just ignored her.

Finally, Ashley made the dragon an offer she couldnâ€™t refuse. She promised to bring Fluffy a delicious snack each day if he would just show her some magic.
