Once upon a time, there was a sunflower that was all alone. It was white and empty and it felt sad.

The sunflower wanted a friend, so it started to look around. Then it saw a caterpillar and the sunflower smiled.

The caterpillar was grey and fuzzy. They were so happy to see each other, they became best friends.

Every day they did fun things together. They jumped, they raced and they even sang songs.

But then one day the caterpillar started to rot. The sunflower was so sad to see its friend getting smaller, but it stayed and watched over it until all the rot was gone.

And when the sunflower opened its eyes, it saw that the caterpillar had turned into a beautiful butterfly with white wings.

The sunflower and the butterfly were so happy to be together again, they flew off into the sky to explore the world.

Timmy was so excited - he was going to ride his bike up the hill. He hopped onto his bike and peddled up the hill with excitement.

But halfway up the hill, he started to worry. "I'm so alone! What if I can't get to the top?", he thought. He stopped peddling and just sat there.

Suddenly he heard a voice. "Hey, don't worry! I'm right here." It was his mom. She had run up the hill after him "I'm not going to let you go alone," she smiled.

Timmy felt so relieved and happy. His mom had come to make sure he was safe! He hopped back on his bike and, with his mom walking next to him, finished going up the hill.

At the top of the hill, Timmy and his mom both cheered. His mom threw her arms around him and said "Nobody has to feel lonely when I'm around".

Then, with a smile, Timmy started to peddle back down the hill. Now he was not worried - he was with his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat. The boat had a big anchor. One day, the boat arrived at a beautiful beach. The boat saw many other boats playing together. The boat felt jealous because it wanted to play too.

One small boat saw the big boat and said, "Hi, big boat! Why are you sad?" The big boat replied, "I am jealous. I want to play with you and the other boats." The small boat smiled and said, "Come play with us! We will have fun together."

The big boat was happy and played with the small boat and the other boats. They all had a great time. The big boat was not jealous anymore. It was happy to have new friends to play with. And they all lived happily ever after.

Nick wanted to ride his bike. He was excited and put on his helmet. Nick was careful when he pedaled down the street. He went faster and smiled with delight.

But then he rode past a big dog. The dog barked loudly and scared Nick. He peddled faster and didn't look back.

When Nick got home he regreted not being more careful. He was so fast that he didn't get to pet the friendly dog. He promised to be more careful next time.

Nick carefully hopped off his bike and put away his helmet. He vowed to pay more attention when he was riding his bike. Nick was determined to be careful and have fun at the same time.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play together. They had many toys, but Lily's favorite was a big doll with long hair and a pink dress. Ben liked the doll too, but he had a car that made noises and lights.

One day, Lily's mom made rice for lunch. She gave Lily and Ben each a bowl and a spoon. "Eat well, children," she said. "Rice is good for you."

Lily and Ben started to eat, but Ben was not very hungry. He looked at Lily's doll and wanted to play with it. He put his spoon down and reached for the doll. "Can I have your doll, Lily?" he asked.

Lily was not happy. She loved her doll and did not want to share it. She held the doll tightly and said, "No, Ben. This is my doll. You have your car."

Ben felt jealous. He thought Lily's doll was better than his car. He tried to grab the doll from Lily, but Lily pulled it back. They started to fight over the doll. They did not hear Lily's mom coming back to the kitchen.

Lily's mom saw them fighting and was angry. She recognized the doll as a gift from Lily's grandma. She took the doll from them and said, "Stop it, both of you. Fighting is not nice. You should share your toys and be kind to each other."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They did not want to make Lily's mom angry. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We won't fight again."

Lily's mom smiled and said, "That's good. Now finish your rice and then you can play nicely. And remember, the doll and the car are both special. You can take turns and enjoy them together."

Lily and Ben nodded and ate their rice. They learned their lesson and decided to be better friends. They played with the doll and the car and had fun. They were not jealous anymore.

Once there was a girl named Piper. She was only 3 years old, but she loved tasks. No matter how small or big the task seemed, Piper was there to fill it.

One day, Piper decided to go for a walk. She stopped to admire the flowers and saw a task no one had filled before. The task looked different from all the other tasks Piper had seen before.

Piper bravely decided to fill the task, no matter the size or difficulty. But the task was too big for her to fill alone. So instead of trying to do it on her own, Piper asked her parents and friends to help.

Soon, all the different tasks were finished. Piper's parents and friends were very proud of her. Together they had learned an important lesson: no task is too big when you ask for help.

Once upon a time there was a mom and a dad. The mom was in the kitchen, prepare dinner. She had made a big pot of soup.

The dad was in the living room. He was so careful to not make a mess. He was looking out the window and saw a bird outside. He called the mom over. "Come look fast! There's a bird outside the window!"

The mom came and saw the bird. They watched it for a minute. Then, the bird flew away.

Suddenly, the mom and dad heard a noise. It sounded like it was coming from the bedroom. They went in and saw that the bedroom door was open. It was their daughter! She had been careless and had opened the bedroom door.

The mom and dad were so surprised. They hadn't thought she was awake.

The mom smiled and hugged her daughter. "Now it's time to prepare for bed, sweetie. Come on, let's go get ready.â€

Once upon a time there was an old lady who lived in a big, white house. She had a big garden with lots of tasty, ripe fruit.

One day a small, furry creature came to her door. The old lady said hello and the creature said it was very hungry.

The old lady smiled and said, "My name is Grandma, what is yours?"

The small creature said, "My name is Toto. Can you please provide me some food?"

Grandma said, "Of course I can! Let's pick some of my white pear and fresh apples to share."

And so Toto and Grandma enjoyed a feast of white pears and red apples. They had so much fun sharing stories and eating together.

Grandma said, "You are always welcome here Toto!"

Toto thanked Grandma and promised to come back soon.

Once upon a time, there was a brave sailor who wanted to unite the world. He wanted everyone to get along. But it was hard. The sailor took a long journey across the sea. He got on his tall ship, full of hope and determination.

He encountered lots of storms along his way. But with each one, he stayed strong and kept going. He wanted to find peace for everyone. He wanted everyone to come together and be friends.

Finally, after a long, hard journey, the sailor arrived at his destination. Everyone he met was able to unite and be kind to one another. They all shared the same goal now. The sailor felt proud that he was able to bring people together.

The end!

Johnny and his mom were in the park. Johnny skipped around the pathways, scanning for interesting things. He discovered a tiny bug, just a few centimeters long. He was very excited and picked it up carefully. As he watched it, the bug began to shrink! Johnny was amazed and asked his mom to explain.

"The bug isn't really shrinking, Johnny," his mom said. "It's playing a trick on you. That's called camouflaging. It's shrinking its body to look like other things around it and protect itself."

"It's kind of like when I have to hide behind the couch," Johnny said.

His mom laughed. "Exactly," she replied. "Animals are so clever. You have to be careful around them. We have to show them value and respect."

Johnny looked at the bug intently. He was full of admiration and respect. "Okay," he said. "I promise to be careful."

Today, Jake and Anny were playing in the garden. Jake had a rough toy train that he liked to push around. Suddenly, when they weren't looking, the toy train vanished! Jake and Anny were very surprised. They looked all around and couldn't find the train anywhere. They asked mum, but she said she didn't know what had happened to it.

Jake and Anny decided to look for the train. They searched high and low and still couldn't find it. They looked inside the shed, around the trees, and all over the garden, but it was nowhere to be seen. They were so disapointed.

Suddenly they heard a noise coming from the sky. They looked up and saw the train flying above them! It was circling around in the sky. Anny laughed and clapped her hands. Jake shouted for excitement. Then, the toy train vanished and flew away.

They said goodbye to their train and waved. Jake and Anny looked at each other with a big smile, and knew that their toy train was having an adventure in the sky. What an exciting day!

Anna loves pandas. She has a big panda toy that she hugs every night. She calls him Pandy. Pandy is soft and black and white. He has a smile on his face.

One day, Anna goes to the zoo with her mom and dad. She is very excited. She wants to see the real pandas. She runs to the panda enclosure. She sees two pandas eating bamboo. They are lazy and slow. They do not look at Anna.

"Mom, why are the pandas not playing?" Anna asks.

"They are not playing because they are full and tired," Mom says. "They like to rest after eating. They are patient animals. They wait for the right time to play."

Anna nods. She understands. She is patient too. She waits for the pandas to finish eating. She hopes they will play soon.

She sees a third panda in the corner. He is smaller than the others. He is not eating. He is looking at Anna. He has a curious expression. He walks towards Anna. He stops at the fence. He reaches out his paw.

Anna is surprised. She smiles. She reaches out her hand. She touches the panda's paw. It is warm and fuzzy. The panda makes a soft noise. He sounds happy.

"Hi, panda," Anna says. "Do you want to play with me?"

The panda nods. He shakes his paw. He wants to play. He looks at Pandy. He likes Pandy. He thinks Pandy is his friend.

Anna laughs. She gives Pandy to the panda. The panda hugs Pandy. He shakes Pandy gently. He makes Pandy dance. He makes Pandy smile.

Anna claps. She is happy. She has made a new friend. She thinks the panda is patient and kind. She thinks the panda is fun. She thinks the panda is the best.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She left the house early one morning to go visit her favorite vendor in town. When she arrived all she found was an empty market with no sign of her beloved vendor. She was so sad and a tear ran down her cheek.

Just then Jane heard a voice call out to her. "Where did you think I was little one?"

Jane looked up and saw her vendor standing right there. She ran up to him and hugged him tight. "I missed you!" she said.

The vendor hugged her back and said, "I've been working really hard to make the market better, so I had to leave for a while. I'm glad you came back to see me!"

Jane and the vendor shared a hug and Jane said goodbye. She went home feeling happy that she had found her beloved vendor again.

Susie was playing at the beach. She picked up a shell and held it in her hand. She could feel how smooth and hard it was and it looked so pretty. She thought it would be a great toy to play with.

Susie carried the shell around the beach and stopped to look at all the other shells. She put her shell down and paused to look around. She saw a healthy looking seagull flying around in the bright blue sky.

Susie decided to take her shell and explore the other parts of the beach. She wanted to find more shells like the one she was holding. She looked and looked and eventually found another shell, but this one was bigger than the one she already had!

Susie smiled as she looked around the beach. She had a lot of healthy shells to play with now. She was so happy that she decided to stay a bit longer and enjoy her new shells.

Once there was a little boy named Josh. He was three years old and he loved to explore the world. He loved to follow the birds, explore the garden and run around in the park.

One day, Josh saw a brown rabbit. He wanted to follow the rabbit and see where it went. So he slowly walked after the rabbit, being careful not to scare it away. The rabbit hopped away until it came to a burrow in the ground.

Josh wanted to give the rabbit a name, so he called out, "Hello, Mr Brown Rabbit!" He smiled as he said the name and the rabbit turned around and hopped off, disappearing into the burrow. Josh laughed and waved goodbye to his new friend.

Josh followed the rabbit's tracks back home, where he told his parents all about his adventure. His parents were so proud of him - Josh had made a new friend and seen what amazing things he could find when he followed his curiosity.

Once there was a brave jeep. He was an old jeep and had been around for many years. One day he decided he wanted to have an adventure! He drove off into the night.

Everywhere he looked, he could see animals and stars in the sky. After a while he came across a big hill. He wanted to climb the hill but it was too steep. He tried and tried but he couldn't make it to the top.

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. It was a group of brave soldiers in a jeep coming up the hill! The jeep was very strong and brave. He knew he would never be able to beat the jeep. So, he decided to surrender and let them drive up the hill.

The jeep and the soldiers climbed to the top of the hill. The jeep was very proud. He was no match for the brave jeep and the soldiers. He had surrendered but he learned what it meant to be brave.

Once there was a lonely foot. He didn't have any friends and he was very sad. Every day he went to the park but no one wanted to play with him.

One day, while he was in the park, he heard a voice. It said "I need help! Can you solve my problem?" The foot couldn't believe it, someone wanted his help!

The foot looked around but he couldn't see anyone so he called out "Where are you?"

Then he looked up and saw a bird high up in the tree. The bird was stuck in some sticky sap and it couldn't get down.

The foot laughed and said "I know how to solve that problem!" He quickly ran and found some stones which he put around the tree. Then the foot climbed up the stones and rescued the bird.

The foot and the bird became good friends and now they go to the park together every day. The foot is no longer lonely, and he is so proud that he solved the bird's problem.

Tommy was playing in his room when his friend Sarah came to visit. Sarah was always so noisy and loud. Tommy asked, "Why are you so noisy?"

Sarah just laughed and said, "I am excited to see you!"

"Oh," said Tommy, not sure what to do.

Sarah said, "Let's go to bed now. We can sleep in my bed together."

Tommy was so happy to have a friend to sleep with, so he said, "Yes, let's go!"

The two friends had a wonderful time sleeping in Sarah's bed until morning. Tommy was so happy that he had a new and noisy friend like Sarah.

Lily liked to dance. She danced in her room, in the garden, and in the park. She made up her own dances. They were original and fun. She felt happy when she danced.

But her brother Ben did not like her dances. He liked to play with his cars and trucks. He did not like the music Lily played. He did not like the noise Lily made. He did not like the way Lily moved. He thought she was silly and weird.

One day, Lily was dancing in the living room. She had a new dance. It was about a butterfly. She wore a dress with wings. She spun and jumped and fluttered. She smiled and sang.

Ben was in his room. He was playing with his cars and trucks. He heard Lily's music. He heard Lily's noise. He heard Lily's voice. He felt angry and annoyed. He wanted Lily to stop. He went to the living room. He saw Lily's dance. He said, "Stop it, Lily! You are stupid and ugly! Your dance is dumb and boring! Go away!"

Lily felt sad and hurt. She liked her dance. She thought it was beautiful and fun. She did not want to stop. She said, "No, Ben! You are mean and rude! My dance is original and creative! I can dance if I want to!"

Ben and Lily started to fight. They yelled and pushed and pulled. They knocked over the lamp and the table. They made a big mess.

Mom heard the noise. She came to the living room. She saw Ben and Lily fighting. She saw the lamp and the table broken. She felt angry and disappointed. She said, "Stop it, Ben and Lily! You are naughty and bad! You have to share and be nice! Go to your rooms and shut the door!"

Ben and Lily stopped fighting. They felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "Sorry, Mom." They went to their rooms and shut the door. They did not dance or play. They sat on their beds and thought. They wished they had been kinder and happier. They wished they had not fought. They wished they could dance and play together.

Tim was feeling very nervous. He didn't like to talk in front of big crowds. Everyone was watching him and he felt scared. He just wanted to be alone and hide.

But Tim couldn't hide. He heard his mom calling him to talk in front of the crowd. He was so afraid that he started to cry. But he didn't want to look silly in front of everyone, so he wiped his tears away and slowly stepped forward.

He was shocked to see all the junk in the room. There were all sorts of broken toys and trash strewn about. He realized it was a junkyard, and he felt even more nervous. He wanted to go back home, but his mom was encouraging him forward.

He took a deep breath and slowly started to talk. At first it was hard, but soon the words were coming easier and he was no longer scared. He looked out over the crowd and he could tell they were listening.

When he was finished talking, there was a big cheer from the crowd. Tim couldn't believe it. He had done it and he was so proud. He looked back over the junkyard and smiled. He was no longer scared.

One day, Papa took Sally outside to play on the swings. Sally loved swinging high in the wind. She was swinging and smiling, but suddenly she got confused.

Papa said, "What's wrong Sally?".

Sally replied, "I don't like the wind."

Papa smiled and said, "Why don't we test it out and see if we can be friends?".

Sally agreed and climbed back onto the swing. This time, she watched the wind for a few moments before she started swinging again. She smiled and laughed, feeling like the wind was her friend.

The wind blew Sally higher and higher and she felt like she was flying. She was no longer confused, she was happy!

Once upon a time, there was a big gray elephant named Elly. Elly was sad because she thought she was ugly. She had big ears and a long nose, and she felt different from the other animals.

One day, a little bird named Benny flew to Elly. Benny saw that Elly was sad and asked, "Why are you sad, Elly?" Elly told Benny that she felt ugly and did not like her big ears and long nose. Benny looked at Elly and said, "I think you are not ugly. You are special."

Benny promised to show Elly how her big ears and long nose made her special. They went to the river, and Benny asked Elly to use her long nose to spray water on the dry plants. Elly did and the plants grew happy and green. Then, Benny asked Elly to use her big ears to fan the hot animals. Elly did, and all the animals felt cool and happy.

Elly learned that being different was not ugly. She was special and had her own way to help others. Elly and Benny became best friends, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a very hairy cat. The cat lived in a small house with a nice family. The family loved the cat very much. They played with the cat every day. The cat was very happy.

One day, the cat went outside to play. It was a sunny day. The cat saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. The cat climbed up and up. It was so high! The cat was scared.

The cat cried for help. The family could hear the cat. They came outside and saw the cat in the tree. The family called for the cat to come down. The cat was brave and climbed down. The family was so happy to have their hairy cat safe. They all lived happily ever after.

Cherie had a special bond with her daddy. Whenever Cherie was feeling lonely, she would urge her daddy to play with her. The two of them would have the best time with laughter, games and cuddles - until one day, daddy was no longer available.

"Where is daddy?", Cherie asked her mommy.

"He has gone away for a little while", mummy replied.

Cherie felt an urge to be with her daddy, but felt resigned that it was not possible. She knew that her daddy was special and always made her feel loved but she just wished he would come back to her.

Days passed, until one day, mummy told Cherie the exciting news - Daddy was back home! Cherie was so happy that he was once again available to her. She rushed to daddy and hugged him tight.

"Welcome home, Daddy!", Cherie said happily.

Once there was a little boy called Sam who was very excited about his first visit to the golf course. His Grandad had brought him to see all the amazing things he could do there.

Sam was shocked when he saw the size of the golf course. It seemed to stretch on forever, with all kinds of paths he had never seen before. But Grandad warned him that he must not go off exploring on his own.

So they stayed together, walking up and down the green paths and looking at all the different trees and plants. They watched some people playing golf and Grandad told Sam how it works.

When it was time to go home, Grandad warned Sam not to forget what they had learnt today so they can come back again soon. Sam nodded and smiled because he was very excited to come back soon and learn more about golf.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were walking in the woods when they saw a turkey.

â€œLetâ€™s get the turkey!" said Jack.

Jill was scared so she said, â€œNo. That turkey is too fast. We wonâ€™t be able to get it."

Jack didnâ€™t give up and said, â€œI can get the turkey if I run fast."

Jack ran fast, but the turkey ran faster. Then something amazing happened. Jack received help from a friendly animal! The animal ran after the turkey and caught it.

Jack was very happy and said, â€œThank you for helping me get the turkey.â€

The animal smiled and said, â€œYouâ€™re welcome. Now you can enjoy the turkey. Have a good day!â€

Jack and Jill received the turkey and ran home. They had a wonderful dinner that day and were very happy.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Grace. She was three years old and liked to dress up in fancy clothes.

One day, Grace put on a beautiful dress. As she looked in the mirror, she felt so happy.

But when she saw her friend, she felt envious. Her friend was wearing a party dress, too. It was more sparkly than Grace's. She wished she had a dress like that.

So, Grace took a deep breath and closed her eyes. She said a little prayer. She asked God to give her a dress like her friend's.

The next day, Grace was very excited. She opened her wardrobe and saw a beautiful dress in there. It was just like her friend's!

Grace smiled and thanked God for his kindness. From then on, she thanked him every day for all the blessings in her life.

One summer morning, a little boy named Andy was walking around outside. He saw a white rabbit in the grass and wanted to touch it. He walked over to the rabbit and reached out his hand, but he stopped just before he touched it. There were two green spiders crawling on the rabbit. He had never seen anything like this before, and he was scared! He stepped back and thought of a plan. He quietly reached inside his pocket and found some small stones. He threw the stones at the spiders and they ran away! He was so happy, he could touch the rabbit now. But then, the rabbit hopped away. Andy was a bit sad but quickly remembered he still got to touch the white rabbit. It was a special moment.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy called Andy. He was an adventurous boy and always liked trying new things. He was especially curious about the world around him.

One day, Andy went to the park with his mom. As he ran around, playing with the other kids, he saw a beautiful butterfly with purple and yellow wings. He watched in amazement as it flew away and shouted with joy.

His mom was so proud of him - she smiled and clapped! This made Andy feel so special. He looked up at her and smiled back with love.

The next day, Andy decided to go on an adventure and explore the park even more. As he ventured through the woods, he heard a loud noise. To his surprise, it was the same butterfly from the day before!

Andy was so happy that he wanted to thank the butterfly. He started to applaud and waved his hands in the air with excitement. The butterfly fluttered around him, enjoying the moment.

Andy's mom was filled with pride. He had been so adventurous that day and she was so proud of him. She said, "You make me so happy Andy!" And they hugged and filled each other with love.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Tilly who lived in a big white house surrounded by the lovely countryside. Tilly loved the morning, when the sun filled the morning sky. She walked around the house, entering each room to explore.

On one such Monday morning, Tilly stumbled upon a room with a old radio. She was intrigued by it, so she decided to try and switch it on. She pressed all the switches and pressed the big red button. The radio started to make a clear noise, as if it was calling out to her.

Tilly: "What is this?"

Mum: "It's called a radio, sweetie. You can listen to the news, different music and people talking."

Tilly was so excited to hear the radio; she loved the sound of all the different conversations coming from it. Every morning after that, Tilly would enter the room, turn on the radio and listen to it with her Mum.

At times, the radio noises seemed so clear, as if it was coming from some far away place. Together, mum and Tilly listened for hours, sharing stories and discovering things about each other. They might have been miles away from the radio, but it was like the stories came from their own home.

The end.

Alvin was excited as he was unpacking his suitcase. Inside, he found a big surprise - a toy boat! The boat was blue and had a funny flag on the top. Alvin couldn't wait to play with it. He grabbed it and ran to the nearest river.

He lined the boat up carefully and said goodbye as he watched the boat sail away. It went very far, until he couldn't see it anymore.

Soon, it was getting dark and Alvin was a little worried. He started to dream about his boat getting lost or stuck. Suddenly, he saw a light in the distance. He ran closer and noticed it was his boat!

Alvin was so happy he had found it. He rushed over and picked it up. But when he got closer, he noticed the back of it was wet. He looked around and saw it had been pushed onto some big rocks. He reached out and ran his finger along the side. He felt a deep cut.

Alvin was sad. He knew it was time to go home. He carefully packed the boat into his suitcase and walked back. Even though his boat was hurt, he knew he had a great adventure.

Once there was a little bird who wanted to win a race. All the other birds were ready and excited for the race, but the little bird was nervous. He just wanted to do his best and was hopeful for success.

The race began and the little bird flew with all his might. He felt happy and blew through the wind with joy. He worked very hard and was determined to win.

The little bird had almost made it across the finish line when he began to slip and fall behind. He looked sad and tired, but he did not give up! With one last burst of energy, the little bird flew over the finish line and won the race!

Everyone was so glad the little bird had won. Bird friends cheered and celebrated with him. The little bird was filled with accomplishment and joy. He had achieved success and was proud.

The little bird was glad he had won the race and happy he could make all his bird friends proud. It was a special moment he would never forget.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the park with their ball. One day, they see an elderly cat sitting on a bench. The cat is black and white and has a collar with a bell.

"Look, a cat!" Tom says. He runs to the cat and tries to pet it. The cat hisses and scratches Tom's hand. Tom cries and runs back to Sam.

"Bad cat!" Sam says. He is angry at the cat for hurting his brother. He picks up the ball and kicks it hard at the cat. The ball hits the cat on the head and makes a loud noise. The cat meows and jumps off the bench.

"Hey, stop that!" a voice says. It is an elderly lady who owns the cat. She walks to the bench and picks up the cat. She glares at Sam and Tom. "You should not kick my cat! He is old and sick. He does not like strangers. You should be nice to animals!"

Sam and Tom feel sorry for the cat and the lady. They did not know the cat was old and sick. They did not mean to hurt him.

"We are sorry, lady," Sam says. "We did not know. We like animals. We have a dog at home. He is friendly and likes to play."

The lady softens her look. She sees that Sam and Tom are not bad boys. They just made a mistake.

"It's okay, boys," she says. "But you should be careful with your ball. You could hurt someone or something. And you should always ask before you pet a cat. Some cats are shy or scared. They need time to trust you."

Sam and Tom nod. They understand. They apologize again to the lady and the cat. They promise to be more careful and respectful. The lady smiles and thanks them. She walks away with the cat in her arms. The cat looks at Sam and Tom and purrs. Sam and Tom wave goodbye and go back to playing with their ball. They are happy and have learned a lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a proud crane who lived by the lake. Every day, the crane would fly through the sky and enjoy the view.
One day, the crane noticed a small boat that had been abandoned. The boat was starting to rot. The crane felt sad to see such a beautiful boat in such a terrible state.
The crane turned to the sky and said, "I will have to fix this boat so no one else has to see it like this."
So the crane flapped his wings and flew from tree to tree, gathering wood and strong leaves. He worked hard to rebuild the boat until it was as strong as it was before.
The crane was proud of his work and stared proudly at the boat before taking off back to the lake.
He said to himself, "No one else has to see this boat rotted and in ruins. It's all fixed now!"

Once upon a time there was a cute little girl. Every day she would love to play and sing her favorite song. Her song was so catchy! Every day she would repeat her song over and over again, until it was almost dark.

One day, the little girl was walking around and singing her song when she met a big mean monster. He was so ugly and he growled at the little girl. He asked her to stop singing her song, but the little girl refused.

The monster got very angry and he grabbed the little girl. She was so scared that she started to cry. But the monster didn't care, he just held the girl tightly and refused to let her go.

The little girl never sang her song again. The monster kept her trapped and made sure that she never sang again. So the little girl never shared her cute song with the world again. This is why you should always be careful who you meet when you are out and about in the world.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emily. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her.

One day Emily was playing in her room and noticed a modern rug on the floor. She reached down to touch it and said, "What is this?"

Her mom replied, "It's a rug."

Emily asked, "What is a rug?"

Her mom said, "A rug is a special thing that makes your room cozy and warm."

Emily smiled and said, "I know! I can sit on it and be comfy!"

So Emily sat on the rug, feeling very cozy and happy. She didn't know it yet, but she now knew a lot more about rugs and the world around her.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey who lived in the jungle. The monkey was very wise and knew how to find the best bananas to eat. One day, the monkey saw a man walking through the jungle with a big bag. The man said he wanted to sell things to the animals in the jungle.

The monkey was curious and went to see what the man had to sell. But when he got closer, he saw that the man had traps in his bag! The monkey knew he had to warn the other animals in the jungle. He ran as fast as he could and told everyone about the man and his traps.

Thanks to the wise monkey, the animals in the jungle were safe and the man didn't sell anything that day. From then on, the animals were more careful and always looked out for each other.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to go on adventures. His mommy bought him a scooter to help him get around. On the first day, he was a bit weak and struggled to manage the scooter. But, after some practice, he got better and better. He got so good that he scooted all around the park. Everywhere he went, he felt so adventurous. He explored all of the paths, trees and rocks.

When he got tired, he would rest for a bit. He knew that he had to manage his energy so he could keep having fun. And he did! He managed his energy perfectly so he could play all day. He even managed to show off to his friends and pretend he knew how to do all sorts of tricks.

He quickly became a pro at scootering around the park. He was so proud of himself and his mommy was very proud too. He smiled as he scootered around, knowing he had managed to get really good at it.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Maya. She liked to pick flowers, but one day she made a mistake. She was picking a flower from the neighbor's garden when she got caught.

The neighbor was so angry and put Maya in jail. Maya was very scared and she had no idea what to do. She started to cry and told the jailer she was sorry for her mistake.

Then, the jailer had an idea. She was not too fond of the neighbor either and thought it was very stupid of him to put Maya in jail. So the jailer let Maya go and told her never to pick the neighbor's flowers again.

Maya thanked the jailer and vowed never to make that mistake again. From then on, she only picked flowers from her own garden.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bunny named Rosie. Rosie loved to play with her whistle. She would blow it all day long. One day, Rosie's mom said, "Rosie, you have blown your whistle too much. It's time to stop."

But Rosie didn't listen. She kept blowing her whistle. Then, her dad came in and said, "Rosie, you need to listen to your mom. If you don't stop blowing your whistle, we will have to punish you."

Rosie didn't want to be punished, so she stopped blowing her whistle. She felt sad, but she knew it was the right thing to do. From that day on, Rosie only blew her whistle when it was okay to do so.

Once upon a time, there was a wise march. It marched through the woods, keeping time with a soft beat. All around it, the sun shone and birds chirped.

The march went on and on, and as it did, its tummy began to rumble. It stopped for a rest and gave a big yawn. Then it looked around, taking in the beauty of the sunshine and the trees.

When it renewed its march forward, it felt more energized! It walked past flowers and bushes, taking it all in. It soon noticed an animal nearby and followed it until they reached a large body of water.

The march stopped at the edge of the water and watched as the animal drank. Then the march splashed into the water and took a long sip as well. Refreshed, it marched back out of the water and continued on its way, feeling happy and wise.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. The bird loved to fly high in the sky and feel the wind on its wings. One day, the bird saw a TV in a window. It was playing a show about other birds flying and soaring in the sky. The bird felt proud of its own flying skills and wanted to soar even higher.

The bird flew up and up, flapping its wings with all its might. It felt the wind pushing against it, but it kept going. Finally, the bird reached the clouds and soared even higher. From up there, it could see the whole town and all the other birds flying below. The bird felt very proud of itself for reaching such great heights.

As the sun began to set, the bird knew it was time to come back down. It flew back to its nest, feeling happy and content. From that day on, the bird soared higher and higher every time it flew. It never forgot the feeling of pride it had when it first saw the TV show about soaring birds.

One morning, a little boy woke up and looked out the window. It was incredibly interesting. The sunrise was a beautiful mix of blue and yellow.

He was so excited he couldn't wait for the day to start. He quickly got out of bed and put on his shoes.

The little boy was ready for the day, so he went outside. Suddenly, his friend came running up, shouting "Hi!"

The two boys smiled at each other and then started to separate. They wanted to explore different things in the garden.

The little boy was curious, so he wandered around, looking at the flowers and listening to the birds singing.

The sun was shining higher in the sky now and the little boy noticed a butterfly. He watched as it gracefully fluttered away, a reminder of the beauty of the sunrise.

He spent the morning happily exploring and when he got tired he returned to the house with a smile on his face. He had had an interesting morning.

One day, a girl named Sue went to her mom's kitchen. She saw her mom kneel down to get a cup. The cup was for coffee. Sue thought coffee was dull. She liked juice better.

Sue's mom said, "Sue, I have a surprise for you later." Sue was excited. She thought about the surprise all day.

In the afternoon, Sue's mom called her to the kitchen. There was a big, bright cup with a straw. Sue's mom said, "Here is your surprise, Sue! It's a new cup for your juice!" Sue was so happy. She knew her mom's coffee cup was dull, but her juice cup was the best.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who loved to hop. One day, he hopped to a big tree where all the animals were meeting. They were meeting to see who could hop the farthest.

The bunny was worried because he had never hopped in front of so many animals before. He saw a wise old owl sitting on a branch. The owl was the judge of the hopping game. The bunny asked the owl, "Can I hop too?"

The owl said, "Yes, little bunny, you can hop too." So, the bunny hopped as far as he could. All the animals clapped and cheered. The wise old owl, the judge, said, "You did a great job, little bunny! You hopped very far."

The bunny was very happy and not worried anymore. He knew that he could hop far and make new friends. From that day on, the bunny hopped and played with all the animals under the big tree. They all had lots of fun together.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. They want to go on the slide.

"Let's go on the slide!" Tom says.

"OK!" Sue says.

They run to the slide. But there is a problem. The slide is wet. It rained last night. The slide is slippery.

"Be careful!" Sue says.

"I am careful!" Tom says.

But Tom is not careful. He goes too fast. He slides down the slide. He does not stop. He hits the exit. He breaks the exit. He falls on the ground. He hurts his arm.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Tom cries.

Sue runs to Tom. She sees his arm. His arm is red. His arm is bad.

"Tom, are you OK?" Sue asks.

"No, I am not OK!" Tom says. "My arm is broken! I need help!"

Sue is scared. She does not know what to do. She looks for help. But there is no one in the park. They are alone.

"Help! Help! Help!" Sue shouts.

But no one hears her. No one comes. Tom and Sue are stuck in the park. They are wet. They are cold. They are sad. They have no fun. They have a bad day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny carrot. Bunny carrot was thick and bouncy. He was always smiling and his yellow teeth shone in the sun.

One day, bunny carrot hopped down the road and met a friendly squirrel. The squirrel was very happy to meet bunny carrot and smiled at him.

Bunny carrot thought it was so cool to make a new friend, so he hopped back home. He ran to the garden and grabbed a carrot as a present for his new friend.

The next day, bunny carrot brought the carrot to the squirrel. The squirrel was so excited! He smiled at bunny carrot and thanked him for the gift.

The two friends became best friends and every day, they would play together and share carrots. They were so happy and would always smile at each other.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and skip around. One day, Lily went to the ocean with her family. She loved the sound of the waves and the feeling of the wet sand on her feet.

Lily wanted to skip across the ocean, but her parents told her it was too dangerous. She didn't listen and ran into the water. Suddenly, a big wave knocked her down and she couldn't get back up.

Her parents tried to save her, but it was too late. Lily had drowned in the ocean. Her family was very sad and missed her very much. They wished she had listened to them and stayed safe on the shore.

Mandy and her friends were playing in the park near a beautiful fountain. "Wow!" Mandy said. "It looks so peaceful." She admired the fountain and the children watched as the water bubbled. Suddenly, Mandy had an idea. "Let's stir the water!" she exclaimed.

The children laughed and walked up to the fountain. They grabbed sticks and began to stir the water. The water swirled and splashed as they moved the sticks around.

Mandy noticed that the churning water was getting stronger and stronger. "Let's get out of here," she said. "Something isn't right." Her friends followed her lead and they ran away from the fountain. Just then, the fountain burst through the top and water came flying out.

Mandy and her friends watched in awe at the display. "That was close," she said. "I'm glad I had a feeling that something was wrong."

The children eventually went back to the fountain, this time to admire its force and beauty. They had stirred the fountain in the most peaceful way.

Once upon a time there was a mixer. The mixer liked to wave hi to everyone. It was an easy thing for it to do. The mixer waved to the birds in the sky and the ants on the ground. Everyone was happy to see the mixer wave.

One day the mixer had an idea. It wanted to mix some things together. It waved to the trees and asked if it could have some leaves. The trees said yes and waved back. The mixer then waved to the sun and asked if it could have some heat. The sun agreed and waved back.

The mixer waved to the clouds and asked if they would give it some water. The clouds did and the mixer had everything it needed. The mixer then waved its arms around and mixed all the things together.

The mixer had made something new and it was very happy. The end.

Jack was a brave 3 year old boy who liked to explore. One day, while he was playing outside, he saw an old door. He had never seen it before. He walked slowly towards it, because he was curious. Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run really fast, but he also loved to scatter his toys all over the house. His mom would always tell him to pick them up, but he never listened.

One day, Timmy's mom told him that she had a present for him. Timmy was so excited! He asked his mom what the present was, but she wouldn't tell him. She said he had to pick up all his toys first.

Timmy didn't want to pick up his toys, so he ran away. His mom was sad because she wanted to give him the present, but Timmy was too busy scattering his toys everywhere.

Later that day, Timmy's friend came over to play. Timmy showed him all his toys, but his friend accidentally stepped on one and broke it. Timmy got very upset and started crying. His friend said sorry, but Timmy didn't want to forgive him.

Timmy's mom came in and saw what happened. She told Timmy that it's okay to be upset, but it's important to forgive his friend. She also reminded him that if he had picked up his toys, they wouldn't have gotten broken. Timmy realized his mistake and apologized to his friend. His mom then gave him the present she had been saving, and Timmy was so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a smelly stable. In the stable, there were many animals. There was a big horse, a small dog, and a tiny mouse. They all lived together and were good friends.

One day, they heard a loud shout. It was a man who needed help. The big horse, the small dog, and the tiny mouse all went outside to see what was wrong. The man's cart was stuck in the mud.

The big horse, the small dog, and the tiny mouse all worked together to help the man. The big horse pulled the cart, the small dog pushed, and the tiny mouse cheered them on. Soon, the cart was out of the mud.

The man was so happy and said thank you to the animals. The big horse, the small dog, and the tiny mouse went back to their smelly stable. They were proud of their hard work and happy to be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy's mom told him they were going to a special place called a church. Timmy didn't know what a church was, but he was excited to go.

As they walked to the church, Timmy saw lots of people dressed in their Sunday best. They all looked happy and smiled at him. When they got inside, Timmy saw lots of chairs and a big stage. He didn't know what was going to happen, but he was excited to find out.

Suddenly, a man came up to the stage and started talking. Timmy didn't understand everything he said, but he saw lots of people nodding their heads and clapping their hands. The man was talking about being successful and helping others. Timmy didn't know what that meant, but he knew it must be important.

After the man was finished talking, Timmy and his mom left the church. As they walked back home, Timmy thought about what he had seen and heard. He didn't know exactly what it all meant, but he knew that going to church was a special thing and he wanted to do it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jill. She was so full of life and energy that she never sat still!

One day, Jill's mother gave her some colorful dough and asked her to play with it. "Please don't go too fast," her mom cautioned.

Jill agreed, but as soon as Mom left the room, she started rolling the dough across the floor. She made a game of seeing who could make their dough move the fastest!

When Mom came back in the room, she saw Jill with dough all over her dress and scattered on the floor. â€œWhat happened?â€ Mom asked. Jill, feeling embarrassed, told her mother the truth.

Mom smiled and said something important, â€œJill, it's ok to want to speed up sometimes, but know that it's best to go slow. That way you can take the time to do a good job and make sure everything is the way you want it.â€

Jill understood and learned her lesson: impatience may not yield the best results. She now always remembers to go slow and the results are much more colorful!

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Bill. He was very tired, having been out in the woods folding fur. As he climbed the mountain, he heard a loud roar. To his surprise, a big, angry lion was standing in his way.

The lion said, "What are you doing in my woods?" Bill replied nervously, "I'm just folding fur, sir." The lion scowled. "I don't like outsiders in my woods," he growled.

Bill knew he had to think of something quickly. He thought back to what his mum had said to him when he was just a cub---"be brave and kind, no matter what." So, he put on his bravest voice and said, "Can't I help? I'm very tired and could use a rest."

The lion thought for a moment and then smiled. He said, "Okay, you can stay. But you must help the other animals in the woods." Bill smiled. He was relieved.

So, Bill stayed in the woods, helping the animals with folding fur and doing other jobs. He soon became the lion's best friend!

Once upon a time, there was a very gifted dinosaur named Dippy. Dippy was such a clever dinosaur and could measure things like an adult.

One day, he was measuring the biggest tree in the forest. Suddenly, he heard a loud and scary roar. He quickly looked behind him, and saw a giant T-Rex!

Dippy was scared but he bravely said to T-Rex, "What do you want?"

T-Rex replied, â€œI want all of your measurements!â€

Dippy refused. He did not want the T-Rex to threaten other dinosaurs. However, T-Rex refused to leave until he had all of the measurements.

So, Dippy had to give up all of his measurements to T-Rex. Unfortunately, T-Rex used Dippy's measurements to cause trouble in the forest.

The end.

One day there was a reliable balloon. It started out floating in the air and was very bouncy. All around it were other balloons but none compared to this one. It was different.

The reliable balloon had something special. It had a message on it. This message said "Happy Birthday". Such a special message was worth showing off!

So the reliable balloon decided to proudly display itself. It flew around for everyone to see. It had never felt so special before.

But soon people started talking about the reliable balloon. It looked like it was time for a celebration. Everyone started singing happy birthday and Blowing up lots of colourful balloons.

The reliable balloon was very happy. After all its hard work it was finally getting the recognition it deserved. It was like a dream come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. He loved to play outside. One day, Joe saw a big blue top. He was so excited, he ran over to it. Joe picked up the top, put it on the ground, and started to spin it. He laughed as it spun round and round.

The top stopped spinning, but Joe wanted it to keep going. He stepped away and yelled, "I want the top to spin!"

Suddenly a voice came out of the sky. It said, "If Joe wants the top to keep spinning, he needs to take the spin test."

Joe wasn't sure what a spin test was, but he was brave. He looked up and said, "Okay, I'll take the test!"

The voice said, "Good! To finish the spin test, you must spin the top until it stops by itself. Go ahead and try."

So Joe stepped forward, blew on the top to make it spin, and watched as it spun round and round. Finally, it stopped spinning on its own. Joe had passed the spin test!

The voice said, "Congratulations Joe! Now the top will spin forever."

Joe was so happy, he jumped for joy! Now he could enjoy spinning his big blue top as long as he wanted.

Once upon a time there was a fit girl named Pepper. She loved to jog every day. She would run and run until her mom called her home.

One day she was jogging in the park. She saw a big hill and decided to jog up it. She ran up and down, up and down until she could jog no more.

She stopped and looked around. She saw a big tree with lots of leaves and flowers. She also saw some birds flying around in circles. It made Pepper feel very happy.

Pepper jogged all the way home. When she arrived, she was even more fit than before. She smiled and went inside to take a rest.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big red ball. The ball was very bouncy and fun to play with. But one day, the ball got a hole in it and it couldn't bounce anymore. The owner of the ball was very sad because they loved playing with it.

The owner tried to fix the ball, but it was too broken. So they went to the store to replace the ball with a new one. They found a blue ball that was just as bouncy as the red one. The owner was very happy to have a new ball to play with.

The red ball was left behind, but it wasn't sad. It knew that it had been loved and played with a lot. It was happy to rest and wait for someone new to come along and play with it. The end.

Ben and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But today, Mom says they have to help with the laundry. She gives them a big basket of dirty clothes and tells them to take it to the washing machine.

Ben and Lily do not want to do laundry. They think it is boring and hard. They want to play with their toys. They hope Mom will forget about the laundry and let them play.

They walk slowly to the washing machine. They see a big pile of clean clothes on the sofa. They have an idea. They put the basket of dirty clothes on the floor and start to throw the clean clothes in the air. They pretend they are snowflakes and catch them with their hands. They laugh and have fun.

Mom hears them and comes to see what they are doing. She is not happy. She sees the clean clothes all over the floor and the dirty clothes still in the basket. She says, "Ben and Lily, what are you doing? You are making a mess. You are supposed to do the laundry, not play with it. Now you have to pick up all the clothes and put them back where they belong. And then you have to do the laundry. No more playing until you finish."

Ben and Lily are sad. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We did not want to do the laundry. We wanted to play. We thought laundry was easy. But it is not. It is hard and boring."

Mom says, "I know, laundry is not fun. But it is something we have to do. It is part of being a family. We all have to help with the chores. If we do them together, they will be easier and faster. And then we can have more time to play. Come on, I will help you. Let's do the laundry together. And then we can play with your toys. OK?"

Ben and Lily nod. They say, "OK, Mom. Thank you. We will help you. We will do the laundry together. And then we can play."

They pick up the clothes and put them back where they belong. They take the basket of dirty clothes to the washing machine. They help Mom put the clothes in and press the buttons. They watch the clothes spin and make bubbles. They think it is a little bit fun. They hope the laundry will be done soon. And then they can play.

Once upon a time, Jack was playing in the park. Suddenly â€" something mysterious caught Jack's eye. It was a mask! Jack thought it looked cool and picked it up. He put it on and it fit perfectly.

Jack really liked it and he decided to take it home. When he got home, he showed his mom the mysterious mask. His mom said he could keep it, as long as he took good care of it.

Jack put the mask on every single day. He loved playing with it. One day, while playing outside, he left the mask in the grass. He started to look for it, but it had disappeared! He was so worried and started crying.

But then, Jack remembered something his mom had said. She said that when he loses something, he should always look for it later in the same place - and just like that, the mask reappeared! Jack was so happy that he hugged it tight.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a shy cat named Kitty. She lived in a small house with a porch. Kitty loved to rub her soft fur on the porch steps.

So, Kitty let Timmy rub her soft fur gently. They played together on the porch and became good friends. From that day on, Kitty was not shy anymore, and she loved playing with Timmy every day.

Max had a wooden box that he kept all his things in. It was the original box Grandma gave him. The box made Max feel happy.

Max was so happy! Grandma understood what he wanted, and gave him permission to use the wood.

Together with Dad and Grandma, Max used the wood to complete his special box home. He was so proud and everyone clapped for him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a towel that she loved to use after her bath. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to help open a jar of pickles. Lily tried and tried, but she couldn't do it.

Suddenly, Lily's cat jumped on the counter and knocked the jar over. The pickles spilled all over the floor and made a big mess. Lily's mommy was very upset, but Lily just laughed and said, "Silly cat!"

Later that day, Lily and her mommy went for a walk in the park. They saw a dead bird on the ground. Lily asked her mommy what happened to the bird. Her mommy explained that sometimes animals die and go to heaven. Lily didn't understand, but she gave the bird a little kiss on its head and said, "Goodbye, birdie."

Once upon a time, Lucy the bee was flying in the meadow. She was looking for a place to build her hive.

Suddenly, she saw a small, hairy bush. She flew over to take a closer look and saw that it was perfect!

"I'll make my home here," she said happily. She started to gather pieces of wood and flowers to build her hive.

Just then, a butterfly flew by. "What are you doing?" asked the butterfly.

"I'm building my home," Lucy said.

The butterfly smiled. "That's very nice," he said. "But what if something happens to it?"

"I don't know," Lucy said, frowning.

The butterfly nodded. "That's why it's important to build your hive with friends," he said. "If something happens, everyone can help."

Lucy smiled, and set to work with her new friends. After much hard work, they managed to finish the hive together.

The moral of this story is that it is always better to work with friends. That way, if something happens, we can help each other out.

One day, a mysterious man came to a small town. He walked down the street and everyone noticed him.

The mayor of the town was very curious and asked him why he was there. The mysterious man said he wanted to build something.

The mayor asked what it was that the man wanted to build. The man said he wanted to build a score.

The mayor was amazed. He asked what it was for. The man said it was a surprise and it was for everyone in the town.

The townspeople worked together to help the mysterious man build his score.

The townspeople cheered even louder and celebrated the mysterious score they had built together.

Once there was a mom and a daughter. The daughter wanted to play with a laser toy. She asked her mom. Mom did not permit it.

"No," said Mom. "Laser toys are bad and I do not want you to play with them."

The daughter looked sadly at her mom. "But I want to play," she said.

"No," said Mom. "It is not safe. Lasers can be bad, and I do not want you to get hurt."

The daughter did not understand. She started to cry.

Mom hugged her daughter. "I know you want to play," said Mom, "but I cannot permit it. It is not safe."

The daughter sniffed and wiped her tears away. "Ok," she said.

Mom was relieved. She hugged her daughter again and kissed her forehead.

"There are lots of other things you can do that are much safer," said Mom.

The daughter smiled and hugged her mom. She decided to forget about the laser and play with something else.

Once upon a time there was a very wealthy family who owned many things, but the family's most cherished possession was the puppy that the father had bought for the children that same day. The puppy was small and fluffy with big, black eyes.

The family went outside to play with the puppy, and they laughed with joy as they watched the puppy chase around butterflies. Suddenly, the puppy started to shiver with cold and the family looked up to see storm clouds gathering in the sky.

The mother said to the father, "Let's go inside quick and get the pup warm." But the father said, "It's ok, the pup will be fine in this weather," and he began to walk away.

The children were about to shiver too, but the mother quickly picked up the puppy and rushed everyone inside to safety.

The family was so thankful that the mother had acted quickly and that the puppy was safe. The mom said to the dad, "See, that's why I always listen to my instincts." The family smiled and hugged their beloved puppy tight, thanking the mom for her wisdom.

Once upon a time, there was a lion who wanted something very delicious. He asked a little girl, "Please, can you help me? I am looking for something very delicious!"

The little girl thought for a moment and then replied, "Yes, follow me. I can help you!"

So, they set off on an adventure. The lion followed the little girl through the forest. They came across a field of ripe apples. The little girl said, "Look, there are lots of delicious apples here! Please try one!"

The lion was so happy. He tried an apple, and it was delicious! He thanked the little girl and they said goodbye.

The lion was so pleased that the little girl had helped him find something so delicious. From that day on, he was always happy to see her.

Lily and Ben were playing in the bathroom. They liked to splash water on each other and make bubbles with the soap. They did not hear Mom calling them for dinner.

"Look, Ben, I can make the water go fast or slow!" Lily said. She turned the faucet left and right. The water made a loud noise.

Ben wanted to try too. He reached for the faucet, but Lily pushed him away. "No, it's my turn!" she said.

Ben was angry. He pushed Lily back. They both fell into the bathtub. The faucet hit Lily's head. She cried out in pain.

Mom heard the cry and ran to the bathroom. She saw blood on Lily's head and water on the floor. She was scared. She picked up Lily and wrapped a towel around her head. She shouted at Ben. "What did you do? You hurt your sister! You are a bad boy!"

Ben felt sorry. He did not mean to hurt Lily. He just wanted to play with the faucet. He started to cry too. He wished he had listened to Mom. He wished he had not pushed Lily. He wished he could say sorry. But Mom was too angry to listen. She took Lily to the car and drove to the hospital. She left Ben alone in the bathroom. He was scared. He did not know what to do. He did not know if Lily would be okay. He did not know if Mom would love him again. He sat on the floor and cried. He did not think anyone would come back for him. He did not think anyone would care. He did not think anyone would forgive him. He did not think he could ever be happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a big farm with lots of animals. There was a bull named Billy who loved to eat grass all day long. One day, the farmer noticed that Billy was looking a little sad. He realized that Billy needed some new hay to eat.

So, the farmer went to the barn to supply Billy with some fresh hay. Billy was so happy and started eating it right away. The hay was so fancy and smelled so good that Billy felt like a king.

From that day on, Billy was the happiest bull on the farm. He loved the farmer for always supplying him with the best hay. And the farmer loved Billy for being such a happy and healthy bull. The end.

It was a very hot day and Marty the Bear was feeling lazy and tired. He wanted to find something fun to do, but he couldn't think of anything. Suddenly he remembered something. "I know!" said Marty, as he remembered a special challenge from his friends. They had told him about a large oak tree in the forest under which a mystery was hidden. Marty knew that if he solved the mystery, he would have loads of fun.

Excited, he got up and ran off to the woods. As he arrived, he saw the large oak tree up ahead of him and he was filled with anticipation. He searched the tree's trunk and branches, but he couldn't find the mystery. Just then, he spotted a small hole behind the tree. He carefully peered inside and saw a shiny object. "What's this?" he said. Marty had solved the mystery.

He reached inside and pulled out a shining golden treasure chest. Inside were lots of bright and colourful toys and treats. Marty was so happy, he decided to stay in the shade of the large oak tree to play with his new treasures. His solved the mystery and it was a day of fun and adventure.

Once upon a time, there was an old rabbit. He lived in the woods with many other animals. Every day, he wanted to learn something new. He saw the other animals scurrying around and noticed how much they knew. He wanted to be just like them!

One day, he decided to learn how to climb the trees. He hopped to the base of the tree, but it was too high. He tried and tried, but he couldn't reach the top. He was starting to get frustrated.

Then, a beautiful blue bird flew by. She noticed the old rabbit trying to climb the tree. She swooped down and offered to help. She flew to the branches above and told the old rabbit which way to jump.

Finally, the old rabbit made it to the top of the tree. He was so excited! He could feel the wind in his fur and see the other animals below. He had learned a new trick! From then on, the old rabbit was never afraid to try something new.

Once upon a time, there was a player. He was amazing. He liked to dream. He dreamed of being the best player ever. One day, he went outside and played a game. He was so fast and so good. Everyone was amazed. When he came home, his mum gave him a big hug and told him how wonderful he was. He smiled and went to sleep. Every night he had amazing dreams of being the very best player ever. He was so happy and his dreams kept getting better and better. One day, he became the best player ever just like he had dreamed. Everyone was so amazed and happy for him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went to her grandma's house for lunch. Her grandma made her favorite food - spaghetti with a spicy sauce.

Lily loved the taste of the spicy sauce, but she didn't realize that it would make her mouth feel hot. She ate and ate, not realizing that she was getting hotter and hotter. Suddenly, she felt like she needed something to cool her down.

That's when she saw it - a big glass of cold milk on the table. She reached out to grab it, but her hand slipped and she accidentally knocked over a whip that was on the table. The whip fell to the ground with a loud thud.

Lily's grandma quickly got up to grab the whip and put it away. Lily was relieved that she didn't get in trouble, but she knew she had to be more careful in the future. From that day on, she always made sure to grab things carefully and pay attention to her surroundings.

Once there was a little girl who was very kind. She wanted to help those in need and spread happiness. Every day she would take a walk down the street and look for people to care for.

One day she saw an old man, walking with a vase. He was walking very slowly and seemed to be struggling. The little girl knew she could help him. She walked up to the man and said 'Hello, can I help you with your vase?'

The old man was very happy and said 'Yes, thank you so much!' He was relieved to be able to carry the vase with less effort.

The little girl took the vase and walked alongside the old man. She was not aware that some people who were passing by had noticed what she had done and quietly admired her for her kindness.

The little girl had learned an important lesson that day: it is important to always be kind to those around you and care for those in need. Being ignorant of the feelings of others is not the way to be.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat cherries, especially the soft ones. One day, her mom gave her a big bowl of cherries to eat. But when Lily started to eat them, she saw that one of the cherries was not soft, it was hard.

Lily didn't want to eat the hard cherry, but she also didn't want to waste it. She thought about what to do and then came up with an idea. She decided to give the hard cherry to her little brother who loved to eat anything.

When Lily gave the hard cherry to her brother, he was so happy and ate it right away. Lily felt happy too because she was able to solve the conflict and make her brother happy at the same time. From that day on, Lily always remembered to check if the cherries were soft before she ate them.

Jimmy and Jaqui were twins. They loved to play together. Today, they wanted to build a castle. So they grabbed their blocks, and started to build.

Jimmy said, "Let's make it tall!" Jaqui agreed.

But then Jaqui grabbed too many and the castle got very messy.
Jimmy said, "Hold on! We need to clean it up. Help me put the blocks away, Jaqui." So they both went to work.

After a few minutes, their castle was neat and tidy.
Jimmy smiled and said, "Now it's perfect!"

Jaqui jumped up and said, "Let's play!" And they did.

Once there was a girl called Katie. She was 3 years old. One day, she wanted to take a nice cross - it was bright and colourful, and she thought it was very pretty.

So, she went outside and found a cross. She took it and hugged it tight. She was very happy to have her own nice cross.

Katie took her cross to the garden and played with it. She made a game where she pretended to be an explorer looking for a hidden treasure. She pretended to take her nice cross with her on her adventure - just like all the brave explorers did.

Katie played for a long time until it was time to go back inside. She took her cross and hugged it one last time. She felt very happy and excited to keep playing the next day with her special cross.

Sammy wanted to play outside. He wanted to feel the bright sunshine on his face. He saw a slide in the park and wanted to go on it. He ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. Once at the top, he looked down, and it seemed so high! But Sammy did not hesitate, he pushed off and down he went! He had so much fun going up and down, up and down on the slide. Every time he went down, the slide was so bright and pretty in the sunshine. Sammy wanted to play on the slide forever. When his mom called, he reluctantly got off the slide and went home. Sammy said goodbye to the slide, dreaming that he would play on it again someday.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to bounce. She could bounce higher than anyone else!

One day, she saw a yellow pond. She wanted to bounce on the pond so she did. She bounced once, twice, three times and then she heard a splash!

The little girl had bounced so hard that she fell into the pond! She was scared at first, but she started to laugh. She swam around, splashed and had lots of fun in the yellow pond.

It was so much fun that she started to bounce in the pond. She bounced once, twice, three times. She was so happy and she even taught the frogs how to bounce!

Once there was a small boy. He was very happy because he had a new sock. He couldn't wait to wear it and show off to his friends.

The boy bounced around the room in excitement until he found the perfect spot to put it on. As he looked down at the small sock, he smiled.

The boy put on the sock and felt his foot become warm and comfortable. He hopped around the room, feeling both silly and proud.

He ran out of the house and into the park. He showed off his new sock to all his friends. They thought it was very cool.

With his new sock, the boy was gaining confidence and feeling more happy. He was so proud of his small new sock and the confidence he gained from wearing it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat rice with her family every day. One day, Lily's little brother got a toy that she really wanted. She felt jealous and sad.

But then, Lily's brother did something amazing! He danced and sang a silly song. Everyone in the family applauded him and cheered. Lily felt happy for her brother and forgot all about her jealousy.

After dinner, Lily's mom gave her a big hug and told her how proud she was of her for being happy for her brother. Lily felt warm and loved inside. From that day on, Lily learned that it's better to be happy for others than to feel jealous.

Lily and Max were friends who liked to play with blocks. They could build towers, bridges, and houses with their blocks. One day, they decided to make a network with their blocks. A network was a lot of blocks that were connected by other blocks.

Lily and Max worked hard to make their network. They picked different colors and shapes of blocks and put them together. They made a network that had many parts and looked very nice.

But then, Ben came to play with them. Ben was a boy who lived next door. He saw their network and wanted to play with it too. But he did not ask Lily and Max. He just grabbed some blocks and tried to add them to the network.

"Hey, stop!" Lily said. "That is our network. You can't just take our blocks."

"Yes, I can," Ben said. "I want to play with your network. It looks fun."

"No, you can't," Max said. "You have to ask us first. And you have to be careful. You might break our network."

Ben did not listen. He kept picking blocks and putting them where he wanted. He did not care if they matched or fit. He made the network look messy and ugly.

Lily and Max were very angry and sad. They did not like what Ben was doing. They felt envious of Ben. He had so many blocks and he did not share. He did not respect their work. He did not care about their feelings.

They tried to stop Ben, but he was bigger and stronger. He pushed them away and laughed. He thought he was better than them. He thought he could do whatever he wanted.

Lily and Max did not know what to do. They wanted to save their network. They wanted to play with their blocks. They wanted to have fun with their friend. But Ben was not a good friend. He was a mean boy. He was a bully.

What do you think Lily and Max should do? How do you think the story should end?

Once upon a time there was a gentle oat. It grew in a field and it had little green leaves. One day a three year old child came walking through the field and started to look around. He found the gentle oat, and recognized that it was something special. He touched the leaves and felt how gentle it was. He decided to take the oat home with him.

Back at home, he showed his family the gentle oat. They were very surprised when they recognized how special it was. Everyone took care of it and it soon grew even bigger. Every day they would look at the gentle oat, and they were so happy that the child had recognized it. The gentle oat was part of their family now.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wander in the great outdoors. One day, she wandered into a forest and got lost. She was scared and started to cry.

Suddenly, she saw a little bird in a cell. The bird was sad and wanted to fly free. Lily asked the bird, "Why are you in the cell?" The bird replied, "I was caught by a mean man who wanted to keep me as a pet."

Lily felt sorry for the bird and decided to help. She found the key to the cell and set the bird free. The bird was so happy and thanked Lily. Together, they wandered through the forest and became the best of friends.

Sara was a charming girl who liked to speak to everyone. She had many friends at her school and at her home. She also liked to play with her toys, especially her black cat, Luna.

One day, Sara went to the park with her mom and Luna. She saw a boy who had a big red ball. She wanted to play with him and his ball. She ran to him and said, "Hi, I am Sara. Can I play with you and your ball?"

The boy looked at her and said, "No, you can't. This is my ball and you are a girl. Girls can't play with balls. And your cat is ugly. It is black and has green eyes. Go away!"

Sara felt sad and angry. She did not like what the boy said. She loved Luna and she liked to play with balls. She said, "That is not nice. You are mean. Girls can play with balls too. And my cat is not ugly. She is beautiful and smart. She can do tricks. Look!"

Sara whistled and Luna jumped on her shoulder. Then Luna rolled over and meowed. Sara smiled and said, "See? Luna is amazing. You are just jealous."

The boy was surprised and scared. He did not know that cats could do tricks. He dropped his ball and ran away. He said, "Ahh! Your cat is a witch. It is evil. Stay away from me!"

Sara picked up the ball and said, "Bye, bye, mean boy. Come on, Luna. Let's play with the ball. We don't need him. We have each other."

Sara and Luna had fun playing with the ball. They met some other nice kids who wanted to play with them too. Sara was happy and proud. She said, "Luna, you are the best cat in the world. You are my friend and you are charming."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a small town with his mom and dad. One day, Timmy wanted to play with his ball, but it was stuck on the roof of his house. He asked his dad to help him lift him up to get it.

His dad said, "Okay, Timmy, I'll lift you up, but be careful." Timmy was so happy when he got his ball back. He played with it for a while, but then he accidentally kicked it too hard and it went into the neighbor's yard. Timmy was too embarrassed to go get it back.

His mom saw that Timmy was sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her what happened and his mom said, "Don't be embarrassed, Timmy. We'll go get your ball together." So, they went to the neighbor's yard and got the ball back. Timmy was so happy that he gave his mom a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty boy named James. He had big, blue eyes that twinkled in the sunshine.

One day, he went outside to play. He didn't worry about getting sunburnt, because the sunshine was very bright.

James ran around the garden, playing hide and seek. He ran for so long that he got tired and had to sit down. While he was sitting there, he slowly blinked his eyes to rest them from the sunshine.

Suddenly, he heard a soft giggle. It was the sunshine, playing with James! He laughed and jumped up, chasing the sunshine. As he ran, his eyes blinked even more as he couldn't help himself from smiling.

The sunshine kept playing with James for a very long time. Eventually, it was time for dinner and James had to go inside. He waved goodbye to the sunshine and went inside with a smile on his face.

Once there was a green frog. He liked to hang from the trees in the meadow. The sun shone bright, and the frog loved the light feeling.

The frog could see the blue sky above and the bright colors of the flowers. He stretched out his legs and smiled.

The frog spent his days hanging from the tree, watching the world go by. He saw the birds flying around and a butterfly fluttering past. He liked to look at the different colors of the animals around.

Then one day, he saw something special. A light was hanging from the branch of his tree. It was sparkling so brightly and it had beautiful red, yellow and blue colors. The frog loved it. He hung from the tree and watched the light sparkle and dance in the breeze.

The frog decided to stay in the meadow near the light. He enjoyed seeing the pretty colors and feeling the light on his skin. The frog was happy to be in the meadow with the light around.

Once there was a little girl called Sarah. She was only three years old, and she used to love watching cartoons. Every day, her mum bought her a new DVD of different cartoon movies, and she was so excited to watch them.
