Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Jane lived on a farm and her best friend was a mule. The mule's name was Joe. Jane and Joe had lots of fun together.

Every day, Jane and Joe would go for a walk in the open fields. They would enjoy the sunshine and play games. Sometimes they would play tag and hide and seek. Other times they would make believe they were knights and dragons.

When they would tire of pretending, they would go to the open barn and take a nap. They would snuggle up close together with the mule's warm fur tickling Jane's face.

Then Jane and Joe would go back to the open fields. They would run and laugh and giggle. Jane and Joe were the best of friends.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mia. She was three years old and loved to look at the stars in the night sky. Every night, she would rush out of her house and look up at the sparkling stars.

One night, she rushed out of her house and called out loudly, â€œWhere are you, stars?â€ Then, to her surprise, one of the stars started to move. As it moved closer to her, Mia realised that it wasnâ€™t a star at all, but a fairy!

The fairy asked Mia, â€œWhat are you doing out here so late, little one?â€ Mia replied, â€œI am looking for a serious star.â€ The fairy smiled and said, â€œYou donâ€™t need to look far. All stars are serious and wonderful.â€

Mia smiled and thanked the fairy. Then, she rushed back inside to show her mum that she had found a real star.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to observe what was going on near her. She saw a thermometer and thought it was very interesting. She got closer to get a much better look.

Suddenly a rude man appeared and began to shout at her. The little girl was very scared and started to cry. She ran away quickly.

The little girl was sad, because she couldn't observe the thermometer anymore. She wanted to know more about it and find out why the rude man didn't want her to look at it.

The little girl decided that one day she would go back to observe the thermometer and find out why the rude man had been so mean. She was determined to get the answer!

Mandy and her mom were walking through a big park. Mandy saw lots of boats in the lake and she was excited to ride one. She asked her mom if they could go for a boat ride.

Her mom said, "Maybe later, Mandy. It looks a bit cold out there."

Mandy shivered and wrapped her blanket around her. Her mom smiled and said, "It looks like you need to get inside to stay warm."

Mandy and her mom headed towards the house. When they got there, her mom said, "Let's make something to eat. We can use the dishwasher to help us cook."

Mandy liked the idea and they began cooking. But when they opened the dishwasher, they saw a mouse inside! Mandy's mom looked very serious and said, "We can't turn it on now. We will have to find another way to cook the food."

Mandy started to look around the kitchen. She finally found an old pot and said, "We can use this pot to cook the food."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a great idea, Mandy!"

So Mandy and her mom were able to cook their dinner without the dishwasher. Mandy was glad that even though there was a problem, she could help to solve it.

John was playing with his blocks in the park. His mom was watching him as he built a big tower. Suddenly, a big dog came close to John. John felt scared and his mom said, "Don't you dare run away! Stand your ground". John tried to stand tall and tough but he was trembling with fear.

The dog started to bark and growl. John's mom stepped forward and said, "Be tough, darling. I know you can do it". John stepped forward bravely and the dog stopped barking.

John was so happy and proud of himself. He smiled at the dog and said, "See, I dared to be tough and win!".

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys and his dog, Max. One day, Timmy and Max went for a walk in the park.

As they walked, Timmy saw a big tree with lots of leaves. "Wow, Max! Look at that tree! I admire it," Timmy said. Max barked happily.

Suddenly, Timmy heard a loud noise. It was a group of kids playing soccer. Timmy felt nervous because he didn't know them. "Don't worry, Timmy. They look friendly," Max said.

Timmy took a deep breath and walked over to the kids. "Hi, my name is Timmy. Can I play with you?" he asked. The kids smiled and said yes. Timmy felt happy and left his nerves behind.

One day, two children, Jack and Alex, were playing in a forest. They were running around and having so much fun. Suddenly, Jack heard a noise coming from the bush.

Jacob thought it was a chicken, so he asked his brother to help him find it. Alex also heard the noise and agreed to help. Soon, they found the chicken, who was looking quite funny with its colorful feathers.

At first, the chicken was scared of the two children. But eventually it warmed up to them, when Jack supplied her with some food. Then the chicken even ran around with them and played.

The fun that Jack and Alex had with the chicken that day gave them a valuable lesson. They learnt that even if something looks strange and funny, it can still be a source of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a barber who had never met anyone like him before. He was different in a very special way. Every day he used to strike his clippers and comb his hair.

One day, he heard a little knock at his door. He opened the door and a little girl with big brown eyes was standing there. She said, "I need a haircut, can I come in please?"

The barber smiled and said, "Of course!" He motioned for her to come in and take a seat. He then began to strike his clippers and comb her hair. He was careful to not make it too short.

When he was done, the little girl said, "Thank you! It looks so different!" The barber smiled and said, "You're welcome! Come back anytime!"

The little girl left with a new haircut and the barber felt happy. He liked giving people haircuts and making them look different. He thought it was the best job ever.

Once upon a time, Mummy, Daddy and their daughter, Isabel, sat down at the dinner table. Daddy looked at Isabel and asked her what she wanted to discuss. She smiled and said she wanted to talk about something unusual.

Mummy and Daddy started to discuss dinner and Isabel heard them talk about something unusual. She wondered what it was and asked them what it was. Mummy said that it was a special dinner that she had cooked. She had put lots of unusual ingredients together, like carrots, celery and some strange spices.

Isabel was very excited and couldn't wait to see what it tasted like. Mummy smiled and said the dinner was a surprise and that Isabel would have to wait until it was ready. After a short while, Mummy brought in the dinner. When Isabel saw it, her eyes went wide. It looked so delicious!

Mummy asked Isabel what she thought of the dinner. Isabel said it was the most unusual dinner she had ever seen. She tried a bit of everything and said it tasted delicious.

Mummy, Daddy and Isabel all smiled as they enjoyed the dinner together. Every time they ate dinner after that, Isabel would always ask if there was something unusual to talk about!

Once there was a little boy who had a pretty red wagon. He liked to take it everywhere he went and feel the wind on his face as it pulled him along. One day, the little boy was having a wild adventure and his wagon rolled further away from him than it ever had before. He called out, but the little wagon had gone too far. The little boy was so sad. He looked everywhere, but he couldn't find it. He had lost his wagon!

For days, the little boy searched and asked around but without luck. He was so upset he couldn't enjoy the wild outdoor adventures anymore.

One day, he was walking along a street and he heard something strange - it was the sound of his little red wagon! The little boy raced towards the sound and there, to his surprise and delight, was his wagon! He was so happy he had found his wagon. He hugged it tightly and never let it out of his sight again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She was three years old and very curious. One day, Sarah decided to go for a walk outside. She put on her furry boots and stepped into the garden. She stepped down a small hill and through some tall grass. Her furry boots kept her feet warm as she stepped along. As she went, she heard a strange noise coming from the bushes. She stopped and stepped closer. There, lying in the ground was a huge, furry animal. Sarah was very excited. She grabbed one of her boots and stepped closer. The furry animal looked up at her and started to move. It was a small puppy. Sarah was so excited and she bent down to pick up the puppy. She felt its soft fur in her hands. She looked up and saw a small basket beside the puppy. In it, was a note for Sarah. It said "This puppy is yours to look after!" Sarah was so happy and hugged the furry puppy tight. She stepped back into her furry boots and took the puppy back home. She loved it and cared for it like it was her own.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a kite. They run and laugh and have fun.

One day, a big dog comes to the park. The dog is not nice. He barks and chases Sara and Tom. He wants their ball and their kite. Sara and Tom are scared. They run away from the dog. They look for a safe place.

They see a fence. The fence is tall and strong. It has a gate. Sara and Tom run to the gate. They open it and go inside. They close the gate. The dog cannot get in. He is angry. He jumps and scratches at the fence. He makes a loud noise.

Sara and Tom are inside the fence. They see a house. The house is small and cozy. It has a window and a door. They see a lady. The lady is kind. She smiles and waves at Sara and Tom. She comes to the gate. She opens it and talks to the dog. She tells the dog to go away. The dog listens. He stops barking and chasing. He walks away.

Sara and Tom are happy. They thank the lady. The lady invites them to her house. She gives them cookies and milk. She tells them stories and sings them songs. She is a grandma. She likes Sara and Tom. Sara and Tom like her too.

They are glad they found the fence. They are glad they met the grandma. They are glad they are safe and warm. They do not weep anymore. They smile and hug the grandma. They are friends.

Frankie was very excited. He had a new puppy and it needed a name. So, he thought and thought and thought. He couldn't decide and then he had a great idea! He decided to paint a picture of his pup and give it a name based on the painting. He got out his paints and chose blue, yellow, and green. He started to paint, and when he was finished he saw the most beautiful puppy. It had sparkling blue eyes, wiggly yellow ears and a soft green nose. Frankie had named his puppy - Unknown!

Once upon a time, there was a little pig named Peppa. Peppa was very shy and didn't like to talk to other animals. One day, Peppa's mom bought some meat from the store and asked Peppa to help organize it in the fridge.

Peppa didn't know how to organize the meat, so she asked her mom for help. "Mommy, how do I organize the meat?" Peppa asked. "Just put it in the fridge in a neat pile, Peppa," her mom replied.

Peppa organized the meat in the fridge and felt very proud of herself. "Look, Mommy! I organized the meat!" Peppa said. Her mom smiled and said, "Good job, Peppa. You did a great job organizing the meat."

Once upon a time there was a temple deep in the forest. Inside the temple was a fragile chair. Every day an old man would come and sit in the chair and relax.

One day, a curious fox came and peeked through the temple window. He saw the old man relaxing and he wanted to try it too!

So the fox hopped through the window and made himself comfortable in the old man's chair. He relaxed, and was very happy.

But when the old man returned, he was very surprised to see the fox in his chair. He quickly chased the fox away and put the chair back in its original place. The old man took a deep breath, relaxed, and the forest was still again.

Sam had a watch that he liked very much. It was blue and shiny and it made a tick-tock sound. He wore it every day and showed it to his friends. He felt mighty with his watch.

One day, a man came to his house. He had a big bag full of toys and books. He said he wanted to sell them to Sam and his mom. He saw Sam's watch and said, "What a nice watch you have! Do you want to trade it for something in my bag?"

Sam looked at the bag and saw many things that he wanted. He saw a red car, a yellow ball, a green dinosaur, a brown bear, and a big book with pictures. He thought they were all very fun and cool. He said, "Yes, I want to trade my watch for something in your bag. What can I have?"

The man smiled and said, "You can have anything you want, but only one thing. Choose wisely, because you can't change your mind later." He opened the bag and let Sam see all the things inside.

Sam thought hard. He liked his watch, but he also liked the toys and books. He wanted to have them all, but he knew he had to pick one. He looked at the red car, the yellow ball, the green dinosaur, the brown bear, and the big book. He wondered which one he would play with the most. He wondered which one would make him feel mighty.

He decided to trade his watch for the big book. He liked books because they had stories and pictures that he could look at and read. He thought the book would make him learn new things and have new adventures. He said, "I want the big book, please."

The man nodded and said, "Okay, here you go. Give me your watch and take the book. It's a fair trade." He took Sam's watch and gave him the book. He said, "Thank you, Sam. Enjoy your book. Goodbye." He left with his bag and Sam's watch.

Sam opened the book and saw many pages with words and drawings. He felt happy and excited. He said, "Mom, look at my book! It's so big and nice! Can you read it to me?"

His mom smiled and said, "Sure, Sam. I'm glad you like your book. It looks very interesting. Let's sit down and read it together." She hugged him and said, "You are a mighty boy, Sam. You made a good choice."

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to fish. They had a big pole that their dad gave them. They went to the lake with their pole and a bucket. They hoped to catch many fish and sell them at the market.

They saw a man with a loud voice and a sign that said "Fish for sale". He had many fish in his cart. He shouted, "Come and buy my fresh fish! They are tasty and cheap!" Tim and Sam wanted to sell their fish like him. They thought he was very smart and rich.

They threw their pole in the water and waited. They waited for a long time, but no fish came. They felt sad and bored. They wondered why the man had so many fish and they had none. They decided to ask him for a tip.

They walked to the man and said, "Hello, sir. We are trying to catch fish and sell them, but we have no luck. Can you tell us your secret?"

The man looked at them and smiled. He said, "Sure, boys. I'll tell you my secret. I don't catch fish. I buy them from the store and sell them here. It's easier and faster. Do you want to buy some?"

Tim and Sam were shocked and angry. They felt cheated and lied to. They said, "No, thank you. We don't want your fish. You are not smart and rich. You are sneaky and bad. We will catch our own fish with our pole. Goodbye!"

They ran back to their pole and bucket. They hoped to catch a big fish and show the man. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that not everyone is honest and that fishing is hard work. But they also learned that fishing is fun and rewarding. They enjoyed their time at the lake with their pole and their bucket.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She wanted to perform a very special show.

So she went outside to find the perfect thing to use. She found a big yellow pine tree. She loved it!

She grabbed some of leaves and twigs from around the tree and used them to create a stage. Then she began her performance.

She sang and danced and played games in front of the yellow pine tree. Everyone in the neighbourhood came to watch her and were amazed at her performance.

When the show was over, the little girl was very proud. She said, "I knew I could perform a wonderful show!"

Once upon a time, there was a big forest. In the forest, there was a wild lion. The lion was very hungry and wanted to eat something tasty. So, he went to a nearby farm where he saw a cow. The lion thought the cow looked delicious, so he tried to catch it. But the farmer saw the lion and quickly came to serve the lion some beef. The lion was happy and ate the beef instead of the cow. From that day on, the lion visited the farmer every time he was hungry, and the farmer always served him beef.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Timmy. Timmy loved pastries, especially the ones his mom made. One day, Timmy's mom made a big pastry that was too heavy for her to carry. So, Timmy decided to help his mom and carried the pastry to the kitchen table. Timmy was so strong and flexible that he didn't even drop the pastry! Timmy's mom was so proud of him and gave him a big hug. From that day on, Timmy knew he could always help his mom carry heavy things.

Mama and Papa had a party for their little girl. It was her third birthday. Everyone had come over to celebrate. There was cake, games, and balloons. The little girl was so excited.

The guests all cheered as Mama and Papa gave the little girl a shiny new toy. "Thank you," she said with a smile.

Mama and Papa then revealed to the guests that the toy was actually a surprise. They said it was a trap. The little girl was curious and asked what it was. Papa explained it was like a game. He said if she did something the trap would make a noise and they would all applaud.

The little girl was embarrassed, but she was excited too. She stepped up to the trap and tried her best. When the trap finally made a sound, everyone clapped and cheered. She was so proud of herself.

"See," Papa said, "you were brave and you did it!" The little girl smiled and hugged Papa. She was so happy to have accomplished something and everyone else was proud of her. It was her best birthday yet.

Once upon a time, there was a fancy piano. It was shiny, white and smooth. It just begged to be tickled and played! Everyone wanted a turn on that piano.

There were two siblings who were always fighting over it. The older brother would tease his little sister, saying he would only let her play if she played a certain song. She would huff and puff, but eventually she'd figure it out and play it perfectly! Then he'd cheer, 'You did it!'.

At other times, the brother would tell his little sister that only he knew how to play the piano. She could try, of course, but he was the only one with the talent. Then he'd play his fingers across the keys of the fancy piano, showing off his skill.

The little sister might pout, but eventually she'd join in, playing a song as brilliant as her brother's. They'd pause, then laugh and clap each other's hands. In the end, no one ever tired of playing the fancy piano, and it brought the brother and sister closer together each day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane liked to go swimming at the pool. She went swimming with her mom every Saturday.

One Saturday, Jane accidentally got her hair wet. Her mom said, "Oh no, we need to get shampoo and clean up that wet hair."

Then, Jane and her mom went to the store and bought some shampoo.

When they got home, Jane's mom filled the bathtub with warm water and bubbles. She gently put some shampoo in Jane's hair and started to massage her head. Jane felt so cozy and relaxed.

After Jane's hair was nice and clean, she and her mom hugged. The hug was so comforting and warm.

Jane said, "I love swimming, mom!"

Her mom replied, "Me too, sweetheart!"

Bunny was a famous hopper. He could hop very high and very far. He liked to hop all over the forest and show off his skills. He made many friends with the other animals, who cheered for him and gave him carrots.

One day, Bunny saw a hut in a clearing. He had never seen a hut before. He was curious and wanted to hop inside. He hopped closer and closer, until he reached the door. He knocked with his paw, but no one answered. He pushed the door and it opened.

Bunny hopped inside the hut. It was dark and dusty. He saw a big bed, a table, a chair, and a cupboard. He also saw a basket full of food. He smelled honey and bread and cheese. He was hungry and wanted to taste them.

He hopped to the basket and took a bite of the cheese. It was yummy. He took another bite, and another. He did not hear the footsteps outside. He did not see the shadow on the wall. He did not notice the big bad wolf who lived in the hut.

The wolf came in and saw Bunny eating his cheese. He was angry and hungry. He roared and showed his teeth. He wanted to eat Bunny for his lunch. Bunny was scared and sorry. He dropped the cheese and tried to hop away. But the wolf was faster and blocked the door.

Bunny was trapped. He wished he had not hopped inside the hut. He wished he had stayed with his friends in the forest. He wished he had listened to his mother, who told him not to go near the hut. He closed his eyes and waited for the end.

But then, he heard a loud noise. He opened his eyes and saw a big axe. It smashed the door and made a hole. He saw a man with a beard and a hat. He was a woodcutter, who worked in the forest. He saw the wolf and the bunny. He was brave and strong. He swung his axe and hit the wolf. The wolf howled and ran away.

Bunny was saved. He was happy and grateful. He thanked the woodcutter, who smiled and patted his head. He gave him some honey and bread and told him to go back to his friends. He warned him not to hop inside strange huts again. He said goodbye and left.

Bunny hopped out of the hut. He felt lucky and learned a lesson. He decided to be more careful and not to be too curious. He hopped back to the forest and found his friends. He told them what happened and they hugged him and gave him carrots. He was still a famous hopper, but he was also a wiser bunny.

One day, a little red car named Zoomy loved to zoom around his town. He liked to make a loud whistle sound as he went fast. The sun was warm and bright today, so Zoomy went out to play.

Zoomy saw his friend, a big blue car named Biggy. Biggy said, "Zoomy, can I join you to play?" Zoomy said, "Yes, but we must race to see who is the fastest!" Biggy agreed, and they started to race. Zoomy went zoom and made a loud whistle sound, but Biggy was going faster.

THE ELVES AND THE SHOEMAKER

There was once a shoemaker, who worked very hard and was very honest:

but still he could not earn enough to live upon; and at last all he

had in the world was gone, save just leather enough to make one pair of

shoes.

Then he cut his leather out, all ready to make up the next day, meaning

to rise early in the morning to his work. His conscience was clear and

his heart light amidst all his troubles; so he went peaceably to bed,

left all his cares to Heaven, and soon fell asleep. In the morning after

he had said his prayers, he sat himself down to his work; when, to his

great wonder, there stood the shoes all ready made, upon the table. The

good man knew not what to say or think at such an odd thing happening.

He looked at the workmanship; there was not one false stitch in the

whole job; all was so neat and true, that it was quite a masterpiece.

The same day a customer came in, and the shoes suited him so well that

he willingly paid a price higher than usual for them; and the poor

shoemaker, with the money, bought leather enough to make two pairs more.

In the evening he cut out the work, and went to bed early, that he might

get up and begin betimes next day; but he was saved all the trouble, for

when he got up in the morning the work was done ready to his hand. Soon

in came buyers, who paid him handsomely for his goods, so that he bought

leather enough for four pair more. He cut out the work again overnight

and found it done in the morning, as before; and so it went on for some

time: what was got ready in the evening was always done by daybreak, and

the good man soon became thriving and well off again.

One evening, about Christmas-time, as he and his wife were sitting over

the fire chatting together, he said to her, 'I should like to sit up and

watch tonight, that we may see who it is that comes and does my work for

me.' The wife liked the thought; so they left a light burning, and hid

themselves in a corner of the room, behind a curtain that was hung up

there, and watched what would happen.

As soon as it was midnight, there came in two little naked dwarfs; and

they sat themselves upon the shoemaker's bench, took up all the work

that was cut out, and began to ply with their little fingers, stitching

and rapping and tapping away at such a rate, that the shoemaker was all

wonder, and could not take his eyes off them. And on they went, till the

job was quite done, and the shoes stood ready for use upon the table.

This was long before daybreak; and then they bustled away as quick as

lightning.

The next day the wife said to the shoemaker. 'These little wights have

made us rich, and we ought to be thankful to them, and do them a good

turn if we can. I am quite sorry to see them run about as they do; and

indeed it is not very decent, for they have nothing upon their backs to

keep off the cold. I'll tell you what, I will make each of them a shirt,

and a coat and waistcoat, and a pair of pantaloons into the bargain; and

do you make each of them a little pair of shoes.'

The thought pleased the good cobbler very much; and one evening, when

all the things were ready, they laid them on the table, instead of the

work that they used to cut out, and then went and hid themselves, to

watch what the little elves would do.

About midnight in they came, dancing and skipping, hopped round the

room, and then went to sit down to their work as usual; but when they

saw the clothes lying for them, they laughed and chuckled, and seemed

mightily delighted.

Then they dressed themselves in the twinkling of an eye, and danced and

capered and sprang about, as merry as could be; till at last they danced

out at the door, and away over the green.

The good couple saw them no more; but everything went well with them

from that time forward, as long as they lived.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to eat delicious things. One day, her mom gave her a lemon. Lucy had never seen a lemon before. She thought it was a delicious yellow ball.

Lucy wanted to eat the lemon, but her mom did not allow her. She told Lucy to wait until after dinner. Lucy was sad, but she listened to her mom. She played with her toys and forgot about the lemon for a while.

After dinner, Lucy's mom gave her the lemon. Lucy took a big bite and made a funny face. It was not delicious like she thought! It was sour! Lucy laughed and her mom laughed too. The moral of the story is to listen to your parents because they know best.

Once upon a time, there was a charming little girl named Lucy. She had beautiful blonde hair and a big, happy smile. Her favorite thing was to play outside and explore nature.

One day, Lucy was walking through the woods when she came across a big cookie. She was so excited that she shouted, "Oh wow! A cookie!" She started to run towards the cookie, but then she remembered she was supposed to quit eating sweets.

Lucy sighed and said out loud, "I know mom said to quit eating sweets, but this cookie looks soooooo yummy!" She was trying so hard to decide what to do. Then a charming little squirrel came out of the trees and scolded, "Quit eating that cookie and go play outside, silly Lucy!"

Lucy smiled and said, "Thank you, squirrel. I think I'll quit eating the cookie and play outside instead." She waved goodbye to the squirrel and ran off to explore and find adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play football with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend asked him if he wanted to join a football team. Timmy felt excited but also a little scared because he knew football could be difficult.

Timmy decided to give it a try and joined the team. At first, he found it very difficult to keep up with the other players. He felt sad and wanted to quit. However, his coach encouraged him and told him that with practice, he could become a great football player.

Timmy kept practicing and soon he started to feel more confident. He was able to keep up with the other players and even scored a goal in a game! Timmy learned that even when things feel difficult, if he keeps trying and practicing, he can achieve anything he wants.

Lily was a tall girl who liked to eat toast for breakfast. She liked to put butter and jam on her toast and make it sweet and soft. She also liked to tell stories to her little brother, Ben, who was still in his crib.

One morning, Lily woke up early and went to the kitchen. She saw a big loaf of bread on the counter and decided to make toast for herself and Ben. She took two slices of bread and put them in the toaster. She waited for them to pop up and then took them out. She put butter and jam on them and put them on a plate.

She carried the plate to Ben's room and saw him sleeping. She smiled and said, "Wake up, Ben! I have toast for you!" She put the plate on his nightstand and climbed into his crib. She gave him a hug and a kiss and said, "Good morning, Ben! Do you want to hear a story?"

Ben opened his eyes and saw Lily and the toast. He smiled and said, "Yes, please! I love your stories!" He took a bite of the toast and said, "Mmm, this is yummy! Thank you, Lily!"

Lily said, "You're welcome, Ben! Now, listen to my story. It's about a tall princess who lived in a castle with a dragon. She was brave and smart and kind. Do you want to know what she did?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, yes, tell me more!"

Lily smiled and began to tell her story. She used her voice and her hands to make it fun and exciting. Ben listened and laughed and asked questions. They ate their toast and enjoyed their story. They were happy and loved each other very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside in the dirt and mud. One day, his mom told him to come inside and wash his hands before eating his food. Timmy didn't want to stop playing, so he ignored his mom's reminder.

Later that day, Timmy's tummy started to hurt. He realized he had eaten his food with dirty hands. He went to his mom and said, "Mommy, my tummy hurts. I think I ate my food with dirty hands." His mom said, "I reminded you to wash your hands before eating. Now you know why it's important."

From that day on, Timmy always remembered to wash his hands before eating his food. He didn't want his tummy to hurt again.

Once upon a time there was a black goat who loved to delay his bedtime. Every night, he would sneak out of the barn and make his way to the meadow. He liked to run in the grass and pick clover flowers.

One night, the farmer noticed him leaving and followed behind him. He was very frustrated with the goat delaying his bedtime and wanted to teach him a lesson. As the farmer approached, the goat panicked and quickly ran away in the other direction!

He found himself in a dark, scary forest and couldn't find his way out. The goat was so scared he brayed as loud as he could. The farmer heard and followed in the direction of the sound. Eventually they both made it out of the forest and the farmer realised how late it had gotten.

The farmer then scolded the goat for delaying his bedtime and signed him up for goat training classes. After many months of classes, the goat finally understood the importance of getting to bed at a reasonable time. The farmer was so pleased that he rewarded the goat with some fresh clover flowers. The black goat never delayed bedtime again and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was rich and the other wasn't. One day, they decided to have a race. The rich one had a triangle and the other one had a long stick. They both put their objects on the floor, ready to race.

"Ready, set, go!" shouted the rich friend. Both of them started to speed across the room. The triangle whizzed faster than the other one, because it was so light. The rich friend won the race, but it was fun for both of them.

When they finished, the poor friend said, "That was fun! But I think I'll stick to using my stick from now on!" The rich friend replied, "That's a good idea!"

The two friends laughed and enjoyed the race. It was a fun time for both of them. They enjoyed playing together and running as fast as they could!

Once upon a time there was a famous wall. All the people in the neighbourhood would talk about how special it was.

One day, a little girl named Sarah was walking past, when she heard two voices coming from the wall. She stopped to listen, and realised that it was coming from a cat and a bird who were both sitting on the wall.

The cat said to the bird, "I want to be famous too!"

The bird replied, "You already are famous! Everyone in the neighbourhood talks about how special you are."

Sarah smiled and continued on her way, feeling lucky that she had heard the conversation.

Charles was anxious to explore outside. He looked out of his window and saw an interesting garage. He wondered what was inside.

Charles put on his shoes and ran outside to observe the garage. He approached the garage door, but it was locked. No matter how hard he tried, it wouldn't budge.

Charles stepped back to look around. Suddenly, he noticed a key hidden beneath the doormat. He took the key and inserted it into the door lock. It opened!

Charles went inside and was amazed by all the tools and gadgets. He saw tools he hadn't seen before and felt excited to explore and play. He looked around and enjoyed the adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit, who lived in a wood. He hopped along until he came across a white flea. He looked at it very carefully, with his big brown eyes.

The rabbit was very curious and couldn't help but wonder why the flea was so white. The flea said, "I've been eating a lot of snow!"

The rabbit was so shocked that he was speechless. He couldn't believe what he had heard.

The flea thought the rabbit was so cute. He asked, "Would you like to join me for breakfast? I've got some yummy snow over here!"

The rabbit was very excited, so he nodded and hopped over. They enjoyed their tasty meal together, talking and laughing all morning long.

At the end of the day, they said goodbye to each other and the white flea hopped away.

The rabbit thought of his white friend fondly whenever he saw the snow.

One day, a fast driver named Tim went for a ride in his loud car. He loved to speed down the street and feel the wind in his hair. As he drove, he saw his friend, Sam, standing by the road.

"Hi, Sam!" Tim called out. "Do you want to go for a ride?"

"Yes, please!" Sam said, and he got in the car. They drove around the town, going fast and having fun. The car was very loud, and everyone could hear them coming.

At last, they stopped at the park to play. They ran and laughed until it was time to go home. Tim and Sam had a great day together, speeding in the loud car and playing in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond with his friends. One day, it started to rain a lot and the pond started to get bigger and bigger. The water was coming so fast that it looked like a big river. Ducky got scared and started to swim faster and faster to get away from the flood.

Ducky's friends were also swimming fast to get away from the flood. They all swam to a big tree and climbed up to stay safe. Ducky was very ashamed because he was the last one to get up the tree. But his friends were happy that he made it.

After the rain stopped, the flood went away and the pond was back to normal. Ducky and his friends were happy to be back in the pond, but they knew they had to be careful when it rained so they wouldn't have to speed away from a flood again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books with big pictures. One day, she went to the library with her mommy. She looked at all the books on the shelves, but she couldn't find any with pictures that she liked.

Suddenly, she saw a book with a wild animal on the cover. It was a lion with a big, furry mane. She stared at the lion and said to her mommy, "Look at this book! It has a big, wild lion on it!"

Her mommy smiled and said, "Let's check it out and see if the print inside is as good as the cover." They took the book home and Lily read it over and over again. She loved the pictures and the story about the lion's adventures. From that day on, she always looked for books with big, wild animals on the cover.

Once upon a time there was a gifted hockey player. He was very good at playing the sport. Every day he practiced his skills in the park.

He would rest between drills and games. He would take a break and sip some water. After resting he was ready to practice again.

Sometimes his hockey marbles would go very fast. He was so proud when his mom cheered him on. He could feel that he was getting gifted at playing hockey.

At the end of the day he was tired. He needed to rest his body and mind. So he grabbed his hockey stick and went home. He needed some rest to be ready for the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to walk with his cane. He would take it with him everywhere he went. One day, Tim went for a walk in the park. He walked and walked, but he couldn't find his cane. He looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found.

Tim was very sad. He sat down on a bench and started to cry. Suddenly, he heard a noise behind him. He turned around and saw his persistent little dog, Max, carrying his cane in his mouth. Tim was so surprised and happy to see his cane again. He hugged Max and gave him a big kiss. From that day on, Tim and Max went on many walks together with Tim's trusty cane.

One day, the little girl went to the beach. She saw lots of other kids swimming and playing in the water. But one man caught her eye. He had a big mustache and a very lively personality.

It was a lovely summer morning, and two children were out in the forest. They were looking for animals and feeling the breeze on their faces.

Suddenly, they spotted a deer sleeping in the shade of a tree. "Look!" said the first child, "Let's not wake the deer. Let's just watch."

The children sat down and looked at the deer for a long time. "Isn't it lovely?" said the second child.

The deer slept peacefully. Just when the children were about to move on, the deer opened its beautiful eyes and looked at them. "Don't be scared," said the first child, "You can rest here".

The deer looked at them with its big eyes, then nodded a silent thanks. And so the children stayed with the lovely deer and watched it rest in the morning sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park. One day, Timmy wanted to go to the park with his mom, but his mom was feeling very cold. Timmy asked his mom, "Mommy, are you cold?"

His mom replied, "Yes, Timmy, I am very cold. I don't think I can start the car to go to the park."

Timmy wanted to help his mom. He said, "I can carry your coat, Mommy. That will make you feel warm."

His mom smiled and said, "Thank you, Timmy. That is very kind of you." Timmy carried his mom's coat and they started walking to the park. They had a great time playing together and Timmy felt happy that he could help his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy cart. He would push it around the house and fill it with his favorite toys.

One day, Tim saw his friend, Sam, playing with a big, shiny new cart. Tim felt envious of Sam's cart. He wanted one just like it. Tim's face showed a frown because he was sad.

Tim's mom saw his frown and asked him what was wrong. Tim told her about Sam's cart. His mom said, "It's okay to feel envious, but remember to be happy with what you have." Tim thought about it and smiled. He played with his cart, happy that he had a toy he loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a small pocket in his red shirt. One day, Tim put a spicy pepper in his pocket. He wanted to play a fun game with his friends.

At the park, Tim met his friends, Sam and Lily. They played on the swings and slides. Tim forgot about the spicy pepper in his pocket. He blinked as he thought of his game.

Later, Tim, Sam, and Lily were very hungry. They sat down to eat their lunch. Tim blinked and remembered the spicy pepper in his pocket. He took it out and put it in his sandwich. When he took a big bite, his mouth felt hot! Tim laughed and shared the spicy pepper with Sam and Lily. They all laughed and had a fun, spicy lunch.

Once upon a time, there was a nice little boy named Tim. He loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Tim met a quiet little girl named Sue. They decided to play together and became good friends.

While they were playing, Tim said, "Let's finish our game of blocks!" Sue nodded and they both started to build a big tower. They worked together and soon had a very tall tower. Tim and Sue were very happy with their tower.

As they played, Tim and Sue learned to share and be nice to each other. They had so much fun playing together that they didn't want the day to end. But when it was time to go home, they said goodbye and promised to play again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily who loved to play in her garden. She liked to smell the flowers and watch the butterflies. One day, her mom asked her to help provide some water for the plants. Lily was happy to help and got a big watering can. She watered all the flowers and plants until they were happy and healthy.

But then, Lily's friend came over to play and saw her watering the garden. She laughed and said, "You look embarrassed with that big watering can!" Lily felt shy and didn't want to play anymore. But her mom came and said, "Don't be embarrassed, Lily. You did a great job providing water for the garden. The plants are so happy now!" Lily smiled and felt happy again. From that day on, she was proud to help take care of her garden.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. There is a big slide in the park. Lily and Ben want to go on the slide.

But the slide is too high for them. They cannot reach the ladder. They try to jump, but they fall. They are sad.

"Let's climb the tree!" Ben says. He has an idea. He sees a tree next to the slide. The tree has many branches.

They reach the top of the tree. They can see the slide. They can see the whole park. They are happy.

"Look, Lily, we are so high!" Ben says.

"Yes, Ben, we are!" Lily says.

They smile at each other. They are proud. They have fun in the tree. They forget about the slide.

Tommy was playing in the sand. He forgot his bucket. He wanted to make a sandcastle but he didn't have a bucket. He felt sad.

Then, he saw a pretty blue egg in the sand. He picked it up and smiled. He quickly ran home with the egg so he could show his mom.

When Tommy got inside, he found his mom. She was feeling jealous because his dad had bought a new toy for his sister.

Tommy showed his mom the egg and said "Look Mommy! I found a special egg!". His mom smiled and hugged him. She suddenly felt better. Tommy was happy that he could make his mom feel better.

They put the egg in a bowl on the kitchen table. Tommy and his mom looked at the egg and smiled together. Tommy was glad that he didn't forget his egg.

Once upon a time, in a big house there was a little boy named Timmy. He was three years old and was always very curious. One day, while playing in the garden, Timmy saw something white in the sky. It seemed to be a fly. He darted over to look more closely.

"What is this thing?" He asked.

As he investigated, he heard a little voice. It was the fly speaking. She said, "My name is Daisy. I am here to reveal something to you."

Timmy was surprised, but he asked Daisy to tell him what the secret was.

She replied, "The secret is that everyone needs to be kind and helpful to each other. We can all work together to make the world a better place."

Timmy was so excited about Daisy's secret and he couldn't wait to tell everyone. He wanted to make sure that everyone he knew knew the secret too, so that the world could become a better place.

The moral of the story is that a little kindness and help can go a long way and make the world a happier place.

Once upon a time there was a wise tank. He was a friendly tank who liked to help everyone he could. One day he noticed that a delivery truck was delayed. He quickly ran over to the truck to see what was wrong. He saw that the driver was stuck trying to fix the engine. The wise tank decided to help the driver. He used his strong hands to tighten the engine and soon enough the truck was able to drive away. Everyone cheered and thanked the wise tank for his help. The wise tank just smiled and was happy that he could help.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sue. Sue really wanted to improve her house, so she decided to paint her toilet! She got the paint from the store and she made it a lovely bright blue.

Sue was very proud of her new toilet and she invited all her friends over to admire it. Even Sue's mom and dad were impressed by the paint job!

Sue's mom was so happy that she decided to make everyone a very tasty treat as a reward. She made a big cake with lots of sprinkles, and everyone ate it up with joy.

Sue was so proud of her improved house, and her sister was so happy too. They decided that they would help the rest of the family improve their homes too. Sue and her sister had made their home much better and brighter!

Mia was a little girl and she was three years old. She had a pretty dress and she loved to wear it with her shoes. One day, Mia and her mama decided to go the pool. Mia couldn't wait to get there.

When they arrived, Mia was very excited. She put on her swimming suit and jumped in the pool. She swam around and around and had so much fun. After a while, mama said "Mia it's time for lunch, let's go eat something."

Mia jumped out of the pool and dried off. She put on her pretty dress and followed Mama to a restaurant. Mama said "Mia, what do you want to eat?" Mia said, "I want a yummy hamburger with French fries!" Mama told her that sounded delicious.

Mia and Mama ate their lunch together. After they finished eating, they went back to the pool. Mia had so much fun splashing around. She said to Mama, "This was a pretty great day!"

Once upon a time, there was a famous, long haired princess. Her hair was so beautiful that it even made grown-up kings and queens jealous!

One day, the princess decided to go to the market. She told her mom, "I am going to the market". When she was finished shopping, the princess visited a magical castle. Inside, she met a fairy and they became fast friends.

The fairy asked the princess, "What can I do to serve you today?" The princess answered, "I would love to have a new hairstyle".

The fairy smiled and said, "I will be more than happy to serve you". She waved her wand and the princess' hair changed into an even more beautiful style.

The princess was so excited about her new hair! "Thank you so much for serving me," she said to the fairy.

The fairy replied, "You are so welcome! I am glad to make you even more famous!" The fairy and the princess laughed and hugged. Together, they went for a walk in the beautiful, magical forest.

Sammy was playing in the backyard when it started to rain. He ran inside to the laundry room and saw his mom. She was washing the dark laundry in the big sink. Sammy's mom smiled and said, "Come help me wash the laundry, Sammy!" So he ran to her, took off his shoes, and jumped into the sink. He grabbed a wet pair of pants and scrubbed and scrubbed until the pants were clean. Mom put the clean, dark laundry into the basket and said, "Good job, Sammy! You helped me wash the laundry." Sammy smiled and said, "Let's do it again!"

Tommy enjoyed travelling with his family. They had been on the road all day and were very hungry.

Just as Tommy was about to cry, he opened his eyes to find himself standing in front of an incredible fridge! He was so excited and asked his mom, "Mommy, what's in the fridge?"

"Oh Tommy, that is special fridge full of yummy treats!"

His mom opened the door and started to take out the snacks. Inside were all of Tommy's favorite ice creams, cupcakes and chocolates.

Tommy was jumping with joy! His mom smiled lovingly and said, "Let's release these treats for everyone to enjoy!"

Tommy clapped his hands happily and began to share the treats with his family and friends. They all had an incredible time.

The trip was now complete, and Tommy was the happiest 3 year old around!

Once upon a time, there was a cabin in the woods. It was a very old cabin, but Jack liked it. He was a little boy who lived alone in the cabin with his puppy.

One day, Jack was very confused; he could smell something strange. It wasn't his puppy's food, it was something else. So, he followed his nose and went to the back of the cabin.

When Jack got to the back of the cabin, he saw smoke! The cabin had caught fire. It was burning so fast; he couldn't do anything to put it out.

Jack tried to run into the cabin, but it was already too late. He shouted out to his puppy, but it was too scared to come out. He cried, "My puppy's still inside! Help me!"

But no one came. Jack was alone, confused and scared. His cabin burned to the ground until nothing remained. Jack and his puppy were both gone forever.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to play together. They had different skin colors: Ben's skin was brown and Lily's skin was white. They did not care about that. They cared about having fun.

One day, they went to the park with their moms. They saw a big slide and ran to it. Ben went first and slid down fast. He laughed and said, "That was fun! Come on, Lily!"

Lily climbed up the ladder and got ready to slide. But then she saw a boy with red hair and green eyes. He was waiting for his turn. He looked at Lily and said, "Hey, you have weird skin. What is your name?"

Lily felt sad and scared. She did not like the boy's words. She said, "My name is Lily. What is your name?"

The boy said, "My name is Max. And I have the best skin. It is red and green, like a firework. You have boring skin. It is white, like snow. I am envious of nothing."

Ben heard what Max said. He felt angry and brave. He climbed up the ladder and stood next to Lily. He said, "You are wrong, Max. Lily's skin is not boring. It is beautiful, like a flower. And my skin is not weird. It is cool, like chocolate. We have different skin, but we are both good. You are envious of everything."

Max did not know what to say. He felt ashamed and small. He ran away from the slide. Ben and Lily smiled at each other. They slid down together and hugged. They were happy and proud. Their moms saw them and clapped. They had the best skin. It was the skin of friends.

Once there was a little boy named Jamie. He was curious and always wanted to learn new things. One day, Jamie asked his mom for help.

"Mom, what is that?" Jamie pointed to a beautiful metal box on the dresser.

His mom smiled. "That is a special box. I can send things in it to people far away. It's like magic!"

Jamie was excited. He wanted to send something too. He looked around his room and found a shiny marble. He put it in the box and closed the lid.

"Now what do I do?" he asked.

"Close your eyes and picture the person you want to send it to," his mom said.

Jamie closed his eyes and thought of his friend, Ryan. He imagined Ryan opening the box and being surprised by the beautiful marble.

Mom said that the box would make the marble travel to faraway places. Jamie wondered how the box could do such a thing. He opened his eyes and smiled. He was sure that Ryan would love his surprise.

Lila liked to jog with her dad. They jogged by the sea every morning. Lila loved to see the dolphins jump in the water. They were big and gray and had happy smiles.

One day, Lila saw a dolphin that was hurt. It had a net around its tail and it could not swim well. Lila felt sad for the dolphin. She wanted to help it. She told her dad to stop jogging and pointed at the dolphin.

Her dad saw the dolphin too. He said they had to be careful, but they could try to help. He took Lila to a boat nearby and asked the man if they could borrow it. The man said yes and gave them a knife. Lila and her dad got on the boat and went to the dolphin.

The dolphin was scared and tried to swim away, but it was too weak. Lila and her dad talked to the dolphin in soft voices. They said they were friends and they wanted to help. The dolphin calmed down and let them come closer. Lila's dad used the knife to cut the net from the dolphin's tail. The dolphin was free and happy. It thanked Lila and her dad with a loud splash and a big smile.

Lila and her dad went back to the shore. They were happy too. They had done a good thing. They hugged each other and jogged home. Lila learned that it is good to help others who are hurt. She hoped to see the dolphin again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in a small town. One day, she went out to the park to play. As she skipped around, she spotted a red ball. With a squeal of delight, she ran towards the ball and began to bounce it.

"Look at me, Mommy! I'm bouncing the ball!" the little girl exclaimed.

Her mom smiled. "Yes, you are! You look so happy!", she said.

The girl kept bouncing the ball until she got too tired. All of a sudden, she felt guilty. She had taken the ball without asking.

"Mommy, I'm sorry. I took the ball without asking," she said softly.

Her mom smiled. "It's okay, sweetheart. Let's take it back to the park tomorrow and let someone else have a turn," she said kindly.

The little girl smiled and hugged her mom. She felt much better now that she had taken responsibility for her actions.

The moral of the story is that it's important to take responsibility and not to feel guilty when we make mistakes.

Once upon a time there was a girl, she was very compassionate and always put others before her own needs. One day, she was walking down the street with her purse, when a mean gentleman stepped in front of her. He demanded that she give him her purse and he would not take no for an answer.

The girl was scared but also determined to stay strong. She replied, "No, I need my purse. I can't give it to you."

The gentleman becoming frustrated, started to raise his voice at her. He said, "You must give me the purse."

The girl feeling very brave, said, "No, I will never give it to you. You need to respect my decision."

The gentleman, realising he had come across someone with self-respect, sadly nodded and stepped aside, leaving her to walk on with her purse in hand. The girl was relieved, but also grateful that her compassion had helped her stay strong in a difficult situation.

Once upon a time there was a rich flower. The flower was very special and it was the most beautiful flower in the world. Every day, it would bloom the brightest colours. It made all the other flowers in the garden look dull in comparison.

One day, a little girl visited the garden. When she saw the flower, she was amazed by its beauty. She wanted to take the flower home with her. She had a fork in her pocket and she carefully dug it up with the fork.

When she took the flower home, something truly magical happened. Every day, the flower would bloom again and again. It kept giving the little girl gifts. She had the most beautiful garden in the world with the flower. Everybody was very happy.

The end.

Once there was a little boy named Ben. Ben liked shiny things, so when he saw a copper penny on the ground he ran over to get it. He liked the way the penny glinted in the sun.

But when Ben picked the penny up, he noticed a little ant underneath. The ant was trying hard to carry a small piece of food back to its nest. Ben knew the penny was too heavy for the ant, so he decided to help.

He knew the ant would not give up, so Ben insisted that he take the penny inside his house. He placed the penny in a special place in his room and promised to help the ant get its food back. He was determined and very persistent.

After several tries Ben was able to get the food to the ant's nest. The ant was very happy and thanked Ben for his kindness. Ben smiled and thanked the ant back. He was glad the ant was safe, and now he could keep the shiny copper penny that he found.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, especially near the river. One day, she saw a poor, little bird who couldn't fly because its wing was hurt. Lily felt sad for the bird and wanted to help it.

She thought that she could hold the bird and take it to the river to give it some water. But when she picked up the bird, it was too weak and slipped from her hands. The bird fell into the river and Lily couldn't save it. She felt very sad and cried.

Lily learned that holding things can be hard and sometimes it can make things worse. She realized that she should have asked for help instead of trying to do everything by herself. From then on, she promised to always ask for help when she needed it.

THE FOX AND THE CAT

It happened that the cat met the fox in a forest, and as she thought to

herself: 'He is clever and full of experience, and much esteemed in the

world,' she spoke to him in a friendly way. 'Good day, dear Mr Fox,

how are you? How is all with you? How are you getting on in these hard

times?' The fox, full of all kinds of arrogance, looked at the cat from

head to foot, and for a long time did not know whether he would give

any answer or not. At last he said: 'Oh, you wretched beard-cleaner, you

piebald fool, you hungry mouse-hunter, what can you be thinking of? Have

you the cheek to ask how I am getting on? What have you learnt? How

many arts do you understand?' 'I understand but one,' replied the

cat, modestly. 'What art is that?' asked the fox. 'When the hounds are

following me, I can spring into a tree and save myself.' 'Is that all?'

said the fox. 'I am master of a hundred arts, and have into the bargain

a sackful of cunning. You make me sorry for you; come with me, I will

teach you how people get away from the hounds.' Just then came a hunter

with four dogs. The cat sprang nimbly up a tree, and sat down at the top

of it, where the branches and foliage quite concealed her. 'Open your

sack, Mr Fox, open your sack,' cried the cat to him, but the dogs had

already seized him, and were holding him fast. 'Ah, Mr Fox,' cried the

cat. 'You with your hundred arts are left in the lurch! Had you been

able to climb like me, you would not have lost your life.'

Once upon a time there was a quiet attic. Inside the attic were two sisters. The older sister, named Emma, was always in charge.

One day while they were in the attic, Emma said to her younger sister, Lily. "Let's paint the walls of the attic!" Lily grinned, she had never painted before.

Emma gave Lily a pot of bright green paint and a brush. "Paint the wall! Go on! Be brave!"

Lily held the brush and took a deep breath. She dipped the brush into the pot of paint and started painting. She painted little circles, big circles and even triangles until the whole wall was covered in bright green.

When she finished painting, Lily looked around the attic. It was so quiet and even more wonderful with the walls painted green.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Lucy. She was three years old.

Every morning, Lucy's mommy would raise her up and give her a big smile. Then she'd give her some yummy breakfast. Sometimes it was pancakes with lots of sugar. Lucy's favorite!

After breakfast, Lucy would go outside and play. She was very impatient, always running and jumping around. She wanted to do more and more and more.

One day, Lucy saw her mommy raising a kite in the sky. It flew so high and far away. Lucy was so excited! She wanted to go higher and higher too. So her mommy said, "Why don't you raise your arms and see how high you can fly?"

So Lucy raised her arms and shouted, "Higher and higher!" Lucy was amazed at how high she could fly. She smiled and laughed with joy.

Lucy loved to raise things and see how far she could go. It made her happy. Sugar and patience had nothing on her energy!

Once upon a time, there was a little boat that loved to sail on the big blue sea. The boat was made of wood and had a white sail that would catch the wind and take it wherever it wanted to go. One day, the boat sailed to a faraway island where it saw a tall pine tree. The tree was so tall that it touched the sky! The boat was amazed by the tree's beauty and decided to stay there for a while.

But as the day turned into night, the sky turned pale and the wind started to blow very hard. The boat tried to sail away, but the wind was too strong and it couldn't move. Suddenly, a big wave came and hit the boat, making it crash into the pine tree. The boat was broken and it couldn't sail anymore. The little boat was very sad because it couldn't sail on the big blue sea anymore.

Bubba the bear was so excited to wake up in the morning. He couldn't wait to explore the forest. He was very hairy and loved the feel of the sun's warmth on his fur.

As he started walking, he saw something on the ground. He got closer and saw it was a piece of gum. He knew he wasn't allowed to eat it, so he bent down and grabbed it carefully.

"What are you going to do with that?" asked a nearby squirrel.

Bubba smiled. "I'm going to rub it on that big tree up ahead. I heard the gum can make it nice and shiny!"

The squirrel thought this sounded like fun and wanted to help. So the two friends took turns rubbing the gum on the tree, until it was nice and shiny. The tree looked so happy!

Bubba and his squirrel friend enjoyed the sunny day and went on to play the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She was three years old and loved to play. One day, she was playing with her toys when she saw something. It was small and moved fast. What was it? It was a little mouse! The mouse ran all around Amy's room and Amy wanted to catch it. She closed the door so the mouse couldn't get away. She wanted the mouse to be her friend. She said, "That mouse is mine!" She opened the door slowly and chased the mouse. She was so fast. She caught it in her hands and said, "I caught you!" But then she shut the door and opened it again quickly. The mouse was gone! That was why she had to shut the door so quickly. Now, Amy and the mouse were friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong jet. It could fly very high in the sky and go very fast. The jet belonged to a kind pilot who loved to take people on trips.

One day, the pilot decided to allow some children to come on board the jet. The children were very happy and excited to ride in the jet. They put on their seatbelts and held on tight as the jet took off into the sky.

As they flew, the children looked out the window and saw the clouds and the birds. They felt the wind blowing through their hair and the jet shaking a little bit. But they knew they were safe because the pilot was very experienced.

After a while, the jet landed safely back on the ground. The children thanked the pilot for allowing them to ride in the jet and they went home with big smiles on their faces, feeling very lucky to have had such a fun adventure.

Once there was a boy called Tom. Tom's mummy brought him a thermometer from the shop. It was an original thermometer, not a copy.

At school, all of Tom's friends were very impressed! They loved the original thermometer and wanted to touch it. Tom was very proud to show it off.
He brought it back home to keep it safe. Now, Tom and his mummy can use the thermometer to measure everyone's temperature when they are not feeling well.

Mummy and Daddy took their daughter to the beach. It was a lovely day. The little girl loved the clear blue sea, the white sand and the sunshine.

Mummy and Daddy wanted her to try something new. "Let's buy a surfboard," said Daddy. So they found a big, colourful surfboard and bought it.

The little girl had so much fun! She laughed as the waves carried her board forward and she felt the spray of the water on her face.

When it was time to go home, the little girl hugged the surfboard. The sun was setting and it looked even more lovely than it had that morning. Mummy and Daddy smiled at each other. They were so happy that their daughter was having such a great time at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy bear who didn't like to do anything. He always stayed in his cave, and never went for walks.

One day, he decided to go for a walk, but he quickly became annoyed. Everywhere he looked, there were leaves and stones on the ground, and he had to keep stopping to clean them away.

"Oh," said the bunny, "Well, why don't you let me help you clean up? That way, you can go on your walk without getting grumpy!"

The bear thought about it for a moment, then smiled. He and the bunny started cleaning the ground together, until everything was clean and neat. Then, the bear happily waved goodbye to the little bunny and went off on his walk.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Bella. She loved playing outside. One day, she went to the park with her mom. As she played on the swings, she saw an apple on the ground. She ran over and picked it up.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside and explore. One day, Timmy went on a walk and discovered a big, unusual rock. He thought it was so cool and wanted to show his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was only three years old, and loved making new friends. One day she saw a funny looking creature in the park. It was a little furry thing with pointy ears and a funny, long nose. The little girl thought it looked very mysterious.

Once, there was a little girl called Ruby. She was three years old and was always so curious and full of energy! She was very generous, and always wanted to help everyone.

One day, she went out to play in the park. She was wearing her favourite red coat, but it wasn't very warm and she was starting to feel cold. Then she saw a gentleman walking towards her. He smiled, and said "Hello. I'm feeling very generous today - would you like my coat?"

Once upon a time there was a faucet, who wanted to change. But at first, nothing happened. The faucet just sat there, all alone.

Mama and Dad were in the hall, looking at something. Mama looked very worried.

Once there was a little girl named Lily who loved to run. She would run all around her house and yard, giggling and laughing as she went. One day, her mom brought home a new scale to weigh themselves on. Lily was curious and wanted to see how much she weighed, but her mom told her she was too little to use the scale.

Lily was disappointed, but she didn't give up. She kept running and playing, hoping one day she would be big enough to use the scale. One day, she woke up feeling terrible. Her head hurt and her tummy felt funny. She didn't feel like running or playing at all.

Her mom took her to the doctor, who said she had a bad cold. The doctor gave her some medicine and told her to rest. Lily was sad she couldn't run or play, but she knew she needed to get better. After a few days of rest, Lily felt much better. Her mom let her use the scale, and she was so happy to see she had grown a little bit. From then on, Lily knew that taking care of herself was just as important as running and playing.

Once upon a time, there lived a chubby little girl. Every day, she would skip around the park and take a look at the fire. She was mesmerised by its beauty and warmth.

The old man showed the little girl how he could use fire to make cookies and cakes. The little girl smiled and had so much fun. The old man filled her heart with joy and it made her feel safe.

From that day, the chubby little girl wasn't scared of the fire anymore. She knew how to use it in a safe and fun way.

Bob was excited for the challenge and together he and his mom began to clean up the area. Slowly but surely, Bob's playground went back to being the happy place it had been before.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird was very hungry and wanted to eat some food. So, the bird flew to a tree and saw some berries. The bird ate the berries and felt happy.

After the dance, Tom and his mom went to the freezer and picked out a big box of ice cream. They went home and had a nice dinner. After dinner, they had the ice cream for dessert. Tom was very happy, and he knew that his dance made his mom happy too.

Once upon a time, a little girl lived in a big house. One day it was her birthday and her mummy and daddy had a surprise for her! They brought out a big box - inside was a beautiful red cushion! The little girl was so excited she jumped up and down.

The little girl would take the red cushion with her everywhere she went - it was such a beautiful and comfy cushion! Even when she was all grown up and moved away, she would take the cushion with her and act out stories. She was never too old for a red cushion with special magical powers!

Once upon a time there were two rabbits. They were hopping around in a field looking for something tasty to eat.

Suddenly, one of the rabbits stopped hopping. "Look over there,â€ it said. â€œIt's a pretty carrot!"
