One day, a small girl was walking through her garden. She saw a white oak tree standing tall and strong in the middle. She stopped and looked up at it in wonder.

The girl wanted to climb it so she carefully scaled the tree and soon found herself perched in a seat high up in the white oak. She was so happy with the view she had, she almost didn't want to come down!

But eventually, the girl tired and had to go. She climbed down carefully, never forgetting the wonderful white oak and the seat she sat in. From then on, she would visit the tree every day and be happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emily. She was three years old, and she liked finding new things.

One day, Emily went on a walk with her mom. They were in the garden, and Mom said, "Look, Emily! What do you see?"

"I see a zipper!" said Emily excitedly. Emily was very curious about the zipper, so she decided to be polite and ask.

"Mommy, what is that?"

"It's a zipper," replied Mom.

Emily then discovered she could open the zipper. She carefully opened it and found a box inside. She was so excited to open the box!

The box was full of fun toys! Emily had a great time playing with them. She and Mom played hide and seek with the toys for the rest of the day.

At the end, Emily was happy and tired. She had a wonderful day discovering new things.

Once upon a time, there were two little bees called Buzz and Zizz.
They lived in a big hive made of thick wood and warm wax. Everyday, Buzz and Zizz flew out of the hive to collect sweet nectar from the flowers in the garden.
They were very happy and lived happily together in the hive.
But one day, the hive was so full of nectar that Buzz and Zizz knew they had to find a way to store it.
So they decided to fold leaves and use them as little boats to sail their nectar away.
They worked together, folding many leaves and soon the hive was much less full. They were so proud of all their hard work!
Every day they went out and collected nectar, and filled the hive with their treasures. Life was good in their thick and cozy hive.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. They lived in a big house with a garden. Every day, the mom would prepare yummy food for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. She would use lots of colorful veggies and fruits to make the food healthy and tasty.

The dad would go to work with his folder full of papers. He was a busy man, but he always made time to play with his lively little girl. They would run and jump and laugh together in the garden.

One day, the family decided to have a picnic. The mom prepared sandwiches and fruit, while the dad packed the folder with some important papers. The little girl was so lively and excited to go on a picnic with her family. They had so much fun playing games and eating yummy food. It was a day they would always remember.

In the park, there was a big slide. Jack's eyes lit up as he ran up to it, looking handsome in his cute blue trousers and yellow shirt.

"Mommy, look!" he exclaimed.

Jack's mother smiled. "Wow, Jack, it looks so much fun!"

The two of them raced up the steps together, and Jack reached the top first. He looked around eagerly.

"Go, Jack!" his Mommy said with a laugh.

Jack took a deep breath and then pushed off. He slid all the way to the bottom, whooping with delight.

Mommy met him with a melon slice.

"Here you go, sweetheart," she said, handing it to him. "You look so cute!"

Jack smiled as he took a bite of the juicy melon.

Then, he ran back to the top of the slide, ready to do it all over again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red boat. It loved to sail on the water. The boat had a friend, a little blue car. The blue car lived in a garage.

One day, the boat asked the blue car to sail with it. The blue car was scared, but the boat said it would be fun. So, the blue car got on the boat. They sailed together on the water.

The sun was shining, and the blue car felt comfortable on the boat. They laughed and played all day. When the sun went down, they went back to the blue car's garage. The boat and the blue car were happy to be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big blue pool. It was a hot day and many kids were swimming in the pool. A little infant was sitting by the pool with her mom. She looked at the water and wanted to dive in. But she was too small and her mom said no.

Suddenly, a big boy ran past the infant and pushed her into the pool. The infant started to sink slowly. The big boy didn't notice and kept playing. The infant's mom saw what happened and quickly dove into the pool. She grabbed her infant and brought her back to the surface.

From that day on, the infant's mom never let her out of her sight near the pool. The infant learned to swim slowly and safely. And the big boy learned to be more careful around little kids.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Bun. Bun loved to hop around and play with his friends. One day, Bun felt very tired and needed to rest. He found a cozy spot under a big tree and closed his eyes.

As he rested, he thought about how much he loved his family and friends. He felt a warm feeling in his heart and knew that love was a wonderful thing.

After a while, Bun woke up feeling refreshed and ready to play again. He was persistent in his desire to have fun and didn't give up until he found his friends. They played together all day, and Bun was happy knowing that he could always rest when he needed to.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived an ugly duck. The duck was sad because no one wanted to play with him. He would sit by the pond and watch the other ducks swim and have fun.

One day, a little girl named Sue came to the pond. She saw the ugly duck and felt bad for him. Sue walked up to the duck and said, "Hi, do you want to play with me?" The ugly duck was surprised and happy. He requested, "Can I have some water to swim in?"

Sue nodded and found a bucket. She filled it with water and poured it into the pond. The ugly duck jumped in and splashed around. They both laughed and played together all day long.

From that day on, the ugly duck and Sue became best friends. They would meet at the pond every day to play and have fun. The other ducks saw how happy the ugly duck was and wanted to join in too. Soon, the ugly duck wasn't lonely anymore, and everyone in the village loved him.

Jimmy's mom was in the kitchen cooking dinner. It was nice and clean like it usually was. "What are you doing in there?" Jimmy asked.

His mom smiled and answered, "I am making your favorite food for tonight!"

Jimmy felt very excited about that and went to the kitchen to show his mom something. Once he got there, he noticed something was not right. The kitchen was filthy! There were food scraps on the floor, grease on the walls and spills on the counter.

"Mommy, what happened?" Jimmy asked. "I was cleaning up mess the neighbors made," his mom answered.

Jimmy was sad because he didn't get to show his mom his surprise. Then, he ran out to the neighbors house and knocked on the door. He asked the neighbors to please clean up the mess they made. But the neighbors just laughed and shut the door.

Jimmy was so sad he started to cry. His mom felt bad and tried to clean up as much as she could, but it was too late. The kitchen was a mess and Jimmy's surprise was ruined.

Lily liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna had a pink dress and a yellow hat. Lily liked to dress Anna and comb her hair.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the park. Lily brought Anna with her. She saw a big slide and wanted to go on it. She asked her mom if she could go. Her mom said yes, but told her to hold Anna tight.

Lily climbed up the stairs and sat on the slide. She held Anna tight. She slid down fast and laughed. She liked the slide. She wanted to go again.

But when she got up, she saw a stranger. The stranger was a boy. He had a blue shirt and a green cap. He was holding Anna. He had taken Anna from Lily.

Lily was scared and angry. She ran to the boy and shouted, "Give me Anna! She is mine! You are a bad stranger!"

The boy looked at Lily and said, "No, she is mine! I like her! She is pretty!"

He tried to run away with Anna, but Lily was faster. She caught up with him and grabbed Anna. She pulled hard and got Anna back.

The boy cried and said, "That is not fair! You are mean!"

Lily hugged Anna and said, "No, you are mean! You took Anna from me! She does not fit you! She fits me!"

She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom was proud of Lily. She said, "You are brave, Lily. You did the right thing. Anna is yours. You love her and take care of her. The stranger was wrong. He should not take things that are not his."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you and Anna. Can we go on the slide again?"

Her mom said, "Yes, we can. But be careful and watch out for strangers."

Lily nodded and said, "I will, mom. I will hold Anna tight."

They went on the slide again and had fun. Lily and Anna were happy.

Once there was a little boy called John. He was only three years old. One day, he had an idea. He wanted to swing in his garden. So he looked around for something he could use. Suddenly he saw a green rope! He took the rope and ran to the biggest tree in the garden. John demanded that his mum help him to tie the rope to the tree.

Mum smiled and carefully tied the green rope around the tree. John got very excited and jumped onto the rope. He laughed and laughed as he swung higher and higher! He had so much fun in his garden that day.

It was very tiring, so at the end of the day, John curled up in his favourite chair, ready to take a nap. It was going to be a special summer.

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl who loved to play games. One day, she saw a marble on the ground. It was very hard and shiny. The brave girl wanted to save it, so she put it in her pocket.

Then, the brave girl went to play in a tree. But suddenly, she heard a loud crack. The tree was falling down! The brave girl tried to jump away, but she couldn't.

The brave girl held her pocket tight. She wanted to save the marble. But it was too late. The tree fell on her and she couldn't move.

The brave girl said goodbye to the hard marble. She couldn't save it. In the end, she was very sad.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a lot of trees. They wanted to discover what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Lily!" Ben said. "Maybe we can find a treasure or a secret cave!"

"OK, Ben!" Lily said. "But be careful. It looks dark and spooky over there."

They ran up the hill, holding hands. They heard a loud noise. It was the wind. It was blowing hard and making the trees shake and the leaves fly.

"Wow, look at the wind, Lily!" Ben said. "It's so strong and fast!"

Lily felt scared. She did not like the wind. It made her cold and it made her hair go in her eyes. She wanted to go back to the park.

"Ben, I don't like the wind," Lily said. "Can we go back, please?"

Ben looked at Lily. He saw that she was scared. He wanted to make her feel better.

"OK, Lily," Ben said. "We can go back. But first, let's do something fun. Let's make a kite!"

Ben found a stick and a plastic bag. He tied the bag to the stick with a string. He gave it to Lily.

"Here, Lily," Ben said. "This is a kite. You can hold it and let the wind lift it up. It will fly like a bird!"

Lily took the kite. She felt curious. She wanted to try it.

"Thank you, Ben," Lily said. "How do I make it fly?"

Ben showed her how to hold the string and run with the kite. They ran down the hill, laughing and shouting. The kite flew high in the sky, dancing with the wind.

Lily felt happy. She liked the kite. She liked the wind. She was not scared anymore.

She hugged Ben and said, "You are the best, Ben. You made me discover something new and fun. I love you."

Ben hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the best, too. You made me discover something new and sweet."

Sara and Ben like to watch videos on the big screen. They have many videos of animals, songs and stories. Sometimes they share the videos, and sometimes they want different ones.

One day, Sara wants to watch a video of a princess, but Ben wants to watch a video of a dinosaur. They both grab the same video and pull hard. The video tears in half and makes a loud noise. Sara and Ben start to cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see what happened. She sees the broken video and the sad children. She is not happy. She says, "Sara and Ben, you should not tear the video. That is not nice. You should be modest and take turns. Now you cannot watch any video today. Go to your rooms and think about what you did."

Sara and Ben feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not mean to tear the video. We just wanted to watch it. Can we say sorry to each other and hug?"

Mom smiles and says, "That is a good idea. You can say sorry and hug, and then you can play with your toys. Maybe tomorrow you can watch a new video, if you are modest and share."

Sara and Ben say sorry and hug. They go to their rooms and play with their toys. They learn to be modest and share. They are happy again.

Tim and his mom went to the park. Tim liked to play with the swings and the slide. He saw a big dog with a leash. The dog was brown and had long hair. Tim thought the dog was ugly.

"Mom, can I pet the dog?" Tim asked.

"No, Tim, you don't know the dog. He might bite you," Mom said.

"But he looks nice. He has a leash. He can't run away," Tim said.

"That doesn't mean he is nice, Tim. The leash is for the owner to manage the dog, not for you to pet him. Come on, let's go to the sandbox," Mom said.

Tim was sad. He wanted to pet the dog. He followed Mom to the sandbox. He saw another dog there. The dog was small and white and had short hair. Tim thought the dog was cute.

"Mom, can I pet this dog?" Tim asked.

"Yes, Tim, you can. This dog belongs to our friend Lily. She is here with her dad. The dog is friendly and likes children. But you have to ask Lily first," Mom said.

Tim ran to Lily and her dad. He asked if he could pet the dog. Lily said yes. She gave Tim the leash. Tim petted the dog. The dog licked his face. Tim was happy. He liked the dog. He thanked Lily and gave her back the leash.

"See, Tim, not all dogs are the same. Some are ugly and some are cute. Some are nice and some are not. You have to be careful and ask before you pet them," Mom said.

"I understand, Mom. I like cute and nice dogs. I don't like ugly and not nice dogs," Tim said.

"Good, Tim. Now let's go have some ice cream," Mom said.

Tim and his mom left the park. They had a good day.

One day, Timmy went to the beach by himself. He was feeling lonely. When he got there, he noticed the sand all around. It was so soft and golden. Especially the sand near the shore which was glimmering in the sun.

He had his bucket with him and he started to collect shells and small rocks. After a while, he heard a voice behind him.

"What do you observe?" said the voice.

Timmy turned around and saw a small crab. He smiled and said, "I can see the sand. It's so beautiful and sparkly".

The crab replied, "Yes, the sand is amazing. I like the sand too".

And then Timmy continued to explore the beach. He was no longer lonely and he enjoyed his time there observing the sand and everything else around.

Once there was a wise old lady. One day she went outside her house and saw a board lying in the grass. She seemed to think it was a special board. She took it inside and put it in the corner of her living room.

The next day when the old lady awoke, the board seemed to be glowing. She was so excited. She picked up the board and walked outside. She shouted, "This board is magical!"

The old lady soon found out what the board could do. When she held it up high and sang, wonderful music seemed to play from it. The old lady was so happy and sang all day.

The old lady was wise and she knew it was important to share this special board with others. So she decided to let all the kids in the neighbourhood play with the board. They sang and danced to the magical music. Soon everyone was having fun!

The old lady and the kids smiled at each other. It seemed like the magical board brought them all together. They shared many stories and laughed a lot. It was a happy day!

Once upon a time there was a dog called Rover. Rover wanted to reach a big goal.

Rover's goal was to run up the huge and rough hill. Everyone said it was impossible, but Rover was determined to try. Rover's legs were trembling with excitement as he began the climb.

But Rover soon saw that the hill was too rough to climb. He tried and tried but just couldn't reach the top.

"Don't give up," said a friendly voice. It was a bird, perched in a nearby tree.

"You can do it, Rover!"

Rover took a deep breath, and with a new hope, he began to climb the hill. Trembling with effort, he kept on going until he reached the top.

At the top, Rover felt so proud and happy. He had achieved his goal!

One day, a little girl named Sue was playing in her room. She saw a big curtain near her bed. Sue felt comfortable sitting near the curtain. She liked how soft it was.

Sue's mom came into the room and said, "Sue, it's time to eat." But Sue did not want to eat. She refused to go to the table. Sue said, "No, I want to play with the curtain."

Sue's mom thought for a moment. Then she said, "How about we eat near the curtain? That way, you can still play after we eat." Sue liked the idea. So, they ate near the curtain, and Sue was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she found a shiny rock on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her mom.

"Look, Mommy! I found a pretty rock!" Lily said.

"That's lovely, sweetie," her mom replied. "Let's go inside and wash it off in the sink."

Lily followed her mom inside and watched as she turned on the faucet. She put the rock under the water and gently rubbed it with her fingers. When she was done, she handed it back to Lily.

"Wow! It looks even more beautiful now!" Lily exclaimed.

"Yes, it's the original color," her mom said with a smile.

Lily was so happy with her new treasure and she kept it in her pocket all day long. She loved how it sparkled in the sunlight and how it felt smooth in her hand. She couldn't wait to show it to her friends at preschool the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a baby named Timmy. Timmy was very weak and couldn't walk or talk yet. One day, Timmy's mom put him down for a nap in his crib. When she came back to check on him, she saw that Timmy had vanished! She looked everywhere but couldn't find him. Timmy's mom was very worried and started to cry. Suddenly, she heard a little giggle coming from under the bed. She looked and there was Timmy, smiling and happy as can be!

One day, Therese was very bored. She was just three years old, but she already had a telephone. She decided to call her Grandma to see if she wanted to come and play.

When Grandma answered the telephone, she and Therese had a plan. They would both go to the park. There was a big tree there and they could play underneath it.

At the park, Therese found a big log. She wanted to climb it, but it was too hard. But then Grandma showed her how to be flexible. She showed Therese how to twist her body to fit over the log. Then, Therese could easily climb it.

When Therese made it to the top, she was so happy. She shouted, "Look at me! I did it!" Grandma clapped and cheered.

Before they left the park, they took a picture. Grandma snapped the picture with her phone and Theyse smiled big.

That day was so much fun. Now, whenever Therese gets bored, she looks at the picture of her and Grandma at the park and remembers how flexible she can be.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the yard. They have a ball, a bike, and a doll.

One day, they see a bird in the yard. The bird is red and blue. It is pretty. Lily and Ben want to see the bird.

They go near the bird. They say, "Hello, bird. Do you want to play with us?" The bird looks at them. It says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet."

Lily and Ben laugh. They say, "You are funny, bird. What is your name?" The bird says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet."

Lily and Ben think. They say, "We will call you Tweet. You are our new friend, Tweet." The bird says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet."

They play with the bird. They throw the ball, ride the bike, and hug the doll. The bird flies and sings. They have fun in the yard. They are happy.

One day, there was a deep hive in a tree. It was summertime. A honeybee was living inside the hive and was very happy.

The honeybee flew around and gathered nectar to make honey. Then it flew back to the hive.

But one day, something bad happened. The honeybee heard a loud noise. It was a boy hitting the hive with a stick! He was trying to get the honey in the hive.

The bee was very sad and the hive was starting to break. The bee quickly flew out and away from the boy.

The next day, the bee found a new, safe hive in a different tree. It made its home there, and was able to make even more honey and be very happy again.

Once there was a boy. He wanted to play in his green garden. He saw a tree and he wanted to climb it. He started to climb but then he fell. He felt sad. Then his mommy came over to him. She saw that he was sad and she asked him what happened. He told his mommy that he fell from the tree. So his mommy decided to go and fix it. She grabbed some heavy tools and went over to the tree. She worked hard and was able to fix the tree. Now the boy could climb it again. He was happy and went back to the tree. He carefully climbed it and was able to reach the top. He had a lot of fun and thanked his mommy for fixing the tree.

Once upon a time there was an octopus named Sam. Sam liked to organize things - he liked to organize them in specific ways to make sure that everything was in its place.

One day, Sam decided to organize two big rocks together to make a rock tower. Sam worked hard, and he was almost done.

"Sam, be careful!" called out Sam's mother. "You can be clumsy sometimes!"

Sam was careful, and he was able to finish the tower. But then the ground began shaking, and the tower started wobbling and then falling.

Sam was scared, but then he noticed something strange. Another octopus had just come out of the rocks! It was organizing and stacking the rocks back up!

Sam smiled as he was able to get his rock tower back because of the clumsy octopus!

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She lived in a house full of amazing things. Every day she explored her house and discovered something new.

One day, Lucy found a cherry tree in her garden. She saw the cherry tree had lots of sweet, red fruits. She didn't know what it was, so she asked her mother.

Her mum said, "That is a cherry tree. Do you want to try one of the cherries?"

Lucy was so excited. She plucked a juicy cherry off the tree and ate it. It was the most amazing thing she had ever tasted. She knew she loved cherries and wanted to eat them every day.

Mum said, "Cherries are very special, so we won't pick them all. We will just pick a few, so that the cherry tree can grow lots more fruit."

So every day Lucy would head out into the garden, pick one or two cherries, then she'd run inside and enjoy a delicious snack. She knew that cherries were amazing and always looked forward to picking them.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who loved playing with his toys. He would match them in a tray, carefully putting the pieces together whenever he could.

One particular day, he wanted to use the tray to match his blocks, but was quickly won over by an old toy he had never seen before. It was a harsh looking toy, and the young boy was quickly enthralled by it. He grabbed it and ignored the tray, instead choosing to match the pieces all over the floor.

Moments before his mother arrived, he quickly tried to put all the pieces together, but it was too late. His mother saw all the pieces littered around the room and was not happy.

"You must put all of your pieces away in the tray when you are finished, ' she said' sternly.

The young boy nodded, scared of his mother's harsh voice. He knew he had to put all the pieces away in the tray before he could play with his toys again. He carefully matched the pieces one by one, remembering the warning of his mother.

Once upon a time, there was a little pig. He lived on a farm with his family. The pig had a hidden spot he liked to play in. It was behind the big red barn. He loved to hide there and play with his toys.

One day, the little pig found a small seed in his hidden spot. He thought it would be fun to grow something. So, he dug a hole with his little pig feet and put the seed in the ground. He covered it up and gave it some water.

Every day, the pig went to his hidden spot to check on the seed. He gave it water and talked to it. Soon, a tiny green plant began to grow. The pig was so happy! He watched as the plant grew bigger and bigger. The little pig had grown a beautiful flower in his hidden spot. He was so proud of his flower and loved to sit by it every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to wear his cozy bathrobe after taking a bath. One day, he put on his bathrobe and went to the kitchen to get some milk. But when he got there, he saw his cat staring at him with its big eyes.

Timmy thought it was crazy that the cat was staring at him like that. He tried to shoo the cat away, but it wouldn't budge. So, Timmy just stared back at the cat until it finally walked away. From that day on, Timmy made sure to always wear his bathrobe when he went to get milk, just in case the crazy cat was there again.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max was very hungry. He wanted some food to eat. Max's friend, a big cat named Sam, wanted to help Max feel better.

Sam had an idea. He went to the kitchen and put some food on a tray. Sam wanted to deliver the tray to Max. He carried the tray very carefully so he wouldn't drop the food.

When Max saw the tray, his eyes got big and happy. Max ate all the food from the tray. Now, Max was not hungry anymore. Max and Sam played together all day, and they were both very happy.

Lily felt better after talking to her mom and drinking the warm milk. She went back to bed and fell asleep, dreaming of rainbows and unicorns instead of nightmares.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess. This princess had an amazing chest. Inside the chest was something special. For hours and hours every day, the princess would raise the lid and look inside.

Once, when the princess opened the chest, she saw a perfect diamond. It was her most treasured item. She kept this precious diamond in the chest and made sure to take good care of it.

The princess wanted to make sure the diamond stayed perfect so by day she used sunshine to help it sparkle and by night she used moonlight to help it shine.

Every day, the princess would admire the diamond and she was proud of her perfect chest. She knew nothing could ever beat it.

Once upon a time, there was a big red apple. It was so big that it could feed a whole family. One day, a little boy took the apple and ran away. The owner of the apple saw the boy and ran after him. When he caught up to the boy, he slapped him on the hand and took the apple back. The boy ran away crying and learned his lesson to never take things that don't belong to him. As the sun set in the west, the owner of the apple went home and enjoyed a delicious snack.

Once there was a tall boy. He was trying to decide what he should do. He thought and thought but he just couldn't make up his mind.

Suddenly he had an idea. He decided to get his knife. With the knife he knew he could do many things. He figured solving his problem would be easy.

So he took the knife and went outside. He started cutting a tree with it. After a little bit, he had enough wood to build something. He made a tall house on the ground.

He was very pleased with his work. He had decided what he wanted to do and he had made it happen. It was his special tall house and he was proud.

Once upon a time, there lived a generous little fish named Tiny. He often helped his neighbors whenever they were in need.

One day, one of his friends, a crab named Bobby, said to him, "Tiny, I need your help! Please lend me some tuna, or else I won't have enough for dinner." Tiny, who was always generous to others, gladly lent some of his tuna to Bobby.

After dinner, Bobby returned to Tiny, who was waiting to see if he had enjoyed his dinner. Bobby said, "Thank you so much, Tiny! I had the most wonderful dinner because I had your tuna. You are so generous!"

From that day onward, Tiny learned the valuable lesson of lending a helping hand to those in need. This made Tiny even more generous and kind to others. Even when he had little, he was always willing to share what he had with his friends.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play in the bath with their toys. They have a boat, a duck, a fish and a frog. They make bubbles with the soap and splash each other.

One day, they see a new soap on the shelf. It is big and round and has a picture of a star on it. They wonder what it is.

"Can we use the new soap?" Tom asks Lily.

"I don't know. Maybe it is not for us. Maybe it is for Mom or Dad." Lily says.

They decide to discuss it with their toys. They ask the boat, the duck, the fish and the frog what they think.

The boat says, "The new soap is too big for me. I like the small soap that makes me slippery and fast."

The duck says, "The new soap is too round for me. I like the flat soap that I can quack on and make noise."

The fish says, "The new soap is too dry for me. I like the wet soap that I can swim in and make bubbles."

The frog says, "The new soap is too shiny for me. I like the dull soap that I can hide in and surprise you."

Tom and Lily listen to their toys. They think they are smart. They agree that the new soap is not for them. They put it back on the shelf and use the old soap that they like. They have fun in the bath with their toys. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was an infant who loved to play. Every day, she would explore her distant world. One day, she looked up and saw two bright moons in the sky. She was so amazed, she waved her little arms in joy.

The infant's mom loved to watch her daughter so full of joy and love. She was so thankful to be a mom seeing her infant be so curious.The infant's happiness was infectious! Whenever anyone saw her, they couldn't help but smile too.

The infant loved her mom and dad, and they too loved her very much. They would take her out to different places to play, and although some of the places were distant, the infant loved exploring and being with the people she loved.

The infant was so loved. Everywhere she went, she was surrounded by a big warm hug of love.

Once there was a clumsy rat. He was always making silly mistakes and he loved stealing from people's homes. One day, he decided to steal from an old house near his.

As he entered the house, the rat noticed that all the furniture and walls had been broken and destroyed. He walked around, looking for something valuable. Suddenly, the rat saw a beautiful chair. He quickly grabbed it, thinking he had scored a big prize.

He tried to leave the house with the chair, but he ended up making a lot of noise and accidentally disturbed a family living nearby. The family opened their door and saw the rat with the chair in his mouth.

The family was really angry and decided to restore the house. The rat was so sad to see all his efforts go to waste. He tried to explain himself, but it was too late.

The family took away the chair and the rat was never seen again. He had learned his lesson and realized that the old house was not the place for him.

Sara and Tom love to play with their kayak. It is brown and big and floats on the water. They like to paddle and splash and see the fish and the birds. One day, they find a small island with a lot of flowers and trees. They decide to explore it and have a picnic.

"Look, Sara, what a pretty necklace!" Tom says, picking up a string of shells and beads. He puts it around Sara's neck and smiles. "You are very pretty, Sara. Do you want to marry me?"

Sara giggles and nods. "Yes, Tom, I want to marry you. You are very nice and funny. But how can we marry?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He remembers that his mom and dad had a ring and a cake and a party when they married. He looks around and sees a big leaf and a berry. He takes the leaf and makes a hole in it. He puts the berry in the hole and makes a ring. He gives it to Sara and says, "Here, Sara, this is your ring. Now we are married."

Sara puts the ring on her finger and hugs Tom. "Thank you, Tom, this is a beautiful ring. Now we are married."

They share their sandwich and juice and have a cake of cookies. They dance and sing and laugh. They are very happy. They get back in their kayak and paddle home. They tell their mom and dad that they are married. Their mom and dad smile and hug them. They are proud of their children. They say, "You are very sweet, Sara and Tom. But you are still very young. You can play and pretend, but you are not really married. You have to grow up and learn a lot of things before you can marry. But we love you very much and we are happy that you are friends."

Sara and Tom understand. They are not sad. They know that they are still children and have a lot of fun to have. They keep their necklace and ring and kayak. They play and pretend and dream. They are still friends. And maybe, one day, when they are big, they will marry for real.

Once upon a time, there was a black cave. Inside the cave lived two friends, a mouse and a bat. The mouse was very brave and always wanted to explore.

One day, the mouse wanted to see what was outside the cave. He poked his head out and saw a beautiful, blue sky. He was so excited that he wanted to explore further, so he opened the cave door.

Suddenly, there was a loud hissing noise. The mouse looked worried and asked the bat, â€œWhat is that noise?â€

The bat replied, â€œThatâ€™s the sound of oxygen leaving the cave. We need to close the door quick or we wonâ€™t be able to breathe.â€ So the mouse and the bat quickly closed the door and the noise stopped.

The mouse and the bat both breathed a sigh of relief. From then on, they promised to always close the door to keep the oxygen inside the cave.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Suzie. She had big, blue eyes and loved to play with her toys.

One day, Suzie was playing in her garden when she saw a train rolling through the village. She marvelled at the bright, shiny carriage and wondered what it would be like to ride inside it.

The train was going very fast, but Suzie hoped she could one day go on a train too.

Until then, Suzie decided to imagine she was on the train. She pretended she was on a smooth journey with lots of surprises around every corner. She imagined she could be anywhere when the train came to a stop.

Suzie imagined she could go anywhere and do anything she wanted. She knew that her journey was just beginning, and she began to hope for the future.

One day, a girl named Sophie went to the beach with her mum. They gazed at the bright shining sea for a long time, it was beautiful!

Sophie was having so much fun building sand castles. She made them big and tall. Suddenly, a stupid seagull came and knocked down her castle. Sophie was so mad, she shouted and jumped around.

Mum said it was time to go home. But Sophie wanted to stay! She gazed out at the sea, with its shimmering waves. She wanted to stay and play here forever.

Mum said they had to go back but promised they could come back another day. Sophie smiled and they walked back, dreaming of their next beach visit.

One day, there was a little boy called Sam. He had a tiny sword. Sam went to see his friend Annie. But when he got there, he saw that she had been crying.

"What's wrong, Annie?" asked Sam.

Annie said, "My mom and dad had a fight and it was really scary."

Sam was sad to hear this but he wanted to help Annie. He asked her if she wanted to play with his sword.

Annie smiled and said, "Yes, I would love to."

Sam smiled back and gave her the sword. They ran around the garden, pretending to be knights. They had so much fun.

Afterwards, Sam said to Annie, "I know it's hard, but maybe you could forgive your mom and dad."

Annie thought about this for a moment. Then she nodded her head and said, "Yes, I can forgive them."

It made Sam happy to see Annie feeling better. He gave her a hug and said, "That's the right thing to do. Just remember that it's OK to forgive."

Annie smiled and gave Sam a big hug. From that day on, they were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. Each afternoon, the bird tried to build its home. The bird wanted to make a cozy nest in a tree.

The first day, the bird collected sticks from the ground. But it was hard work, and the bird soon got frustrated.

The next afternoon, the bird tried again. This time, the bird found some leaves to make the nest even cozier.

But then the rain came, and the breeze blew the nest apart. The bird was very sad and frustrated.

The bird looked up at the sky and said, "Who will help me build my nest?"

The bird tried again and again, but it couldn't make the nest stay together. No matter what the bird tried, the nest wouldn't stay put. The bird was so frustrated that it eventually gave up.

The bird never got to live in its cozy nest. And it was a very sad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man. He went to an old, abandoned building and saw a brick on the ground. He wanted to surprise himself, so he picked up the brick and threw it through a window.

The man heard a loud crash and soon he was surrounded by policemen. They shouted, "Sir, what have you done?".

The man was embarrassed and he said, "I was just trying to surprise myself!". But the policemen did not believe him and they arrested him and took him away.

The man was never able to surprise himself with the brick again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old, but she was very smart. Her mother took her to the library, so she could learn some new things.

When they got there, Amy's mother said, "I'm going to the cafe while you listen to the lecture."

Amy didn't want to stay, she was so restless. But mother said, "Be a good girl and listen to the lecture. I'll be back in an hour."

So Amy stayed and listened to the lecture. It was about animals and she liked it. She learned new things and couldn't wait to act them out when she got home. After the lecture, her mother was back to pick her up.

"You did so well and I'm so proud of you," she said.

Amy smiled. She was happy to have acted like such a good girl.

THE ROBBER BRIDEGROOM

There was once a miller who had one beautiful daughter, and as she was

grown up, he was anxious that she should be well married and provided

for. He said to himself, 'I will give her to the first suitable man who

comes and asks for her hand.' Not long after a suitor appeared, and as

he appeared to be very rich and the miller could see nothing in him with

which to find fault, he betrothed his daughter to him. But the girl did

not care for the man as a girl ought to care for her betrothed husband.

She did not feel that she could trust him, and she could not look at him

nor think of him without an inward shudder. One day he said to her, 'You

have not yet paid me a visit, although we have been betrothed for some

time.' 'I do not know where your house is,' she answered. 'My house is

out there in the dark forest,' he said. She tried to excuse herself by

saying that she would not be able to find the way thither. Her betrothed

only replied, 'You must come and see me next Sunday; I have already

invited guests for that day, and that you may not mistake the way, I

will strew ashes along the path.'

When Sunday came, and it was time for the girl to start, a feeling of

dread came over her which she could not explain, and that she might

be able to find her path again, she filled her pockets with peas and

lentils to sprinkle on the ground as she went along. On reaching the

entrance to the forest she found the path strewed with ashes, and these

she followed, throwing down some peas on either side of her at every

step she took. She walked the whole day until she came to the deepest,

darkest part of the forest. There she saw a lonely house, looking so

grim and mysterious, that it did not please her at all. She stepped

inside, but not a soul was to be seen, and a great silence reigned

throughout. Suddenly a voice cried:

'Turn back, turn back, young maiden fair,

Linger not in this murderers' lair.'

The girl looked up and saw that the voice came from a bird hanging in a

cage on the wall. Again it cried:

'Turn back, turn back, young maiden fair,

Linger not in this murderers' lair.'

The girl passed on, going from room to room of the house, but they were

all empty, and still she saw no one. At last she came to the cellar,

and there sat a very, very old woman, who could not keep her head from

shaking. 'Can you tell me,' asked the girl, 'if my betrothed husband

lives here?'

'Ah, you poor child,' answered the old woman, 'what a place for you to

come to! This is a murderers' den. You think yourself a promised bride,

and that your marriage will soon take place, but it is with death that

you will keep your marriage feast. Look, do you see that large cauldron

of water which I am obliged to keep on the fire! As soon as they have

you in their power they will kill you without mercy, and cook and eat

you, for they are eaters of men. If I did not take pity on you and save

you, you would be lost.'

Thereupon the old woman led her behind a large cask, which quite hid her

from view. 'Keep as still as a mouse,' she said; 'do not move or speak,

or it will be all over with you. Tonight, when the robbers are

all asleep, we will flee together. I have long been waiting for an

opportunity to escape.'

The words were hardly out of her mouth when the godless crew returned,

dragging another young girl along with them. They were all drunk, and

paid no heed to her cries and lamentations. They gave her wine to drink,

three glasses full, one of white wine, one of red, and one of yellow,

and with that her heart gave way and she died. Then they tore off her

dainty clothing, laid her on a table, and cut her beautiful body into

pieces, and sprinkled salt upon it.

The poor betrothed girl crouched trembling and shuddering behind the

cask, for she saw what a terrible fate had been intended for her by

the robbers. One of them now noticed a gold ring still remaining on

the little finger of the murdered girl, and as he could not draw it off

easily, he took a hatchet and cut off the finger; but the finger sprang

into the air, and fell behind the cask into the lap of the girl who was

hiding there. The robber took a light and began looking for it, but he

could not find it. 'Have you looked behind the large cask?' said one of

the others. But the old woman called out, 'Come and eat your suppers,

and let the thing be till tomorrow; the finger won't run away.'

'The old woman is right,' said the robbers, and they ceased looking for

the finger and sat down.

The old woman then mixed a sleeping draught with their wine, and before

long they were all lying on the floor of the cellar, fast asleep and

snoring. As soon as the girl was assured of this, she came from behind

the cask. She was obliged to step over the bodies of the sleepers, who

were lying close together, and every moment she was filled with renewed

dread lest she should awaken them. But God helped her, so that she

passed safely over them, and then she and the old woman went upstairs,

opened the door, and hastened as fast as they could from the murderers'

den. They found the ashes scattered by the wind, but the peas and

lentils had sprouted, and grown sufficiently above the ground, to guide

them in the moonlight along the path. All night long they walked, and it

was morning before they reached the mill. Then the girl told her father

all that had happened.

The day came that had been fixed for the marriage. The bridegroom

arrived and also a large company of guests, for the miller had taken

care to invite all his friends and relations. As they sat at the feast,

each guest in turn was asked to tell a tale; the bride sat still and did

not say a word.

'And you, my love,' said the bridegroom, turning to her, 'is there no

tale you know? Tell us something.'

'I will tell you a dream, then,' said the bride. 'I went alone through a

forest and came at last to a house; not a soul could I find within, but

a bird that was hanging in a cage on the wall cried:

'Turn back, turn back, young maiden fair,

Linger not in this murderers' lair.'

and again a second time it said these words.'

'My darling, this is only a dream.'

'I went on through the house from room to room, but they were all empty,

and everything was so grim and mysterious. At last I went down to the

cellar, and there sat a very, very old woman, who could not keep her

head still. I asked her if my betrothed lived here, and she answered,

"Ah, you poor child, you are come to a murderers' den; your betrothed

does indeed live here, but he will kill you without mercy and afterwards

cook and eat you."'

'My darling, this is only a dream.'

'The old woman hid me behind a large cask, and scarcely had she done

this when the robbers returned home, dragging a young girl along with

them. They gave her three kinds of wine to drink, white, red, and

yellow, and with that she died.'

'My darling, this is only a dream.'

'Then they tore off her dainty clothing, and cut her beautiful body into

pieces and sprinkled salt upon it.'

'My darling, this is only a dream.'

'And one of the robbers saw that there was a gold ring still left on her

finger, and as it was difficult to draw off, he took a hatchet and cut

off her finger; but the finger sprang into the air and fell behind the

great cask into my lap. And here is the finger with the ring.' And

with these words the bride drew forth the finger and shewed it to the

assembled guests.

The bridegroom, who during this recital had grown deadly pale, up and

tried to escape, but the guests seized him and held him fast. They

delivered him up to justice, and he and all his murderous band were

condemned to death for their wicked deeds.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and trucks more than anything. One day, Timmy's dad took him to a gas station to get some fuel for their car. Timmy thought the gas station was impressive because there were so many cars there.

While they were getting gas, Timmy's dad warned him not to touch anything. Timmy listened carefully and promised not to touch anything. But as they were leaving, Timmy saw a toy truck on the shelf and he really wanted it. He asked his dad if he could have it, but his dad said no. Timmy was sad, but he knew he had to listen to his dad.

As they drove away from the gas station, Timmy looked out the window and saw all the cars on the road. He was happy to be in his car with his dad and he knew they had enough fuel to get where they were going. Timmy was grateful for his dad's warning and he felt safe knowing his dad was taking care of him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy had a jolly day in her backyard, playing with her dolls. The sun was shining brightly and Daisy was so happy.

Suddenly, her mom came out of the house and called her. 'Daisy, come here! I have a surprise for you,' her mom said. Daisy was filled with excitement and quickly ran to her mom.

'Here you go, darling. I bought this for you,' her mom said holding out a toy. Daisy was so excited, she thanked her mom for the surprise.

After that, every day Daisy would ask her mom to supply her with new toys. And every day her mom would fulfill her wish.

But one day, her mom told Daisy 'No' when Daisy asked her for a new toy. Daisy was so disappointed, she started crying and begging her mom.

Her mom shook her head and said, 'I can't always supply you with everything you want, Daisy. You should learn to be content.'

This made Daisy understand that she shouldn't always expect to be given things. It was a bad ending, but it was good to learn a moral lesson. Excessive wanting is not always a good thing.

Once upon a time there was a flexible beef. He was really bouncy and he loved collecting. He loved to collect rocks and sticks and leaves. He even collected flowers to give to his friends.

One day, the beef went to the park to collect. He saw a big rock which he wanted to bring home, but it was too heavy to carry on his own. Suddenly, he heard a voice talking to him.

The beef looked up to find a friendly dog standing near him. He was so happy to have a friend.

Once there was a little boy whose name was Bob. Bob wanted to draw a picture. He went to his bedroom and found a black marker, some paper and a red crayon. Bob was excited to try and draw a picture.

Bob took the marker and started to draw a big black circle, then he started to draw lots of smaller black circles around it. He then tried to draw a big black tree with big green leaves and a black bird at the top.

Bob was so proud of his picture, but he was missing something. He had a little bit of red crayon left, so he decided to add a red sun in the top corner. Now the picture was complete!

Bob showed the picture to his mom, who hugged him and said it was beautiful. Bob was so proud of himself because he had tried to draw the picture all by himself.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red cap that he loved to wear every day. It made him feel happy and powerful.

One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. He was having so much fun that he didn't notice when his cap fell off his head. Timmy didn't realize he had lost his cap until he got home.

He looked everywhere for it, but it was nowhere to be found. Timmy missed his cap so much that he cried himself to sleep that night.

The next day, Timmy went back to the park to look for his cap. But it was gone forever. Timmy was so sad and couldn't stop crying. He missed his cap and felt powerless without it. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice cream and always got a cone when she went to the ice cream shop. One day, she was walking in the park and saw a cone on the ground. She picked it up and saw that it was not smooth, but instead it was bumpy and dirty.

Lily wanted to bury the cone so nobody would see it and step on it. She found a spot under a tree and dug a little hole with her hands. She put the cone in the hole and covered it with dirt.

As she walked away, she felt happy that she did something good for the park. She learned that even small actions, like burying a cone, can make a big difference. It's important to take care of our environment and keep it clean for everyone to enjoy.

Once upon a time, a little bird was chirping in the sky. She was wearing a golden crown and was very important. As she was flying, she whistled a sweet song. Soon, two children saw her fly by.

"Look!" one child said. "Is that a princess?"

The other child smiled. "Yes, it is! I like her crown."

The little bird kept flying and the children watched in awe. The little bird kept whistling her sweet song, until she flew out of sight. The children waved goodbye and the bird flew off into the sky.

The children talked and smiled, they had just seen something special. The little bird with the golden crown was very important indeed.

Once upon a time, there was a big family of rabbits. They lived in a cozy home in the forest. The rabbits were very happy together and loved to play and eat carrots.

One day, a new rabbit came to their home. Her name was Rosie and she was very envious of the other rabbits. She wanted to have all the carrots for herself and didn't want to share with anyone.

The other rabbits noticed that Rosie was not very friendly and they decided to separate from her. They knew that it was not nice to be envious and selfish. They wanted to teach Rosie a lesson and show her the importance of kindness and sharing.

After some time, Rosie realized her mistake and apologized to the other rabbits. She learned that it was better to be friends and share the carrots. From that day on, they all played together and shared their food. The rabbits lived happily ever after.

Lily and Anna are sisters. Lily is big and Anna is little. They like to play together in the park. They swing on the swings, slide on the slide, and run on the grass.

One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a long tail and a wet nose. The dog runs to Lily and Anna and licks their faces. Lily and Anna laugh and pet the dog.

The dog barks and wags its tail. It likes Lily and Anna.

"His name is Max," a voice says. Lily and Anna look up and see a boy. The boy is holding a leash. He is the dog's owner.

"Hi, I'm Lily and this is Anna," Lily says. "We like your dog. He is very friendly."

"Hi, I'm Ben," the boy says. "Max likes you too. Do you want to play with him?"

"Yes, please!" Anna says. She smiles and hugs the dog.

Lily, Anna, Ben, and Max play together in the park. They have a lot of fun. They are happy and smile a lot. They make new friends.

Once upon a time there was a rocket ship. It was big and shiny. One day a little boy named Timmy wanted to open the rocket. He said, "I want to open the rocket and see inside."

His dad said, "You can open the rocket, but it might be smelly in there."

Then Timmy shouted, "Let's go! Come on Dad, let's go fly the rocket."

Dad said, "OK, let's go." So they went on a wonderful rocket ride and had a lot of fun.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a big and strong tree. The tree liked to stretch its branches and leaves in the sunshine. One day, a little boy came and decided to climb to the top of the tree. He wanted to reach one of the most beautiful apples hanging high up.

Once upon a time there was a clever bunny. His name was Jack. He had a special weapon which he used to protect his friends.

One silly day, Jack was out walking in the forest with his friends. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise! What was it?

"Let me take a look," said Jack bravely. So he bravely grabbed his weapon and ran off to the source of the noise.

But Jack bravely held up his weapon and shouted back, "No, you won't! I will protect my friends!"

The monster saw that Jack was brave. He knew that he had met his match! So the monster turned and ran away.

Once upon a time, there was a gray fish who lived in the sea. Her name was Jelly. One day, Jelly got a silly idea. She wanted to see what it was like to live on land.

Jelly swam up to the shore and peered out of the water. A little boy was playing in the sand. The little boy saw Jelly and ran to get his mommy.
