Once upon a time, there was a serious shop. It stayed in one place, like when you park a car. Every day the shop opened up and sold new things.

One day, a little girl named Lynne wanted to go to the shop. She asked her mom if they could go. Her mom said, "Yes, we can go!"

So they got in their car and parked it near the shop. When they got out, Lynne took her mom's hand and they walked to the shop.

When they got there, Lynne was so excited! She saw all kinds of silly things like colored lollipops and sparkly toys. She wanted to buy something, but her mom told her to be serious and think about what she really needed.

So, Lynne thought carefully, and decided to buy a brush for her dolls. She went up to the counter and paid for her brush with her own money.

When they left the shop, Lynne was very proud of herself for being so serious. She hopped in the car with her new brush and off they drove!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Abby. Abby was three years old and she was playing in the garden one day.
Suddenly, dark clouds started to gather in the sky, and soon a huge flood started. Abby was scared that she would be washed away so she started to run for the house.
Suddenly she heard a noise. It was her mom calling from the house.
"Abby, hurry inside! We need to manage this flood together".
Abby ran inside and together she and her mom managed to put sand bags around the house.
The scary flood started to subside, and Abby and her mom were so relieved.
The next day after the flood, Abby was playing in the garden again, thankful that she and her mom managed to stay safe.

Lily liked to feel her thumb in her mouth. It made her calm and happy. She did not like to share her toys or her books. She kept them organized in her room. She did not want anyone to touch them or mess them up.

One day, her cousin Max came to visit. He wanted to play with Lily. He saw her toys and books and ran to them. He picked up a doll and a car and a book. He threw them on the floor. He laughed and said, "Let's play!"

Lily was angry. She ran to Max and pushed him. She yelled, "No! Those are mine! Go away!" She grabbed her toys and books and put them back in their places. She did not care that Max was crying. She did not care that he was hurt. She only cared about her things.

Max's mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Max on the floor with a bruise on his arm. She saw Lily with her thumb in her mouth and her toys and books organized. She was sad and angry. She said to Lily, "You are a bad girl. You hurt your cousin. You do not know how to share or be kind. You are selfish and mean. You have to say sorry to Max and give him a hug. And you have to let him play with your toys and books. Or you will have no friends and no fun."

Lily did not want to say sorry or hug Max. She did not want to let him play with her things. She shook her head and said, "No! I don't care. I like my thumb and my things. I don't need friends or fun."

Max's mom took Max and left. She said, "We will not come back until you learn how to be nice. Goodbye, Lily."

Lily was alone in her room. She felt her thumb in her mouth. She looked at her toys and books. They were organized. But they were not fun. They did not talk to her or hug her or laugh with her. They were just things. She felt sad and lonely. She wished she had a friend. She wished she had been nice to Max. She wished she had shared and played. But it was too late. She had made a bad choice. And she had to live with it.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Being kind is better than being organized. Friends are more important than things.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a clean, shiny treasure. The treasure was hidden under a tall tree. Many animals lived in the forest, but no one knew where the treasure was.

One day, a little rabbit was hopping around the forest. He saw the tall tree and wanted to stand near it. As he stood there, he saw something shiny under the tree. He dug and dug, and found the clean treasure.

The little rabbit was so happy to find the treasure. He shared it with all his animal friends in the forest. They all played with the treasure and had a lot of fun. From that day on, the animals always stood near the tall tree and played with their clean, shiny treasure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy who liked to daydream. Every day, she would close her eyes and pretend to be a star of her own movie and she was always so happy!

One day, Daisy told her mommy about her dreams. â€œMummy, I want to be in a real film!â€ She said. â€œOh, Daisy, thatâ€™s a big dreamâ€ her mommy said. â€œBut if youâ€™re persistent, you can make it happen!â€

Then, Daisy and her mommy went to the park and Daisy imagined what a real film would be like. She thought about all the people who would help make it come alive. She felt so excited!

The next day, Daisy wrote a letter to a famous movie director and asked for his help to bring her dreams to life.

Months passed and Daisy almost forgot about her letter but then, one day, the director wrote back! He said he could help Daisy make her dream come true!

Today, Daisy is living her dream and she is one of the stars in her very own movie! Daisy is so proud of her hard work and her persistence really paid off!

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack. He was three years old and really liked to play outside.

One day, Jack looked out of the window. Outside he saw a lot of kids running and playing a sport. He wanted to do the same. So he opened the door and stepped outside.

The other kids saw Jack and waved at him to come over. Jack smiled and went to join them.

He walked up to a boy and said, "Hey! Can I play?"
The other boy frowned and said, "No! We don't want you here."

Jack felt very sad. He stood and gazed at them for a moment.

Suddenly, another boy stepped forward and said, "Of course you can join us! Here, you can have my ball!" He smiled at Jack.

Jack smiled back and happily joined the other kids. As they all laughed and played, they all forgot to be angry.

Once upon a time there was a great big sea. One day, an opportunistic little fish made a very special request. He asked the sea to give him three wishes.

The sea was so grateful for the fish's kind request, it gave him all three wishes and more! The fish was so happy!

First, he wished he could have lots of delicious food. Instantly, the sea filled up with colourful fish, shrimp, and crab. The fish was delighted and he feasted on the delicious treats.

Second, the fish wanted a safe place to live. The sea was very generous, it created a special home for the fish and filled it with colourful coral and rocks. The fish was safe and secure in his new home.

Finally, the fish wanted lots of fun and playtime. The sea created a great playground with lots of fun activities. The fish had lots of fun.

The fish was very pleased with all the great things the sea had given him. He thanked the sea for being so kind and generous. The little fish was happy and content and lived happily ever after.

Tim and Mia are playing in the park. They see a big tent with many animals inside. They want to go and look at them.

"Can we go, Mom?" Tim asks.

"OK, but be careful and stay close to me," Mom says.

They go inside the tent and see many animals. They see a lion, a monkey, a zebra, and a leopard. The leopard is sleeping on a big rock. He has spots on his fur.

"Wow, look at the leopard!" Mia says. "He is so pretty!"

She goes closer to the leopard and tries to touch him. But the leopard wakes up and sees Mia. He is angry. He does not like strangers. He growls and shows his teeth.

"Roar!" the leopard says.

Mia is scared. She runs back to Tim and Mom. The leopard jumps off the rock and chases Mia.

"Help!" Mia cries.

Mom grabs Mia and covers her with her coat. She protects her from the leopard. Tim runs to a man who works in the tent. He tells him about the leopard.

"Help! The leopard is angry and wants to hurt Mia!" Tim says.

The man hears Tim and sees the leopard. He gets a big net and throws it over the leopard. He catches the leopard and puts him back on the rock.

"Sorry, kids. The leopard is not used to people. He is not a pet. He is a wild animal. You should not go near him or touch him. He can be dangerous," the man says.

Mom hugs Mia and Tim. She is glad they are safe.

"Thank you, sir. We are sorry. We did not know. We will not do it again," Mom says.

The man smiles and nods. He gives them some stickers of animals. They say sorry to the leopard and leave the tent. They go to the swings and have fun. They learn to respect the animals and their space.

Once upon a time, there was a young child named Leo. Leo loved playing with all his toys, his stuffed animals and his car. One sunny day, Leo wanted to go outside and play in the park.

When Leo arrived to the park, he was so excited to run and play on the monkey bars. But when he got there, something strange had happened. All of the fellow children were standing still, they weren't moving at all! Leo was so surprised and asked what was happening.

The other children told him that they were playing a game called "freeze". He had to stop when someone yelled out "freeze". It was a lot of fun, so Leo joined in with them.

But as the game went on, Leo started to feel a little upset because he was playing for so long and felt like he was missing out on something. One of the other children explained to Leo that he could stop playing at any time, and then do his job.

The other children called out to Leo and reminded him that he had work to do too. Leo was happy that his friends were looking out for him and he finished the game and went off to do his job.

The moral of the story is that it is important to take breaks between playing and doing your job. Doing something you are required to do can prevent us from feeling upset in the long run.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was always ready to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom told him to clean up his toys before going outside. Timmy said, "Okay, Mommy. I will clean up my toys."

But Timmy got distracted by his toys and forgot to clean them up. He went outside to play with his friends. When Timmy came back inside, he saw that his mom had cleaned up his toys for him. Timmy felt regret for not listening to his mom. He said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I regret not cleaning up my toys."

His mom hugged him and said, "It's okay, Timmy. I was shocked when I saw your toys on the floor, but I'm glad you're sorry." Timmy promised to always listen to his mom from then on.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mary. Mary was very happy and always wanted to play.

Today, Mary had a great time playing with her toys. Until she heard a loud sound. It was so hot that Mary felt scared. She began to cry and was very upset.

Mary looked out the window and saw a huge wave coming closer and closer. Mary tried to close the windows but it was too late. She was hit by the waves and wet all over. She was so cold and upset.

The wave went back out but Mary was never the same. She couldn't stop shaking and feeling very scared. She was so sad and scared that she never wanted to play again.

The bad wave changed Mary forever.

One day, Jane and her daddy were at the park. Jane saw something very special - a big green tree with green powder around it. Jane walked closer to the tree and saw that the powder was made of tiny green pieces.

"What is that Daddy?" Jane asked.

"That's special powder, Jane," her daddy replied. "Let's gather some of it together and take it home with us."

So Jane and her daddy started gathering the powder into a bucket. They filled the bucket up with the powder and started walking home.

When they got home, Daddy asked Jane what she wanted to do with the green powder.

"Let's make a special cake with it," she said.

So, Jane and her daddy used the green powder to make a special cake. They cut it up and shared it between them. Jane smiled, as it was the yummiest cake she had ever tasted.

The end.

John was playing in the garden when he heard the birds singing. He looked up and saw a pretty sunset coming. The sky was dark with pink and orange colors. He smiled when he saw how beautiful it was.

John wanted to show his mom the sunset so he ran over to her. She said it was even prettier when it was closer. They both watched as the sun slowly went down.

They stayed out until the last bit of the sun went away. As the sky got darker and the stars came out, John said it was the prettiest sunset he had ever seen. His mom smiled and said, "Yes, it was so beautiful." They went back inside and John smiled all night, thinking about the pretty sunset he had seen.

Once upon a time, in a small place, there was an ugly bug. The bug had a big nose and funny legs. It lived under a rock where it could hide from the sun. The ugly bug liked to poke things with its nose.

One day, the ugly bug met a little bird. The bird was sad because it lost its friend. The ugly bug wanted to help the bird. So, they went to look for the bird's friend together. They walked and walked until they found the bird's friend.

The bird's friend was stuck in a hole. The ugly bug used its nose to poke the dirt and make the hole bigger. The bird's friend was free! The birds were happy and thanked the ugly bug. From that day on, they all lived together in the small place and became the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was so very careful. One day she went outside to play and she found a caterpillar! She was so excited!

The girl carefully put the caterpillar in her pocket so she could take him home. She stopped and said to the caterpillar, "Let's go home," and the caterpillar smiled.

When they arrived, she put the caterpillar in her garden and said, "You can stay here and have lots of adventures." The caterpillar nodded.

The girl gave the caterpillar a hug and said, "Be careful and remember to stay safe." She watched as the caterpillar crawled away, feeling sure he would have a wonderful time in her garden.

Lily liked to draw pictures with her crayons. She had many colors and shapes to make her drawings. She kept her crayons in a box on her desk in her room. Her desk was big and brown and had a chair that was too high for her. She felt uncomfortable when she sat on the chair, but she did not have another place to draw.

One day, her brother Max came into her room. He wanted to play with her crayons. He did not ask Lily, he just took the box from her desk. Lily was angry. She said, "No, Max, those are my crayons. Give them back to me. You have your own toys to play with." Max did not listen. He ran away with the box to his room. He locked the door and started to break the crayons and throw them on the floor.

Lily cried. She knocked on the door and said, "Max, please, open the door. You are ruining my crayons. I need them to draw. They are my supply of colors." Max did not care. He laughed and said, "Too bad, Lily. I like to play with your crayons. They are fun to break and throw. You can't have them back."

Lily was very sad. She did not know what to do. She went to her mom and told her what Max did. Mom was not happy. She said, "Max, that is not nice. You have to share with your sister. You have to respect her things. You have to apologize and give her back her crayons." She went to Max's room and opened the door. She saw the mess of broken crayons on the floor. She said, "Max, look what you did. You wasted Lily's crayons. You have to clean this up and buy her new ones with your allowance. You also have to say sorry to Lily and hug her."

Max felt bad. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was mean to you. I should not have taken your crayons. I should have asked you first. I will buy you new ones and help you draw. Can you forgive me?" Lily nodded. She said, "I forgive you, Max. Thank you for saying sorry. I love you, brother. Can we play together?" Max said, "I love you, too, sister. Yes, we can play together. But first, let's clean this up and put the crayons back on your desk." They hugged and smiled. Mom was proud of them. She said, "That's good, kids. You learned how to solve your problem and be kind to each other. Now, let's go and have some cookies and milk." They all went to the kitchen and had a happy snack.

Once upon a time, there was a big rhinoceros. He was troubled because he had no friends. He walked around the forest, feeling very sad.

One day, he met a little bird who was also troubled. The bird had lost her way home. The rhinoceros wanted to help the bird. They looked for her home together.

After a while, they found the bird's home. The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you! You are my friend now!" The rhinoceros felt happy too. The bird welcomed the rhinoceros to her home, and they played all day. From that day, the rhinoceros was not troubled anymore.

Tommy was sick. He had a bad cough and a hot head. He did not want to play or eat. His mom took him to the doctor. The doctor was nice. He looked at Tommy's ears, nose and throat. He gave him some medicine.

"Tommy, you need to take this medicine every day. It will help you feel better," the doctor said.

"OK, doctor. Thank you," Tommy said.

The doctor smiled. He gave Tommy a sticker. It had a picture of a lion. Tommy liked lions. He put the sticker on his shirt.

"Good boy, Tommy. Now, follow the nurse. She will lead you to the exit," the doctor said.

The nurse was kind. She held Tommy's hand. She walked with him and his mom to the door.

"Bye, Tommy. I hope you get well soon," the nurse said.

"Bye, nurse. You are good," Tommy said.

Tommy and his mom went home. Tommy took his medicine. He drank some water. He rested on the couch. He felt a little better. He looked at his sticker. He smiled. He was brave like a lion.

DOCTOR KNOWALL

There was once upon a time a poor peasant called Crabb, who drove with

two oxen a load of wood to the town, and sold it to a doctor for two

talers. When the money was being counted out to him, it so happened that

the doctor was sitting at table, and when the peasant saw how well he

ate and drank, his heart desired what he saw, and would willingly

have been a doctor too. So he remained standing a while, and at length

inquired if he too could not be a doctor. 'Oh, yes,' said the doctor,

'that is soon managed.' 'What must I do?' asked the peasant. 'In the

first place buy yourself an A B C book of the kind which has a cock on

the frontispiece; in the second, turn your cart and your two oxen into

money, and get yourself some clothes, and whatsoever else pertains to

medicine; thirdly, have a sign painted for yourself with the words: "I

am Doctor Knowall," and have that nailed up above your house-door.' The

peasant did everything that he had been told to do. When he had doctored

people awhile, but not long, a rich and great lord had some money

stolen. Then he was told about Doctor Knowall who lived in such and such

a village, and must know what had become of the money. So the lord had

the horses harnessed to his carriage, drove out to the village, and

asked Crabb if he were Doctor Knowall. Yes, he was, he said. Then he was

to go with him and bring back the stolen money. 'Oh, yes, but Grete, my

wife, must go too.' The lord was willing, and let both of them have a

seat in the carriage, and they all drove away together. When they came

to the nobleman's castle, the table was spread, and Crabb was told to

sit down and eat. 'Yes, but my wife, Grete, too,' said he, and he seated

himself with her at the table. And when the first servant came with a

dish of delicate fare, the peasant nudged his wife, and said: 'Grete,

that was the first,' meaning that was the servant who brought the first

dish. The servant, however, thought he intended by that to say: 'That is

the first thief,' and as he actually was so, he was terrified, and said

to his comrade outside: 'The doctor knows all: we shall fare ill, he

said I was the first.' The second did not want to go in at all, but was

forced. So when he went in with his dish, the peasant nudged his wife,

and said: 'Grete, that is the second.' This servant was equally alarmed,

and he got out as fast as he could. The third fared no better, for the

peasant again said: 'Grete, that is the third.' The fourth had to carry

in a dish that was covered, and the lord told the doctor that he was to

show his skill, and guess what was beneath the cover. Actually, there

were crabs. The doctor looked at the dish, had no idea what to say, and

cried: 'Ah, poor Crabb.' When the lord heard that, he cried: 'There! he

knows it; he must also know who has the money!'

On this the servants looked terribly uneasy, and made a sign to the

doctor that they wished him to step outside for a moment. When therefore

he went out, all four of them confessed to him that they had stolen

the money, and said that they would willingly restore it and give him a

heavy sum into the bargain, if he would not denounce them, for if he

did they would be hanged. They led him to the spot where the money was

concealed. With this the doctor was satisfied, and returned to the hall,

sat down to the table, and said: 'My lord, now will I search in my book

where the gold is hidden.' The fifth servant, however, crept into the

stove to hear if the doctor knew still more. But the doctor sat still

and opened his A B C book, turned the pages backwards and forwards, and

looked for the cock. As he could not find it immediately he said: 'I

know you are there, so you had better come out!' Then the fellow in the

stove thought that the doctor meant him, and full of terror, sprang out,

crying: 'That man knows everything!' Then Doctor Knowall showed the lord

where the money was, but did not say who had stolen it, and received

from both sides much money in reward, and became a renowned man.

One morning, Sara was making her toast when she heard a loud noise outside. She ran to the window and saw a big truck with a deep hole in the back. The truck was full of dirt and rocks. Sara wondered what the truck was doing. She asked her mom, who was in the kitchen.

"Mom, what is that truck for?" Sara said.

"That truck is for digging a new pool in our backyard, honey," Mom said. "Remember, we talked about it yesterday? We are going to have a lot of fun in the summer."

Sara nodded. She remembered that Mom and Dad had told her that they were going to build a pool for her and her brother. She was very excited. She wanted to swim and splash and play with her toys in the water.

Sara went back to her toast. She finished spreading the jam and cutting the pieces. She was about to take a bite when she heard another loud noise. She looked out the window again and saw the truck dumping the dirt and rocks into the hole. She gasped. She saw something shiny and red in the dirt. It looked like her favorite toy car. "Mom, Mom, look!" Sara cried. "My car, my car! It's in the dirt!"

Mom came to the window and saw the car too. She frowned. She remembered that Sara had left it outside yesterday and had forgotten to bring it in.

"Oh, Sara, I'm sorry," Mom said. "That was your car. It must have been in the grass and the truck picked it up. We can't get it back now. It's buried under the dirt."

Sara felt a big lump in her throat. She felt tears in her eyes. She loved her car. She did not want to lose it. She did not care about the pool anymore. She only wanted her car.

She dropped her toast on the plate and ran to her room. She threw herself on her bed and sobbed. She wished she had taken better care of her car. She wished she had not left it outside. She wished the truck had not taken it away.

She hugged her pillow and covered her face. She did not want to see anything. She did not want to hear anything. She did not want to eat anything. She only wanted her car.

The little girl was so excited that Grandma had helped her. They quickly went back to work on the delicious cake.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to dream about flying in the sky. One day, Timmy woke up from a rare dream and went to his mom. "Mommy, can you answer a question for me?" Timmy asked. "Of course, sweetie," his mom replied. "In my dream, I was flying. Can people really fly like birds?" Timmy asked. His mom smiled and said, "No, people can't fly like birds, but you can use your imagination to fly in your dreams." Timmy was happy with his mom's answer and went back to bed to dream about flying again.

Once, there was a girl. She had a garage. Inside the garage she kept her toys.

One day, the girl noticed something was wrong with her toys. She went in the garage and saw that they had broken.

She decided she would repair them and make them as good as new. She made sure to wash them all so they were nice and healthy.

Then she took some glue and fixed all the toys until they looked perfect. She was very pleased with her work.

When she was done, the girl could play with her toys again and have lots of fun. She was very happy.

There were two friends, Rory and Jack. Rory had a strong brush. Jack asked Rory why he had the brush. Rory said, "I need it to learn how to brush my hair." Jack said," That's smart! Can I learn too?" Rory said, "Sure! Just watch me."

Rory showed Jack how to brush his own hair. First, he put the brush on top of his head. Then, he ran the brush through his hair in long strokes. Finally, he brushed his hair all the way down.

Jack tried it too. He grabbed the brush and started brushing his hair. Jack said, "Wow! I'm learning something new!" Rory smiled and said, "Yep, brushing is fun!"

Jack and Rory kept brushing their hair until it was perfect. They were both proud of themselves. They both had learned something new!

Mama and papa were busy in the kitchen. Mama had a bowl in her hands, and she was stirring something with a spoon. Papa had a bowl, too. He was adding something to it.

"What are you preparing?" asked Mama.

"I am making a mild whip," said Papa.

Mama smiled. She added some more of the ingredients to her bowl.

"Let's see who can make a better whip!" said Papa.

Mama finished preparing the ingredients in her bowl, while Papa stirred his ingredients until they were all combined.

When they were both done, Mama put the bowl in the oven, and Papa whipped up the contents of his bowl.

The whip was light and fluffy. Papa tasted it and smiled.

"This is so mild," said Papa.

Mama smiled, too. They had both prepared a delicious and mild whip!

Jack was feeling happy. He was playing outside in his backyard. He hopped along the fence, trying to touch his toes as he walked. Suddenly, he spotted a lazy rabbit eating the grass. Jack stopped to stare. He was fascinated by the cute animal. He wanted to pet it.

But Jack couldn't get over the fence because it was too high. So Jack grabbed a box and tried to boost himself up, but he could not reach the top. He was frustrated and started to cry.

Suddenly, his dad appeared with a chair. He gave it to Jack and said, "Put this by the fence and you can use it to climb over." Jack felt so relieved. He put the chair against the fence and was able to climb over. He quickly ran to the rabbit and gave it a gentle pat. At last, Jack was happy.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the kitchen. She wanted to make lemon juice. She saw a big bowl on the table. Lily picked up a lemon and began to squeeze it into the bowl. The juice went into the bowl, and Lily was happy.

Just then, Lily's dog, Max, came into the kitchen. He barked loud, "Woof! Woof!" Lily said, "Max, you are so loud! I am making lemon juice. Do you want some?" Max wagged his tail and barked again, "Woof! Woof!"

Lily poured some lemon juice into a small bowl for Max. He lapped it up and made a funny face. "It's sour, isn't it, Max?" Lily giggled. Max barked softly, "Woof!" They both laughed and enjoyed the lemon juice together.

Once there was a bird. The bird was fit and strong. He was always happy to be outside flying in the sky. But one day he found himself in a cage and couldn't fly away. All day long he tried to find a way out but it was too hard.

Then one day a kind man saw the bird and was sad that it was in the cage. He wanted to help. The man opened the cage and went to get something. He came back with a piece of string and tied it to the cage door. He then said to the bird, "You are free now".

The bird was so happy. He arose up into the air and flew off to find a new home. He flew high and he flew far. He was so glad to be released and free. He never forgot how the kind man had helped him and was always thankful to be fit and able to fly.

Once upon a time there was a hunter who was looking for something to hunt. Everywhere that the hunter looked, he could not find any prey. But then suddenly he saw a lively fox jumping around in a meadow. The hunter was eager to catch the fox, but the fox was even more eager to escape.

The hunter yelled, "Hey fox, stop running around and be my prey!" But the fox didn't listen and kept running. He shouted louder and louder, but the fox kept on.

The fox exclaimed, "No way! I will resist you and keep running!" With that, the fox hopped and skipped around the meadow, dodging the hunter as best as he could.

The hunter was frustrated and angry. He tried to come up with different plans to catch the fox, but nothing worked. The fox was too lively! So the hunter gave up and went home without any prey that day.

Once upon a time there was a stubborn little tank.

He lived on the beach and he always made jokes about how slow he moved. All the other tanks were much faster, but he loved to tease them.

One day, the little tank met a girl. She laughed at his jokes and said she was very friendly. He was so happy! He decided to ask her to be his friend and come with him for a drive.

But the girl said no. She said she wanted a faster tank. She was so stubborn. The little tank felt very sad.

He tried to joke again, but the girl just rolled her eyes and left him alone on the beach. He was very heartbroken.

The little tank never saw the girl again and his jokes stopped being funny. He was very lonely.

The moral of the story is that stubbornness can have a bad ending.

Once there was a generous little bear. He had a big notebook full of things he wanted to do. Every day, he would stretch his arms, take a deep breath, and dream big.

One day, he wanted to give something to all his friends in the forest. So he used his notebook and wrote down all their favourite things. He had a big list of things like honey, flowers, and nuts and berries.

Then he stretched his arms out wide and made a plan to deliver a little gift to each of his friends. He was so excited. He wrote down where each of his friends lived and hopped on his bike.

All the animals in the forest were so surprised and happy. Even the most grumpiest of them all was smiling from ear to ear. The generous little bear was filled with joy and he knew that he had made many friends smile.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful little fly. The fly liked to help others. One day, the fly saw a big dog shiver in the cold. The fly wanted to help the dog, so it went to find a warm place for the dog to sleep.

The fly found a small, warm house. It went back to the dog and said, "I found a warm place for you to sleep. Follow me!" The dog followed the fly to the small house. The dog was happy and stopped shivering.

But the house belonged to a big cat. The cat saw the dog and was not happy. The cat chased the dog and the fly out of the house. The dog and the fly ran away and were cold again. They did not find a warm place to sleep that night.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily liked to pretend she was a popular princess. She lived in a big castle with her best friends, a cat and a dog.

One day, while playing in the castle, Lily found a big cobweb. The cobweb was in the way of her fun game. She wanted to get rid of it, but she was scared of the spider that lived there.

Lily asked her friends, the cat and the dog, to help her. They all worked together to clean the cobweb. The spider was sad, but it found a new home outside. Lily, the cat, and the dog were happy they could play without the cobweb in the way. And they all lived happily ever after.

Lily was deaf. She could not hear what the teacher said in the classroom. She could not hear what the other kids said to her. She felt sad and lonely.

One day, a new kid came to the classroom. His name was Ben. He was deaf too. He could use his hands to talk. He showed Lily how to do it. Lily was happy. She had a friend.

They played together at recess. They shared their toys and snacks. They learned new words with their hands. They had fun.

But some kids were mean. They did not like Ben and Lily. They said bad things about them. They laughed at them. They took their toys and snacks. They pushed them and hurt them.

Lily and Ben tried to tell the teacher. But the teacher did not understand. She did not know how to use her hands to talk. She did not help them. She said they had to grow up and stop being silly.

Lily and Ben felt angry and scared. They did not want to go to the classroom anymore. They did not want to learn anymore. They did not want to play anymore. They lost their happiness.

Once there was a girl named Ana who was three years old. All day, she was very busy playing with her toys and coloring in her coloring books. She loved all the colors.

One day, Ana decided she wanted to learn math. She ran to her Mom and said, "Mom, I want to learn math!" Her Mom said, "That's great honey".

The next day, Ana was so excited to learn math that she started screaming when she woke up. Her Mom said, "What's wrong honey?" Ana replied, "I'm just so excited to learn math!". Her Mom said, "That's great, let's get started!"

Ana was so busy learning math that she forgot to take a break! She was counting, adding and subtracting like a pro.

Once she was done with math, she started to scream for joy because she had learned so much. As Ana opened her arms wide and yelled, "I DID IT!" her Mom smiled with pride and said, "You did great honey!"

Tom is a boy who likes to play with balloons. He has many balloons of different colors and shapes. He likes to blow them up and tie them with strings. He likes to make them bounce and fly in the air.

One day, Tom finds a big yellow balloon in his room. He thinks it is a lemon balloon. He likes lemons because they are sour and make his mouth pucker. He decides to blow up the lemon balloon and see how it tastes. He puts the balloon in his mouth and blows hard.

But the balloon is not a lemon balloon. It is a balloon filled with sour water. When Tom blows hard, the balloon pops and the sour water sprays all over his face. Tom feels a sting in his eyes and a burn in his mouth. He spits out the balloon and screams.

"Ow! Ow! Ow! That hurts! That is not a lemon balloon! That is a bad balloon!" Tom cries.

His mom hears him and runs to his room. She sees him with his face wet and red. She sees the balloon on the floor. She understands what happened. She hugs him and wipes his face with a towel.

"I'm sorry, Tom. That was not a lemon balloon. That was a prank balloon. Someone gave it to me as a joke. I forgot to throw it away. It was not meant for you. It was meant to release sour water and make people laugh. But it was not funny. It was mean. Are you okay?" she asks.

Tom nods. He feels better. He still likes lemons, but he does not like sour water. He does not like prank balloons. He likes his mom. He likes his other balloons. He decides to play with them instead. He picks a blue balloon and ties it with a string. He smiles and releases it in the air. He watches it fly and bounce. He feels happy. He likes balloons.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very fond of plants and herbs. Every day she would raise them with love and care, turning them into beautiful oasis of colour and life.

One day, a little pale herb caught the little girl's attention. She raised it with special care, making sure it was always the happiest one in the garden.

Some time later, the little girl noticed that with all the nurturing and love she was giving the little herb, it was becoming ever more beautiful and full of life. This made her realise that when you truly care and raise others with love, you can witness the beauty of the world grow right before your eyes.

So, the little girl concluded that if you raise others gently and kindly, everyone in the world, big and small, will become a bit more beautiful each day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went to the beach with her mom and found an oyster. She was very excited and wanted to take it home to show her dad.

As they were walking home, Lily's mom noticed that Lily was shivering. "Are you cold?" she asked. "Yes, I am freezing," replied Lily. "Let's hurry home so we can warm up," said her mom.

When they finally got home, Lily's dad was very patient as she showed him the oyster. But then, she accidentally dropped it and it broke into a million pieces. Lily started to cry and her dad hugged her tightly. "It's okay, we can always find another oyster," he said.

Lily stopped crying and smiled. She was happy to have such a kind and patient dad.

Mommy had two special presents to give to her three year old daughter.

The first was a dependable teddy bear. It was warm and fluffy and perfect for cuddling. The little girl hugged her bear tight and smiled.

The second present was a bit more unusual. It was an oyster! She had never seen one before and the little one was curious. Mommy told her to hold it and feel the smooth surface. Then Mommy showed her how to fold the shell open. Inside was a beautiful pearl! The little girl had never seen anything so pretty before. She was delighted.

From that time on, the teddy bear and the oyster were her two most dependable friends. She held them every day, sure they would always be there to comfort her.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Max. Max loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, while she was playing, a big bad monster appeared. The monster had three heads and wiggly arms.

Max was scared and wanted to run away. But the monster offered her some sweets. "If you come a bit closer, I can give you some nice sweets," said the monster.

Max was still scared and didn't want to get too close. But then the monster said, "I won't hurt you. I just want to give you a gentle touch to show I'm a nice monster." Max could see the monster looked different than usual monsters and decided to take a closer look.

She reached out to take the sweets and noticed the monster was giving her a gentle touch instead of a bad one. Max started to feel much better. After that, they became friends and they would often play together in the sunshine.

Imagine a big field. It's full of bright, green grass. In the middle of the big field, there was a football. All around the football were lots of excited children. They were running, jumping and trying to kick the football.

The sun was shining down, making the field feel safe and warm. There were no worries, only fun. The children were playing together, enjoying their time.

Suddenly, one of the children kicked the football. It soared up and flew across the sky. Everyone on the field was filled with excitement. All of them cheered and clapped as soon as the ball landed safely at the other end of the field.

The children went to get the ball and kept playing. They all wanted to feel the same happiness as when the ball soared. Imagined and thought about what it feel like to kick the ball so high in the air. It was a wonderful feeling!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Joe. He was only 3 years old and he loved to stay outside and play with his friends. One day, Joe wanted to climb up to the top of a big tree in the backyard. His mom said it was okay, so he started climbing.

When he reached the top, he was so happy! But then he saw something wild! A large bird was sitting in the tree and it didn't look very friendly. Joe was scared, but he decided to stay and see what would happen.

The bird said to Joe: "You should not stay here! It is too dangerous!" But Joe was scared, he didn't know what to do. Then the bird flew away very quickly, and Joe was left alone on the top of the tree.

It got dark outside, and Joe started to cry. He wanted to get down, but he was too scared to move. He stayed up there, feeling cold and hungry, until the morning came.

Joe's mom found him the next morning, still on the top of the tree. She was so worried, and thankfully Joe was safe, but he never went climbing again.

Nana was walking in the garden one day when she stopped and watched the baby. The baby was very small and was wandering around. Nana smiled when she saw the baby and said, "Where are you going?"

The baby looked up at Nana and pointed to a butterfly that was fluttering in the air. Nana said, "Let's follow it!" together they started to wander through the garden.

The baby was very excited as he saw the colorful flowers, saw birds singing and heard a bee buzzing by. But then his foot got caught in a bush and he felt a small cut on his foot. Nana was very kind and knew just what to do. She took off her scarf and wrapped it around the baby's foot to make it feel better.

The baby smiled and thanked Nana before they continued to wander around the garden. They both shared stories and looked at all the beautiful things in the garden. In the end, they were both content with the day they had spent together.

One day, there was an old man. He lived in the east, far away from the city. Whenever the sun went down, he liked to stand outside and look up at the stars.

One night, the old man looked up and saw something very special. The moon was so big and so bright, it looked like it was touching the top of the sky. The old man was so excited, he wanted to show everyone how beautiful the moon was.

So the old man closed his eyes and began to pray. He prayed loud and clear, and his voice echoed over the trees. He prayed and prayed and then, suddenly, the moon began to shine brighter than ever before. The old man smiled, knowing his prayers had been answered.

And from then on, every night the old man would go out, look up at the moon, and pray.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who lived in a castle. She had a tiny empty room with no one in it. One day, a magical perfume arrived in the room, and an amazing light shone in the empty walls.

The princess was so excited, and she danced with joy. The magical perfume had a special power, it could unite people together. Everywhere the princess went, she spread the magical perfume and the people started to unite.

Soon the world was filled with love and happiness. The princess was very happy and thanked the magical perfume. But all of a sudden, the magic perfume disappeared, and the princess was sad.

But then the kind people who had been united by the perfume remembered it, and the magical scent filled the air again. Everyone celebrated and hugged each other, rejoicing in being united by the magical perfume.

The princess was so happy and thanked the perfume for uniting everyone together. From then on, the princess spread the magical perfume wherever she went, uniting people together in love and joy.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck with a lot of boxes. The truck stops near the park.

"What is in the boxes?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Let's go and see," Anna says.

They run to the truck. They see a man with a paper. He is counting the boxes.

"Hello, sir. What are you doing?" Tom asks.

"Hello, kids. I am counting the boxes. I have to deliver them to the shops. They have news in them," the man says.

"News? What is news?" Anna asks.

"News is something that tells you what is happening in the world. Like who is the president, or what is the weather, or if there is a fire, or a new animal, or anything like that. News is in the paper, or on the TV, or on the phone," the man says.

"Wow, that sounds interesting. Can we see the news?" Tom asks.

"Sure, you can have one paper. But be careful, don't rip it or get it dirty. And don't go too far, it is getting dark soon," the man says.

He gives them a paper. They say thank you and run to a bench. They look at the paper. They see a lot of words and pictures. They try to read the words, but they are too hard. They look at the pictures. They see a big building, a big cake, a big dog, and a big smile.

"Look, Tom, this is a big building. It is very tall and shiny. Maybe it is where the president lives," Anna says.

"Look, Anna, this is a big cake. It has a lot of candles and frosting. Maybe it is someone's birthday," Tom says.

"Look, Tom, this is a big dog. It has a lot of fur and a big collar. Maybe it is a new animal," Anna says.

"Look, Anna, this is a big smile. It has a lot of teeth and a big nose. Maybe it is the man who makes the news," Tom says.

They laugh and have fun. They count the pictures. They count one, two, three, four. They are happy. They learn something new. They like the news.

One day, there was an old wise man. He lived in a big house with an old carpet that led up to the front door. The wise man was looking out his window and saw a little boy.

The wise man opened his door and said hello to the little boy.

The little boy said, "Hello! Can I come in and play?"

The wise man saw that the little boy was very curious, so he said, "Yes, come in and take a look around!"

The little boy was excited. He carefully stepped on the old carpet and followed the wise man into his living room. Then, the wise man showed the boy some books and taught him about the alphabet. For a while, the little boy stayed and learned from the wise man.

When it was time for the boy to go home, the wise man gave him one last piece of advice. He said, "Be smart and always think before you make a decision."

The little boy thanked the wise man, then happily walked out of the house and back down the old carpet, feeling more wise than before.

Once upon a time, in a big pond, there was a lazy frog named Lily. She liked to sit on her big green leaf and watch the fish swim by. One sunny day, a little bug flew by and asked, "Why are you so lazy, Lily?"

Lily just shrugged and said, "I like being lazy. It's fun to watch the fish and enjoy the sun." The little bug didn't understand and flew away.

The next day, a big rain came. All the other frogs were busy swimming and playing in the water. But Lily just sat on her leaf, being lazy. A small fish swam up to her and said, "Come play with us, Lily!"

Lily shrugged again and said, "No, thank you. I like being lazy on my leaf." The small fish swam away, sad that Lily didn't want to play.

In the end, Lily stayed lazy on her leaf, watching the world go by. She liked her simple, lazy life, and that was okay.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Sally. Tom had a very creative idea for the day. He was going to make a turkey.

Tom said to Sally, "Would you like to help me make a turkey?" Sally agreed and the two of them started gathering the things they needed.

Tom asked Sally, "What do you think we need for a turkey?"

Sally replied, "We need some feathers and some glue." So Tom and Sally got some feathers and glue, and set off on their creative mission.

Tom said, "We need to make a turkey shape". So they got to work cutting the feathers and gluing them to the paper.

When they were done, they stepped back and admired their work.

"It looks so good," said Sally.

"Let's show everybody," said Tom.

So they ran off to show all of their friends their turkey. Everyone was impressed by their creative work and allowed them to keep it!

The two friends had so much fun making the turkey and were so happy that all their friends allowed them to keep it. They decided to make a different turkey every week, and each one was more creative than the last!

Once there was a boy. He didn't know what a pit was, but he soon found out. One day, he and his mom were in the park. He saw a big, round, empty pit. It was very strange and he was curious. He asked his mom, "What is that?" She said, "That's a pit, my love. It's so deep and empty."

The boy was amazed. He wanted to explore it, so he asked his mom if he could. She said yes. He walked to the edge of the pit and stared into it. He felt so small. He put his hands on the edge and looked down. It was so deep, but he wasn't scared.

The boy knew he wanted to climb down. He asked his mom if he could and she said yes. He was so excited. He grabbed a big stick and started to carefully climb down. He looked around as he went. He could see all the way to the bottom and there were lots of interesting rocks and pebbles.

Reaching the bottom, the boy felt so proud. He knew he had achieved something great. He showed his mom what he had discovered and she was so proud of him too. Together, they climbed back out of the pit. It was an adventure the boy would never forget.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw an elderly lady sitting on a bench. She had a big bag with her and a small dog on a leash.

"Let's go and say hello to her," Anna said. "Maybe she will give us a treat or let us pet her dog."

"OK," Ben agreed. They ran towards the lady and smiled.

"Hello, lady," Anna said. "What is your name? What is your dog's name?"

The lady looked at them and frowned. She did not answer. She pulled her bag closer to her and held her dog tighter.

"Go away, you naughty children," she said. "You want to steal my things and hurt my dog. Leave me alone!"

Anna and Ben were shocked. They did not want to steal or hurt anything. They just wanted to be friendly.

"Why are you so mean, lady?" Ben asked. "We are not naughty. We are nice. We just want to talk to you."

The lady did not listen. She started to scream and wave her arms. She shouted for help. She said the twins were trying to rob her and attack her.

People in the park heard her and came to see what was wrong. They saw the lady and the twins and did not know what to do. Some of them believed the lady and thought the twins were bad. Some of them doubted the lady and thought she was crazy.

Anna and Ben were scared and confused. They did not know why the lady was lying and why some people were angry at them. They wanted to explain, but no one would listen. They wanted to run away, but they were surrounded.

They wished they had never tried to talk to the lady. They wished they had stayed away from her. They wished they had never gone to the park that day.

RAPUNZEL

There were once a man and a woman who had long in vain wished for a

child. At length the woman hoped that God was about to grant her desire.

These people had a little window at the back of their house from which

a splendid garden could be seen, which was full of the most beautiful

flowers and herbs. It was, however, surrounded by a high wall, and no

one dared to go into it because it belonged to an enchantress, who had

great power and was dreaded by all the world. One day the woman was

standing by this window and looking down into the garden, when she saw a

bed which was planted with the most beautiful rampion (rapunzel), and it

looked so fresh and green that she longed for it, she quite pined away,

and began to look pale and miserable. Then her husband was alarmed, and

asked: 'What ails you, dear wife?' 'Ah,' she replied, 'if I can't eat

some of the rampion, which is in the garden behind our house, I shall

die.' The man, who loved her, thought: 'Sooner than let your wife die,

bring her some of the rampion yourself, let it cost what it will.'

At twilight, he clambered down over the wall into the garden of the

enchantress, hastily clutched a handful of rampion, and took it to his

wife. She at once made herself a salad of it, and ate it greedily. It

tasted so good to her--so very good, that the next day she longed for it

three times as much as before. If he was to have any rest, her husband

must once more descend into the garden. In the gloom of evening

therefore, he let himself down again; but when he had clambered down the

wall he was terribly afraid, for he saw the enchantress standing before

him. 'How can you dare,' said she with angry look, 'descend into my

garden and steal my rampion like a thief? You shall suffer for it!'

'Ah,' answered he, 'let mercy take the place of justice, I only made

up my mind to do it out of necessity. My wife saw your rampion from the

window, and felt such a longing for it that she would have died if she

had not got some to eat.' Then the enchantress allowed her anger to be

softened, and said to him: 'If the case be as you say, I will allow

you to take away with you as much rampion as you will, only I make one

condition, you must give me the child which your wife will bring into

the world; it shall be well treated, and I will care for it like a

mother.' The man in his terror consented to everything, and when the

woman was brought to bed, the enchantress appeared at once, gave the

child the name of Rapunzel, and took it away with her.

Rapunzel grew into the most beautiful child under the sun. When she was

twelve years old, the enchantress shut her into a tower, which lay in

a forest, and had neither stairs nor door, but quite at the top was a

little window. When the enchantress wanted to go in, she placed herself

beneath it and cried:

'Rapunzel, Rapunzel,

Let down your hair to me.'

Rapunzel had magnificent long hair, fine as spun gold, and when she

heard the voice of the enchantress she unfastened her braided tresses,

wound them round one of the hooks of the window above, and then the hair

fell twenty ells down, and the enchantress climbed up by it.

After a year or two, it came to pass that the king's son rode through

the forest and passed by the tower. Then he heard a song, which was so

charming that he stood still and listened. This was Rapunzel, who in her

solitude passed her time in letting her sweet voice resound. The king's

son wanted to climb up to her, and looked for the door of the tower,

but none was to be found. He rode home, but the singing had so deeply

touched his heart, that every day he went out into the forest and

listened to it. Once when he was thus standing behind a tree, he saw

that an enchantress came there, and he heard how she cried:

'Rapunzel, Rapunzel,

Let down your hair to me.'

Then Rapunzel let down the braids of her hair, and the enchantress

climbed up to her. 'If that is the ladder by which one mounts, I too

will try my fortune,' said he, and the next day when it began to grow

dark, he went to the tower and cried:

'Rapunzel, Rapunzel,

Let down your hair to me.'

Immediately the hair fell down and the king's son climbed up.

At first Rapunzel was terribly frightened when a man, such as her eyes

had never yet beheld, came to her; but the king's son began to talk to

her quite like a friend, and told her that his heart had been so stirred

that it had let him have no rest, and he had been forced to see her.

Then Rapunzel lost her fear, and when he asked her if she would take

him for her husband, and she saw that he was young and handsome, she

thought: 'He will love me more than old Dame Gothel does'; and she said

yes, and laid her hand in his. She said: 'I will willingly go away with

you, but I do not know how to get down. Bring with you a skein of silk

every time that you come, and I will weave a ladder with it, and when

that is ready I will descend, and you will take me on your horse.' They

agreed that until that time he should come to her every evening, for the

old woman came by day. The enchantress remarked nothing of this, until

once Rapunzel said to her: 'Tell me, Dame Gothel, how it happens that

you are so much heavier for me to draw up than the young king's son--he

is with me in a moment.' 'Ah! you wicked child,' cried the enchantress.

'What do I hear you say! I thought I had separated you from all

the world, and yet you have deceived me!' In her anger she clutched

Rapunzel's beautiful tresses, wrapped them twice round her left hand,

seized a pair of scissors with the right, and snip, snap, they were cut

off, and the lovely braids lay on the ground. And she was so pitiless

that she took poor Rapunzel into a desert where she had to live in great

grief and misery.

On the same day that she cast out Rapunzel, however, the enchantress

fastened the braids of hair, which she had cut off, to the hook of the

window, and when the king's son came and cried:

'Rapunzel, Rapunzel,

Let down your hair to me.'

she let the hair down. The king's son ascended, but instead of finding

his dearest Rapunzel, he found the enchantress, who gazed at him with

wicked and venomous looks. 'Aha!' she cried mockingly, 'you would fetch

your dearest, but the beautiful bird sits no longer singing in the nest;

the cat has got it, and will scratch out your eyes as well. Rapunzel is

lost to you; you will never see her again.' The king's son was beside

himself with pain, and in his despair he leapt down from the tower. He

escaped with his life, but the thorns into which he fell pierced his

eyes. Then he wandered quite blind about the forest, ate nothing but

roots and berries, and did naught but lament and weep over the loss of

his dearest wife. Thus he roamed about in misery for some years, and at

length came to the desert where Rapunzel, with the twins to which she

had given birth, a boy and a girl, lived in wretchedness. He heard a

voice, and it seemed so familiar to him that he went towards it, and

when he approached, Rapunzel knew him and fell on his neck and wept. Two

of her tears wetted his eyes and they grew clear again, and he could

see with them as before. He led her to his kingdom where he was

joyfully received, and they lived for a long time afterwards, happy and

contented.

Once upon a time, there were two people who were very happy - their names were Jack and Jane.
They loved each other very much, and so they decided to get married. They had a big party, and all the people at the party were happy and excited.

After they got married, Jack and Jane went to sleep in their cozy bed. They were so tired from all the excitement that they fell asleep very quickly.

The next morning, Jack and Jane woke up and hugged each other. They were very happy because they were married now, and they loved each other very much.

Jack and Jane were so happy that they went back to sleep, cuddling each other. So they slept and stayed very tired, but they were still very happy and in love.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys every evening. One day, her mom brought home a new toy for her. It was a shiny red car.

Lily was very happy and she said, "Mommy, can we play with my new car tonight?"

Her mom replied, "Of course, Lily! We can play together."

That evening, Lily and her mom played with the new car until it was time for bed. Lily was so happy that she fell asleep with a big smile on her face. From that day on, Lily played with her new toy car every evening with her mom.

It was round and smelled so good! Sammy looked around, but there was no one in sight. She cautiously walked over to the pastry and picked it up.
