Later that day, the mom and dad and the little boy went on vacation. The dad said, "Let's play by the pond and be careful to not get too close."

The mom cheered, "Yes! Let's make sure we protect each other"

The little boy led the way. He laughed when he saw the big, thick trees. He ran around and felt so happy!

Maybe next time, they can go on vacation again!

Tim and Sam are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and houses and cars. Tim has a red block and Sam has a blue block. They want to make a big tower.

"Let me add my block to your block," Tim says. He puts his red block on top of Sam's blue block.

"No, I don't like that," Sam says. He pushes Tim's block away. "I want to add my block to your block."

They both try to add their blocks to each other's blocks. They start to fight. They pull and push and shout.

"Stop it, stop it!" Mom says. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees the blocks on the floor. She sees Tim and Sam crying.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. "Why are you fighting?"

"We want to add our blocks," Tim says.

"But we don't like the same colors," Sam says.

Mom picks up a yellow block. She shows it to Tim and Sam.

"Look, this is a useful block," Mom says. "It can make your tower more colorful. It can also make a flame for your car. Do you want to try?"

Tim and Sam nod. They wipe their tears. They take the yellow block from Mom. They take turns to add it to their blocks. They make a tall tower with a red, blue and yellow block. They make a car with a yellow flame. They smile and hug.

"Thank you, Mom," Tim and Sam say. "You are useful too."

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He had a tough day and he was so very tired. He blinked and saw the sun was setting. He knew it was time for dinner.

So he got up, and went to the kitchen. He worked hard to make a delicious dinner. After stirring and chopping, the food was ready. He put it on the table and smiled with delight.

He blinked again, and his eyes lit up. It was time to eat! He took a bite and it was very tough. But then he tasted the flavor and it was so yummy. So he just kept eating and eating till the dinner was done.

The old man smiled, very happy. It was a tough day, but the dinner made it all good. He was content and knew that everything would be alright.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the mall with her mommy. They would walk around and look at all the pretty things in the stores. One day, Lily saw a dress she really liked. It was pink and had a zipper on the back. She asked her mommy to buy it for her.

When they got home, Lily tried on her new dress. It was a little big, but that was okay. She zipped it up all by herself. She felt very proud. Later that day, they went outside to play. The weather was mild and the sun was shining. Lily twirled around in her new dress, feeling happy and free.

Once there was a little girl named Ella. She was the most popular girl in school. She loved to play on the balancing beam in the playground. She was so good at balancing that she never had to use her muscles.

One day, all the kids gathered around Ella, asking her to show them what she could do. She smiled and got on the beam. She balanced so well that the kids all applauded.

Ella's teacher came out and told her not to stay on the beam too long. "Sometimes, muscles get tired," he said.

But Ella didn't listen. She stayed on the beam for a really long time. Eventually, her muscles got tired and she fell off. Everyone was very sad. Ella's teacher told her to be careful next time.

But Ella didn't listen and she fell off the beam the next time too. And the next time. The kids in school stopped asking Ella to balance on the beam, since they were afraid something bad might happen. Ella was no longer the most popular girl at school.

Angie was a little girl and she wanted to help her mum. She saw her mum washing the clothes and wanted to join in. She asked what she could do and her mum said she could wash the lung. Angie was excited and got to work. She filled up the basin with warm water and squirted in some special washing liquid.

Then, she put the lung in the basin. Angie started to wash it. She rubbed and scrubbed and swirled until it was all nice and clean. She was very happy with her work.

When the lung was washed and dried, Angie and her mum headed off to the park. On the way, Angie held the lung up high so everyone could see how clean and useful it was. Everyone was very impressed.

Angie was so proud of herself for helping to wash the lung! She had made a very useful and special thing.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Angie and Sarah. They were best friends, and they did everything together.

One day, they decided to go for a walk in the woods. As they walked, they came to a hill with a large tree on the top.

"Let's climb up the hill," said Sarah.

Angie and Sarah scrambled up the hill, and when they reached the top, they noticed a patch of soft, brown earth.

"Let's bury our wish!" said Angie.

"Yes!" Sarah agreed.

So they each drew an ordinary wish on a piece of paper and then they put the two pieces of paper in the patch of brown earth and buried them.

"Do you think our wish will come true?" Angie asked.

Sarah smiled and nodded. "I hope so," she said.

And they both went on their way, with a smile and hope in their hearts.

Once upon a time, there was a little butterfly. The butterfly loved to fly and play in the sun. One day, the butterfly saw a big pond. The water in the pond was blue and shiny.

The butterfly wanted to swim in the pond. It was very careful not to get wet. It flew close to the water and touched it with its wings. The butterfly liked the cool water on its wings.

The butterfly swam in the pond all day. It was happy and had lots of fun. When the sun went down, the butterfly flew back home. It told all its friends about the fun day swimming in the pond.

Bob was a little boat. One day, he decided to sail away. He waved goodbye to his mom and dad and they blew him kisses as he sailed away.

Bob sailed and sailed until he saw an island. it was very messy. Bob sailed to the shore, but he couldn't get to the land because it was too muddy.

But then, Bob saw someone! It was a lawyer.

"Hello!" Bob yelled to the lawyer.

"Hello there, little boat!" the lawyer said. "I can help you get to the land. I'm a lawyer and I know the law of the sea. Follow me!"

The lawyer waved to Bob and Bob followed him. With the lawyer's help, Bob made it to the messy land.

Bob was so happy! He had made it to the island without getting stuck in the mud.

The lawyer smiled and said, "You did it! Good job, little boat!" Then he waved goodbye and sailed away.

Bob was very proud of himself. He had sailed to a new adventure on his own.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy bear. He didn't like to play, he just liked to be alone. One day, he decided he wanted to try something new. He decided to the swing in the park.

He hopped onto the swing and pushed off the ground. He whooshed back and forth, feeling happier than before. As he was swinging, he spotted something soar through the sky - it was a missile.

He got excited and decided to try to grab the missile. He jumped off the swing and ran to the sky, but he was too slow! The missile kept flying higher and higher, until it was out of sight.

The grumpy bear was sad. He had missed the missile. He shuffled back to the swing, but suddenly felt much happier. Even though he had missed the missile, he realized that the swing was fun. And he never stopped swinging again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to perform a special task. She had to put all the dirty dishes in the dishwasher. Lily was very happy to help, but she found it hard to reach the top shelf.

"Mommy, it's too hard," Lily said.

"Don't worry, sweetie. I'll help you," her mommy replied.

Together, they put all the dishes in the dishwasher. Lily was so proud of herself for helping. But then, something bad happened. When they turned on the dishwasher, it made a loud noise and started to shake. Suddenly, the dishwasher exploded and water went everywhere.

Lily and her mommy were very scared and wet. They hugged each other and cried. "I'm sorry, Mommy. I didn't mean to do it," Lily said.

"It's okay, sweetie. We're just glad we're safe," her mommy replied.

From that day on, they never used the dishwasher again. They washed their dishes by hand and Lily always helped.

Once upon a time, there was a nice hill. The hill was green and had flowers on it. A little girl named Lily liked to go to the hill and set up a picnic with her mommy. They would eat sandwiches and drink juice.

One day, Lily and her mommy went to the hill and saw a big bird. The bird had a nest on the hill. Lily and her mommy were very happy to see the bird. They set down their picnic basket and watched the bird.

After a while, the bird flew away. Lily and her mommy finished their picnic and went home. They had a nice day on the hill and were happy to see the bird's nest. From then on, they went back to the hill often to see the bird and have picnics.

Once there was a little dog named Jack. He was so little and helpless, he could only crawl around. One day, Jack decided to explore the world around him. He started to climb up the stairs, but suddenly he saw something strange in the corner - a big pile of spaghetti! He just couldn't resist trying it.

Jack started crawling closer and he could smell the delicious spaghetti. He was about to eat it when suddenly he heard a voice: "No, Jack! You can't eat this spaghetti!" It was Jack's mommy. She had found him trying to eat spaghetti and she knew he was too little to do it on his own.

Jack was so embarrassed and he crawled away, feeling so helpless. His mommy smiled and said, "Don't worry, Jack. I'll make you your own plate of spaghetti for dinner later. You can have it then!" Jack was so happy and he crawled away to find something else to do.

He never forgot that day, and he still loves spaghetti to this day.

Once upon a time, there was an animal. He was a large, brown bear. But he was broken. One day, he was walking and carrying a big stick, but he was too heavy. The stick dropped to the ground and made a loud noise. The animal was sad and he started to cry.

But then out of the corner of his eye, he saw a bright, yellow butterfly. He watched as it fluttered around and lit up the sky. Seeing the butterfly made him feel better and he stopped crying. He bent down and picked up the stick. Then, he went on his way.

As the animal went on his way, he saw a broken bird in a tree. He reached up and carefully dropped the stick. Then, he used the stick to help the bird and carefully carried her away until she felt safe.

The animal was happy that he was able to help the bird, but he felt a little sad about his broken stick. He put the stick back where he had found it and smiled as he saw the bright, yellow butterfly flying around again.

The animal was still broken, but he was content knowing that he had made the world a brighter, and safer, place for one small animal.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom with the laundry. One day, Lily's mom asked her to send the laundry to the washing machine.

Lily was very enthusiastic about helping her mom. She gathered all the dirty clothes and put them in a basket. She then sent the basket to the washing machine.

While the laundry was washing, Lily and her mom had a conversation. Lily told her mom how much she loved helping with the laundry. Her mom was very proud of her and told her that she was a great helper.

After the laundry was done, Lily's mom asked her to help her fold the clothes. Lily was happy to help and they both worked together to fold the laundry. They finished quickly and Lily's mom thanked her for being such a good helper. From that day on, Lily helped her mom with the laundry every week.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside, especially on cold days. He would run around and jump in the leaves, feeling the wind on his face.

One day, Timmy's mom gave him a big, warm coat to wear. It was so cozy! Timmy put it on and ran outside to play. He felt so warm and happy.

But as the sun started to go down, Timmy began to shiver. He was so cold! That's when he remembered the uniform his dad wore when he went to work. It was warm and thick, just like his coat. Timmy wished he had a uniform too.

The next day, Timmy's mom surprised him with a uniform of his own. It was a humble uniform, but Timmy didn't care. He was so happy to have something warm to wear on cold days. From that day on, Timmy wore his uniform whenever he played outside, and he never shivered again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was only three years old. One day Amy went to visit her grandmother who lived in a fancy house. Amy's grandma showed her around the house and stopped in front of a special room.

"This is my special room," Grandma said. "It's very fancy and I don't let anyone but me go in here."

Amy was very excited and asked, "What's inside your fancy room?"

Grandma smiled. "Come on in and find out," she said. So Amy walked into the room and the first thing she saw was a toy gun. It was pink and had sparkles on it.

"This is for you! It's a toy gun," Grandma said. "You can use it to shoot at pretend targets."

Amy was so happy - she couldn't wait to start shooting. With Grandma's help, she aimed the gun and chose a target. Then she pulled the trigger and ...POW! She had shot her first target!

Amy was so proud of herself and had lots of fun shooting the toy gun. From that day on, she spent hours playing in the fancy room with her toy gun.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny who loved to have fun. One day, the bunny wanted to play with his friends, so he hopped along the forest path to find them. But it was very foggy and the bunny couldn't see. He started to worry, but then he remembered that he had something with him that he could use. He looked at his backpack and smiled, because he remembered that he had a mist in there. He opened the bag and pulled out the mist. He used it to make it so that he could see his way.

The bunny was so happy! He was able to find his friends, and soon they were all having a great time playing together. The mist was very useful, and the bunny was glad he remembered to bring it along. He made sure to keep the mist in his bag, so he could use it whenever he needed to find his way in the fog. He was very thankful for his mist!

Once there was a nosy little plant. She wanted to explore the world. So, one day, she was in a rush to get out of her pot. She pushed and pushed until she suddenly fell out the door.

The plant was so excited. The world was so big. She saw a big tree, and an even bigger sun. She wanted to explore more.

So, the little nosy plant ran and ran. She wanted to know everything. She ran into a river and splashed around. She ran up a hill and jumped on its bumpy top.

Then suddenly, she heard a voice. "Hey, where are you going!" it said. It was a friendly butterfly. The plant was so happy to meet him.

The butterfly flew with the plant through the sky and showed her all the secret places it had explored. Together they flew high, and together they raced through the air.

The little nosy plant had so much fun with the butterfly. She had explored far and wide. She was so glad that she had rushed out of the pot.

Once upon a time, there was a mechanic named Dave. He loved his job and enjoyed fixing things for people. One day, Dave got a very special job - he had to fix an orange truck.

When Dave arrived at the garage, he couldn't believe his eyes. The truck was so orange! Dave was excited to get started on the job.

But as he began to work, Dave realized it was a hard job. He worked and worked, but still the truck wouldn't work.

Dave became discouraged, and was starting to give up. He thought to himself, "I don't think I can fix it!"

Just then, Dave heard the voice of his friend, who said, "Don't give up, Dave! If you try hard enough, you can do anything!"

With new determination and courage, Dave worked harder. In the end, he was able to fix the truck. He proved to himself that if you don't give up, and if you keep trying, you can achieve anything.

Once upon a time there was a butterfly. He was so pretty and perfect that everyone loved him.

The butterfly wanted to find a new home, so he started to look. He saw lots of places, but none seemed quite right.

Then, he saw a perfect spot underneath a microscope. "Yes!" he said. "This is it!"

He flew underneath the microscope and started to settle down. But then, he relalized that he was stuck! No matter how much he fluttered and tried to move, he could not yield.

The butterfly was so sad. He stayed underneath the microscope forever, trapped and alone.

Once there was a little girl called Mandy. She had a wonderful model plane. Every day after school, she would take it out and throw it high into the sky. She loved to watch it soar up high, faster and faster.

One day, Mandy was practising throwing her model plane, when suddenly she saw an eagle soaring in the sky. It was so beautiful, she decided she wanted to throw her plane higher so she could be like the eagle.

But this time, her plane flew too high and too far away. Mandy began to worry. She searched everywhere, but the plane was gone. She was sad and upset.

Suddenly, she heard a rustling sound in the nearby bushes. She looked over and saw her plane was safely perched on a branch. She was so relieved and quickly ran over to retrieve it.

From then on, Mandy was very careful when throwing her model plane. She wanted to make sure it was safe and she never wanted to lose it again.

A battery sat in a small room, alone. Then a graceful woman arrived - she was excited to see it. She picked up the battery, feeling its weight in her hands, and then placed it on the table.

The battery seemed to know what was about to happen, and it started bouncing up and down. The woman chuckled happily, and soon the whole room was filled with the sound of her joy.

The woman then reached for a small box, opening its lid. She carefully placed the battery inside, before connecting a few wires. Suddenly, the room was illuminated with bright lights.

The woman was delighted. It felt as though the simple battery had given her an unexpected gift of light. She thanked the battery, then ran out of the room in excitement.

The battery watched its new friend leave, happy to have had the chance to make someone smile. It then gently rested in its new home, content and graceful.

Sara and Tom are playing in the kitchen. They want to make a cake for Mom. They have a big bowl, some flour, some eggs, some milk and some sugar. They also have a spoon to stir.

"Tom, can you stir the flour and the eggs?" Sara asks.

"OK, Sara, I can stir," Tom says. He takes the spoon and stirs the flour and the eggs. He stirs and stirs until they are mixed.

"Good job, Tom! Now we need to add the milk and the sugar," Sara says. She pours the milk and the sugar into the bowl. "Can you stir some more, Tom?"

"OK, Sara, I can stir some more," Tom says. He stirs and stirs until the milk and the sugar are mixed with the flour and the eggs. He stirs and stirs until the batter is smooth.

"Wow, Tom, you are a good stirrer!" Sara says. "Now we need to put the batter in the pan and bake the cake."

"OK, Sara, let's do that," Tom says. They pour the batter in the pan and put the pan in the oven. They set the timer and wait for the cake to be done.

While they wait, they see a letter on the table. It is from Grandma. Sara picks up the letter and opens it. She reads it out loud to Tom.

"Dear Sara and Tom, I miss you very much. I hope you are having fun and being good. I sent you a nice surprise in the mail. It should arrive soon. I love you. Grandma."

"Wow, Sara, Grandma is so nice!" Tom says. "I wonder what the surprise is."

"Me too, Tom. Maybe it is a toy or a book or a candy," Sara says. "I love Grandma."

"I love Grandma too," Tom says. They hug each other and smile.

Then they hear the timer beep. The cake is done. They take it out of the oven and let it cool. They decorate it with frosting and sprinkles. They write "We love you, Mom" on the cake with a squeeze bottle.

They are very proud of their cake. They can't wait to show it to Mom and share it with her. They know Mom will love it. They know Mom is nice. They love Mom.

Once upon a time a little boy named Sam was playing in the park with his friends. He noticed that some people were making a big tank in the middle of the park. Sam was fascinated and wanted to know what it was for.

The people explained that the tank was for preventing fires from happening. They said it was a popular way of protecting the park from danger.

Sam and his friends decided this was a great idea and that they wanted to help. So they filled the tank with water and washed the ground around it to help prevent fires.

When they were done, Sam's friends clapped and cheered. Sam was so proud that he had helped to prevent fires, and it had become very popular with all his friends and the people who visit the park.

Once upon a time, there was a small town. Everything was going great until one day a small tornado came. The tornado made a mess of the town that it touched. It tore everything apart. The people in the town had to clean up the mess that the tornado left.

They worked all day long, but they couldn't clean up all of the mess. Finally, they got most of the mess cleaned up. But by the time they had finished it was too dark and they still had a lot of mess left.

The next morning they woke up to find that the small tornado had come back during the night and destroyed all the work that they had done. The people were very sad and had to start all over again.

No matter how hard they tried, the town people could not get the town cleaned up from the tornado's destruction. They were left feeling helpless and small, and they never found a way to clean up their town again.

Once upon a time there was a white tray. It was big and fuzzy but very soft. It sat on the kitchen counter waiting.

Suddenly, something appeared. It was a tiny mouse. It was small and cute and it hopped onto the tray. It didn't take long before the mouse found a big piece of cheese.

The mouse happily gobbled up the cheese and started to look around the tray. The tray was filled with different foods. There were treats, fruits and vegetables. The mouse hopped around the tray and tried everything.

When the mouse finished, it didn't seem to want to leave. So he sat on the tray and enjoyed the view. He stayed all day until he finally went away.

The white tray was left all alone, until something else appeared. A big orange cat hopped onto the tray, and started to eat the food. But that's another story for another day.

Once there was a little girl named Judy. She tried on lots of pretty dresses in the store. One dress was pink and she loved it so much. But it was very expensive.

Suddenly, a selfish lady came and bought the dress before Judy could. Judy was very sad. She wanted the pink dress so badly!

The lady felt bad and wanted to make it right, so she gave Judy another dress. It was not pink but she liked it too. Judy was so happy!

She used a stick to twirl around and the dress made a beautiful swirl. Suddenly, Judy fell on the ground. She was not hurt, but her dress was dirty. Judy was sad, but she knew she could wash the dress and wear it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He had a robot toy that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy and his sister Sarah were playing hide and seek. Timmy decided to hide his robot so Sarah wouldn't find it. He put the robot in a box and covered it with a blanket.

Sarah looked everywhere for Timmy's robot, but she couldn't find it. She asked Timmy where it was, but he said he didn't know. Sarah was getting upset because she really wanted to play with the robot too.

Timmy realized that he was being selfish and decided to show Sarah where he hid the robot. He carefully uncovered the box and showed Sarah the robot. She was so happy and thanked Timmy for being kind and sharing his toy. From that day on, they played with the robot together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there lived two tigers. They were best friends and always wanted to play. One day, the tigers started to fight. The smaller tiger roared at the bigger one. The bigger tiger was scared and said, â€œStop! Donâ€™t be so loud!â€ But the smaller tiger didnâ€™t stop roaring and kept going.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sarah. She loved to imagine things. One day she imagined that she was standing in front of a big plate of spaghetti. She imagined the spaghetti was long and yummy. It was the best spaghetti ever!

Sarah loved the taste of spaghetti. She wanted to eat it, so she grabbed a fork and started eating. It was so delicious that she ate it all. She was full and happy.

But then she started feeling competitive. She wanted to know if she could eat even more spaghetti! So she imagined a big bowl of spaghetti was in front of her. This time it was even bigger than before! It was a big challenge for Sarah.

Sarah had to be brave and eat it all. But she was brave and she ate the whole bowl of spaghetti! She was so proud of herself. She had managed to eat the biggest bowl of spaghetti!

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a white cat. The cat is very pretty. Anna and Ben want to pet the cat.

But the cat is scared. It runs away from Anna and Ben. It goes into a big box. The box has a hole. The cat goes inside the hole. Anna and Ben follow the cat. They want to say hello.

But the box is a trap. When the cat goes inside, the hole closes. The cat is stuck. Anna and Ben are stuck too. They cannot get out. They are very worried. They cry for help.

A man hears them. He comes to the box. He sees the cat and the children. He is surprised. He opens the box. He lets the cat and the children out. He is very nice. He tells them not to go into traps. He says traps are for bad animals, not for cats and children.

Anna and Ben say sorry. They hug the cat. The cat is happy. It purrs. The man smiles. He gives them a cookie. Anna and Ben say thank you. They learn a lesson. They do not go into traps again. They play with the cat in the park. They are very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy loved to design things. She would draw and make things out of paper and string. One day, she made a long chain out of paper. It was very pretty and colorful.

Amy wanted to make her chain useful. She thought and thought. Then, she had an idea! She could use her chain to help her mommy. Amy's mommy was always losing her keys. So, Amy took her chain and tied it to her mommy's keys.

Now, Amy's mommy could always find her keys. The chain was very useful. Amy was happy to help her mommy. She learned that when you make something pretty and useful, it can make others happy too. And that is a good thing to do.

Once upon a time there was a bald man. He wanted to get married so he went out in the morning to find a bride. By noon he had found the sweetest lady in the whole world and asked her to marry him. She said, "Yes!" Everyone in the town was so excited that they had a feast that night to celebrate the happy couple. They kissed and danced until the sun set. And they lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue ocean. One day, Nemo saw a plastic bag in the water. "Oh no! That's waste!" Nemo said. "We must tell our friends to be careful of waste."

Nemo and his friends swam to the other side of the ocean to warn their friends. "Hey, friends! We saw waste in the water! We need to be careful!" Nemo said.

One of Nemo's friends, Sammy, asked, "What is waste?" Nemo explained, "Waste is when we throw things away that we don't need anymore. It can hurt us and our home."

Suddenly, they saw a spoiled apple floating in the water. "Ew, that looks gross!" Sammy said. "We should pick it up and put it in the trash." Nemo and his friends worked together to clean up the waste and keep their home safe.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer named Suzy. She had a big brown gate. Every day, Suzy went outside and opened the gate. She would go to the market and sell her vegetables.

One day, Suzy opened her gate, but the sun was so warm and bright! She was too tired to go to the market. Instead, Suzy decided to take a nap under the big brown gate.

Suddenly, there was a knock on the gate. Suzy awoke to find a market buyer.

"Hi Suzy, I'm here to buy your vegetables," said the buyer.

"Oh, that's wonderful," said Suzy. She joyfully sold her vegetables to the buyer and thanked him for coming by.

"No problem," said the buyer, as he waved goodbye.

Since then, Suzy always opened her big brown gate to the market, but sometimes she would take a nap under it.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. It was a hot day, and the heat made Tim feel tired. He saw his friend, Sue, playing with a ball. The ball was big and dull, but Tim wanted to play too.

"Can I play with you?" Tim asked Sue. Sue replied, "Yes, let's play!" They played with the ball under the hot sun. They had a lot of fun, but soon they were very thirsty.

Tim's mom gave them some cold water to drink. They drank the water and felt better. "Thank you, Mom," Tim said. His mom replied, "You're welcome. Have fun!" Tim and Sue continued to play until the sun went down and the heat was gone.

Tommy liked his scooter very much. He rode it every day in the park with his mom and dad. He liked to go fast and make loud noises with his mouth. He also liked to wave at the other kids and dogs he saw.

One day, he saw a girl with a pink scooter. She looked sad and lonely. Tommy wanted to be her friend. He rode his scooter to her and said hello.

"Hi, I'm Tommy. What's your name?" he asked.

"I'm Lily. I'm new here. I don't have any friends," she said.

Tommy felt sorry for her. He had an idea. He was a thoughtful boy.

"Do you want to play with me and my scooter? We can take turns and have fun," he offered.

Lily smiled and nodded. She liked Tommy's scooter. It was blue and shiny. She thanked him for being nice.

Tommy and Lily played with the scooter for a long time. They went fast and slow, up and down, and around and around. They laughed and talked and made new noises. They became good friends.

Tommy's mom and dad watched them and smiled. They were proud of their son. He was a thoughtful boy. He shared his scooter and made a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to go for walks. One day, Timmy was walking to the top of a hill. On the hill he saw a broken bike. It looked like it had been pushed over.

"Wow!" said Timmy. "I bet I could ride this!" He started to push the bike and it moved fast.

Timmy went faster and faster. He heard his mom calling him from the bottom of the hill. But he didn't want to stop. Suddenly, he hit a bump. The broken bike broke even more. Timmy went flying off.

"Oh no!" said his mom. She ran to him. Timmy was crying. He had broken his arm.

The moral of the story is to not go too fast. Timmy was lucky that he only hurt his arm and not something worse. Always listen to your mom so you don't get hurt.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved playing the flute. She would practice every day and dreamt of playing in a big concert one day. One day, she met a boy named Max who had never heard a flute before. He asked Lily if he could try playing it.

Lily handed him the flute and watched as he tried to play it. He blew into it, but no sound came out. He tried again and again, but still no sound. Lily realized that the flute was broken and needed to be fixed.

She told Max, "I need to test the flute to see what's wrong with it. Maybe we can fix it together." Max agreed and they worked together to fix the flute. After some time, they were able to fix it and it sounded beautiful.

Lily was so happy and thanked Max for helping her fix the flute. Max smiled and said, "Even though we live in distant places, we can still help each other." From that day on, they became good friends and would play music together whenever they had the chance.

Once upon a time, there was a turkey who was looking for someone to help him. He wanted to find a friend who would lead him.

One day, he met a harmless mouse. The turkey asked the mouse if he could help him. The mouse said he would try his best.

So the mouse decided to help the turkey and he showed the turkey the way. He led the turkey through the forest until they found a special place with tasty fruits and berries.

The turkey was so happy he had been led to this wonderful place, and he thanked the mouse for his help. The mouse said it was a pleasure, and the two of them enjoyed their time together in the lovely place.

The little mouse and the harmless turkey stayed friends forever, and they were happy to have each other's company.

Here is one possible story, but there are many other ways to write it.

Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big maze made of tall plants. They wanted to play in the maze. Mom said, "Be careful, don't get lost. I will wait for you here."

Ben and Lily ran into the maze. They had fun finding new paths and hiding from each other. But soon they realized they did not know how to get out. They started to feel scared and sad. They called for mom, but she did not hear them.

They saw a sign that said, "Exit this way." They followed the sign, hoping to see mom. But the sign was a trick. It led them to a dead end. There was a camera and a speaker. A voice said, "Ha ha, you fell for it. This is a modern maze. It is a prank. You are on TV. Everyone can see how silly you are."

Ben and Lily felt very embarrassed. They wanted to cry. They wished they never went into the maze. They wished they stayed with mom. They did not like the modern maze. They did not like the prank. They did not like the voice. They did not like the TV. They did not like anything.

One day, a furry kitten named Bob went to church with his mother. Everyone was very quiet and still inside the church and Bob started to feel very sleepy. He tried his best to stay awake and listen, but eventually he let out a big yawn. At first everyone in the church was quiet, but soon they started to smile and giggle a little. Bob's mom smiled too and everyone went back to listening to the sermon. Afterwards, Bob was glad that he was able to go to church, but he was also happy to go home and take a nap!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was a very curious three-year-old who liked to explore. One day, she decided to go for a walk in the park.

On her way she saw a big hill. It looked fun, so Jane decided to take a few steps up it. It was easy, so she kept going and soon she was at the top!

Jane was so proud of herself. Just then she heard someone say, "Wow! You made it up here so quickly!"

Jane turned around and saw a tall man wearing a hat. She smiled and said, "Yes, I was going very fast!"

The man laughed and said, "You sure were! Great job!"

Jane thanked him and continued on her way. With a smile on her face, she knew she could do anything if she put her mind to it.

Once upon a time there was a kind farmer. He was always looking out for a helping hand. One day he loaded up his wagon and went to the market. He had a lot of goods and needed some help to get them all in. He looked around and then he saw a small boy. He asked the boy if he could help him. The boy said yes and they worked together to load up the wagon. The goods were heavy and it was a tight fit, but they managed to get it all loaded up. The farmer thanked the boy for helping him and gave him a few coins for his help. The boy thanked the farmer and ran off. From that day on, the farmer always knew he could count on a helping hand when he needed to load things up.

Once upon a time there was an orange frog called Sam. Sam lived in a small pond near a wood. Everyday Sam would sun himself on a rock in the middle of the pond.

One day, Sam heard a noise. He hopped out of the pond to see what was happening. He saw two animals, a rabbit and a squirrel, squabbling by a tree. The rabbit and the squirrel were shouting at each other and their fur was all ruffled.

Sam hopped over to them and he said, "What is wrong here? Why are you both so angry?"

The rabbit said, "That squirrel won't share his nuts with me."

The squirrel said, "But you didn't ask nicely!"

Sam thought for a moment and said, "Maybe you could both take turns? That would be fairer."

The rabbit and the squirrel thought that was a good idea. So the squirrel gave some of his nuts to the rabbit and the rabbit shared some apples with the squirrel. After that they both said their goodbyes and went their separate ways.

Sam watched them go and was very pleased that he had been able to help out. Then he hopped back into the pond and sunned himself, feeling very content.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a new ice cream shop. In this shop, there was a magic ice cream cone. This cone could grow bigger and bigger when you said the magic word.

One sunny day, a little girl named Lily came to the shop. She saw the magic cone and asked the shopkeeper, "What is this cone for?" The shopkeeper smiled and said, "This is a magic cone. When you say 'grow', it will get bigger and bigger!"

Lily was very excited. She bought the magic cone and said, "Grow!" The cone grew bigger and bigger, just like the shopkeeper said. Lily shared her big ice cream with her friends. They all laughed and enjoyed the sweet treat together.

From that day on, Lily and her friends would visit the new ice cream shop every day. They loved the magic cone and the fun it brought to their little village. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a bright rabbit. She loved to bite things. She especially liked to bite leaves and blades of grass.
One day she found the most delicious leaf in the forest. She took a bite and it tasted so yummy! But after she ate it, she was left with a mark on her fur.
The bright rabbit was so confused. She tried scrubbing the mark with water but it wouldn't come off.
So she tried other things like rubbing mud on it and tapping it with her paw. Nothing worked though.
Finally the bright rabbit came up with an idea. She licked the mark until it slowly disappeared.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but they do not share them well. Sometimes they fight over the toys and make a lot of noise.

One day, their mom says, "Lily and Ben, I have a surprise for you. Come and see." She takes them to the living room, where she has a big table. On the table, she has displayed many books, puzzles, and games. "These are for you to play with," she says. "But you have to follow some rules. You have to take turns, and you have to ask before you touch anything. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nod. They are very excited. They see many things they like. Lily sees a book with animals. She loves animals. She asks, "Mom, can I touch this book?" Mom says, "Yes, you can. But you have to let Ben look at it too, when he wants to." Lily says, "OK." She picks up the book and opens it. She sees a picture of a lion. She says, "Look, Ben, a lion! It is big and yellow and has a mane."

Ben sees a puzzle with cars. He loves cars. He asks, "Mom, can I touch this puzzle?" Mom says, "Yes, you can. But you have to let Lily help you too, when she wants to." Ben says, "OK." He picks up the puzzle and starts to put the pieces together. He sees a picture of a red car. He says, "Look, Lily, a car! It is fast and shiny and has four wheels."

Lily and Ben play with the books and the puzzles for a while. They take turns and ask before they touch. They show each other what they find. They have fun. Mom is happy. She says, "You are playing very well. You are being fair and kind. I am proud of you." Lily and Ben smile. They hug their mom and say, "Thank you, mom. We love you."

Anna loved animals. She wanted to be a veterinarian when she grew up. She liked to read books about animals and watch them on TV. She also liked to play with her stuffed animals and pretend they were sick or hurt. She would use her toy stethoscope and bandages to make them feel better.

One day, Anna went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a lot of animals there. She saw birds, squirrels, dogs, and cats. She wanted to pet them all, but her mom and dad told her to be careful and ask the owners first. Anna was impatient. She wanted to touch the animals and hear their hearts.

She saw a big dog with a red collar. He looked friendly and wagged his tail. Anna ran towards him, but he barked and growled. He did not like strangers. Anna was scared and cried. The dog's owner came and apologized. He said his dog was nervous and needed to see a veterinarian. He said the veterinarian would help his dog feel calm and happy.

Anna felt sorry for the dog. She wondered what a veterinarian was. She asked her mom and dad. They explained that a veterinarian was a doctor for animals. They said a veterinarian could check the animals' health and give them medicine or surgery if they needed it. They said a veterinarian could also teach the owners how to take care of their animals and prevent them from getting sick or hurt.

Anna was amazed. She wanted to learn more about veterinarians. She decided to be more patient and respectful with the animals. She thought that maybe one day, she could be a veterinarian too. She smiled and hugged her stuffed animals. She said she would take them to the veterinarian if they ever felt bad. She said she loved animals and wanted to help them.

Once upon a time there was a kid who loved to unpack. One day, the kid was so excited that they ran outside in their garden. When they stepped out, they felt surprised! It was cold and icy! The kid looked around, and noticed all the boxes that had been delivered. They were full of toys and treats.

The kid quickly ran towards the boxes, and started unpacking. One by one, they pulled out all the things from the boxes. Their eyes sparkled as they found each new toy. They found cars, and dolls, and a big stuffed bear.

The kid danced around in the cold icy air, laughed, and jumped around. They were so happy! After all the boxes had been unpacked, the kid slept soundly, dreaming of all their new toys.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old. She liked to dream about things she wanted to do and places she wanted to go. She also liked to see her neighbor.

Her neighbor was fierce but kind too. He always helped the little girl and made her feel safe. The little girl liked to visit her neighbor.

One day, the little girl had a dream that she went on a big adventure. She went to new places, saw amazing things and had so much fun.

When she woke up, she smiled. She remembered her dream and was excited to tell her neighbor about it. She ran over to his house and began to tell him all about it. He listened carefully and smiled.

The little girl was so happy that she and her neighbor shared her dream together.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little eraser. The eraser was sad because it was broken. It wanted to fix itself so it could help kids with their drawings. The eraser knew that if it could find a special glue, it could fix itself and be happy again.

One day, the eraser met a kind boy named Tim. Tim saw the poor eraser and wanted to help. He remembered that his dad had special glue in the garage. Tim thought that the glue could fix the eraser. So, they went on a fun journey to find the special glue.

When they found the glue, Tim was very careful to fix the eraser. The eraser was so happy to be whole again! From that day on, the eraser and Tim became best friends. The eraser always helped Tim with his drawings, and they had lots of fun together.

One day, Jack and his mom were at the park. They were having a lot of fun! Suddenly, Jack spotted something shiny near the slide. He quickly ran up to it.

It was a smooth piece of cardboard! Jack was very excited. He picked it up and showed it to his mom.

"Look, Mommy!" he said. "Look what I found!"

His mom smiled. "That's lovely, Jack," she said. "What are you going to do with it?"

Jack thought for a moment. He realized he could make a kite out of the cardboard! He smiled and grabbed the piece of cardboard and ran off.

Mom watched him go. Jack dropped the cardboard several times but he kept picking it up and running.

Eventually, Jack made it to the top of the hill. He tied the cardboard together, and made a perfect kite. He couldn't wait to fly it!

Jack and his mom had lots of fun that day, thanks to the smooth piece of cardboard.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop around the forest and play with his friends. One day, Benny's friend, a little bird named Billy, came to him and said, "Benny, I want to introduce you to my new friend, a big bad wolf."

Benny was scared of the big bad wolf, but he didn't want to be rude to Billy's new friend. So, he went with Billy to meet the wolf. The wolf seemed nice at first, but Benny noticed that he was eyeing him hungrily. Suddenly, the wolf pounced on Benny and chased him through the forest.

Benny tried to run away, but he couldn't shake the wolf. He ran and ran until he came to a track that led to a cliff. Benny didn't know it was a dead end, and the wolf quickly caught up to him. The wolf gobbled up Benny in one big bite, and poor Benny was never seen again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was eager to go to the park. When she got there, she saw a huge balloon just waiting for her. She jumped up and down in excitement.

"What's inside, Mommy?" Lucy asked.

"I don't know," her mom answered. "Let's find out!"

Lucy grabbed the ribbon tied to the balloon and pulled it open. Inside, a flower began to bloom! It was the most beautiful flower she had ever seen. She smiled with delight.

"It's so pretty!" Lucy said.

"Yes it is," her Mom agreed.

Lucy couldn't wait to show her friends the beautiful flower. She was as eager as ever to share her new discovery. The flower was her favorite thing in the whole park!

Once upon a time there was a bear named Bob who lived in the woods. One day, Bob felt very sleepy and he didn't feel like doing anything. Unfortunately, he had to find some food, so he started to walk around to look for something to eat.

Suddenly, Bob heard a loud noise. He was a bit scared so he slowly peeked around the corner. What he saw made him very surprised! It was two foxes, arguing and fighting over something. Bob felt bad for them, so he decided to try and help.

He stepped into the clearing and said, "Hey! Why are you fighting?"

The foxes looked at Bob and stopped. The bigger fox said, "This is my food, but the other fox said that it was his too."

Bob thought for a minute, then he said, "I have an idea. Why don't you both step back and I'll increase the amount of food so that there's enough for both of you?"

The foxes looked at each other and then agreed with Bob's plan. As Bob had promised, he added more food so that both of the foxes could have equal amounts. The foxes thanked him and promised him to not fight again.

Bob was glad that he could help. He felt really happy as he continued his journey to find food.

Lila and her mom went to the park. Lila saw a big round thing that she could sit on and spin. She ran to it and climbed on. She asked her mom to push her.

"Mom, push me! Push me!" she said.

"Okay, Lila, but not too fast. You might get dizzy," her mom said.

Lila liked to spin. She felt the wind on her face and the sun on her hair. She laughed and waved her arms. She saw other kids playing on the swings and the slide. She wanted to play with them too.

"Mom, can I go play with them?" she asked.

"Sure, Lila, but be polite. Say hello and ask if you can join them," her mom said.

Lila nodded. She got off the round thing and ran to the swings. She saw a girl with curly hair and a blue dress. She smiled and said, "Hi, I'm Lila. Can I swing with you?"

The girl smiled back and said, "Hi, I'm Mia. Yes, you can swing with me. Do you want to go high?"

Lila nodded again. She sat on the swing next to Mia. Mia's mom pushed them both. They swung high and low. They had fun.

Lila's mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of her daughter. She was polite and friendly. She liked to spin and swing. She was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and her daughter. The daughter was very obedient and was always kind to everybody.

One day, the mom asked her daughter, "Would you like to go for a picnic today?"

The daughter was very excited, "Yes mommy!"

They spent the day together, playing games and laughing. When they were nearly done, the mom decided to spoil her daughter: "Let's have a victory picnic!"

The daughter was so happy. She said, "Yes please, mommy!"

So the mom packed their food and they ate until they were full. The daughter was so happy that her mom had spoiled her with a victory picnic. They both returned home with smiles on their faces.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a deaf, three year old girl. She loved going to the library every day and read books.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a big toy box where he kept all his toys. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to tidy up his toys and put them back in the toy box. Timmy didn't want to tidy up because he wanted to keep playing.

But then, Timmy's little sister came in and wanted to play too. She wanted to play with Timmy's favorite toy car, but she couldn't find it because all the toys were scattered around the room. Timmy saw that his sister was sad, so he decided to cover her with a blanket to make her happy.

After that, Timmy realized that he couldn't play with his toys if they were all over the place. So, he decided to slide all his toys back into the toy box. It was hard work, but he felt good when he was finished. Timmy's mom was very happy that he tidied up and he got to play with his sister and his toys again!

Little Jack was so proud of his igloo. It was the biggest one in the neighbourhood and he had worked so hard on it with his dad.

Little Jack's dad called to him from the porch. "Let's go for a walk!" he said.

Jack eagerly jumped up and ran over. "Where will we go?" he asked.

Dad smiled. "Let's go and visit the Arctic Igloos," he replied.

Little Jack was so excited. He ran ahead of his dad as they made their way to the igloo village. As they got closer and closer, they could see all the igloos in their bright colours.

Little Jack gasped in amazement. Dad pointed to the biggest one in the village. "I bet that's the most important one," he said.

Little Jack smiled. His dad was right. He ran ahead and urged his dad to follow. As they got closer, Jack could see his dad's proud smile.

Lily and Anna were best friends. They liked to play dress-up with their dolls. One day, they found a big box of old clothes in the attic. They wanted to decorate their dolls with the clothes.

They saw a cool skirt in the box. It was pink and had many flowers on it. Lily and Anna both wanted the skirt for their dolls. They started to pull the skirt from each other.

"Give me the skirt! It is mine!" Lily shouted.

"No, it is mine! I saw it first!" Anna yelled.

They pulled harder and harder. The skirt ripped in half. Lily and Anna both cried. They had ruined the cool skirt.

Their mom heard them and came to the attic. She saw the ripped skirt and the sad girls. She hugged them and said, "Why did you fight over the skirt? You are best friends. You should share and be kind to each other."

Lily and Anna felt sorry. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to use the two halves of the skirt to decorate their dolls. They made two cool skirts out of one. They were happy again.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Fighting is not nice. Friends should help each other.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They sat down to eat lunch. Tim noticed his mom had a rare sauce on her sandwich. "Mom, what is that?" he asked.

His mom said, "This is a rare sauce that I found at the store. It is very tasty. Do you want to try some, Tim?" Tim said yes and his mom put some sauce on his sandwich.

Tim took a bite and smiled. "I like the sauce, Mom!" he said. They enjoyed their lunch at the park and played on the swings. They had a fun day and Tim was happy he got to try the rare sauce.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and watch cartoons on his modern TV. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a present. It was a big, shiny present with a pretty wrap on it.

Timmy was so excited to open the present, but when he did, he didn't like what was inside. It was a shirt that he didn't like. Timmy's mom asked him why he didn't like the shirt, and Timmy just shrugged his shoulders.

Later that day, Timmy saw a homeless man on the street who didn't have any clothes to wear. Timmy remembered the shirt his mom gave him and realized that he could give it to the homeless man. Timmy felt happy that he could help someone in need and learned that sometimes things may not seem important, but they can be helpful to others.

One day, Mommy gave Little Jimmy a very special job. "Can you help me clean up the garage?" she asked. Little Jimmy was very obedient and immediately said yes. He began to look around for something to clean. He spotted something shiny on the floor. It was a screw!

He picked it up and took it to Mommy. "What is this?" Little Jimmy asked.

Mommy smiled. "That's a screw," she said. "Thank you for picking it up! That was a very obedient thing to do."

Little Jimmy was so proud that he had done something helpful. He stuck the screw in his pocket and continued cleaning the garage. In no time, the garage was all nice and neat!

Mommy hugged Little Jimmy and said, "I am so proud of you. You did a wonderful job cleaning the garage." Little Jimmy smiled. He had been so obedient and he felt very proud.

One day in the park, Louie saw a big bag. He wanted to find out what was inside. He was very curious and persistent in his search.

"What's in the bag?" he asked his mom.

Louie played with his puppy and his new toys. He was so happy to have found such wonderful surprises. This was one of his best days ever and he was so happy to be persistent in finding out what was inside the bag.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Billy. He was only three years old and loved to play in the garden. Every day, his mom told him to wash his hands after playing outside.

One day, Billy found something very exciting in the garden. It looked like a little comet, like the ones he'd seen in books about space. It was a bit spoiled from being in the garden, but Billy thought it was the most wonderful thing he'd ever seen.

Billy didn't want to wash his hands, he wanted to keep playing with the comet. His mom said, "Billy, you need to wash your hands. That comet is very dirty."

But Billy wasn't listening and he kept playing with it. His mom got angry and shouted, "Billy, come here right now and wash your hands!"

Billy was scared but he knew that he had to do what his mom said. So he reluctantly washed his hands, dried them off and put the spoiled comet back in the garden. He looked at it sadly as he left, wishing that he could keep playing with it.

Once upon a time there was a big, hot spider. He lived in a dark cave, but he was very brave.

One day, the spider had an idea. He wanted to try brewing a special drink. He mixed many special ingredients, including poison.

The drink was very hot, so the spider had to be careful. He put on his special gloves and drank a little bit. He felt very strange afterwards, but he was glad he was brave enough to try his special drink.

The spider was so happy with his drink that he decided to share it. He cooked up more of his special potion, and gave it out to all the other spiders. They all loved it so much that they made it their favorite drink!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a big toy box with lots of fun things inside. But the box was very heavy and she couldn't open it. Once upon a time there was a young boy. His name was John and he loved to play. One day, he was playing in his backyard when he bumped his knee. It really hurt!

John started to cry and his mum came to help him. She was very kind, and gave John a big hug. That made John feel better, because hugs can heal a broken heart.

The next day, John went to the park with his mum. As they walked, they saw a wall that was very high. John was so excited that he wanted to jump and touch it. His mum said, "you can try, but if you hurt yourself again I will have to give you another hug!"

John bravely jumped until he could touch the wall. He did it! His mum gave him a tasty treat to celebrate his success.

John's knee soon healed, but he will never forget the day he jumped to touch the wall.

Once upon a time, there were two twins who loved to play together. They were always honest with each other and never told lies. One day, they went to the park to play on the swings. After a while, it started to get dark, and their mother called out to them to come home.

The twins started to walk home, but they got lost. They didn't know which way to go, and it was getting colder and darker. They tried to find their way back, but they couldn't. Finally, they saw a house with a light on, so they went to ask for help.

The person who answered the door seemed nice, but they weren't honest. They told the twins to come inside and wait for their parents. But they didn't call the twins' parents, and they didn't let the twins leave. The twins were scared and wanted to go home, but the person wouldn't let them. They were trapped, and they couldn't escape. The twins wished they had never left the park and closed their eyes, hoping to wake up from this bad dream.

Once upon a time there was a sack. In the sack there was a welcome. It was a friendly welcome.

"Who is there?" asked the sack.
"It's me, your friend," replied the welcome.

The sack was so happy to have a friendly visitor. She opened to let the welcome inside.

The welcome was so excited to be inside. She thanked the sack and said, "This will be a very fun visit!"

The sack smiled and nodded in agreement. They spent the day playing and having lots of fun.

At the end of the day the welcome said her goodbyes and promised to come again soon.

The sack was very sad to see her friend go, but was happy because they made such wonderful memories together. And with this, the sack knew she had something special that she could always welcome back.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Jane and John. They always liked to play together, but today they disagreed.

"I want to play with the cars," said John.

"No! I want to play with the dolls," said Jane.

The two friends were silent. Neither of them wanted to give in.

Then, John had a clever idea. "Let's do both! We can play with the dolls and use the cars to drive them, too."

Jane thought it was a great idea and they both agreed. They were so happy that they could work together and still have fun.

The moral of the story is that you should never disagree with a friend. Working together can make the most fun for everyone. So the next time you disagree with someone, try to find a way to work together.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went outside to play. She saw her friend, a little boy named Timmy, and ran over to him.

"Hi Timmy, what are you doing?" asked Lily.

"I'm trying to catch a ball," replied Timmy.

Lily saw the ball and picked it up. "This object is warm," she said, feeling the sun on the ball.

"Yes please," said Timmy.

Lily threw the ball to Timmy and he caught it. They played catch together for a long time and had lots of fun. When it started to get dark, they said goodbye and went home.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little puppy who lived with its family in a cozy home. He always loved to explore the house and play with everyone. One day, the puppy noticed something really interesting near the kitchen: an oven.

The puppy bounded over to the oven and started jumping around excitedly. He was fascinated by the sight of the oven and was determined to get inside it.

The puppy's mom noticed her little pup and smiled. "Oh my, what are you up to little one?" she asked.

The puppy responded with a bark and kept jumping around the oven.

The mom opened the oven and the puppy was so excited to see what was in there! He jumped around, sniffing and exploring. As the puppy scampered around, the mom could not help but smile at his adorable antics.

The puppy explored the oven, making sure to use only his nose of course! He was so happy to have seen the inside of the oven and soon went back to playing with his family.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to rush around. She was very active and loved to explore. One day she heard a rustling in the trees and she was curious to find out what it was. Once there was a wide and open field. In the field, there were two children playing. They were running and laughing, having lots of fun.

But he was too stupid and instead of picking the leaf he dropped it. The little squirrel looked down and got very sad. The leaf floated away in the wind and he wanted it back.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sun. One day, he fell and hurt his knee. It hurt a lot and he cried.

His friend agreed and they played until it was time to go home. Timmy was happy that his knee was healing and that he had a fun day with his friend. He went to bed with a smile on his face, knowing that tomorrow would be another great day.

Once there was a girl named Maya. She was three years old. One day, Maya and her mom went to a store. Maya saw a pretty cup. It was bright blue with stars all around. She felt so excited. She asked her mom to buy it for her.

Mom smiled and said, "Sure, this cup looks great. Let's get it for you."

Maya was so happy she could hardly contain herself. She grabbed the cup and hugged it tight. Then she said thank you to her Mom.

On the way home, Maya held the cup tightly in her hands. She felt so happy and excited, like she was the luckiest girl in the world. When she reached home, she put the cup on her shelf and smiled. It made her feel great.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Freddy. Freddy lived in a pond with his friends. One day, Freddy saw a beautiful frog named Lily. He asked her, "Will you marry me?" Lily said, "Yes!"

Freddy was so happy, but his friends were miserable. They didn't like Lily because she was different from them. They said, "We don't want you to marry her, Freddy." But Freddy loved Lily and didn't listen to his friends.

Finally, Freddy and Lily got married by the pond. All of their friends came to the wedding and saw how happy Freddy was with Lily. They realized that being different was okay and they all became friends again. Freddy and Lily lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little red grill. It was all alone in the backyard and didn't have any friends. The grill wanted to have a party, but he was afraid nobody would come.

Then, one day, someone heard the grill's cries for help. With a big smile, the person poured special red sauce on the grill. The sauce spread out like a blanket and soon the whole grill was glowing red.

THE SEVEN RAVENS

There was once a man who had seven sons, and last of all one daughter.

Although the little girl was very pretty, she was so weak and small that

they thought she could not live; but they said she should at once be

christened.

So the father sent one of his sons in haste to the spring to get some

water, but the other six ran with him. Each wanted to be first at

drawing the water, and so they were in such a hurry that all let their

pitchers fall into the well, and they stood very foolishly looking at

one another, and did not know what to do, for none dared go home. In the

meantime the father was uneasy, and could not tell what made the

young men stay so long. 'Surely,' said he, 'the whole seven must have

forgotten themselves over some game of play'; and when he had waited

still longer and they yet did not come, he flew into a rage and wished

them all turned into ravens. Scarcely had he spoken these words when he

heard a croaking over his head, and looked up and saw seven ravens as

black as coal flying round and round. Sorry as he was to see his wish

so fulfilled, he did not know how what was done could be undone, and

comforted himself as well as he could for the loss of his seven sons

with his dear little daughter, who soon became stronger and every day

more beautiful.

For a long time she did not know that she had ever had any brothers; for

her father and mother took care not to speak of them before her: but one

day by chance she heard the people about her speak of them. 'Yes,' said

they, 'she is beautiful indeed, but still 'tis a pity that her brothers

should have been lost for her sake.' Then she was much grieved, and went

to her father and mother, and asked if she had any brothers, and what

had become of them. So they dared no longer hide the truth from her, but

said it was the will of Heaven, and that her birth was only the innocent

cause of it; but the little girl mourned sadly about it every day, and

thought herself bound to do all she could to bring her brothers back;

and she had neither rest nor ease, till at length one day she stole

away, and set out into the wide world to find her brothers, wherever

they might be, and free them, whatever it might cost her.

She took nothing with her but a little ring which her father and mother

had given her, a loaf of bread in case she should be hungry, a little

pitcher of water in case she should be thirsty, and a little stool

to rest upon when she should be weary. Thus she went on and on, and

journeyed till she came to the world's end; then she came to the sun,

but the sun looked much too hot and fiery; so she ran away quickly to

the moon, but the moon was cold and chilly, and said, 'I smell flesh

and blood this way!' so she took herself away in a hurry and came to the

stars, and the stars were friendly and kind to her, and each star sat

upon his own little stool; but the morning star rose up and gave her a

little piece of wood, and said, 'If you have not this little piece of

wood, you cannot unlock the castle that stands on the glass-mountain,

and there your brothers live.' The little girl took the piece of wood,

rolled it up in a little cloth, and went on again until she came to the

glass-mountain, and found the door shut. Then she felt for the little

piece of wood; but when she unwrapped the cloth it was not there, and

she saw she had lost the gift of the good stars. What was to be done?

She wanted to save her brothers, and had no key of the castle of the

glass-mountain; so this faithful little sister took a knife out of her

pocket and cut off her little finger, that was just the size of the

piece of wood she had lost, and put it in the door and opened it.

As she went in, a little dwarf came up to her, and said, 'What are you

seeking for?' 'I seek for my brothers, the seven ravens,' answered she.

Then the dwarf said, 'My masters are not at home; but if you will wait

till they come, pray step in.' Now the little dwarf was getting their

dinner ready, and he brought their food upon seven little plates, and

their drink in seven little glasses, and set them upon the table, and

out of each little plate their sister ate a small piece, and out of each

little glass she drank a small drop; but she let the ring that she had

brought with her fall into the last glass.

On a sudden she heard a fluttering and croaking in the air, and the

dwarf said, 'Here come my masters.' When they came in, they wanted to

eat and drink, and looked for their little plates and glasses. Then said

one after the other,

'Who has eaten from my little plate? And who has been drinking out of my

little glass?'

'Caw! Caw! well I ween

Mortal lips have this way been.'

When the seventh came to the bottom of his glass, and found there the

ring, he looked at it, and knew that it was his father's and mother's,

and said, 'O that our little sister would but come! then we should be

free.' When the little girl heard this (for she stood behind the door

all the time and listened), she ran forward, and in an instant all

the ravens took their right form again; and all hugged and kissed each

other, and went merrily home.

John was a curious little boy. He liked to wander around and explore new places. One day, he decided to explore the living room in his home. There were many things to discover - books, toys, a big TV and interesting looking objects.

John saw a plate on the shelf. It was colourful and round and it looked so inviting. He decided to pick it up and take a closer look. It was thick and it had pictures on it. He couldn't help but touch it. He felt the smoothness of its edges and was delighted with his find.

He continued to wander around the living room, eventually deciding to put the plate back on the shelf with an air of satisfaction. He was glad he had gone exploring!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Joe. Joe was three years old and he loved to explore the world.

One day, Joe went outside. He saw a big puddle and he decided to jump in it! But when he tried to jump, he slipped and almost fell in.

Luckily, his mom came to help him. She put her arm around him and gave him a big hug. She said, "Don't worry, I'm here to support you!" Joe thanked her and he felt much better.

Then, Joe had a very creative idea! He gave his mom a big smile and said, "Let's jump together!" So they jumped into the puddle, and they had so much fun!

Afterwards, Joe and his mom held hands and they laughed together. Joe was so happy and he thanked his mom for all her support. Joe and his mom continued to explore the world together!

Once upon a time, there was a generous lady who had an important job. Her job was to remind the people in her town to be kind. She helped people who were in jail and made sure they had enough to eat. She always gave them a big smile when she visited.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she found a pretty daisy in the grass. It was normal, just like all the others, but to Lily, it was special.

Lily picked up the daisy and showed it to her friend, Timmy. "Look, Timmy! I found a pretty flower," she said. Timmy smiled and said, "That's nice, Lily. Can we play now?"

Lily paused for a moment, looking at the daisy in her hand. "Okay, let's play!" she said, and they ran off together. But Lily didn't forget about her special daisy. She carried it with her all day, showing it to everyone she met. And every time she looked at it, she felt happy.

The boy was ready to dive into the pool. It was so much fun splashing around and feeling like he was flying. He liked it so much he dove in again and again.

The lawyer watched from outside the pool. He was so impressed with the boy's diving skills he decided he wanted to join in. So the lawyer dove into the pool too, splashing around and feeling like flying just like the boy. They both had so much fun diving together.

Finally, when they were both all done, they climbed out of the pool. The boy and the lawyer were ready to do it all again!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bike with his friends. One day, Timmy's tire popped and he fell off his bike. He was sad because he couldn't ride his bike anymore.

But Timmy's friends were there to support him. They helped him fix his tire so he could ride his bike again. Timmy was so happy and grateful for his friends.

From then on, Timmy always made sure to be alert and check his bike tire before riding. He didn't want to have another accident and miss out on all the fun with his friends.

Once there was a rare crane that flew in the sky. It was the most wonderful crane anyone had ever seen! It was so beautiful, people came from all around the world just for a chance to glimpse the crane.

One day, a little boy wanted to catch the crane. So he grabbed his net and set off looking for the crane. Everywhere he went, people said the crane had gone, but he kept looking.

From that day on, the little boy never gave up looking for a rare crane again. He always remembered how special it was to catch one.

Lily was a daughter who liked to play with her toys. She had a doll, a bear, a ball and a car. She loved them all very much and took good care of them. She always put them away when she was done playing.

One day, her mom said, "Lily, we have to go to the store. Can you help me get ready?" Lily nodded and ran to her room. She wanted to bring her doll with her, but she could not find it. She looked under her bed, in her closet, in her drawers, but it was not there. She felt sad and scared. Where was her doll?

She ran to her mom and said, "Mom, I can't find my doll. I want to bring her with me. Where is she?" Her mom frowned and said, "I don't know, Lily. Did you put her away last time you played with her?" Lily nodded, but she was not sure. Maybe she left her somewhere else. Maybe someone took her. She started to cry.

Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will find your doll. Maybe she is in the living room or the kitchen. Let's go look together." They walked to the living room and saw Lily's brother, Tom, sitting on the couch. He was holding Lily's doll and making her talk in a funny voice. He was pretending that the doll was his friend and that they were going on a trip.

Lily saw her doll and shouted, "Tom, that's my doll! Give her back to me! You are bad!" She ran to him and tried to grab her doll, but Tom held it tight. He said, "No, Lily, this is my doll now. She likes me better than you. You are bad!" He stuck out his tongue at her.

Lily and Tom started to fight over the doll. They pulled and pushed and yelled. Their mom saw them and said, "Stop it, both of you! You are being very naughty. Tom, give Lily her doll back. She is not yours. Lily, don't hit your brother. He is not bad. You are both good, but you need to share and be nice." She took the doll from Tom and gave it to Lily. She said, "Lily, I'm sorry that Tom took your doll. He was wrong to do that. But you can let him play with her sometimes, if he asks nicely. Tom, I'm sorry that Lily hit you. She was angry and scared. But you can't take her toys without asking. You have to respect her things and her feelings."

Lily and Tom looked at each other and felt sorry. They said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, Tom." They hugged each other and their mom. They said, "We love you, mom. We love you, Lily. We love you, Tom." They smiled and decided to play together with the doll, the bear, the ball and the car. They had fun and were happy. Their mom smiled and said, "That's better. Now, let's go to the store." They put away their toys and went to the store. They were a good family.

Once upon a time, there was an elephant. He was very creative and wanted to try something different. He decided to increase his age to become bigger. One day, he used his magic to become older. Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing basketball with his friends at the park. One day, a new boy named Billy came to the park and wanted to play too. But Billy was very bossy and always wanted the ball.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But they also liked to look for bugs. They had a jar with holes in the lid. They put some grass and leaves in the jar. Then they searched for bugs to put in the jar.

"Look, Lily, I found a green bug!" Ben said. He showed Lily a small beetle with shiny green wings. "It is so pretty! Can we keep it?"

Lily nodded. She liked the green bug too. She opened the jar and Ben put the bug inside. They closed the lid and shook the jar gently. The bug crawled on the grass and leaves.

"Let's find more bugs!" Lily said. She ran to a flower bed and looked for more bugs. Ben followed her.

They found a red bug, a yellow bug, a black bug and a blue bug. They put them all in the jar. They were happy. They had a lot of bugs.

But then they heard a loud buzz. A big bee flew near them. It saw the jar with the bugs. It wanted to see the bugs too. It flew to the jar and tried to get in. It pushed the lid with its head.

"Go away, bee!" Ben said. He waved his hand at the bee. "These are our bugs! You can't have them!"

But the bee did not go away. It was angry. It stung Ben on his lip. Ben cried out. His lip hurt. It was red and swollen.

Lily saw Ben's lip. She felt sorry for him. She hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. The bee was mean. Let's go to mom. She will make your lip better."

Ben nodded. He held Lily's hand. They took the jar with the bugs. They ran to their mom. She was sitting on a bench. She saw Ben's lip. She said, "Oh, Ben, what happened? Did a bee sting you?"

Ben nodded. He said, "Yes, mom. The bee wanted our bugs. We found a lot of bugs. Look, mom, we have a green bug!"

Mom smiled. She said, "You have a lot of bugs. They are very pretty. But you have to be careful with bees. They can sting you. Let me see your lip."

Mom took a tissue and put some ice on Ben's lip. She said, "This will make your lip feel better. It will go down soon. Don't worry."

Ben felt better. He said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

Mom said, "You're welcome, Ben. You are very brave. Now, why don't you and Lily settle on the grass and watch your bugs? Maybe they will do something funny."

Ben and Lily settled on the grass. They watched their bugs. They saw the green bug fly, the red bug crawl, the yellow bug jump, the black bug hide and the blue bug shine. They laughed. They were happy. They forgot about the bee. They had fun with their bugs.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and her toys. One day, her mommy asked her to help move some furniture around in the living room. Lily was happy to help and started to push the sofa.

One day, there was a modern horn. It was a loud horn! It made noise every day. The noise was so loud, everyone could hear it.
