Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Bob who loved to wander. One hot summer morning, Bob hopped along a path that led to a pine forest. Bob sniffed the air and was so excited!

When Bob reached the forest, the big pine trees were refreshingly cool and shady. He hopped around the trunks, running and exploring happily. Suddenly, Bob stopped and looked around. He was lost!

Bob started to worry. He wondered how he would ever find his way out of the forest. Just then, a friendly starling flew down and landed on a branch next to Bob.

"Excuse me," Bob said. "Can you help me get out of this pine forest?"

The starling smiled, "I sure can! Just follow this path and it will take you home."

Lila and Ben were bored. They had no toys to play with. All their toys were in a big box. But the box had a lock. And they did not have the key.

"Where is the key?" Lila asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe Mom has it."

"Maybe we can use something to unlock it," Ben said.

"Maybe this will work," Ben said. He took the knife. He went to the box. He tried to put the knife in the lock. But it did not fit.

"Be careful, Ben," Lila said. "You might hurt yourself."

Ben did not listen. He pushed harder. He twisted the knife. He heard a click. He smiled.

"I did it!" he said. "I unlocked the box!"

He opened the box. He saw all their toys. He was happy. He took out his favorite car. He gave Lila her favorite doll.

"Look, Lila," he said. "We can play now!"

Lila was happy too. She hugged her doll. She thanked Ben.

"You're smart, Ben," she said. "You unlocked the box!"

They played with their toys. They had fun. They forgot about Mom and the dough. They did not hear Mom calling them.

"Kids, come here!" Mom said. "The cake is ready!"

But Lila and Ben did not hear. They were too busy playing. They were not bored anymore. They were happy.

But then, something bad happens. Her brother Tom comes into her room. He sees the eraser on the bed. He likes erasers. He thinks they are fun to play with. He does not ask Sara. He takes the eraser and runs away.

"Hey, that's mine!" Sara shouts. "Give it back!"

Sara runs after Tom. She is very upset. She does not want to lose her new friend. She does not want to stop singing.

"Tom, stop!" Sara cries. "That's not yours! That's my eraser!"

But Tom does not stop. He does not listen. He laughs and runs faster.

Sara feels sad and angry. She does not know what to do. She wants her mom and dad to help her. She wants her eraser back. She wants to sing again.

Once upon a time there were two best friends: Jenny and Lily.

One summer day Jenny asked Lily, "How can we make this summer special?"

Lily thought for a moment then said, "Let's add a holiday!"

Jenny smiled and said, "That's a great idea."

So Jenny and Lily made a list of all the activities they wanted to do on their holiday. Once they finished their list, they took a big paper and painted a thick black line across it.

The next day they crossed the thick black line and started their holiday! They went swimming, ate ice-cream and played outdoors. It was a lot of fun.

At the end of the holiday, Lily said to Jenny, "We had so much fun on this special holiday. That's because we added something new and exciting to our summer."

The moral of the story is: Adding something fun and different can make a special occasion even more enjoyable.

Once upon a time, there was a cat. The cat was curious and liked to explore.

One day, the cat noticed a special pattern on the ground. It was made up of stones and the cat really liked it. The cat wanted to add something to the pattern, so he decided to bring some flowers. He placed them carefully and added them to the pattern.

The cat thought the pattern looked even better now, but then something unexpected happened. One of the rocks in the pattern was broken and the flowers were scattered around.

The cat was sad and wanted to make things better. He gathered all of the rocks, carefully placed them back in the pattern, and then added more flowers.

The cat smiled with satisfaction because the pattern now looked beautiful. He knew he had fixed it.

Once upon a time, there was a tall snowman in a secret garden. One day, the snowman talked to a little girl.

The snowman said, "I can reveal a secret to you. Can you keep it safe?"

The little girl was so excited and nodded. Then the snowman whispered something in her ear.

The girl smiled and said, "Wow! That is so neat! I will keep it safe!"

The snowman nodded and said, "I am glad you like my secret. You can now see the secret garden."

The little girl opened the gate and stepped into the garden. Everywhere she looked, there was snow! The snow sparkled in the sunlight and the girl laughed with glee.

The tall snowman stood in the middle of the garden, smiling at the little girl. She thanked the snowman with a hug, before skipping homewards.

The little girl never told anyone the snowman's secret, and still treasures it to this day.

The bear said to the police, â€œLet me go! I donâ€™t want to get into any trouble!â€ The police said, â€œWe just want to help. We will take care of you.â€

The police took the bear to the doctorâ€™s office. The doctor gave the bear a checkup and made sure he was safe.

Then, the police drove the bear back to his home in the woods. Before they said goodbye, the police said, â€œStay out of trouble and be happy!â€

The bear was so happy that he started singing and dancing. He thanked the police for their help and ran off into the woods. From that day on, he always stayed out of trouble and was never scared of the police again.

Once upon a time there was an independent pumpkin. It was very special. Every day it suggested going on an adventure. One day the pumpkin decided to take its own advice. It rolled away from its patch and started exploring.

The pumpkin met a rabbit, two birds, and a frog. They all suggested things to do. The pumpkin enjoyed learning about the world and finding new experiences. The rabbit suggested they hunt for mushrooms, the two birds suggested picking berries in the forest, and the frog suggested catching tadpoles in a nearby stream.

The pumpkin was so excited. It tried all their suggestions and had an amazing day. At the end of the day, the pumpkin said goodbye to its new friends, thanked them for all the suggestions, and went on its way back to the pumpkin patch.

The independent pumpkin had learned many new things and felt full of excitement. It had a wonderful day thanks to its friends' help.

One day, a little girl named Abigail went to the park. The park was very fun, with lots of tall trees and a long slide. Abigail was so excited that she forgot to stand still. Suddenly, the ground started to shake. Abigail was scared and didn't know what was happening. The ground was noisy and shaking. Abigail realized she was in an earthquake.

She quickly ran to a nearby tree and she started to stand still. Everyone around Abigail was standing still, too. Abigail was so scared that she started to cry. But then, she remembered what her parents had told her about earthquakes. Stay still and wait until the shaking stops.

Finally, the shaking stopped. Abigail was relieved. She ran to her mom and gave her a big hug. Together, they walked back home. Abigail had learned an important lesson. Next time, she would stand still when the ground starts shaking.

It was a beautiful morning, and Bill and Suzy were excited to go to the park. They had planned a picnic together.

They grabbed their lunch basket and started walking to the park.

But on their way, they noticed something strange. It was a bird, perched high up in a tree. It looked scared, shivering and chirping.

Suzy, being the kind-hearted girl she was, wanted to help the bird. She said, "Let's try to help the bird, Bill!"

"How can we help it, Suzy?" asked Bill.

"Let's attach a piece of string to the top of the tree, then stay and wait," she suggested.

Bill was a bit fearful, but followed Suzy's lead. They found a long string and carefully attached it to the top of the tree. Then, they waited at the bottom of the tree.

It was a bit scary to wait there, because a sudden gust of wind could have blown away the bird. But, as luck would have it, the bird stayed put. After a while, the bird flew away into the sky.

"Phew, we did it!" They said.

And they continued on their walk to the park, happy and relieved that they could help the bird.

Sam and Mia liked to play with their toys in the living room. They had many toys, like cars, dolls, blocks and books. But they did not like to put their toys away when they were done. They left them on the floor, on the couch, on the table and everywhere.

One day, their mom came home from work and saw the mess. She was not happy. She said to Sam and Mia, "You need to return your toys to their places. The living room is not organized. It is hard to walk and find things. And it is not safe. You can trip and fall and hurt yourself or break something. Please, help me clean up."

Sam and Mia did not want to clean up. They wanted to keep playing. They said to their mom, "But mom, we are having fun. We will clean up later. Can we play for a little longer?"

Their mom said, "No, you cannot play for a little longer. You have played enough. It is time to return your toys to their places. You can play again tomorrow, but only if you keep the living room organized. Now, come on, let's do it together. It will be faster and easier."

Sam and Mia sighed. They knew their mom was right. They did not want to trip and fall and hurt themselves or break something. They did not want to make their mom unhappy. They decided to help their mom clean up. They returned their toys to their places. They put the cars in the box, the dolls in the basket, the blocks in the bag and the books on the shelf. They made the living room organized.

Their mom smiled. She said to Sam and Mia, "Thank you, Sam and Mia. You did a good job. The living room looks much better. I am proud of you. Now, how about we have some cookies and milk as a reward?"

Sam and Mia smiled too. They said to their mom, "Yes, please. We love cookies and milk. And we love you, mom."

They hugged their mom and went to the kitchen. They enjoyed their cookies and milk. They were happy. They learned to return their toys to their places and keep the living room organized.

Once upon a time there was a modest thing. It was small, but it was always getting bigger.

The thing started by being small and very quiet. But it always wanted more. So one day it decided to start getting bigger.

First it started to get higher. Then it started to get wider. Soon, it was as tall and wide as a big tree.

Next, it started to get stronger. It started to shine brightly and look more important. Finally, it started to make noise. Suddenly it was loud and happy.

The thing had started as small and modest. But now it was huge and strong.

Once there was a curious bear. He was walking through the woods one day when he saw something up in a tree. He wondered what it was and he was eager to find out.

Suddenly he saw that it was a cherry! He was so excited and he wanted to get it. He got his bow and arrow from his pocket and he took aim.

He shot the arrow and it hit the cherry. The cherry fell off the tree and down to the ground. The bear clapped his paws in happiness.

He quickly picked up the cherry and took a big bite. It was so sweet and delicious. The bear thought that it was the best he had ever tasted!

Riley and Madeline were best friends. Every day they would play together in the park near their house. Riley always wanted to play on the swings, and Madeline always wanted to play on the slide. They often argued over which one was more fun.

One day, they got into a huge quarrel about what to play with. Neither one wanted to compromise. So they decided to play a game to decide - the game of hide and seek. Madeline chose to hide in the cupboard, and Riley searched for her.

While searching for Madeline, Riley discovered something very important - a key. Riley immediately grabbed the key and ran away from the cupboard. The key felt really special and he tried using it on various locks around the house. But nothing opened.

Madeline soon emerged from the cupboard and saw that Riley had the key. She asked him where he got it from, and Riley replied that he had found it while looking for her. Madeline smiled - it seemed very important. They soon forgot about their quarrel, and started a new adventure together to find out what the important key unlocked.

Once upon a time, there was a calm summer day in the spring. A family of four â€" Mom, Dad, Grandma, and a three-year-old â€" decided to part ways and go off on their own special adventure.

The three-year-old followed Mom and Dad into the fields, hopping and skipping along the dirt path. Everywhere they explored, the fields were so green and fresh with new life. The three-year-old was so excited about their adventure.

Next, the family came upon the edge of a lake. They were in awe of its beauty, the calm, peaceful water, and the warm breeze that passed by. Dad pointed out to the three-year-old how the lake was full of fish, and he also highlighted a group of ducks in the distance. The three-year-old was so amazed at how perfect this moment was during the spring.

As the three-year-old played on the shore, Dad went for a swim in the lake. To the three-year-old's surprise, he jumped right back out and started to run up the shore. It turns out that Dad disturbed a swarm of bees! The three-year-old started to laugh and chase after them.

One night, Sally and Henry had a fight. They were both 3 years old and were very mad at each other.

Sally was so mad that she decided to go for a walk in the dark. She grabbed her flashlight and marched away from the house. As she walked, she thought about how mean Henry had been.

Suddenly, Sally heard a noise coming from the bushes. It sounded friendly, but Sally was still scared. She shone her flashlight in the direction of the noise and saw a big, friendly dog.

The dog did not bark or bark or run away. Instead, it remained in the bushes and wagged its tail. It seemed to understand that Sally was mad.

Sally smiled and took a step closer to the dog. She reached out and pet it, thankful for its friendly presence. Then, Sally and the dog walked back to the house together.

Once upon a time, there was a purple couch. It was big and comfy. While sitting on it, a girl and her brother liked to make silly faces together. One day, they were on the purple couch, playing a silly game. But then something happened! All of a sudden, there was a big noise and the couch split right in the middle! The girl and her brother were so surprised! They screamed and laughed at the same time. Then, the girl said she was gonna fix the couch. She got some glue and a special tool. After a few tries, the couch was all patched up and good as new. It was just like nothing ever happened. The girl and her brother were so happy! From then on, they always made sure to be a bit more gentle with the purple couch. The End.

There were two best friends. One day, one of them suggested going on a ship. The other one was jealous and said no. The friend suggested again, but the jealous one still said no. The friend was sad and said goodbye.

The jealous one felt bad and thought of a plan to get back at the other one. He quickly decided to make a ship by himself. The jealous one was so excited and started building right away.

He worked very hard and eventually finished the ship. But before he could show it to the other one, a big storm hit and destroyed the ship. The jealous one was very sad and could not believe it.

When the friend found out he felt sorry for the other one. Even though the jealous one had been mean, the friend wanted to help him. But it was too late. The jealous one had caused a bad ending by being too jealous.

Once upon a time, there were two twins called Tim and Tom. They loved to play together in the park. One day, they were running around and playing tag. Suddenly, Tim pointed to a big red trampoline and shouted, "Let's jump!".

Tom and Tim both ran over to the trampoline. They jumped and jumped and jumped. Tom jumped high and long. Tim jumped lower and shorter. The twins laughed and shouted happily as they jumped around.

They jumped in the air and around on the trampoline. Soon, they were jumping and jumping so much, they were both out of breath. Tom and Tim said goodbye and each went home. They were both so happy and they were looking forward to their next visit to the big red trampoline.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the ice cream truck and received a cone with her favorite flavor, chocolate. She was so happy and ate it quickly.

Suddenly, the sky turned gloomy and it started to rain. Lily didn't like the rain because it made her wet and she couldn't play outside. She said to her mom, "Mommy, I don't like the rain. It's gloomy outside."

Her mom replied, "Don't worry, Lily. We can play inside and have fun. Maybe we can make some cookies together." Lily smiled and said, "Yay! I love cookies. Thank you, Mommy." And they spent the rest of the day baking and playing together.

The new pilot felt excited. She was finally going to fly her first plane! She put on her pilot hat and buckle her seatbelt.

"Ready for take-off?" asked Grandpa. He was coming along with her today.

"Yes!" She smiled.

The plane began to move. Faster and faster it went until it left the ground. The pilot felt happy.

"Woah, look at that!" said Grandpa, pointing down. The pilot looked and saw big farms, houses and a river.

"Look! We can wave to the people," Grandpa said. The pilot waved to the people below and smiled.

The plane flew for a while until it was time to land. Grandpa and the pilot felt proud.

"That was awesome!" said Grandpa.

"Yes," said the happy pilot, "flying a plane is the best!"

Once upon a time there were two friends, Emma and Jack. One day, they wanted to discuss furniture.

"Let's talk about furniture," said Emma.

"Yes," said Jack.

They looked around the room and saw a small table.

"What is that?" asked Emma pointing to the table.

"That is a small table," answered Jack.

They looked at the small table and discussed what they could do with it.

"We could use it as a game table," said Emma.

"Yes!" said Jack.

They discussed other ideas until they had the perfect plan. They agreed to use the small table as a game table. They laughed and cheered and had lots of fun.

The end!

One day, three year old Daisy was playing in her backyard. Suddenly, she noticed a bright blue bird perched at the top of the stairs. It chirped loudly and she smiled.

Suddenly, the bird flew into the air and twirled around. With one graceful movement, the bird dove into the bushes.

Daisy hopped up and ran to the top of the stairs. She peered into the bush but the bird was gone! She was a bit sad but then she heard a noise coming from the other side of the bushes.

She crept over to the other side and saw the blue bird resting in a bright pink flower. She couldn't believe how colourful it was! Clapping her hands loudly, Daisy asked the bird, "Hello, where did you go?".

The bird chirped and flew away. Daisy watched it dive into the sky and smiled. She ran back to the stairs and waved goodbye to her new friend.

Once there was a little boy. He loved to peek around. Every day he would explore and look in new places. One day the little boy wanted to find something special. He went to the garden to peek around. He saw something red and round. It was an apple! He reached out and picked it up. The apple felt tough. He knew he needed to work to get it. The little boy put the apple in his pocket and started to run. He ran all the way to his house and showed the apple to his family. Everyone was excited! The little boy smiled and felt so proud of his apple. He had done it himself. He had found a tough apple. It made him feel brave.

Once there was a charming little girl named Tessa. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad.

One day, Tessa and her parents went for a walk in the park. Tessa loved the crunchy leaves and beautiful trees. She began to run around, turning in circles and giggling with delight.

Suddenly, Tessa heard a voice. She stopped and looked around. That voice sounded so familiar!

She realised that the voice was from her dad. He was standing by a tree and singing. It was a sweet, charming song. Tessa was so happy that she started singing along with her dad. Soon, him, her mom, and Tessa were all singing together.

It was a special moment that Tessa would never forget.

Once upon a time there was a soldier who was in a big hurry. He had to do something very important, but he did not know what it was. He ran and ran until he came to a big, tall hill. At the top of the hill he saw a crazy lion. The soldier was scared so he ran away! He had to hurry to get away from the lion, so he ran faster than he had ever run before. Finally, he made it to safety and that made him feel very happy. The End.

James was walking down the street with mommy. It was a sunny day, the sun was shining and the birds were singing.

"Mommy, why is there a sign up ahead?" asked James.

"That's a stop sign," said mommy.

Suddenly, it started to rain. Mommy frowned and grabbed James's hand. She raced to a nearby store.

When they got inside, James was embarrassed. Everyone was staring at him and mommy.

"It's ok James," said mommy, giving James a hug. "The rain will stop soon, and the sun will be back out."

Sure enough, the rain stopped and soon rays of sunlight were streaming through the window.

James smiled up at mommy. "I'm glad the sun is back out," he said.

Mommy smiled and agreed, happy they didn't have to be embarrassed any longer.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the forest. She saw a wolf. The wolf was not a real wolf. It was a fake wolf. The fake wolf was sad because it could not scare anyone.

Lily said, "Why are you sad, fake wolf?" The fake wolf said, "I am sad because I cannot scare anyone. No one is scared of a fake wolf."

Lily had an idea. She said, "I will lend you my scary mask. Then you can scare people." The fake wolf was happy.

Lily lent the fake wolf her scary mask. The fake wolf put on the mask and scared people. The fake wolf was not sad anymore. Lily and the fake wolf became good friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Stella. Stella was a very curious three year old who loved to explore.

One day, Stella's mom decided to take her to a very special place called a palace. When they arrived, Stella's eyes sparkled in amazement. The palace garden was filled with beautiful flowers and the walls were made of shiny white stones.

Stella asked her mom, "What is this place?" Her mom replied, "This is a very popular castle. Everyone wants to visit this wonderful place!"

Stella ran through the hallways and up the grand stairways. Everywhere she looked, there was something new and exciting. She saw portraits, tapestries and many other grand decorations.

At the end of the day, Stella's mom asked her if she enjoyed the palace. She said, "Yes, it was wonderful! I would highly recommend it to all my friends!"

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Jim. Jim wanted to buy a new toy sail so he went to the shop to find one. He looked through all the sails but they were all too expensive.

Then he found one that was very cheap. It had a bright red colour and a big sail, so Jim bought it.

When Jim got home, he was so excited to play with his new sail. He opened the box and rolled the sail around his room hoping it would take him to far away lands.

But then the sail started to shake and the wind blew it really hard. Jim tried to hold on to it, but the sail was too strong, so it rolled out of the window and flew away.

Jim stood in his bedroom and looked sadly at the window. He had wanted to explore the world, but his cheap sail had broken. Jim had a bad ending.

The little girl showed her dolly to her mom. She was smiling and showing off the new dress she had put on the dolly.

Mommy looked at the dolly and smiled. "It looks very nice, sweetheart," she said.

The little girl nodded excitedly. She wanted to show mommy something else.

"Mommy! Look," she said and ran to the kitchen. She took a carton of milk from the fridge. "This is reliable milk," she said.

Mommy laughed. "Yes, it is reliable. You did a good job picking it out," she said.

The little girl smiled and ran off to play with her dolly again. Mommy had shown her how to choose reliable milk for her dolly to drink, and she was proud of her accomplishment.

One day, a little girl named Mia went for a walk. She saw a delicate butterfly sitting on a flower. Mia said, "Hello, butterfly! I am Mia. What is your name?" The butterfly did not say anything, but it danced in the air.

Mia wanted to introduce the butterfly to her friends. She took the butterfly to her friends, Tom and Lily. Mia said, "Tom, Lily, meet my new friend, the butterfly!" Tom and Lily said, "Hello, butterfly!"

Together, they decided to have a march around the garden. Mia, Tom, Lily, and the butterfly marched and danced in the sun. They had a fun day playing together.

One day, a fish was swimming in the deep sea. He liked to look at the bright colors of the coral and the plants. He was happy and curious.

He saw a big shadow above him. He swam up to meet it. He thought it was a friend. But it was a shark! The shark had sharp teeth and a hungry look. The fish was scared and tried to swim away.

But the shark was faster and chased him. The fish saw a small hole in a rock. He swam inside and hid. The shark could not fit in the hole. He was angry and went away.

The fish was safe, but he learned a lesson. He learned that not everyone he meets is a friend. He learned that he should be careful and not go too close to strangers. He learned that the deep sea can be dangerous. He was glad that he had a safe home in the rock. He thanked the rock for saving him.

Once upon a time, there was a good friend called Bob. He had a thick, fluffy coat of fur, so it was always nice to cuddle him.

One day Bob decided to go for a walk in the woods. But it was getting dark, so he started to worry.

Suddenly, Bob heard a voice. It was a small voice, crying out for help. The voice was coming from behind a big tree.

Bob leaned in, and saw a tiny bear cub. He was scared and alone, so Bob decided to help him. He invited the little bear to come with him and they started walking towards home.

But when the little bear saw Bob's home, he started to weep. He said it reminded him of his own home - and that he was very, very far away from his family.

Bob was sad to hear this, and he decided that he would help the little bear find his way back home. He was sure his thick coat of fur, would keep the little bear safe and warm on their journey.

And so, Bob and the little bear went on a very long adventure - but with Bob's help, he soon found his way home. In the end, the little bear was reunited with his family and they all hugged and laughed together. Bob and the little bear were happy to be friends forever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was feeling sad because she hadn't seen her friends in a long time. So, one day, Daisy's mum arranged a surprise for her! When Daisy opened the door, she discovered her friends all holding a very big, light pie. Daisy was delighted!

They all ate the pie together and had lots of fun. As they ate, Daisy laughed and laughed. She was so happy that her friends had come to surprise her with the pie. When Daisy had finished eating all the pie, her friends said goodbye. Daisy felt so happy and excited that she had seen them at last.

The surprise of the light pie had put a big smile on Daisy's face. From that moment on, every time Daisy saw a light pie, she would remember the wonderful surprise her friends had given her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and watch cartoons. One day, she found a roll of tape and got very excited. She loved to stick things together with it.

Lily decided to peek outside her window to see what she could tape. She saw a beautiful butterfly and wanted to catch it. She ran outside with the tape and tried to catch the butterfly, but she accidentally got stuck to the tape instead.

Lily was very scared and tried to get the tape off, but it was too strong. She cried for help, but no one heard her. Eventually, she fell asleep and never woke up. The tape had suffocated her. From that day on, her parents always reminded her to be careful with tape and to never play with it alone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to store her toys in a special space in her room. One day, she became anxious because she could not find her favorite toy, a small blue car.

Amy looked everywhere in her room, but the blue car was not there. She felt sad and asked her mom for help. "Mom, I can't find my blue car. Can you help me?" Her mom said, "Of course, Amy. Let's look together."

They searched the whole house, and finally, they found the blue car under the couch. Amy was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mom!" From that day on, Amy always made sure to store her toys in the special space in her room, so she would never feel anxious about losing them again.

Once upon a time, there was a big machine. It was the most important thing in the world and it kept everyone safe. One day, the people who used the machine lost it. They looked and looked but they couldn't find it.

They were very unhappy and didn't know what to do so they asked their friends for help. One friend had an idea to make a new machine to keep everyone safe. Everyone was excited and started building the machine together.

Finally, after a lot of hard work, the new machine was finished. Everyone cheered and the people were so happy to have a safe machine that would keep them safe again. Everyone congratulated each other for their hard work and celebrated with a big party.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She was three years old and loved playing with her toys.

One day, Sue was looking for something new to do. Suddenly, she saw an interesting box. She opened it up, and inside she found lots of brightly colored thread.

Sue was so excited. She chose one of the softest and brightest threads, and began to grow it. She wrapped the thread around a special toy bear, and the thread fit perfectly.

"Oh, how beautiful!" said Sue.

She continued wrapping the thread until the bear was completely covered. Sue was very proud of her work.

The next day, Sue showed her bear to all her friends. They were all so impressed. Sue had grown something truly special.

From then on Sue decided, she would always take the time to grow something new with thread.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures with her crayons. One day, she drew a square with different colors. She showed it to her friend, Timmy.

Timmy said, "That's not a good picture. It's not pretty."

Lily felt sad and cried. Her mom came and asked what happened. Lily told her what Timmy said.

Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. Timmy didn't mean to hurt your feelings. Let's forgive him. Your picture is sweet and special to me."

Lily felt better and smiled. She forgave Timmy and they played together again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was an enthusiastic dancer who loved to perform. Whenever he danced, he felt happy and full of joy. Everywhere he went, the people around him stopped and watched in awe.

One day, the dancer went to a new place and saw someone who looked familiar. He couldn't place where he recognized the person from, so he went over to ask who she was. It turned out that she was also an enthusiastic dancer, who had grown up in the same town as the dancer.

The two of them spent the day tucked away in a corner of the town, talking about their shared love for dancing. They shared ideas and laughed, until finally the night had come to an end.

The dancer couldn't believe that he had gone all that time without recognizing the talented dancer he had just met. He was so glad he had gone over to ask her who she was, because now he had a new friend. They stayed in touch and continued to share their love of dancing together.

Molly and her dad were walking along the beach and looking at the ocean. It sparkled like a thousand diamonds in the sun.

"Isn't it beautiful, Molly?" said Dad.

"Yes, Daddy," said Molly, who was really excited to be there.

"Let's go for a swim," he said.

Molly jumped with joy and ran to the delicate water. She put her toes in first and then waded in further. As she went deeper, the water was cool and refreshing.

She started splashing around, kicking her feet and making the biggest waves that she could. She was having so much fun!

Dad watched her, smiling. "Be careful, Molly," he said, "the ocean can be dangerous."

Molly laughed and kept on splashing. "I'm careful," she said.

Molly was a cheerful three year old who loved to play. She especially loved to play dress up. She would wear Mommy's high heels, Daddy's hat, and Grandpa's glasses. One day, Molly was playing dress up with her yellow raincoat. She decided to wear it outside and find something fun to do.

First, she walked to the playground. But the park was too quiet and she wanted to find something more exciting. So she continued walking and eventually, she came across a peanut street vendor. The peanuts looked so delicious and smelled so good! Molly was so excited and cheerful, she asked the vendor for some peanuts.

The vendor gave her a big bag of peanuts and Molly couldn't wait to eat them. She started eating them, one at a time and enjoyed every single peanut. She was so happy and cheerful, she finished the whole bag in no time.

Molly was so full, she didn't want to play dress up anymore. She thanked the peanut vendor and went back home. From then on, Molly tried to go outside and find new exciting things to do and eat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Amy and she was three years old. She loved to go to the playground.

Amy's favorite thing to do at the playground was to go down the slide. She would climb up the steps and sit down on the slide. Then with a big smile, she would push off and go down the slide. She would giggle all the way down.

But, one day, the slide was too slippery. With one careless push, she rose up into the air, higher than she normally did. She was so surprised that she couldn't help but to giggle with delight. But then she landed with a thud in the sand!

Amy was okay though, and she was excited to go down the slide again and again.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit who liked to go on adventures. She liked to explore the world around her.

One day, the rabbit found a valley filled with different kinds of flowers. She was so excited that she started hopping around in glee.

The rabbit asked her friends, "Do you want to explore the valley with me?"

But her friends didn't want to go, so the rabbit decided to venture off alone.

As she hopped and explored the valley, she noticed something different. It seemed like something was calling her to come closer.

Suddenly, she saw a tall figure at the end of the valley. She approached the figure and it was then that realized it was a giant.

The giant smiled warmly at the rabbit and said, "I've been waiting for you, little one. Let's rest in the valley together."

The rabbit smiled and knew that the valley was her special place. She and the giant stayed there often, talking and resting together under the stars. The rabbit's adventures were always different-- filled with joy and laughter.

The little girl was very excited. She had been walking around the field with her parents. It was a beautiful day and the sun was shining. The little girl's father asked her if she wanted to take a walk and she said yes.

The little girl skipped around the field and played. She saw all kinds of animals and plants. She was so excited that she wanted to pick some of the flowers. Her father let her pick one flower, but not too many.

Soon the little girl's father said it was time to go home. The little girl felt a little sad, but she was happy that she had been permitted to go for a walk in the field. She promised to come back the next day.

Once there was a fierce tooth. It was sitting in a park, near the swings. Suddenly, it spotted a small girl walking by and waved to her. She smiled and waved back.

The tooth was very happy and waved to the girl again. She smiled and waved back. This happened over and over again, every time the tooth waved, the girl waved back.

Finally, after a few weeks, the tooth and the girl met in the park. The tooth waved and the girl happily waved back. She laughed and asked the tooth what it was doing there by itself.

The tooth smiled and said â€œI've been waiting all this time just to be friends with you!â€ The girl was so happy that she gave the fierce tooth a big hug. From that day forward, the tooth and the girl were best friends. They both waved at each other every day as a sign of their friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a duck who liked to rub himself. He would make circles on his feathers, back and forth. He did it so fast, it looked very impressive.

One day, he got very caught up in his rubbing. He was so busy he didn't even notice the green pond in front of him. He kept rubbing until he noticed a reflection in the water.

It was a small duckling, looking up at him. He was so cute! The duck stopped rubbing and smiled down at the little duck. That made the duckling so happy it started to rub its feathers too!

The bigger duck watched in surprise. He was so impressed! The smaller duck was already so good at rubbing his feathers.

The bigger duck was proud and smiled happily at his duckling friend. Together they rubbed and played in the water. It was the happiest day ever!

Once there was an old lady who wanted to go for a walk in the park. She carefully put on her shoes and stepped out into the warm sunshine. Everywhere she stepped, birds sang and flowers bloomed.

But soon, it began to rain! She quickly stepped back under a tall tree and waited for the rain to stop. When it finally did, the lady smiled and stepped off down the path.

But she could not find a safe place to stay. Everywhere she stepped, the ground seemed to crumble under her feet. She tried to look for an old house or barn, but nothing was in sight.

Finally, at the edge of the park, she spotted an old, crumbling stone wall. She stepped closer and, sure enough, there was an old, safe house hidden behind the wall. She quickly stepped through the door and settled in the snug and warm home.

The old lady was safe from the rain and the inevitable thunder that would soon follow. She smiled and thanked the old, safe wall.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old and loved to play with all sorts of things.

One day, she found a funny machine which made prints on a piece of paper. She had never seen anything like it before and began to play with it.

"What can this do?" said Lucy.

Mummy said, "That's called a printer. It can make things out of words."

"What do you mean?" asked Lucy.

"It can print words so that you can read them. It can also print pictures," said Mummy.

"Wow!" said Lucy.

Mummy explained that there were lots of different languages which the printer could print in. She said that some of them were very difficult to learn.

Lucy was so excited to start learning about the different languages the printer could print in. She couldn't wait to start trying out the printer and explore all the different words.

Once upon a time there was a dependable man named Mr. Smith. He had a very important job. Everyday, Mr. Smith would get up early and go to work. His job was to mail cereal every day.

One day, Mr. Smith was getting ready for work and he noticed that his cereal was running low. "Oh no! I need to get more cereal for work today!" he exclaimed.

Mr. Smith put on his shoes and coat and grabbed his mail bag. He walked to the grocery store and asked the cashier for a box of cereal. The cashier said, "Of course! Here you go Mr. Smith."

Mr. Smith happily thanked the cashier and walked back to work. He was glad he could be dependable to his job. He filled up his mail bag with the cereal and set off mailing it to all its special destinations.

The end.

Jane and her mom were having a picnic in the park. Jane's mom spread the red and white checked cloth napkin on the grass. Jane looked at her mom and said, "What should I do now?"

Her mom smiled and pointed to the sky. "Let's gaze up at the deep blue sky and look at the fluffy white clouds," she said. Jane looked up and saw many shapes in the clouds.

Then, she looked for a bird in a tree and noticed a big yellow feather floating on the ground. She picked it up and put it under the napkin to save it for later.

Jane looked back up and said, "Can we gaze at the clouds again?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, let's take a napkin break and gaze at the clouds."

They both laid back and watched the fluffy clouds float by above them. Jane smiled and said, "This gazing is so much fun!" Her mom agreed and said, "Yes, it is!"

Once there was a boy named Jim. He was only 3 years old and he loved to eat yogurt. He always asked his mom to give him some yogurt to eat. Today, however, his mom did not give him any. "Why won't you give me any yogurt?" he asked his mom.

His mom said, "I'm sorry, Jim. I don't have any yogurt right now. It's all gone." Jim was so sad. He did not understand why there was no yogurt anymore.

Suddenly, he smelled something terrible. He ran to the kitchen to look and he saw that the yogurt was all spilled on the floor. It had gone bad and was now stinky. Jim was very sad and angry.

"Who spilled the yogurt?" he yelled. His mom shook her head and said, "I'm sorry, Jim. I guess it was just a terrible accident."

Jim was still very sad, but at least he knew what happened. His mom gave him a big hug and said, "Don't worry, Jim. You can come with me to the store and we can buy some more yogurt." That made Jim happy again and he smiled.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Billy. He was very excited because he had a new pair of shoes. The shoes were blue and had lots of sparkles.

Billy couldn't wait to try them out. He ran around the house with them on and showed them to everyone. His dad smiled and said, "Wow, those are very nice shoes!"

That night, while everyone else was sleeping, Billy stayed up to study with his new shoes on. He read lots of books and did lots of sums. He was excited to learn something new.

The next day, he told his family all about what he had studied. His mom was so proud of him.

"You studied so hard! Well done for trying so hard," she said.

Billy looked down at his new shoes, feeling proud and excited. He had learned something new and he had done it in his special shoes!

One day it was raining. The rain was cold and wet. A little girl named Grace was looking out of a window. She saw an old man outside. He was grumpy. He had an umbrella, but the rain was coming down so hard that it did not help much.

Grace felt sorry for the old man, so she got a glass from the kitchen. She opened the window and offered it to the old man. He smiled. He thanked her and put the glass over his head. The glass kept him dry and he thanked Grace again.

Grace smiled and waved goodbye. She was happy that she could help the grumpy old man.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his red toy train. He would put the train on the rail and watch it go round and round.

One sunny day, Tim took his red train outside to play. He put the train on the rail in his backyard. His friend, Sam, came over and saw the train. Sam said, "Wow, your red train is so cool! Can I play with it too?"

Tim smiled and said, "Yes, you can play with my red train." So, Tim and Sam put the train on the rail and watched it go round and round. They laughed and had so much fun playing with the red train together.

As the sun began to set, Tim's mom called out, "Tim, it's time to come in!" Tim and Sam picked up the red train and the rail. They said goodbye and went inside.

That night, Tim put his red train on the rail by his bed. He smiled as he thought about the fun day he had with his friend, Sam. Tim knew that he would have many more happy days playing with his red train.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Lucy. She was out walking one day and she had an urge to go searching for something. She walked for miles and miles until she came across a deep and dark cave. She wanted to explore it so she stepped inside.

The cave was something terrible. It was full of strange noises and Lucy couldn't see anything. Suddenly, a voice called out from the darkness: "Who are you?"

Lucy was scared but she bravely shouted out: "I'm Lucy. Who are you?"

The voice replied: "I am the King of the Cave, and you have come to search my kingdom. What do you seek?"

Lucy thought for a moment and said: "I'm looking for adventure!"

The King was pleased and he said: "Then come with me and I shall show you the way!"

So with the King leading the way, Lucy began her exciting search.

THE GOLDEN GOOSE

There was a man who had three sons, the youngest of whom was called

Dummling,[*] and was despised, mocked, and sneered at on every occasion.

[*] Simpleton

It happened that the eldest wanted to go into the forest to hew wood,

and before he went his mother gave him a beautiful sweet cake and a

bottle of wine in order that he might not suffer from hunger or thirst.

When he entered the forest he met a little grey-haired old man who bade

him good day, and said: 'Do give me a piece of cake out of your pocket,

and let me have a draught of your wine; I am so hungry and thirsty.' But

the clever son answered: 'If I give you my cake and wine, I shall have

none for myself; be off with you,' and he left the little man standing

and went on.

But when he began to hew down a tree, it was not long before he made a

false stroke, and the axe cut him in the arm, so that he had to go home

and have it bound up. And this was the little grey man's doing.

After this the second son went into the forest, and his mother gave him,

like the eldest, a cake and a bottle of wine. The little old grey man

met him likewise, and asked him for a piece of cake and a drink of wine.

But the second son, too, said sensibly enough: 'What I give you will be

taken away from myself; be off!' and he left the little man standing and

went on. His punishment, however, was not delayed; when he had made a

few blows at the tree he struck himself in the leg, so that he had to be

carried home.

Then Dummling said: 'Father, do let me go and cut wood.' The father

answered: 'Your brothers have hurt themselves with it, leave it alone,

you do not understand anything about it.' But Dummling begged so long

that at last he said: 'Just go then, you will get wiser by hurting

yourself.' His mother gave him a cake made with water and baked in the

cinders, and with it a bottle of sour beer.

When he came to the forest the little old grey man met him likewise,

and greeting him, said: 'Give me a piece of your cake and a drink out

of your bottle; I am so hungry and thirsty.' Dummling answered: 'I have

only cinder-cake and sour beer; if that pleases you, we will sit

down and eat.' So they sat down, and when Dummling pulled out his

cinder-cake, it was a fine sweet cake, and the sour beer had become good

wine. So they ate and drank, and after that the little man said: 'Since

you have a good heart, and are willing to divide what you have, I will

give you good luck. There stands an old tree, cut it down, and you will

find something at the roots.' Then the little man took leave of him.

Dummling went and cut down the tree, and when it fell there was a goose

sitting in the roots with feathers of pure gold. He lifted her up, and

taking her with him, went to an inn where he thought he would stay the

night. Now the host had three daughters, who saw the goose and were

curious to know what such a wonderful bird might be, and would have

liked to have one of its golden feathers.

The eldest thought: 'I shall soon find an opportunity of pulling out a

feather,' and as soon as Dummling had gone out she seized the goose by

the wing, but her finger and hand remained sticking fast to it.

The second came soon afterwards, thinking only of how she might get a

feather for herself, but she had scarcely touched her sister than she

was held fast.

At last the third also came with the like intent, and the others

screamed out: 'Keep away; for goodness' sake keep away!' But she did

not understand why she was to keep away. 'The others are there,' she

thought, 'I may as well be there too,' and ran to them; but as soon as

she had touched her sister, she remained sticking fast to her. So they

had to spend the night with the goose.

The next morning Dummling took the goose under his arm and set out,

without troubling himself about the three girls who were hanging on to

it. They were obliged to run after him continually, now left, now right,

wherever his legs took him.

In the middle of the fields the parson met them, and when he saw the

procession he said: 'For shame, you good-for-nothing girls, why are you

running across the fields after this young man? Is that seemly?' At the

same time he seized the youngest by the hand in order to pull her away,

but as soon as he touched her he likewise stuck fast, and was himself

obliged to run behind.

Before long the sexton came by and saw his master, the parson, running

behind three girls. He was astonished at this and called out: 'Hi!

your reverence, whither away so quickly? Do not forget that we have a

christening today!' and running after him he took him by the sleeve, but

was also held fast to it.

Whilst the five were trotting thus one behind the other, two labourers

came with their hoes from the fields; the parson called out to them

and begged that they would set him and the sexton free. But they had

scarcely touched the sexton when they were held fast, and now there were

seven of them running behind Dummling and the goose.

Soon afterwards he came to a city, where a king ruled who had a daughter

who was so serious that no one could make her laugh. So he had put forth

a decree that whosoever should be able to make her laugh should marry

her. When Dummling heard this, he went with his goose and all her train

before the king's daughter, and as soon as she saw the seven people

running on and on, one behind the other, she began to laugh quite

loudly, and as if she would never stop. Thereupon Dummling asked to have

her for his wife; but the king did not like the son-in-law, and made all

manner of excuses and said he must first produce a man who could drink

a cellarful of wine. Dummling thought of the little grey man, who could

certainly help him; so he went into the forest, and in the same place

where he had felled the tree, he saw a man sitting, who had a very

sorrowful face. Dummling asked him what he was taking to heart so

sorely, and he answered: 'I have such a great thirst and cannot quench

it; cold water I cannot stand, a barrel of wine I have just emptied, but

that to me is like a drop on a hot stone!'

'There, I can help you,' said Dummling, 'just come with me and you shall

be satisfied.'

He led him into the king's cellar, and the man bent over the huge

barrels, and drank and drank till his loins hurt, and before the day was

out he had emptied all the barrels. Then Dummling asked once more

for his bride, but the king was vexed that such an ugly fellow, whom

everyone called Dummling, should take away his daughter, and he made a

new condition; he must first find a man who could eat a whole mountain

of bread. Dummling did not think long, but went straight into the

forest, where in the same place there sat a man who was tying up his

body with a strap, and making an awful face, and saying: 'I have eaten a

whole ovenful of rolls, but what good is that when one has such a hunger

as I? My stomach remains empty, and I must tie myself up if I am not to

die of hunger.'

At this Dummling was glad, and said: 'Get up and come with me; you shall

eat yourself full.' He led him to the king's palace where all the

flour in the whole Kingdom was collected, and from it he caused a huge

mountain of bread to be baked. The man from the forest stood before it,

began to eat, and by the end of one day the whole mountain had vanished.

Then Dummling for the third time asked for his bride; but the king again

sought a way out, and ordered a ship which could sail on land and on

water. 'As soon as you come sailing back in it,' said he, 'you shall

have my daughter for wife.'

Dummling went straight into the forest, and there sat the little grey

man to whom he had given his cake. When he heard what Dummling wanted,

he said: 'Since you have given me to eat and to drink, I will give you

the ship; and I do all this because you once were kind to me.' Then he

gave him the ship which could sail on land and water, and when the king

saw that, he could no longer prevent him from having his daughter. The

wedding was celebrated, and after the king's death, Dummling inherited

his kingdom and lived for a long time contentedly with his wife.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Emma who loved to swing in her backyard. She enjoyed the warm summer days when she could fly up high into the sky, feeling the breeze on her face.

One day, Emma was swinging with her brother, when she noticed that her brother was looking a bit weak. She asked him what was wrong, "What's the matter?"

Her brother replied, "My throat feels a bit sore, so my mom brought out the thermometer to take my temperature."

So, Emma and her brother stayed very still as the thermometer was put in his mouth to take his temperature. Unfortunately, the thermometer showed that his temperature was very high.

Emma was really worried, she felt her brother needed to rest. But her brother wanted to keep playing and swinging. Emma tried to convince him to sleep instead, but it was too difficult.

Finally, Emma had an idea - she suggested if they swing together, they could swing slowly like they were taking a nap. Her brother was really happy with the idea, and they spent the rest of the day swinging gently together in the backyard.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park. There, he saw a big wheel that he wanted to ride. However, Timmy's mom said it was too boring.

Timmy was sad and started to cry. A little girl saw Timmy crying and went to ask him what was wrong. Timmy told her that he wanted to ride the big wheel but his mom said no. The little girl told Timmy to shout, "I want to ride the big wheel!"

Timmy shouted as loud as he could, "I want to ride the big wheel!" His mom heard him and saw how sad he was. She changed her mind and let Timmy ride the big wheel. Timmy was so happy that he thanked the little girl for helping him. From that day on, Timmy learned that sometimes shouting can help you get what you want.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with cardboard boxes. One day, she found a big cardboard box and decided to make a house out of it.

Lily's mommy came into the room and asked, "What are you doing, Lily?"

"I'm making a house!" Lily replied with a big smile.

Mommy said, "That's great! When you're finished, we can rest inside your new house."

Lily worked hard and finally, her cardboard house was ready. She and her mommy crawled inside and lay down to rest. Lily was so happy that she had made a cozy house for them to rest in.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to help his mom in the kitchen. One day, they decided to make muffins together. Tim was very excited to work with his mom.

As they mixed the batter, Mom said, "Tim, we need to add something sweet. If we don't, the muffins will taste bitter." Tim nodded and added some sweet stuff to the mix. They put the muffins in the oven and waited for them to bake.

When the muffins were ready, Tim and his mom took them out of the oven. They smelled so good! Tim took a big bite of a muffin and smiled. "Mom, these are the best muffins ever!" he said. Mom smiled too, happy that they had worked together to make the muffins taste just right.

Once there was a bird who lived in a forest. One day it wanted to fly, so it flapped its wings and rose high into the sky. Its wings were strong and it felt so free.

But then it started to feel something strange, a thick, dark ash was filling the air. What was it? The bird wondered.

Suddenly it heard a voice from down below.
"Haha!" Someone laughed, "that's my fire! I burnt it bigger and stronger, so the ash would fly!"

The bird flew down to see what was happening. It saw a small figure standing by a campfire.

The bird asked, "Why do you want the ash to fly?"

"Because," the figure replied, "when it floats across the land, it makes things more bitter for the people who live here. That's why I like to make my fire bigger and stronger."

The bird was shocked. It didn't want anyone to be made miserable like that. It flew back up into the sky and spread its wings wide, creating a gust of wind. This blew the ashes away, removing any bitter taste they might bring.

The figure watched in amazement as this kindness of the bird.

The bird said before it flew away, "Don't ever forget that kindness can spread hope and joy, even in the darkest of places."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red wagon with four big wheels. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park to play. Timmy wanted to bring his wagon, so he rolled it all the way to the park.

At the park, Timmy saw a man who was deaf. The man couldn't hear anything, but he was very nice. Timmy wanted to share his wagon with the man, so he let him roll it around the park. The man smiled and thanked Timmy for being so kind.

After playing with the wagon, Timmy and the man sat on a bench and watched the other kids play. Timmy was happy to have made a new friend, even if he couldn't hear very well. They rolled the wagon back home together, and Timmy promised to visit the man again soon.

Once upon a time there was a big bear, called Doug. He loved to play outside, but one day he found something special in his garden. It was a big curtain! Doug wanted to play with it so he started to pull it. But when the curtain started to move, it made a lot of noise!

Doug was scared, he wanted to stop but he was so curious. And he kept pulling the curtain until it finally came off! Doug was so happy with his new toy, he couldn't wait to play with it.

Suddenly, Doug heard a loud growl and he was so shocked to see a big bear standing in front of him! The bear said: "You should be careful with things that don't belong to you. You should never take things without asking!"

Doug was so sorry, he knew he should have stopped earlier. He understood his mistake and promised to be more careful in the future. Doug and the bear became good friends from that day onwards.

The moral of the story is: Always be respectful and ask for permission before taking anything that does not belong to you.

Dog and Cat were best friends. One day they were playing in the garden when they spotted something strange. It was a smelly old box. Curiosity got the better of them and the two pets decided to take a closer look.

Dog pricked up his ears and said, "I think I can hear something inside." Cat carefully used her claws to cut open the top of the box and out popped a little purple mouse! It was holding a shiny golden key in its paws.

The mouse saw the two pets and started to shiver. It had been trying to steal the key when they found it! Dog and Cat quickly scooped it up and set it free.

The mouse thanked them and scurried away, leaving the wonderful golden key behind. Dog and Cat looked at each other in surprise and couldn't help but laugh. They had caught the thief and saved the day!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy and his mom. The little boy was very brave and always looking for an adventure. One day, the little boy asked his mom, "Can I go and peek in the garden?" His mom smiled, and said, "Yes, but be careful". The little boy ran off to the garden, with a shiny rake in his hand.

He suddenly stopped when he saw something moving in the grass. "What is that?" he thought. He was a little worried, but he was brave and he wanted to peek. He slowly peeked closer. All of a sudden, he heard a loud "Meow!" He jumped back and saw a small, black kitten. The boy smiled. He knew he had nothing to be worried about. He slowly reached out and petted the kitten.

The little boy was so happy that he opened the garden gate and called out from the garden to his mom. "Mom, look! I found a kitty!" His mom came running, and the family welcomed the kitten into their home.

The little boy was very proud of himself, and he went to bed with a happy smile on his face that night.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was very hungry. She looked all around the place, but she couldn't find anything to eat. Then she found a little house and she decided to go inside.

When she opened the door, she saw lots of food. She was so happy. She said, "Please give me something to eat."

The house was filled with kind people who were happy to help. They gave her lots of yummy food and the little girl ate it all.

When she was done, everyone gave her a big hug and said, "We are so happy you're no longer hungry. Come back anytime you're hungry."

The little girl smiled and said, "I will, thank you!"

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl who was three years old. She had curly blonde hair and bright blue eyes. Whenever she was scared or sad, she would pray.

One sunny day, she was playing in the park when she lost her sunglasses. She was very sad. She looked everywhere and asked her mom, but she couldn't find them.

The kind girl stopped playing and took a deep breath. She closed her eyes and began to pray. As she prayed, she asked God to help her find her sunglasses.

Suddenly, she heard a voice saying â€œLook over there.â€ She opened her eyes and saw her sunglasses right next to her. She was so happy and thanked God for helping her. She put on her sunglasses and went back to playing in the park.

The kind girl always remembered to pray whenever she needed help.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly bear named Benny. He loved to eat waffles for breakfast every day. One morning, when Benny woke up, he demanded his waffles right away. But his mom told him to wait a little bit because she was making them fresh.

Benny didn't want to wait, so he went outside to play with his friends. They played tag and hide-and-seek until Benny's mom called him in for breakfast. When Benny saw the waffles, he was so happy! He ate them all up and felt very full.

After breakfast, Benny and his friends went to the park to play some more. They had so much fun together and were very friendly to each other. Benny was grateful for his friends and his yummy waffles.

Once upon a time, there was a little green frog that lived in the garden. Every day, it would hop and sneak to find treats like flies and worms.

One day, the frog found a pepper! It was pink, round and looked so yummy. The frog carefully took it in its tiny little hands and started to eat it.

Suddenly, it felt a burning sensation and started to jump around. It wanted to escape the pepper!

The frog jumped and hopped back to the garden and shouted, "Help me! Help me!"

Luckily, a little bird was nearby and heard the frog's cries. It pecked the pepper out of the frog's hands and said, "There, you don't have to eat it anymore!"

The frog was happy and thanked the little bird. From that day on, the frog learned to be more careful when it comes to food!

One day, little Jack wanted to go for a drive in his toy car. He hopped in excitedly, but soon he noticed something strange. His car was not moving! He couldn't understand why.

So he called out to his mum, "Mum, my car won't go!" His mum replied, "It looks like someone's blocking the way. Come outside and you'll see for yourself."

Jack looked outside and saw a large hill. On the hill was a big scary-looking man. He was wearing a big-earring, so Jack guessed he must be deaf. He shouted, "Hey! Please move your car!"

The man just stared at Jack and stayed where he was. Jack had an idea. He started to climb the hill, pushing his car up at the same time. After a while, the man realised what Jack was doing and moved his car out of the way.

Jack was so relieved! He reached the top of the hill and looked down. It was the most thrilling thing he had ever done. He waved to the man, thanking him for helping him. Then he revved his engine and drove off happily. Experience won!

Sara was a big sister. She had a baby brother named Tom. Sara loved Tom very much, but sometimes she was jealous. She wanted to play with Mom and Dad, but they were busy with Tom.

One day, Sara saw Tom sleeping in his crib. She had an idea. She took her doctor kit and went to examine Tom. She put a stethoscope on his chest, a thermometer in his mouth, and a band-aid on his arm. She said, "I am a doctor. I will make you better, Tom."

But Tom did not like Sara's game. He woke up and started to cry. He spit out the thermometer and pulled off the band-aid. He was scared and hurt. He wanted Mom and Dad.

Mom and Dad heard Tom's cry and ran to his room. They saw Sara and her doctor kit. They were angry and worried. They said, "Sara, what did you do to Tom? You should not play with him like that. You could hurt him or make him sick. He is a baby. He needs love and care, not games and toys."

Sara felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I am sorry, Mom and Dad. I wanted to play with you, but you were busy with Tom. I wanted to examine him, like you do. I wanted to be intelligent, like you are."

Mom and Dad hugged Sara and said, "Sara, we love you very much. You are a big sister and a smart girl. You can play with us and with Tom, but you have to be gentle and kind. You can examine him, but only with your eyes and your words. You can ask him questions, like how he feels, what he likes, and what he learns. You can help him grow and learn, too. That is how you show your intelligence and your love."

Sara smiled and said, "Thank you, Mom and Dad. I understand. I will be a good sister and a good doctor. I will love Tom and play with him nicely."

She went to Tom's crib and said, "Hi, Tom. I am sorry I scared you. I love you. Do you want to play with me?"

Tom stopped crying and looked at Sara. He smiled and reached for her hand. He said, "Yes, Sara. I love you, too. You are my sister. You are intelligent."

The end.

Jack was walking through the hallway. He saw an enormous mess! Everywhere he looked there was something spilled on the floor. Jack knew he couldn't leave the mess there, he needed to clean it.

He went to the closet and grabbed a mop. The mop was too big for Jack but he needed it to clean the mess. He tried to lift it but it was so heavy he couldn't carry it.

Then his big brother came by and saw the mess. He said he would help and grabbed the enormous mop. He started to mop the floor and it didn't take long before the hallway was clean! Both Jack and his brother were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a kind rabbit. The rabbit lived in a big garden with lots of fruit trees. One day, the rabbit saw a squirrel steal some fruit from the garden.

The rabbit said, "Why did you steal the fruit?"

The squirrel replied, "I'm sorry. I was hungry and had no food."

The kind rabbit said, "That's okay. You can have some of my fruit. I have plenty to share."

From that day on, the rabbit and the squirrel became friends and shared the fruit in the garden. They never had to steal again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore the world around him. One day, Timmy found an interesting bug crawling on the ground.

"Mommy, look at this bug!" Timmy said excitedly.

"That's a cool bug, Timmy," replied his mom. "But be careful, it might bite you."

Timmy continued to watch the bug crawl around until it finally completed its journey and flew away.

Later that day, Timmy's dad came home from work and went to shave with his razor. Timmy watched curiously as his dad shaved his face.

"Daddy, what's that thing you're using?" Timmy asked.

"It's called a razor, Timmy," replied his dad. "It helps me shave my beard."

Timmy thought the razor was interesting too and couldn't wait to grow up and shave like his dad.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved his bathrobe because it was soft and cozy. One day, Timmy put on his bathrobe and felt very silly because it was too big for him. He ran around the house pretending to be a superhero.

Timmy's mom came into the room and saw him running around. She asked him why he was acting so silly. Timmy told his mom that he felt like a superhero in his big bathrobe. His mom smiled and said that he looked very cute.

Timmy felt happy that his mom liked his silly superhero outfit. He continued to run around the house in his bathrobe, feeling like a superhero. From that day on, Timmy loved wearing his bathrobe and feeling silly.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to rush and play in the thick green grass. He liked to hop and jump all day long. The sun was bright and warm, and Remy was very happy.

One day, Remy found a big hole in the ground. He thought it was a fun new place to play. But it was a trap! A big net came up and caught Remy. He was scared and sad. He wanted to go back to the thick green grass.

Remy's friend, a small bird named Bella, saw him in the trap. She was very smart and knew how to help. Bella flew down and used her beak to open the trap. Remy was free! Remy and Bella went back to the thick green grass to play. They were both very happy and played together all day long.

Once upon a time there was a chubby bunny named Pancake. Pancake lived in the woods with her friends, but she was having a problem. Pancake was feeling very sick and achy.

She knew she had to go see a veterinarian so she hopped to the doctor's office. The veterinarian had a lot of tools and machines, so Pancake felt a bit scared.

But the veterinarian was very kind and explained that he would need to repair her. He put some cream on her, gave her a big hug, and soon Pancake felt better.

Pancake thanked the vet for helping her and hopped off to find her friends. She was feeling much better and running around in no time.

The end!

Jane and her mom were going to a restaurant. Jane was very excited. They arrived at the restaurant and it was so lovely. It had a nice garden and some birds were singing. Jane and her mom went inside.

When they stepped in, the restaurant seemed very clean. Everything was in its place. Jane said, "Mommy, this restaurant is so nice! Look, it's so clean."

Her mom smiled and said, "This place looks lovely, Jane. It's clean, so we can eat here without worry."

Jane was happy that the restaurant was clean. She smiled and said, "Let's eat here! Then we can have a lovely time."

Mom smiled and said, "Yes! Now let's have a lovely time with lots of delicious food." Jane couldn't wait to start eating in the clean and lovely restaurant.

Molly and her mom were walking in the park. Molly saw a fat tree. She ran over to it and saw a big, green leaf. Molly reached out her hands and squeezed the leaf. She chuckled when it made a funny sound.

Molly's mom smiled and said, "Now I'm going to show you something special!" Molly's mom put a big, fat leaf between her hands. She squeezed the leaf and, whoosh, a big gust of air blew out of the leaf! "Wow!" exclaimed Molly.

Molly and her mom played with the leaf for a while. Molly would squeeze the leaf and a big gust of air would come out. Molly and her mom laughed and laughed.

Finally, Molly said, "Let's go home." They waved goodbye to the tree and walked away. Molly held her fat leaf close. She would always remember the fun they had that day.

Tom is a boy who likes to write. He has a new book with many pages. He writes his name on the first page. He writes what he sees on the second page. He sees a big mill near his house. The mill has a wheel that turns and turns.

One day, Tom goes to the mill with his dad. His dad works at the mill. He makes flour from wheat. Tom wants to write about the mill. He takes his book and a pen. He looks at the mill and writes what he sees. He writes "mill", "wheel", "flour", "wheat".

Tom is happy. He shows his book to his dad. His dad is proud. He says "You are a good writer, Tom. You write what you see. You write simple words. You write a nice story." Tom smiles. He likes to write. He likes his new book. He likes the mill.

Lily and Ben are playing with blocks. They like to make different patterns with the blocks. They use red, blue, yellow and green blocks.

"Look, I made a pattern with red and blue blocks!" Lily says. She shows Ben her pattern. It is red, blue, red, blue, red, blue.

"That is a nice pattern, Lily!" Ben says. He makes a pattern with yellow and green blocks. It is yellow, green, yellow, green, yellow, green.

"Can I see your pattern, Ben?" Lily asks. She wants to see Ben's pattern.

"Sure, Lily. Here is my pattern." Ben shows Lily his pattern. He is proud of his pattern.

Lily and Ben look at each other's patterns. They like both patterns. They smile and say, "Good job!"

Then they hear a noise. It is their mom. She is calling them for lunch.

"Come on, kids. It is time for lunch. Please wash your hands and come to the table." Mom says. She is in the kitchen.

"OK, Mom. We are coming." Lily and Ben say. They put their blocks away. They run to the bathroom. They wash their hands. They are fast.

They go to the kitchen. They see their mom. She has made sandwiches and fruit for them. They are hungry.

"Thank you, Mom. This looks yummy." Lily and Ben say. They sit at the table. They eat their lunch. They are happy.

Once upon a time, a witch lived in a big house. Every night she would go out for a walk. One night, when the witch was walking, she saw a spicy red ball.

The witch said, "I must catch that ball."

So the witch ran and jumped and stretched. She did everything she could but she couldn't catch the ball.

The witch started to get sad and she said, "Will someone help me catch that spicy red ball?"

Just then, a small boy came up to her. The boy said, "I can help. I can catch the ball for you."

The witch thanked him and the boy ran and caught the ball. The witch was so happy. She said, "Thank you so much! Now I have my red ball!"

The witch went back to her house with the ball and the boy went back home. The boy was very happy that he could help the witch catch her spicy red ball.

Once upon a time, there was a big field with lots of grass and flowers. A cow named Betsy lived in the field and she loved to eat the grass. One day, Betsy was feeling very hungry because she had not eaten much that day. She walked around the field looking for more grass to eat.

Suddenly, Betsy saw a patch of grass that looked very yummy. She ran over to it and started to eat. After a while, Betsy's tummy started to settle down and she felt much better. She walked around the field some more, feeling happy and content. From that day on, Betsy made sure to eat enough so she would never feel hungry again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She loved to dance. Every day she would twirl and jump around with joy.

One day, Sally heard music coming from a nearby station. She skipped over and saw a big pile of soft pillows. She plopped down and started to dance. She jumped, twirled and laughed with delight.

Soon all the other children joined Sally. They twirled and spun together in a circle. Everyone was having so much fun! Even the birds and the bees were dancing to the music.

When their dance was finished, Sally's mother called her home. Sally said goodbye to the other children and skipped away. As she walked, she could still feel the rhythm of the music in her heart.

Once upon a time, there was a pink princess who loved to ride her horse. Her horse was very fast and could speed through the forest. One day, while they were riding, they saw a big fire in the distance. The princess was scared and asked her horse what they should do.

The horse said, "Don't worry, I can speed us away from the fire." So they rode as fast as they could, and soon they were far away from the fire. The princess was so happy that her horse was so fast and thanked him for keeping her safe.

From then on, whenever they went for a ride, the princess would tell her horse to speed up and they would race through the forest, feeling the wind in their hair. They were the best of friends and always had fun together.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They liked to dig in the sand, splash in the water, and chase the birds. But they did not like to wash their hands and faces when they came home. They said it was boring and itchy.

One day, their mom told them they had a lovely surprise. She said they could go to the park and have a picnic with their friends. Anna and Ben were very happy and ran to get their hats and shoes. But mom stopped them and said, "Wait, you have to wash your hands and faces first. You are very dirty and you don't want to make your friends sick."

Anna and Ben did not want to wash. They said, "No, mom, we don't need to wash. We are not dirty and we are not sick. We have our own opinion and we think washing is silly."

Mom was not happy. She said, "I'm sorry, but you have to respect my opinion too. I am your mom and I know what is best for you. Washing is not silly, it is important and healthy. If you don't wash, you can't go to the park and have the picnic."

Anna and Ben did not like this. They wanted to go to the park and have the picnic. They looked at each other and decided to listen to mom. They said, "Okay, mom, we will wash. We are sorry for being rude. We love you and we want to make you happy."

Mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "Thank you, Anna and Ben. I love you too and I want to make you happy. I'm glad you understand that washing is good for you and for others. Now you can go to the park and have the picnic. And I have another lovely surprise for you. I made your favorite cookies for dessert."

Anna and Ben were very happy and thanked mom. They washed their hands and faces and went to the park. They had a lot of fun with their friends and enjoyed the picnic. They also shared their cookies with their friends and said they were delicious. They learned that washing was not so bad after all and that listening to mom was a good thing. They also learned that having an opinion was okay, but respecting other people's opinions was also important. They had a lovely day and went to bed with a smile.

There was a little girl named Julie. She was only 3 years old. One day she wanted to play with her ball. She ran outside to the garden with it. She was so happy. She ran and ran, kicking her ball further and further away from her.
