Lily felt better and said, "Thank you, mommy. I love you." And her mom replied, "I love you too, my little tall girl."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and always wanted to ride in an automobile. One day, Timmy's parents promised him that they would take him for a ride in an automobile. Timmy was very excited and couldn't wait to go for the ride.

The next day, Timmy's parents organized everything and they all got into the automobile. Timmy was so happy to be in the car and he looked out of the window at all the trees and houses. They drove around for a while and then stopped at a park. Timmy had so much fun playing in the park and he was very happy that his parents kept their promise.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with cardboard boxes and making forts out of them. One day, she found a big purple cardboard box in the garage. She was so excited and thought it would be perfect for her new fort.

Lily's mom warned her that the box was very old and might not be strong enough. But Lily didn't listen and started building her fort. Suddenly, the box collapsed and Lily fell down. She was very sad and hurt.

Lily's mom hugged her and said, "I think we should always listen to grown-ups when they warn us about things. And we should always be careful with old things, like that purple cardboard box."

From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful and always listen to her mom. She also learned that sometimes things that look fun and exciting can be dangerous, so it's important to be safe.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit called Tony. Tony had a prune in his mouth and he was running really fast. He was on his way to a secret hideout he found. It was a big hole in the ground filled with lots of long grass and flowers.

Tony loved to have private picnics there and he was so excited to eat his prune in peace. But suddenly he heard a noise! It was a loud sound that disturbed the peacefulness. Tony was so scared that he dropped his prune and ran away.

He stopped at the top of a hill and looked back. He just saw a big bird, flapping its wings. Tony was so relieved that there was nothing to worry about.

He then went and picked up his prune again and hopped back down the hill. He was so happy he didn't let the noise disturb his special treat.

Mum was shopping for a present for her little daughter's birthday. She looked around the shop and found something perfect. It was a modern toy of a white dove.

Mum took the toy to the counter and paid for it. She then took the present and quickly went outside to her car.

When mum got back home, her little daughter was already waiting for her. She got very excited when she saw the present. She ran up to her mother and asked, "What is it?"

Mum said, "It's a toy of a white dove. Pull the string and watch what happens."

The little girl pulled the string and the toy bird began to snap its wings. She was so happy!

"Thank you, Mum," she said as she hugged her mother. Now she had a modern toy to play with.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Sarah and Tony, who loved to go for walks in their town. One day, they wanted to explore a part of town they hadn't seen before. They had to choose which way to go. There was a beautiful creek with a bridge that crossed over it or a dark, mysterious forest.

Tony chose the creek and they headed towards the bridge. It was a beautiful walk and they found a lot of new things to explore. But when they reached the bridge, they stopped. It looked old and dangerous, and they weren't sure if it was safe to cross.

Sarah stopped and thought for a moment. She said to Tony, "Let's not cross it, Tony. It looks too dangerous. Let's find another way."

Tony realized Sarah was right, and they chose the safe option. They found a nicer, safer bridge to cross, and they safely made it to the other side of the creek and found some wonderful things to explore.

The moral of the story is that it is important to choose the safe option, even if it is not the most exciting. Taking chances can be dangerous and it is better to make wise choices.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She had lots of stuff. Her stuff was new and pretty.
Every day, the girl would go outside and play for hours. One day, when she was done playing, she came back inside... and all her stuff was gone. She looked around, but she couldn't see it anywhere.
Suddenly she realized - someone had taken her stuff! Her stuff had disappeared.
The girl felt very sad. She was upset that someone had taken her pretty new stuff.
But then, something really magical happened! The girl looked around and she realized that her stuff had come back! She was so happy - all her stuff was there, just as it was before.
The girl was so glad to have her stuff back - she promised to take better care of it from now on. And she was never sad again!

John was a little boy. He lived in a small house. One day, it got very cold outside. So cold, that John started to feel frightened. He wanted to find a way to keep warm. He looked around the house but he couldn't find anything.

Suddenly, John saw a big sack. He knew that the sack would be warm. He jumped and grabbed it. The sack was so warm, it felt like a hug! He wrapped the sack around himself and it was so cozy and warm.

John felt safe and happy. He ran around the house, having fun. Even though it was cold outside, John was warm and happy inside the sack.

Jeff was a 3 year old who loved playing hide and seek. One day he was playing and he noticed something unknown behind the couch. Jeff was very curious, so he decided to explore.

When he peeked behind the couch he noticed that his room was full of water. He had no idea why his room was wet and he was very scared. Jeff quickly realized that he was in trouble.

He started thinking of ways he could dry the room. Then Jeff remembered that his parents had a big fan which he could use. So he grabbed the fan and started blowing the water out of the room.

After a few minutes, Jeff was able to dry the room and make it safe. He was happy he could help and he felt like a big hero. He settled onto the couch and took a nap. He had never seen such big trouble and he was proud of himself for figuring out a solution.

Once there was a family who had a little girl called Grace. Grace loved playing on the board with her toys every day. One day, she wanted to play with her toys but her parents said it was time for a nap. Grace sighed and went to her bed.

When she was about to sleep, her mummy came over and gave her a kiss. She asked Grace to always be patient and gentle. Grace nodded â€œYes, Mummyâ€. Her mummy replied with a gentle smile, â€œI will always remind youâ€.

Grace felt better with the reminder from her mummy. She closed her eyes and drifted off to sleep. When she woke up, she was excited to play with her toys on the board again. She smiled and happily ran off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved drinking juice, especially the fancy kind her mommy would make for her. One day, she asked her mommy for some juice but her mommy was busy on the phone. Lily waited patiently for her mommy to finish her call.

Finally, her mommy hung up the phone and turned to Lily. "What would you like, sweetie?" her mommy asked. "Juice please," Lily replied. Her mommy smiled and went to the kitchen to make her some fancy juice.

Lily was so happy to have her juice and she drank it all up. "Thank you, mommy," she said. Her mommy replied, "You're welcome, my dear. Anytime you want some juice, just let me know." Lily smiled and hugged her mommy. She loved her mommy's fancy juice and her mommy's love even more.

Once upon a time, there was a painter named Tom. He loved to paint pretty pictures with many colors. One day, Tom felt worried. He did not know what to paint next. He looked around for ideas but found none.

Tom went for a walk and met a little girl named Sue. Sue said, "Hi, Tom! Why do you look worried?" Tom told her, "I don't know what to paint next." Sue thought for a moment and said, "Why don't you paint the park? We can enjoy the pretty flowers and trees together."

Tom smiled and said, "Great idea, Sue!" They went to the park and enjoyed looking at the flowers and trees. Tom painted a beautiful picture with many colors. Sue and Tom were happy. From that day on, they enjoyed painting together and were never worried again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl walking by a field. She came across a large number of animals who were struggling. The little girl felt sorry for the animals, so she went over to help them. She worked tirelessly to try and make their lives better.

After a while, the little girl got tired and felt very dizzy. She plopped onto the ground and took a quick break, which seemed like forever.

Soon enough, she was feeling better and was able to help the animals again. She worked together with them to solve the problems they were facing. Together they felt like a big happy family.

The animals thanked the little girl for all of her help and told her that she had made a huge difference. She smiled, happy to have done something good, and waved goodbye to all of her animal friends.

The little girl had worked very hard and achieved a great number of successes for the animals. She had worked so hard, and it made her so proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to buy a toy at the store, but her mom said they didn't have enough money. Lily felt sad, but her mom said they could still have fun together without buying anything.

They went to the park and played on the swings and slide. Lily's mom pushed her high in the air and caught her tight when she slid down. Lily laughed and giggled with joy.

After playing, they went to the hospital to see Lily's grandma. Grandma was feeling better because the nurse took good care of her. Lily gave her a big hug and felt happy because she made her grandma smile.

Even though they didn't buy anything, Lily had a fun day with her mom and grandma. She learned that you don't always need to buy things to be happy.

Once there was a group of friends. They were all very excited to go to the theater. They each dressed up in silly outfits.

They got there, and the theater was full of people. The children looked around in wonder. The theater was so big and bright.

They found a fun seat and they all hugged each other. Then a funny show began!

The friends laughed and cheered and watched a silly movie. They saw silly monsters, and the theater filled with laughter.

When the show was over, they all hugged again and left the theater. They all had a great time looking at the silly show.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little bunny named Floppy. Floppy loved to travel around the forest and meet new friends. One day, Floppy met a friendly squirrel named Nutty. They played together and had fun.

After a while, they decided to play a game of hide-and-seek. Nutty was very good at hiding, and Floppy had a hard time finding him. Finally, Floppy found Nutty hiding in a tree. They were both happy and excited.

But then, as they were playing, a big, scary wolf appeared. The wolf wanted to score a meal and chased after Floppy and Nutty. They ran as fast as they could, but the wolf was too fast. Sadly, the wolf caught them both and they never saw their forest friends again.

Once upon a time, there was a rod that was very big and strong. It was an enormous rod and it had a special name. Everyone called it "Super Rod". Super Rod was so strong that it could lift anything. All the children wanted to try Super Rod and see what it could do.

One day, a little 3 year old boy named Robbie heard about Super Rod and wanted to try it. He asked his mom if could lift it, and she said yes.

So, Robbie and his mom went to go find Super Rod. When they arrived, they saw that it was even bigger and more powerful in real life. Robbie was very excited and he asked his mom if he could try it. She said yes and began to help him.

Robbie was able to move Super Rod! He was so proud of himself. He felt happy and strong. The other children were amazed that he could lift such an enormous rod. From then on, everyone knew the 3 year old boy as Super Robbie.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He liked to play games with his friends. They were very competitive and always wanted to win. One day, they decided to have a race to see who was the fastest.

The old man tried his best, but he was very slow. His friends all ran ahead of him. But then, something magical happened. The old man's granddaughter came to watch the race. She ran up to him and gave him a big kiss on the cheek.

Suddenly, the old man felt like he could run faster than ever before. He started to catch up with his friends. They were all amazed at how fast he was going. In the end, the old man won the race! His friends were happy for him and they all hugged and laughed together.

Tom and Mia were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big tree with many branches. Tom wanted to climb the tree and see how high he could go. He said to Mia, "Let's climb the tree! It will be fun!"

Mia was fearful of the tree. She thought it was too tall and dangerous. She said to Tom, "No, I don't want to climb the tree. I'm scared. What if we fall?"

Tom said, "Don't be scared. I will help you. Climbing the tree will make us strong and brave. We will have power over the tree."

Mia was not sure, but she wanted to be strong and brave too. She agreed to climb the tree with Tom. They held hands and started to climb. They climbed slowly and carefully, looking for places to put their feet and hands.

They climbed higher and higher, until they reached a big branch. They sat on the branch and looked around. They saw the sky, the birds, the flowers, and the other trees. They felt happy and proud. They had climbed the tree!

They smiled at each other and said, "We did it! We climbed the tree! We are strong and brave! We have power over the tree!"

They hugged and decided to climb down. They climbed down slowly and carefully, until they reached the ground. They ran to their parents and told them what they had done. Their parents were happy and proud too. They praised Tom and Mia for their courage and skill.

Tom and Mia felt good. They had overcome their fear and had a new adventure. They had learned something new and had fun. They had climbed the tree!

One day, a boy named Tim found a big drum in his room. He was very happy. He wanted to play the drum all day. Tim hit the drum fast and slow. The drum made a loud sound.

Tim's sister, Sue, was not happy. She said, "Tim, please stop! The drum is too loud!" Tim sighed and stopped playing. He felt sad because he wanted to play the drum, but he did not want to make Sue upset.

Then, Tim had an idea. He asked Sue to play with him. They took turns playing the drum, hitting it slow and soft. They both had fun and were happy. The conflict was over, and they played the drum together.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Sam, who was three years old. Sam loved learning about the world around him. One day, Sam heard something mysterious coming from his living room. Thinking it must be something exciting, he ran in to investigate.

Sam saw a man sitting in his favorite armchair. The man had bright, shining eyes hidden behind thick glasses. He looked very mysterious.

"Hello, my name is Mr. McQueen," said the man. "I've come all the way from a faraway place, and I'd like to teach you something very special."

Sam was excited. He had never heard of Mr. McQueen before and he just knew that learning something special had to be fun.

"I'm a science teacher," the man said. "But what I want to teach you is something even more special, something that nobody else knows. I want to teach you the secrets of the human eye."

Sam wasn't sure what the man meant by this. But he couldn't help but be curious and he eagerly agreed to learn.

The man then explained to Sam that the eye has tiny parts called pupils which can see things that are unknown to most people. Sam was so interested, he couldn't wait to learn more.

That evening, Sam learned that his pupils could help him see things his eyes normally wouldn't pick up - things that were happening in the world

Tom had a huge toy car that he loved to play with. It was red and shiny and made loud noises. He liked to drive it around the yard and pretend he was a racer. But he had a problem. His toy car was too big to fit in the garage. The garage was where he kept his other toys, like his bike and his ball and his teddy bear.

One day, Tom had an idea. He saw his dad's car parked in the driveway. His dad's car was also red and shiny and made loud noises. Maybe his dad's car could fit in the garage, and then he could put his toy car in the driveway. Tom thought that was a good plan. He ran to his dad's car and opened the door. He climbed inside and tried to find the keys. He did not know how to drive a real car, but he thought it was easy. He just had to turn the wheel and push the pedals.

Tom found the keys and put them in the hole. He turned them and the car started. He was very happy. He pushed the pedal and the car moved. He turned the wheel and the car turned. He did not see the fence or the tree or the mailbox. He only saw the garage. He wanted to fit his dad's car in the garage. He pushed the pedal harder and the car went faster. He turned the wheel more and the car went straight to the garage.

But the car did not fit in the garage. The car was too big and the garage was too small. The car crashed into the garage and made a huge noise. The garage broke and fell down. The car broke and stopped. Tom was scared and sad. He did not know what he did. He did not know what his dad would say. He did not know what to do. He started to cry. He wished he never touched his dad's car. He wished he played with his toy car instead. He wished he could fit his toy car in the garage. But he could not. He made a big mess. He made a big mistake. He made a bad ending.

Once there was an old man who was so restless he couldn't stay still. He wanted to go outside and do something new. So he asked his wife if he could go for a walk. But she refused. She said, "No, you need to stay inside and rest." He was sad, but he knew his wife was right.

So he stayed inside and did some chores. He still felt restless though and all he could do was think about how he wanted to go outside. Then he had an idea! He got up and put on his coat. He was nearly out the door when his wife saw him.

He asked again if he could go out. His wife refused again. She said, "No, stay inside and rest." The old man was disappointed, but he knew his wife was right. He was too old to go out anyway. So he went back to his chores and tried to be content.

Once there was an infant playing in a garden. He was with his mom and dad. The infant looked around, examining the colourful flowers and plants. He noticed another infant in the garden who was also playing.

The two infants said hi to each other and quickly became friends. They laughed and talked about how helpful their parents were.

Together, they explored the garden. The little friends looked at all sorts of things, some furry, some wet and some slimy! Suddenly, they heard a loud noise coming from above.

They looked up to see a big dark cloud. The cloud was growing bigger and bigger. Then, the two infants heard their parents calling them. The infant told his friend he had to go, but promised to make up for it.

Unfortunately, the infant never got to see his friend again. When he returned to the garden later, he saw a big storm had destroyed the garden. He said goodbye to his friend in his heart, knowing he'd never see him again.

Once upon a time, there was a mummy and daddy. Mummy and daddy wanted to build a very special house. They worked really hard and were very successful. Mummy painted the walls with pretty colours. Daddy put in special lights and carpets.

Once the house was built, mummy and daddy celebrated by making lots of toast. Mummy and daddy could now live in a nice and cosy house.

They looked around and smiled. They were so happy with their new house and what a successful job they had done.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a man who was very, very rich. He had a lot of money and lived in a big house. One day, he went to a restaurant and ordered some soup. He ate the soup and then left, but he forgot his hat on the table.

When he got home, he realized he didn't have his hat. He was very sad because it was his favorite hat. He decided to return to the restaurant to look for it. When he got there, he asked the waitress if she had seen his hat. She smiled and said, "Yes! It's right here!"

The man was so happy to have his hat back. He thanked the waitress and left the restaurant feeling very wealthy indeed.

Once upon a time there lived a small noisy bear. He liked to make a lot of noise, but sometimes it made him sad. Then one day he found an escape. It was a special place where he could hide away. The place was very quiet and he felt comforted there. He would stay and relax until the noise had gone away.

So every day he would escape to this special place and feel happy and comforted. All the other animals in the forest knew the bear had a special place he went to when he was feeling sad. Whenever they heard the bear getting too noisy, they knew it was time for him to go and find his escape.

The bear was very happy because he always knew that his special place was there for him if he ever needed it. He could go there and find comfort when he felt overwhelmed by the noise. Thanks to his special escape, the bear never had to feel alone or scared in the noisy forest.

Mia was playing outside in the enormous park. She could see so many things. There were trees, and rocks, and slides. She wanted to slide, but it was too high for her.

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. Mia turned around and saw a giant striking the ground very hard. Mia was scared and hid behind a tree.

The giant noticed her and said, "Hello Mia". Mia was so surprised that he knew her name. The giant asked, "Do you want to play with me?" Mia thought for a moment and said, "Yes, I would like that."

So Mia and the giant played a game together. They rolled rocks, laughed and had fun! After a while, the giant struck the ground with his foot and said goodbye.

Mia waved goodbye to the giant and couldn't believe he was so enormous and friendly!

Anna and Ben like to play in the kitchen. They pretend to cook and wash dishes. One day, they find a big green apple on the table. Anna wants to eat it, but Ben has an idea.

"Let's put the apple in the sink and see what happens," he says.

"Why?" Anna asks.

"Maybe it will float or sink or make bubbles," Ben says.

They fill the sink with water and drop the apple in. The apple sinks to the bottom. Anna and Ben are surprised.

"Look, the apple is under the water," Anna says.

"Maybe it is too heavy to float," Ben says.

They try to reach the apple with their hands, but the water is too deep. They look for a spoon or a fork, but they cannot find any.

"Mom, can you help us?" Anna calls.

Mom comes to the kitchen and sees the apple in the sink. She smiles and shakes her head.

"What are you doing, kids?" she asks.

"We wanted to see what the apple would do in the water," Ben says.

"Well, it looks like it remains in the sink," Mom says.

She drains the water and takes out the apple. She wipes it with a towel and cuts it into pieces.

"Here, you can share the apple now," she says.

Anna and Ben are happy. They thank Mom and eat the apple. They think it is very sweet and juicy. They decide to play with something else next time.

Once upon a time, there was a pale gem which nobody knew the power of. One day a teacher appeared in the village and told the people, "I know the power of the pale gem! I will teach you how to use it." Everyone was excited and gathered around the teacher.

The teacher said, "Now, I will teach you how to make the pale gem magical. First you must find a special vessel and fill it with water. Then place the pale gem in the vessel and watch as it glows." Everyone was amazed!

The teacher continued, "While holding the vessel with the pale gem in it, you must say a very special spell. Say the words 'Pale Gem, I call on you to bring us luck and fortune!' and the gem will become magical and bring us luck and fortune."

Everyone was thrilled and thanked the teacher. The village was now filled with more luck and fortune than ever before, all thanks to the teacher who taught them all how to use the pale gem.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved playing in the snow. One day, she looked outside and saw that it was snowing! She put on her coat, hat, and gloves, and ran outside to play.

Lily built a snowman and had so much fun throwing snowballs. But then she realized that she couldn't find her scarf. She looked and looked, but it was nowhere to be found.

Her mom came outside and asked what was wrong. Lily said, "I lost my scarf. I hope I can find it." Her mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, we will look for it together. But first, let's go inside and warm up with some hot cocoa."

After they drank their hot cocoa, they went back outside to look for the scarf. It was very stubborn and didn't want to be found. But finally, Lily saw a little bit of red peeking out from under the snow. She dug and dug until she found her scarf. She was so happy and said, "Yay! I found it! Thank you, Mom."

Sophia was very tired after a long day. She had been polishing all day, and hadn't much free time to play.

Sophia looked out the window. She saw the most beautiful sunset. She wanted to go outside to see it up close.

Sophia asked her mom, "Can I go out and see the sunset?"

Her mom replied, "No, not now. Its getting dark and you're tired - you must rest."

Sophia nodded and said, "Ok, I'll stay inside and rest. But can I still polish something?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can polish a few things. That way you can still enjoy the sunset from here."

So Sophia polished her toys while watching the beautiful sunset. She was so happy and relaxed. As the sun set, Sophia lay down and fell asleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He had a basket of blocks that were all different colors. The boy wanted to play with the blocks, but his parents said he had to wait. So he waited and waited, until he could not wait any longer.

One day, when no one was looking, the boy stealthily opened the basket and started playing with the blocks. He built towers and castles and even a big car. It was so much fun!

But he started to feel something strange. He felt guilty and stopped playing with the blocks. He quickly put them back in the basket and walked away, feeling ashamed.

After that day, the boy was extra careful not to part with the blocks any more. He knew it was not right to take them without asking.

Once upon a time, there was a big, graceful cat. The cat had pretty, soft fur. One day, the cat saw a shiny copper toy. The cat wanted to play with the toy. But, the toy was in a small house.

The cat tried to enter the small house. But, the door was too little. The cat could not go in. The cat was sad. The cat wanted the copper toy so much.

Then, the cat saw a big dog. The dog was strong. The cat asked the dog for help. The dog pushed the small house. The house fell down. The cat got the shiny copper toy. The cat and the dog were happy. They played with the toy together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and make things with paper. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a big envelope with some mail inside. Lily was so excited to see what was inside the envelope.

As she was looking at the mail, she accidentally dropped it on the floor. But instead of being sad, Lily had a creative idea. She decided to use the envelope to make a special card for her mommy.

Lily drew a beautiful picture on the front of the envelope and wrote a sweet message inside. When she gave the card to her mommy, she was so happy and proud of herself for being so creative. From that day on, Lily loved to make special things with paper and mail them to her loved ones.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy bunny that she loved very much. One day, Lily's big brother took the bunny and wouldn't give it back. Lily felt very sad and cried a lot. But then, her brother said he was sorry and gave the bunny back. Lily forgave him and felt happy again.

Another day, Lily was playing at the park. She saw a boy who was very weak and couldn't climb the big slide. Lily asked if he wanted help and together they climbed to the top. The boy thanked Lily and gave her a shiny thing as a present. Lily felt proud that she could help someone who was weak.

At bedtime, Lily's mom read her a story about a kind princess who forgave everyone who did something wrong. Lily asked her mom what "forgive" meant. Her mom explained that it's when you decide to not be mad at someone anymore and be friends again. Lily thought that was a good thing to do and fell asleep with her toy bunny and shiny thing beside her.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy he loved very much. It was a toy knife. He played with it all day long. He liked to pretend he was a big, strong hero with his toy knife.

One day, Tim found a real knife in the kitchen. He thought it looked just like his toy knife. He wanted to play with it, but he remembered what his mom had told him. She said real knives are not for playing. They can hurt people.

Tim put the real knife back and went to find his toy knife. He played with it and had lots of fun. He was glad he listened to his mom. The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents because they know what is best for you.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Annie. She was only three years old but she was full of energy and liked to explore. One day, she was walking in the forest and came across a clearing. In the middle of the clearing was an arrow.
Annie was nosy and wanted to take a closer look. She walked up to the arrow and suddenly a voice shouted at her from behind, â€œBe careful not to touch it!â€ Annie jumped back in fright and saw an old man.

The old man said, â€œMy name is Wilbur and I was just minding my own business when I saw you walking towards the arrow. I was worried that you may get injured, so I shouted.â€
Annie smiled and said, â€œThank you Wilbur, I will mind your advice."
Wilbur smiled back and replied, â€œThatâ€™s very wise young lady. Now why donâ€™t we just run away and leave the arrow in peace?â€
And so, Annie and Wilbur ran away. Annie learned that even if you are nosy, it is important to follow the advice of others and mind what you are doing.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play outside and look at the sky. They see many white clouds in the blue sky. They try to guess what the clouds look like.

"Look, Anna, that cloud looks like a bunny!" Ben says, pointing at a fluffy cloud.

"I see it, Ben, it has long ears and a tail. And that cloud looks like a flower!" Anna says, pointing at another cloud.

They giggle and clap their hands. They see more clouds that look like animals, fruits, and toys. They have fun making up stories about the clouds.

But then, the wind blows hard and the clouds start to move. Some of the clouds get smaller and some get bigger. Some of the clouds join together and some separate.

"Oh no, the bunny cloud is gone!" Ben says, looking sad.

"And the flower cloud too!" Anna says, frowning.

They watch as the clouds change shape and color. They do not look like anything they know anymore.

"Maybe the clouds are playing too," Anna says, trying to cheer up Ben.

"Maybe they are," Ben says, nodding.

They decide to keep watching the clouds and see what they do next. They hope the clouds will make new shapes that they can guess. They hold hands and smile. They still like the clouds, even if they are different.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she decided to create a special dessert for her mom. She picked some cherries from the tree and mixed them with sugar and milk. Her mom was happy and said, "This is delicious, Lily! You are a great chef!"

CAT-SKIN

There was once a king, whose queen had hair of the purest gold, and was

so beautiful that her match was not to be met with on the whole face of

the earth. But this beautiful queen fell ill, and when she felt that her

end drew near she called the king to her and said, 'Promise me that you

will never marry again, unless you meet with a wife who is as beautiful

as I am, and who has golden hair like mine.' Then when the king in his

grief promised all she asked, she shut her eyes and died. But the king

was not to be comforted, and for a long time never thought of taking

another wife. At last, however, his wise men said, 'this will not do;

the king must marry again, that we may have a queen.' So messengers were

sent far and wide, to seek for a bride as beautiful as the late queen.

But there was no princess in the world so beautiful; and if there had

been, still there was not one to be found who had golden hair. So the

messengers came home, and had had all their trouble for nothing.

Now the king had a daughter, who was just as beautiful as her mother,

and had the same golden hair. And when she was grown up, the king looked

at her and saw that she was just like this late queen: then he said to

his courtiers, 'May I not marry my daughter? She is the very image of my

dead wife: unless I have her, I shall not find any bride upon the whole

earth, and you say there must be a queen.' When the courtiers heard this

they were shocked, and said, 'Heaven forbid that a father should marry

his daughter! Out of so great a sin no good can come.' And his daughter

was also shocked, but hoped the king would soon give up such thoughts;

so she said to him, 'Before I marry anyone I must have three dresses:

one must be of gold, like the sun; another must be of shining silver,

like the moon; and a third must be dazzling as the stars: besides this,

I want a mantle of a thousand different kinds of fur put together, to

which every beast in the kingdom must give a part of his skin.' And thus

she thought he would think of the matter no more. But the king made the

most skilful workmen in his kingdom weave the three dresses: one golden,

like the sun; another silvery, like the moon; and a third sparkling,

like the stars: and his hunters were told to hunt out all the beasts in

his kingdom, and to take the finest fur out of their skins: and thus a

mantle of a thousand furs was made.

When all were ready, the king sent them to her; but she got up in the

night when all were asleep, and took three of her trinkets, a golden

ring, a golden necklace, and a golden brooch, and packed the three

dresses--of the sun, the moon, and the stars--up in a nutshell, and

wrapped herself up in the mantle made of all sorts of fur, and besmeared

her face and hands with soot. Then she threw herself upon Heaven for

help in her need, and went away, and journeyed on the whole night, till

at last she came to a large wood. As she was very tired, she sat herself

down in the hollow of a tree and soon fell asleep: and there she slept

on till it was midday.

Now as the king to whom the wood belonged was hunting in it, his dogs

came to the tree, and began to snuff about, and run round and round, and

bark. 'Look sharp!' said the king to the huntsmen, 'and see what sort

of game lies there.' And the huntsmen went up to the tree, and when they

came back again said, 'In the hollow tree there lies a most wonderful

beast, such as we never saw before; its skin seems to be of a thousand

kinds of fur, but there it lies fast asleep.' 'See,' said the king, 'if

you can catch it alive, and we will take it with us.' So the huntsmen

took it up, and the maiden awoke and was greatly frightened, and said,

'I am a poor child that has neither father nor mother left; have pity on

me and take me with you.' Then they said, 'Yes, Miss Cat-skin, you will

do for the kitchen; you can sweep up the ashes, and do things of that

sort.' So they put her into the coach, and took her home to the king's

palace. Then they showed her a little corner under the staircase, where

no light of day ever peeped in, and said, 'Cat-skin, you may lie and

sleep there.' And she was sent into the kitchen, and made to fetch wood

and water, to blow the fire, pluck the poultry, pick the herbs, sift the

ashes, and do all the dirty work.

Thus Cat-skin lived for a long time very sorrowfully. 'Ah! pretty

princess!' thought she, 'what will now become of thee?' But it happened

one day that a feast was to be held in the king's castle, so she said to

the cook, 'May I go up a little while and see what is going on? I will

take care and stand behind the door.' And the cook said, 'Yes, you may

go, but be back again in half an hour's time, to rake out the ashes.'

Then she took her little lamp, and went into her cabin, and took off the

fur skin, and washed the soot from off her face and hands, so that her

beauty shone forth like the sun from behind the clouds. She next opened

her nutshell, and brought out of it the dress that shone like the sun,

and so went to the feast. Everyone made way for her, for nobody knew

her, and they thought she could be no less than a king's daughter. But

the king came up to her, and held out his hand and danced with her; and

he thought in his heart, 'I never saw any one half so beautiful.'

When the dance was at an end she curtsied; and when the king looked

round for her, she was gone, no one knew wither. The guards that stood

at the castle gate were called in: but they had seen no one. The truth

was, that she had run into her little cabin, pulled off her dress,

blackened her face and hands, put on the fur-skin cloak, and was

Cat-skin again. When she went into the kitchen to her work, and began

to rake the ashes, the cook said, 'Let that alone till the morning, and

heat the king's soup; I should like to run up now and give a peep: but

take care you don't let a hair fall into it, or you will run a chance of

never eating again.'

As soon as the cook went away, Cat-skin heated the king's soup, and

toasted a slice of bread first, as nicely as ever she could; and when it

was ready, she went and looked in the cabin for her little golden ring,

and put it into the dish in which the soup was. When the dance was over,

the king ordered his soup to be brought in; and it pleased him so well,

that he thought he had never tasted any so good before. At the bottom

he saw a gold ring lying; and as he could not make out how it had got

there, he ordered the cook to be sent for. The cook was frightened when

he heard the order, and said to Cat-skin, 'You must have let a hair fall

into the soup; if it be so, you will have a good beating.' Then he went

before the king, and he asked him who had cooked the soup. 'I did,'

answered the cook. But the king said, 'That is not true; it was better

done than you could do it.' Then he answered, 'To tell the truth I did

not cook it, but Cat-skin did.' 'Then let Cat-skin come up,' said the

king: and when she came he said to her, 'Who are you?' 'I am a poor

child,' said she, 'that has lost both father and mother.' 'How came you

in my palace?' asked he. 'I am good for nothing,' said she, 'but to be

scullion-girl, and to have boots and shoes thrown at my head.' 'But how

did you get the ring that was in the soup?' asked the king. Then she

would not own that she knew anything about the ring; so the king sent

her away again about her business.

After a time there was another feast, and Cat-skin asked the cook to let

her go up and see it as before. 'Yes,' said he, 'but come again in half

an hour, and cook the king the soup that he likes so much.' Then she

ran to her little cabin, washed herself quickly, and took her dress

out which was silvery as the moon, and put it on; and when she went in,

looking like a king's daughter, the king went up to her, and rejoiced at

seeing her again, and when the dance began he danced with her. After the

dance was at an end she managed to slip out, so slyly that the king did

not see where she was gone; but she sprang into her little cabin, and

made herself into Cat-skin again, and went into the kitchen to cook the

soup. Whilst the cook was above stairs, she got the golden necklace and

dropped it into the soup; then it was brought to the king, who ate it,

and it pleased him as well as before; so he sent for the cook, who

was again forced to tell him that Cat-skin had cooked it. Cat-skin was

brought again before the king, but she still told him that she was only

fit to have boots and shoes thrown at her head.

But when the king had ordered a feast to be got ready for the third

time, it happened just the same as before. 'You must be a witch,

Cat-skin,' said the cook; 'for you always put something into your soup,

so that it pleases the king better than mine.' However, he let her go up

as before. Then she put on her dress which sparkled like the stars, and

went into the ball-room in it; and the king danced with her again, and

thought she had never looked so beautiful as she did then. So whilst

he was dancing with her, he put a gold ring on her finger without her

seeing it, and ordered that the dance should be kept up a long time.

When it was at an end, he would have held her fast by the hand, but she

slipped away, and sprang so quickly through the crowd that he lost sight

of her: and she ran as fast as she could into her little cabin under

the stairs. But this time she kept away too long, and stayed beyond the

half-hour; so she had not time to take off her fine dress, and threw her

fur mantle over it, and in her haste did not blacken herself all over

with soot, but left one of her fingers white.

Then she ran into the kitchen, and cooked the king's soup; and as soon

as the cook was gone, she put the golden brooch into the dish. When the

king got to the bottom, he ordered Cat-skin to be called once more, and

soon saw the white finger, and the ring that he had put on it whilst

they were dancing: so he seized her hand, and kept fast hold of it, and

when she wanted to loose herself and spring away, the fur cloak fell off

a little on one side, and the starry dress sparkled underneath it.

Then he got hold of the fur and tore it off, and her golden hair and

beautiful form were seen, and she could no longer hide herself: so she

washed the soot and ashes from her face, and showed herself to be the

most beautiful princess upon the face of the earth. But the king said,

'You are my beloved bride, and we will never more be parted from each

other.' And the wedding feast was held, and a merry day it was, as ever

was heard of or seen in that country, or indeed in any other.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play with toys. They had a toy phone that could record their voices. They liked to pretend they were talking to each other or to other people.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big kite in the sky. It is red and yellow and has a long tail.

They see a man. He is walking in the field. He has a hat and a coat. He sees the kite. He catches it. He brings it to them.

"Okay, then," he says. "Let's go to my house. I have some tools and materials. We can fix the kite together. And then we can fly it again. How does that sound?"

"Good, good," Tom and Lily say. "Thank you, thank you."

They go with the man. They fix the kite. They fly it again. They are happy. The end.

And so Beth kept dancing, allowing her intelligence, joy and energy to fill the room.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Sammy. Sammy lived in a big oak tree with his family. One day, Sammy's mom told him they were going on a trip. "Sammy, we need to pack our things for our trip," said his mom.

Sammy was very excited and asked, "Where are we going?" His mom replied, "We are going to visit our cousins who live in a fancy tree. They have lots of acorns to share with us."

Sammy and his family packed their acorns and set off on their trip. When they arrived at their cousins' tree, Sammy was amazed. The tree was very fancy, with twinkling lights and colorful leaves. Sammy and his cousins played and shared their acorns together.

As the sun began to set, Sammy's mom said it was time to go back to their own tree. Sammy was sad to leave his cousins, but he knew he would see them again soon. He packed his things and said goodbye to his new friends. Sammy and his family returned home, happy and tired from their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little girl named Lily. She loved to play with cards and collect them. One day, she met a boy named Max who also liked cards. They became friends and played together every day.

One day, they found a special card that they both wanted. They started to quarrel about who would get it. Lily said, "I saw it first!" but Max said, "I want it more!" They argued and argued until they both got upset and went home.

The next day, Lily brought a surprise for Max. She gave him a shiny new card that she found. Max was happy and said, "Thank you, Lily! You are my best friend!" From then on, they shared their cards and never quarreled again.

John had a scooter. He was very alert and always like to watch what was going on around him. He was determined to be the first to try out his scooter.

One day, he decided to take it out for a ride. So he put on his helmet, jumped on the scooter and started to roll. He had a lot of fun rolling around the block. The wind blew in his hair and his face was filled with joy!

John kept rolling until he got to the park. But when he arrived, he saw that there were lots of other kids with scooters. He was a little scared, but he was still alert. He was determined to have a great time and show off his scooter riding skills.

John started to roll around the park and soon he was racing the other kids. He rolled faster and faster and kept up with the other kids. He was so excited by how fast he was going!

At the end of the day, John was tired but very happy. He had a lot of fun rolling around with his scooter and showing off his skills. He couldn't wait for the next time he could come out and roll around!

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Fido. He loved to play in the sun and feel the warm heat. Every day he would run around with his friends and enjoy being in the sunshine.

One day, Fido and his friends heard about a big hard hill. They all wanted to climb it. Fido said, "Let's go! I bet it will be fun to go up the hill."

So, they all started climbing the big hard hill. Fido was getting tired from going up so fast. But his friends were very brave and kept going.

Finally, they reached the top of the hill. They were so happy and enjoyed the view. They all laughed and hugged each other.

When it was time to go back down, Fido said, "Let's slide down the hill! That will be more fun." So, they all had a great time going down the hill, feeling the heat of the sun on their faces.

At the end of the day, Fido and his friends were all very tired but very happy. They had enjoyed their fun adventure!

Lily and Ben went to the park with Mom. They saw a big fountain with water that went up and down. Lily and Ben liked the fountain. They ran to it and tried to touch the water.

"Look, Mom, look!" Lily shouted. "The water is so pretty!"

Mom smiled and took a picture of them. "Be careful, don't get wet!" she said.

Then they saw a duck swimming in the fountain. The duck was yellow and brown. It had a long neck and a flat beak. Lily and Ben thought the duck was cute.

"Quack, quack!" the duck said.

"Hello, duck!" Lily and Ben said. They clapped their hands and waved to the duck.

The duck liked Lily and Ben. It swam closer to them and splashed some water with its wings.

Lily and Ben laughed and clapped some more. They had fun with the duck and the fountain. Mom was happy to see them. She gave them a hug and a snack. They thanked the duck and said goodbye. They had a good day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a big hurricane. The wind was blowing very hard and the rain was pouring down. A little girl named Lily was scared and asked her mom, "What's happening?"

Her mom replied, "There's a big storm outside. But don't worry, we're safe inside our house."

Suddenly, the power went out and it was very dark. But then, the lightning revealed a surprise. Lily's mom had lit candles all around the room, making it feel cozy and warm. Lily smiled and said, "I like the candles. They make me feel safe."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm glad. Sometimes, even in the midst of a scary storm, we can find something beautiful and comforting."

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and excited about studying.

One day she was playing with a bubble. She watched it closely and studied how it floated in the air, wide and round. "This bubble is so pretty," she said.

Suddenly, the bubble floated away. The girl ran after it to try and catch it. It was so wide and she couldn't catch up. Suddenly the wind picked up and the bubble flew away.

The little girl was sad and started to cry. But then, she saw a rainbow in the sky. She smiled and studied it closely. She thought she could reach the rainbow if she flew on the back of a bird.

The end.

Once upon a time, two good friends named Jack and Jill lived together. They liked to do lots of fun things together. One day, they went to the park together.

At the park, they saw lots of people playing a game. It looked like lots of fun so Jack and Jill asked them what they were playing. The people told them it was called tag. Jack asked, "Can we play too?" The people said yes, so Jack and Jill started playing tag.

At first, Jack was very good at the game and he would tag Jill every day. Jill was beginning to feel a bit jealous. She said to Jack, "Why do you always tag me?" Jack replied, "Because you're the fastest one here so it's easy for me to catch you. That's why I tag you." Jill smiled.

Everyday, Jack and Jill would play tag and Jack would repeatly tag Jill. Jack and Jill were having lots of fun together and also became best friends. They played tag every day until they grew old.

Once upon a time, there was a wild sugar. It was so sweet that even the birds wanted to eat it. But the sugar would not budge. All it did all day was sleep.

One day a little boy came along. He had three years, and was very brave. He wanted to wake up the sugar.

So he shook it and shouted. But nothing happened. The sugar was still sleeping. So the boy took some water and sprinkled it on the sugar.

Suddenly, the wild sugar woke up! It was so happy and jumped around. Then it ran away and disappeared. The little boy was so excited but all he could do was watch as the wild sugar scampered away.
The next day, the little boy went back to the spot he had seen the wild sugar, and found a sweet treat waiting for him! The wild sugar had left a surprise for him - a little sugary treat.

Once upon a time, there was a foolish boy who wanted to fly a helicopter. He set about building one. He collected some pieces and tried to piece them together. But he couldn't make it work.

He kept trying and eventually the foolish boy thought he'd made it work. So he set off to fly the helicopter. But it still wasn't working! He flew too high up into the sky.

The foolish boy was stuck and he couldn't get down. After a while, he ran out of energy and tumbled to the ground. He wasn't hurt, but he was stuck there. Nobody could help him get back up.

The foolish boy learned his lesson and he never tried to fly a helicopter again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing games with his daddy. They played all kinds of games together like hide and seek, tag, and catch. Timmy's daddy was very competitive and always wanted to win.

One day, Timmy and his daddy went to the park to play. They brought a special game that Timmy's daddy had made. It was a surprise for Timmy. Daddy told Timmy that they were going to play a game where they had to open a special box. Timmy was very excited to play.

Daddy and Timmy started playing the game. Daddy was very competitive and tried his best to open the box before Timmy. But Timmy was very clever and opened the box first! Inside the box was a special prize for Timmy. Daddy was very happy for Timmy and they both laughed and played together for the rest of the day. Timmy learned that sometimes it's not about winning, but about having fun with your daddy.

Once upon a time, there was a queen who lived in a big castle. She loved to paint pictures of flowers and birds. One day, she was feeling anxious because she couldn't find her favorite paintbrush. She looked everywhere but it was nowhere to be found.

The queen asked her helpers to help her find the paintbrush. They looked in the garden, in the kitchen, and even in the stable, but they couldn't find it. The queen was getting more and more anxious because she wanted to finish her painting.

Just when the queen was about to give up, she saw her little dog running towards her with the missing paintbrush in its mouth. The queen was so happy that she hugged her dog and started to paint right away. She finished her painting and it was the most beautiful picture she had ever painted. The end.

Mia had a birthday. She was very excited. She wanted to see what was inside the present. But it was hard to open. She tried hard to open the package. Finally it opened. She saw a blue bike! She was so happy she jumped up and down. She ran to show her mom and dad. They said it was the best birthday present ever. Mia went outside and rode her bike. She had so much fun. She said it was the best birthday ever.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. Sometimes they share, but sometimes they fight. One day, they both want the same red car. They pull and tug and yell.

"Mine!" Anna says.

"No, mine!" Ben says.

They are so loud that Mom comes in. She looks sad and angry.

"Stop it, you two!" Mom says. "Why are you fighting over a toy? You have so many toys. Can't you be nice to each other?"

Anna and Ben stop and look at Mom. They realize that they are making Mom unhappy. They also realize that they love each other more than the red car. They feel sorry.

"Sorry, Mom," Anna says.

"Sorry, Mom," Ben says.

They hug Mom and then hug each other. They decide to take turns with the red car. They also find other toys to play with together. They laugh and smile and have fun.

Mom smiles too. She is glad that Anna and Ben are getting along. She says, "That's better. Now you are being good twins. I love you both very much."

Anna and Ben say, "We love you too, Mom."

They play in peace until it is time for dinner. They see the bright sun shining through the window. They think it is a beautiful day.

Once upon a time there was a young man who was ready for his journey. He had all his luggage packed, and he was set to go. He had never imagined that he would find himself kneeling in front of the door with tears in his eyes.

He knocked on the door and the door opened. His love stood in front of him, with a sad look on her face.

â€œWhy are you here?â€ she asked.

He had never expected this would be their last meeting. â€œI just wanted to say goodbye," he said, his voice shaking.

She hugged him. â€œI canâ€™t stop you from going,â€ she said.

He nodded and stepped away. She knew he had to go, but it still hurt. He took one last look at her and kneeled on the ground.

The young man never came back. His love waited for him for a long time, but he never returned. He was gone and her heart was broken.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit. The rabbit was very hot. He wanted to find a cool place. So, he went to a river. He saw some birds singing. The rabbit sang with them. He felt happy and cool. The end.

Jill and Ben like to play in the park. They see a big slide and run to it. Jill goes first. She climbs up the steps and sits on the slide. She slides down fast and laughs. Ben follows her. He slides down too and smiles.

They see a man with a big pink balloon. The balloon is filled with gas. The man gives the balloon to Jill and Ben. They say thank you and hold the balloon. The balloon is light and floats in the air.

They want to play with the balloon. They try to balance the balloon on their heads, their hands, and their feet. They giggle and have fun. But the wind is strong. It blows the balloon away from them. They chase the balloon. They run and jump and try to catch it.

But the balloon flies higher and higher. It goes over the trees and the houses. Jill and Ben can't reach it. They stop and look at the balloon. They feel sad. They lose their balloon.

They go back to the slide. They slide down again and again. They forget about the balloon. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his ball in the park. One day, he saw a big, impressive tree. He wanted to become friends with the tree, so he went closer.

Spot had a question for the tree. He asked, "Can we be friends?" The tree didn't say anything, but Spot knew the tree liked him. They played together all day, and Spot was very happy.

Every day, Spot and the tree played together. They became best friends. The other dogs and kids in the park thought it was fun to play with Spot and the tree too. And they all lived happily ever after.

Tim and his mom were in the store. Tim saw a great pair of pants. He asked his mom if he could get them. His mom said, "Yes, those look great on you."

Tim was so excited. He put them on and hopped up and down saying, "Look, Mommy, look how I stand in them!" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, you look very handsome in those pants. Great job!"

Tim was so proud of himself. He asked one more time if he could keep the pants. His mom said, "Yes, let's get them. You look super sharp in them!"

Tim was so happy. He said, "I love my new pants!"

His mom said, "I'm glad you love them. They look great on you!"

Tim was the happiest he had ever been. Now he had a great pair of pants to show off to his friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to push things. She liked to push her toys, her brother and even her mom. She would push them when she was playing and when she was mad. But when she tried to push too much, mom would not let her.

One day the little girl was feeling so restless that she needed to push something. So she went outside and she pushed her swing as hard as she could. But the swing didn't move. Then the little girl thought of a new style. She decided to jump onto the swing and push it with her feet.

It worked! The swing started moving, higher and higher. The little girl had a lot of fun, pushing and swinging until she got tired. Then she had to stop, but she knew that she could push the swing again the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a bird that lived in the sky. Its feathers were soft, and its wings were strong. The bird liked to soar through the sky, feeling the wind and the sun's warmth on its wings.

One day the bird saw something wonderful. On the ground below it there was a meadow full of beautiful flowers and small animals. The bird wanted to find out more about this new life on the ground, so it flew down to take a closer look.

The bird was amazed at what it saw. The animals ran around, and the flowers seemed to be very happy. The bird knew that it wanted to stay in this new place and experience the beauty of life.

The bird spent all day in the meadow, and when it was time for it to leave, it was feeling very sleepy. With big, slow wingbeats, the bird rose up into the sky, and the meadow disappeared from view.

The bird's life had changed. From then on it was not just soaring, but experiencing life from both the sky and the ground.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old and loved playing outside. She was always looking for something exciting to do!

One day, Sarah saw something unusual in the nearby park. It was a big machine with lots of colored lights on it. She was curious and decided to investigate.

As Sarah got closer to the machine, she saw something amazing. It had a big red button on the front! She was curious and pushed the button.

Suddenly, the machine started to make loud noises and shake really hard. The lights on the machine were flashing and it moved high up into the air! Sarah screamed with excitement and joy.

After a few minutes, the machine stopped shaking and slowly lowered back down to the ground. Sarah was so happy to have had this amazing experience. She went back home with a huge smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who was very brave. She wanted to explore the world, so she set off on an adventure. On her journey, she came across a big, messy castle. She was a bit scared, but then she saw a friendly face peeking out of the window - it was a dragon!

The dragon invited her in and she nodded her head. The inside of the castle was even more messy than outside, but the dragon looked kind. He told her, â€œI have been in pain for a very long time. Would you help me?â€

The princess was frightened, but she nodded her head. They worked together to clean up the mess, and bit by bit the castle became shiny and sparkly. The dragon felt better, and the princess was happy.

She thanked the dragon for helping her on her adventure and set off on the next leg of her journey. She remembered the lessons she had learnt from the dragon, and with a nod of her head, she was off!

Once there was a little girl named Lily. She was three years old and loved to go fast. Today, she had on her favorite shirt - a white one with a big red heart on it.

Lily was playing outside when she suddenly spotted her best friend, James. He was running really fast and didn't even see her. Lily wanted to speed like James, so she took off after him.

Lily ran really fast, but she couldn't catch up. She began to get upset and tears started to roll down her cheeks. Suddenly, James stopped and turned around.

He said "Hi Lily, you were going so fast I didn't even see you!" Lily smiled and wiped away her tears. She said, "I tried to speed like you, but I couldn't keep up!"

James laughed and said, "Let's race! I'll go slow so you can keep up!" Lily smiled, and the two raced. It was so much fun!

At the end of the race, Lily was so proud of herself. She had sped enough to keep up with James and won the race!

Leo was a little lion who loved to roar. He roared when he woke up, he roared when he played, and he roared when he was hungry. He roared so loud that all the animals in the jungle heard him.

One day, Leo was roaring near a big tree. He saw a bird with bright feathers on a branch. He wanted to play with the bird, so he roared at it. But the bird was scared of Leo's roar and flew away.

"Come back, bird! I want to be your friend!" Leo shouted.

But the bird did not come back. Leo felt sad and lonely. He wished he had a friend who liked his roar.

Then he heard a noise in the bushes. He saw a little monkey with a long tail. The monkey was curious about Leo and came closer.

"Hello, lion. What are you doing?" the monkey asked.

"I'm looking for a friend who likes my roar. Do you like my roar?" Leo asked.

The monkey nodded. "Yes, I like your roar. It sounds strong and brave. Can I hear it again?"

Leo smiled and roared as loud as he could. The monkey clapped his hands and cheered.

"Wow, that was a great roar! You are a hero, lion!" the monkey said.

Leo felt happy and proud. He had found a friend who liked his roar.

"Thank you, monkey. You are very patient and kind. Do you want to play with me?" Leo asked.

The monkey nodded again. "Yes, I want to play with you. You are fun and friendly. What do you want to play?"

Leo thought for a moment. Then he had an idea.

"Let's play hide and seek. I will count to ten and you hide. Then I will find you with my roar. OK?"

The monkey agreed. He ran to find a hiding spot. Leo closed his eyes and counted to ten. Then he opened his eyes and roared.

"Ready or not, here I come!" he said.

He followed his roar to find his friend. They played hide and seek for a long time. They had a lot of fun. They became the best of friends. They roared and laughed together. Leo was happy. He had learned that his roar was not scary, but special. And he had learned that a friend who likes you for who you are is a true hero.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She was 3 years old and liked to explore. One day Lucy was walking in the park and looking around. She saw an olive. It was a big, round, green olive. Lucy thought it was interesting so she picked it up.

When she looked closer, she saw that the olive was not completely green. It had a bit of pink on it. She was really excited. She thought it looked like a special kind of olive.

Lucy wanted to show her mom, so she went home. When she got home she showed her mom what she had found. She was really proud of her special olive.

The next day, Lucy took the olive back to the park. She wanted more children to see her special, pink olive.

From that day on, Lucy always looked for other special olives when she was out exploring.

Once upon a time, there was a boat. It was empty but the sea was nice and blue.

One day, a little girl got on the boat. She was so happy to be sailing and saw the world around her. Suddenly, the sky changed from blue to grey. Storm clouds were forming and the sea started to move.

The little girl was scared, but she stayed in the boat. It started bouncing up and down and she could feel the wind. The waves got bigger and bigger and the boat continued to rock.

Finally, the storm passed and the little girl was relieved. The sea turned back to blue and she was safe. Now, the boat was not empty anymore: the little girl was inside and the adventure had just begun!

Once upon a time there was a car. The car was old and rusty. One day it got so rusty that it rot. The car was sad and angry.

The car said to a nearby tree, "This is so stupid! I don't want to rot!"

The tree said, "But that's how cars get when they're old. You need to accept it."

The car replied, "No! I wish I could still drive around like I used to."

The tree shook its leaves sadly. "I know. But life isn't always fair. You will just have to rot and accept your fate."

And that's how the car learned to accept its fate and rot away in peace.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a humble girl named Lily. She loved to give and help others. One day, she saw an old lady who looked sad.

Lily went to the lady and said, "Why are you sad?" The old lady said, "I am hungry, and I have no food." Lily wanted to help her, so she ran home to get some food.

Lily put some food on a plate and went back to the old lady. She gave the plate to the lady and said, "Here, eat this." The old lady smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind."

The old lady was happy, and Lily felt good that she could help. From that day on, Lily always looked for ways to help others and share what she had. And everyone in the town loved the humble girl who loved to give.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She was excited to play on the swings and slide. When they arrived, Lily saw a lot of leaves on the ground. She picked up a red leaf and showed it to her mom. "Look mommy, pretty leaf!" she said.

As Lily played, she saw a boy who was crying. She went up to him and asked, "Why are you crying?" The boy replied, "I lost my toy car." Lily said, "Don't worry, we will help you find it." They looked around and finally found the toy car under a pile of leaves. The boy was happy and said, "Thank you, Lily!"

As they were leaving the park, Lily's mom asked her if she had fun. Lily replied, "Yes, but I heard some people complain about the leaves. I like the leaves, they are pretty." Her mom smiled and said, "I like the leaves too, Lily."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. Jack wanted to play with his ball, but it was stuck on the roof. Jack felt sad because he couldn't get his ball.

Then, Jack saw his friend Lily walking by. Jack asked Lily to help him get his ball. Lily said yes and together they got a ladder. Lily climbed up the ladder and passed the ball down to Jack. Jack was happy and thanked Lily for her help.

Lily smiled and said it was fair to help friends in need. Jack agreed and they played together with the ball. The end.

Sara liked to fold paper. She could make many shapes with paper. She could make a hat, a boat, a bird, and a star. She was proud of her paper shapes. She showed them to her mom and dad. They smiled and clapped.

One day, Sara had a new baby brother. His name was Ben. Sara wanted to show Ben her paper shapes. She went to his crib with a paper hat. She put the hat on his head. But Ben did not like the hat. He cried and kicked. He tore the hat with his hands. Sara was sad and angry. She said, "Ben is rude! He broke my hat!"

Mom heard Sara and Ben. She came to the crib. She saw the torn hat and the crying baby. She said, "Sara, Ben is just an infant. He does not know how to play with paper. He did not mean to be rude. He was scared of the hat. You have to be gentle and patient with him. He will learn to like your paper shapes when he is older."

Sara felt sorry for Ben. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I did not want to scare you. I wanted to share my hat with you." She gave him a hug and a kiss. She took another paper and folded a boat. She said, "Look, Ben. This is a boat. It can float on water. Do you want to see?" Ben stopped crying and looked at the boat. He smiled and reached for it. Sara smiled too. She said, "Maybe Ben is not so rude after all. Maybe he is just curious." Mom smiled and said, "That's right, Sara. You are a good big sister. You can teach Ben many things with your paper shapes." Sara and Ben played with the paper boat. They were happy.

One day, Bob was sitting on the floor playing with his toy truck. He saw a small cop outside his window. He went to the window and waved. The cop waved back and then knocked on the door.

Bob opened the door and the cop asked if he would like to share his toy truck. Bob smiled and said yes. The cop asked if he had any other toys and Bob showed her his collection.

The cop liked what she saw, so she gave Bob a small toy car in return for sharing his truck. Bob was so excited and thanked the cop. He gave the truck to the cop and she waved goodbye. Bob ran inside to show his parents the toy car. They were so proud of him for sharing his toys.

Bob learned an important lesson that day - that sharing truly is a wonderful thing!

One day a nice princess was walking in the forest. She noticed a big tree with lots of shiny apples. She wanted to pick the apples and add them to her basket.

The princess said to the tree, â€œPlease, may I add some of your apples to my basket?â€

The tree said, â€œYes, you may take five apples, but please do not take too many. Itâ€™s important to be nice to the trees!â€

So the princess only added five apples to her basket and thanked the tree. Then she went on her way, feeling nice and happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Daisy. She liked to do yoga. One day, her mom suggested that she take a serious yoga class. So Daisy found a seat in the classroom and listened to the teacher.

The teacher said, "Tonight, we will start with a very serious yoga pose. It's very tricky and it takes lots of practice." Daisy thought it sounded fun, so she eagerly nodded her head.

But then, Daisy started to think: what if she couldn't do this tricky yoga pose? Would she still be able to do yoga? Daisy was getting more and more worried, so she asked her teacher what would happen.

The teacher replied, "If you don't get this pose right, then you can't do yoga anymore." Daisy was sad and scared, but she tried her best. Unfortunately, Daisy couldn't do the pose and her teacher said she would have to leave the class.

And they all lived sadly ever after.

Once there was a girl called Jane. She was very polite and kind. One day, she wanted to help her Mom in the kitchen.

She went to the cupboard and found a plate. She was so excited and carried it to the kitchen table.

Suddenly, Jane heard her Mom calling her, "Jane honey, could you be a polite girl and carry the plate to the dining room?"

Jane smiled and said, "Yes Mommy, I can do that". She neatly carried the plate to the dining room, and put it on the table.

Jane's Mom hugged her and said, "Thank you sweetheart, you are such a good girl!" Jane was so pleased and could not stop smiling.

Jimmy was a three-year-old boy with a lot of energy. He loved to go outside and play in his backyard. Whenever he was there, he loved to swing on the swingset.

One day, Mommy came outside with a bottle for him to play with. Jimmy was very excited and he quickly grabbed it. He looked at it and said, "Mommy, this bottle is so interesting!"

Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it is! What do you want to do with it?" Jimmy thought for a moment and then said, "I want to swing with it!"

Mommy smiled again and said, "Okay, let's swing. Hold onto the bottle tight and have fun!" Jimmy held the bottle tight and began to swing. He was laughing and smiling the whole time.

When it was time to go inside, Mommy asked, "Did you have fun swinging with the bottle, Jimmy?"

Jimmy smiled and said, "It was the best day ever!"

George was very excited. He was going to the park with his mom. He grabbed a key and skipped to the door. He wanted to open it on his own. He tried the key in the door, but it wouldn't turn. He tugged and tugged, but nothing happened. Suddenly, the key snapped! George was ashamed. He started to tear.

Mommy came over and said "It's ok, George. We can use my key instead." She put the broken key in her pocket. She hugged George and wiped away his tears.

George was still ashamed, but he felt better. Mommy opened the door with her key, and the two of them went to the park. They had a wonderful time playing games and eating ice cream. Before the day was over, George had forgotten all about the broken key.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cookies more than anything in the world. One day, Lily's mom made some cookies for her, but she couldn't find them anywhere. She looked under the bed, in the closet, and even in the toy box, but the cookies were nowhere to be found.

Lily was sad and started to cry. Her mom saw her crying and asked what was wrong. Lily told her that she couldn't find her cookies. Her mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, I'll help you find them." They looked everywhere together, but the cookies were still distant.

Finally, they found the cookies in the kitchen on the counter. Lily was so happy that she hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for helping me find my cookies!" From that day on, Lily learned to always ask for help when she couldn't find something.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy lived in a tunnel under the ground. He loved to play with his friends and eat cheese.

One day, Timmy and his friends were playing when they heard a loud noise. It was a big fair coming to town! Timmy had never been to a fair before, so he was very excited.

But when they got there, it was very crowded and noisy. Timmy felt scared and wanted to go back to his tunnel. His friends tried to help him settle down and enjoy the fair, but he just couldn't.

Finally, they decided to go on a ride that went through a tunnel. Timmy loved it! The ride was so much fun and he felt safe in the dark tunnel. From then on, Timmy wasn't scared of fairs anymore and he couldn't wait to go on more rides.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to go camping with his family. One day, Timmy and his family went to a campsite near the woods. They set up a tent and made a fire to cook their dinner.

Timmy's dad said, "Timmy, be careful around the fire. It can burn you." Timmy nodded his head and said, "I will be careful, Dad."

After dinner, Timmy and his family went for a walk in the woods. They saw a big, clear lake and decided to go for a swim. Timmy splashed around in the water and had so much fun.

Later that night, they went back to their tent and sat around the fire. Timmy's mom said, "It's getting late, we should go to bed." Timmy said, "I don't want to go to bed, I want to stay up and watch the fire burn." His dad replied, "Okay, but only for a little while." Timmy watched the fire burn until he fell asleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. One day, Jack was helping his mom do the chores and he was given a special job. His mom said, "Jack, I need you to find the hidden leak in the kitchen and clean it up".

Jack was excited to help his mom. He went to the kitchen and searched high and low, but he couldn't find the leak anywhere. He went to his mom and said, "Mommy, I can't find the leak". His mom smiled and said, "Look behind the curtains, Jack. That's usually where it's hiding".

Jack looked behind the curtains and sure enough, he found the leak. He quickly got a rag and cleaned up the mess. His mom thanked him for doing such a good job, and gave him a hug. Jack was very happy to have helped his mom.

The sun was shining on the beautiful lake. A family was out for a picnic. They laughed and played together and it was a perfect day.

The little boy was so excited. He wanted to explore the lake. So he asked his dad if he could get in and go for a swim. His dad said yes, so he splashed into the water.

The water was so cool and the little boy was having so much fun. He paddled and floated around, exploring the lake.

After some time, the little boy became very tired, so he decided to get out of the lake. All of a sudden, he was surprised to find his dad had brought a boat and he knew just what his dad had planned. They set off in the boat, moving slowly and peacefully across the lake, soaking in its beautiful surroundings.

The family sailed around the lake until the sun began to set and the stars came out. It was a perfect way to end their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a famous dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his favorite toy, a ball. One day, Spot's ball broke. He was very sad.

Spot's friend, a cat named Kitty, had an idea. She found some tape to fix the ball. Kitty put the tape on the ball and made it all better. Spot was so happy!

Now, Spot and Kitty played with the ball all day. They would cover their eyes and try to find the ball. They had lots of fun and laughed a lot. And they were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Max and Ben. They were very happy and they always played together.

One day, they wanted to perform a very special show. Max thought it would be fun to make a sandwich to share with the audience during the show. So they raced to the kitchen to make one.

But they soon got very frustrated because they couldn't figure out how to make the sandwich. Max kept putting way too much pepper on it and Ben kept messing up the cheese.

Finally, after a few tries, they managed to make a delicious sandwich together. Everyone was very happy, Max and Ben performed a wonderful show and everyone was treated to a yummy sandwich!
