Once upon a time, there was a parrot named Polly. Polly was very healthy because she ate lots of fruits and veggies. One day, Polly saw a man who wanted to buy her. The man said, "I want to take you home with me, Polly. You can be my pet." Polly didn't want to go with the man, so she signed with her wings and said, "No, thank you. I like living here in the jungle with my friends." The man was sad, but he understood what Polly wanted. From that day on, Polly lived happily in the jungle with her friends, eating healthy foods and signing with her wings whenever someone wanted to take her away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toy models. She had a model of a car, a plane, and a boat. She loved to keep them in her room and play with them every day.

One day, Lily's little brother came into her room and started playing with her models. Lily didn't like that because she wanted to keep them all to herself. She told her brother to stop, but he wouldn't listen.

Lily's mom came into the room and saw what was happening. She told Lily's brother to stop playing with the models and to be more independent by finding his own toys to play with. Lily was happy that her mom helped her keep her models safe and sound. From that day on, Lily and her brother played with their own toys and were independent in their playtime. The end.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to pretend that they were tiny and their toys were big. They used a frame from a picture to make a door for their toy house.

"Knock, knock," Ben said, tapping on the frame. "Can I come in?"

"Of course, you can," Lily said, opening the frame. "You are very polite. Do you want some tea?"

"Yes, please," Ben said, sitting on a cushion. Lily poured some water from a bottle cap into a thimble. They pretended to sip their tea and chat.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was their mom, coming home from work. She saw the frame on the floor and picked it up.

"Oh, what a nice frame," she said. "I wonder where it came from. I think I'll hang it on the wall."

She did not see Ben and Lily inside the frame. They were too small. They shouted and waved, but their mom did not hear them.

"Help, help!" Ben cried. "We are in the frame!"

"How did we shrink?" Lily asked. "We need to get out!"

They looked around and saw a window in the frame. They ran to it and pushed it open. They saw a bird outside. They hoped it would not eat them.

"Maybe we can fly with the bird," Ben said. "Maybe it will take us to our mom."

They climbed on the bird's back and held on tight. The bird flew away with them. They hoped it would not fly too far. They wanted to go back to their mom and their toys. They wanted to be big again.

Lily and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat something yummy. They went to the kitchen and looked at the fridge. The fridge was big and cold. It had a lot of food inside.

"Can we open the fridge?" Lily asked Ben.

"Yes, we can. But we need to ask Mom first," Ben said. He was a good big brother. He knew the rules.

They ran to the living room, where Mom was reading a book. She looked comfortable on the sofa.

"Mom, can we have a snack?" they asked together.

"Sure, my loves. What do you want?" Mom said with a smile.

"We want to open the fridge and see what's inside," Lily said.

"Okay, but be careful. And don't make a mess," Mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded and ran back to the kitchen. They opened the fridge and saw many things. They saw milk, cheese, eggs, fruit, juice, and more. They decided to have some cheese and crackers. They took them out of the fridge and put them on a plate.

"Can you help me, Ben?" Lily asked. She was too small to reach the cupboard where the crackers were.

"Of course, Lily. I'll help you," Ben said. He lifted Lily up and helped her get the crackers. They put them on the plate with the cheese.

They carried the plate to the table and sat down. They ate their snack and enjoyed it. They were happy and full.

"Thank you for helping me, Ben," Lily said.

"You're welcome, Lily. You're my best sister," Ben said.

They hugged each other and smiled. They loved each other very much.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Emily. She liked to dance and jump around, especially when she was feeling happy. One day, Emily stumbled across a gray memory. She wasn't quite sure what it was, but it made her curious.

"What's that?" Emily said as she pointed to the gray memory.

Her mom came over and said, "These are memories, darling. They are special moments that we can keep forever." Emily nodded, understanding.

That evening, Emily decided to make the gray memory her own. She danced around it, swirling in circles and stomping her feet. She was so happy to have her very own memory. Emily joyfully spun around and around until the night sky began to come alive with stars.

As the stars shined, Emily felt as if the gray memory had come to life. She knew then that she would always remember that special moment and she would always be able to choose to dance and be happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pocket in her dress where she kept her favorite toys. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. While playing, she found a shiny rock on the ground. She picked it up and put it in her pocket, thinking it was special.

When she got home, she showed her mom the rock. Her mom told her that it was just a regular rock, but Lily still thought it was valuable. She kept the rock in her pocket and took it with her everywhere she went, even though it was very light.

One day, Lily's little brother wanted to play with the rock. Lily told him how much she valued it and that she didn't want him to lose it. Her brother promised to take good care of it, and Lily let him play with it. From that day on, Lily and her brother shared the rock and both thought it was very special.

One day, Emma was very excited for something special. She grabbed a big box of crayons with every color imaginable! She was so excited she could hardly wait.

Emma had a reliable friend who was always willing to help, so she asked for help to open the box of crayons. Together, they opened the box and all the colors were just as bright and vivid as she had imagined.

With her crayons in hand, Emma couldn't wait to start drawing. She wanted to draw a beautiful rainbow with all of the colors of the crayons. So, she started drawing and the colors were so perfect!

When Emma was finished, she was amazed by her art and so proud of herself. She excitedly showed her mom and dad and they thought it was the most beautiful picture they had ever seen.

Emma was so proud of her work and it excited her to create something that was so beautiful with her crayons!

Once upon a time, there was a lonely monkey living in a jungle. Every day, he would hop from tree to tree in search of a friend, but never did he find one. He felt so alone.

One day, as he was swinging from a vine, a monkey revealed himself from behind a bush. He said, â€œHi! Iâ€™m Bob. Whatâ€™s your name?â€ The lonely monkey was so happy. â€œMy name is Tim!â€, he said with a smile.

From then on, Tim and Bob were the best of friends. They would always play together, hopping from vine to vine, and never would they ever be lonely again. And they lived happily ever after!

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to swing, slide and run on the grass. They saw some other kids with masks on their faces. They wondered why they had masks.

"Mom, why do they have masks?" Lily asked.

"Because there is a bad germ that can make people sick. The masks help to keep the germ away," mom said.

"Can we have masks too?" Ben asked.

"Sure, I have some in my bag. But you have to wear them all the time when we are outside, okay?" mom said.

She gave them each a mask and helped them put it on. Lily and Ben felt funny with the masks. They could not see their noses and mouths. They could not breathe as well. They could not smile or talk as loud.

They tried to play with the masks, but they did not like them. They wanted to take them off.

"Mom, can we take off the masks?" Lily asked.

"No, sweetie, you have to keep them on. It is for your safety and for others too," mom said.

"But they are not fun. They are itchy and hot and hard to breathe," Ben said.

"I know, honey, but you have to resist the urge to take them off. It is only for a little while. Then we can go home and take them off and have some ice cream," mom said.

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They liked ice cream. They wanted to go home. They decided to listen to mom and keep the masks on. They hoped the bad germ would go away soon. They wanted to play without masks. They wanted to see their friends' faces. They wanted to be happy.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Lucy. One day, Lucy was feeling very sad. She wanted to fly away so she could be happy but she was too young.

Then, a bright flame appeared in the sky. She was scared at first, but then she saw that the flame was made of magic.

Lucy asked the flame, "Can you let me fly away so I can be happy again?"

The flame answered, "Yes, I can permit you to fly away but first you must promise to take care of your family."

Lucy smiled and said, "I will certainly take care of them. Please let me fly away!"

The flame permitted Lucy to spread her arms and fly away into the night. She felt happy, free and no longer sad. Lucy waved goodbye to the flame and continued with her adventures.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends called Tom and Jim. Every morning they would rush to the park together and have lots of fun.

Every day they would play catch with a ball, or look at the sky and pick out shapes in the clouds. But today something was different.

Tom's dad had taken him to the art gallery the day before and he had seen the most incredible picture.

He asked Jim if they could go back to the art gallery the next morning, forgetting that his dad had only brought him there once. Jim was confused, but he said okay anyway.

The next morning they both rushed to the art gallery, so excited to see Tom's incredible picture. But when they got there, the picture was gone.

All that was left were two frames that were empty. Tom was very sad, but Jim smiled and said, "I'm sure we will find it again one day".

Tom smiled too and the two of them rushed off to the park to play. They knew that wherever it was, the incredible picture was waiting for them.

Once upon a time there was a goat named Sam. Sam was a funny goat with a big, round head and long ears. He lived on a farm with his friends.

Every day, Sam would play near the river. One day, when Sam was at the river, he saw a big wave. It was so big and smooth! Sam loved it and wanted to see it again.

Sam thought and thought and came up with an idea. He decided to try to balance on his two hooves and see the wave again. He hopped up and down, up and down and slowly built up his balance.

Finally, after a few tries, the wave appeared from around the corner and Sam saw it! He was so excited!

"Hooray! I found it!", he said with a loud, happy voice.

His friends heard him and came running to join Sam and his big, smooth wave.

They all had the best time jumping, playing and balancing together next to the wave!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went for a walk in the park with her mommy. They saw lots of lovely flowers and trees.

Lily said, "Mommy, look at the pretty flowers! I see pink ones and yellow ones and purple ones too!"

Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, they are very lovely. Let's walk a bit more and see what else we can find."

As they walked, Lily saw a big dog with a wagging tail. She said, "Mommy, can we pet the doggy?"

Mommy replied, "Let's ask the owner first." The owner said it was okay and Lily petted the doggy. It was a very nice walk in the park!

Once upon a time, there was a leopard named Smith. Smith liked to complain about his life all the time. Every morning, he would complain about how he didn't have money or friends.

One day, Smith saw a fast cheetah running in the savannah. Smith was astonished at how fast the cheetah was. He started to complain to a nearby monkey.

"This cheetah is so fast,â€ Smith said. â€œIt's not fair!â€

The monkey replied, "No one said life is fair, Smith. Maybe you should try running - it can help you feel better."

Smith thought about this and decided to give it a try. He started running every morning. With practice, he soon became faster and faster.

One day he ran so fast, he beat the cheetah. He was so proud and happy! Smith no longer complained about his life, because he was having so much fun.

Once upon a time, Jack wanted to learn. He knew he had to go to school to do that, but he was scared. He asked his mom, "Will school help me learn?"

"Yes, Jack," his mom said. "School is a safe and reliable place for you to learn."

So Jack went to school. He was nervous at first, but gradually he started learning things. He learned how to count, how to write his name and how to draw a picture. Jack even made some new friends along the way.

Before long Jack wasn't scared of school anymore. He looked forward to going each day because he knew that school was a reliable place where he could learn new things.

Once upon a time there was a fox who loved to swing. The fox could be seen in the park each day, enjoying the feel of the wind blowing in its fur.

One day, a bad wolf appeared and said, "Hey Fox, why are you here all alone?"

The fox said, "I'm here to swing. Don't you like to swing too?"

The wolf shook its head and said, "No, I don't like to swing. I like to eat foxes like you! Get ready! I'm coming to get you!"

But the fox was clever and knew that the wolf was trying to trick him. "No! I like to swing and you don't scare me!" shouted the fox.

The wolf ran away and the fox went back to having fun, safely swinging in the park. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a smart bull. He was a very special bull, because he could do things that no other bulls could do. He could write his name and spell words.

Every day, the smart bull would go to a field to play. He would take his friends with him and they would run around and have fun.

One day, the smart bull and his friends were playing tag. The bull was going so fast that he ran straight through a fence and into a farmer's garden.

The farmer saw the smart bull in his garden, and was very angry. He chased after the bull, trying to catch it.

But the smart bull was too quick for the farmer. He ran away, escaping through a hole in the fence.

When all the bulls got home, they all laughed, because the smart bull had been able to outsmart the farmer. Ever since then, he's been known as the Smart Bull.

Mum and Dad were at the beach with their three-year-old daughter. They wanted to show her something exciting.

"Look!" said Dad, pointing out to the sea. "An octopus!"

The little girl jumped with excitement. She had never seen one before.

The octopus had lots of arms and it was a clear, bright day.

Mum looked at it and smiled. "Do you know what? Octopuses are very clever. And they like to joke!"

Mum and Dad laughed, then Dad said, "Let's find out if it can joke too!"

He waved his hands and shouted, "Hey octopus! Tell us a joke!"

The octopus splashed its arms against the water and made silly noises.

The little girl giggled. "That octopus was telling you a joke!"

One day, a mommy and her little girl were walking in the forest. They came across a beautiful lake, surrounded by tall trees and a house in the distance. The mommy said, "This is a wonderful place to play. Let's go explore."

The little girl smiled and stepped forward, but suddenly she started to scream. Without thinking, the mommy raced to her daughter's side. She saw a mop lying on the ground and a dead bird beside it. The mommy said, "My darling, don't scream. It must have been a hunter."

The little girl was scared, so the mommy hugged her tight. That night, the mommy said, "Remember what you saw today, darling. It will help you in the future."

The little girl didn't understand, but she nodded anyway.

Years later, when the little girl was grown up, she returned to the same spot. While exploring the area, she heard a hunter shouting and a gunshot firing. Suddenly, she remembered the mop and dead bird from long ago. She knew it was a warning and quickly left.

The mommy was right. The little girl remembered the earlier foreshadowing, and it saved her life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures, especially ones with lots of yellow. One day, she drew a picture of a big, yellow sun.

Lily's mom saw the picture and said, "Wow, Lily! That's a beautiful picture you drew! Can I request that you draw another one for me?"

Lily smiled and said, "Sure, Mommy! What color picture do you want me to draw?"

"I would love a picture with lots of yellow, just like the sun in your first picture," said Mom.

Lily happily got to work on her new picture, using lots of yellow and other bright colors. When she was finished, she showed it to her mom who exclaimed, "This is even more beautiful than the first one! Thank you for fulfilling my request, Lily!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures with her crayons. One day, she drew a pretty pattern with lots of colors. Her mommy saw it and smiled.

Lily felt happy when her mommy smiled. She thought her mommy was very thoughtful because she always helped her with her drawings. Lily decided to draw a picture for her mommy to say thank you.

She drew a picture of a flower with a smiley face. When her mommy saw it, she smiled again and gave Lily a big hug. Lily felt very happy that her mommy liked her picture. From that day on, she drew pictures every day to make her mommy smile.

Once upon a time a wise owl had to deal with a problem. Everywhere he looked, things seemed to be breaking. He wanted to find a solution to make all the broken things work again.

He thought and thought but he could not come up with a plan. Suddenly he had an idea. He suggested that he use a laser. He flew off to get one.

When he came back, he carefully used the laser and all the broken things worked! He was very happy. He told all the other animals about his wise suggestion and soon everyone knew that a laser could be used to fix broken things.

THE GOOSE-GIRL

The king of a great land died, and left his queen to take care of their

only child. This child was a daughter, who was very beautiful; and her

mother loved her dearly, and was very kind to her. And there was a good

fairy too, who was fond of the princess, and helped her mother to watch

over her. When she grew up, she was betrothed to a prince who lived a

great way off; and as the time drew near for her to be married, she

got ready to set off on her journey to his country. Then the queen her

mother, packed up a great many costly things; jewels, and gold, and

silver; trinkets, fine dresses, and in short everything that became a

royal bride. And she gave her a waiting-maid to ride with her, and give

her into the bridegroom's hands; and each had a horse for the journey.

Now the princess's horse was the fairy's gift, and it was called Falada,

and could speak.

When the time came for them to set out, the fairy went into her

bed-chamber, and took a little knife, and cut off a lock of her hair,

and gave it to the princess, and said, 'Take care of it, dear child; for

it is a charm that may be of use to you on the road.' Then they all took

a sorrowful leave of the princess; and she put the lock of hair into

her bosom, got upon her horse, and set off on her journey to her

bridegroom's kingdom.

One day, as they were riding along by a brook, the princess began to

feel very thirsty: and she said to her maid, 'Pray get down, and fetch

me some water in my golden cup out of yonder brook, for I want to

drink.' 'Nay,' said the maid, 'if you are thirsty, get off yourself, and

stoop down by the water and drink; I shall not be your waiting-maid any

longer.' Then she was so thirsty that she got down, and knelt over the

little brook, and drank; for she was frightened, and dared not bring out

her golden cup; and she wept and said, 'Alas! what will become of me?'

And the lock answered her, and said:

'Alas! alas! if thy mother knew it,

Sadly, sadly, would she rue it.'

But the princess was very gentle and meek, so she said nothing to her

maid's ill behaviour, but got upon her horse again.

Then all rode farther on their journey, till the day grew so warm, and

the sun so scorching, that the bride began to feel very thirsty again;

and at last, when they came to a river, she forgot her maid's rude

speech, and said, 'Pray get down, and fetch me some water to drink in

my golden cup.' But the maid answered her, and even spoke more haughtily

than before: 'Drink if you will, but I shall not be your waiting-maid.'

Then the princess was so thirsty that she got off her horse, and lay

down, and held her head over the running stream, and cried and said,

'What will become of me?' And the lock of hair answered her again:

'Alas! alas! if thy mother knew it,

Sadly, sadly, would she rue it.'

And as she leaned down to drink, the lock of hair fell from her bosom,

and floated away with the water. Now she was so frightened that she did

not see it; but her maid saw it, and was very glad, for she knew the

charm; and she saw that the poor bride would be in her power, now that

she had lost the hair. So when the bride had done drinking, and would

have got upon Falada again, the maid said, 'I shall ride upon Falada,

and you may have my horse instead'; so she was forced to give up her

horse, and soon afterwards to take off her royal clothes and put on her

maid's shabby ones.

At last, as they drew near the end of their journey, this treacherous

servant threatened to kill her mistress if she ever told anyone what had

happened. But Falada saw it all, and marked it well.

Then the waiting-maid got upon Falada, and the real bride rode upon the

other horse, and they went on in this way till at last they came to the

royal court. There was great joy at their coming, and the prince flew to

meet them, and lifted the maid from her horse, thinking she was the one

who was to be his wife; and she was led upstairs to the royal chamber;

but the true princess was told to stay in the court below.

Now the old king happened just then to have nothing else to do; so he

amused himself by sitting at his kitchen window, looking at what was

going on; and he saw her in the courtyard. As she looked very pretty,

and too delicate for a waiting-maid, he went up into the royal chamber

to ask the bride who it was she had brought with her, that was thus left

standing in the court below. 'I brought her with me for the sake of her

company on the road,' said she; 'pray give the girl some work to do,

that she may not be idle.' The old king could not for some time think

of any work for her to do; but at last he said, 'I have a lad who takes

care of my geese; she may go and help him.' Now the name of this lad,

that the real bride was to help in watching the king's geese, was

Curdken.

But the false bride said to the prince, 'Dear husband, pray do me one

piece of kindness.' 'That I will,' said the prince. 'Then tell one of

your slaughterers to cut off the head of the horse I rode upon, for it

was very unruly, and plagued me sadly on the road'; but the truth was,

she was very much afraid lest Falada should some day or other speak, and

tell all she had done to the princess. She carried her point, and the

faithful Falada was killed; but when the true princess heard of it, she

wept, and begged the man to nail up Falada's head against a large

dark gate of the city, through which she had to pass every morning

and evening, that there she might still see him sometimes. Then the

slaughterer said he would do as she wished; and cut off the head, and

nailed it up under the dark gate.

Early the next morning, as she and Curdken went out through the gate,

she said sorrowfully:

'Falada, Falada, there thou hangest!'

and the head answered:

'Bride, bride, there thou gangest!

Alas! alas! if thy mother knew it,

Sadly, sadly, would she rue it.'

Then they went out of the city, and drove the geese on. And when she

came to the meadow, she sat down upon a bank there, and let down her

waving locks of hair, which were all of pure silver; and when Curdken

saw it glitter in the sun, he ran up, and would have pulled some of the

locks out, but she cried:

'Blow, breezes, blow!

Let Curdken's hat go!

Blow, breezes, blow!

Let him after it go!

O'er hills, dales, and rocks,

Away be it whirl'd

Till the silvery locks

Are all comb'd and curl'd!

Then there came a wind, so strong that it blew off Curdken's hat; and

away it flew over the hills: and he was forced to turn and run after

it; till, by the time he came back, she had done combing and curling her

hair, and had put it up again safe. Then he was very angry and sulky,

and would not speak to her at all; but they watched the geese until it

grew dark in the evening, and then drove them homewards.

The next morning, as they were going through the dark gate, the poor

girl looked up at Falada's head, and cried:

'Falada, Falada, there thou hangest!'

and the head answered:

'Bride, bride, there thou gangest!

Alas! alas! if thy mother knew it,

Sadly, sadly, would she rue it.'

Then she drove on the geese, and sat down again in the meadow, and began

to comb out her hair as before; and Curdken ran up to her, and wanted to

take hold of it; but she cried out quickly:

'Blow, breezes, blow!

Let Curdken's hat go!

Blow, breezes, blow!

Let him after it go!

O'er hills, dales, and rocks,

Away be it whirl'd

Till the silvery locks

Are all comb'd and curl'd!

Then the wind came and blew away his hat; and off it flew a great way,

over the hills and far away, so that he had to run after it; and when

he came back she had bound up her hair again, and all was safe. So they

watched the geese till it grew dark.

In the evening, after they came home, Curdken went to the old king, and

said, 'I cannot have that strange girl to help me to keep the geese any

longer.' 'Why?' said the king. 'Because, instead of doing any good, she

does nothing but tease me all day long.' Then the king made him tell him

what had happened. And Curdken said, 'When we go in the morning through

the dark gate with our flock of geese, she cries and talks with the head

of a horse that hangs upon the wall, and says:

'Falada, Falada, there thou hangest!'

and the head answers:

'Bride, bride, there thou gangest!

Alas! alas! if thy mother knew it,

Sadly, sadly, would she rue it.'

And Curdken went on telling the king what had happened upon the meadow

where the geese fed; how his hat was blown away; and how he was forced

to run after it, and to leave his flock of geese to themselves. But the

old king told the boy to go out again the next day: and when morning

came, he placed himself behind the dark gate, and heard how she spoke

to Falada, and how Falada answered. Then he went into the field, and

hid himself in a bush by the meadow's side; and he soon saw with his own

eyes how they drove the flock of geese; and how, after a little time,

she let down her hair that glittered in the sun. And then he heard her

say:

'Blow, breezes, blow!

Let Curdken's hat go!

Blow, breezes, blow!

Let him after it go!

O'er hills, dales, and rocks,

Away be it whirl'd

Till the silvery locks

Are all comb'd and curl'd!

And soon came a gale of wind, and carried away Curdken's hat, and away

went Curdken after it, while the girl went on combing and curling her

hair. All this the old king saw: so he went home without being seen; and

when the little goose-girl came back in the evening he called her aside,

and asked her why she did so: but she burst into tears, and said, 'That

I must not tell you or any man, or I shall lose my life.'

But the old king begged so hard, that she had no peace till she had told

him all the tale, from beginning to end, word for word. And it was very

lucky for her that she did so, for when she had done the king ordered

royal clothes to be put upon her, and gazed on her with wonder, she was

so beautiful. Then he called his son and told him that he had only a

false bride; for that she was merely a waiting-maid, while the true

bride stood by. And the young king rejoiced when he saw her beauty, and

heard how meek and patient she had been; and without saying anything to

the false bride, the king ordered a great feast to be got ready for all

his court. The bridegroom sat at the top, with the false princess on one

side, and the true one on the other; but nobody knew her again, for her

beauty was quite dazzling to their eyes; and she did not seem at all

like the little goose-girl, now that she had her brilliant dress on.

When they had eaten and drank, and were very merry, the old king said

he would tell them a tale. So he began, and told all the story of the

princess, as if it was one that he had once heard; and he asked the

true waiting-maid what she thought ought to be done to anyone who would

behave thus. 'Nothing better,' said this false bride, 'than that she

should be thrown into a cask stuck round with sharp nails, and that

two white horses should be put to it, and should drag it from street to

street till she was dead.' 'Thou art she!' said the old king; 'and as

thou has judged thyself, so shall it be done to thee.' And the young

king was then married to his true wife, and they reigned over the

kingdom in peace and happiness all their lives; and the good fairy came

to see them, and restored the faithful Falada to life again.

One day, a girl named Mia went for a walk. She saw a big, scary house. It had a tall door and small windows. Mia was brave, so she went inside the house.

In the house, Mia saw a birdcage. Inside the birdcage, there was a little bird. The bird was sad. It wanted to fly and be free. Mia wanted to help the bird.

Mia opened the birdcage door. The bird flew out and was happy. It was not scary anymore. Mia and the bird were friends. They played and had fun all day.

Once there was a girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved looking at animals. Lily loved going to the park and examining the animals that lived there.

One day, Lily saw an owl sitting on a tree. She was so excited. The owl was so pretty! With its white feathers, round eyes and pointy ears. She wanted to get closer to get a better look.

Lily slowly tiptoed towards the tree where the owl was perched on. The owl looked down at her but did not move. Lily was so close that she could even touch the owl. She looked carefully at all its features and examined every detail.

The owl was sitting so still and seemed happy that Lily was there. Lily smiled at it and said 'hello'. The owl didn't say anything. Lily said goodbye and thanked the owl for letting her examine it.

Lily left feeling very happy. She had seen a pretty owl and been able to get so close!

Once upon a time there lived a girl called Jane. Jane loved to dance. Every day she would fly around the room and dance the afternoon away.

One day Jane father asked her to do the dishes instead of dancing. Jane was sad, but she agreed.

Jane dragged her feet as she did the dishes. It took her a long time and it didn't feel easy. Suddenly she had an idea.

"Daddy," Jane said, "What if I do the dishes while I fly and dance around the room?"

Jane's father smiled. "That sounds like a great idea! You can have fun while doing chores."

So Jane put on her favourite music and started to fly and dance around the room while she did the dishes. And when the dishes were done Jane had had a lot of fun and the chore didn't seem so hard after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy named Teddy, who was her best friend. One day, Lily accidentally dropped Teddy and he broke. She was sad and cried a lot.

Her mom came to her and asked, "What happened, Lily?"

Lily said, "Teddy broke. I want him to be okay."

Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we can fix him. Let's find some glue."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy. You make me feel peace."

After they fixed Teddy, Lily hugged him tightly and said, "I won't let you fall again. I'll always take care of you."

Suddenly, Teddy slapped Lily with his paw and said, "Thank you, Lily. You're the best friend ever."

Lily laughed and hugged Teddy again. They were both happy and peaceful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she was playing with her dolls when her mom called her for lunch. Lily was nervous because she didn't want to stop playing.

"Lily, it's time for lunch," said her mom.

"I don't want to stop playing," said Lily.

"You have to surrender your toys for a little while and come eat," said her mom.

Lily didn't want to surrender her toys, but she knew she had to. She put her dolls away and went to eat lunch with her mom. After lunch, Lily went back to playing with her dolls. The result of surrendering her toys was that she got to eat a yummy lunch and then continue playing with her toys.

Once upon a time, a little squirrel named Nutty loved to collect acorns. One day, she found a big, shiny acorn and was very happy. But then, she saw another squirrel named Sammy who also wanted the acorn. They both wanted it so much that they started to fight over it.

Nutty was very fast and managed to get the acorn first, but then she realized she had hurt Sammy. She felt guilty and sad. She knew she shouldn't have fought over the acorn.

Later that day, Nutty saw Sammy again. She felt bad and wanted to make things right. So she went over to Sammy and gave her the acorn. Sammy was surprised and happy. She clapped her hands and thanked Nutty.

Nutty learned that it's better to share than to fight over things. She felt happy that she had made Sammy happy and knew that she had done the right thing. From that day on, Nutty always shared her acorns with her friends.

Once upon a time a little girl went for a walk in the park. As she went, she looked around at all of the interesting things she saw. Suddenly, she saw a unique shape in the sky. It was a triangle with a circle on top. She turned to her mom and asked, "What is that?" Her mom smiled and said, "That is a kite. It is a special shape that you can show in the sky." So the little girl got excited and ran to the kite store. She picked out the most beautiful kite and took it to the park. With her mom's help she got the kite up in the sky, and watched it fly around. Everyone was impressed by the unique shape of the kite!

Once upon a time, there was a fearful silver fox who lived deep in the forest. She was always very careful, for she knew that her enemies could be everywhere. One day, the fox noticed something shiny near the base of a giant tree. She cautiously crept over to investigate and saw that it was a silver plate filled with delicious food. The fox sniffed the plate and understood that it was meant to serve as a meal for her.

The fox slowly started to eat the food. She quickly realized that this was by far the most delicious meal she had ever tasted. She ate every last scrap and felt so happy and content. With her belly full, she remembered that this meal had been served to her and she promised to always be grateful. The fox thanked the mysterious figure and scurried off into the darkness, feeling thankful and safe.

Molly wanted to have an adventure! She had just heard about igloos and she wanted to see one for herself. She put on her hat and mittens and went outside. She looked around for an igloo and saw something different. She saw a castle made of ice â€" it looked just like an igloo!

Molly was amazed. She had never seen anything like it. She wanted to explore the castle, so she ran up to the door and knocked. "Let me in!" she demanded.

But no one answered the door. Molly knocked again, a little louder this time. "Let me in!" she demanded.

Finally, the door opened and an old-looking polar bear stepped out. Molly was a bit scared, but she was also very curious. The polar bear smiled and said, "Come in, Molly! I'll show you around my igloo!"

Molly was delighted! She stepped inside and found all kinds of different things. She saw chairs made of ice and ice sculptures. She even saw a mini igloo inside the bigger igloo. At the end of the tour, Molly thanked the polar bear and said farewell.

Molly couldn't wait to tell her friends about her adventure and all the different things she had seen in the igloo.

Once upon a time, there was a furry bear. He had fluffy fur and a long, hairy tail. He was always curious about the world and he wanted to wander.

One day, the bear had an idea. He was going to explore the big, cold freezer. It was a very tall place, filled with strange things! But the bear didn't know what it was.

He was so excited to explore the freezer. He crept inside. Inside it was dark and very cold, but the bear wasn't scared. He felt so brave as he wandered around. He found lots of interesting shapes and colours.

The bear wanted to stay in the freezer forever. He loved discovering all the new things but he knew it was time to leave. He soon stepped out of the freezer and was met with the warm sunshine. He knew he would be back soon to explore the freezer again.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little mouse. His name was Peter. Peter liked to play all day and never listen to his mom.

One day, Peter took a walk in the forest. Suddenly, he saw something that made him blink - a secret door! He ran quickly to the door and peeked inside.

"Oh wow!" Peter said.

"Who goes there?" a voice said from inside.

Peter was so scared that he couldn't say a word. After a few moments, the voice spoke again.

"If you want to enter this secret door, you must answer a riddle. If you can't answer it, you must go away."

Peter thought for a minute and then asked, "What is the answer?"

The voice replied, "Beware the naughty ones!"

Peter smiled and said, "I know the answer! I'm naughty, but I'm also very curious! May I enter please?"

The voice laughed and said, "Yes, you may come in and explore the secret door!"

And so, Peter did. He explored the secret door with great curiosity and had many adventures!

Once upon a time, there was a big bird called a raven. The raven had black feathers and a sharp beak. One day, the raven found a useful stick on the ground. The raven picked up the stick with its beak and flew away.

Later, the raven saw a little mouse running around. The raven wanted to play with the mouse, but the stick was in the way. So, the raven decided to remove the stick from its beak. The raven dropped the stick and played with the mouse happily.

After a while, the raven got tired and flew back to its nest. The raven was happy that it found a useful stick and that it got to play with a little mouse. The end.

Sam liked to study golf. He watched his dad play golf on TV and learned the names of the clubs and the holes. He also had a toy golf set that he played with in the yard. He wanted to be a good golfer like his dad.

One day, his dad said, "Sam, do you want to come with me to the golf course? I have a lesson with the coach and you can watch and learn."

Sam was very happy and said, "Yes, dad, I want to go!"

They got in the car and drove to the golf course. Sam saw many people playing golf and hitting the ball with different clubs. He also saw the coach, who was a tall and friendly man. He said hello to Sam and his dad and gave them some tips.

"Sam, do you want to try hitting the ball?" the coach asked.

Sam nodded and took a small club from his toy set. He put the ball on the ground and swung the club. But he missed the ball and fell down. He felt embarrassed and sad.

The coach and his dad helped him up and said, "Don't worry, Sam, it's okay. Golf is hard and you need to practice a lot. You are doing great for your age. Just keep studying and trying and you will get better."

Sam felt better and said, "Thank you, coach, thank you, dad. I will keep studying and trying. I want to be a dependable golfer like you."

The coach and his dad smiled and said, "You are welcome, Sam. We are proud of you. You are a dependable son and a good learner. You have a bright future in golf."

Sam hugged them and said, "I love you, coach, I love you, dad. You are the best teachers."

The moral of the story is: study hard, try your best, and don't give up. You will learn from your mistakes and improve your skills. You will also earn the respect and love of your teachers and parents.

Once there was a girl named Jane. She was playing with her toys in her bedroom. Suddenly, something out of the window caught her eye. Jane saw a bright dragonfly waving its wings outside her window.

"Wow!" said Jane in disbelief. She opened the window and the dragonfly flew in. Jane was thrilled and held out her hand for the dragonfly to land on.

The dragonfly flew away and made a little swirl in the air, leaving a spiraling trail of black ink. Jane held out her hand again, but the dragonfly was gone.

But the trail of ink stayed. Jane clapped her hands as she saw the beautiful original design that had just been created. She smiled and waved goodbye to her magical friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was three years old and loved to play.

One day, Lily was playing with her toys in the backyard. In the middle of playing she heard a loud number. Startled, Lily looked up and saw her mother. She asked her mother why she was counting so loudly. Her mother smiled and told her that she was counting how many times Lily had embarrassed her.

Lily was confused and asked for an explanation. Her mother told her that she was embarrassed when Lily had thrown her food at the dinner table the night before. Lily felt embarrassed too and apologised for her behaviour.

To make it up to her mother, Lily asked if there was anything she could do. Her mother thought for a moment and then smiled. She said that she had an empty jar with a lid and asked Lily to try and fill it with nice things.

Filled with excitement, Lily agreed. She ran off to start collecting nice things.

Once upon a time there was a hairy raven called Bob. Bob had decided to go on an adventure, so he flew off into the sky. As he flew, he got really tired and decided he needed to take a break.

Bob eventually found a perfect spot - a big tree near a lake. He flew up to the tree and perched on one of the branches. While he was sitting there, he noticed a small boy. The boy was standing by the edge of the lake, looking at the water.

Bob flew down to the edge of the lake and asked the boy what he was doing.

The boy said he was trying to catch some fish with his hands, but he couldn't manage it.

Bob said, "I can help! I'm a very hairy raven, so I can catch fish easily with my claws!"

The boy was so excited and said, "Can you really manage it?"

Bob flew to the middle of the lake, dipped his claws into the water and caught a fish!

The boy was so amazed. He thanked Bob for helping him and said goodbye. Bob flew away, off on another adventure.

One day, a boy named Tim found a hidden box under his bed. Inside the box, there was a game called chess. Tim did not know how to play chess. He asked his mom, "Mom, can you teach me how to play chess?"

His mom said, "Yes, I can teach you. First, I will show you the pieces and how they move." She took out the pieces and lead Tim through the game. They played chess together, and Tim started to learn.

Soon, Tim got better at chess. He played with his friends and even won a game. Tim was happy that he found the hidden chess game and that his mom lead him to learn it.

Once there was a boy called Jake. Jake wanted fruit but the fruit was icy! He didnâ€™t know how to use it.

But then Jake had an idea. He put the ice covered fruit in a big bowl and he used a spoon to break it up. He stirred it around and around until it was all smooshy.

Then he found some melted ice in the bowl and realised that he could use this too! He added some milk and some sugar, and before long it was yummy.

Jake was very happy with his creation. From then on, every morning he would make icy fruit juice!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy pipe that he liked to play with. The pipe was very popular with all of his friends, and they all wanted to play with it too.

One day, Timmy and his friends were playing at the park when they saw two birds fighting in the sky. They all looked up and saw the birds flying around and making lots of noise. Timmy thought it looked like fun, so he pretended to fight with his friends too.

After they finished playing, Timmy went home and showed his mom the pipe. She thought it was a nice toy, but reminded him to be careful with it. Timmy promised to take good care of it and put it away in his toy box.

From that day on, Timmy and his friends played with the pipe every day. They never fought over it because they knew they could all have a turn. And whenever they saw birds fighting in the sky, they would pretend to fight too, just like Timmy did that day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved sweets, especially lollipops. One day, Lily and her mom went to the store to buy some candy. Lily saw a big, red lollipop and asked her mom if she could have it.

"Can I have that lollipop, please?" Lily asked her mom.

"Of course, you can have it!" her mom replied.

As they were walking home, Lily saw a spider crawling on the sidewalk. She was scared and didn't want to step on it.

"Mommy, there's a spider! Can we go around it?" Lily asked.

"Sure, let's go around it so we don't hurt it," her mom said.

Finally, they arrived home and Lily happily enjoyed her sweet lollipop.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sue. She was three years old and she loved to watch movies. One day she asked her mom if they could watch a movie together. Her mom said yes, but then it started to rain outside. Sue was sad because she wanted to watch a movie in the clear sky.

Then mom had an idea. She said, "Let's make a movie!" She gave Sue an old webcam and told her to act out a movie by herself. Sue was so happy and she asked if she could wear a costume. Mom said yes and they went around the house finding different materials to make Sue's costume.

Finally, Sue was all dressed up. She used the old webcam to record her movie and it came out perfectly clear. Sue was very proud of her movie and showed it to all her friends. Mom was so proud of Sue for the hard work she put into it. Together they enjoyed the movie under the clear sky.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Abby. She was three years old and she liked to play at night. One night, Abby wanted to go outside, so her mom gave her a flashlight. She was so excited! She held it tightly as she opened the door and stepped outside.

Suddenly, it was very dark. Abby felt embarrassed and scared, but she held the flashlight up and shone it around. The light made everything better and much brighter.

Abby began to explore. She found the furry cat hiding in the bushes, and the big bird sleeping in the tree. Everywhere she looked, the flashlight made things easier to see.

Abby had so much fun exploring with her flashlight. It made her feel brave and not scared anymore. Later she went back inside, still holding the flashlight tightly. The end.

Jack was feeling a bit sad. He wanted some wine but he didn't have any. He walked up to a store and asked the shopkeeper, "Do you have any wine?"

The shopkeeper replied, "Yes, I have some. It's bad though. Are you sure you want it?"

Jack thought for a moment then said, "Yes, I will take it."

The shopkeeper counted out two bottles of wine and handed them to Jack. Jack thanked the shopkeeper and went home.

When Jack got home he opened a bottle of the bad wine and took a sip - it tasted horrible! He thought to himself, "Maybe I should have asked for something else!"

John saw something cute on the other side of the playground. He wanted to know what it was. He ran to the other side and saw a prize. He wanted it! He ran to the prize but then he saw that someone else was coming for it too.

John said to the other person, "I want the prize!"

The other person said, "I want it too!"

John thought for a moment, then he said, "I know. We can both have it. We can share the prize!"

The other person agreed and they shared the prize. They were both happy. John was glad he got to keep a part of the cute prize.

Once upon a time there was an orange leak. The leak was always getting bigger and bigger. Until one day it split. The orange leak split into two. Each part of the orange leak was still leaking and getting bigger. Soon the two orange leaks had spread across the floor. But then something surprising happened. A big sunny ray of light came down from the sky and filled the two orange leaks with sunshine. The orange leaks smiled and started to jump and dance in the sunshine. From that day on, the orange leaks never split again and always stayed together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a special lamp that he loved very much. The lamp was very bright and helped Timmy see in the dark. One night, Timmy fell asleep with the lamp on.

In the middle of the night, Timmy woke up and saw that the lamp was still on. He knew he had to turn it off because it was not wise to waste electricity. Timmy turned off the lamp and went back to sleep.

The next morning, Timmy's mom was very proud of him for being so wise and turning off the lamp. She gave him a big hug and told him how much she loved him. From that day on, Timmy always remembered to turn off the lamp before he went to sleep.

Sam and Mia liked to travel with their mom and dad. They went to many places and saw many things. One day, they went to a farm where they could play with animals and make things with clay.

Sam and Mia saw a big pile of clay and ran to it. They wanted to make animals with clay. Sam made a cow and Mia made a sheep. They were very happy with their clay animals.

But then, they saw a little pig who was sad. The pig had no friends and no clay. He wanted to play with Sam and Mia, but he was shy. He looked at their clay animals and wished he had one too.

Sam and Mia saw the pig and felt sorry for him. They were compassionate and wanted to help him. They decided to share their clay with the pig and make him a friend.

"Hi, little pig," Sam said. "Do you want to play with us? We have some clay for you. You can make an animal too."

"Really?" the pig said. "Thank you, Sam and Mia. You are very kind. I would like to make a pig with clay."

Sam and Mia gave some clay to the pig and helped him make a pig. The pig was very happy and proud of his clay pig. He hugged Sam and Mia and thanked them again.

Sam and Mia were happy too. They learned that sharing is caring and that making friends is fun. They played with the pig and their clay animals until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to the pig and promised to come back soon. The pig waved to them and smiled. He was not sad anymore. He had friends and clay.

Once there lived two brothers. One was named Shaun and one was named Joe. They were very different, but they always got along. One day Joe was feeling nervous. He was looking for something, but he didn't know what it was.

So, he went to find his brother Shaun and asked for help. Shaun was very clever and thought he might be able to solve the mystery. So, Shaun and Joe went to search for the answer.

They went to a nearby well and chose the biggest copper coin they could find. They dropped it inside and waited to see what would happen. After a few moments, a message came out of the well and told them the answer they had been looking for.

Joe was so excited and Shaun felt very proud of himself for helping his brother solve the mystery. They hugged each other happily and continued on their way.

The brothers enjoyed the rest of their day and never forgot how they solved the mystery with the help of the well.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl named Lily. She loved to chew gum all day long. One day, she accidentally swallowed her gum and started to weep. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, sweetie. The gum will come out soon."

Lily stopped weeping and waited for the gum to come out. She drank lots of water and ate some bananas to help it come out faster. The next day, she woke up feeling much better. She ran to her mom and said, "Look, Mommy! The gum came out!"

Her mom was so happy and gave her a big hug. From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful when chewing gum. She also learned that it's okay to weep sometimes, as long as you have someone to hug you and make you feel better.

Once there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy loved exploring the world around her. Her favorite thing was looking for her special treasures.

One day Daisy found something very special. It was gray, fragile and sparkly. Daisy was so excited to have found her special treasure. She carefully put it in her pocket and ran to show her mom.

When Daisy got home she couldn't find her treasure! She looked in her pocket and it was gone! Daisy was so sad and started to cry. She missed her treasure and was sad that it was gone.

Daisy's mom smiled when she saw how sad Daisy was. "Don't worry, my sweet," she said. She pulled out a similar gray and fragile treasure and handed it to Daisy.

Daisy smiled with delight! She hugged her mom and thanked her for her special gift. Daisy never missed her special treasure again.

Henry was a cheerful little boy. He loved to explore and learn new things. One day he was exploring with his Mom and Dad. They arrived at a huge volcano. Henry was amazed and couldn't stop looking at it.

Henry's Dad urged him to stay away from the volcano. He said it was very dangerous. Henry was scared but also excited. He asked his Dad lots of questions about the volcano. He wanted to know the names of all the different rocks.

Henry's Dad continued to urge Henry to stay away from the volcano. He said it was important to be careful. But Henry kept asking questions and kept exploring. Henry's Dad smiled and said he was curious and had a lot of energy.

At the end of the day, they hugged and said goodbye to the volcano. Henry was sad to go but his dad urged him to be happy and said they would come back soon. Henry smiled and felt cheerful. They were all so excited to explore the volcano together again.

One day, a little girl named Julia went exploring in the woods. She found a unique crystal! It was sparkly and shiny and very pretty. She wanted to keep it, so she put it in her pocket and kept walking.

Suddenly, Julia heard a mysterious voice. It said "Tell me! Tell me!" She looked all around, but she couldn't see anyone. Julia was scared, so she just stayed where she was.

Then the voice said again, "Tell me about the crystal!" Julia went closer and saw that it was a fairy who was talking to her! She told the fairy all about the unique crystal she had found.

The fairy smiled, and said "I'm so glad you found the special crystal. You can keep it if you like." Julia smiled too, and thanked the fairy. Then she said goodbye and went running back home, happy with her special crystal.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to hop on the grass and look for bugs. They saw a big frog near the pond. It was green and wet.

"Look, a frog!" Lily said. "Can we catch it?"

Ben nodded. He ran to the frog and tried to grab it. But the frog was fast. It hopped away from Ben and into the water.

"Come back, frog!" Ben shouted. He was angry. He wanted to play with the frog.

Lily followed Ben to the pond. She saw the frog under the water. It looked at them with big eyes.

"Maybe the frog is scared," Lily said. "Maybe it does not like to be caught."

Ben frowned. He did not understand. He liked to catch things.

"Let's try again," he said. He reached for the frog.

But the frog did not want to be caught. It hopped out of the water and onto the shore. It made a loud croak. It sounded angry.

"Go away, kids!" the frog said. "This is my home. Leave me alone!"

Lily and Ben were surprised. They did not know that frogs could talk. They felt sorry for the frog.

"Sorry, frog," Lily said. "We did not mean to bother you. We just wanted to be your friends."

The frog looked at them. It saw that they were not bad. It felt a little less angry.

"Friends?" the frog said. "Well, maybe. But you have to be nice. And you have to hop with me. Do you like to hop?"

Lily and Ben smiled. They liked to hop. They nodded.

"OK, frog," Ben said. "We will hop with you. And we will be nice."

The frog smiled too. It hopped with Lily and Ben on the grass. They had fun. They became friends. They forgot about the dark.

THE FROG-PRINCE

One fine evening a young princess put on her bonnet and clogs, and went

out to take a walk by herself in a wood; and when she came to a cool

spring of water, that rose in the midst of it, she sat herself down

to rest a while. Now she had a golden ball in her hand, which was her

favourite plaything; and she was always tossing it up into the air, and

catching it again as it fell. After a time she threw it up so high that

she missed catching it as it fell; and the ball bounded away, and rolled

along upon the ground, till at last it fell down into the spring. The

princess looked into the spring after her ball, but it was very deep, so

deep that she could not see the bottom of it. Then she began to bewail

her loss, and said, 'Alas! if I could only get my ball again, I would

give all my fine clothes and jewels, and everything that I have in the

world.'

Whilst she was speaking, a frog put its head out of the water, and said,

'Princess, why do you weep so bitterly?' 'Alas!' said she, 'what can you

do for me, you nasty frog? My golden ball has fallen into the spring.'

The frog said, 'I want not your pearls, and jewels, and fine clothes;

but if you will love me, and let me live with you and eat from off

your golden plate, and sleep upon your bed, I will bring you your ball

again.' 'What nonsense,' thought the princess, 'this silly frog is

talking! He can never even get out of the spring to visit me, though

he may be able to get my ball for me, and therefore I will tell him he

shall have what he asks.' So she said to the frog, 'Well, if you will

bring me my ball, I will do all you ask.' Then the frog put his head

down, and dived deep under the water; and after a little while he came

up again, with the ball in his mouth, and threw it on the edge of the

spring. As soon as the young princess saw her ball, she ran to pick

it up; and she was so overjoyed to have it in her hand again, that she

never thought of the frog, but ran home with it as fast as she could.

The frog called after her, 'Stay, princess, and take me with you as you

said,' But she did not stop to hear a word.

The next day, just as the princess had sat down to dinner, she heard a

strange noise--tap, tap--plash, plash--as if something was coming up the

marble staircase: and soon afterwards there was a gentle knock at the

door, and a little voice cried out and said:

'Open the door, my princess dear,

Open the door to thy true love here!

And mind the words that thou and I said

By the fountain cool, in the greenwood shade.'

Then the princess ran to the door and opened it, and there she saw

the frog, whom she had quite forgotten. At this sight she was sadly

frightened, and shutting the door as fast as she could came back to her

seat. The king, her father, seeing that something had frightened her,

asked her what was the matter. 'There is a nasty frog,' said she, 'at

the door, that lifted my ball for me out of the spring this morning: I

told him that he should live with me here, thinking that he could never

get out of the spring; but there he is at the door, and he wants to come

in.'

While she was speaking the frog knocked again at the door, and said:

'Open the door, my princess dear,

Open the door to thy true love here!

And mind the words that thou and I said

By the fountain cool, in the greenwood shade.'

Then the king said to the young princess, 'As you have given your word

you must keep it; so go and let him in.' She did so, and the frog hopped

into the room, and then straight on--tap, tap--plash, plash--from the

bottom of the room to the top, till he came up close to the table where

the princess sat. 'Pray lift me upon chair,' said he to the princess,

'and let me sit next to you.' As soon as she had done this, the frog

said, 'Put your plate nearer to me, that I may eat out of it.' This

she did, and when he had eaten as much as he could, he said, 'Now I am

tired; carry me upstairs, and put me into your bed.' And the princess,

though very unwilling, took him up in her hand, and put him upon the

pillow of her own bed, where he slept all night long. As soon as it was

light he jumped up, hopped downstairs, and went out of the house.

'Now, then,' thought the princess, 'at last he is gone, and I shall be

troubled with him no more.'

But she was mistaken; for when night came again she heard the same

tapping at the door; and the frog came once more, and said:

'Open the door, my princess dear,

Open the door to thy true love here!

And mind the words that thou and I said

By the fountain cool, in the greenwood shade.'

And when the princess opened the door the frog came in, and slept upon

her pillow as before, till the morning broke. And the third night he did

the same. But when the princess awoke on the following morning she was

astonished to see, instead of the frog, a handsome prince, gazing on her

with the most beautiful eyes she had ever seen, and standing at the head

of her bed.

He told her that he had been enchanted by a spiteful fairy, who had

changed him into a frog; and that he had been fated so to abide till

some princess should take him out of the spring, and let him eat from

her plate, and sleep upon her bed for three nights. 'You,' said the

prince, 'have broken his cruel charm, and now I have nothing to wish for

but that you should go with me into my father's kingdom, where I will

marry you, and love you as long as you live.'

The young princess, you may be sure, was not long in saying 'Yes' to

all this; and as they spoke a gay coach drove up, with eight beautiful

horses, decked with plumes of feathers and a golden harness; and behind

the coach rode the prince's servant, faithful Heinrich, who had bewailed

the misfortunes of his dear master during his enchantment so long and so

bitterly, that his heart had well-nigh burst.

They then took leave of the king, and got into the coach with eight

horses, and all set out, full of joy and merriment, for the prince's

kingdom, which they reached safely; and there they lived happily a great

many years.

The sun was shining in the east, and the birds were singing their favourite songs in the trees. Everything was perfect for a day of play.

Lily and her brother Sam were looking for something fun to do. They thought and thought, but nothing came to mind.

Suddenly, Lily had an idea.

Sam shrugged. He wasn't sure if this was a good idea.

They went hopping and skipping through the meadow. Lily was excited, but Sam was getting bored. He started to do some naughty things, like hide in the bushes and jump out and scare Lily.

Lily tried to ignore him. She wanted to focus on the treasure hunt. Every time Sam did something naughty, Lily just shook her head and shrugged.

Eventually they got tired. They had had a lot of fun, but they hadn't found any treasure.

Sam looked up at Lily. "Maybe we'll find some treasure tomorrow," he said.

Lily smiled. "Maybe," she said, and they made their way home.

Billy loved to decorate. He always gardened by his porch and created unique designs to put around it.

One day, his mom wanted to decorate the porch too. She bought a big box of decorations, but they didn't look as good as what Billy had made.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a village with her mommy and daddy. The village was very calm and peaceful.

Once upon a time, there was a small boat named Bobby. Bobby lived in a port with other boats. The port was near the sea, and it was very useful for boats to rest and play.

The sun was shining and the sky was a peaceful blue. Tommy was playing in the garden when he saw an aeroplane flying across the sky. He shouted "Wow!" and watched it fly away in the distance.

Once upon a time, there was a kid named Leo. Leo was playful and always smiling. He loved to tell jokes and make people laugh.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had an ordinary day playing with his toys until he heard a loud snap. It was his sister, Sally, who had broken his favorite toy. Timmy got very upset and raised his finger to scold Sally.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was very obedient. She always listened to her mom and dad and was very kind to her friends. But there was one thing she loved to do more than anything- she loved to roll!

The little girl learned her lesson and knew to always be obedient, but also to listen to her own instincts and find a way to get the best of both worlds.

There once was a little girl called Jenna who lived in a very big, old house. One day, she decided to explore her garden. As she slowly wandered around, she saw something very interesting. From then on, the crab would always look back fondly on the day she had taken a ride on the beautiful duck's back and gone swimming in the sea.

Once upon a time, there was a normal deer. The deer went outside to play in the sun and look for something to do.
The deer went to a nearby field and the field included lots of things the deer could play with.
The deer saw some horses, cows, and sheep. It also saw some squirrels and birds.
The deer had a great time playing in the field with the animals. It even made some new friends.
The deer spent the whole day in the field, playing and having fun with its new animal friends.
When the day was done, the deer went home feeling happy and content. It could not wait to come back and play with its friends again. The end.

Once upon a time there lived a mouse and a squirrel. They lived together near a big, strong tree.

The squirrel was always carrying a large piece of steel around. The mouse wanted to play and asked the squirrel if he could borrow it.

But the squirrel said "No! My steel is mine, and you can't have it".

The two animals started to quarrel. The mouse was angry and ran away.

He ran to the pond and found a stick. Then he went back to the squirrel with the stick and said "I want to play with this".

The squirrel thought for a moment and said "Yes".

The squirrel and the mouse played together with the stick for a long time. They even found success at building a fortress out of the stick!

The mouse and the squirrel were very happy that they had stopped their quarrel and started to play such a fun game. They lived together happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a small boy. He wanted to climb up to the cupboard. So he asked his mom to carry him up. His mom said yes and she carried him up. When they got to the top, the boy was so happy! He was in a peaceful place. He opened the cupboard and found lots of fun things inside. His mom said he could keep them all. So he carefully took out all the things one by one and looked at them. He was very happy! He had a big smile on his face and his mom smiled too. They both enjoyed the peaceful place on top of the cupboard.

Once upon a time, there was a tank. It looked just like any ordinary tank. Inside the tank was a long, stretchy rope. Every day, a little girl named Sarah would play with the rope.

She would take both ends of the rope and stretch it out until it was super long. Then she would let it go, and it would shrink back down. She would do this many times and laugh.

One day, Sarah decided to take the rope for a walk. She went outside with the rope and started to stretch it out again. She kept stretching it until it was so long that it reached all the way to the end of her street.

Sarah and the rope had lots of fun! When it was time to go home, Sarah gathered both ends of the rope and put them back in the tank. She didn't want to leave the rope out in the ordinary street.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a corn field. It was full of tall stalks. Each one was loaded with juicy yellow corn. It was the sweetest corn ever!

One day, a careless wind blew across the field. It covered the corn with dust and dirt. The stalks were hidden and the corn was hidden too.

The farmer was very sad. He had no way to find his precious corn. He looked and looked, but it was gone.

Suddenly, a funny bird flew down. He had a big yellow corn cob in his beak! He dropped it in the farmer's hand. The farmer was so happy.

The bird had covered the corn with its feathers to keep it safe. The farmer was so thankful! He thanked the bird and raced back to the corn field. The stalks looked happy to see him. He carefully planted the corn cob back in the earth.

The farmer found all his corn! He was so happy! From then on he was extra careful to make sure the corn was safe.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy wanted to go outside and play. Her mom said, "we have to go to the grocery store first".

Lucy was disappointed, but she didn't complain. She stepped off the porch, careful not to trip on the stairs.

When they arrived at the store, Lucy saw a giant screen in the checkout aisle, showing a graceful ballerina dancing. Lucy was fascinated! She asked her mom, "Where did that dancer come from?"

Her mom said, "It's a movie". "It's very graceful, isn't it?"

Lucy nodded. She watched the dancer until it was time to leave. As they stepped out of the store, Lucy beamed with joy and said, "It was so graceful!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and she loved playing in the garden.

One day, she saw a red frog sitting on a rock. She walked up to the frog and said, "Hi, frog! What are you doing?"

The red frog said, "I'm just sitting here enjoying the sun!"

The little girl said, "That's nice. Will you be my friend?"

The red frog smiled and asked, "Do you want to sit with me and play?"

The girl smiled and nodded. They both sat on the rock together and enjoyed some fun games.

The girl and the red frog became best friends and played together every day.

The end.

Once, there was a man who had an expensive van. He drove it everywhere and never wanted to let it go.

One day, the man was driving it and he heard a noise. He stopped to take a look and he saw the engine was broken! He was very sad.

He couldn't afford to fix it so he threw the van away. Everyone was sad, but was happy that the van was gone.

The man decided that he no longer needed a van. And he promised himself he would never buy an expensive van again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to pray. One day, she went outside and saw a mysterious plant growing in her garden. She said, "This must be a special plant! What should I do?"

The little girl thought and then said, "I should pray to find out what this plant needs."

So, the little girl folded her hands and began to pray. Suddenly, she heard a voice from the mysterious plant.

The plant said, "I need some sunshine and water, and I will grow tall and strong."

The little girl smiled and said, "Thank you for telling me what you need. I will give you plenty of sunshine and water, so you can keep growing."

The little girl took care of the mysterious plant and it soon became tall and strong. She was very proud and happy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a rat. His name was Peter and he was very brave. One day, Peter started to explore the world outside his house. He came across a bottle full of a strange liquid. Peter sniffed it and it smelled bad. He thought it was poison.

Though he was scared, Peter decided to drink a drop. Suddenly, the poison tasted sweet! Peter was so surprised that he dropped the bottle and it broke. From the poison spilled out a rare gem.

Peter was so excited that he started jumping up and down. A nearby rabbit watched him curiously.

The rabbit asked, "What happened? Why are you so happy?"

Peter smiled and said, "I found something very special. It's a rare gem that I found in the bottle of poison I drank!"

Mummy was talking to Grandma on the telephone. Grandma was asking questions from far away.

Mummy explained, "It's a very long cord that stretches from here to Grandma's house so we can talk. It's a special cord."

Teddy, a three-year-old, was watching with wide eyes. He was jealous of the cord. He wanted one!

Mummy said, "Now Teddy, your Grandma is so far away we can't just drive to her house. But when she talks to us on the telephone it's like she's right here."

Teddy was very excited. He wanted to play with the cord!

Mummy explained, "We can't play with the cord Teddy. It's too special. We just use it to talk to Grandma, but it won't last forever. That's why we have to talk to each other as much as we can."

Teddy smiled and hugged his Mummy, happy to have her close. He wasn't jealous of the cord anymore, now he understood its purpose.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Charlie. Charlie was three years old, and he loved to imagine the coolest things.

One day, Charlie was in the kitchen with his mom. He saw one of the cabinets open, and he gasped with excitement. Inside was a mixer!

Charlie said, "Mom, what is a mixer?"

His mother replied, "It's a special machine that helps mix things together. What would you like to make with it?"

Charlie thought for a few moments and then said, "Let's make something spicy!"

His mother smiled and carefully opened a cupboard. She pulled out some onions, peppers, and some spices. Charlie imagined how delicious it would taste.

His mother helped him put the ingredients into the mixer, and she pressed the button. The mixer began to whir and the ingredients all blended together.

When the mixture was done, it looked and smelled great. Charlie and his mom tasted it, and it was the most delicious and spicy thing they'd ever eaten!

Once there was a strong stone. It wanted to stay by itself so it could be alone. But that was hard to do in the forest. Every day an animal would come by and try to move the stone. But the stone was strong and wouldn't budge.

Then one day, a butterfly flew by and asked the stone why it wanted to stay by itself. The butterfly said it would like to be friends with the stone. The stone was very happy.

The butterfly and the stone became great friends. Every day, the butterfly would come to visit and stay with the stone. The stone was so glad that it didn't have to be alone any more. It was strong and would stay with its friend forever.

Once upon a time there was a poor alligator. He was always very shy and didn't have many friends. One day, he met a friendly little girl. She was so kind and asked him if he wanted to play. The alligator was so surprised and happy, he said yes right away.

The girl said "Come on, I'll spoil you!" and they both laughed. Together they played many games and had lots of fun. The alligator felt right at home with the little girl.

"Thank you so much for spoiling me!" said the alligator as they were saying goodbye. The little girl smiled and said "No problem, I had lots of fun!"

The little girl and the alligator were great friends from then on. They would always play together and have so much fun. The alligator went from being poor and lonely to being spoiled and happy.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a team. They were spread all over the world. They were very excited to start their work together.

But then something boring happened. Every day all the team members had to do the same chores. Wash the dishes, vacuum the floors, and sweep the yard. The tasks were boring and tiring and the team was not happy.

One day the team decided to do something different. They all spread out and started looking for exciting things to do. They went to the park, explored a cave full of spiders, and built giant sandcastles on the beach.

The team was having so much fun that they decided to keep spreading out to discover new things. They explored mountain tops, swam in lakes, and jumped in puddles.

The team had the best adventures together and they were never bored again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sally. She wanted to find something special, something no one else had. So one day she set off on an adventure.
Sally walked to the top of a big hill. When she got there she started to dig. She dug for hours, and eventually she found something amazing - a mine! It was full of sparkly treasures, more than she'd ever seen before.

Sally was so excited. She decided to keep her mine secret and kept it a secret from everyone.

Every day Sally went to her mine, full of honest joy. She'd settle down in the corner and play with the sparkly treasures until tea time.

Sally would often tell her parents about her mine. She told them it was her little secret and asked them to keep it that way.
