Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with dough and make all sorts of shapes. One day, she made a big ball and rolled it high up in the air.

Her little brother, Max, saw it and said, "Wow, Lily! That's so high!"

Lily replied, "Yes, it is! Let's march around it and see how big it is." So they marched around the ball of dough, singing and laughing.

Suddenly, the ball of dough fell and splattered all over the ground. Max said, "Oh no! What happened?"

Lily explained, "I rolled it too high and it couldn't stay up anymore. That's okay though, we can make another one!" And they happily went back to playing with dough.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess who wore a veil on her head. The veil was like a pretty scarf that covered her hair. The princess loved her veil because it made her feel special and pretty.

One day, the princess was going to a big party. She needed a dependable horse to take her there. She asked her friend who had many horses to supply her with one. Her friend gave her a strong and dependable horse that would take her to the party safely.

As the princess rode on the horse, her veil fluttered in the wind. She felt happy and excited to go to the party. When she arrived, everyone admired her beautiful veil and the dependable horse that brought her there. The princess had a wonderful time and was grateful to her friend for supplying her with such a great horse.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl. She was a happy child who liked to explore outside. One day, she decided to adventure around her neighborhood.

When she arrived, she saw her neighbor. He was a kindly old man with a big, friendly smile. She smiled back and decided to make a request. She asked if he could give her a surprise.

The neighbor smiled and said yes! He took her to his garden and picked some beautiful flowers. He gave them to the little girl, who was so excited.

The brave little girl thanked him and took the flowers home. She was so pleased with her surprise and thanked her neighbor for being so kind. She knew that her neighbor was a very special friend.

Once upon a time, there was a funny cat named Fluffy. Fluffy lived in a big house with his best friend, a little boy named Tim. They loved to play and have fun together. Fluffy had soft fur that Tim liked to rub.

One day, Fluffy and Tim were playing in the yard. Fluffy did not know where his favorite toy was. He looked and looked, but he could not find it. Tim saw Fluffy was sad, so he said, "Don't worry, Fluffy. I will help you find your toy."

Tim and Fluffy looked all around the yard. They looked under the big tree, behind the little bush, and even in the tall grass. Then, Tim saw the toy hiding in the flowers. "There it is, Fluffy!" he said. Fluffy was so happy to have his toy back.

They played with the toy for a long time. Fluffy and Tim laughed and had lots of fun. After they were tired, Tim gave Fluffy a big rub. They were very happy to have each other as friends.

Once upon a time, there was a kind person. This person needed to paint a picture for their friend. But before the person started to paint, they decided to have a snack. They ate a yummy treat to give them energy for the painting.

The kind person was painting for a very long time. They used the paintbrush to make a beautiful picture of a rainbow. The picture was so colorful it made people smile.

Finally, the painting was done. The kind person thought the picture was wonderful. Then they ran to show their friend the completed painting.

The friend was thrilled with the painting. They thanked the kind person and gave them a hug. It was a happy ending to the kind person's painting adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a clever little girl who loved to go on adventures. Her favorite thing to do was go to the fun camp in her town. Whenever she went to camp, she loved to learn and improve her skills.

At camp, she would play games, practice sports, and make new friends. Every day she did something new, something to make her even cleverer and better at the things she enjoyed.

The camp was always so much fun, and she could not wait to go back again. Even though the little girl improved her skills each time she went, the camp was always a magical new experience.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He went to the beach with his mommy and daddy. The beach was very big and had lots of sand.

Timmy saw a new friend playing in the sand. His name was Billy. Timmy's mommy and daddy introduced him to Billy. Billy was very charming and had a big smile.

Timmy and Billy played in the sand and built a big castle together. They had so much fun and became good friends. Timmy was happy that his mommy and daddy introduced him to Billy. They all had a great day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was an orange dolphin in the ocean. He loved swimming around and having adventures with his friends.

One day, he came across a big, shiny object floating in the water. He wanted to get a closer look, so he swam to it. Suddenly, the object began to move and it locked him inside!

The orange dolphin started to panic and he cried out for help. A school of fishes swam over and told him that he must look for a key to unlock the object.

The orange dolphin searched further in the ocean and he found a small key inside a clam. He used the key to unlock the object and he was set free!

The moral of the story is that it is important never to give up when something gets in the way. If you stay positive and keep looking for solutions, you can find a way to overcome any problem.

Once there was a boy named Bob. He was not very wealthy, but he was happy. One day Bob was walking in the park and he saw a big, fluffy cloud in the sky. He thought it looked so soft and snugly that he wanted to steal it! So Bob reached up high and tried to grab the cloud. But it was too far away.

Bob was sad and he thought he could never get the cloud. A kindly wealthy man saw Bob and said, "I can help you, Bob." The man pulled a long stick out of his coat and gave it to Bob. He said, "Now you can reach the cloud!"

Bob took the stick and swung it up to the sky. He had never seen anything so beautiful! He grabbed hold of the cloud and held tight. Before the man could say a word, Bob ran off with his stolen cloud.

Bob was so happy! He ran around, laughing and twirling all day with his new cloud close to him. He showed it to his friends, who all thought it was the best cloud ever. And Bob never felt so happy and wealthy.

Timmy and Tim were two brothers who loved to explore the streets of their town. One day, they decided to separate and each take a different street. Timmy was very eager to get started but Tim was a little bit scared to walk off on his own.

Timmy said, "Let's go! We can explore different streets and meet up at the corner!"

Tim nervously said, "Okay, I guess." So, the two of them hugged and said goodbye.

Timmy ran eagerly down the street, looking around at all the sights. He passed by a big park and saw some funny red birds. He even stopped to feed a squirrel by the pond.

Meanwhile, Tim was cautiously walking to the corner. He tried not to look around too much and got there faster than he expected.

When Tim arrived at the corner, there was Timmy waiting for him with a big smile and a surprise! It was a small toy car they had spotted in the park.

Timmy laughed and said, "Let's go home now!" And so, the two brothers happily skipped along the street, holding hands.

Once upon a time there was a skeleton. He was very polite and he liked to move around. He danced in the fields and skipped by the trees. He even moved inside some big, old houses! The skeleton moved all day.

He was so polite that he said 'hello' and 'thank you' to everyone he came across. He heard them call him the 'polite skeleton' and he was so proud!

One day he was walking down a big road and he came across a river. The skeleton moved to the other side and thought he would take a rest. He laid down by the river and closed his eyes for a nap. Suddenly, he felt something move around his feet! He opened his eyes and it was a little three year old child playing with him!

The skeleton was so polite that he said 'hello' to the little boy and acted friendly. And from then on, the polite skeleton and the little three year old boy were the best of friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to fish with his dad. They would go to the lake and sit on the dock with their fishing poles. Timmy's dad would put a worm on the hook and they would wait for a fish to come.

One day, Timmy felt something tug on his line. He grabbed the fishing pole and started to reel it in. It was a big fish! Timmy was so excited. He showed his dad the fish and they took a picture together.

After they caught some more fish, they went home. Timmy's mom cooked the fish for dinner. It tasted normal, but Timmy was proud that he caught it himself. He couldn't wait to go fishing again with his dad.

Once upon a time there was a white hippo. The hippo was so cute and small. It could not walk or run, so it had to crawl everywhere.
One day, the white hippo saw a little boy. He was playing in the garden and he was very happy.
The white hippo crawled closer to the boy and said in a soft voice, "Hello there! What are you doing?"

The boy looked at the white hippo in surprise and said, "I'm playing hide and seek with my friends!"

The white hippo smiled and said, "That sounds like a lot of fun. Can I play too?"

The boy nodded and said, "Yes, let's play! You have to try to find us and we have to try to find you!"

The white hippo crawled around the garden a few times and enjoyed the game very much. When everyone was tired and the game was over, the white hippo said goodbye and crawled away.

The boy was sad to say goodbye to the white hippo, but he knew that soon enough he would be back to play hide and seek with him again.

Jack was in his office when he heard a knock on the door. He opened it and saw Mark standing in the doorway. Mark said, "Can I come in?"

Jack smiled and said, "Sure! What can I do for you?"

Mark replied, "I wanted to talk to you about something foolish I did. I wanted to see if you could help me."

Jack said, "What did you do?"

Mark sighed and said, "I broke my friend's toy. I didn't mean to, but I was playing too rough and I made a mistake."

Jack said, "That was foolish, Mark. We should talk about how to make things right with your friend." So Jack and Mark talked through the situation together. In the end, Mark promised to apologize to his friend and explain what had happened. Jack said, "That sounds like a plan. You are a smart kid, Mark!"

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily wanted to go to the park. She put on her shoes and asked her mom, "Can I go to the park, please?" Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful, and don't go too far."

At the park, Lily saw a fragile butterfly. She wanted to play with it. She tried to turn around to catch it, but she was not fast enough. The butterfly flew away. Lily was sad and wanted to find the butterfly again.

Lily looked everywhere in the park for the butterfly. She saw a big tree and thought the butterfly might be there. As she went to the tree, she found a boy named Tim. Tim was also looking for the butterfly. They both wanted the butterfly, but there was only one. They decided to take turns to catch it. Lily tried first, but she could not catch it. Then Tim tried, and he caught the butterfly. He shared it with Lily, and they both were happy. They played together at the park until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time there was a cat. His name was Billy. He liked to jog a lot. Every morning he would wake up and run around the neighbourhood. He was so graceful and fast.

One day, he left his house and started to jog. But when he came around the corner he saw something he had never seen before. It was a lot of traffic. Cars, buses and people were all in his way. But Billy was still brave. He gathered his courage and started to jog through the traffic.

Everyone stopped and looked at Billy. They couldn't believe how gracefully he weaved between the vehicles. Even the loudest cars thanked Billy for making the traffic less noisy.

Billy felt proud and kept jogging. He showed everyone that anyone can be brave and graceful if they try.

LILY AND THE LION

A merchant, who had three daughters, was once setting out upon a

journey; but before he went he asked each daughter what gift he should

bring back for her. The eldest wished for pearls; the second for jewels;

but the third, who was called Lily, said, 'Dear father, bring me a

rose.' Now it was no easy task to find a rose, for it was the middle

of winter; yet as she was his prettiest daughter, and was very fond of

flowers, her father said he would try what he could do. So he kissed all

three, and bid them goodbye.

And when the time came for him to go home, he had bought pearls and

jewels for the two eldest, but he had sought everywhere in vain for the

rose; and when he went into any garden and asked for such a thing, the

people laughed at him, and asked him whether he thought roses grew in

snow. This grieved him very much, for Lily was his dearest child; and as

he was journeying home, thinking what he should bring her, he came to a

fine castle; and around the castle was a garden, in one half of which it

seemed to be summer-time and in the other half winter. On one side the

finest flowers were in full bloom, and on the other everything looked

dreary and buried in the snow. 'A lucky hit!' said he, as he called to

his servant, and told him to go to a beautiful bed of roses that was

there, and bring him away one of the finest flowers.

This done, they were riding away well pleased, when up sprang a fierce

lion, and roared out, 'Whoever has stolen my roses shall be eaten up

alive!' Then the man said, 'I knew not that the garden belonged to you;

can nothing save my life?' 'No!' said the lion, 'nothing, unless you

undertake to give me whatever meets you on your return home; if you

agree to this, I will give you your life, and the rose too for your

daughter.' But the man was unwilling to do so and said, 'It may be my

youngest daughter, who loves me most, and always runs to meet me when

I go home.' Then the servant was greatly frightened, and said, 'It may

perhaps be only a cat or a dog.' And at last the man yielded with a

heavy heart, and took the rose; and said he would give the lion whatever

should meet him first on his return.

And as he came near home, it was Lily, his youngest and dearest

daughter, that met him; she came running, and kissed him, and welcomed

him home; and when she saw that he had brought her the rose, she was

still more glad. But her father began to be very sorrowful, and to weep,

saying, 'Alas, my dearest child! I have bought this flower at a high

price, for I have said I would give you to a wild lion; and when he has

you, he will tear you in pieces, and eat you.' Then he told her all that

had happened, and said she should not go, let what would happen.

But she comforted him, and said, 'Dear father, the word you have given

must be kept; I will go to the lion, and soothe him: perhaps he will let

me come safe home again.'

The next morning she asked the way she was to go, and took leave of her

father, and went forth with a bold heart into the wood. But the lion was

an enchanted prince. By day he and all his court were lions, but in the

evening they took their right forms again. And when Lily came to the

castle, he welcomed her so courteously that she agreed to marry him. The

wedding-feast was held, and they lived happily together a long time. The

prince was only to be seen as soon as evening came, and then he held his

court; but every morning he left his bride, and went away by himself,

she knew not whither, till the night came again.

After some time he said to her, 'Tomorrow there will be a great feast in

your father's house, for your eldest sister is to be married; and if

you wish to go and visit her my lions shall lead you thither.' Then she

rejoiced much at the thoughts of seeing her father once more, and set

out with the lions; and everyone was overjoyed to see her, for they had

thought her dead long since. But she told them how happy she was, and

stayed till the feast was over, and then went back to the wood.

Her second sister was soon after married, and when Lily was asked to

go to the wedding, she said to the prince, 'I will not go alone this

time--you must go with me.' But he would not, and said that it would be

a very hazardous thing; for if the least ray of the torch-light should

fall upon him his enchantment would become still worse, for he should be

changed into a dove, and be forced to wander about the world for seven

long years. However, she gave him no rest, and said she would take care

no light should fall upon him. So at last they set out together, and

took with them their little child; and she chose a large hall with thick

walls for him to sit in while the wedding-torches were lighted; but,

unluckily, no one saw that there was a crack in the door. Then the

wedding was held with great pomp, but as the train came from the church,

and passed with the torches before the hall, a very small ray of light

fell upon the prince. In a moment he disappeared, and when his wife came

in and looked for him, she found only a white dove; and it said to her,

'Seven years must I fly up and down over the face of the earth, but

every now and then I will let fall a white feather, that will show you

the way I am going; follow it, and at last you may overtake and set me

free.'

This said, he flew out at the door, and poor Lily followed; and every

now and then a white feather fell, and showed her the way she was to

journey. Thus she went roving on through the wide world, and looked

neither to the right hand nor to the left, nor took any rest, for seven

years. Then she began to be glad, and thought to herself that the time

was fast coming when all her troubles should end; yet repose was still

far off, for one day as she was travelling on she missed the white

feather, and when she lifted up her eyes she could nowhere see the dove.

'Now,' thought she to herself, 'no aid of man can be of use to me.' So

she went to the sun and said, 'Thou shinest everywhere, on the hill's

top and the valley's depth--hast thou anywhere seen my white dove?'

'No,' said the sun, 'I have not seen it; but I will give thee a

casket--open it when thy hour of need comes.'

So she thanked the sun, and went on her way till eventide; and when

the moon arose, she cried unto it, and said, 'Thou shinest through the

night, over field and grove--hast thou nowhere seen my white dove?'

'No,' said the moon, 'I cannot help thee but I will give thee an

egg--break it when need comes.'

Then she thanked the moon, and went on till the night-wind blew; and she

raised up her voice to it, and said, 'Thou blowest through every tree

and under every leaf--hast thou not seen my white dove?' 'No,' said the

night-wind, 'but I will ask three other winds; perhaps they have seen

it.' Then the east wind and the west wind came, and said they too had

not seen it, but the south wind said, 'I have seen the white dove--he

has fled to the Red Sea, and is changed once more into a lion, for the

seven years are passed away, and there he is fighting with a dragon;

and the dragon is an enchanted princess, who seeks to separate him from

you.' Then the night-wind said, 'I will give thee counsel. Go to the

Red Sea; on the right shore stand many rods--count them, and when thou

comest to the eleventh, break it off, and smite the dragon with it; and

so the lion will have the victory, and both of them will appear to you

in their own forms. Then look round and thou wilt see a griffin, winged

like bird, sitting by the Red Sea; jump on to his back with thy beloved

one as quickly as possible, and he will carry you over the waters to

your home. I will also give thee this nut,' continued the night-wind.

'When you are half-way over, throw it down, and out of the waters will

immediately spring up a high nut-tree on which the griffin will be able

to rest, otherwise he would not have the strength to bear you the whole

way; if, therefore, thou dost forget to throw down the nut, he will let

you both fall into the sea.'

So our poor wanderer went forth, and found all as the night-wind had

said; and she plucked the eleventh rod, and smote the dragon, and the

lion forthwith became a prince, and the dragon a princess again. But

no sooner was the princess released from the spell, than she seized

the prince by the arm and sprang on to the griffin's back, and went off

carrying the prince away with her.

Thus the unhappy traveller was again forsaken and forlorn; but she

took heart and said, 'As far as the wind blows, and so long as the cock

crows, I will journey on, till I find him once again.' She went on for

a long, long way, till at length she came to the castle whither the

princess had carried the prince; and there was a feast got ready, and

she heard that the wedding was about to be held. 'Heaven aid me now!'

said she; and she took the casket that the sun had given her, and found

that within it lay a dress as dazzling as the sun itself. So she put it

on, and went into the palace, and all the people gazed upon her; and

the dress pleased the bride so much that she asked whether it was to be

sold. 'Not for gold and silver.' said she, 'but for flesh and blood.'

The princess asked what she meant, and she said, 'Let me speak with the

bridegroom this night in his chamber, and I will give thee the dress.'

At last the princess agreed, but she told her chamberlain to give the

prince a sleeping draught, that he might not hear or see her. When

evening came, and the prince had fallen asleep, she was led into

his chamber, and she sat herself down at his feet, and said: 'I have

followed thee seven years. I have been to the sun, the moon, and the

night-wind, to seek thee, and at last I have helped thee to overcome

the dragon. Wilt thou then forget me quite?' But the prince all the time

slept so soundly, that her voice only passed over him, and seemed like

the whistling of the wind among the fir-trees.

Then poor Lily was led away, and forced to give up the golden dress; and

when she saw that there was no help for her, she went out into a meadow,

and sat herself down and wept. But as she sat she bethought herself of

the egg that the moon had given her; and when she broke it, there ran

out a hen and twelve chickens of pure gold, that played about, and then

nestled under the old one's wings, so as to form the most beautiful

sight in the world. And she rose up and drove them before her, till the

bride saw them from her window, and was so pleased that she came forth

and asked her if she would sell the brood. 'Not for gold or silver, but

for flesh and blood: let me again this evening speak with the bridegroom

in his chamber, and I will give thee the whole brood.'

Then the princess thought to betray her as before, and agreed to

what she asked: but when the prince went to his chamber he asked

the chamberlain why the wind had whistled so in the night. And the

chamberlain told him all--how he had given him a sleeping draught, and

how a poor maiden had come and spoken to him in his chamber, and was

to come again that night. Then the prince took care to throw away the

sleeping draught; and when Lily came and began again to tell him what

woes had befallen her, and how faithful and true to him she had been,

he knew his beloved wife's voice, and sprang up, and said, 'You have

awakened me as from a dream, for the strange princess had thrown a spell

around me, so that I had altogether forgotten you; but Heaven hath sent

you to me in a lucky hour.'

And they stole away out of the palace by night unawares, and seated

themselves on the griffin, who flew back with them over the Red Sea.

When they were half-way across Lily let the nut fall into the water,

and immediately a large nut-tree arose from the sea, whereon the griffin

rested for a while, and then carried them safely home. There they found

their child, now grown up to be comely and fair; and after all their

troubles they lived happily together to the end of their days.

THE OLD MAN AND HIS GRANDSON

There was once a very old man, whose eyes had become dim, his ears dull

of hearing, his knees trembled, and when he sat at table he could hardly

hold the spoon, and spilt the broth upon the table-cloth or let it run

out of his mouth. His son and his son's wife were disgusted at this, so

the old grandfather at last had to sit in the corner behind the stove,

and they gave him his food in an earthenware bowl, and not even enough

of it. And he used to look towards the table with his eyes full of

tears. Once, too, his trembling hands could not hold the bowl, and it

fell to the ground and broke. The young wife scolded him, but he said

nothing and only sighed. Then they brought him a wooden bowl for a few

half-pence, out of which he had to eat.

They were once sitting thus when the little grandson of four years old

began to gather together some bits of wood upon the ground. 'What are

you doing there?' asked the father. 'I am making a little trough,'

answered the child, 'for father and mother to eat out of when I am big.'

The man and his wife looked at each other for a while, and presently

began to cry. Then they took the old grandfather to the table, and

henceforth always let him eat with them, and likewise said nothing if he

did spill a little of anything.

One day, a little girl saw the two mice leaning together. She was so excited! She picked them up and put them into her pocket, then took them home.

The little girl loved when the mice leaned against each other, so she put them back in the same position and they continued to be best friends. The little girl was very happy. The real mouse and the fake mouse were very happy too, leaning together side by side.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Molly. She was only three years old but already very brave. One day, Molly decided to explore the forest near her house. As she walked, she heard a deep growl. Molly was scared as she looked up and saw a big monster.

The monster said, "Hi Molly. I'm Richie the Rich Monster. I'm stuck in this tree and I need your help to get out. Can you lift me? Please?"

Molly smiled as she watched Richie slowly make his way out of the forest. He waved farewell and said, "Goodbye, Molly!"

Jim was a chubby 3 year old boy who loved to eat. One day, he reached for his spoon, but it wasn't there! He turned to his mom and asked, "Where's my spoon?"

Mom replied, "I lent it to your sister. She needed it for her lunch."

"Can I have it back?" Jim asked.

"Sure," Mom said, handing him the spoon. "Here you go!"

Jim smiled and scooped up a big spoonful of food to eat. He was so happy to have his spoon back.

Tom liked to ride his horse, Spot. Spot was big and brown and fast. Tom and Spot went to the farm every day. They helped with the cows and the sheep and the pigs.

One day, Tom saw a new horse at the farm. It was black and shiny and had a long mane. Tom wanted to ride the new horse. He asked the farmer, "Can I ride that horse?"

The farmer said, "No, Tom. That horse is not for you. That horse is wild and mean. He will buck you off and hurt you. You should stay with Spot. He is a good horse."

But Tom did not listen. He waited until the farmer was busy. Then he sneaked to the new horse. He put a saddle and a bridle on the horse. He climbed on the horse. He said, "Giddy up!"

The horse did not like Tom. He did not like the saddle and the bridle. He did not like to be told what to do. He started to run and jump and kick. He tried to throw Tom off.

Tom was scared. He held on to the horse. He felt the saddle and the bridle were tight. He felt his arms and legs were tired. He wanted to quit. He wanted to go back to Spot. He cried, "Help! Help!"

The farmer heard Tom. He ran to the horse. He grabbed the reins and stopped the horse. He helped Tom get off the horse. He said, "Tom, are you okay? You should not have ridden that horse. Tom was sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, farmer. I'm sorry, Spot. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. I should have stayed with you. You are a good horse. Can I ride you again?"

Spot nuzzled Tom. He forgave Tom. He let Tom ride him again. Tom and Spot went back to the farm. They helped with the cows and the sheep and the pigs. They were happy.

Once there was a little girl who was three years old. She liked exploring and going for adventures. One day she decided to explore on her own in the woods and went in her vehicle. She felt safe and enjoyed the scenery all around her.

Suddenly, she heard a sound. It was very loud and surprised her. She started to feel scared. She looked around and saw a large animal at the edge of the woods. She became scared and drove her vehicle quickly away from the animal.

Finally, the little girl was able to drive to safety and she felt relieved. She was happy that she had been safe and was able to get away. She now knew to be careful whenever she is exploring on her own.

Once upon a time, there was a patch of grass. It was very small and it was in the middle of a big city. The patch was brilliant because it was the only bit of nature in the whole area.
Next to the patch, lived a small girl. She was only three years old and loved to play in the grass. She liked to pick the little flowers, and tell stories to the clouds.

But the patch was not always happy, the people around it walked on it, dogs ran on it and it didn't have enough rain. It started to look grey and dull.

One day, the girl decided to help the patch. She went and bought some special things to help it grow back to its brilliant colour. She put some special water and food on the patch, and she planted some new flowers.

Then she sat back and waited. A few days later, the patch had grown to be even greener and brighter than before. The little girl was so happy to see the patch back to its old self. She could now relax and play on it everyday.

Once upon a time there was a store. The store sold all sorts of things. Every day the store was perfect. People came from far away to visit it and buy things.

The store was also very kind. If someone needed help, the people at the store would support them. They would show them around and offer lots of friendly advice. Everybody loved the store.

One day an old lady came to visit the store. She wanted to buy some toys for her grandkids. The store was so helpful that she was able to buy the perfect toys.

The old lady was very happy and thanked the store. She said that the store and the people who worked there were so kind. Thanks to the store, she was able to find the perfect gifts for her grandkids. Everybody was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go to church with her family every Sunday. One day, Lily's mom asked her to count how many people were in the church. Lily counted and found out there were 50 people in the church.

After church, Lily's family went to a restaurant for lunch. Lily's food was not perfect, it was cold and not tasty. She was sad and didn't want to eat it. But her mom told her that it's important to be grateful for what we have, even if it's not perfect.

Lily learned that counting people in church is fun, but being grateful for what we have is more important. She promised to always be thankful for everything in her life, even if it's not perfect.

Once upon a time there was a ship that sailed on the sea. All of the people on board were having a wonderful time until they saw something terrible. A giant wave was coming towards them! Everyone was so scared, so they held on tight.

Suddenly, the wave came and it was so big that it made the ship go up and down. The people were terrified and clung to each other. But then something amazing happened. A big blue whale jumped out of the wave and started pushing the ship away from the wave. Everyone cheered with excitement and hugged each other.

The whale kept pushing until the wave was gone. The ship was safe. The whale then swam away. Everyone thanked the whale and knew that it had saved their lives.

The people all hugged each other, some even squeezed each other really tight. Everyone was so happy that they were safe and that the whale had saved them all.

Once there was a wise old owl. He was the wisest owl in the forest. Late one night, he began to think. "What is the meaning of life?" he thought.

Just then, he heard a tiny voice in the darkness. "Hello, Mr. Owl," said a small voice.

Startled, the owl looked around. Then he spotted the source of the voice - a small mouse was standing nearby.

The owl blinked in surprise. "What can I do for you, little friend?" he asked.

The mouse smiled shyly. "I think the meaning of life is to be happy," she said.

The owl thought for a moment, then smiled. "You are very wise for one so small," he said.

The mouse smiled back. Then, with a tiny wave, she scampered away.

The owl watched her go, still smiling. He knew that the mouse was right - being happy was indeed the meaning of life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved magic and dreamed of being a magician when she grew up. One day, she found a magic wand in the park. She waved it around, but nothing happened.

Suddenly, a bird fell out of a tree and hurt its wing. Lily wanted to help the bird, so she lifted it up gently and held it in her hands. She closed her eyes and whispered a magic spell. When she opened her eyes, the bird's wing was healed!

Lily was so happy and proud of herself. She knew that she was successful in using her magic. From that day on, she carried the magic wand with her wherever she went, always ready to help anyone in need.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Peter. Peter was only 3 years old, but he was already very brave. One day, he decided that he wanted to learn how to swim. So he went to his friends house and asked to learn.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the bakery with her mommy. Lily wanted to eat a yummy pastry, but her mommy said she had to wait until they got home. Lily was sad, but she didn't cry.

Suddenly, it started to rain outside. Lily's mommy said, "Oh no, our car seat is going to get wet!" Lily said, "Mommy, can we sit in the bakery and eat my pastry while we wait for the rain to stop?" Her mommy thought it was a good idea, so they went inside.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride the subway train with his mommy. One day, Timmy and his mommy were riding the blue subway train when they heard a loud noise.

"What was that noise?" asked Timmy.

Once upon a time, a little raven flew from its nest in search of something special. After flying for a while, the raven spotted a bright lake. As it perched on a nearby tree, it heard the most beautiful music coming from the lake.

The raven flew closer and saw a little girl by the lake's edge. In her hands the girl held a beautiful golden flute. She played her music which made the raven so happy that it began to dance.

The girl laughed and put down her flute. She looked up at the raven and said: "Oh, little raven, please accept my gift of music." The raven hopped down from the tree and lightly ate from the girl's hand. From then on the raven visited the girl every day and accepted her gift of music.

The little raven and the girl became great friends. They both enjoyed each others company and the music the girl played. The little raven looked forward to hearing the girl's music each and every day.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They had a big bag with toys and snacks. They liked to share and have fun.

But then a big dog came. It was orange and loud. It ran to the bag and grabbed it with its teeth. It ran away with the bag.

Tom and Lily were scared and sad. They wanted their bag back. They shouted at the dog, but it did not listen. It was too fast and too far.

They started to weep. They wept loud and hard. They did not know what to do.

A nice lady saw them. She had a blue hat and a green coat. She came to them and asked what was wrong.

"We lost our bag!" Tom said. "A big dog took it!"

"That's not good!" the lady said. "Do you know where the dog went?"

Lily pointed to the woods. "It went there!"

"Come with me," the lady said. "Maybe we can find it."

She took their hands and walked with them to the woods. She was kind and brave. She helped them look for the dog and the bag.

They found them behind a tree. The dog was playing with the toys and eating the snacks. It did not see them.

The lady had a plan. She took a stick and threw it. The dog saw the stick and ran after it. It dropped the bag.

Tom and Lily ran to the bag. They were happy and relieved. They hugged the bag and thanked the lady.

The lady smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you got your bag back. Now, let's go back to the park and have some more fun."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved tea parties with his friends. One day, Timmy's mommy made him a special tea party. THE WOLF AND THE SEVEN LITTLE KIDS

There was once upon a time an old goat who had seven little kids, and

loved them with all the love of a mother for her children. One day she

wanted to go into the forest and fetch some food. So she called all

seven to her and said: 'Dear children, I have to go into the forest,

be on your guard against the wolf; if he comes in, he will devour you

all--skin, hair, and everything. The wretch often disguises himself, but

you will know him at once by his rough voice and his black feet.' The

kids said: 'Dear mother, we will take good care of ourselves; you may go

away without any anxiety.' Then the old one bleated, and went on her way

with an easy mind.

It was not long before someone knocked at the house-door and called:

'Open the door, dear children; your mother is here, and has brought

something back with her for each of you.' But the little kids knew that

it was the wolf, by the rough voice. 'We will not open the door,' cried

they, 'you are not our mother. She has a soft, pleasant voice, but

your voice is rough; you are the wolf!' Then the wolf went away to a

shopkeeper and bought himself a great lump of chalk, ate this and made

his voice soft with it. Then he came back, knocked at the door of the

house, and called: 'Open the door, dear children, your mother is here

and has brought something back with her for each of you.' But the wolf

had laid his black paws against the window, and the children saw them

and cried: 'We will not open the door, our mother has not black feet

like you: you are the wolf!' Then the wolf ran to a baker and said: 'I

have hurt my feet, rub some dough over them for me.' And when the baker

had rubbed his feet over, he ran to the miller and said: 'Strew some

white meal over my feet for me.' The miller thought to himself: 'The

wolf wants to deceive someone,' and refused; but the wolf said: 'If you

will not do it, I will devour you.' Then the miller was afraid, and made

his paws white for him. Truly, this is the way of mankind.

So now the wretch went for the third time to the house-door, knocked at

it and said: 'Open the door for me, children, your dear little mother

has come home, and has brought every one of you something back from the

forest with her.' The little kids cried: 'First show us your paws that

we may know if you are our dear little mother.' Then he put his paws

in through the window and when the kids saw that they were white, they

believed that all he said was true, and opened the door. But who should

come in but the wolf! They were terrified and wanted to hide themselves.

One sprang under the table, the second into the bed, the third into the

stove, the fourth into the kitchen, the fifth into the cupboard, the

sixth under the washing-bowl, and the seventh into the clock-case. But

the wolf found them all, and used no great ceremony; one after the

other he swallowed them down his throat. The youngest, who was in

the clock-case, was the only one he did not find. When the wolf had

satisfied his appetite he took himself off, laid himself down under a

tree in the green meadow outside, and began to sleep. Soon afterwards

the old goat came home again from the forest. Ah! what a sight she saw

there! The house-door stood wide open. The table, chairs, and benches

were thrown down, the washing-bowl lay broken to pieces, and the quilts

and pillows were pulled off the bed. She sought her children, but they

were nowhere to be found. She called them one after another by name, but

no one answered. At last, when she came to the youngest, a soft voice

cried: 'Dear mother, I am in the clock-case.' She took the kid out, and

it told her that the wolf had come and had eaten all the others. Then

you may imagine how she wept over her poor children.

At length in her grief she went out, and the youngest kid ran with her.

When they came to the meadow, there lay the wolf by the tree and snored

so loud that the branches shook. She looked at him on every side and

saw that something was moving and struggling in his gorged belly. 'Ah,

heavens,' she said, 'is it possible that my poor children whom he has

swallowed down for his supper, can be still alive?' Then the kid had to

run home and fetch scissors, and a needle and thread, and the goat cut

open the monster's stomach, and hardly had she made one cut, than one

little kid thrust its head out, and when she had cut farther, all six

sprang out one after another, and were all still alive, and had suffered

no injury whatever, for in his greediness the monster had swallowed them

down whole. What rejoicing there was! They embraced their dear mother,

and jumped like a tailor at his wedding. The mother, however, said: 'Now

go and look for some big stones, and we will fill the wicked beast's

stomach with them while he is still asleep.' Then the seven kids dragged

the stones thither with all speed, and put as many of them into this

stomach as they could get in; and the mother sewed him up again in the

greatest haste, so that he was not aware of anything and never once

stirred.

When the wolf at length had had his fill of sleep, he got on his legs,

and as the stones in his stomach made him very thirsty, he wanted to

go to a well to drink. But when he began to walk and to move about, the

stones in his stomach knocked against each other and rattled. Then cried

he:

'What rumbles and tumbles

Against my poor bones?

I thought 'twas six kids,

But it feels like big stones.'

And when he got to the well and stooped over the water to drink, the

heavy stones made him fall in, and he drowned miserably. When the seven

kids saw that, they came running to the spot and cried aloud: 'The wolf

is dead! The wolf is dead!' and danced for joy round about the well with

their mother.

Peter was a little boy who loved adventure. He was out in his backyard, exploring one day when he saw something sparkly. He pushed away the leaves and saw it was a tiny box. He opened it up and saw a bright green mint inside. It looked clean and smelled sweet.

Peter was amazed. He didn't know what a mint was but he wanted to try it. He picked it up, and it felt cold and smooth in his palm. He put it in his mouth and was surprised by how it tasted. It was delicious and refreshing.

Grandma became very rude and shouted, "Answer me, John!" John suddenly remembered that he had brought a toy car, so he showed it to Grandma.

Grandma smiled and said, "That's nice, let's play with it together." John felt much better and he happily said "Yes!"

Tom likes to polish his dad's razor. He thinks it is a shiny toy that makes his dad's face smooth. He waits for his dad to go to work, then he sneaks into the bathroom and takes the razor from the drawer. He rubs it with a cloth until it sparkles.

One day, Tom sees a unique thing on the wall. It is a big mirror that shows him and the razor. He wonders what will happen if he touches the razor to his face. He thinks it will make him look like his dad. He lifts the razor and moves it closer to his cheek.

But the razor is not a toy. It is sharp and hurts Tom. He feels a sting and sees red on his face and on the mirror. He drops the razor and starts to cry. He runs to his mom and shows her his boo-boo. She is scared and angry. She hugs him and puts a band-aid on his cut. She tells him to never touch the razor again. She says it is dangerous and not for kids.

Tom is sorry and sad. He does not want to polish the razor anymore. He says he is sorry to his mom and his dad. He learns his lesson and plays with his safe toys instead. He likes his cars and his blocks and his teddy bear. He does not need the razor to look like his dad. He loves his dad and his dad loves him, even with a band-aid on his face.

Mummy was playing a puzzle with her daughter. She held up a piece that fit in the puzzle and said to her daughter, "I think this piece goes here."

The daughter smiled and replied, "It does! I can see it now." She took the piece and placed it in the puzzle.

Mummy was so proud of her and said, "You are so dependable. You make me very happy."

The daughter smiled and replied, "Thanks Mummy!" Then she kept playing with the puzzle.

Mummy wanted to make sure her daughter had fun, so she said, "Do you need some help?"

The daughter shook her head and replied, "No, I can do it. I'm a dependable puzzle master!"

Mummy laughed and gave her daughter a hug. "You make me so proud. I love you."

The daughter smiled and replied, "I love you too, Mummy."

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl who was very adventurous. She often dreamed of traveling to far away places. One day, she ventured deep into the forest; her heart full of excitement.

As she wandered through the trees, she stumbled upon a deep and dark chest. She had no idea what was inside! She peered into the chest, and was surprised to recognize something glimmering in the shadows. She opened the chest, and found a beautiful map!

The girl's eyes lit up with wonder. With this magical map, she could navigate to any place she wanted. She quickly tucked the map into her pocket and hurried off on many exciting adventures.

Happy and fulfilled with each journey, the little girl thanked the mysterious chest for aiding her on her way. She will recognize the magical chest whenever she passes by.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved playing hockey. He would go to the park every day to play with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend Billy fell down and hurt his leg. Timmy said, "Billy, are you okay?" Billy said, "No, my leg hurts so much. I can't seat." Timmy said, "Don't worry, I'll help you." Timmy helped Billy to seat down on the bench. Billy said, "Thank you, Timmy. You're a good friend." Timmy said, "No problem, I don't want you to be dead."

Mary was playing in the garden. She had her favourite toy car and she was driving it around, around and around.

Suddenly, she heard a sigh. She looked up and saw an old man. He was sitting near the garden, and he looked frustrated.

Mary walked up to him. "What's wrong?" she asked.

The man smiled. "I'm trying to remember something," he said. "But I can't. I'm so frustrated!"

Mary put her hand on his shoulder. "I have some memories," she said. "Do you want to play with me and make some new memories?"

The man smiled again and nodded.

So they started playing. Soon enough they both laughed and they it was like they had known each other for a long time. They made some great memories that day.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Julia. They both loved to do Fun things together. One day they decided to go to the park.

When they got there, they saw a funny looking tree. It had lots of colorful arrows sticking out of the trunk!

Jack said to Julia, "Let's share some arrows!" Julia was really excited.

So, they each picked one arrow and got comfortable. Jack looked up to the sky and said, "Let's fly our arrows and watch them soar!"

So, they both flew their arrows into the air and watched them soar. They laughed and shouted in excitement until the arrows came down.

At the end of the day, Jack and Julia high-fived each other and said, "That was so Fun!"

Once upon a time there was a reliable car that liked to drive. Every spring it would drive up and down the road. It would take people to places like the park and the store. One day, the car drove to the park. It stopped in front of the playground. Out came two kids, one was three and one was five. They quickly ran to the slide, giggling and laughing. Then, the car drove to the store. The three year old got out and ran inside to buy candy. The five year old stayed in the car. The car drove the kid home and parked in the driveway. The kids said goodbye to the car and thanked it for taking them on such a fun drive. The reliable car drove off, happy it had made the kids so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty kitty who lived with its mommy in a nice home. The kitty was always so careful, but one day it noticed something strange. A thief had snuck into their home while they were sleeping. The kitty grazed the furry creature and soon realized it was not its mommy.

The thief was scared, so it quickly ran away. The kitty jumped up and chased after it. The thief could not get away fast enough, but it was still able to make it far away. Mommy came out of the house and saw the kitty gone. She called for her, but the kitty was too far away and couldn't hear.

Mommy searched the entire neighborhood, but she couldn't recognize the thief or the kitty. She started to get scared and soon worried that the thief had taken away her pretty kitty. After much searching, she sadly went home without the kitty. The kitty never returned home and was never seen again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day she saw a big curtain on the wall. She was curious and wanted to see what was behind it. She pulled the curtain open and saw a room filled with delicious treats! She was so excited but confused too.

Lucy had found a kitchen! There were cakes, ice cream, and juice galore! Her mouth was watering at what she saw. So she decided to try some of the delicious drinks. She grabbed a cup off the counter and took a sip. It was so yummy! She drank some more and more until the cup was empty. Lucy felt happy and content.

But just then, the curtain moved! Lucy was so surprised and confused! It was her mom! Mom had been looking for her and was relieved to find out she was safe. Lucy's mom hugged her tightly and they both returned to the living room. Mom said "No more exploring without permission!"

And from then on, Lucy never forgot to ask her mom if she could explore.

Once there was a fisherman who loved to go out on the lake. Every morning he would go out to try and catch some fish. One day, he decided to go a little further out than usual. He was very alert as he looked around, hoping to spot some fish. Suddenly, he saw a big school of fish swimming by! He started to cast his net quickly, hoping to supply himself with some fish. The fisherman was very successful, and he managed to catch lots of fish! He was so pleased with his catch that he went home very happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old, and she loved exploring.

One day, Anna went on a search for a special rock. She searched and searched and searched, but she couldn't find one that she liked. Suddenly, she saw a delicate rock by a tree.

Anna ran over to it, and she was so excited. She picked it up carefully in her hands and said:

"Wow! This rock is perfect!"

Anna took the rock home and kept it forever. Whenever she held it, it reminded her of her special search!

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old, but she was already so smart. On this sunny day, she wanted to go play in the park.

Lucy's mom put on her shoes and took her to the park. The park was filled with lots of fun things. But Lucy's favorite was the swing. She ran up to the swing and sat down. Then she put her hands on the rope and said, "Mommy, swing me!"

Her mom smiled and said, "Okay". She held the swing and pushed Lucy back and forth. It felt like Lucy was flying through the air! She laughed and said, "Again, again!"

Suddenly, Lucy noticed a wealthy family with a little boy playing on the other side of the park. She pointed to them and said, "Mommy, look! What are they doing?"

Her mom replied, "That little boy and his family are playing a game. See, they are kicking a ball with their knees. It's called soccer."

Lucy jumped off the swing and said, "I want to play soccer too, Mommy!"

So Lucy and her Mom played a game of soccer with their knees. They had a lot of fun and laughed the whole time. Lucy was so happy that she wanted to play soccer every day!

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to swim. She wanted to go swim in the sea but it was too far away, so she decided to swim in the lake near her home. She was so excited!

When she reached the lake, the girl was amazed by the sparkly, still water. She put on her special swimsuit and jumped into the lake. She swam around for a long time, feeling the powerful strength of the water.

The girl decided to try something new and she began to stir the water with her hands and feet. She was amazed by what happened: the water formed into beautiful patterns! She continued stirring and it made her feel so excited and happy.

Once she was done, the girl felt very proud of herself. She had discovered a new way to enjoy the water and she felt so powerful.

The girl smiled and silently thanked the lake for such a wonderful experience. She then jumped back in and enjoyed her swim.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Blue. Blue loved to sing and fly around with his friends. One day, Blue noticed that his singing was not as good as his friends' songs. He felt sad and wanted to improve his singing.

Blue decided to practice every day. He would sing in the morning, afternoon, and evening. His friends noticed that Blue was working hard and started to encourage him. They would sing along with him and give him tips on how to improve.

One day, Blue's friend Red got very sick and couldn't fly anymore. Blue was sad and didn't know what to do. He wanted to help his friend turn better. Blue remembered that his mother had told him about a special seed that could make sick things better.

Blue flew to his mother and asked for the seed. She gave it to him and Blue flew back to Red. He put the seed in Red's nest and waited. After a few days, Red started to turn better. He could fly again and sing with Blue. Blue was very happy that he could help his friend turn better from being dead.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mommy cook in the kitchen. One day, her mommy was making a cake and asked Lily to mix the batter. Lily loved to mix and stir things, so she happily did it.

After the cake was in the oven, Lily went outside to play. She found some wood and started building a little house for her dolls. She loved the smell of the wood and how it felt in her hands.

When the cake was done, Lily's mommy took it out of the oven and put some spicy frosting on top. Lily couldn't wait to try it. She took a big bite, but it was too spicy for her. She didn't like it at all.

Lily started to feel sick and her mommy had to take her to the hospital. The doctor said that the spicy frosting made her very sick and she had to stay in the hospital for a long time. Lily learned that sometimes things that look and smell good can be bad for you.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to clap her hands. She would often applaud her family, friends and teachers when something special happened. One day, she decided to show her appreciation for her mother when she cooked up some delicious broccoli.

"Yay!" the little girl shouted as she jumped up and down and started to applaud.

Her mother smiled and said "Thank you, sweetie. That sure was nice."

The little girl's face suddenly fell. "I'm sorry, Mama," she said. "I didn't realize that I made a mess. I'm so sorry!"

The mother stopped what she was doing and said "It's alright, sweetie. Accidents happen. Don't worry, I forgive you."

The little girl smiled and celebrated by clapping her hands even louder. This time, both of them applauded together. The little girl knew that her mum always understood her, and that made her very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful palace that everyone wanted to visit. Inside the palace lived a kind and friendly King. His subjects were very happy and content because the King was so generous.

One day, the King decided to raise a baby elephant. He loved the little elephant so much and every day he would spend hours taking care of it. Soon, the King's subjects became jealous of the attention that the King lavished on the baby elephant.

They grew even more jealous when the King decided to build a special palace for the elephant. It had the best beds, and the most delicious food. Everyone wanted to live in the palace, but the King made sure that only the elephant was able to enjoy its comforts.

The King and the elephant lived happily together in their palace, and everyone around them recognized that the King had made the right decision by raising the elephant.

Ben and Lily are brother and sister. They like to play together. Sometimes they play with toys, sometimes they play with books, sometimes they play with puzzles.

One day, they want to play with TV. TV is big and shiny. It has many colors and sounds. Ben and Lily like to watch TV.

But Mom says, "No, TV is not for playing. TV is for watching. You can watch TV for a little time, but then you have to play with something else."

Ben and Lily are sad. They want to play with TV more. They ask Mom, "Why can't we play with TV? TV is fun. TV is nice."

Mom says, "TV is fun and nice, but TV is not good for you if you watch too much. TV can make your eyes tired and your brain sleepy. You need to play with other things that make your eyes happy and your brain smart. Like toys, books, puzzles, or outside."

Ben and Lily think about it. They like to make their eyes happy and their brain smart. They say, "OK, Mom. We will watch TV for a little time, and then we will play with other things."

Mom smiles and says, "Good. I love you, Ben and Lily. You are good children."

Ben and Lily watch TV for a little time. They see animals and songs and stories. They laugh and clap and sing. Then they turn off TV and go to play with other things. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient castle. Inside the castle was a beautiful garden full of flowers and trees. In the garden there was a special strawberry patch. Every day the prince and princess would walk in the garden and admire the display of strawberries.

The strawberries were very tasty, and the prince and princess would pick them and eat them. They liked their sweet taste and would laugh as they ate them. Soon the birds heard about the delicious strawberries and would come to take a few to eat.

The prince and princess liked to share the strawberries with the birds. They would watch as they flew away with the ancient strawberries they had given them. Every day they enjoyed the strawberry display in their garden. They were the happiest prince and princess around!

The two friends were very excited. They were travelling to a new country. There were going to be so many busy and interesting things to see and do.

The two friends arrived at their destination. The first thing they had to do was to unpack their bags. One of the friends asked: "What's an unpack?"

The other friend replied: "An unpack means you take the things out of your bag so that you can use them."

The first friend was so excited. He asked: "Can I unpack my bag too?"

The second friend said: "Yes, of course you can!"

So the two friends unpacked their bags. Inside, there were lots of new, exciting things from the new country. They couldn't wait to explore and have fun.

The two friends were so happy. They were ready to have a busy and fun adventure in the new country!

One day, Tim woke up early. Outside, there was a heavy mist. Everything was grey and cloudy. He looked outside and saw that the fog was so thick he could not even see his friend's house!

He wanted to go outside and play, so he put on his jacket. He was careful not to get lost in the thick mist. Instead of going too far, he stayed in the garden.

He played in the mist for a while, running around, feeling the wet drops of mist on his face. He chased his dog and felt the cold and heavy mist wrap around him.

He laughed and smiled as he ran, until finally he was all tuckered out and went back inside, safe and happy after his morning adventure in the mist.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very excited because he was going to take a bath. He loved playing with his toy boat and making big splashes in the water.

"Mom, can I have the soap?" Tim asked. His mom gave him the soap, and he started to make lots of bubbles. But then, he saw a big spider on the wall. Tim began to panic. "Mom, help! There's a spider!" he cried.

His mom came running and saw the spider. But when she tried to catch it, the spider jumped into the water. Tim screamed and jumped out of the tub. The spider swam away, and Tim was too scared to take a bath again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Grace. Grace liked to play outside in the sunshine. One day, Grace walked to the market to get a melon. She looked around the market, but there were none. She was getting a little restless.

But then, she heard a voice. It was the voice of a kind shopkeeper. He said to Grace, "I can order a special melon for you!" Grace smiled.

The shopkeeper went away and came back a few minutes later with a huge, juicy melon. Grace was very happy. She thanked the shopkeeper and took it home.

At home, Grace ate the melon and it was so sweet and delicious. She felt so happy.

The end.

Once upon a time, a young boy named Tim liked to study his toys. One day, he found a long chain in his toy box. He looked at it and thought it was very interesting.

Tim showed the chain to his friend, Sally. "Look at my chain," he said. Sally looked at it and said, "Wow, that's a big chain!" Tim and Sally played with the chain all day. They made it into a big circle and pretended it was a race track for their toy cars.

As the sun went down, Tim and Sally knew it was time to go home. They put the chain back in the toy box and said goodbye. Tim was happy that he had a fun day with his friend and the chain. He knew he would study it more tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely tree in a big park. All the other trees had many friends, but the lonely tree had none. The lonely tree was very sad.

One sunny day, a little girl named Lucy came to the park. She saw the lonely tree and said, "Hello, tree! Why are you so sad?" The tree replied, "I am lonely because I have no friends."

Lucy thought for a moment and said, "I will be your friend!" The lonely tree was happy to gain a new friend. They played together in the park every day. The tree was not lonely anymore, and they both lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Jake. He was three years old and he was always looking for something new to do and explore.

One day, Jake wanted to find a new restaurant. He asked his mom and dad if he could go with them to one. They said yes and they drove away.

When they got to the restaurant, Jake was so excited. He peeked through the windows and saw how clean it was. He wanted to go inside, but he had to wait until they were done eating.

Finally, they were done, and they let Jake enter. He couldn't wait to explore. He peeked behind the counter and looked in the back rooms. He even peeked in the kitchen and saw the chefs cooking!

Jake was so happy that he got to peek in the restaurant. He promised himself he would come back to peek again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she was playing with her toy car when her mom came in and said, "Lily, it's time to clean up your toys."

Lily didn't want to stop playing, but she knew she had to listen to her mom. So, she turned off her toy car and started putting away all of her toys. As she was cleaning, she found a puzzle that she had never finished before. She thought it would be interesting to try and finish it, so she asked her mom if she could keep playing for a little longer.

Her mom said yes, and Lily started working on the puzzle. It was really hard, but she didn't give up. After a while, she finally finished it! She was so happy with the result and showed her mom.

Her mom was proud of her for not giving up and finishing the puzzle. She told Lily that sometimes things might be hard, but if she keeps trying, she can accomplish anything. Lily learned that it's important to never give up and to always try her best.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sandy who was always looking for adventure. One day, Sandy decided to go explore a quiet valley nearby. She walked and walked until she reached the valley. When she got there, Sandy was in for a big surprise.

In the middle of the valley was a big tree with a strange box beneath it! Sandy was very curious and opened it - she found a big pile of sweets inside! Her eyes were wide with joy.

Suddenly, another little girl appeared on the other side of the valley. She saw the box and ran towards it too. Sandy and the other girl started to fight for the candy. Sandy wasn't sure what to do - should she share the sweets with the other girl or keep them for herself?

In the end, Sandy decided to share and split the sweets. Both of them were smiling and happy! Sandy realised that it was much better to be kind and share than to fight. She left the valley with a lesson learned.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny called Chloe. Chloe was so excited because today she was going to have a nap. She took off down the garden path and hopped until she reached a beautiful tree. She saw a big, soft bed of grass and snuggled into it.

Just as Chloe was settling down, she heard a loud shock. She knew it wasn't thunder and it scared her. She opened her eyes and saw a big loud monster. Chloe looked so scared and sad.

The monster said, "Why did you come here? I was just about to have a nap! You ruined my nap, so now you have to leave". Chloe was so sad. She didn't want to lose her nap, so she said, "I'm sorry. I will leave".

The monster stopped for a minute and looked at Chloe. He said, "No, you can stay and have a nap. I will go and find somewhere else to sleep. Goodbye Chloe!"

So Chloe had a nice nap under the big tree, and never saw the monster again. The end.

Lily liked to create things with her crayons and paper. She made pictures of flowers, stars, and animals. One day, she wanted to create something new. She looked at a book and saw a picture of a shrimp. It was pink and had many legs and a long tail. Lily thought it looked funny and cute.

She took a pink crayon and started to draw a shrimp on her paper. She gave it big eyes, a smile, and some dots. She was happy with her creation. She showed it to her mom and said, "Look, mom, I made a shrimp!"

Mom smiled and said, "That's very nice, Lily. What is your shrimp's name?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "His name is Bob. He is a friendly shrimp."

Mom nodded and said, "That's a good name. Do you want to hang your shrimp on the fridge?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want everyone to see Bob."

Mom helped Lily to hang her shrimp on the fridge with a magnet. Lily was proud of her shrimp. She said, "Bye, Bob. I'll see you later."

But when Lily came back from playing outside, she saw that her shrimp was gone. She looked around and saw her brother, Tom, holding her paper. He had torn it into pieces and was laughing. He said, "Your shrimp is silly and ugly. I don't like it. I made it better."

Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "No, you didn't. You ruined it. That was my shrimp. His name was Bob. He was friendly. You are mean and fierce. Give me back my shrimp."

Tom said, "No, I won't. It's mine now. Go away."

Lily ran to mom and told her what Tom did. Mom was not happy. She said, "Tom, that was not nice. You should not take and destroy Lily's things. You should apologize and make it up to her."

Tom said, "But I don't like her shrimp. It's stupid."

Mom said, "It doesn't matter if you like it or not. It was her creation. She worked hard on it and she loved it. You should respect her feelings and her work. How would you feel if someone did that to your things?"

Tom thought for a while and realized that he would feel bad if someone did that to his things. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I shouldn't have taken and torn your shrimp. Can I help you make a new one?"

Lily said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. Yes, you can help me make a new one. Maybe we can make a friend for Bob."

Tom said, "Okay, let's do that. What should we name him?"

Lily said, "How about Tim?"

Tom said, "That sounds good. Let's go get some crayons and paper."

Mom smiled and said, "That's very nice of you, Tom. I'm proud of you. And I'm proud of you, Lily. You are very creative and kind. You both learned a valuable lesson today. You should always treat others the way you want to be treated."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and have fun. One day, Lily's mom gave her some money and told her to go to the store to buy a pot for their dinner. Lily was excited to go on her own and pay for something.

As Lily walked to the store, she saw a mysterious man with a big hat. He looked at her and said, "Hello little girl, do you want to buy something special?" But Lily knew she had to buy the pot for her mom, so she said no thank you and kept walking.

When Lily got to the store, she saw a shiny pot that she really liked. But when she went to pay, she realized she didn't have enough money. She felt sad and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, the mysterious man appeared again and gave Lily the rest of the money she needed to buy the pot. Lily was surprised and grateful.

As Lily walked home with her new pot, she saw the mysterious man walking away. She realized he was a kind person who helped her when she needed it. From that day on, Lily always remembered to be kind to others, just like the mysterious man was kind to her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. Emma loved to play in the garden. She would run around the garden, picking flowers and finding shells to admire.
One day, Emma noticed a shield displaying in the garden and became very curious.

She walked up to the shield and asked her mother, "What is this?"

Her mother replied, "It's a shield, sweetie. It's here to protect us."

Emma was not content with this answer and said, "But I want to play with it!"

Her mother said, "I'm sorry, Emma. The shield is not a toy. It's here to be useful, so it shouldn't be played with."

Emma didn't understand. She started to cry and said, "But I just want to have fun."

Her mother hugged her and said, "I know, Emma. But the shield is here to help us, not for playing. Sometimes we need to use things for the right reasons, even if we don't understand why."

Emma calmed down and realized that her mother was right. She admired the shield, understanding that it was there to be useful and help protect them.

The moral of the story is that it's important to use things in the right way, even when we don't understand why.

Nina was riding in the car with her parents one sunny day. They drove for a long time until they reached a river. It was a quiet river and it sparkled in the sunlight. Nina was so excited to see it.

When her parents stopped the car, Nina jumped out and kneeled by the river. She saw little fish swimming in the river and big leaves floating. She felt the water. It was cold on her fingers but so gentle and harmless.

Nina smiled to herself and stayed there for a while. She soon stood up and hugged her parents as she said goodbye to the river. She knew she would come and visit it soon.

Mommy smiled and said, "We're going to grandma's house. And I promise you will have lots of fun there!"

The little girl smiled, but then she frowned. "But what about the gun?"

Mommy looked at her daughter with a puzzled expression. "What do you mean, Sweetie? What gun?"

The little girl pointed to a house nearby. "At the house over there. I saw Daddy take a gun out of the house yesterday. Will he take it to Grandma's too?"

Mommy laughed and hugged her daughter. "No, Sweetie, Daddy won't take any guns to Grandma's. He promised me. And he will never break that promise."

The little girl hugged her mommy back. "Good. I'm glad Daddy promised. I don't want any guns at Grandma's house. I want it to be a safe and happy place."

Mommy smiled and said, "Me too. Now let's go, so we can get to Grandma's house and have some fun!"

The ocean was calm and beautiful. There were lots of fish in the water and they were swimming around and having a great time. Suddenly, an octopus started to splash in the water. It was so happy! The octopus was loyal to its friends, and they all wanted to hang out together.

The octopus started to play a game with the other fish. It would splash near them, and the fish would swim away really fast. It was so funny! The fish loved the game, and the octopus was very proud of being loyal.

The fish kept swimming away from the octopus each time it splashed, but they eventually realized that the octopus was only playing. They all swam back to the octopus and surrounded it in a big circle. They started to splish and splash together and have lots of fun.

The octopus was so happy and loyal to its new friends. All the fish learned that having a loyal friend can be the best thing in the world!

One day, a rat was in the garden, and he saw a mysterious hole. He was curious and wanted to explore it. So, he bravely went in.

Suddenly, he felt like he was in a prison, walls everywhere. He was scared and wanted to get out, but he could not find the way.

The rat tried to find his way out but it was no use. He looked around and saw a big cat, staring at him.

The rat knew he was doomed, and so he surrendered. The cat let him go free.

The rat was so happy to be free. He learnt from his mistake and never went inside mysterious places again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to ride his red bike. He rode it every day in the park with his friends. Tim had a lot of fun riding his bike.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to visit her grandma's farm. There were many animals on the farm, like cows, pigs, and chickens. Lily loved to pet the animals, but she was scared of the cows because they were very big.
