But you can always try to pinch them!" Lily didn't understand what her grandma meant, but she was happy to hear her grandma's kind words.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved her rubber. Every day she found special ways to play with it. She would make it into perfect shapes and pretend it was a little ballerina.

One day she brought it to the park. She was so excited to show off her rubber! As she happily skipped around, a little doggie came up to her. He looked so friendly and cute, so she asked "Can I pet you?" The doggie barked a little and started to lick her hand. She was so happy and gave him a big hug.

Suddenly, the doggie gave her a surprise by biting her rubber! The little girl was very shocked, she cried and said "No, no, why did you bite my rubber?!" The doggie just cocked his head to one side and looked sad. The little girl felt bad and said, "It's ok, I forgive you!" Then they played together, just like old friends. And from then on, the doggie had the most perfect rubber toy.

One day, a little cat named Kitty was very hungry. She went outside to look for some food. She saw a big, red ball. Kitty thought, "I can play with the ball and find food later."

Kitty used her paw to push the ball. It rolled and rolled. The ball hit a bush, and out came a little mouse with a long tail. The mouse saw Kitty and said, "Why did you push the ball into my home?"

Kitty said, "I'm sorry, Mouse. I was hungry and wanted to play. Can we be friends?" The mouse nodded, and they played with the ball together. After playing, they found some food and shared it. Kitty and Mouse were happy and full.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a great day playing with her toys and eating cookies. But then, she wanted to find her favorite cup. She looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found.

Lily went to her mom and said, "Mommy, my cup is gone. Where did it disappear?" Her mom replied, "Did you check the cupboard?" Lily went to the cupboard and opened it. She found her cup and said, "Yay! My cup is here! Thank you, Mommy!"

Lily was happy that her cup was found. She hugged her mom and said, "You're the best, Mommy!" From that day on, Lily always checked the cupboard first when she couldn't find something.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went for a walk. She saw a big, red strawberry. She thought it was mighty. She wanted to eat it.

Lucy picked the strawberry and took it home. She showed it to her mom. Her mom thought it was a mighty strawberry too. They decided to share it.

They cut the mighty strawberry in half. Lucy and her mom each took a bite. It was so sweet and yummy. They were happy they found the mighty strawberry.

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big sign. The sign says: "East Fair. Fun and games for all!"

"Let's go to the fair!" Sam says. "Maybe we can ride the horses or eat some candy."

"OK!" Mia says. "But we have to ask our moms first."

They run to their moms, who are sitting on a bench. They ask if they can go to the fair. Their moms say yes, but they have to stay together and be careful.

Sam and Mia are happy. They hold hands and walk to the fair. They see many people and colors and sounds. They smell popcorn and cotton candy. They hear music and laughter.

They go to a booth that sells lemonade. They are thirsty. They each get a cup and drink. But the lemonade is not sweet. It is bitter. They make a face and spit it out.

"Yuck!" Sam says. "This lemonade is bad. It tastes like soap."

"I don't like it either," Mia says. "It hurts my tongue."

They throw away their cups and look for something else to drink. They see a man with a big jug. He says he has apple juice. They think apple juice is good. They ask for some.

The man smiles and pours them some juice. They take a sip. But the juice is not good. It is bitter too. They make another face and spit it out.

"Yuck!" Mia says. "This juice is worse than the lemonade. It tastes like dirt."

"I agree," Sam says. "It is awful. Why is everything so bitter here?"

They look at the man. He is not smiling anymore. He is angry. He says: "You are rude kids. You don't appreciate my drinks. They are not bitter. They are sour. Sour is good. Sour is east. East is the best. You are west. West is the worst."

Sam and Mia are confused. They don't understand what the man is saying. They don't know what east and west are. They only know that they don't like his drinks. They are scared of him. They run away from him.

They find their moms and tell them what happened. Their moms hug them and say they are sorry. They say they will take them to another fair. A fair that has sweet drinks and nice people. A fair that is not east or west. A fair that is just fun.

Once upon a time there was a popular secret. Everyone wanted to know what it was but no one knew. Some said it was a funny joke, others said it was a special treat. But no one had the secret.

One day, a small girl was walking through the woods and she stumbled upon the secret. It was a small flower with a bright yellow center. She picked it and put it in her pocket. She was very excited about her find.

That night she went to school and she told all of her friends about the secret. They were amazed that she could find the secret. She showed them the flower and everyone thought it was the most beautiful thing ever.

The little girl shared the secret with all of her friends. Now it was a popular secret that everyone knew. They all agreed it was the best secret ever!

The bald man sat in his chair, holding a journal. He was wearing a big, red hat and looked very serious. He read the journal for a long time. Suddenly, he began to cry. His cries were so loud that everyone in the room stopped what they were doing to look at him.

The bald man kept reading the journal. He cried and cried until his face was all wet and his clothes were all wet too. No one knew what was wrong. Then, the bald man took a deep breath and said, "It's all been a terrible mistake, there's no way to fix it."

The bald man walked out of the room, never to return. Everyone was very worried. What had happened? What was in the journal? No one knew. They all just sat there, feeling sad and worried.

The bad ending of the story was the bald man's strange behavior and words. What had been the mistake he had made? Would anyone ever find out?

Once upon a time there was an adorable little bear. He lived on the top of a tall mountain. Every day, he would wake up and balance on a log. He did this so he could stand and watch the sun rise. He enjoyed the peaceful morning, and it made him feel happy.

One day, the little bear decided to go exploring. He tumbled and hopped his way down the mountain. He looked around and found new things to balance on. Everywhere he went, he stopped and tried to balance. He balanced on rocks, logs, and even a big tree branch.

But then, something special happened. The bear found a big round rock. He stood on it and tried to balance. Suddenly, he was spinning high in the air. Around and around he went and it was so much fun!

The little bear enjoyed spinning and balancing on the rock. When it was time to go home, he returned to the top of the mountain with a very happy heart.

Once there was a little girl named Anna. She was curious and always wanted to explore. One day, Anna wanted to go on an adventure and find a mystery. She stopped at the edge of a forest and said, "Today I'm going to find a mystery!"

So Anna took a few steps into the forest. It was very dark and she couldn't see anything. But as she kept walking, she saw something. There were lots of leaves all over the ground. It was very messy!

Then Anna heard a noise. It was loud and made her stop. What could it be? Anna kept walking and soon she saw something. It was a big, old tree with a door on it. Anna opened the door and saw a very big secret inside. It was amazing!

Anna was so excited that she couldn't stop exploring. She found a lot of neat things. But eventually, she knew it was time to go home.

So Anna left the forest with lots of new stories and adventures. She had found a mystery and it was even messier than she ever expected!

Once upon a time, there was a big garden. In the garden, there was a rake. The rake was very useful to clean up the leaves. One day, a fierce wind blew and many leaves fell on the ground. The garden owner took the rake and started cleaning. It seemed like a lot of work, but the garden looked better when the leaves were gone. The rake was happy to help!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sam. Sam was very brave, but she was also very small.

One day, Sam had to travel across the sea to a new place, but she didn't have a passport. So she had to suffer.

Sam travelled for a long time. The journey was dangerous, but Sam kept going until she arrived at a strange place.

When she got to the new place, she found a passport. She smiled and laughed, because now she could travel safely.

The End.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in their big house. They had many toys and clothes and books, but their favorite thing was their comb. The comb was very special, because it could glow in the dark. When they combed their hair with it, their hair would shine like stars.

One night, they decided to sneak out of their room and explore the house with their comb. They turned off the lights and held the comb in front of them. They saw many things that looked different in the dark. They saw the big sofa, the shiny vase, the soft rug, and the tall clock. They giggled and whispered as they walked around.

"Look, Anna, there is a door we never opened!" Ben said, pointing to a small door under the stairs. "Let's see what's inside!"

"OK, Ben, but be careful!" Anna said, following him. They opened the door and saw a dark and dusty room. There were boxes and bags and old things piled up. They used their comb to see better.

"Wow, look at all this stuff!" Ben said, picking up a hat and a coat. "Maybe this was our grandpa's room. He was very rich and traveled a lot."

"Maybe, Ben, but we should not touch his things. They are very old and fragile." Anna said, looking at a picture of a smiling man. "He looks nice. I wish we met him."

"Me too, Anna. He must have had many stories to tell." Ben said, putting the hat and coat back. "Hey, what's that?" He saw something shiny under a box. He moved the box and found a necklace with a big jewel. The jewel was red and sparkled in the dark.

"Wow, Ben, that's beautiful!" Anna said, admiring the necklace. "It glows like our comb!"

"Maybe it's magic, Anna. Maybe it can grant wishes." Ben said, holding the necklace. "What would you wish for?"

"I don't know, Ben. We already have everything we need. We have a big house, many toys, and each other." Anna said, smiling. "What would you wish for?"

"I would wish for the same, Anna. And maybe for some cookies." Ben said, laughing. "Come on, let's go back to our room. It's late and we don't want to get in trouble."

"OK, Ben, let's go. But let's leave the necklace here. It belongs to grandpa. Maybe he will come back for it someday." Anna said, putting the necklace back under the box. "Maybe he will be happy to see that we found his comb."

They closed the door and ran back to their room. They combed their hair with their comb and tucked themselves in bed. They dreamed of grandpa and his adventures. They were happy and rich.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny named Ben. Ben loved to hop around and explore the world. One day Ben decided to go on an adventure and he hopped off into the sunny meadow.

As Ben hopped along he came to a hedge that he had never seen before. It was tall and green and Ben thought it looked safe. He carefully hopped through a tiny gap in the hedge and was surprised at how much brighter and sunnier the other side was!

He hopped around and suddenly felt the ground move beneath his feet. Ben looked down and he was standing on a trampoline! He jumped up and down so that he could feel the springs bouncing him back up. He laughed and laughed as he jumped and jumped.

Ben was so busy jumping that he didn't realise he was getting tired! Suddenly, he hopped back through the hedge, feeling safe, and made his way back home to his bunny hole, ready for a nap.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Kelly. She was playing bow and arrow with her best friend, Todd. Todd had a great big arrow that went very far and Kelly was very impressed. She asked if she could try it.

Todd handed the arrow to Kelly, but then he forgot to tell her how to use it. Kelly was embarrassed and put the arrow down on the ground.

Todd saw Kelly feeling silly and said, "I'm sorry! I forgot to tell you how it works. Here, let me show you how to do it. Put the arrow on your bow like this, then pull back and let go."

Kelly tried it and was amazed by how far the arrow flew. She smiled and said, "Thanks for teaching me how to use it Todd! Let's play again!"

Once upon a time, there was a happy mine. Inside the mine were lots of treasure. Every day, the mine held something special.

One day, a little girl found the mine. She was so happy. She held out her hands and started to fill them with the treasure. The girl felt so lucky! She ran back home and showed her mom what she had found.

Her mom was so pleased. She smiled and said, "This is your special mine. You can keep all the treasure for yourself." The little girl was so excited!

From that day, the mine was the little girl's special place. Whenever she wanted, she went back to the mine. She held the treasure close and was happy.

Tom and Lily liked to play golf with their dad. He had a big bag of golf balls and clubs that he let them use in the park. Sometimes he taught them how to hit the ball far and straight, and sometimes he let them make up their own rules.

One day, Tom had a new idea. He wanted to test how high he could hit the ball. He took the biggest club and the smallest ball and waited for his dad to look away. Then he swung the club as hard as he could and hit the ball into the air.

"Wow!" Lily said. "That was so high!"

But Tom did not feel happy. He felt guilty. He knew he was not supposed to hit the ball so hard. He saw the ball fly over the trees and disappear. He wondered where it would land. He hoped it would not hit anyone or anything.

"Tom, what did you do?" his dad asked. He had heard the loud sound of the club hitting the ball. He looked at Tom and saw his guilty face.

"I'm sorry, dad," Tom said. "I wanted to test how high I could hit the ball. I didn't mean to lose it."

His dad was not angry. He was glad that Tom told the truth. He hugged him and said, "It's okay, son. I'm proud of you for being honest. But next time, please ask me before you try something like that. Golf is a fun game, but it can also be dangerous if you don't follow the rules."

Tom nodded. He felt better. He said, "I love you, dad. Can we play golf again?"

"Of course, we can," his dad said. "But first, let's go and see if we can find your ball. Maybe someone else found it and wants to play golf too."

One sunny day, Betty went outside to play. She saw a cube and she was so excited. She invited her friend Daisy over to play with her.

Betty and Daisy played for a long time. They built towers with the cube and rolled it around the backyard. Soon, they got a little too excited and accidentally knocked over their tower.

Betty and Daisy felt a bit guilty. They knew they shouldn't play too hard with the cube. Betty gave Daisy a hug and told her it was OK. Then they cleaned up the cube and put it back in the same place.

At the end of the day, they invited each other over to play again the next day. They both smiled and waved goodbye, feeling happy and much less guilty.

John loved to ride. He loved the way the wind felt on his face, the way the bike seemed to move beneath him like a wild animal. He was an independent rider, not afraid of anything. Everywhere he went he saw a new landscape.

One day, John decided he wanted to explore. He grabbed his bike and rode as far as his legs could take him. He was surrounded by rolling hills, trees, and bright blue skies. He felt free and alive as he rode.

As he rode, he made up stories about the places he visited. He imagined that the trees were tall enough to touch the clouds and that the dirt was as soft as velvet. He thought the setting sun was god and the mountains were their stands.

Finally, John stopped and looked around. He'd ridden so far that it had started to get dark. But John didn't feel afraid, he was proud of how independent he'd been. He decided right then that he'd always remember that day, and the magical landscape he'd discovered.

Once upon a time, there lived a bald figure in the forest. He was called the Acceptor. Everyone in the forest respected him very much because he would accept anything that was given to him with a kind and friendly heart.

Once a week, all the animals in the forest would give him special presents. The Acceptor would accept them all with a big smile. He was so kind and happy to accept every gift that was given to him.

From then on, the Acceptor and Mary became best friends. Every week, Mary would bring the Acceptor a special present. The Acceptor was happy to accept them all and thanked Mary very much.

And that is why the forest was always full of peace and joy, thanks to the Acceptor's kind heart.

Once upon a time there was a little girl, who was very excited. She loved playing outside, especially in her garden. One day, when she was playing in the garden, she spotted something unusual. She saw a vine had started growing up one of the walls near her window.

The little girl carefully climbed the vine to the top of the wall, and she was so proud of herself. She was excited to have done something so special and was looking forward to doing it again!

Once upon a time there was a vegetable. It was very useful. Everyone wanted to get it. One day, a little girl named Jane remembered the vegetable. She wanted to try it. She ran to the store and asked the man for it. The man smiled and gave it to her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sophie. She liked to have fun and explore the world around her. One day, Sophie decided to explore her mommy's kitchen.

Once upon a time there was a brave bear. He wanted to explore the world. He looked around, but all he saw was a cold landscape.

The bear was feeling a bit sad he didn't have anywhere to go. So he decided to make a request. He asked the wind to take him somewhere new.

The wind heard his request and became very excited. It picked up the bear and blew him all around the world.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Ellie who was 3 years old.
One day, Ellie was feeling chilly and cold so she decided to find something to keep her warm. She searched all around the house but couldn't find anything.

Suddenly Ellie had a super idea. She remembered seeing a blanket in the wardrobe a few days ago, so she opened it and grabbed it. She wrapped the blanket around her and felt its warmth. It was hot!

John was feeling very alert one day. He had a lot of fun painting his bedroom. He loved the feeling of the brush on the wall and the way the paint smelled as he was rolling it on.

The next day, John shared his painting with everyone. They all liked it too. They thought it was so colourful and bright.

John was happy that he could share his memory with others. He was so proud of his painting. He was even more alert now to get busy and paint some more.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue liked to ride her red bike. She rode it every day.

Sue used the brush on the cat's fur. The cat liked it. Sue and the cat became friends. They played together every day. Sue was happy to have a new friend.

Once there was a cheerful little boy called Ben. He loved to ride in the elevator. Every time he did, he would be so excited he couldn't help but make funny noises.

One morning, Ben was in the elevator with his Grandma. As they reached the top floor, Ben pressed the button to open the doors. "Ahchoo!" he sneezed.

Grandma smiled. "Bless you, Ben," she said. She looked at him, with a gleam in her eye. "You must be feeling very cheerful."

Ben smiled back, before dancing out of the elevator. They were going to have a fun day together, and he couldn't wait!

Lily was a daughter who loved flowers. She liked to smell them, touch them, and look at their colors. She had a garden with many flowers, but her favorite was the rose. She waited for the rose to bloom every spring.

One day, she saw a bud on the rose. She was very happy and ran to tell her mom. "Mom, mom, look! The rose is going to bloom soon!" she said. Her mom smiled and hugged her. "That's wonderful, Lily. The rose is a very delicate flower. You have to be gentle with it and give it water and sun."

Lily nodded and ran back to the garden. She watched the bud every day, hoping to see a petal. She talked to the rose and sang to it. She watered it and shaded it from the hot sun. She was very careful not to hurt it.

One morning, she woke up and ran to the garden. She gasped when she saw the rose. It had bloomed! It was a beautiful pink color, with soft and smooth petals. It smelled sweet and fresh. Lily was so happy, she clapped her hands and danced around. "You did it, rose! You bloomed! You are the most beautiful flower in the world!" she said.

The rose seemed to smile at her. It whispered in her ear, "Thank you, Lily. You are the best friend a flower could have. You helped me bloom with your love and care. You are the most beautiful daughter in the world." Lily hugged the rose gently and kissed it. She felt the rose hug her back and kiss her. They were both very happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to go faster. She asked her mom if she could run and her mom said yes. So the girl started running as fast as she could and she was going so fast it was like she was flying. All of her friends were so amazed and excited.

Suddenly, she stopped running. She had remembered that she was supposed to be calm and peaceful like her mom had told her. She felt a little bit ashamed that she had forgotten and gone so fast.

But even though she felt ashamed, she was still proud of how fast she had gone. That night, when she went to bed, she had a dream that she was back at the park, running and flying as fast as the wind. She felt so peaceful and happy in the dream.

The next day when she woke up, she still remembered how peaceful and happy she had felt in her dream. She knew that she can still have her speed and her peace â€" she just needs to remember when to go fast and when to slow down.

Lily and Ben were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and make castles and tunnels. They also liked to swim in the water, but only when it was not too cold or too deep.

Once upon a time there was a little bear named Bob. Bob had a very loyal friend, a dog named Skip. Skip and Bob would go on adventures every day.

Once there was a small boy named Tom. Tom always wanted to go to the shop. One day, his mother told him he could go. Tom was so happy! He put on his shoes, grabbed his hat and ran out the door.

When he arrived at the shop, the door was open. He stepped inside and looked around. "Wow!", he said. "This looks amazing!"

Sara likes to play with her dolls. She has many dolls with different hair. Some have long hair, some have short hair, some have curly hair, some have straight hair. Sara likes to comb their hair and make them look pretty.

One day, Sara wants to take her dolls outside. She puts them in a big bag and carries them to the garden. She finds a nice spot under a tree and lays them on a blanket. She starts to comb their hair and talk to them.

But then, she hears a loud noise. It is a big dog. The dog sees Sara and her dolls and runs towards them. He wants to play too. He jumps on the blanket and grabs a doll in his mouth. He shakes the doll and makes it wet with his spit.

Sara is scared and angry. She shouts at the dog and tries to get her doll back. But the dog is too strong and fast. He runs away with the doll and leaves Sara and the other dolls behind.

Sara cries and hugs her dolls. She is sad that the dog took her doll. She hopes that her doll is okay and that her hair is not ruined. She wishes that the dog would bring her doll back and say sorry. She wishes that her doll would be dry and happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a green raft. It was in a big river. A boy saw it and wanted to grab it. He jumped in the water and swam to the raft. He climbed on it and started to float away.

But the river was very strong. The boy couldn't control the raft. It went faster and faster. The boy was scared. He tried to grab the sides of the raft, but it was too slippery. Suddenly, the raft hit a big rock and the boy fell into the water. He couldn't swim well and the river took him away. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Seth. Seth loved watching his favorite show on the television. One day, the television did something very strange. The show started to freeze! Seth was very surprised and felt a bit scared. It was so weird.

Seth's mom saw what was happening and she came over to help. She started pushing buttons and adjusting the settings on the television. After a few minutes, she seemed to figure out what the problem was. She pushed one last button and the show started playing again. Seth was so excited and relieved.

From that day on, Seth was always careful to turn off the television before he left the room. He didn't want it doing anything weird again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go outside to play. One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a big slide and wanted to go down it. Her mom and dad said it was okay, but to be careful.

Lily climbed up the ladder and went down the slide. She felt dizzy and giggled. Then, she saw a little boy who had dropped his toy in the pond. Lily wanted to help, so she went over to the pond. But, she got too close and accidentally fell in. She started to sink!

Luckily, her mom and dad were there to save her. They reminded her that it's important to always be careful and listen to their instructions. Lily learned her lesson and promised to be more careful in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a big, thick cat named Tom. Tom loved to eat. He would eat and eat all day long. Tom's favorite thing to do was to eat in front of the television.

One day, Tom was eating a big bowl of yummy food while watching his favorite show on the television. He was very happy. But then, the television turned off. Tom was sad and did not know what to do.

Tom went to his friend, a little girl named Sue. Sue was very smart. She helped Tom fix the television. They turned it back on and watched their favorite show together. Tom was happy again, and they both ate yummy food in front of the television.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. She was three years old and she loved to spin. Every morning Daisy would spin around and around in circles. The twists and turns made her giggle and laugh.

One day Daisy noticed something strange. Off in the distance she could see fluffy clouds of blue smoke. Daisy ran to ask what it was. Her mum said it was a special type of smoke called steam.

Daisy became fascinated with the steam and she wanted to see what would happen if she spun with it. So, while the steam puffed blue in the sky, Daisy spun around and around. In and out of the smoke she spun faster and faster.

Since then, every day Daisy has played in the steam. She swirls and twirls and the blue smoke follows her. Daisy loves to spin and the steam loves her right back.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The little bird lived in a tree with its family. One winter day, the little bird was very tired. It had been flying around all day looking for food. The little bird decided to rest on a branch.

Suddenly, the wind began to shake the branch! The little bird was scared and started to fly away, but it was too tired to fly far. The little bird fell to the ground.

The little bird learned that it's important to rest when you're tired, especially in the winter when it's cold and windy. From then on, the little bird made sure to take breaks and rest when it needed to.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable monkey named James who lived in the woods. He went out every day looking for food and play. All the animals in the forest respected him and always followed his lead.

One day James heard a strange noise coming from the top of the tallest tree. He asked his friends what it was and they told him it sounded like a x-ray machine. James wanted to find out what it was, so he started climbing up the tree.

When he got to the top of the tree, James saw a man was spraying a weird powder all around. The man noticed James and said "Hey kid, don't you never spray anything without thinking first. It could be dangerous".

James understood the message and thanked the man for his advice. From then on James was more thoughtful when it came to taking risks. He remembered that being dependable is the most important thing to be.

The moral of the story is to always be careful when taking risks and to trust yourself when it comes to making decisions. Always remember to be dependable!

Once upon a time there was a heavy truck. The truck belonged to a man called Ben. One day, the truck stopped working, so Ben took it to a mechanic.

When Ben arrived at the mechanic's shop, the mechanic told him that the truck had frozen. He said it needed fixing before Ben could drive it away.

Ben asked the mechanic, "Can you fix it?"

The mechanic looked at the truck and said, "Yes, I will fix it. But it will take me some time."

So Ben left the truck at the mechanic's shop and came back a few days later.

When he arrived, the mechanic said, "It is fixed! You can drive your truck away now."

Ben was so happy. He drove the truck home, and it never froze again.

Once there was a little girl. She loved exploring and one day she went outside to the playground.
She noticed a pebble on the ground and she picked it up. It was so dull and dull. She wanted to do something with it.

The little girl decided to count with it. She put the pebble in one hand and then she used her other hand to count how many pebbles she had in her first hand.

One, two, three ... all the way until she got to ten. She was so excited when she reached ten! She showed her mom how she could count and she was so proud of herself.

The little girl kept playing and exploring but she always had her pebble with her. Every once in while she would take out her pebble and count all over again.

Counting was fun for the little girl and she was so happy that she found her dull pebble.

John and his family had a special day planned. They were going to go camping and have lots of fun. John couldn't wait! He loaded the car with all the camping supplies and away they went.

John and his family pitched the tent in a nice spot by a lake. John grabbed the hose and started to spray the tent to keep it cool. He loved the feeling of the water on his skin.

After they finished setting up the tent, they went to explore. John liked to find animals and plants but today he was feeling lazy. So he found a tree and just sat in the shade and watched the birds and bugs fly by.

John's family went swimming in the lake. The sun was now getting ready to set. John joined them and they had a lot of fun splashing around in the water.

At the end of the day, John was tired and happy. He had started the day with a spray and now it was time to go to sleep with wonderful memories from the day.

Once upon a time there was a beetle who was ashamed. He had never seen anything like the other beetles and he felt really lonely.

One day he decided to explore a bit. He saw a flower in the garden and he wanted to examine it. As he looked closer, he saw there were lots of creatures living inside the flower!

He was so excited and he said 'hello' to them all. They all said hello back and were very friendly. The beetle was so happy he had made some friends.

He wanted to thank the flower so he gave it a big hug. He was so glad he decided to examine it! From then on he was never ashamed again.

One day, Mommy and Daddy took Sara the 3-year-old to the park. Mommy and Daddy were happy, but Sara was scared. She saw a cop. The cop looked dangerous. Mommy and Daddy talked to the cop. After that, they all walked away together.

Sara didn't know why they talked to the cop. She was too scared to ask. Daddy held her hand tight and told her everything was OK.

When they got home, Daddy told her that the cop was there to keep everyone safe. He said the cop was like a big friend who made sure no-one was in danger.

Sara felt better and knew the cop was there to help keep her safe. She was no longer scared.

Once upon a time there was a fat penny. She looked so shiny and beautiful that she made a young boy smile. The boy picked up the penny and decided to take it home with him.

When he arrived home, the boy's mother said, "You can't keep the penny, it doesn't belong to us. You have to return it."

The boy wasn't too happy about that but he had no choice. He slowly walked back to the place where he had found the penny and put it back on the ground.

Suddenly, a fat rat jumped out of nowhere and snatched the penny away. The boy was so surprised that he forgot to chase after the rat.

The boy never saw his penny again. He was very sad.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside in the park. One day, Spot saw a big bone on the ground. Spot was so happy and ran to get the bone. But when Spot got close to the bone, the ground started to tremble. Spot was scared and ran away.

Spot saw his friend, a little bird named Tweety, and told her what happened. Tweety said, "Maybe the ground trembled because there is a big, harsh monster under the ground." Spot was even more scared now.

But then, Spot thought about the bone again. He really wanted it. So, he went back to the bone, even though he was trembling with fear. When he got there, he saw that the ground was only shaking because there was a big truck driving by. Spot was relieved and happy to finally have his bone.

At first, it was sunny outside. Then, the sky became serious and it started to rain.

Mama and Lily were very sad. They were hoping to go outside and play. But it was too wet and rainy to do that now.

Mama had an idea. She said, "Let's make a special treat inside! We can be serious and do our best."

So that's what they did. They worked together to make a delicious cake. Lily started mixing the ingredients, while Mama put it in the oven.

When it was done baking, the cake smelled and looked so good! They had fun eating it and even shared some with their neighbors.

Even though it was raining outside, Lily and Mama had a happy time together inside.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to run and play, but one day he got lost in the woods. He was very scared and didn't know what to do.

Luckily, a kind boy named Tim saw Max and wanted to help him. Tim put a leash on Max and took him home. Max was so tired from running around all day that he fell asleep right away.

The next day, Max's owner came to Tim's house to rescue him. Max was so happy to see his owner again and wagged his tail with joy. Max's owner thanked Tim for finding Max and giving him a safe place to stay. From that day on, Max never ran away again and always stayed close to his owner.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He was really tired and wanted to rest. He looked for a soft and comfy spot to lay his head. He found an old iron fence and laid on it, but it was not very comfortable. He thought it was too bitter to rest there. Then, he found a big and fluffy pillow near the iron fence. He laid his head on it and fell asleep. He slept all night and by morning the pillow felt like a cloud! The old man was so happy and rested. He thanked the pillow and said goodbye. He went on his way feeling strong and full of energy. The end.

Grandpa and Noah were very excited. Grandpa had something for Noah to unpack. Noah smiled. He knew it would be something special.

"What is it, Grandpa?" he asked.

"It's a surprise!" Grandpa said.

Grandpa opened the box and Noah carefully unpacked it. Inside was a gentle, juicy pear.

"I love pears, Grandpa!" Noah said.

Grandpa smiled. "I thought you would. You can have it as a snack, sweetheart."

So Noah ate the pear. It was sweet, juicy and delicious. Noah was very happy.

"Thank you, Grandpa!" he said with a big smile on his face.

Grandpa hugged him. "You're welcome, my love. I'm so glad you liked it."

Molly was walking down the lane when she spotted an old mule. Molly was very curious and walked up to the mule to get closer.

"Hi, mule!" She said.

The mule blinked but didn't answer. Molly patted the mule and kept talking.

"Do you want to come with me? I promise I will take good care of you."

The mule still wasn't answering but Molly decided to take the mule home with her. She made sure to keep the mule tidy and clean, and she fed it good food.

Every day, Molly would come out and play with the mule. She would brush it, give it treats and talk to it. She loved taking care of the mule and was very proud of it.

After a while, Molly's mom noticed how happy Molly was with the mule and told her, "It looks like you have done a really good job taking care of the mule. You have been very tidy and responsible!"

Molly beamed with pride and hugged the mule. From that day onwards, Molly and her mule were the best of friends.

One day, Mummy was helping the little boy organize his toy basket. She said "Let's make the basket nice and tidy, so the toys are all available and easy to find."

The boy said, "Alright, Mummy!" He and Mummy sorted through the toys and carefully put them away. The boy enjoyed being organized and helping Mummy.

That night, when it was time for bed, Mummy said, "Why donâ€™t you pick a toy to play with in bed?"

The boy was excited. "Where should I look first?" he asked.

Mummy pointed to the basket. "Remember when we organized it today? All the toys should be available and easy to find now."

The little boy smiled and went over to the basket. Once he found his favorite toy, he was ready for bed.

Mummy smiled back. She was proud that her little boy had helped organize the toy basket, and even more proud that he had remembered what to do when it was time to find his favorite toy.

Clara and her mom were at the park. Clara was playing with her toys while Mom sat on a bench and watched.
"Look, Mom!" Clara said excitedly, pointing at a pile of yarn in the grass.
Mom smiled. "Oh, that's nice, Clara."
But then, Clara noticed an odd smell rising up from the yarn. She wrinkled her nose.
"It smells bad, Mom," she said.
"Yes, that's probably because it's been in the sun too long," Mom answered.
Clara kept thinking about the smelly yarn, so she let out a big yawn.
Mom looked over with a stern face. "Clara, no one wants to breathe in the smelly air from that yarn. Let's move away, okay?"
"Okay, Mom," Clara said.
So Clara and Mom went to a new spot in the park, far away from the smelly yarn. Clara happily started to play with her toys again.

John and Sam were best friends. Today, they were going on an adventure.

John said, â€œLetâ€™s go explore the hidden place!â€ Sam was happy.

They packed up food and their backpacks, and headed off. As they walked, they talked and laughed.

The hidden place was so exciting! There were trees, rocks, and a river.

John and Sam decided to take a break and eat their lunch. They unpacked the food and set it up on a log.

Suddenly, John noticed an animal. It was taking their lunch!

John yelled, â€œStop! Thatâ€™s our lunch!â€ The animal ran away, and John and Sam chased it.

Finally, John and Sam caught the animal. They managed to get the lunch back, and they unpacked it.

John and Sam had a great adventure. They learned that hidden things are not always bad, but sometimes they can be fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go to the market with her mom to buy fruits and vegetables. One day, while they were at the market, Lily saw a deep blue balloon. She wanted it so badly, but her mom said they couldn't buy it because it was too expensive.

Lily felt sad, but her mom promised to buy her a different balloon that would fit their budget. They finally found a red balloon that Lily liked and they bought it.

Later that day, Lily and her mom went to the park to play with the balloon. Suddenly, the wind blew the balloon away and it got stuck in a tree. Lily was sad again because she couldn't play with her balloon.

But then, a man passing by saw the balloon and climbed the tree to get it for Lily. She was so happy and thanked the man. Her mom told her that it's always good to be kind to others because you never know when someone will help you out.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had hair as yellow as the sun, and a smile that shone brighter than all the stars in the sky. The little girl requested her mum to open the drawer in the kitchen. Her mum obliged, and the little girl let out an excited yelp of joy.

Inside the drawer, there were amazing things! Bars of chocolate, colourful plastic badges, and a toy car. The little girl was so excited that she couldn't pick just one thing. She took out all of the amazing items in the drawer and placed them on the kitchen table.

She smiled and thanked her mum as she raced out of the kitchen with her treasures. The little girl was so happy with the amazing items in the drawer that she told all of her friends in the playground about it. Everyone was so excited to come visit her and explore the drawer!

Once there was a little girl called Tilly. She had a box of toys she liked to play with. One day she wanted to play with her toys, but her mom said no.

"Tilly, we have to delay the fun for now," Mom said.
"But why?" Tilly asked, feeling weak.
"We have to go to the store first," said her mom.

Tilly was upset, but she came along with her mom to the store. She wanted to go home and get back to playing with her box of toys.

At the store, Tilly saw a lot of interesting things. She was so happy to be out and about, she forgot about her box of toys at home.

When they got home, Tilly ran to the box of toys and laughed as she played with them.

Mom smiled, relieved that Tilly was happy and had forgotten about the delay.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle bunny named Lucy. Lucy loved to skip and play with her friends in the sunny meadow. One day, Lucy and her friends decided to watch a movie together.

They found a movie about a big, happy family of animals. Lucy and her friends sat down and watched the movie. They laughed and clapped as the animals on the screen played and had fun together.

When the movie was over, Lucy and her friends went outside to play. They skipped and hopped, just like the animals in the movie. They were all very happy and had a great day together.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lily. She loved spending time with her jolly auntie, who always made her laugh. One day, they went on a trip to the park. Auntie brought a big bag with her, and Lily asked what was inside.

Auntie said, "I have a surprise for you, Lily! It's a toy that we can play with together." She reached into her bag and pulled out a toy car. Lily's eyes got big and she clapped her hands with joy. Auntie helped her load the toy car with little dolls and they had a fun time playing together at the park.

When it was time to go home, Auntie gave Lily a big hug and said, "I had so much fun with you today, my little sunshine!" Lily smiled and hugged her back, feeling happy and loved. She couldn't wait to play with Auntie again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play outside. One day, she went to the beach with her family. The tide was high and the waves were big. Lily's mom told her to be careful and not go too close to the water.

But Lily wanted to feel the waves on her feet, so she ran towards the water. Suddenly, a big wave came and hit her hard. Lily fell down and got wet. She was scared and cried for her mom.

Her mom came running and picked her up. She hugged her tight and told her everything was okay. From that day on, Lily knew to be careful around the tide and to always listen to her mom.

Mama and Sara were playing together one day in the sunshine. Mama said to Sara, "Sara, let's go for a walk." Sara was excited, she loved going for walks!

Mama and Sara went outside and saw two big tires. Mama said, "Sara, I think we can peek into the tires and see what's inside." Sara loved exploring, so she and Mama peeked into the tires.

Inside the tires were two dependable, glowing rocks. Sara gasped, "Mama, these rocks are pretty!" Mama agreed, "They are dependable. They won't change or go away like the clouds do."

Sara liked the dependable rocks, so she asked Mama if she could hug them. Mama said, "Yes, you can hug the rocks, but remember to take care of them and always put them back inside the tires." Sara was so happy! She hugged the rocks and said, "Thank you, Mama!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very stubborn. He never wanted to do what his mommy and daddy told him to do. One day, Timmy got very sick and his mommy took him to see the doctor. The doctor was very nice and gave Timmy some medicine to make him feel better. After a few days, Timmy started to feel better and his mommy told him it was time to settle down and rest. Timmy listened to his mommy and went to bed early. The next day, Timmy felt much better and he knew it was because he listened to his mommy and the doctor.

Once upon a time, there was a caterpillar called Bill. He had 8 small legs and loved exploring in the garden.

One day, Bill was walking around when he heard a noise in the bushes. Curious, he crept closer to take a look.

Suddenly, a big, tough frog jumped out from the bushes. Bill was so scared, he blinked his eyes and scurried away.

The frog bellowed "Where are you going? Don't be a scaredy-cat!"

It made Bill feel better as he stopped and said shyly, "I'm sorry, I thought you were scary."

The frog smiled and said, "There's nothing wrong with being scared, just always be brave and face your fear. Everyone gets scared sometimes."

Bill smiled back, thanked the frog, and continued his adventure. He soon realized that sometimes, being brave and facing tough things can be quiet rewarding.

From that day forth, Bill always remembered the frog's advice and faced his fear, no matter how tough it seemed.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Sam. He loved to drive his yellow car all around town.

One day, Sam decided to take a drive into the nearby shop. He looked out his window and saw the big yellow shop. Sam got out of the car and ran into the shop.

Inside the shop, he found lots of yellow things. He saw yellow dresses, yellow books and yellow toys. Sam was very happy.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. It said: "What do you want?" Sam looked around and saw a shopkeeper.

The shopkeeper said: "What can I do for you, young man?"

Sam said: "I want a yellow toy please!"

The shopkeeper smiled and said: "I think I have just the thing for you." He handed Sam a yellow toy car.

Sam said: "Thank you! I will drive this car all around town!" He smiled and went out of the shop, back to his yellow car. And he lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He was only three years old, but he was very bright.

One day, John heard a funny sound. It sounded like a call. He looked around, but he couldnâ€™t figure out where it was coming from.

John asked his mom, â€œMom, what is that sound?â€

His mom smiled and said, â€œItâ€™s the call of a bird.â€

John was so excited! He wanted to find it, so he asked his mom, â€œCan we go find it?â€

His mom said, â€œYes, we can go look for it. You can take the way to the park.â€

So, John and his mom went for a walk. Soon, John spotted a bright yellow bird, sitting on a tree branch. John smiled and pointed to the bird.

â€œMom, look at that bird!â€ he said.

His mom smiled. â€œThatâ€™s the bird that was calling!â€ she said.

John laughed and waved. The bird waved back and then flew away.

John and his mom watched it fly away until it was out of sight. They had a lot of fun that day, and John would never forget the call of the bright yellow bird.

Once upon a time, there was a nice lady. She had an orange in her hand. She wanted to carry it to the park.

The lady was very safe. She walked slowly so that she would not fall down. She crossed the street carefully.

When she reached the park, she saw lots of children playing. She put down the orange and said, "Who wants to have some yummy orange?"

All the children came running to the orange. They laughed and giggled as they ate the orange. The lady smiled and was happy.

The lady was happy that she had carried the orange to the park. All of the children were happy too.

Lily and Max were playing in the yard. They liked to kick the ball and run after it. Sometimes they kicked it too hard and it went over the fence. Then they had to ask the neighbor, Mr. Brown, to give it back.

One day, they saw a shiny thing on the ground. It was a screw. Lily picked it up and showed it to Max. "Look, a screw!" she said. "What is it for?"

"I don't know," Max said. "Maybe it fell from a car or a bike. Let's keep it. It's cool."

They put the screw in their pocket and went back to kicking the ball. They did not see Mr. Brown watching them from his window. He looked angry. He had been fixing his lawnmower and he needed that screw.

The next time they kicked the ball over the fence, they ran to the gate and called Mr. Brown. "Mr. Brown, can we have our ball back, please?" they asked.

Mr. Brown came out with the ball in his hand. He looked at them and said, "Sure, you can have your ball back. But first, you have to give me something back. Something that belongs to me. Something that you took from my yard."

Lily and Max looked at each other. They did not know what he meant. They had not taken anything from his yard. They only played with their ball. They felt scared.

"What do you want, Mr. Brown?" Lily asked.

Mr. Brown pointed at their pocket. "I want my screw back. The one you found on the ground. The one that I need to fix my lawnmower. The one that you stole from me."

Lily and Max gasped. They remembered the screw. They did not know it was his. They did not mean to steal it. They took it out of their pocket and gave it to him. "We're sorry, Mr. Brown," they said. "We didn't know it was yours. We thought it was just a regular screw. We won't take anything from your yard again."

Mr. Brown took the screw and nodded. He gave them their ball back. "Thank you, kids," he said. "Now you know. Don't take things that are not yours. And don't kick the ball so hard. It might break something."

Lily and Max nodded. They said thank you and ran back to their yard. They decided to play something else. They did not want to make Mr. Brown angry again. They learned their lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends. One day, she decided to peek behind the curtains in her living room. She saw her mom singing along to an opera song on the TV. Lily was amazed by her mom's beautiful voice.

Suddenly, Lily heard a loud noise from the kitchen. She became alert and ran to see what was happening. It was just her little brother playing with pots and pans. Lily laughed and went back to watch her mom sing. From that day on, Lily loved to peek behind curtains and listen to her mom sing opera.

One day, a big dog named Max went for a walk. He saw a little boy named Tim. Tim had a red ball. Max wanted to play with the ball, so he asked Tim, "Can I play with your ball, please?"

Tim was very generous. He said, "Yes, you can play with my ball." Tim threw the ball far away, and Max ran to get it. Max was so happy that he gave Tim a big rub with his head.

Then, Tim's mom came and said, "It's time to go home, Tim." Tim looked at Max and said, "Max, I have to go now. But, I will release the ball for you to catch one more time." Tim threw the ball again, and Max ran after it. Max caught the ball and was very happy.

As Tim and his mom walked away, Max watched them go. He knew he had made a new friend. Max went back home, excited to play with Tim and the red ball again soon.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with a crack in the trunk. They want to see what is inside the crack.

"Let's stand on this rock and look inside the crack," Anna says.

"OK, but be careful," Ben says.

They climb on the rock and peek into the crack. They see a nest with three baby birds. The baby birds are fluffy and yellow. They open their mouths and make noises.

"Wow, look at the baby birds! They are so cute!" Anna says.

"They are impressive! I wonder where their mom is," Ben says.

Suddenly, they hear a loud squawk. They look up and see a big bird flying towards them. It is the mom bird. She is angry and scared. She thinks Anna and Ben want to hurt her babies.

"Uh-oh, we have to go!" Ben says.

They jump off the rock and run away. The mom bird chases them for a while, then goes back to her nest. Anna and Ben are safe, but they are also sorry.

"We didn't mean to bother the baby birds. We just wanted to see them," Anna says.

"Me too. Maybe we can come back another day and watch them from far away," Ben says.

They hug each other and go home. They learned a lesson. They should not touch or disturb wild animals. They should respect and admire them.

Once upon a time there was a lazy pipe. He didn't like to move very much and so spent most of his days sleeping.

One day, he was awoken by a voice. It was a number! The number said, "Hey pipe! Wake up! Let's go exploring!". The pipe sighed and replied, "No thanks. I'm too lazy to move."

But the number was persistent. He said, "Come on, pipe! Moving will make you feel better, I promise!"

The pipe thought about it for a minute, and then decided to give it a try. So, he moved his long body around and even danced a bit. He was surprised to find that he actually enjoyed it!

So, from then on the lazy pipe and the number went on many fun adventures. No matter what, the pipe was always happy to go exploring with his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat candy, but his mom said it was bad for his teeth. One day, Timmy went to the barber with his dad. The barber had a sour face and didn't smile at Timmy. Timmy tried to make the barber happy by telling him a joke, but the barber didn't laugh.

After the haircut, Timmy and his dad went to the store to buy some candy. Timmy remembered what his mom said and decided to try not to eat too much candy. He only picked one piece and saved the rest for later. When they got home, Timmy's mom was proud of him for not eating too much candy. She told him that even though candy tastes good, it's important to take care of your teeth.

The moral of the story is that it's important to try new things and listen to your parents. Even if something tastes good, it's important to think about what's best for you in the long run. And sometimes, even if someone seems sour, you can still try to make them smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was feeling sick and her mommy wanted to check her temperature. She put a thermometer in Lily's mouth, but Lily didn't like it. She refused to keep it in her mouth and cried.

Lily's mommy was worried and wanted to take her to the doctor. But Lily refused to go. She was scared of the doctor's office and didn't want to leave the house. Her mommy tried to convince her, but Lily was stubborn.

Days went by and Lily's sickness got worse. She started coughing and had a high fever. Her mommy was ashamed that she didn't take her to the doctor earlier. She called an ambulance, but it was too late. Lily had to go to the hospital, but she didn't make it. Her mommy was heartbroken and regretted not taking her to the doctor when she had the chance.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to a restaurant with her parents. The waiter gave them a menu to choose what they wanted to eat. Lily was excited to try something new.

She ordered a big burger with fries and a milkshake. But after eating, she started to feel dizzy. Her parents noticed and asked if she was okay. Lily said she didn't feel good.

Later, they found out that Lily was allergic to the ingredients in the burger. They had to rush her to the hospital. From that day on, they always checked the menu for any allergens before ordering.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Lily. She loved to look at herself in the mirror. One day, she was looking at herself in the mirror when her mom came in.

"Hi, Lily! What are you doing?" her mom asked.

"I'm looking at myself in the mirror. I like my small nose and my pretty dress," Lily said.

"That's nice, Lily. But remember to always mind what you say to yourself in the mirror. You are beautiful just the way you are," her mom said.

Lily smiled and hugged her mom. "Thank you, Mommy. I will always mind what I say to myself in the mirror."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing hide and seek. Lily was hiding behind a grill, but she accidentally stepped on it and it made a loud noise.

Her friend, Timmy, heard the noise and came over to see what happened. "Are you okay, Lily?" he asked. "Yes, I'm okay," Lily replied. "I just stepped on the grill by accident."

Timmy noticed that the grill was unique and different from the other grills in the neighborhood. "Wow, this grill is really cool! It's so unique," he said.

Lily and Timmy decided to ask the owner of the grill if they could learn more about it. The owner was happy to show them how it worked and even let them help cook some food on it.

The moral of the story is that accidents can lead to new discoveries and it's important to always ask for permission before using something that doesn't belong to you.

Emma was a 3 year old with a bright imagination. She loved to design things and one day she thought of something new. She decided she would design a bucket.

She went out to the garden in search of materials. She found some colourful stones, delicate twigs and some leaves. After she had gathered them, she went back to her room to see what she could do.

As she set about making the bucket, she heard her mum calling. "Emma, what have you designed?"

"I'm making a bucket," said Emma proudly.

Mum smiled. "That sounds like an exciting project. Are you using the materials you found in the garden?"

"Yes! Look," Emma said as she held up the bucket she had made.

Mum was impressed and said, "That looks great Emma. What will you use the bucket for?"

"It's available for all sorts of things!" said Emma with a smile.

Mum was so proud of Emma's creativity. Together they went and hung the bucket in the garden, ready for use. Emma smiled as she imagined all the things that the bucket could do.

Anna and Ben were playing in the garden. They found a big hole in the ground. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's fill the hole with water and make a pond!" said Anna.

"No, let's fill the hole with sand and make a castle!" said Ben.

They started to argue. They did not want to share the hole.

Suddenly, they saw something shiny in the hole. They stopped arguing and looked closer. It was a tooth!

"Wow, a tooth! Whose tooth is it?" asked Anna.

"Maybe it is a dinosaur tooth!" said Ben.

"Maybe it is a fairy tooth!" said Anna.

They picked up the tooth and examined it. It was big and white and had a mysterious mark on it.

They heard a loud roar behind them. They turned around and saw a lion. The lion was angry. He had a gap in his mouth where the tooth was missing.

"Give me back my tooth!" he roared.

Anna and Ben were scared. They dropped the tooth and ran away. They hid behind a tree.

They realized they had been silly. They should not have fought over the hole. They should have respected the lion's tooth.

They learned a lesson. They decided to be kind and share with each other. They also decided to leave the hole alone. It was not theirs to fill.

I woke up in my bed. I felt so happy and excited! I had a soft blanket and my stuffed animal was snuggled close to me. I saw a knob on my dresser and I walked over to it. I touched it and I heard a noise. I looked up and saw a surprise. It was a special breakfast made just for me!

The breakfast was so thoughtful. On the table were scrambled eggs, toast, and a glass of milk. I sat down in my chair and started to eat. I smiled and thanked whoever made this breakfast for me.

I enjoyed every bite and I felt so happy. I was thankful someone was so thoughtful to make a special breakfast for me. After I finished, I went back to bed and went fast asleep.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was curious and wanted to explore the world around him. Every day he would look for something new to discover.

One day he went on a walk and found something strange. He discovered a large pile of waste! He was sad to see so much stuff thrown away.

The little boy decided to do something. He had an idea; maybe he could help clean up the waste.

He asked his friends if they wanted to help and they said yes! Together they worked and cleaned up the waste. They took turns carrying the stupid things away until it was all gone.

The little boy was proud of himself. He felt good knowing that he had made a difference. He had discovered a way to help the world and make it a better place.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Frank. Frank loved to play with his sock. He thought it was so fun to throw the sock in the air and catch it. One day, Frank jumped into his garden and decided to play forever. He threw the sock up as high as he could and ran to catch it. He ran so fast that, poof! The sock disappeared.

Frank was very confused. He started thinking about where the sock had gone. He looked up in the sky and shouted, â€œsock, where are you?!â€

Just then, Frank heard a voice from up above. â€œI'm up here!â€ it said. Frank looked up and saw the sock floating in the air.

The sock said, â€œI'm flying now! I jumped up so fast that I flew into the sky!â€

Frank laughed. He waved goodbye to the sock and ran off to find something else to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. He was a very naughty bird who played in the dirt. One day, he saw a twig in the dirt. He grabbed it and wanted to display it. He wanted everyone to see how shiny and special it was.

The twig was very dirty and covered in mud. The bird was sad and tried to clean the twig and make it look nice. He used water and special cleaning tools to make it shiny again.

Finally, the twig looked clean and sparkly. The bird was so excited he spread his wings and flew around. He showed the twig to all of the birds and animals in the forest. Everyone admired the twig and said it was very pretty.

The bird was very happy now. He flew home with the twig and placed it in his nest. It was safe and sound now, and he was very proud of his work. From that day on, all the animals in the forest admired his shiny twig.

One day, a small mouse wanted to escape from his cage. He looked for a way out, but the cage seemed too tight. Suddenly, he saw a snake slithering nearby. The mouse was scared, but he knew he had to escape.

He bravely scurried to the snake's tail. He grabbed it and slid down. The snake was so surprised that it quickly wriggled away. The mouse leapt off the snake's tail and ran away as fast as he could.

The mouse made it out of the cage and found a cozy spot to hide. He had escaped! From now on, he vowed to never get stuck in another tight cage ever again.

Once upon a time there was a big family who lived in a big house. One day the little boy wanted to play outside so his mummy said 'OK'. She warned him to stay away from the naughty square, but the little boy wasn't listening. He was too busy running and playing.

The naughty square was a wild place. All sorts of animals lived there, but the little boy wanted to explore. He saw a rabbit and tried to catch it, but it hopped away just in time.

Suddenly, the little boy heard a loud noise from the naughty square. He ran to see what it was, and there he found his daddy had been punished. His mummy was very angry, and said 'you should have listened!'. But the little boy was too scared to say anything.

The little boy learned an important lesson that day: never go to the naughty square again. He promised himself he would never disobey his mummy's instructions again. He kept this promise, never again entering the naughty square and living happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe. He was three years old and loved to write. He wrote stories about all sorts of things: animals, food, even the sky.

One day, Joe found a funny looking patch on the ground. It was a black patch and Joe knew he had to write a story about it. He ran and got his notebook, eager to start writing.

Just then, Joe's mom called out to him. She said, "Joe, what are you doing?"

Joe said, "I'm writing a story about this funny black patch!"

Joe's mom smiled. "That sounds really fun," she said.

So Joe went back to the black patch and started writing. He wrote and wrote until he had finished the story. When it was done, he was very proud of what he had written.

The End.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys in their room. They had many toys, but their favorite ones were the blocks. They could make many things with the blocks, like houses, cars, and animals. They had a big shelf where they kept their blocks and other toys.

One day, they decided to make a big tower with their blocks. They wanted to make the tallest tower ever. They took all the blocks from the shelf and started to attach them together. They made the tower higher and higher, until it reached the ceiling.

"Wow, look at our tower!" Ben said. "It is so big and original!"

"Yes, it is amazing!" Lily said. "Let's show it to Mom and Dad!"

They ran out of the room to find their parents. They wanted to make them proud of their tower. They did not see that their tower was not very stable. Some of the blocks were loose and wobbly.

When they were gone, the tower started to shake. It leaned to one side, then to the other. It could not stand anymore. It fell down with a loud crash. It hit the shelf and made it fall too. The shelf and the tower broke into many pieces. The blocks and the other toys scattered all over the floor.

When Ben and Lily came back with their parents, they saw the mess. They were shocked and sad. Their tower was gone. Their shelf was broken. Their toys were ruined.

"Oh no, what happened?" Mom asked.

"Our tower fell down!" Ben cried.

"And it broke our shelf and our toys!" Lily sobbed.

Mom and Dad were angry and disappointed. They scolded Ben and Lily for being careless and wasteful. They told them to clean up the mess and to go to bed without dinner. They took away their blocks and said they could not play with them for a long time.

Ben and Lily felt very sorry and ashamed. They wished they had not made such a big tower. They wished they had been more careful and respectful. They learned a hard lesson that day. They never forgot it.

Once upon a time there was a nice red couch. On the couch sat a boy. His nose started to tickle and he had to sneeze! He put his hand to his face and said, "Ah-choo!" All around him, everyone laughed. It was fun to sneeze!

The boy liked the red couch. He liked to sit on it and look around the room. He noticed a plush toy on the couch and picked it up. He hugged it and grinned. Then, he sneezed again! "Ah-choo!" He laughed and put the toy down.

The boy kept looking around the room. Everything was so nice and colourful. Then, he sneezed one more time, saying, "Ah-choo!" He looked around and laughed again. It was funny to sneeze! He loved his red couch and the funny feeling that came with it when he sneezed.

Tommy loved ice cream. He liked to feel the cold and sweet in his mouth. He liked to lick the cone and make it last. He liked to choose different flavors every time.

One day, he went to the park with his mom. He saw a big ice cream truck. He ran to it and asked for a cone. The man gave him a cone with three scoops: chocolate, vanilla and strawberry. Tommy was very happy. He thanked the man and paid with his mom's money.

He walked back to his mom, holding his cone carefully. He saw a little girl on a bench. She had no ice cream. She looked sad. Tommy felt sorry for her. He wanted to share his ice cream with her. He walked to her and said, "Hi, I'm Tommy. Do you want some of my ice cream? It's delicious."

The little girl smiled. She said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Thank you, that's very nice of you. I would love some of your ice cream." She took a lick of the strawberry scoop. She said, "Mmm, this is my favorite flavor. You are very kind, Tommy."

Tommy and Lily became friends. They shared the cone and talked. They had fun. Tommy's mom saw them and smiled. She was proud of Tommy. She knew he had a big heart. She thought, "Sharing is caring. Tommy learned a good lesson today."

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy painter. He wanted to paint a picture of a beautiful rainbow. But he didn't know how.

So he went to ask his friend for help. He said, "Please, can you help me paint this picture?" His friend said, "Yes, I can help you!"

Then the clumsy painter and his friend got to work. They used lots of colorful paints, and worked until the picture was complete.

When the picture was finished, the clumsy painter was very happy! He said, "Thank you for helping me. I'm so glad I asked for your help!"

The end.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and a daddy that wanted their little girl to have a great birthday. So daddy went to the store and bought lots of toys, a big cake and lots of presents for the special day.

The day of the party arrived and the little girl was so excited! As everyone sang 'Happy Birthday', the little girl beamed with joy as she opened each of her presents. Then, mommy and daddy showed her something very special, lots and lots of money! They said that she could keep it and use it to buy whatever she wanted.

The little girl was so happy that she could spoil herself, however, the money had to last a long time. Mommy and daddy told her she had to save some of it. It was a big decision but the little girl knew it was the right thing to do.

The little girl was very careful; she didnâ€™t spend too much of the money at once. She put most of her money away and would only get something when she really wanted it. After a while, the money was still there, and the little girl was super proud of herself!

One sunny day, Andrew was walking through the woods when he heard a strange sound. He stopped and looked around. What was it? He followed the sound and found a well in the middle of the clearing. The sound was coming from inside the well. He looked over the edge and saw a fluffy grey bird perched on a log inside the well. The bird was whistling a happy song.

Andrew was amazed. He said "Hello! Can you whistle for me?" The grey bird stopped and looked up at him. Then it began to whistle again, this time a little louder. Andrew's eyes sparkled. He said "Wow! That's amazing!"

The bird hopped forward and said "Look at the thick walls of the well. I can make my whistles louder in here. Clap your hands and I will whistle louder!"

Andrew was overjoyed. He clapped his hands, and the bird whistled louder and louder. Andrew smiled and said "Thank you for the beautiful song!" The bird smiled back, and flew away with a final happy whistle.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside and explore the woods behind his house. One day, he found a skull on the ground. It seemed very old and he was a little scared.

Timmy felt ashamed because he was scared, but he knew he had to be brave. He picked up the skull and brought it to his mom. She told him that it was just a bone from a long time ago and that there was nothing to be afraid of.

Timmy learned that sometimes things can seem scary, but they are not really scary at all. He felt proud that he was able to overcome his fear and he continued to explore the woods with excitement.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy bear. He was so tired that he could barely keep his eyes open. He went out for a walk and stumbled upon a big hill. He was so sleepy that he wanted to take a nap. He started to push and push at the hill, trying to make it smaller.

Suddenly, he saw something between the rocks. It was a big block of cheese! The bear was so excited! He stopped pushing and started to eat the cheese. It was so tasty!

When the bear had finished the cheese, he was feeling much better. He wasn't so sleepy anymore. He went back down the hill and back to his home. From that day on, he was never so sleepy again!

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to play with his best friend, a little boy named Tim. They played all day in the sun, running and laughing together.

One day, Tim wanted to play a joke on Buddy. He put on a funny costume that looked like a big cat. Tim hid behind a tree and jumped out at Buddy. "Boo!" he said. Buddy was surprised, but then he saw it was Tim and wagged his tail. They both laughed and laughed.

From that day on, Buddy and Tim played more jokes on each other. They had so much fun together. And no matter what, Buddy stayed a loyal friend to Tim, always by his side. They were the best of friends and lived happily ever after.

One day, a little dog named Spot wanted to join his friends outside. It was a warm day, and all the animals were playing. Spot was very happy to see his friends. They all played together under the big tree.

After playing, Spot felt tired and wanted to rest. He went to his house and found a soft blanket. The blanket was warm and cozy. Spot loved to sleep on the blanket when he was tired.

But one day, when Spot went to his house, the blanket was gone. He looked everywhere, but he could not find it. Spot was very sad and cold. He missed his warm blanket and could not sleep well. He wished he could find it, but the blanket was lost forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to spin around and around in her room. She would spin so fast that she would get dizzy and fall down, but she would always get up and spin again.

One day, Lily found a candle in her room. It was a very pretty candle, and she wanted to show it to her friend, Max. Max came over to play, and they decided to spin with the candle. But Max was a bit spoiled, and he wanted to spin faster than Lily.

"Let's spin faster!" Max said. So they both spun faster and faster, holding the candle. Suddenly, the candle flew out of their hands and landed on the floor. The candle broke, and Lily and Max were sad.

Lily's mom came into the room and saw the broken candle. She was not happy, but she knew that accidents happen. She told Lily and Max to be more careful next time.

From that day on, Lily and Max learned to be more careful when they played. They still loved to spin, but they made sure not to spin with candles or other things that could break. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a wise cat named Tom. Tom loved to sing songs. One day, he found a microphone in the park. He was very happy and carried it home.

Tom decided to sing with his new microphone. He sang loud and clear. All the other animals in the park came to listen. They danced and clapped as Tom sang.

After a while, Tom got tired. He shut his eyes and rested. The other animals went home too. They all knew that Tom was a wise cat who could sing beautiful songs with his special microphone.

Once upon a time there were two pupils who were very good friends. Every day, they celebrated by jumping and playing together in the sunshine. One day, the sky went pale and it started to rain. The two pupils were sad because they could no longer play together.

However, when the sky cleared, the two pupils were so happy! The sky was no longer pale, but instead it was a brilliant blue. They celebrated by having a picnic while squinting in the sunshine.

They chose a spot under a tree and opened their lunch boxes. They ate sandwiches, drank juice, and enjoyed their special picnic. After they ate their lunch, they tossed around a ball and ran up and down hills.

They celebrated their friendship as they enjoyed the sunshine and played together. Even when the clouds come, they always have something to celebrate!

Once there was a little boy named Joe. He wanted to create something fun. So with his daddy, he went to a store. It sold lots of things, like navy paint. Joe wanted to paint something special, but the paint was too expensive. He saw some cheap navy paint and asked his dad to buy it.

Joe painted his old toy car with the navy paint. He made it look like a navy car. He felt so proud of it and showed it to everyone. Joe thought his new navy car was the best!

Joe's dad was proud of him for using his imaginations to create something fun. Joe and his dad were so happy that Joe got to create something with the cheap navy paint!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and sing, but sometimes she felt shy. Her mom would always encourage her to be brave and show her style.

One day, Lily's family went to a restaurant. Her dad ordered some spicy food, but Lily was scared to try it. Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. You can try a little bit. It's okay if you don't like it."

Lily took a small bite and her mouth felt hot. She drank some water and said, "It's too spicy for me." Her mom smiled and said, "That's okay. Everyone has different tastes. You can try something else next time."

Lily felt happy that her mom encouraged her to try something new, even if it was too spicy for her. She knew that her mom loved her and wanted her to be brave and confident in everything she did.

The elderly caterpillar wanted to add something to his life. He was feeling a bit lonely, so he decided to try something new. He started crawling around, looking for a new adventure.

One day, he spotted another caterpillar nearby. He slowly made his way closer and asked, "Hey! Hi there! Do you want to be my friend?"

The other caterpillar said yes and they had a lot of fun together. They compared colors and patterns and even spun cocoons together. They liked each other so much that they decided they would add a best friend activity every day.

They added jumping, singing, and even eating treats together. Soon, their friendship grew even stronger and their days were filled with laughter.

The elderly caterpillar was grateful that he had added a new friend to his life. He knew that his days would never be lonely again.
