Mama said, "You two were being very naughty, but because you were having fun I will give you each a cookie!"

With that, Mary and Sam stopped clapping and each one grabbed a cookie. They were both very happy.

Mama said that from now on, they had to be good whenever they clapped because it was too loud. Mary and Sam agreed, giggling and eating their cookies.

The two had so much fun together, and Mama was happy to see them happy.

Susie was a 3 year old girl who loved color. Everywhere she went she pointed out the different colors she could see. She was always talking about how she loved color, and how she wanted to learn as much as she could about them.

One day Susie was playing in the park with her mom when she noticed a strange thing in the sky. It was a different color than she had ever seen before! She was so excited, and she wanted to know what it was and why it was there.

Her mom couldn't explain the mysterious object, but she did mention that sometimes amazing things happen when you least expect it. Susie didn't know what this meant, but she was sure she would learn soon.

That night, when Susie was tucking into bed, all of a sudden she heard a loud, bright bang outside. She rushed to the window, and to her surprise it was a beautiful fireworks display with all kinds of different colors! She couldn't believe it and she was so excited, clapping and laughing.

Susie's mom had to explain that the mysterious object she had seen in the sky earlier was the sign that a fireworks show was going to start. She said that whenever something out of the ordinary happens, it's always special. Susie smiled, now understanding what her mom had been trying to tell her earlier in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a young mouse who lived in a big house. One day, the young mouse was feeling very sad because he had lost his cheese. He began to cry, when suddenly he saw a friend coming down the stairs.

The friend said, "Why are you crying? Is something wrong?"

The young mouse said, "Yes, I have lost my cheese and I don't know how to fix it."

The friend smiled and said, "Don't worry! I have an idea. Follow me!"

The two friends went to the kitchen and the friend found some cheese in the cupboard. He said with a smile, "Look, here is some cheese. Let's fix it!"

The young mouse was so happy! He hugged the friend and said, "Thank you for fixing my problem!"

The two friends enjoyed the cheese together, and the young mouse learned an important lesson about asking for help when you need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She had a good friend called John. Every day they went outside to play.

One day, they looked out of their window. They saw something very special.

"What is it?" asked Lucy.

John said, "It's a busy bee. Watch it buzz around the flowers. It's so busy."

Lucy was amazed. She admired the bee flying so quickly. The bee was the busiest she ever saw.

John said, "It's a good friend of ours."

Then Lucy smiled and said, "Yes, a friend who never stops working!"

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful horse called Daisy. Daisy lived in a stable and loved eating hay. She was very fragile, and not very strong, but she was extremely kind to everyone she met.

One day, Daisy was feeling very lonely, and wished she had someone to share the hay with. Then, she heard a rustling noise coming from the back of the stable. She walked towards it, and saw a little foal lying in the hay.

Daisy was so surprised and happy to meet the foal. She quickly ran up, and nuzzled the new friend. The foal was also very happy to meet Daisy, and it recognized her right away. They instantly became best friends, and shared their hay everyday.

They laughed and ran and played together. Daisy made sure to take extra care of the foal, because she knew it was very fragile.

The two friends never parted and were inseparable. They loved their hay and each other, and they both recognized that they had something special.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sarah. She loved going up to the attic and playing with all the unknown things stored up there. One day, she went to the attic and found a big pot. It was unknown to her, so she wondered what she could make.

Sarah thought, "Maybe I can cook something in it". She went downstairs to the kitchen and found ingredients to cook with. She put them in the pot and stirred them around. The smell was delicious!

Her mom came in and said, "What have you been cooking?" Sarah replied with a smile, "Look what I made in the attic!" Her mom took a look and smiled too, "It looks delicious!"

So Sarah and her mom sat down to enjoy the meal she had cooked in the attic with the unknown pot. Together they laughed and enjoyed their tasty food. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a very lonely cloud. Every day he would look down from the sky and see the happy people on the ground smiling and laughing. He felt so lonely and wished he had someone to talk to.

One day, it started to rain. The lonely cloud wasn't so lonely anymore because now he could talk to the people below. He felt happy to make them laugh and smile. As he rained he said, "Hi everyone! I'm a lonely cloud and I'm here to visit you!"

Suddenly, a little girl below shouted, "Look Mama! A talking cloud!"

The little girl and her mama stared up at the cloud astonished.

The cloud asked, "Do you want to be my friend?"

The little girl nodded and ran over to her mom.

"Mama, can I be friends with the cloud? Please!?"

The mom smiled and said, "Of course you can. Just reach up and touch your nose to his raindrops and make a wish."

The little girl closed her eyes and did what her mom said. When she opened them, the cloud was gone. But the little girl kept her friendship with the lonely cloud in her heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat candy and cookies, but her mom said she could only have one treat a day. One night, Lily had a nightmare about a big scary monster. She woke up and felt scared.

But then, her mom came in and gave her a big hug. Lily squeezed her mom back and felt better. Her mom also had a surprise for her - a delicious chocolate chip cookie! Lily was so happy and took a big bite. It was the best cookie she had ever tasted.

From that night on, Lily knew that even if she had a nightmare, her mom would always be there to give her a hug and a delicious treat to make her feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was going on a trip with his family. They were going to a faraway place called Hawaii. Timmy was very excited to go on the trip.

On the day of the trip, Timmy's mom realized that she had lost her passport. Timmy's dad said, "We need to save the trip. Let's look for the passport together." They searched the whole house and finally found the passport in a messy drawer.

Timmy's mom was relieved and said, "Thank you for helping me find my passport. We can go on our trip now!" Timmy smiled and said, "I'm happy we saved the trip. Let's go to Hawaii!"

The sun shined bright in the sky and Jack felt its heat on his face. He was excited for today. He was going to visit the farm with his mom.

They went to the barn and got a basket of vegetables. Jack liked the carrots best. He took a carrot out of the basket and felt its crunch in his hand. He was so happy that he hopped up and down.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to scatter in the morning. Every morning, she would skip around the garden and scatter all the tiny pieces of light she found there. One morning though, she came across something new; coffee. She had never seen coffee before and she was so excited that she just had to pick it up and scatter it around. She ran around the garden, sprinkling coffee everywhere and the garden filled with a delicious scent. She ran and jumped, scattering coffee around with a huge grin on her face. After she had scattered the coffee all over, she stood back and admired her work. The garden had been filled with light, and now it was even brighter. She smiled and skipped away, feeling happy and satisfied.

Sam had a pocket. It was a useful pocket. Whenever Sam needed something, he would reach into his pocket and get it.

One day, Sam wanted to call his grandma. He reached into his pocket and pulled out a phone. He knew how to use it to call his grandma.

Sam looked at the number on the phone, then he pressed the buttons one by one. He heard a ringing sound. After a few seconds, his grandma answered.

Sam was so happy to hear her voice on the other end. He asked her about her day and told her about his day. They chatted for a while, then Sam said goodbye and hung up.

Sam was glad he had a useful pocket. It always held everything he needed!

Once upon a time, in a big, dark house, there lived a stubborn little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around the house. One day, while playing, she heard a loud roar coming from the basement. Lily was scared but also very curious.

She went down the stairs to see what made the roar. In the basement, she saw a big, white ghost! The ghost said, "Boo! I am the ghost of this house. Leave now or I will scare you more!" Lily was very brave and said, "No, I live here too. We can be friends and play together."

The ghost didn't want to be friends at first, but Lily was very stubborn. She kept asking the ghost to play with her. Finally, the ghost agreed and they played together all day long. The ghost wasn't scary anymore, and they both had lots of fun. From that day on, Lily and the ghost became best friends, and the house was never scary again.

One day, Tom and his mom had a good idea. They wanted to go ice skating! Tom knew that he needed skates, so they went to the store to get them.

When they arrived at the store, Tom was amazed by all the skates. He wanted to try them all! Tom tried the red pair, the blue pair, and the white pair. None of them felt quite right.

Then Tom and his mom saw the sparkly skates. They were all different colors! Everything about them seemed special. Tom tried them on and they felt perfect.

Tom and his mom went to the icy center to try out the skates. Tom loved the feeling of gliding across the ice. He had a great ideaâ€"he and his mom should go ice skating every week!

Tom and his mom laughed and smiled as they raced around the rink. Tom knew he needed those special sparkly skates!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she saw her neighbor, Mr. Smith, getting into his kayak.

"Hello, Mr. Smith! Where are you going?" asked Lily.

"I'm going for a paddle in the lake," replied Mr. Smith.

Lily watched as Mr. Smith paddled away. She started to worry that he might fall out of his kayak.

Later that day, Lily's mom asked her to help clean up the kitchen. When she opened the fridge, she saw that it was empty.

"Mama, we need to go to the store. The fridge is empty!" said Lily.

So, they went to the store and bought some food. Lily was happy that the fridge was no longer empty.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his toy cars. One day, Timmy's mom told him to clean up his toys before dinner. Timmy didn't want to clean up, so he threw his toys everywhere.

Later that night, Timmy went to bed with his fan on. He loved the sound it made. But Timmy didn't know that his fan was dangerous. The fan was old and broken, and it started to shake. Suddenly, the fan fell off the table and hit Timmy on the head. Timmy was hurt and had to go to the hospital.

Timmy's mom was very sad. She wished Timmy had listened to her and cleaned up his toys. She also wished she had checked the fan before letting Timmy use it. Now, Timmy had to stay in the hospital and relax until he felt better.

One day, a little girl named Lily found a needle in her room. She knew it was difficult to play with it because it was sharp. Lily wanted to share the needle with her mom, so she could sew a button on her shirt.

Lily went to her mom and said, "Mom, I found this needle. Can you share it with me and sew my shirt?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, we can share the needle and fix your shirt."

Together, they shared the needle and sewed the button on Lily's shirt. It was not difficult for them because they were sharing and helping each other. After they finished, Lily thanked her mom for sharing the needle and fixing her shirt. They both felt happy because they had shared and worked together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She was 3 years old. One day, Anna came to an old fireplace. She was very excited and said: "I'm ready to snap!" She got on her tippy toes and stretched out her hands. Snap! Anna clapped her hands together and little sparks started to fly out of the fireplace. She laughed as she watched the tiny glimmering lights flutter in the air.

Anna felt happy, so she kept clapping her hands. Snap! Another burst of sparks flew from the fireplace. Now many of them were dancing around the room. Anna kept clapping and the room became brighter and brighter with each snap she made.

Anna was having so much fun that she didn't want to stop. But soon, she got tired and had to rest. She looked back and smiled. Fireplace was beautiful. Anna had made it all with her little snaps. She was proud and ready for more adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a kid named Joe. Joe was three years old and was very polite. One day, he wanted to open the cup he found on the ground. When he opened it, he saw something shiny inside.

He took it out and asked his mummy, "What is this?"

Mummy looked at it and said, "It is a coin, Joe. It looks like a penny. You can keep it and show it to your friends."

Joe was so excited and thought, "This is great! Now I can buy some ice cream!"

He quickly put the coin inside the cup, closed it and ran off to get his ice cream.

The End.

A little girl named Kayla was walking in the park. She felt the wind in her hair. Suddenly, the wind was so strong, she had to hold onto a tree to keep from blowing away!

She saw something in the bushes and decided to peek to see what it was. Kayla felt a little bit scared, but she was very curious about what was in there, so she looked. It was a small, furry squirrel!

Kayla thought it was so cute, so she tried to feed it a nut. But the squirrel was very shy and quickly ran away. Kayla was sad, but she was also feeling brave, so she walked all around the park.

She saw a difficult looking tree trunk that had fallen across the path. Kayla was scared because she thought she could not get around it. But the wind made the trunk wobble so she was able to squeeze by it.

Kayla was very proud of herself for being brave. She knew she was strong enough to get around the tricky obstacle. She kept walking, feeling the wind in her hair and being thankful for her adventures.

Sara liked to look at the owl in the big tree. The owl had big eyes and soft feathers. Sara thought the owl was attractive. She wanted to be friends with the owl.

One day, Sara brought some nuts and seeds to the tree. She hoped the owl would like them. She called to the owl, "Hello, owl! Do you want to play with me? I have some food for you!"

The owl looked at Sara and blinked. He did not want to play with Sara. He wanted to sleep. He was tired from hunting at night. He said to Sara, "Hoo, hoo, go away! I do not want to play. I do not want your food. Leave me alone!"

Sara felt sad and angry. She did not like the owl's words. She said to the owl, "You are mean and rude! You do not know how to be nice. I quit! I do not want to be your friend anymore!"

She threw the nuts and seeds on the ground and ran away. She did not look at the owl again. The owl did not care. He closed his eyes and went back to sleep. He did not need Sara's friendship. He was happy by himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures. One day, Lily was playing with her toy boat in the bathtub when she saw her dad on the phone.

"Dad, what are you doing?" asked Lily.

"I'm talking to Uncle Tom. He's coming to visit us tomorrow and we need to pick him up at the port," replied her dad.

"What's a port?" asked Lily.

"A port is a place where big boats come to load and unload things," explained her dad.

The next day, Lily and her dad went to the port to pick up Uncle Tom. As they were waiting, Lily saw a big ship with a deep hull. She wondered what it was carrying.

"Look, Dad! That ship is so big and deep. What do you think it's carrying?" asked Lily.

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe it's carrying toys like yours," replied her dad.

Later that day, when they were playing with Lily's toys, Uncle Tom gave her a surprise. He had brought her a big box of toys from the ship he had just unloaded at the port. Lily was so happy and grateful. She knew that the big ship with the deep hull had brought her new toys to play with.

One day, Bobby was playing in his room when his mama called him. She was standing in the living room, holding his new bright red shirt. She said, "Bobby, it's time to dress up."

But Bobby didn't want to put on his shirt. He wanted to play some more. He shouted, "No! I don't want to dress!"

Mama frowned. She said, "You must dress. Mama's very enthusiastic about this outfit."

Bobby was still mad. He didn't want to dress. He said, "No! I want to play more!"

Just then, his papa came out of the kitchen, carrying a big cake from the refrigerator. His papa said, "Come on, Bobby. Don't make mama angry. Put your shirt on and mama will give you a slice of cake."

Bobby smiled. He quickly said, "Okay, papa!" He took the shirt and dressed himself quickly. He was happy to be wearing his new shirt and he was even more excited about the yummy cake.

Once upon a time, in a big sea, there was a sleepy fish named Bob. Bob lived near a reef with many other fish. One day, Bob woke up and saw that his friend, the starfish, was gone. He felt sad and decided to search for his friend.

Bob swam around the reef and asked his other friends, "Have you seen the starfish?" They all said no. But one fish told Bob, "I heard a big fish talking about a starfish. Maybe it's your friend!" Bob thanked the fish and continued his search.

Bob found the big fish and asked, "Have you seen my friend, the starfish?" The big fish smiled and said, "Yes, I found him stuck in the reef. I helped him get out, and he went home." Bob was happy and swam back to the reef. There, he found his friend, the starfish, safe and sound. They were both so happy to see each other and played together all day long.

Sam and Timmy were playing in the park. Sam wanted to climb the tree, but Timmy disagreed.

"Don't go up there, Sam," Timmy said.

"Come on, why not?" asked Sam.

"I don't think it's safe," Timmy said.

Sam shook his head. "You're not the boss of me. I'm going up!"

Timmy shouted loudly, "Everyone knows you should not climb trees, your body isn't strong enough."

Sam thought about this for a moment. Then he said, "Timmy, I really want to try."

Timmy frowned and said, "I still disagree. It looks too risky."

Sam sighed. Then he shouted "I'm the boss of me!" and he climbed the tree. When he realised how loud and strong he felt, he thought to himself that maybe Timmy was right.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor. He loved to sail on the big sea. The sailor had a little boat. He would go far, far away. The sun was hot, and the sky was blue.

One day, the sailor felt dizzy. He did not know why. He sat down in his boat. The boat began to tremble. The sailor was scared. He held on tight to the boat.

The boat stopped trembling. The sailor felt better. He was not dizzy anymore. The sailor smiled. He was happy to sail again. The sailor and his boat went home.

The bird chirped and replied, "I'm singing about the wonderful drink I had this morning. It tasted so sweet and so refreshing."

They flew together until they arrived at the spot where the bird got its drink. Grandpa saw a small pond with murky waters. He asked the bird, "Is this the drink?" His voice trembled with worry. The bird replied, "Yes, it is. My friends and I come here every morning to have a drink."

Grandpa raised his eyebrows and asked, "Is this drink safe to drink?" The bird nodded and said, "Yes, absolutely! Try it and you'll see."

Grandpa took a sip, reluctantly. To his horror, it was bitter and tasted poisonous. He choked and started to feel very sick. He was afraid, so he quickly flew away from the pond.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. They have fun with their friends.

One day, they go to the park with their mom. The sun is bright and warm. They see some flowers. They are yellow and pink and purple. They smell good. Sara and Ben want to pick some flowers for their mom.

They run to the flowers. They see a big bee. It is black and yellow. It buzzes loud. It looks angry. Sara and Ben are scared. They do not like bees. They think bees can hurt them.

The bee flies to Sara. Sara screams. She springs away from the bee. She runs to her mom. The bee follows her. Ben sees the bee. He wants to help Sara. He picks up a stick. He swings the stick at the bee. He misses. The bee flies to Ben. Ben screams. He springs away from the bee. He runs to his mom. The bee follows him.

Sara and Ben reach their mom. They hug her. They cry. They tell her about the bee. Their mom is kind. She hugs them. She tells them not to be afraid. She tells them the bee is gone. She tells them the bee was not mean. She tells them the bee was just doing its job. She tells them the bee makes honey. She tells them honey is sweet and good.

Sara and Ben stop crying. They look at the flowers. They are still pretty. They ask their mom if they can pick some flowers. Their mom says yes. She says they can pick some flowers, but they have to be careful. She says they have to watch out for bees. She says they have to respect the bees. She says the bees are not their enemies. Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat salad for lunch every day. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to hurry up and finish her salad because they needed to go to the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat yogurt because it was yummy and healthy. One day, Lily's mommy said to her, "Lily, it's time to take a bath. You will feel clean and jolly after!"

Lily didn't want to take a bath because she was having too much fun playing with her toys. But, her mommy said, "Come on, Lily. It's important to be clean so we can stay healthy. Plus, we can have more fun after you're all clean!"

So, Lily took a bath and her mommy helped her wash her hair and body. After her bath, Lily felt so fresh and clean. Her mommy gave her a big hug and said, "Now let's go have some more yogurt and play together!" Lily smiled and said, "Yay! I love yogurt and playing with you, mommy!"

Once upon a time, there was a smelly old tree. By the tree, there was a big hole. In the hole, there was a shiny coin. A boy named Tim saw the coin and wanted it.

Once upon a time there was a small jeep that lived in the forest. He was a very happy jeep, always rolling around and making friends with all the animals in the forest. One day, he noticed that a bee was in trouble. The bee was stuck in some thick mud and couldn't get out.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run and play with his friends. One day, he and his friends went to the park to play. They ran around and laughed a lot.

Timmy's mommy told him that he needed to eat healthy food to make his muscles grow big and strong. So, Timmy ate lots of fruits and vegetables.

But sometimes, Timmy could be a little naughty. He would run away from his mommy when she tried to catch him. But when she finally caught him, they would both laugh together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sally. She was only three years old, but she was really brave. One sunny day, Sally was playing in the garden when she heard a very strange voice. It was a voice that sounded unfamiliar and kind of scary.

Sally was a bit scared at first, but then she remembered how brave she was. She stood up and called out, "Who is there?"

The voice replied, "It's me. Don't be afraid. I'm here to settle something."

Sally became more curious. She asked, "What do you want to settle?"

The voice said, "I want to help you find the answer to something you've been looking for. I'm here to settle the unknown."

Sally was amazed. She thought about it for a moment and then said, "Yes, please help me settle the unknown!"

The mysterious voice said, "OK, I'll do my best."

And with that, Sally smiled and went back to playing in the garden. She felt relieved and happy that the unknown had been settled.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who loved blueberries. One day, he saw a big blueberry bush and he ran over to it. He was so excited! He grabbed a big plump blueberry and he bit into it. The sweet juice filled his mouth. He ate a few more of the blueberries and soon the bush was empty. He laughed as he licked his fingers.

Then, he heard a noise. It was a strange sound. The young boy looked everywhere to find out where it was coming from. Finally, he saw a big green frog, tucked away in a corner of the bush. The frog croaked at the boy and the boy said "Oh hello! I'm sorry I ate all the blueberries". The frog didn't seem angry though.

The frog jumped up right next to the boy, and before the boy knew what was happening, the frog had bit him on the hand! The boy gasped and ran away, holding his hand which now hurt. He looked back and saw the frog hopping away, looking proud of itself.

The boy never forgot the lesson he learned that day - even the youngest creatures can bite!

Once upon a time, there was a wild laundry basket. It always wanted to go on an adventure. One day, it decided to take a trip.

It went to the river and enjoyed the sunshine. Then, it heard a noise. It was a bear! The bear was playing in the river and splashing around. The laundry basket tried to scoot away, but the bear saw it.

The bear said, "Little one, why are you so shy? Come sit with me!" So the laundry basket hopped into the river and sat next to the bear. They had lots of fun playing in the river together.

The laundry basket hopped out of the water and said goodbye to the bear. Then, it headed home feeling very happy. It decided to go on more wild adventures in the future.

Anna and Ben are playing with blocks in the living room. They like to build towers and houses and bridges with the blocks. They have many colors of blocks: red, blue, yellow, green, and more.

"Look, Anna, I made a big tower!" Ben says, showing his blocks to his sister. "It is very high and strong!"

Anna looks at Ben's tower and smiles. She likes his tower, but she also wants to make her own. She picks up some blocks and starts to build next to Ben.

"Can I have some of your blocks, Ben?" Anna asks. "I need more to make my tower."

Ben shakes his head. "No, Anna, these are my blocks. You have your own blocks. Go away!"

Anna feels sad and angry. She does not like Ben's answer. She wants to share the blocks with him. She thinks he is being mean and selfish.

She decides to do something bad. She pushes Ben's tower with her hand. The blocks fall down and break. They make a loud noise.

"Anna, why did you do that?" Ben cries. "You broke my tower! You are a bad sister!"

Anna feels sorry for what she did. She sees Ben's tears and hears his cry. She knows she made a mistake.

"I'm sorry, Ben, I'm sorry!" Anna says. "I did not mean to break your tower. I was mad at you, but I should not have pushed your blocks. Can you forgive me?"

Ben looks at Anna and sees her face. She looks sad and sorry too. He remembers that she is his sister and he loves her.

"It's okay, Anna, I forgive you," Ben says. "But don't do that again, okay? It is not nice to break other people's things."

Anna nods and hugs Ben. "Okay, Ben, I won't do that again. I love you, brother."

They hug and make up. They decide to share the blocks and build a new tower together. They have fun and play nicely.

The end.

There was a three year old named Susie who wanted a haircut. Susie asked her mom if she could get a haircut. "Mom, can I please get a haircut?" asked Susie.

Her mom said, "No, not today Susie." Susie was not happy with that answer. She asked why not, but her mom just said "No, not today."

Susie decided to design her own haircut. She ran to the bathroom, grabbed the scissors and didn't think twice. She chopped off a big chunk of her hair.

Mom was very angry when she saw the haircut. She said, "Susie, why did you do that? You must not be very intelligent." Susie felt very sad because her mom called her ignorant.

In the end, Mom apologized for what she said and told Susie that next time she wanted a haircut, she should ask for help. From then on, Susie was more careful with her hair and asked for help before she attempted to design it on her own.

Sam and Mia love to play at the beach. They like to make sand castles, find shells and splash in the water. One day, they see a big surf board near the shore. It is red and shiny and has a rope on it.

"Wow, look at that!" Sam says. "Can we try it?"

"I don't know," Mia says. "It looks hard to use. And maybe it belongs to someone."

"Let's ask Mom," Sam says. They run to their mom, who is sitting on a towel with a book. "Mom, can we use that surf board? Please?"

Mom looks at the surf board and smiles. "Sure, you can use it. But be careful, okay? And stay close to me. The surf board is for the water, not for the sand."

"Yay, thank you, Mom!" Sam and Mia say. They grab the rope and drag the surf board to the water. They take turns to sit on it and paddle with their hands. They feel the waves lift them up and down. They laugh and shout with joy.

"Look, Mom, I'm surfing!" Sam says.

"Me too, me too!" Mia says.

They have so much fun that they don't notice a hidden rock under the water. When a big wave comes, the surf board hits the rock and flips over. Sam and Mia fall into the water. They are scared and wet. They cry for help.

"Mom, Mom, help us!" they scream.

Mom hears them and runs to the water. She grabs the rope and pulls the surf board back. She helps Sam and Mia to get on it. She hugs them and calms them down.

"Are you okay, my sweeties?" she asks.

"Yes, Mom, we're okay," Sam and Mia say. "But we're sorry. We broke the surf board."

Mom looks at the surf board and sees a crack on it. She sighs and says, "Don't worry, we can fix it. Or we can buy a new one. The important thing is that you are safe and happy. But next time, be more careful, okay? And watch out for hidden rocks."

"Okay, Mom, we will," Sam and Mia say. They hug Mom and say, "We love you, Mom."

"I love you too, my darlings," Mom says. She smiles and says, "Now, let's go and have some ice cream. How does that sound?"

"Yummy, yummy, ice cream!" Sam and Mia say. They release the rope and leave the surf board on the shore. They follow Mom to the ice cream truck. They forget about the surf board and the hidden rock. They only think about the ice cream and the fun they had. They are happy.

Johnny was a chubby little rabbit. He loved to explore and play. One day, he was out exploring and he came across a big castle. It had tall walls and stood proud in the sun. Johnny was so excited to explore it.

He scurried inside and noticed that the castle was filled with winding stairways, secret passageways and spooky shadows. It was amazing! Then he heard a sound- it was the sound of a magical door closing.

Johnny looked around and noticed a door. He put his paw on it and it opened! Suddenly, he felt like he was spinning. Everything started to reverse- the shadows were going forwards, the stairways were going backwards, and strange things were happening.

He was now outside the castle again. Johnny was so amazed by what he experienced. He thought to himself, "I need to come back here and reverse through the castle again!"

Ted was a lively little boy. He was always ready for adventure. One day Ted found a shiny red helmet and he couldn't resist trying it on. He wore it everywhere and loved it.

One day, Ted and his friends decided to go biking. Ted proudly put his red helmet on, and prepared to go. Suddenly, his helmet began to tear. Ted's friends laughed.

"Oh Ted, what shall you do now?" one of them asked.

Ted smiled and said: "I don't need a helmet to go biking. I'm too lively for danger!"

Everyone agreed and went off on their bicycles, happily racing each other. Ted was the happiest of all.

Once there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old and loved to play in the park. One day, when she was exploring, she came across a giant scale. She stepped up on the scale and it moved all the way up.

Anna was very excited and began to yell. She loved the feeling of being so high. Her mom saw what she was doing and ran over.

Her mom said, "Anna, you must come down now! You are feeling helpless on the scale!"

Anna tried to ignore her mother's words, but she knew she was right. Slowly she climbed down the scale until she was safely back on the ground.

Her mom smiled and praised her for being such a brave girl. Anna then ran off to find something else to explore.

Once upon a time, there was a small mouse living in a nice, warm cave. He was always very curious, and he questioned a lot of things. One evening he decided to go out of his cave, so he could explore the world.

On his adventure, he came across a big bird who was flying high in the sky. The bird asked him, "Where are you going, Mouse?"

The mouse replied, "I am going exploring, I have an urge to explore the world!"

The bird said, "Things can be dangerous out there. Be careful, no matter how small you are, your courage can take you far."

The mouse nodded and said, "Of course, I will always be careful."

The bird smiled and said, "Good, be brave and never be afraid of asking questions."

The mouse smiled and said, "Thank you for the advice."

From then on, the mouse kept what the bird said in mind, and with his newfound courage and willingness to ask questions, he was able to explore the world without any harm.

The moral of the story is that even something small and timid can be very brave and strong if it questions and asks for advice.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and draw pictures with her crayons. One day, Lily's little brother came into her room and started to take her toys without asking. Lily said "stop" and her brother stopped taking her toys.

Later that day, Lily went to her drawer to get her favorite toy, but it was gone! She looked everywhere but couldn't find it. She felt envious of her brother because she thought he took it. But then, her brother came in with her toy and said he was sorry for taking it without asking. Lily forgave him and they played together happily.

Once upon a time, there was a little goat who lived on a farm. All the animals on the farm were very happy. One day, the little goat found something special. It was a shiny red chilli! It looked so tasty and spicy!

The little goat was so excited. He couldn't wait to try it. But deep down he was afraid. He nervously put the chilli close to his nose, and took a small sniff. Suddenly, he started to tremble, and quickly put it back down.

The goat's friend, a pig, noticed and waved his hoof. "Why don't you try it?" he said. The goat had an idea. He picked up the chilli again and put it in his mouth, then stuck his thumb out to stop it from going any further.

The pig smiled. "Go on, try it!" The goat hesitated, then mustered all his courage and took a brave little bite. Surprisingly, it wasn't as spicy as he'd thought it would be!

The little goat smiled and jumped around with joy. He'd put his fears aside and found out that there was nothing to be so scared of! He had discovered something incredible. He was now brave and happy, thanks to the tasty spicy chilli!

Once there was a train. It was a very mild train. It ran through the sunny fields and over the cool hills. Everyone who rode on the train felt happy and relaxed.

One day, the train went into town. It stopped at the station and picked up the passengers waiting there. The train was so full, but it was a mild train, so everyone was comfortable.

The train started chugging along again. It rolled through hills and mountains and passed lots of animals. Finally, the train came to the end of its journey. Everyone got off and said goodbye to the mild train.

The train's journey was over, but it had been a great trip! Everyone had a wonderful time. The train stopped at the station and gentlly hissed goodbye. Then it left, chugging away until it was gone.

Once upon a time there was an ancient tree. Every morning a little girl would come and sit at the base of the tree and enjoy the warm sun. One day, the little girl heard a strange noise. She looked around the trunk of the tree and noticed a card. It was an old, dry card that she hadn't seen before.

The little girl picked up the card and carried it to show her mom. "Look mommy!" she said as she showed off the card.

"Oh, what an old and dry card," her mom said. She told her that the card must have been left behind by someone a very long time ago. The little girl thought it was so exciting to think that someone else had been there before her! She carried the dry card back to the tree, tapping the trunk and leaving it at the base.

The little girl couldn't wait to come back to the tree the next day to find out what else she would discover!

Once upon a time there was a brave girl named Jane. She loved playing outdoors in the sunshine. One day, she went to walk along the beach. She stumbled across something curious - an empty sea! Jane could not believe her eyes.

She took a few steps closer to the sea and saw a small fish caught in a net. Without hesitation, she jumped in and started trying to free the little fish.

"What are you doing?" asked a voice behind her.

Jane turned around and saw a friendly old man.

"I'm trying to rescue the fish," she said.

The old man smiled. "You're a brave girl!"

Together they managed to rescue the fish, set it free back into the sea, and Jane went home a happy girl.

Once upon a time there was a big yellow boat that lived in the lake. The boat was old and needed to be fixed. So Papa and Maple, the little three-year-old girl, set out to restore the boat.

Maple asked, "What are we doing, Papa?"

Papa looked up from the boat and said, "We are restoring the boat, Maple. We need to make it look new again."

Maple nodded and said, "Yes! It will look so pretty!"

Papa warned Maple to be careful, for the lake was dangerous. Maple said, "Okay Papa, I will be careful."

So Papa and Maple worked together to restore the boat. They cleaned it, painted it and even placed a rainbow flag at the top! When they were finished, they looked at the little yellow boat with pride.

"It looks so pretty now, Papa!" Maple said.

"Yes, it does," Papa replied with a smile.

And from that day on, the little yellow boat in the lake was safe and restored.

One day in the river, an otter named Jack was swimming. As he looked around, he noticed a wide beach. Wanting to explore further, Jack began to swim towards it.

As he got closer to the beach, something strange happened. He felt an urge to explore it. Jack swam closer and closer and soon found himself on the beach. He was amazed to see how wide it was.

As he looked around, another otter appeared. "Hi Jack, why are you here?" the otter asked.

Jack replied, "I felt an urge to explore this wide beach. What about you?"

The otter said, "I felt the same urge. We should explore this beach together!"

Jack and the other otter had a great time exploring the beach and finding new things. They were both very happy that they had followed their urge.

Elsa wanted to go to the bathroom. She was a graceful girl, so she carefully opened the door and stepped inside.

She gasped when she saw the bathroom. It was so beautiful, with colorful floor tiles, a big tub and a super soft bath mat.

She excitedly ran closer and wanted to touch the tiles. But before she could, she heard her mom calling her.

Reluctantly, Elsa left the bathroom. But the graceful girl was happy. She had seen how special the bathroom was!

Once upon a time there was a bunny called Furry. Furry was very excited and couldn't wait to explore the forest.

Furry hopped and hopped until he found a pond. He settled near the edge and started to drink the cool, clear water. Suddenly, Furry saw something oily floating on top of the water. He nibbled the oily thing and it tasted really bad. Furry felt sick and he went to settle on the grass to rest.

Unfortunately, the oil had made Furry very sick. As the hours went by, he felt worse and worse. Furry sadly passed away surrounded by the forest he had been so excited about exploring.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to help her mommy cook dinner. One day, Lily's mommy was making rice for dinner. She put the rice on the stove to cook.

Lily was curious and wanted to see what was happening to the rice. She got too close to the stove and accidentally touched the hot pot. It burned her little finger!

But don't worry, it was a harmless burn. Lily's mommy put some cold water on her finger and gave her a hug. From that day on, Lily knew to be careful around the stove when her mommy was cooking.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Riley. He was three years old and very happy. Riley loved to do exercise every day. He would enter the park and run around until he was tired. He was proud of how much exercise he did and how strong his body was becoming.

One day, he decided to enter a running race. He ran as fast as he could, pushing himself to go even faster. He felt proud as he crossed the finish line. Everyone, including his family, cheered for him and told him how proud they were.

Riley loved doing exercise and he was always proud whenever he finished a race. He had lots of fun and felt great about it.

Mia was walking through the park one day when something small and shiny caught her eye. She decided to pull it out of the grass and it was a toy train. She held it up to her face and smiled.

Mia loved her new toy train and carried it with her everywhere she went. She pulled it around as she explored the park.

Every day she returned to the park with her train to play and explore. Her toy train gave her so many good memories that she never wanted to let it go.

But one day, when Mia returned to the park, she discovered that her toy was gone. She searched everywhere but she couldn't find it. Mia was so sad!

Then Mia's family told her about a local toy store where she could buy a new train. They took her there and Mia was amazed to find cheap toy trains that looked like the one she had lost.

Mia picked out the perfect train and took it home. It was just like the one she had lost but now she had a new toy to make even more memories. Mia was so happy!

Mommy was in the kitchen. She wanted to cook a special dinner. She had a dependable recipe and the ingredients were lined up on the counter. One of the ingredients was pink. Mommy mixed it all together and put it in the oven.

Mommy and the little one watched and waited. Soon, a delicious smell filled the kitchen. Mommy took out the dish and placed it on the table. It was a beautiful pink casserole.

The little one tasted it. It was so yummy! Mommy smiled and said, "See, I told you I could cook something special." Even though she was dependable, the little one could see Mommy was surprised how delicious it was.

From that day on, the little one knew that Mommy was dependable and could cook something yummy anytime.

Once there was a boy named Brian. He was three years old and he loved going to the park. Every day he would wear his favourite blue shoes.

At the park Brian would explore and look for interesting things. One day he came across something special in one of the bushes. It was a golden key!

He knew the key must have been for something special, so he decided to find out what it opened. He looked around the park until he found an exit with a big wooden door. With his key, Brian opened the door and something extraordinary happened!

Behind the door was a secret garden full of magical creatures and plants! Brian was so happy and excited! He ran around and played with the creatures and picked some beautiful flowers.

Finally it was the time to go. Brian put the key back in the bush, said goodbye to the magical creatures and put on his shoes. He left the secret garden, feeling happy and full of joy.

Once upon a time, there was a team of four friends. They were Tom, Tim, Kim, and Jim. They liked to play together every day. They would run, jump, and laugh in the park. They enjoyed being together and having fun.

One sunny day, they decided to have a picnic. They all brought yummy food to share. Tom brought apples, Tim brought sandwiches, Kim brought cookies, and Jim brought juice. They sat on a big blanket under a tree and enjoyed their yummy treats.

After they ate, they played games like tag and hide-and-seek. They laughed and had a great time. When the sun began to set, they said goodbye and went home. They knew they would enjoy more fun days together as a team.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved trains and he had a toy engine that he played with every day. One day, Timmy was playing with his engine when his friend Billy came over.

"Hi Timmy! Can I play with your engine?" asked Billy.

Timmy thought for a moment and then said, "Sure Billy, you can play with it, but you have to be obedient and take good care of it."

Billy promised to take good care of the engine and they played together for a while. But then, Billy started to get rough with the engine and Timmy got upset.

"Hey Billy, you're not being obedient! You promised to take good care of my engine," said Timmy.

Billy realized he had made a mistake and apologized to Timmy. From that day on, Billy learned to be more obedient and take better care of his own toys. And Timmy learned the importance of choosing good friends who keep their promises.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted to eat at a restaurant. Her mom took her to a fair where there were many food stalls. Lily saw a stall with yummy food and wanted to eat there.

Her mom said they didn't have enough money to buy food there. But suddenly, Lily found a coin on the ground! She gained a coin and was very happy. She gave the coin to her mom and they went to the food stall.

Lily ate a delicious hot dog and her mom had a burger. They were both very happy and full. From that day on, Lily always kept an eye out for coins on the ground, hoping to gain more and eat at the restaurant again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Rachel. Rachel loved to ride her bike. She asked her mom if she could ride outside. Her mom said yes and told her to be careful.

Rachel got on her bike and rode around in circles. She was having so much fun! Then she noticed something huge on the other side of the street. Rachel thought it was a table.

Rachel was curious, so she decided to take a closer look. She got off her bike and walked over to the table. When she got closer, she couldn't believe her eyes. It was an enormous table!

Rachel said to herself, "I wish I could ride this table!" Then she heard a voice say, "You can ride it if you want!"

Rachel looked around and she saw a fairy. The fairy said, "I can make your wish come true. Just hop on the table and the magic will begin!"

Rachel was so excited! She hopped onto the huge table and closed her eyes. Suddenly, the table started to move. Rachel was riding the table! She was amazed and shouted out in joy, "This is so much fun!"

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the deep blue sea with his friends. One day, Nemo and his friends were playing a game of tag when suddenly, Nemo saw a shiny pearl at the bottom of the sea.

Excitedly, Nemo swam down to get the pearl, but as he got deeper and deeper, the silence around him grew stronger. Suddenly, Nemo heard a big voice say, "Who goes there?" It was a big, scary octopus!

Nemo was scared, but he knew he had to be brave. He said, "It's just me, Nemo. I saw a pearl and wanted to dive down to get it." The octopus laughed and said, "Well, you're a brave little fish. Take the pearl and go play with your friends." Nemo quickly grabbed the pearl and swam away as fast as he could. He was happy to be back with his friends and told them all about his adventure.

Once upon a time a little girl named Jill was very sad. She wanted to explore the moon but she didn't have a rocket. She could only look up with her big eyes, away from the ground and into the sky.

One day, as she was looking up, she heard a noise. Jill saw a rocket flying towards her! She smiled and bowed her head in thanks. The rocket floated down slowly from the sky and stopped in front of Jill.

Jill thanked the rocket for coming down and asked where it was going. The rocket told her that it was taking a trip to the moon. Excited, Jill asked if she could go with.

The kindly rocket said yes and Jill quickly hopped into the rocket. Up they went into the sky and soon they were high over the clouds. Jill looked out to the moon and couldn't believe her eyes. She thanked the rocket again and they flew back to the ground.

From that day forward, Jill could always look up and dream of visiting the moon with her rocket.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big backyard with lots of trees and flowers. One day, Timmy saw an enormous bird in his backyard. He wanted to watch the bird, but it flew away.

The next day, Timmy decided to peek through the bushes to see if the bird would come back. He waited and waited, and finally, the bird came back! Timmy was so happy to watch the bird for a long time.

After that day, Timmy loved to peek through the bushes and watch the birds in his backyard. He saw many different kinds of birds, but the enormous bird was still his favorite. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to eat radishes. One day, he found a big radish in the garden. Remy thought he was very lucky.

The next morning, Remy did not wake up early. He was very foolish to sleep late. When he woke up, he ran to the garden to eat the big radish. But he was too late.

A big, mean bird saw the radish first. The bird ate the whole radish in front of Remy. Remy was very sad and hungry. He learned that he should not be foolish and always wake up early.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Sam. Sam loved chocolate. He always looked for it in the cupboard, but his mum kept it hidden. Every day, he thought of new ways to find it. One day, he heard his mum talking on the phone. She said something about buying lots of chocolate for a party. Sam was very excited!

So, Sam decided to go and help search for the chocolate. He included his best teddy bear and off they went. He looked in the cupboard, behind the curtains, even under the couch. He searched everywhere!

At last, he found some chocolate hidden in a jar on the shelf. He picked it up and tasted the delicious chocolate. Then, he heard a harsh voice. It was his mum! She was angry because Sam had found the chocolate. He felt sad and put it back in the jar.

Sam bowed his head and thought of a new plan. He knew he had to include his mum too if he wanted to get more chocolate. So, on the next special occasion, he asked her if he could help buy the chocolate together. This time, his mum said yes!

Tom liked to play with his toy iron. It was orange and shiny and made a funny noise when he pressed a button. He liked to pretend he was ironing his clothes like his mom. He had a small board and some old shirts and pants to iron.

One day, his friend Lily came over to play. She saw his toy iron and wanted to play with it too. She asked Tom if she could have a turn. Tom said no, it was his iron and he did not want to share. Lily got angry and tried to grab the iron from Tom. They both pulled and pushed and shouted.

Tom's mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Tom and Lily fighting over the toy iron. She was not happy. She told them to stop and said they had to share. She said Tom could play with the iron for five more minutes, then he had to return it to Lily. She said Lily could play with another toy until then.

Tom did not like this. He wanted to keep the iron for himself. He thought it was not fair. He pouted and said he did not want to play with Lily anymore. He turned away from her and ironed his clothes very fast.

Lily felt sad. She wanted to play with Tom and the iron. She did not understand why Tom was so mean. She looked around and saw a toy truck on the floor. She picked it up and started to roll it on the carpet. She made a vroom-vroom sound and smiled.

Tom heard Lily's sound and looked at her. He saw her playing with the truck and having fun. He felt a little sorry. He realized he was being selfish. He decided to be nice and share. He finished ironing his clothes and put them on the board. He took the iron and walked over to Lily. He said he was sorry and asked if she wanted to play with the iron. He said he would play with the truck.

Lily was surprised and happy. She said thank you and took the iron. She said she was sorry too and asked if he wanted to play with the truck. She said they could take turns. Tom nodded and smiled. He took the truck and rolled it on the carpet. He made a vroom-vroom sound and laughed.

Tom's mom saw them playing nicely and smiled. She was proud of them. She said they were good friends and gave them a hug. She said they could have a snack and watch a cartoon. Tom and Lily agreed and followed her to the kitchen. They held their toys and each other's hand. They were happy.

Once upon a time there were two friends named Fluffy and Daisy. They were very playful and loved to watch the world together.
One day, they decided to go on an adventure. They walked around the meadow and watched the birds as they chirped and flew through the sky.
The friends stopped to admire a nearby pond, where they saw a patient old turtle watching them. Daisy, the more playful of the two, was determined to say hello. She waddled up to the turtle and said â€œHello, are you watching too?â€.
The turtle smiled and quietly replied â€œYes, I always watch the world around meâ€.
Fluffy and Daisy and the turtle enjoyed watching the world for a while together. When it was time for them to go, Daisy waved goodbye, and the two friends continued their journey!

Once upon a time there was a fair bow. It belonged to Rob. Every day he took it to a field to shoot. He would practice over and over and try to shoot the arrows far away.

One day Rob noticed something in the sky. It was a big, round, fair moon. It was more beautiful than ever.

Rob excitedly took aim with his bow and shot an arrow at the moon. The arrow flew so far that it eventually went out of sight.

Rob was amazed and decided to shoot more arrows at the moon. He kept shooting for what felt like hours until, eventually, he hit the moon! Rob cheered and danced around.

He had shot an arrow at the moon and hit it. It was fair and so much fun! And from then on Rob kept coming back to the field to shoot fair arrows at the moon.

Once there was a little girl who loved to dance. Every day she would spin and twirl and move her feet. She was so happy.

One day her mommy took her to the park. The little girl saw a big, loud dancer on the stage. She was so excited that she wanted to try it too!

The little girl ran up to the stage, and without any warning, she started to twirl and move her feet. Everyone laughed and smiled.

"Can I join you?" the little girl asked the dancer.

The dancer smiled and said, "Sure thing! Come on up and show us your moves!"

The little girl and the dancer danced together. The little girl started to throw her arms around, and the dancer threw her head back and laughed. Everyone was so happy and it was so loud. The little girl couldn't believe how much fun she was having.

At the end, the little girl gave the dancer a big hug and thanked her. The little girl said goodbye with a smile and went to go explore the park. She couldn't wait to come back and dance with the loud dancer again!

Once upon a time, there was a silly monkey. He was very foolish and always got into trouble.

One day, he decided he wanted to find a banana. He thought it would be fun. He looked all around, but couldn't find one. He was getting frustrated, so he started to guess. He guessed he should look up in the tree.

Sure enough, when he looked up he found the biggest banana he had ever seen. He grinned from ear to ear, and it was so funny! He grabbed the banana and raced back to his home. He was so happy he had figured it out.

The monkey quickly ate the banana and felt much better. From then on, he was careful not to be so foolish!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy who was very healthy. Every morning Lucy would go to a big, green field with her friend Ben. In the field, Lucy liked to guess how far she could throw her ball.

Ben would measure the "pitch", which was how far Lucy could throw her ball. The longest Lucy had ever thrown it was eight meters.

One day, Lucy had a special ball. She threw it with all her might and with a huge grin on her face. She couldn't believe it when Ben said she had thrown it ten meters!

It was her new personal best and she was very proud. From that day on, Lucy kept guessing how far she could throw the ball, always aiming to beat her previous high score.

The end!

Once there was a grumpy bear. He was always sad and lonely. He had no one to talk to and no one to play with.

One day, a letter arrived for the bear. It was from a wise old owl who wanted to help the bear. The letter told the bear to come to the old forest to be healed.

The bear was excited! He said goodbye to his house and set off on his journey to the old forest.

When he arrived, he found the old owl who told him that if he wanted to be healed, he must be gentle, kind and patient with the animals of the forest. The bear followed these instructions and soon he noticed that he felt better inside. He was healing!

The bear stayed in the old forest for many days. He made friends with the other animals, played with them and had lots of fun. Eventually the bear was so happy, he decided it was time to go home.

He said goodbye to the old owl, thanked him for the letter and left the old forest, fully healed!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a big snack box full of yummy treats. Tim was a bit selfish and did not like to share his snacks with others.

One day, Tim's mom told him to mind his little sister, Sue. Sue was hungry and wanted a snack too. But Tim wanted all the snacks for himself.

Tim's mom saw this and taught Tim to share. Tim learned that sharing was good and made others happy. He shared his snacks with Sue, and they both enjoyed them together. From that day on, Tim was not selfish anymore and always shared his snacks with his friends and family.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jill. Jill lived in a big city, but everyone in her neighborhood was her friend. She was always so excited to arrive home each day and wave hello to her kind neighbor Mrs. Smith.

Mrs. Smith was so compassionate and she always showed it by baking Jill delicious cookies. She never hesitated to lend a helping hand if Jill needed it.

One day, Jill couldn't reach the jam jar that was on top of the shelf. Jill asked Mrs. Smith for help. Mrs. Smith said, â€No problem, my sweet. I'll be right over with my step ladder.â€

Mrs. Smith quickly arrived and handed the jar of jam to Jill. Jill thanked her and asked if they could bake a cake together.

Mrs. Smith happily accepted, and they each added their own special ingredient to make a one of a kind delicious cake. They shared a big slice of the cake, enjoying each other's company.

Jill loved that Mrs. Smith was so compassionate and she was happy to have such a lovely neighbor.

Once upon a time, there was a pig who wanted to escape his pen. He tried pushing the gate open, but it was too hard. He asked the farmer, "Can you fix it?" The farmer said, "No, that gate is too strong. You cannot escape." The pig was sad. He felt so dirty in his pen, and he wanted to be free. Suddenly, the pig had an idea. He went to find some tools and started to work on the gate. After a while, he managed to fix the gate, and set himself free! The pig was so happy he could escape his dirty pen. He raced off through the grass and the flowers and never looked back. From then on, he lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Sam. He loved to explore. Today, he wanted to go for a walk in the woods to find a creek. So he said goodbye to his parents and started walking.

On his way, Sam heard a noise coming from the trees. When he looked between the branches he saw an amazing sight. A group of frogs were jumping from stone to stone in the creek.

Sam wanted to stay and watch but he didn't want to delay his adventure, so he said goodbye to the frogs and continued his walk.

Later, he came across a tall mountain and said, "Wow, that's amazing!" He was quite happy and excited.

He followed the creek until he reached his parents house. When he walked inside he said, "Mummy, look I found a creek! It was amazing!"

His Mummy smiled and said, "I'm glad you had a great adventure, Sam."

Once there was a wise old man. He was very clever, but he had a mysterious secret. Every day he would go out and fold a big blanket. No one could figure out why the man was folding the blanket.

One day a small girl, who was only three, was curious. She asked the man, "What is the secret?" The old man just smiled and said nothing. But the little girl was very smart and she kept asking until the old man finally said, "The mystery behind the blanket is that it is magical. When I fold it just right, it will make my wishes come true!"

The little girl was so excited! She asked the old man to show her how to fold the blanket so that it was magical. And so he did. Together they folded the blanket and made a wish. Suddenly, the air around them was full of magical sparkles!

The little girl and the old man were both so happy. They had solved the mystery and created something wonderful. From then on, every single day, whenever the wise old man was seen outside, he had the magical blanket with him, always ready to help make wishes come true.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big ladder leaning on the wall. Ben wanted to climb the ladder and see what was on the other side. Lily was scared and said, "No, Ben, don't go. It is too high and you might fall."

But Ben did not listen. He ran to the ladder and started to climb. He went up and up until he reached the top. He looked over the wall and saw a wide road with many cars and trucks. He felt dizzy and scared. He wanted to go back down, but he did not know how.

He shouted, "Help, help, I am stuck. Lily, help me!" Lily heard him and ran to the ladder. She looked up and saw Ben crying. She felt sorry for him and said, "Don't cry, Ben, I will help you. Hold on tight and I will get Dad."

She ran to the house and found Dad. She told him, "Dad, Dad, Ben is on the ladder and he can't come down. He is crying and scared. Please help him." Dad followed Lily to the garden and saw Ben on the ladder. He said, "Ben, don't worry, I am here. I will get you down. Just stay calm and listen to me."

Dad climbed the ladder and reached Ben. He hugged him and said, "You are brave, Ben, but you should not climb the ladder without me. It is dangerous and you could get hurt. Next time, ask me first, OK?" Ben nodded and said, "OK, Dad, I am sorry. I won't do it again." Dad carried Ben down the ladder and put him on the ground. He kissed him and said, "I love you, Ben. You are my son and I am proud of you. But please be careful and listen to Lily. She is your sister and she cares for you."

Ben hugged Dad and said, "I love you, Dad. And I love Lily too. She is my sister and she helped me. Thank you, Lily." Lily hugged Ben and said, "You are welcome, Ben. I am glad you are OK. Let's play something else. How about we draw some pictures?" Ben smiled and said, "Yes, let's do that. That sounds fun." They went to the house and got some paper and crayons. They drew some pictures of the garden, the ladder, the road, and their family. They had fun and forgot about their scare. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a beautiful girl who loved to dance. She was graceful and light on her feet and twirled and spun with wonderful grace. Every night, she would move and sway to the music in her room. But one night, she was upset. Her bookcase had fallen over and all of her books were scattered across the room. She stared sadly at the mess and wondered how she could ever be graceful with so much chaos around her.

But then a miracle happened. The books began to float off the floor and quickly gathered themselves into the bookcase. They moved in perfect harmony and with grace, just like the girl danced. Soon the room was back to normal, and the girlâ€™s dancing could continue.

The girl was amazed at the miracle and twirled around the room, happy that she could keep dancing. She moved from corner to corner and let the music take her away. She moved with grace and joy, bonding with the books that now stood tall in her bookcase.

Since then, the girl and the bookcase have been dancing every night, celebrating life and the wonderful world around them. Grace and harmony forever.

Tom and Lily like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They race them on the floor and make loud noises. Sometimes, their cars crash and break. Then, they need to repair them.

One day, Tom's blue car broke its wheel. He was sad and did not want to play anymore. Lily saw him and wanted to help. She said, "Don't worry, Tom. I can repair your car. I have a stamp that can fix it."

Lily took her stamp and showed it to Tom. It was a red stamp with a star on it. She said, "This is a magic stamp. It can make anything better. Watch this." She stamped the broken wheel of the car and said, "Abracadabra!"

Tom looked at his car and saw that the wheel was fixed. He was amazed and happy. He said, "Wow, Lily, you are right. Your stamp is magic. Thank you for repairing my car. You are a good friend."

Lily smiled and said, "You are welcome, Tom. I am glad you like my stamp. It is very reliable. It always works. Do you want to play with me?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, I do. Let's race our cars again. But be careful, don't crash them."

They played with their cars and had fun. They did not crash them again. They used Lily's stamp to decorate their cars with stars. They were happy and proud of their cars. They were good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a unique little bird named Timmy. Timmy was very special because he could talk to people. One day, Timmy went to visit his friend, Sally the squirrel.

Sally was making cookies in her home. She had a big oven to bake the cookies. Timmy saw that Sally's oven was very hot. He wanted to help Sally, so he decided to warn her about the hot oven.

"Be careful, Sally! The oven is very hot!" Timmy said. Sally listened to Timmy's warning and was extra careful not to touch the hot oven. They both waited for the cookies to bake. When the cookies were ready, they shared the tasty treats and had a fun day together.

Once upon a time there was a brave boy named Bob. He liked to explore the woods near his house. One day, he was walking through the woods and saw a strange piece on the ground. He was curious, so he walked up to it and picked it up.

Just as Bob was about to investigate the piece more closely, he heard a loud noise. He quickly looked around but saw nothing. Suddenly, the piece Bob was holding began to shake and disappear! Bob cried out in shock and confusion.

Just then, a wise old elf appeared from behind a tree. He said to Bob, "You must have been brave to have come this far. You found something magical. Now it must vanish. Don't worry, one day it will be back!" The elf smiled and then vanished in a puff of smoke.

Bob was amazed at what he had seen. He remembered the wise elf's words, and continued to explore the woods with a brave spirit.

Once upon a time there was a small white cauliflower who was stuck in a tall tree. He tried to climb down but was too dizzy from the height and he couldn't reach the ground. He called for help but nobody answered.

Just then a brave superhero ran by. He saw the poor cauliflower and knew he had to rescue him. He flew up to the top of the tall tree and carefully picked him up. The superhero held him tight in his arms and flew him down to safety.

The pollen from the flowers made the superhero feel a bit dizzy, but he kept flying until they reached the ground.

The cauliflower thanked the brave superhero with a big hug. He was so glad to be back safely with his friends.

The superhero had rescued the cauliflower and made him very happy.

Tom and Lily are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big truck and Lily has a doll. Tom likes to make loud noises with his truck and zoom it around the floor. Lily likes to brush her doll's hair and dress her up.

"Tom, can I play with your truck?" Lily asks. She thinks the truck looks fun and shiny.

"No, it's mine!" Tom says. He does not want to share his truck. He thinks the doll is boring and ugly.

"Please, Tom, just for a little bit?" Lily begs. She tries to reach for the truck, but Tom pulls it away.

"Go away, Lily!" Tom shouts. He pinches Lily's arm hard. Lily cries out in pain and drops her doll.

"Ow, Tom, that hurts!" Lily says. She feels a big ouch on her arm. She is angry and sad.

"Sorry, Lily, I didn't mean to hurt you," Tom says. He feels bad for pinching Lily. He sees a red mark on her arm. He remembers that Mommy told him not to pinch.

He gives Lily his truck and picks up her doll. He sees a zip on the doll's dress. He tries to open it, but it is stuck. He pulls harder, but the zip does not move. He breaks the zip and tears the dress.

"Oh no, Tom, what did you do?" Lily says. She sees her doll's dress ruined. She is more angry and sad.

"Sorry, Lily, I didn't mean to break it," Tom says. He feels worse for breaking Lily's doll. He remembers that Mommy told him to be gentle.

He hugs Lily and says, "I'm sorry, Lily, I'm a bad brother. I love you."

Lily hugs Tom back and says, "I'm sorry, Tom, I'm a bad sister. I love you."

They wipe their tears and smile. They decide to play together and share their toys. They find a dry cloth and wrap it around the doll's dress. They pretend the cloth is a cape and the doll is a superhero. They have fun and laugh. Mommy comes in and sees them happy. She is proud of them. She gives them a big hug and a kiss. She says, "You are good children. I love you."

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big brown dog with a ball in his mouth. Lily liked dogs and wanted to pet him. Ben was afraid of dogs and stayed away.

"Come on, Ben, he is nice!" Lily urged. She ran to the dog and reached out her hand. The dog growled and showed his teeth. Lily got scared and ran back to Ben.

"See, I told you dogs are bad!" Ben said. He hugged Lily and tried to make her feel better.

A man came and called the dog. He saw Lily and Ben and said, "I'm sorry, kids, he doesn't like strangers. He is very old and grumpy. You should always ask before you touch a dog. They might bite you if they feel threatened."

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We're sorry, sir. We won't do it again."

The man smiled and said, "That's good. Dogs can be good friends, but you have to respect them and their space. Here, you can have his ball. He doesn't play with it anymore."

He gave them the ball and walked away with the dog. Lily and Ben thanked him and played with the ball. They learned to be careful and polite with animals.

One day, Bob the whale was swimming in the ocean. He felt something wet on his back and knew he needed to clean himself. He stopped to take a break and called to his friend Jimmy the starfish.

"Jimmy," he said, "I think I need help cleaning myself."

Jimmy smiled and said, "I'm here to help! Let me take a look."

Jimmy looked at Bob's back and saw that it was very thin. He knew that he could help Bob clean it.

Jimmy swam around Bob, spraying water everywhere. He rubbed Bob's back with a soft cloth until it was clean and shiny.

When Jimmy was finished, Bob smiled. "Thanks for helping me clean, Jimmy," he said.

Jimmy said, "It's my pleasure. It's important to keep yourself nice and clean!"

Bob thanked Jimmy again and the two of them continued to swim around, happy that Bob was now clean again.

Once upon a time there was a long zoo. All the animals were very happy and they enjoyed playing together and eating yummy food.

One day, the animals noticed they were not able to find the giraffe. They looked everywhere but she seemed to have disappeared.

The animals were very sad. They looked for the giraffe all day, but she never came back.

The animals never saw the giraffe again and they were very sad. They never knew what happened to her and why she had disappeared.

The end.

The man ran home, feeling sad and hurt. He had lost his job and he needed money to buy some food. His wife hugged him and said, "Don't worry, we'll figure something out". He had mentioned his wife's name to his boss and he got angry, which lead to getting fired.

The man's wife looked at him with love and said, "I've got an idea! Why don't you start a business selling food?" The man thought about it and replied, "I think that's a great idea!".

So his wife started to help him to get started. She sold snacks and drinks, and the man sold them door to door. They kept going, even when it rained. People soon knew the man's name in the neighborhood and started to call him for more things.

At the end of the month, their business had made enough money that they didn't have to worry. The man and his wife were thankful and they hugged each other tight. Everything was going to be ok.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the rain and jump in puddles. One day, her mommy gave her a present - a new umbrella with a gentle pink color. Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to use it.

The next day, it started to rain. Lily put on her raincoat and took her new umbrella. She went outside to play. She jumped in puddles and twirled around with her umbrella. But then, the wind started to blow harder and harder. Suddenly, Lily's umbrella turned inside out and she got very wet. She tried to run back inside, but she was already soaked.

Lily learned that sometimes presents can't protect you from bad things. She also learned that it's important to be careful when playing outside in the rain.

Once upon a time, there were two small mice named Max and Tim.
Max and Tim were very good friends who loved to explore their big lab together.
One day, Max said to Tim, â€œLetâ€™s go explore the lab!â€
Max and Tim were so excited that they quickly followed each other around the lab.

As they explored the lab, they came across a small room that they had never seen before.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were very important to each other. One was a little boy, and one was a little girl. They liked to play together, running and having fun.

One day, the two friends found something special - two matches. They were so excited to find something that united both of them. The little girl said, "we can use this to keep our friendship together".

The little boy was so happy, he wanted to do something special with the matches. So they each made a special wish on their own match. Then they put the two matches together and created a spark.

The little girl said "This is how we stay united." And so, the two friends stayed together forever, forever linked by their special matches. They both knew that their friendship was very important!

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But sometimes they fight over the same toy. Today they both want to play with the red car.

"Give me the car!" Lily says. She pulls the car from Ben's hand.

"No, it's mine!" Ben says. He pulls the car back from Lily's hand.

They tug and tug until the car breaks in two. They both cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to their room. She sees the broken car and the sad twins.

"What happened here?" Mom asks.

"Lily broke the car!" Ben says.

"No, Ben broke the car!" Lily says.

They both insist that it is not their fault.

Mom sighs. She picks up the pieces of the car and puts them in the trash.

"Listen, my loves," Mom says. "Fighting over toys is not nice. It only makes you unhappy and angry. You have many other toys to play with. Why don't you share and take turns? That way you can have more fun and peace."

Lily and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry for breaking the car and making Mom sad.

"Sorry, Mom," Lily says.

"Sorry, Mom," Ben says.

They hug Mom and say sorry to each other.

Mom smiles. She gives them each a kiss and a hug.

"Good," Mom says. "Now, why don't you play with the blue truck and the yellow bike? You can switch after ten minutes."

Lily and Ben nod. They take the truck and the bike and play nicely together.

Mom leaves their room and closes the door. She hears them laughing and talking.

She is happy that they have learned to share and make peace.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She had a white purse made of the softest silk. Every day, when Sarah was out for her walk, she would carry her purse with her.

One day, Sarah was walking through the park, when she noticed a beautiful white bird. She asked the bird if she could have it as a pet. The bird replied, â€œNo, I canâ€™t. But if you can answer my request, Iâ€™ll think about it.â€

The bird asked Sarah to take her white purse to the far side of the park. Sarah was very excited and ran off towards the other side of the park, with her purse in hand. After she got there, she found a beautiful nest filled with other birds.

The bird thanked Sarah and invited her to come back as often as she liked. Sarah thanked the bird, and went home with a smile on her face. From that day on, Sarah and the birds were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a princess. She had lots of things to do, but she was bored. She wanted to do something different.
The princess thought of a great idea. She decided to make an unusual thing. She gathered lots of things and started to make her unusual thing. She mixed and stirred, and put together lots of pieces.
After a while, the princess finished making her unusual thing. She was very proud of what she had made. She showed everyone her unusual thing.
The princess and everyone else were so happy! They were amazed at what the princess had made.
From that day on, the princess made lots of unusual things. Everytime she made something she felt very proud and happy.

Once upon a time there was a big, strong bear. The bear had a nice cabin all by himself. He was always content in it.
