Once upon a time, there were two friends named Pete and Paul. Pete loved to race and always wanted to be the fastest. Paul thought Pete was too competitive and always wanted him to slow down.

One day, Pete saw a light shining in the distance. He told Paul about it, and they decided to go and explore. As they got closer, they saw it was a trophy of the biggest race in the world! Pete was overjoyed and told Paul he would enter the race and win the trophy.

Paul was worried and said it was too dangerous. He begged Pete to stay and said he didn't want him to get hurt. But Pete was determined and promised Paul he wouldn't get hurt.

Finally, the day of the race arrived. Pete was feeling nervous, but was determined to win the trophy. The race started and Pete ran as fast as he could as he heard Paul cheer him on. As Pete rounded the last corner, he could see the trophy waiting for him. He raced to the finish and won the trophy! Pete celebrated with Paul and they both agreed that Pete had done an amazing job.

Once upon a time, there was a penguin named Pete. Pete loved to travel to new places. One day, he decided to go to the North Pole. It was very icy there, but Pete had a warm coat.

As he was walking, he found a handle on the ground. It was a shiny handle that sparkled in the sun. Pete picked it up and carried it with him on his journey.

After a while, Pete met some other penguins who were lost. They didn't know how to get back home. Pete used the handle to dig a path through the snow and they all followed him. They were very happy to have found their way home.

From that day on, Pete always carried the handle with him on his travels. It helped him and others when they needed it. Pete was a happy penguin who loved to explore new places and help his friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old and very curious. She loved exploring new places. One day, she went to a park and found a violin. She had never seen one before, so she picked it up and it made music. Lucy was so excited and realized it was fun to make music.

The next day, Lucy brought the violin home to show her mum. Her mum said that if Lucy wanted to learn to play the violin she had to practice every day. Lucy happily agreed and so mum found her the best teacher.

The teacher taught her how to read music and play simple tunes. Lucy practiced every day until it was time for the violin recital. When her turn came she played the violin perfectly. Everyone clapped and cheered for her and she felt so proud.

Lucy went home and mum made her a tasty snack to celebrate. She felt so happy and realized making music was even better than she thought. She decided to play the violin every day and to make lots of beautiful music.

The end.

Once there was an ugly sack. It was a big, brown sack, and it was so old that it was starting to rip. It wanted to be stylish just like all of the other sacks, but it was too ugly.

So, the sack decided to go on an adventure. It traveled all around, trying to find its style. Everywhere it went, it only found more ugly sacks, nothing that could make it look special.

The sack kept going until it arrived at a big river. It stopped to rest in the sun, when it saw the most beautiful sack it had ever seen! This sack was colored with bright oranges, purples, and blues, and it was sparkling in the sunlight.

The ugly sack knew the other sack was its style. So it asked the other sack to teach it how to be beautiful. The other sack said yes and started to teach the ugly sack all its secrets. Soon, the ugly sack was looking just like the other sack, and it felt so wonderful!

Now the two sacks travel together, and they can be found walking around the big river. They love showing off their new style and always look so amazing!

One day, two friends decided to go on an adventure.
They grabbed their big map, and took off.
They started walking and soon, the sun was high in the sky.
It was very hot, so they took a break.
They looked at the map and decided to keep going.
Before long, they had gone through the woods and found a big lake.
They both took off their shoes and went swimming.
Then they took some food and ate it by the lake.
It was a great day, and it ended with them looking at the starry sky.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Joe and Grace. They were always playing together and having so much fun. One day, Joe and Grace decided to go to the town's marketplace.

When they got there, they saw a vendor with lots of colorful balloons. Joe wanted one so badly, but he didn't have enough money. Grace saw how sad Joe was and wanted to help. She asked her mom to bring some money so Joe could buy a balloon.

When Grace's mom arrived she saw that Joe wanted a deep red balloon. Joe was so relieved to be able to buy it after his friend helped him. Grace said to Joe, "Remember, if you help a friend in need, you will always be rewarded!"

Joe and Grace smiled and hugged each other, walked away with the deep red balloon, proud of the lesson they had learnt.

Once upon a time there was a poor boy. He was very tired and had no friends. He walked down the street, dragging his feet with every step and feeling sad.

One day he saw a wink in the sky. The boy wondered what it was. He looked up and smiled.

"Maybe something good will happen to me," he said.

He kept walking and walking, and soon he came upon an old man. The old man smiled at the boy and asked him if he wanted to come to his house.

The boy followed the old man, but soon he started to feel very bad. He felt like he was not able to move and something was wrong.

At last they reached the old man's house and the boy started to suffer. He screamed and tried to run away, but the old man had locked the door.

The poor boy was never seen again. No one knew what happened to him and he was never freed. He suffers to this day and his exhausted body never gets any rest.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but he had too much junk in his room. His mommy said he had to clean it up before he could go outside to play.

Timmy tried to pick up the heavy toys, but they were too big for him. He asked his daddy for help, and together they succeeded in cleaning up the room. Timmy was so happy, he hugged his daddy and said thank you.

Now that his room was clean, Timmy could go outside and play with his friends. He ran and played, feeling light and free. He knew that he had succeeded in making his mommy happy, and that made him happy too. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big black bear who loved the morning. Every morning he woke up, happy and content. He would leave his cozy bed and go explore the world. As he walked, he saw all the wonders of nature in the morning light. He loved the way the morning was so still and peaceful.

One morning, something special happened. He saw a small black squirrel. She was so cute and curious. The bear fell in love with her right away. He followed her through the trees and grass, marveling at her beauty.

The bear and the squirrel became the best of friends. They would play together every morning, laughing and having fun. The bear was so happy he had found someone special to love.

The squirrel loved the morning too. She liked playing in the fresh air and feeling the sun on her back. Every morning the bear and the squirrel would explore together, until the sun disappeared into the night.

The bear was so lucky to have found the love of his life, his black squirrel friend.

Once there was a boy who wanted to go on an adventure. He looked around and saw a big danger! He was so troubled.

He started to take a step but then he heard a noise. He stopped and he listened. The noise was coming from a little bush. He went closer to investigate.

He peeked behind it and found a little creature! He was so amazed. The little creature asked him if he wanted to come on an adventure. It sounded exciting so the boy said "Yes!"

They started to run together. The boy stopped to listen to the wind and the birds. Finally, they reached a place filled with trees and flowers. The boy was so happy!

The little creature told the boy that he had to stay quiet. He could hear all kinds of things if he kept still and listened. The boy listened closely and heard different animals and stories from the trees. He was so excited that he wanted to stay and listen for days. The little creature was happy too!

In the end, the boy decided it was time to go home. He thanked the little creature for the amazing adventure and promised to listen carefully next time he went on an adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit called Hop. He was very small and helpless. Every day he would look for something to eat in the meadow.

One day, he came across something colourful and delicious. It was a carrot. When he was about to eat it, a big, strong fox appeared. The fox told Hop to bring him the carrot. Hop felt helpless because he was too small and scared to say no. He handed over the carrot and the fox ran away.

Hop was very upset. Although the fox had taken the carrot away, Hop realised that he should help himself. He went and looked for more carrots in the meadow and eventually, he found them.

Hop brought the carrots to the animal community and they all ate together. Everyone was happy and grateful to Hop. He had taught them the moral of the story: that itâ€™s good to help others, yet donâ€™t forget to help yourself too.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah loved to explore the tidy forest near her home. She would spend hours exploring the different trees and collecting cute little rocks.

One day she was walking in the forest and she noticed something very special; the birds were singing! She was so excited by the beautiful song that she wanted to record it. She asked her Dad for help and he gave her a special machine. She took it with her and set it up in the forest.

With some help from her Dad, Sarah was able to record the beautiful birdsong. She smiled and thanked her Dad for helping her.

Sarah took the recording home and listened to it every day. She loved the way it sounded in the tidy forest and was excited hearing the birds again and again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing and dance, so her mommy signed her up for a show on a big stage. Lily was so excited, but when she got on stage, she started to shiver because it was so cold. Her mommy gave her a warm sweater to wear and she felt better.

Lily sang her heart out and everyone clapped and cheered. After the show, they went to get some ice cream, but Lily didn't like the flavor she got. It was too sour! She made a funny face and her mommy laughed. They went home happy and proud of Lily's performance. The end.

There was a little girl called Lucy. She was a very cheerful person who loved exploring nature. One day she was near the sea. She saw the tides flowing in and out. It was so interesting.

"Look, it's a tide," Lucy said cheerfully.

She started to explore the beach and soon the tide was rising. She was concerned but then she saw the beach start to dry.

"Look, it's drying," Lucy said happily.

Soon, the tide was completely gone and Lucy jumped with joy. She was so glad to see the beach back in its usual state.

She gathered some shells that were on the beach and took them home.

"Mum, I found shells on the beach," Lucy said cheerfully.

Her mum was so glad to see her daughter so happy. They had a wonderful day full of cheerfulness.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cake, especially chocolate cake with sprinkles on top. One day, Lily's mom needed to bake a cake for her friend's birthday party.

Lily was so excited to help her mom. She put on her apron and helped mix the batter. They put the cake in the modern oven and waited patiently for it to bake.

When the cake was done, they decorated it with lots of frosting and sprinkles. Lily's mom was so proud of her little helper. They took the cake to the party and everyone loved it. Lily felt so happy to have helped make such a delicious cake.

Once upon a time there was a little mouse. He was very healthy and strong. He loved to play all day and eat yummy food.

At night, the mouse would take a nap. He would find a cozy place and lay down. As soon as his head touched the ground he would go fast to sleep.

When the mouse woke up he would hop around, looking for food. He would eat little seeds and crunchy bugs. During the day he would also play with his friends.

But no matter how much fun he had, when it was time for bed he would always go back to sleep. He was a happy and healthy mouse. And he liked to sleep a lot.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous blouse. The blouse was so big it covered a whole sofa! But no one could understand why it was so big.

One day a little girl called Sara came along. Sara was only three years old. She wanted to see the blouse so she walked over to it. As she got closer and closer, she realized something amazing!

She could fit inside the blouse! She jumped right in, giggling as she did. Once she was inside, Sara knew why the blouse was so enormous - it was made for someone like her!

Sara stayed inside the blouse for the rest of the day. She felt safe and protected, and for the first time she understood how special the blouse was.

Once there was a wealthy robot who liked to do things in reverse. He reversed all the way to work, then he reversed all the way home again. He reversed when he went shopping and reversed when he went out to play. Everyone thought it was really strange but the robot liked it!

One day, the robot was reversing through the park when he saw a little boy playing. The robot was so excited he reversed right up to the boy. The boy was scared at first, but then he saw the robot was friendly and started to laugh. He asked the robot to reverse all around the park with him and the robot happily agreed!

The boy and the robot had so much fun. The boy chased the robot, and the robot chased the boy. They went around and around until it was time for the boy to go home. Before the robot left, he made sure the boy was safely back with his parents.

The robot and the boy played together a lot after that. They went on many adventures, always reversing and laughing. They were the best of friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to eat yummy candy. One day, he saw a big bag of candy at the store and he wanted it so much. But his mom said no and told him to tie his shoes instead. Timmy didn't want to tie his shoes, so he ignored his mom and ran away to the candy aisle.

When he got there, he saw that the candy was too high for him to reach. He tried to climb the shelves, but he couldn't. Just then, a kind lady saw him and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her he wanted the candy, but he couldn't reach it. The lady helped him get the candy and he was so happy.

But when he got home, his mom was very upset with him for ignoring her and running away. Timmy felt bad and said sorry to his mom. She forgave him and they ate the yummy candy together. From that day on, Timmy learned to listen to his mom and not ignore her.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty workman. He was strong, and worked very hard all day long. But one day he found a task that was too much for him.

The workman stopped to rest on the side of the work. He was very tired! Then he saw a little ant.

The workman asked the ant, "Do you have any ideas on how to finish my work? It's too much for me to do on my own!"

The ant replied, "It may take time and hard work, but if you try hard to yield, you can do it. "

The workman smiled and thanked the ant. He knew he had a lot of work to do, but he said that even he could do mighty things with a lot of hard work and effort.

The workman continued his work, and with each task he completed, he felt stronger. He kept going until he had finished the task! He smiled with pride, realizing that there was nothing too hard or too big for him.

The moral of the story is that with a lot of hard work and effort, even the mighty can yield when faced with a challenge.

THE STRAW, THE COAL, AND THE BEAN

In a village dwelt a poor old woman, who had gathered together a dish

of beans and wanted to cook them. So she made a fire on her hearth, and

that it might burn the quicker, she lighted it with a handful of straw.

When she was emptying the beans into the pan, one dropped without her

observing it, and lay on the ground beside a straw, and soon afterwards

a burning coal from the fire leapt down to the two. Then the straw

began and said: 'Dear friends, from whence do you come here?' The coal

replied: 'I fortunately sprang out of the fire, and if I had not escaped

by sheer force, my death would have been certain,--I should have been

burnt to ashes.' The bean said: 'I too have escaped with a whole skin,

but if the old woman had got me into the pan, I should have been made

into broth without any mercy, like my comrades.' 'And would a better

fate have fallen to my lot?' said the straw. 'The old woman has

destroyed all my brethren in fire and smoke; she seized sixty of them at

once, and took their lives. I luckily slipped through her fingers.'

'But what are we to do now?' said the coal.

'I think,' answered the bean, 'that as we have so fortunately escaped

death, we should keep together like good companions, and lest a new

mischance should overtake us here, we should go away together, and

repair to a foreign country.'

The proposition pleased the two others, and they set out on their way

together. Soon, however, they came to a little brook, and as there was

no bridge or foot-plank, they did not know how they were to get over

it. The straw hit on a good idea, and said: 'I will lay myself straight

across, and then you can walk over on me as on a bridge.' The straw

therefore stretched itself from one bank to the other, and the coal,

who was of an impetuous disposition, tripped quite boldly on to the

newly-built bridge. But when she had reached the middle, and heard the

water rushing beneath her, she was after all, afraid, and stood still,

and ventured no farther. The straw, however, began to burn, broke in

two pieces, and fell into the stream. The coal slipped after her, hissed

when she got into the water, and breathed her last. The bean, who had

prudently stayed behind on the shore, could not but laugh at the event,

was unable to stop, and laughed so heartily that she burst. It would

have been all over with her, likewise, if, by good fortune, a tailor who

was travelling in search of work, had not sat down to rest by the brook.

As he had a compassionate heart he pulled out his needle and thread,

and sewed her together. The bean thanked him most prettily, but as the

tailor used black thread, all beans since then have a black seam.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Benny. He was only three years old, but he was very curious. He wanted to know why things were the way they were.

One day, Benny went outside and found a patch of wet grass. He asked his father why it was so wet. His father told him it was because of the rain. Benny asked his father if he could make it stop raining. His father said, "No, Benny, that's not something we can do."

Benny was a little bit sad but he thanked his father for telling him about the rain. Then he asked his father why people were so modest. His father explained that modesty was a way of showing respect and being polite. Benny thought about this for a minute and then said, "But why do we need to be polite?" His father smiled at him and told him, "Because it's the nice thing to do."

Benny nodded and smiled. He thanked his father again and they went inside the house to have a snack. Benny was thankful that his Father had told him these things. He was sure he was going to learn a lot more by the time he got to be five.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and daddy. She loved to swing and slide, but she forgot to bring her favorite toy with her.

While playing, she saw a police officer walking by. He was wearing a blue uniform and a shiny badge. Lily asked him, "What is your job?" The police officer said, "I enforce the law and keep everyone safe."

Lily was fascinated by the police officer's job. She started twirling around and around until she got dizzy. Her mommy and daddy took her home and tucked her into bed. As she fell asleep, she dreamt about becoming a police officer when she grew up.

One day, Tim saw an enormous rocket in his yard. He was very excited. He wanted to show his friend, Sam. "Sam, come see the big rocket!" Tim said.

Sam came running to see the rocket. It was so big and shiny. But then, Sam did something silly. He tripped and fell on the rocket. It made a loud noise. Tim and Sam felt embarrass.

The rocket started to shake and smoke. "Oh no!" said Tim. The rocket went up into the sky very fast. It made a big boom. Tim and Sam were sad. They knew they should not have touched the rocket. They wished they could have played with it longer.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they decided to build a tent in the backyard. They used blankets and chairs to make it. It was so much fun!

But then, Lily's friend Tommy wanted to play a different game. Lily was stubborn and didn't want to stop playing in the tent. She screamed, "No! I want to stay in the tent!" Her friends tried to convince her to play something else, but she wouldn't listen.

After a while, Lily realized that it was more fun to play with her friends than to be stubborn. She apologized and they all played together happily. And they even used the tent as a secret hideout for their new game. The end.

The sun showed its face in the morning sky and it shone brightly. The birds flew up to the sky and sang their happy song.

Then, a little girl named Lucy came out of her house and looked up. She saw the bright sun and the fluffy clouds. She was so happy that she jumped up with excitement!

Lucy: "Look at the beautiful clouds! I wish I could go up and touch them!"

Suddenly, there was a rumble in the sky. Something had blocked out the sun and the sky had become dark.

Lucy looked up and saw that a big selfish cloud had come between the sun and the sky.

Lucy: "No, not that selfish cloud! Get away!"

But the selfish cloud didn't move. It just stayed there and blocked out the sun.

Lucy was sad and she slowly walked back to her house. The sun slowly returned and the sky became sunny and bright once again.

Lucy was surprised that the selfish cloud had gone away. She was so happy that she smiled and shouted in joy.

Lucy: "Yay! Thank goodness the selfish cloud is gone!"

Once upon a time, two friends, Tom and Jill, decided to go for a walk. They decided to cross a meadow, but when they arrived, they were stopped by a fence. Tom said, "I can't reach the top. What should we do?"

Jill said: "Let's use my wool. It is long and thin, and it will help us climb over the fence."

The friends tried to climb the fence using the wool. It took some time, but after a few attempts, they both managed to get over the fence.

When they were on the other side, they looked back and saw the fence they had climbed. Jill said to Tom, "What a clear fence! We should have seen it earlier".

Moral: It is important to take time and look closely at any obstacle before trying to solve it.

Once upon a time there was a man who had a wife. One day, the man wanted to go on a trip. He asked his wife to come with him, but she said no. The man felt guilty for wanting to go without her. He thought about it for a long time and decided to lead his wife on the journey instead.

When they arrived at their destination, they both had a wonderful time. They explored the area and looked at all the amazing sights. They were very happy to be together.

The man was happy he had decided to lead his wife on this journey. He knew that he did the right thing, and he was no longer feeling guilty. From then on, they decided to make more trips together. They were so happy to be together that each journey was even more special than the last.

Lily liked to do yoga with her mom. Yoga was when they made funny shapes with their bodies on a mat. Sometimes they were trees, sometimes they were cats, sometimes they were stars. Lily liked to stretch and breathe and feel calm.

One day, Lily saw a big sack in the corner of the living room. She wondered what was inside. She asked her mom, but her mom said it was a surprise. Lily was curious. She wanted to see the surprise. She waited until her mom was busy in the kitchen, and then she tiptoed to the sack.

She opened the sack and peeked inside. She saw lots of toys and books and clothes. They were all new and shiny and colorful. Lily was happy. She thought the sack was a gift for her. She pulled out a doll, a puzzle, a hat, and a ball. She played with them on the floor. She made a mess.

Her mom came back and saw the mess. She was not happy. She said, "Lily, what have you done? This sack is not for you. It is for the children who don't have many things. We are going to give it to them tomorrow. You have to put everything back and make it tidy."

Lily felt sad. She did not mean to be naughty. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I thought it was for me. I like the toys and books and clothes. Can I keep one?" Her mom said, "No, Lily. You have enough things. You have to share with others. That is what yoga teaches us. To be kind and generous and grateful. Now, help me put everything back and make it tidy."

Lily helped her mom put everything back in the sack. She said goodbye to the doll, the puzzle, the hat, and the ball. She said, "I hope you make the children happy. Maybe they will do yoga with you." She hugged her mom and said, "I love you, mom. I'm sorry I made a mess. Can we do yoga now?" Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. Yes, we can do yoga now. Let's be trees." They smiled and made funny shapes with their bodies on the mat. They stretched and breathed and felt calm.

Once upon a time, there were two sister called Jane and Sue. Jane's dress was very dull and plain, but Sue had the most beautiful dress. It was the color of a beautiful summer sky and had gorgeous velvet petals that bloomed in the sun. The dress twirled and sparkled when Sue spun around on the grass.

One day, Jane grew very jealous of Sue's dress. She wished she had something as beautiful as her sister. The next morning, Jane got dressed and noticed her dull dress had bloomed with lovely, bright colors. Now her dress was just like Sue's!

Jane skipped to school, beaming with joy. When su see saw Jane she gasped with delight and asked if she had gotten a new dress. Jane smiled and said, "Nope, I guess my old one just bloomed!"

Once upon a time there was a girl named Daisy. She loved to drink tea. Today, she was feeling very serious. She decided to make tea for her mum. But when she went to the kitchen, she noticed that the teapot was broken! Daisy sighed and was about to cry. But then she saw that mum had left a new one for her to replace the old one. Daisy was very happy. She filled up the teapot with water and put in some tea leaves. Soon the tea was ready, and it was very yummy. She poured it into two cups and shared it with her mum. They both were happy and hugged each other. Daisy was so glad that she could replace the old teapot. And from then on, they could drink tea together every day.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with toys, draw pictures and read books. One day, Lily saw a big frame in Ben's room. It had a shiny photo of Ben and his family.

"Wow, what is that?" Lily asked.

"That is my frame. My grandma gave it to me. She is very rich. She lives in a big house with a lot of things. She said this frame is very special and I should keep it safe," Ben said.

Lily felt sad. She did not have a frame like that. She did not have a grandma who was rich. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. They did not have a lot of things. She wished she had a frame like Ben.

"Can I touch it?" Lily asked.

"No, you can't. It is mine. You might break it or make it dirty. Go play with something else," Ben said.

Lily felt hurt. She did not like how Ben talked to her. She thought he was not a good friend. She went to her room and cried.

Later, Ben felt sorry. He did not mean to make Lily cry. He remembered that Lily was his best friend. He liked to play with her and share his toys. He did not care if she had a frame or not. He cared if she was happy or not.

He went to Lily's room and knocked on the door.

"Lily, can I come in?" Ben asked.

Lily opened the door. She saw Ben holding his frame.

"What do you want?" Lily asked.

"I want to say I am sorry. I was not nice to you. I want to share my frame with you. You can touch it and look at it. It is not as special as our friendship," Ben said.

Lily smiled. She felt happy. She hugged Ben and thanked him. She looked at his frame and said it was very pretty. She said she liked his family.

They went back to Ben's room and played with toys, drew pictures and read books. They felt glad. They learned that being rich is not about having things. It is about having friends.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was very impatient. She wanted to write something, but she didn't have a pen. The girl saw a stick! She was so excited. She thought "This stick will do". She started to write with it. The stick was too hard and it broke. The girl was angry. She threw the broken stick away and started to cry. She had to wait until she could buy a pen and write her story. The end.

Root wasnâ€™t quite sure what to make of it all, and felt a little troubled. He had never seen so many different animals around.

He noticed a small rabbit with long ears, who was hopping around in the grass. He decided to talk to her, hoping that she would be friendly.

Once upon a time, there was a unique little girl called Daisy. Daisy was so excited one day when she saw a telephone for the very first time. She ran straight to it and asked her mum, "Can I introduce myself to the phone?"

Mum said, "Yes, of course!" So Daisy started talking to the telephone and said, "Hello, phone. My name is Daisy. What's your name?"

Suddenly, Daisy heard an unfamiliar voice coming from the telephone. The voice said, "My name is Joe. Nice to meet you, Daisy." Daisy was so excited to finally make a new friend.

The next day, Daisy went back to the telephone and said, "Hello, Joe! It's me, Daisy. Let's chat again!" But this time, Joe did not answer. It seemed like Joe was gone forever.

Suddenly, Daisy learned a valuable lesson. She realized that you can never be sure who you are talking to over the telephone.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was an attractive bird named Chirpie. Chirpie wanted to paint the biggest picture anyone had ever seen. Chirpie flew everywhere looking for the perfect color of ink. Finally, Chirpie found the ink, it was a nice, sparkly blue!

Chirpie flew back home, carrying the ink carefully in her beak. She worked all day and all night to get the picture just right. When it was done, she looked at it with delight.

Chirpie proudly hopped up on her perch and called out to her friends. "Come and see what I have made!" she cried.

The other birds flew to her perch and gasped in amazement. It was the most beautiful, colorful picture they had ever seen. Everyone clapped and applauded.

"Well done, Chirpie," they said in unison.

Chirpie smiled, she had never felt so proud. It was just the beginning of her journey as an artist and she knew there would be more beautiful works of art to come.

Once there was a large dog named Jog. He lived in a big house in the country. Every morning, Jog would go for a long jog and enjoy the warm sun.

One day, Jog's owners decided it was time to remove him from their home. They thought he was getting to be too large for them to take care of. Jog was sad to say goodbye to his home and family.

The next day, Jog found himself in a new house on a big farm. He was so excited to explore his new home. Every day, Jog went for long jogs around the farm. He soon made lots of new friends who joined him on his jogs.

Jog still misses his old home and family, but he is happy to have found a loving new home on the farm. He never goes without his daily jog!

Jim was a lonely boy, who often felt alone. But one day, he heard a very special noise. It was the operation of a tractor! He was so excited that he said to the farmer, "Can you teach me to drive a tractor?"

The farmer was glad to teach Jim how to drive a tractor. First, the farmer showed Jim how to operate the controls. He explained that Jim needed to steer the steering wheel and use the pedals to make the tractor move.

Jim was so excited to learn how to drive the tractor. The farmer showed him how to press the pedals in the right order to make the tractor move. Jim was amazed! He said to the farmer, "thank you for teaching me how to drive a tractor!"

Jim was very proud of himself. With the help of the farmer, he had learned to operate the tractor. From that day on, Jim wasn't so lonely anymore. He would take the tractor for joy rides, out in the sunny fields, and explore places he had never been before. He was so proud of himself and his tractor!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play sports. He played soccer, basketball, and baseball. He was very good at all of them.

One day, Timmy's mom took him to the store to buy some new sports equipment. Timmy saw a crazy looking ball that he really wanted. He begged his mom to buy it for him, but she said they couldn't afford it.

Timmy was sad, but he remembered that he had some money saved up from doing chores. He asked his mom if he could pay for the ball himself. She agreed, and Timmy was so happy to have his new crazy ball. He played with it every day and it made him very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called George. He was three years old and one day he wanted to make a drink. He went to the kitchen and he saw his mom's big, messy freezer. He wanted to get something out of it to make his drink.

He opened the freezer door and saw many different things inside. He saw delicious ice creams and yummy popsicles. He also saw special juice boxes. He quickly grabbed one and put it in the freezer again.

George was so excited to make his drink. He quickly opened the juice box and put it in a cup. Then he put the cup in the microwave to warm it. After a few minutes, the drink was ready.

He took a sip and it was yummy. He had made the perfect drink for himself. He was so proud!

Once upon a time there were two friends, Ben and Jack. Ben loved to bounce and Jack loved to mix things. One day, they decided to have a day of play. Ben and Jack took turns, Ben bouncing and Jack mixing.

But while they were playing, they accidentally broke their parents' mixer. Ben and Jack were so scared and they ran away, not knowing what to do.

A nice lady in the neighbourhood saw that the boys were scared and very sorry. She said to them: "Boys, be careful next time. Sometimes things can break when we are playing so we must be careful."

Ben and Jack looked at each other and nodded. They decided to go back home and clean up the mess they made.

The boys knew that from then on they were always going to be careful when playing, so nothing like this would happen again.

Moral of the story: Be careful when playing so you don't make a mess!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Lila. She was playing in her garden one day when a stranger came for a visit. Lila was very scared and started to cry.

The stranger saw her and said, "What's wrong?"

Lila said, "I'm scared! Who are you?"

The stranger replied, "I'm just a kind stranger. I want to help you."

Lila wiped her tears away and said, "Will you carry me away from here?"

The stranger smiled and said, "Yes, I'll carry you away from this miserable place!" He picked up Lila in his arms and slowly carried her away into the distance.

The end.

Lily and Ben are twins who like to play pretend. They have a toy kitchen and a lot of plastic food. One day, they decide to perform a show for their mom and dad. They want to make a menu with healthy food that their parents will like.

Lily says, "I will make a salad with lettuce, tomato, and cheese. What will you make, Ben?"

Ben says, "I will make a pizza with pepperoni, cheese, and sauce. Pizza is yummy!"

Lily says, "But pizza is not healthy, Ben. It has too much fat and salt. Mom and dad will not like it."

Ben says, "Pizza is healthy, Lily. It has cheese and sauce. Cheese and sauce are good for you. Mom and dad will love it."

Lily and Ben start to argue. They do not agree on what is healthy and what is not. They do not want to share their food or their kitchen. They start to pull and push each other.

Mom and dad hear the noise and come to see what is going on. They see Lily and Ben fighting over the toy kitchen and the plastic food. They are not happy.

Mom says, "Lily and Ben, what are you doing? Why are you fighting?"

Dad says, "We thought you were going to perform a show for us. Where is your menu?"

Lily and Ben stop fighting. They feel ashamed. They say, "We are sorry, mom and dad. We wanted to make a menu with healthy food, but we could not agree on what is healthy. We did not want to share our food or our kitchen."

Mom says, "Lily and Ben, it is okay to have different opinions on what is healthy. But it is not okay to fight over it. You have to respect each other and share your toys. You can make a menu with both salad and pizza. That way, you can have some variety and balance."

Dad says, "That sounds like a good idea. We would love to see your show and try your food. Can you work together and make a menu with both salad and pizza?"

Lily and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, mom and dad. We can work together and make a menu with both salad and pizza. We are sorry for fighting. We love you."

Mom and dad hug Lily and Ben. They say, "We love you too. We are proud of you for apologizing and cooperating. Now, let's see your show and your menu!"

Mum and Dad took their 3 year old daughter to the pet shop. She was so excited to see all the puppies and kittens. "Can I get a kitten, please Mum and Dad?" she asked. Mum and Dad looked at each other and grinned.

"We will have to manage. We don't have much money for a pet," said Dad.

Little girl was disappointed and started to walk away. Suddenly, she saw the most adorable little kitten in a cage. She gasped.

"Can I get him, Mum and Dad? Please?"

But Mum and Dad noticed that the kitten was too quiet, almost fake.

"That kitten isn't real, honey," said Mum.

Little girl was so sad that she couldn't get the kitten. But Mum and Dad smiled, gave her a big hug and told her that they could manage to buy her an ice cream on the way home.

Little girl was so excited and beamed with joy. They all laughed and went off to get an ice cream. Even though she didn't have a real live kitten, she was very happy.

One day a little rabbit was walking through the woods. He bumped into a big bear. The bear said, "What do you want?" The little rabbit was so scared, he stuttered, "I...I...I was just walking through."

The bear got angry. He said, "You must yield this bottle to me, or else!" The little rabbit started to cry. He didn't want to give the bear the bottle, but he had no choice. He reluctantly gave it to the bear.

The bear took the bottle and smiled. He said, "You are so selfish, giving me only one bottle." The rabbit was relieved. He thought, "If I had given him more bottles, it would have been even worse!"

The bear said, "Next time, think twice before refusing another bear's request." The rabbit nodded in agreement. He then bowed and walked away quickly, grateful that he had been spared by the selfish bear.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Julie. She was a very brave and adventurous girl who loved doing new things. One day, Julie was walking through a dark and scary forest. She was scared, but she kept walking. As she walked, she heard a strange noise. It sounded like some one was talking.

Julie slowly moved closer and closer to the noise until she spotted a man sitting in the shadows. She couldn't see his face, but he was speaking.

"I'm so thirsty," the man said, "I wish I had some of that nice smelling perfume." He laughed.

Julie felt scared, but she was also curious. She thought to herself, "Maybe I should give him some perfume."
Julie slowly moved closer and closer, but before she could reach the man, he suddenly jumped out of the shadows and grabbed her by the arm.

"Give me your perfume!" he shouted. Julie was so scared, but she still tried to speak.

"Please, let me go," she managed to say. But the man was too angry and wouldn't listen.

He grabbed the perfume from her and ran away, leaving her alone in the dark forest. Julie never saw him again, and that was the last time she ever felt brave enough to do something new.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Joe and Sammy.
Joe and Sammy were both very powerful.

One day, Joe and Sammy decided to go to a restaurant. They gathered up their things and set off.

When they arrived at the restaurant, they saw many delicious treats. Joe said, "Let's get some ice cream!"
Sammy replied, "Yes! That sounds yummy!"

So they gathered up their bowls, spoons and toppings. They ordered their ice cream and began to eat.

The ice cream tasted so good. After they finished, they gave each other a big hug and said goodbye.

Joe and Sammy had a wonderful time gathering at the restaurant, and they were even more powerful friends than before. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a bell. Every morning it lifted everyone out of bed with its cheerful sound. Everyone in the village was so enthusiastic to get up and enjoy the day.

One day, a three year old boy decided he wanted to lift the bell too. He rushed outside and took hold of it. He was so proud that he had managed to do it.

The villagers were impressed by the little boy's enthusiasm. They cheered him on and clapped their hands.

The boy was delighted. Every morning from that day forward, he was the first one to lift the bell and let everyone know it was time to start the day!

Once upon a time, there was an amazing orange. It was a special orange, because it could repeat everything it heard. One day, a three year old boy came across the orange. The boy was so excited. He said "Hello orange!" and the orange said "Hello!" right back.

The little boy couldn't believe it. He kept talking so the orange could repeat the words over and over again. He asked the orange to sing a song, so the orange sang "Twinkle, twinkle little star". The boy was so amazed that he sang right along with the orange.

The boy and his orange had so much fun together. Each day they played and talked. The little boy was so happy. He loved his amazing orange.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big bookcase in her room that was full of books. Lily loved to read books about princesses and animals. One day, she saw a friendly cat outside her window. The cat meowed and Lily meowed back. They started to talk to each other in a friendly way.

The cat told Lily that he liked to climb bookcases too. Lily showed the cat her big bookcase and they both climbed up to the top. They looked at all the books and talked about their favorite stories. Lily was so happy to have a new friendly friend to talk to. From that day on, Lily and the cat would climb the bookcase together and talk about their favorite books.

Once upon a time, there was a small dog named Daisy. Daisy was a very happy dog. Every day, Daisy would go for a walk and explore the world.

One day, Daisy was walking and she noticed something beautiful. It was a match! Daisy was so excited to find a match because she loved to chew things and this was the perfect size.

Daisy picked up the match and chewed it. She was so happy that she jumped up and down and barked to say "Thank you!".

Then a voice came from behind her: "Is that your match?". Daisy turned around and saw a beautiful girl. She was wearing a pink dress and had a big smile.

The girl said: "I like your match. Do you wanna play with me?" Daisy barked happily and said "Yes!". Daisy and the girl had lots of fun playing together. Daisy chewed the match while they ran around and played.

At the end of the day, Daisy was sad to say goodbye, but the girl said, "Don't forget your beautiful match!" Daisy said "Thank you" and hugged the girl. Then, Daisy ran off happily carrying her match with her.

Once upon a time there was an old man who had a funny haircut. He had grey hair that stuck out in all directions and an old straw hat on top.

One day, he was walking down the street when he felt something poke his back. He turned around and saw a small boy with a mischievous twinkle in his eye.

The old man smiled at the boy and said, "What are you doing, young man? Are you trying to give me a haircut?"

The boy giggled and dashed away without saying a word.

The old man shook his head and kept walking. He wanted to laugh, but he knew the boy was just having fun.

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. Lily saw a purple flower that was very pretty. She wanted to smell it.

"Look, Max, a purple flower!" she said. "I want to smell it."

She ran to the flower and bent down. But she did not see the bee that was on the flower. The bee was busy getting nectar. It did not like to be disturbed.

Max saw the bee and got scared. He knew that bees could sting. He wanted to stop Lily.

"Lily, no!" he shouted. "There is a bee! It can hurt you!"

He ran after Lily and tried to pull her away. He urged her to leave the flower alone. But Lily did not listen. She was too curious.

She reached out her hand and touched the flower. The bee felt her and got angry. It flew up and buzzed around her head. Lily screamed and dropped the flower. She ran back to Max and hugged him.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she cried. "The bee is mad! It wants to sting me!"

Max hugged her back and tried to calm her down. He looked around and saw the bee fly away. He was relieved.

"It's okay, Lily," he said. "The bee is gone. It won't sting you. But you should not touch the flowers with bees. They don't like it. They need the flowers for food."

Lily nodded and sniffed. She was sorry for making the bee mad. She learned her lesson.

"I'm sorry, Max," she said. "I won't touch the flowers with bees again. I'll just look at them. They are still pretty."

Max smiled and kissed her cheek.

"That's good, Lily," he said. "Let's go and find some other flowers. Maybe we can find some yellow ones. Or pink ones. Or blue ones. There are many colors of flowers. And they all smell nice."

Lily smiled and wiped her tears. She took Max's hand and followed him. They went to look for more flowers. But they were careful to avoid the bees. They wanted to be friends with the bees, not enemies.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived at the beach. Every day, she would take a bucket and shovel and build a sandcastle. She loved to watch the giant waves crashing against it. One day, she decided to build an extra big sandcastle!

As she was making it, a shark swam towards her. The girl screamed and ran away from the shark. But then, it swam up to her and said, "Don't be scared! I just want to help you build your sandcastle!"

The girl was still afraid, but the shark said, "I'm a friendly shark! I won't hurt you, I promise!" So the girl reached into her pocket and pulled out a little open bag of sand. She sprinkled it over the sandcastle and the shark used his tail to spread it around. Together, they built a beautiful sandcastle.

The girl and her new friend said goodbye and, as the waves gently washed away the sandcastle at the end of the day, the girl was happy knowing that she and the friendly shark had built something wonderful together.

Once upon a time, in a small garden, there was a little caterpillar. The caterpillar was green and liked to eat leaves. He had many friends in the garden, like the birds and the bees.

One sunny day, the caterpillar was feeling dizzy. He didn't know why. His friend, the bird, saw him and said, "Let's go to the pond and splash some water on you." The caterpillar thought it was a good idea.

They went to the pond together. The bird picked up the caterpillar with its beak and splashed water on him. The caterpillar felt better after the splash. He was not dizzy anymore. They both laughed and played by the pond. The caterpillar was happy to have such a good friend.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby beehive. It flew around looking for food. One day, it decided to sail away. It flew high in the sky, looking down on the world below.

The beehive sailed over land and sea. Eventually, it saw a big, beautiful lake. The beehive decided to land there. As it floated down, it heard the sound of music coming from the lake.

The beehive circled around until it found the source of the music. Inside the lake was a chubby boat with people singing and dancing. The beehive joined in their fun and the people welcomed it with open arms.

The beehive stayed with the people and they all sailed away together. The lake was full of adventure and the beehive felt at home. As they floated away, they looked back at the lake with fond memories.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to dance to the rhythm of the music. He had a nice smile on his face whenever he danced. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to name his favorite dance. Timmy replied, "I like the wiggly dance the most!" So, Timmy started wiggling and dancing to the rhythm of the music, and his mom smiled and said, "That's a nice dance, Timmy!"

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sally. She liked to play with her doll named Lucy. One day, Sally met a boy named Tom. Tom had a toy car. They played together and had fun.

Sally said to Tom, "I want to marry you." Tom said, "OK, let's marry." They played a game where they pretended to be married. They had a big party with their toys.

But then, a bad dog came. The dog took Lucy and the toy car. Sally and Tom said, "No, bad dog!" They chased the dog and got their toys back. They were happy and played together again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was three years old and she was very curious. She loved exploring and had lots of adventures.

One day, Daisy's Mommy gave her a very special gear. It was a delicate gear made of wood. Daisy was so excited. She wanted to know how it worked, but she didn't know what to do with it.

So Daisy asked her Daddy for help. Daddy said that Daisy needed to be gentle when handling the gear because it was so delicate. He showed Daisy how to use it and soon she was very proud of her new gear.

Every day, Daisy kept exploring with her gear. She started to know how special it was and how it made her adventures more exciting. Daisy was so happy to know about the gear and kept discovering new things with it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. The girl had a stick. She liked to use the stick to draw in the sand.

One day, she went to the beach. She found a lot of seashells and sea rocks. The girl wanted to keep the shells for herself.

Suddenly, she heard something in the water. It was a fish in trouble! He was stuck in a net that was too tight. The girl was scared, but she knew she had to help. So, she grabbed the stick and started to help the fish. The girl first struggled to cut through the net. But slowly, the net started to tear. Then, the little girl reached in and pulled out the fish. She had saved him!

The fish thanked the girl and swam away back into the sea. The girl was happy. She had used her little stick to save him.

Once upon a time, there was a turkey who loved to laugh. He giggled, cackled and guffawed all the time.

One day, a little boy named Tim found some clay. It was soft and brown. He wanted to make something with it. He thought hard about what to make. Tim was confused.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the grass and watch the bugs. One day, she found a cricket who was stuck in a puddle of water. Lily knew she had to save the cricket, so she carefully picked it up and put it on a leaf.

Her mom came in. The girl showed her the penny. Her mom smiled and said, "Wow! What a tidy penny. You can keep it safe in your room."

The girl nodded, and put the penny in her drawer. Then, she shut the drawer tightly.

The girl was so happy that she had a shiny penny. She hugged it and thanked her mom for letting her keep it. From then on, she kept her room very tidy so she could keep her penny safe.

Once upon a time there was an embarrassed structure. It was all alone in the middle of a field. Every morning the structure wanted to spring, but it had never done it before. One day, it finally gathered all its courage and said "I'm going to spring!" It took a deep breath and jumped. Its jump was so high that it almost touched the sky. Russel decided to make a different request for her and her bunny the next time. They ate the rest of the squash and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who wanted to hang with his friends. He asked Mum if he could go outside and play. Mum said he could go, but he had to be safe. So, the boy ran out with his friends and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to read books. One day, her mom took her to the library. The library was a big building with lots of books.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the beach with her mom and dad. They had a fun day playing in the sand and splashing in the water. Lily found a pretty shell that she wanted to show her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, even when it was very cold and the ground was icy. One day, she was playing with her friend Timmy when they saw a beautiful bird in a tree.

Once upon a time, in a peaceful town, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to run and play outside. One day, Tim saw a race in the park. He was excited and wanted to join the race.

Once upon a time there was a reindeer that belonged to a very strong man. The man loved to show off the reindeer to the other villagers. He was very proud of his reindeer and would always tell them he belonged to him.

Mama told Matty not to wander away, but Matty started walking. He was curious and wanted to explore.

Timmy was walking in the park when he remembered something his teacher had said to him. She said that keeping a diary helps people to show how they feel. He smiled and ran back home to get paper and some pens.

When Timmy got home he told his mom that he wanted to write a diary. His mom quickly said no. Timmy complained and asked why not? She said that writing a diary can take a long time and she wanted him to do something faster.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mommy. They saw a great bird flying in the sky. Lily said, "Mommy, look at that big bird! Can we go see it?"

Mommy said, "Sure, let's go see the bird." But as they walked towards the bird, they saw that there was a big tree in the way. Mommy said, "We have to go around the tree, it will delay us a little bit."

Once upon a time there was an ordinary barber. He cut people's hair and made them feel happy. Every day he watched people come and go from his shop. One day a little boy walked into the shop. He was only three years old and his hair was very messy.

He sat on the barber's chair and the barber started to cut his hair. His little eyes watched as the barber snipped away. When the barber was finished, the little boy's hair looked neat and tidy. He was very pleased and thanked the barber.

The barber watched as the little boy skipped out of the shop. He smiled to himself and thought, "That's why I love being an ordinary barber."

Once upon a time, there was a dull jungle. In this jungle there lived an elephant who loved to move around. Every day, the elephant would move around in her jungle looking for new things. One day as the elephant was moving around, she saw something strange. It was a deep hole in the ground.

The elephant was curious and wanted to know what was inside. She moved closer to take a look. As soon as she moved closer, the ground started to shake and rumble. The elephant felt scared and tried to move away, but it was too late. The ground opened up and the elephant fell into the deep, dark hole.

The elephant tried and tried to get out, but she could not move. She was stuck in the deep, dark hole and she stayed there forever, never to be seen again.

David and Sarah were the best of friends. They lived in the same street and would walk and play together almost every day. One day, they were walking in the park when Sarah spotted a puppy. She ran towards it and kneeled, ready to give it a hug.

"Be careful!" David said as he nodded his head. Sarah knew that he was being kind and trying to protect her from being too rough with the puppy. But a rude man started shouting at them. "Don't touch my dog!" he said.

It scared both of them, so David took Sarah's hand and they ran away. As soon as they were far enough away, David gave Sarah a big hug. "That was a bit scary, wasn't it?" David said. Sarah nodded her head, glad to have her friend with her.

David and Sarah both knew that they had each other when something scary happened. With a big smile, they started to walk home together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the museum with her mommy and daddy. They would see lots of cool things like big dinosaurs and shiny rocks.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint pictures with her mommy. One day, Lily asked if she could paint her room. Her mommy said yes and gave her permission to do so.

Once upon a time, in a modest little house, there lived a girl named Amy. Amy liked to test all things she found. One day, she found a cactus in her yard. The cactus was green and had little spikes on it.

After that, Amy told her friends about the cactus. They all went to see it, but they did not touch it. They knew the cactus was not nice to touch. They played around the modest house and had fun. The cactus stayed in the yard, and Amy never touched it again.

Once upon a time there was a nation. The nation was very obedient and followed the rules. All the people in the nation were happy and content.

From then on, the obedient nation always remembered the special knot that tied them together. They kept it safe and held on to it for always.

One day, two little friends were having a conversation. One of them was very loyal, the other one was not. The loyal one was honest, always speaking kind words.

"Let's go and get some lumber together," said the loyal friend.

When the project was complete, the loyal friend said: "See, I told you it would be worth it. We must always be loyal and speak kind words to those around us.â€

Paula was a very intelligent and curious three year old girl. She loved to explore the world around her, especially when she and her family went for walks through the neighbourhood park. On this particular day, Paula noticed a wagon near the playground. She asked her dad what it was and he told her it was a special wagon just for her!

Paula was so excited and she quickly ran over to the wagon, jumping inside. Her dad smiled and started pushing her around the park. Every time she came across something new, she asked her dad what it was and he patiently answered all her questions.

Paula had a feeling this was going to be the beginning of something special. She couldn't quite put her finger on it, but as they continued walking, more and more crows started appearing around them. Anna and Ben are twins. They like to do many things together, but they are also different. Anna likes to play with dolls and draw pictures. Ben likes to play with cars and build blocks. Sometimes they share, and sometimes they fight.

One day, their mom takes them to the market. The market is a big place with many people and things. Mom wants to buy some food and clothes. Anna and Ben want to see the toys and books.

"Mom, can we go to the toy stall?" Anna asks.

"Mom, can we go to the book stall?" Ben asks.

Mom says, "Not now, we have to get the things we need first. Then we can look at the toys and books."

Anna and Ben are not happy. They complain and whine. They say, "Mom, this is boring. We want to see the toys and books. Why do we have to wait?"

Mom says, "Please be patient and quiet. We will go to the toy and book stalls soon. But first we have to get the food and clothes. They are important for us."

Anna and Ben do not listen. They keep complaining and whining. They make a lot of noise. Mom is angry and tired. She says, "That's enough. If you don't stop complaining and whining, we will not go to the toy and book stalls at all. We will go home right now."

Anna and Ben are scared. They do not want to go home without seeing the toys and books. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We will be good. We will stop complaining and whining. We will wait for you."

Mom says, "Thank you. I'm glad you understand. Now let's finish our shopping and then we can go to the toy and book stalls."

Anna and Ben nod and smile. They hold Mom's hand and follow her. They are quiet and polite. They hope to see some toys and books that they like. They also hope that Mom will buy them something. They think that maybe being different is not so bad, as long as they can share and have fun.

One day, Lily and Ben went to the park with their mom. They saw a big slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They wanted to play with everything.

"Can we go on the slide, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, but be careful. There are some holes in the ground. Don't step on them or you might fall," mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded and ran to the slide. They took turns sliding down and laughing. They had a lot of fun.

But then, Ben saw something shiny in the grass. He ran to it and picked it up. It was a brilliant coin. He was very happy.

"Look, Lily, I found a coin! It's so shiny and pretty!" Ben said.

"Wow, that's cool! Can I see it?" Lily said.

Ben showed her the coin. He was very proud.

"Where did you find it?" Lily asked.

"Over there, in the grass. Maybe there are more. Let's go and look," Ben said.

He ran to the grass again, but he did not watch where he was going. He stepped on a hole and tripped. He fell and hurt his knee. He dropped the coin and it rolled away.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried.

Lily and mom heard him and ran to him. They helped him up and checked his knee. It was bleeding a little.

"Are you okay, Ben?" mom asked.

"It hurts, mom. And I lost my coin," Ben said.

"I'm sorry, Ben. But you should have listened to me. I told you not to step on the holes. They are dangerous. You have to be careful where you walk," mom said.

"I know, mom. I was silly. I only cared about the coin. I should have watched where I was going," Ben said.

He hugged mom and said he was sorry. Mom hugged him back and said she forgave him. She put a band-aid on his knee and gave him a kiss.

Lily gave him a hug too and said she was sorry he lost his coin. She said she would share her toys with him.

Ben smiled and thanked her. He said he was lucky to have a mom and a sister who loved him. He said he learned his lesson. He said he would be more careful and not step on holes again.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of being careful, listening to advice, and caring more about people than things.

Once there was a little boy called Jack. He was three years old and loved to be outside in the garden. One day he saw a hose and asked his mum what it was for.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to go on a wild adventure. So he asked his mom, "Can I please go out into the wild?"

Ben and Lily were twins who shared a room. They liked to play with their toys and read books before they went to sleep. But one night, there was a big storm outside. The wind made loud noises and the rain hit the window. Ben and Lily felt scared.

"Ben, I don't like the storm. It's scary," Lily said, hugging her teddy bear.

"Ben, look! There's water coming from the roof! What if it falls on us?" Lily said, pointing at the leak.

"Oh no, Lily! That's not good. We have to tell Mom and Dad. Maybe they can fix it," Ben said, getting out of bed.

They ran to their parents' room and knocked on the door. Mom and Dad opened it and saw their scared faces.

"Mom, Dad, there's a leak in our room! Water is dripping from the ceiling! Can you help us?" Ben and Lily said together.

Mom and Dad hugged them and said, "Oh, you poor things. We're sorry you're scared. We didn't know there was a leak. Come on, let's go see what we can do."

Once upon a time, there was a big and strong bear. He was walking through the forest and he found something shiny on the ground. He stopped and stared at it. It was a big mineral! The bear was excited. He wanted to pick it up and show it to the other animals in the forest.

Sara and Tom were playing in the yard. Sara had a big nail that she found in the garage. She was curious about it. She wanted to see what it could do.

Sara ran towards Tom with the nail in her hand. She wanted to poke him with it. She wanted to make him hurt. She wanted to make him sorry.

Tom saw Sara coming. He was scared. He tried to run away. But he was too slow. Sara caught him. She poked him with the nail. She poked him hard.

Sara and Tom learned a lesson. They learned that nails are dangerous. They learned that teasing is wrong. They learned that playing with a ball is better. But they did not learn to be friends. They did not like each other. They did not play together again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a huge elephant. He liked to mark his territory every day. He would create a line to show where his space was and would not let any other elephants cross it. The other elephant could see the huge elephant was very serious and began to cry. The huge elephant felt sorry for him and asked him why he wanted to cross the line. The other elephant replied, "I have nothing to eat, my herd has moved and left me behind, I need to find something to eat".

The huge elephant felt bad for the other and said, "You can mark a line too and make this space your own. Together we can create something big". So the two elephants worked together and even though the huge elephant's line was much bigger, the other elephant's line was right next to it, marking the same space.

The two elephants shared the space and food and became good friends. The moral of this story is that working together is always better than going it alone.

After that, Grace was very excited. She had shown that she was smart and strong through exercise. She kept doing her daily exercise and continued to serve her parents whenever she could. From then on, Grace was always happy and healthy. The end.

Ben and Mia were excited to go to the park with Mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They also liked to see the ducks and the squirrels.

When they got to the park, they saw a big sign that said "Free Vaccines". Mom said they had to get a shot to stay healthy and not get sick. Ben and Mia did not like shots. They were scared of the needle.

Mom took them to a tent where a nice lady was giving shots. She smiled and said, "Hello, I'm Nurse Anna. I'm going to give you a little pinch and then you'll get a sticker and a lollipop. It will be over very fast."

Ben went first. He closed his eyes and held Mom's hand. He felt the needle in his arm and shouted, "Ow!" But it was not very bad. Nurse Anna gave him a sticker of a dinosaur and a lollipop. He said, "Thank you."

Mia saw that Ben was okay. She was brave and went next. She also closed her eyes and held Mom's hand. She felt the needle in her arm and shouted, "Ow!" But it was not very bad. Nurse Anna gave her a sticker of a unicorn and a lollipop. She said, "Thank you."

Mom hugged them and said, "You did great, Ben and Mia. I'm so proud of you. Now let's go have some fun at the park." Ben and Mia smiled and ran to the swings. They were happy and healthy.

Once upon a time, there was a big clock in a small room. The clock was mysterious. It had a face and two hands. Every day, the clock went "tick-tock, tick-tock."

One day, a little girl named Lucy came into the room. She looked at the clock and said, "Hello, clock! Why are you so mysterious?" The clock did not answer. It just went "tick-tock, tick-tock." Lucy felt a tickle in her nose. She tried to hold it in, but she could not. "Achoo!" she sneezed.

The sneeze was so big, it made the clock's hands move. The clock said, "Thank you, Lucy! Your sneeze helped me. I was stuck, but now I can move again." Lucy smiled and said, "You're welcome, clock!" From that day on, the mysterious clock and Lucy were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to run and play with her friends. One day, Lily entered a race at her school. She ran as fast as she could and won a huge trophy! Lily was so happy that she smiled from ear to ear. She showed her trophy to everyone she met and they all smiled too. From that day on, Lily felt proud of herself and kept her trophy on her shelf to remind her of her big win.

Once upon a time there was a family who went on a march. The family had two kids, Johnny and Sally. They were very excited to go on the march!

The kids had to walk for a very long time. It was a lot of work and they were getting very tired. Johnny was being very competitive and tried to march faster than his sister. But Sally kept up with him.

When they were almost finished, the kids heard their names being called from the distance. They looked up and saw their mom and dad waving at them! Everyone cheered when the family finished the march.

The kids had a lot of fun on the march and they learned how to be competitive. They will always remember the march!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived in a small village. She loved to play with her toys and her friends, but one day she did something wrong. She took a cookie from the jar without asking her mom first.

When her mom found out, she said, "Lily, you broke the law. Taking things without asking is wrong. You need to be punished."

Lily felt very lonely and sad because she knew she did something bad. She said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I won't do it again."

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. Just remember to always ask before taking things. That's the law."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a toy car, a toy plane and a toy train. But, Timmy had a bad habit of tearing his toys apart when he got angry.

One day, Timmy's mom bought him a new toy. It was a wooden puzzle with attractive colors. Timmy loved it so much that he promised to take care of it. However, one day, Timmy got upset and he started to tear the puzzle apart. He was so sad when he realized what he had done.

His mom saw what happened and she sat down with Timmy to talk about it. She explained that it's important to be kind to our things and not to tear them apart. She also said that we should treat others' things with respect too. From that day on, Timmy learned to take care of his toys and not to tear them apart.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a cat and a dog. They liked to play all day. One day, they saw a shiny chain on the floor. They both wanted it.

The cat had an idea. She rubbed her head on the dog's leg. The dog felt happy and closed his eyes. The cat took the chain and ran away. The dog felt sad and guilty.

Later, the cat felt bad. She went back to the dog and gave him the chain. They both played with the chain and were happy friends again.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted dog named Spot. Spot could do many fun tricks. He could show people how he could jump very high and run very fast. Spot had many friends who liked to watch him play.

One day, Spot met a new friend named Tim. Tim asked, "Can you show me your fun tricks?" Spot said, "Yes, I can!" So, Spot showed Tim how he could jump high and run fast. Tim was very happy to see Spot's tricks.

But then, Spot saw a big car coming fast. Spot wanted to show Tim how brave he was. So, Spot ran towards the car to show he was not scared. But the car hit Spot, and he got hurt. Tim was sad, and everyone missed the gifted dog who had so much fun to share.

One day two young children were marching down the street. One was the older brother and the other was the younger sister. They were walking down the street in a row, when the younger sister said to her brother, "I'm tired, can we have a break?"

The older brother replied, "No, we can't. We need to keep marching. Once we reach the finish line, we can rest."

The younger sister started to cry, but the older brother kept marching. After a while, they reached the finish line and were so proud of themselves.

The older brother said to the younger sister, "You see, with hard work and determination, we can reach our goals."

The sister smiled, happy to have her brother by her side.

The moral of the story is that you can do anything you set your mind to, as long as you work hard and never give up.

Once there was a chubby little bunny. He heard about a cool pass in a far away town. He hopped and hopped until he reached the pass. He was so excited to be there.

When he arrived at the pass, the bunny noticed something in the distance. The sun was beginning to rise above the horizon. He hopped another step forward and the sun shone brighter and brighter. He had never seen a sunrise before and it was beautiful!

The bunny stayed at the pass until the sun had risen completely. He felt so happy and content that he hopped and bounced joyfully back home. As he hopped, he looked forward to the sunset he would see that day.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Ann. She was very shy and always kept to herself. One day, she found a beautiful, sparkly jewel in the garden. The jewel was so shiny and pretty that it made her heart beat fast.

Ann picked up the jewel and went home. She was too shy to show it to her mom, so she just put it away.
