Once upon a time, there was a little tree. It was very young, but it liked to grow. So every day, it would try to get bigger.

One day, though, something bad happened. A mean, ignorant person chopped the little tree into a bunch of pieces. The little tree was so sad and angry!

But then something wonderful happened. The pieces of the little tree started to grow! Even though it was chopped into pieces, it was still able to grow.

Eventually, the pieces grew into a big and beautiful tree. The tree was even bigger than it used to be!

At the end, the little tree taught everyone an important lesson: you should never give up, no matter how ignorant someone is.

Once upon a time there were two bears, one small and one big. The little bear asked the big bear, "Can I stay with you?" The big bear replied, "Yes, come with me and we'll have some fun!" So the little bear followed the big bear.

They roamed around the forest, looking for food and playing games together. The big bear showed the little bear where to find the best berries and how to look for wild mushrooms. On the way, the little bear felt a bit scared about the thick forest.

The big bear sensed that the little bear was afraid and said, "My friend, stay close to me so that you won't be scared. Together, we can make our way through this thick forest."

The little bear thanked the big bear and stayed close to him. Together they made it back home to their den in the forest.

Moral of the story: It's often easier to do something when you have a friend by your side!

Once there was a tidy girl named Amy. She had never had a hair cut. One day, her family decided to take her to a barber for the first time.

When she got to the barberâ€™s, she felt scared and started to weep. She did not want her hair cut. But her family was very kind and talked to her gently. They explained that the barber was nice and he was only going to make her hair look nice.

Finally, Amy calmed down and let the barber cut her hair. He was very gentle and finished quickly. When Amy looked in the mirror she was very happy. Her hair looked so tidy and pretty.

From that day on, Amy was never scared to go to the barber.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to travel with his mom. He was very excited. He took his toy car, his teddy bear, and his thermometer. Tim was a persistent little boy.

On their way, Tim saw a big dog. Tim said to his mom, "Look, a big dog!" The dog looked at them and wagged its tail. Tim's mom said, "Yes, it's a big and friendly dog."

Tim and his mom walked and walked. Tim looked at his thermometer. It was hot. He said, "Mom, it's hot. Can we rest?" His mom said, "Sure, let's rest under that tree."

They sat under the tree and had a snack. Tim was happy he could travel with his mom. He knew being persistent helped him have a fun day.

Anna and Ben were at the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They saw many other kids and some dogs too. They waved to their friends and said hello.

"Mom, can we have ice-cream?" Anna asked. She loved ice-cream, especially chocolate and vanilla. Ben nodded. He liked ice-cream too, but he preferred strawberry and banana.

"Sure, sweeties. Let's go to the ice-cream truck," mom said. She took their hands and walked with them to the truck. There were many flavors and colors of ice-cream. Anna and Ben chose their favorites and mom paid the man.

"Thank you, mom!" Anna and Ben said. They licked their ice-creams and smiled. They were very yummy and cold.

As they were eating their ice-creams, they saw a little girl with a big hat and a pink dress. She was holding a balloon and a teddy bear. She looked very adorable. She waved to Anna and Ben and came closer.

"Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play with me?" she asked. She had a friendly voice and a cute smile.

"Hi, I'm Anna and this is Ben. We would love to play with you," Anna said. She liked Lily's hat and balloon. Ben liked her teddy bear.

"Great! Let's go to the sandbox. I have some toys there," Lily said. She led them to the sandbox and they started to make sandcastles, bridges and tunnels. They had a lot of fun and shared their toys and ice-creams.

Anna, Ben and Lily became good friends. They played until it was time to go home. They hugged and waved goodbye. They promised to see each other again soon. They were very happy.

Once there was a successful dove. That dove was so very happy! One day the dove wanted to celebrate. So the dove flapped its wings and flew around in the air. It was so much fun! Then more doves came from far away and joined the celebration. They flew around and around together in the sky. Everyone was so happy and it felt like a magical time! Everyone was celebrating and being successful!

When the celebration was over the doves said goodbye to each other and flew away. But the first dove stayed and remembered the special day it had celebrated.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Meg. She was very small, but she had a big dream. She wanted to be on the stage!

Meg asked her mom if she could try it. Her mom said yes, so they went to a special place with lots of colorful lights. It was very exciting!

At the special place, Meg asked to be on the stage. Everyone smiled at her and said yes. They gave her pretty clothes to wear and put make-up on her face. She felt very attractive!

Meg went on the stage and sang and danced. Everyone clapped and cheered for her. Meg loved it so much. She had made her request come true!

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Tim. Tim loved playing with his colorful blocks. He would build tall towers and knock them down with a big smile on his face. One day, Tim felt his tummy rumble and he knew it was time for a snack. He ran to the kitchen and asked his mom for a cheerful sandwich. As he took a bite, he felt the ground tremble. Tim looked outside the window and saw a big truck driving by. The blocks on his table started to shake and Tim giggled with excitement.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jack. Jack was three years old. He wanted to go out and have some fun.

Every day, Jack's parents would take him to the playground. It was a great place to play. Jack loved ringing the bell and playing with the swings and slides.

One day, Jack heard a strange noise. It sounded like a bell ringing. He looked around and saw a big, red telephone box. Inside was a telephone and it was ringing.

Jack went to his dad and asked, "What is that?"

His dad said, "It's a telephone. Come and rub the buttons. It makes a great sound!"

So, Jack went to the telephone and rubbed the buttons. He was so excited to hear it ring and he kept rubbing the buttons.

The little boy was so happy and he smiled from ear to ear. He said, "This is great!"

Once upon a time, two friends were playing together. They were having lots of fun together.

The friends decided to share a pizza. They shared the pizza equally and it was tasty!

Suddenly, they had an idea. They would go on an adventure! They ran out of the door and started looking for a beautiful exit.

Finally, the friends found the most beautiful exit. They were so excited. They ran to the exit and laughed together.

The friends had a day they will never forget. They had shared an adventure and a pizza. They were so happy!

Once, there was a girl who liked to perform. She could do many tricks and was very fast. She wanted to learn a new trick.

One day, she saw a square on the ground and decided to use it to perform. She tried it over and over, making it fast every time.

Finally, she did it! She had mastered the square. Everyone cheered and clapped for her. The girl felt very proud of herself.

She continued to perform her trick over and over. She got faster and faster each time. Soon, the girl was an expert at performing the square.

The girl was very happy that she had learnt a new trick. She smiled with joy and felt excited to show everyone her new skill.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She loved to play hide and seek with her family. One day, Lucy decided she would be the one to hide. She hid behind an old photo frame in the lounge. Her family went looking for her. They searched for a long time but soon gave up and decided to sit down on the sofa. But Lucy had been very so still, so they hadn't seen her hiding behind the frame.

Suddenly Lucy piped up, "Boo!" Her family jumped up in surprise. They all laughed, and then Lucy said, "I was hiding very fast!" Everyone smiled, and they decided to play one more round. This time, it would be Lucy who was looking for the others. She ran around the house, peeking under tables and behind the curtains. At last, she found everyone hiding behind the photo frame. She'd done it! Lucy shouted "I found you!" Everyone cheered and then they decided to keep playing the game.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures for her family and friends. One day, Lily made a special card for her mom. It had hearts and flowers on it, and said "I love you" in big letters.

When Lily gave the card to her mom, she was very polite and said "thank you, sweetie". Lily felt happy because her mom liked the card. She loved making her mom happy.

From that day on, Lily made cards for everyone she loved. She would draw pictures and write nice words on them. And everyone was always polite and said thank you. Lily was happy because she loved making people feel happy with her cards.

Once upon a time, there was a pig. He loved to explore. One day, he went on an adventure. As he was walking, he found something interesting. He could not wait to see what it was! When he got closer, he was so excited to reveal the secret. It was a shiny golden coin. He was so happy, he shouted with joy and took the coin home. He was sure it was a big treasure and he would be able to keep it forever. The pig was so proud of his special coin and never forgot that day.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to eat carrots. He would eat carrots all day long! But Benny had a problem. He was very lazy. He didn't like to do anything except eat carrots.

One day, Benny was eating a carrot when his friend, a squirrel named Sammy, came to visit. "Hi, Benny! What are you doing?" asked Sammy. "Eating a carrot," replied Benny. "Do you want to play?" asked Sammy. "No, I'm too lazy," said Benny.

Sammy was sad. "I hate when you're lazy," said Sammy. "You're my friend and I want to play with you." Benny felt bad. "I'm sorry, Sammy. I'll try to be less lazy," said Benny. From that day on, Benny tried to be more active and play with his friend. But he still loved to eat carrots!

Once upon a time, there was a friendly cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to explore and go on adventures. One day, Mittens found a map that showed a big park with lots of trees and birds.

Mittens wanted to go to the park, so she asked her friend, a dog named Max, to come with her. Max was happy to join Mittens on her adventure.

As they walked to the park, Mittens and Max listened to the birds singing and the leaves rustling in the wind. When they finally arrived, they played together and had so much fun.

From then on, Mittens and Max went on many adventures together, always listening to the sounds around them and using their trusty map to guide them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her sunglasses and pretend she was a movie star. One sunny day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She brought her sunglasses with her, but forgot to bring a drink.

After playing for a while, Lily got very thirsty. She asked her friends if they had any drinks, but they didn't. Lily started to feel foolish for forgetting to bring a drink. She didn't know what to do.

Just then, a kind lady walked by and saw Lily looking sad. The lady asked if she needed a drink and gave her a bottle of water. Lily was so happy and grateful. She drank the water and put her sunglasses back on. She felt like a movie star again, but this time, she didn't feel foolish. She learned that it's okay to ask for help when you need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, while she was walking in the woods, she saw a witch. The witch was very scary and had a big, heavy bag.

Lily was scared and ran away. But then she remembered her mom telling her that running away from problems won't solve them. So, she decided to be brave and go back to the witch. She asked the witch what was in her heavy bag.

The witch told her it was all the bad things she had done and wanted to get rid of them. Lily thought for a moment and told the witch that the best way to get rid of bad things was to do good things instead. The witch listened to Lily's advice and felt better.

From that day on, the witch started doing good things and became a kind and friendly witch. Lily learned that being brave and helping others can solve problems and make the world a better place.

Once upon a time, in a hidden land, there lived a little girl named Lily. She loved to skip and play in the mist by the river. One day, while she was skipping, she met a tiny frog.

"Hi, little frog!" said Lily. "Do you want to skip with me?"

The frog looked at Lily and said, "Yes, but first, can you help me find my family? They are hidden in the mist."

Together, Lily and the frog skipped through the mist, looking for the frog's family. As they searched, they talked and became good friends. Finally, they found the frog's family, and they all played and skipped together.

From that day on, Lily and the frog were the best of friends. They learned that helping others can bring happiness and new friends. And they always remembered to be kind and helpful to everyone they met.

Lila and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. It looks like a palace. They want to go on the slide.

They run to the slide. They wait for their turn. Lila goes first. She climbs up the steps. She sits on the slide. She slides down fast. She laughs. She likes the slide.

Sam goes next. He climbs up the steps. He sits on the slide. He slides down fast. He shouts. He likes the slide too.

They go on the slide again and again. They have fun. They see a seesaw. They want to try the seesaw.

They run to the seesaw. They sit on each end. They push with their feet. They go up and down. They smile. They like the seesaw.

They try to balance on the seesaw. They want to make the seesaw stay still. They move their bodies. They try to be the same weight. They try hard. They balance on the seesaw. They clap. They are happy.

They hear a loud noise. They look around. They see a big truck. It is coming to the park. It has a sign. It says "New Toys". They wonder what toys are in the truck. They are curious.

They get off the seesaw. They run to the truck. They want to see the new toys. They hope they are fun. They hope they can play with them. They are excited.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle. It was called a palace. The palace was very pretty and had many rooms. The king and queen lived in the palace. They had a pet dog who was very obedient.

One day, the king and queen decided to have a big party in the palace. They invited many people to come and celebrate. The dog was very excited because he loved when people came to visit. He wagged his tail and barked happily.

The party was a lot of fun. There was music and dancing and lots of yummy food. The dog ran around the palace, making new friends and playing games. He was so happy and excited that he couldn't stop wagging his tail. Everyone had a great time at the palace party.

Once upon a time there was a guard. He was very nervous because he had to stay awake all night. He was watching over something special. He was very careful and he watched all night.

When morning came the guard was very tired. He had been so busy watching that he hadn't slept at all. He needed to sleep. So he found a nice, comfortable spot and dozed off.

But soon the guard was being watched. A sneaky fox had seen the guard asleep and was getting closer and closer. The fox was looking for something special that the guard was protecting.

The guard woke up and was very scared. He was no longer nervous, he was very scared. He saw the fox and he jumped up. He made lots of noise and waved his arms. The fox was so scared that it ran away!

The guard was very happy. He was sure he had saved something special. He knew that he had to stay awake so he stayed on guard for the rest of the night. From then on he was never so nervous and he made sure he slept enough.

Once there was a skin. It was the color of the sun, shiny and bright. But it was hard - so difficult that it hurt if someone touched it.

The skin lay all alone, until one day a little bug came and made a home. The bug loved the skin, and rested their tired legs. But the skin was sad. It wished for someone else to lie with it.

One day, a spider came and saw the skin lying all alone. The spider asked the skin if it could lie with it. The skin was too scared to say yes, so it stayed quiet.

But the spider was brave and went ahead and lay down next to the skin. Together they rested in the sun, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jim. Jim was very careful and never wanted to get into too much trouble. One day he decided to go exploring in the woods near his house. He had heard that there might be a secret hidden in the woods and he wanted to find it!

So Jim set off into the woods in search of the secret. He followed a winding path through the woods, being very careful as he went. Eventually, he came to a clearing! In the middle was a little house. Jim was very excited! He thought that the secret might be inside!

Jim went up to the door and knocked three times. Nothing happened. Then he tried calling out "Is anyone home?". Suddenly he heard a voice from the inside saying "Who is it?". Jim said his name and the door opened. An old man stood there. He said "Come inside, Jim. I have a special secret for you."

Jim followed the man inside. He was shown a special box which contained a secret treasure. The man said "This is your secret. I want you to take good care of it." Jim was delighted! He thanked the man for the secret and carefully took the box home with him. He now had a special secret of his own!

Once there was a baby fox running in the forest. He was so happy; running left and right, zigzagging through the trees. Suddenly, he saw a big bear! The baby fox froze and stopped moving. The bear yawned and looked very sleepy.

The baby fox was scared, but the bear didn't move at all. After a few minutes, the baby fox slowly started to walk to the side. But then he stopped again, because the bear was still there.

The baby fox wanted to get past the bear, so he had an idea. He started to run around the bear, zigzagging in a big circle. The bear was so sleepy it didn't even notice! The baby fox was so happy that he ran even faster, until he disappeared into the trees.

Once upon a time, there was a small walk. It was so small it could only fit one person. Every day, someone would come and take the walk, enjoying the warm sunshine and fresh air.

One day, the person who came was feeling a little lonely, so they decided to surrender to the walk and make it a bit longer. As the person wandered along, something small appeared ahead. When the person got closer, they realized it was a tiny puppy.

The person was so happy and excited to see the new friend, but the puppy was scared and ran away. The person followed and followed, but the puppy ran faster and soon disappeared from sight.

The person felt a bit sad from losing the puppy, but also happy that the puppy was able to surrender to the freedom of running in the woods. And so, the person decided to use the same power of surrender and have a peaceful, longer walk.

And so the person continued with their special walk, never forgetting the small puppy they had seen.

Once upon a time there was a brave warrior who lived far away in the forest.

One day the warrior sailed away to explore the world on a small boat. They sailed around for hours and hours, eventually coming to a new land.

The warrior was curious so they jumped off the boat and started to explore. But it was uncomfortable, so the warrior decided to go back to the boat.

In their hurry to get back, the warrior called out, â€œQuick! Quick!â€. It was then that a friendly bird flew over. The warrior smiled and asked the bird, â€œDo you know a faster way to sail?â€

The bird replied, â€œOf course! Follow me, I'll show you!â€ The warrior quickly hopped on the boat and followed the bird.

The bird showed the warrior how to make the boat sail faster and soon the warrior was on their way. The breeze was gentle and the warrior felt comfortable once again.

The warrior thanked the bird for showing them the way and sailed away, never to forget the bird's kindness.

John had been very disobedient. He had not listened to anything his parents had said. So his parents decided they had to punish him.

John was very sad. He thought he would never have any fun again. But his parents had a different plan.

They took John out for the day. They did not have to spend much money, because they did lots of cheap things. They had a picnic in the park and went for a long walk.

John's parents wanted him to understand that punishment does not have to mean no fun at all. In fact, it can just be a reminder to do the right thing next time. John was glad, and he did not disobey again.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful little girl named Sue. She always wanted to help her mommy and daddy. One day, she saw her daddy trying to fix the door. The door was old and needed some help.

Sue wanted to show her daddy that she knew how to fix the door too. She picked up her toy hammer and started to tap on the door gently. Her daddy smiled and said, "Thank you, Sue, for being so thoughtful."

Together, Sue and her daddy fixed the door. They were both very happy. From that day on, Sue knew she could help her family with anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, especially near the river. One day, Lily's mom asked her a question. "What did you have for lunch?" her mom asked. Lily thought for a moment and then answered, "I had a peanut butter sandwich."

Later that day, Lily was playing by the river when she accidentally dropped her favorite toy in the water. She felt so ashamed that she had been careless. But then, her dad came to the rescue and fished the toy out of the river for her. Lily was so happy and grateful that she hugged her dad tightly.

From that day on, Lily made sure to be extra careful near the river. And whenever her parents asked her a question, she always made sure to answer truthfully.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved playing soccer and would always kick the ball around in his backyard. One day, Timmy's dad took him to a big stadium to watch a soccer game. Timmy was so excited to see all the players and hear the crowd cheering.

As they were walking to their seats, Timmy's dad said, "Be careful not to run too fast or you might trip and fall." Timmy listened and walked slowly to his seat.

During the game, Timmy saw one player who was very good. He scored many goals and the crowd cheered loudly for him. Timmy thought, "I want to be like him when I grow up."

After the game, as they were leaving the stadium, Timmy's dad said, "Remember, it's important to be humble even if you're really good at something." Timmy nodded and said, "I will remember." He also remembered to stop and look both ways before crossing the street.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion in the jungle. He liked to roar very loudly so that all the animals could hear him. One day, a little girl came to the jungle. She had a pretty bracelet on her wrist. The lion saw the bracelet and thought it was very nice. He asked the little girl if he could wear it. She said yes and put the bracelet on the lion's paw. The lion was very happy and felt mild and calm wearing the bracelet. From that day on, the lion would wear the bracelet every time he wanted to feel mild and calm.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was only three years old, but she liked to write. Every day, the little girl would get out her crayons and paper and write stories. One day, the little girl's mommy said, "Would you like some yogurt?"

The little girl was so excited. She said, "Yes! I love yogurt!" Her mommy gave her a spoon, some yogurt and a piece of paper. The little girl started eating the yogurt and writing on the paper.

Suddenly, her mommy said, "What are you writing?" The little girl said, "A story about a little girl with a spoon, eating yogurt."

"That is so cute!" said her mommy, smiling. The little girl finished her yogurt and happily went back to writing her story.

SNOWDROP

It was the middle of winter, when the broad flakes of snow were falling

around, that the queen of a country many thousand miles off sat working

at her window. The frame of the window was made of fine black ebony, and

as she sat looking out upon the snow, she pricked her finger, and three

drops of blood fell upon it. Then she gazed thoughtfully upon the red

drops that sprinkled the white snow, and said, 'Would that my little

daughter may be as white as that snow, as red as that blood, and as

black as this ebony windowframe!' And so the little girl really did grow

up; her skin was as white as snow, her cheeks as rosy as the blood, and

her hair as black as ebony; and she was called Snowdrop.

But this queen died; and the king soon married another wife, who became

queen, and was very beautiful, but so vain that she could not bear

to think that anyone could be handsomer than she was. She had a fairy

looking-glass, to which she used to go, and then she would gaze upon

herself in it, and say:

'Tell me, glass, tell me true!

Of all the ladies in the land,

Who is fairest, tell me, who?'

And the glass had always answered:

'Thou, queen, art the fairest in all the land.'

But Snowdrop grew more and more beautiful; and when she was seven years

old she was as bright as the day, and fairer than the queen herself.

Then the glass one day answered the queen, when she went to look in it

as usual:

'Thou, queen, art fair, and beauteous to see,

But Snowdrop is lovelier far than thee!'

When she heard this she turned pale with rage and envy, and called to

one of her servants, and said, 'Take Snowdrop away into the wide wood,

that I may never see her any more.' Then the servant led her away; but

his heart melted when Snowdrop begged him to spare her life, and he

said, 'I will not hurt you, thou pretty child.' So he left her by

herself; and though he thought it most likely that the wild beasts would

tear her in pieces, he felt as if a great weight were taken off his

heart when he had made up his mind not to kill her but to leave her to

her fate, with the chance of someone finding and saving her.

Then poor Snowdrop wandered along through the wood in great fear; and

the wild beasts roared about her, but none did her any harm. In the

evening she came to a cottage among the hills, and went in to rest, for

her little feet would carry her no further. Everything was spruce and

neat in the cottage: on the table was spread a white cloth, and there

were seven little plates, seven little loaves, and seven little glasses

with wine in them; and seven knives and forks laid in order; and by

the wall stood seven little beds. As she was very hungry, she picked

a little piece of each loaf and drank a very little wine out of each

glass; and after that she thought she would lie down and rest. So she

tried all the little beds; but one was too long, and another was too

short, till at last the seventh suited her: and there she laid herself

down and went to sleep.

By and by in came the masters of the cottage. Now they were seven little

dwarfs, that lived among the mountains, and dug and searched for gold.

They lighted up their seven lamps, and saw at once that all was not

right. The first said, 'Who has been sitting on my stool?' The second,

'Who has been eating off my plate?' The third, 'Who has been picking my

bread?' The fourth, 'Who has been meddling with my spoon?' The fifth,

'Who has been handling my fork?' The sixth, 'Who has been cutting with

my knife?' The seventh, 'Who has been drinking my wine?' Then the first

looked round and said, 'Who has been lying on my bed?' And the rest came

running to him, and everyone cried out that somebody had been upon his

bed. But the seventh saw Snowdrop, and called all his brethren to come

and see her; and they cried out with wonder and astonishment and brought

their lamps to look at her, and said, 'Good heavens! what a lovely child

she is!' And they were very glad to see her, and took care not to wake

her; and the seventh dwarf slept an hour with each of the other dwarfs

in turn, till the night was gone.

In the morning Snowdrop told them all her story; and they pitied her,

and said if she would keep all things in order, and cook and wash and

knit and spin for them, she might stay where she was, and they would

take good care of her. Then they went out all day long to their work,

seeking for gold and silver in the mountains: but Snowdrop was left at

home; and they warned her, and said, 'The queen will soon find out where

you are, so take care and let no one in.'

But the queen, now that she thought Snowdrop was dead, believed that she

must be the handsomest lady in the land; and she went to her glass and

said:

'Tell me, glass, tell me true!

Of all the ladies in the land,

Who is fairest, tell me, who?'

And the glass answered:

'Thou, queen, art the fairest in all this land:

But over the hills, in the greenwood shade,

Where the seven dwarfs their dwelling have made,

There Snowdrop is hiding her head; and she

Is lovelier far, O queen! than thee.'

Then the queen was very much frightened; for she knew that the glass

always spoke the truth, and was sure that the servant had betrayed her.

And she could not bear to think that anyone lived who was more beautiful

than she was; so she dressed herself up as an old pedlar, and went

her way over the hills, to the place where the dwarfs dwelt. Then she

knocked at the door, and cried, 'Fine wares to sell!' Snowdrop looked

out at the window, and said, 'Good day, good woman! what have you to

sell?' 'Good wares, fine wares,' said she; 'laces and bobbins of all

colours.' 'I will let the old lady in; she seems to be a very good

sort of body,' thought Snowdrop, as she ran down and unbolted the door.

'Bless me!' said the old woman, 'how badly your stays are laced! Let me

lace them up with one of my nice new laces.' Snowdrop did not dream of

any mischief; so she stood before the old woman; but she set to work

so nimbly, and pulled the lace so tight, that Snowdrop's breath was

stopped, and she fell down as if she were dead. 'There's an end to all

thy beauty,' said the spiteful queen, and went away home.

In the evening the seven dwarfs came home; and I need not say how

grieved they were to see their faithful Snowdrop stretched out upon the

ground, as if she was quite dead. However, they lifted her up, and when

they found what ailed her, they cut the lace; and in a little time she

began to breathe, and very soon came to life again. Then they said, 'The

old woman was the queen herself; take care another time, and let no one

in when we are away.'

When the queen got home, she went straight to her glass, and spoke to it

as before; but to her great grief it still said:

'Thou, queen, art the fairest in all this land:

But over the hills, in the greenwood shade,

Where the seven dwarfs their dwelling have made,

There Snowdrop is hiding her head; and she

Is lovelier far, O queen! than thee.'

Then the blood ran cold in her heart with spite and malice, to see that

Snowdrop still lived; and she dressed herself up again, but in quite

another dress from the one she wore before, and took with her a poisoned

comb. When she reached the dwarfs' cottage, she knocked at the door, and

cried, 'Fine wares to sell!' But Snowdrop said, 'I dare not let anyone

in.' Then the queen said, 'Only look at my beautiful combs!' and gave

her the poisoned one. And it looked so pretty, that she took it up and

put it into her hair to try it; but the moment it touched her head,

the poison was so powerful that she fell down senseless. 'There you may

lie,' said the queen, and went her way. But by good luck the dwarfs

came in very early that evening; and when they saw Snowdrop lying on

the ground, they thought what had happened, and soon found the poisoned

comb. And when they took it away she got well, and told them all that

had passed; and they warned her once more not to open the door to

anyone.

Meantime the queen went home to her glass, and shook with rage when she

read the very same answer as before; and she said, 'Snowdrop shall die,

if it cost me my life.' So she went by herself into her chamber, and got

ready a poisoned apple: the outside looked very rosy and tempting, but

whoever tasted it was sure to die. Then she dressed herself up as a

peasant's wife, and travelled over the hills to the dwarfs' cottage,

and knocked at the door; but Snowdrop put her head out of the window and

said, 'I dare not let anyone in, for the dwarfs have told me not.' 'Do

as you please,' said the old woman, 'but at any rate take this pretty

apple; I will give it you.' 'No,' said Snowdrop, 'I dare not take it.'

'You silly girl!' answered the other, 'what are you afraid of? Do you

think it is poisoned? Come! do you eat one part, and I will eat the

other.' Now the apple was so made up that one side was good, though the

other side was poisoned. Then Snowdrop was much tempted to taste, for

the apple looked so very nice; and when she saw the old woman eat, she

could wait no longer. But she had scarcely put the piece into her mouth,

when she fell down dead upon the ground. 'This time nothing will save

thee,' said the queen; and she went home to her glass, and at last it

said:

'Thou, queen, art the fairest of all the fair.'

And then her wicked heart was glad, and as happy as such a heart could

be.

When evening came, and the dwarfs had gone home, they found Snowdrop

lying on the ground: no breath came from her lips, and they were afraid

that she was quite dead. They lifted her up, and combed her hair, and

washed her face with wine and water; but all was in vain, for the little

girl seemed quite dead. So they laid her down upon a bier, and all seven

watched and bewailed her three whole days; and then they thought they

would bury her: but her cheeks were still rosy; and her face looked just

as it did while she was alive; so they said, 'We will never bury her in

the cold ground.' And they made a coffin of glass, so that they might

still look at her, and wrote upon it in golden letters what her name

was, and that she was a king's daughter. And the coffin was set among

the hills, and one of the dwarfs always sat by it and watched. And the

birds of the air came too, and bemoaned Snowdrop; and first of all came

an owl, and then a raven, and at last a dove, and sat by her side.

And thus Snowdrop lay for a long, long time, and still only looked as

though she was asleep; for she was even now as white as snow, and as red

as blood, and as black as ebony. At last a prince came and called at the

dwarfs' house; and he saw Snowdrop, and read what was written in golden

letters. Then he offered the dwarfs money, and prayed and besought them

to let him take her away; but they said, 'We will not part with her for

all the gold in the world.' At last, however, they had pity on him, and

gave him the coffin; but the moment he lifted it up to carry it home

with him, the piece of apple fell from between her lips, and Snowdrop

awoke, and said, 'Where am I?' And the prince said, 'Thou art quite safe

with me.'

Then he told her all that had happened, and said, 'I love you far better

than all the world; so come with me to my father's palace, and you shall

be my wife.' And Snowdrop consented, and went home with the prince;

and everything was got ready with great pomp and splendour for their

wedding.

To the feast was asked, among the rest, Snowdrop's old enemy the queen;

and as she was dressing herself in fine rich clothes, she looked in the

glass and said:

'Tell me, glass, tell me true!

Of all the ladies in the land,

Who is fairest, tell me, who?'

And the glass answered:

'Thou, lady, art loveliest here, I ween;

But lovelier far is the new-made queen.'

When she heard this she started with rage; but her envy and curiosity

were so great, that she could not help setting out to see the bride. And

when she got there, and saw that it was no other than Snowdrop, who, as

she thought, had been dead a long while, she choked with rage, and fell

down and died: but Snowdrop and the prince lived and reigned happily

over that land many, many years; and sometimes they went up into the

mountains, and paid a visit to the little dwarfs, who had been so kind

to Snowdrop in her time of need.

Once upon a time there was a cherry tree in a big field. One day, the tree was busy loading lots of big and juicy cherries. It was a mysterious sight to see! Everyone in the village wanted to get a cherry, but they were too high up the tree.

The village men thought of a plan. They brought a ladder and tried to climb up the tree to get the cherries. But the ladder was too small and it didn't reach the cherries.

Then a clever girl had an idea. She told the village men to get a long piece of string and tie it to the cherries. She then pulled the string until the cherries fell down from the tree. Everyone was so happy and the girl was very proud.

The village men loaded all the cherries into a big basket and took them back to the village. Everyone had a wonderful time enjoying the delicious cherries. It was such a mysterious and wonderful day!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old. One day, she was playing in the garden and she saw a big green stand. She didn't know what it was but it looked cool.

Anna went over to have a closer look, and when she got to the stand, something incredible happened. The stand started to move. Anna was so excited and it was so big and green.

Anna went to get her grandparents so they could see the stand too. They came outside and were all amazed. "What is it?" asked Anna's grandmother. Anna was about to find out.

The stand opened its eyes and said, "I'm an evil witch". Anna, her grandparents, and everyone around were so scared. The witch threatened them all and said, "If you don't do as I say, I'll put a spell on you".

So everyone in the garden had to listen to the witch's orders. Anna felt so scared, but she knew that there was nothing she could do. The witch was so powerful and green.

The witch caused so much trouble and the garden was not the same again. Anna never forgot the evil witch and the bad ending that she caused.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Mark. Mark was always looking for food to eat. One day, Mark heard about some hidden food. He wanted to find it so he started to look everywhere.

Mark sniffed the ground, but he still couldn't find anything. He looked inside the fridge, but no luck. Then, he dug in his garden and he was so happy when he found the hidden food. He quickly ate it all up!

Mark looked around his garden and smiled. He was so glad that he was able to find the hidden food. From then on, he always kept an eye out for more secret snacks.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Alice and Betty. Alice loved to play in the snow. She made snowballs and snowmen, but she loved ice best of all.

Betty was jealous of how much fun Alice was having. She said to Alice, "Let's stay and play in the snow all day." Alice smiled and said yes.

The two friends played together in the snow until it was too cold. But before they went home, Alice wanted to play with the ice. She took a big chunk of ice and started to throw it around.

Betty couldn't help but feel jealous. "Let me stay and play with you," she begged. But Alice just kept playing with the ice.

Finally, Betty couldn't take it any longer. "Please, Alice," she said. "Can I stay with you and play with the ice, too?"

Alice smiled and said yes. The two friends had a wonderful time playing with the ice together and soon the sun was setting. Betty had so much fun that she forgot all about her jealous feelings.

The two friends said goodbye and went home for the night. What a happy day!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Daisy. Daisy carried her little pet mole in her arms - it was so small and cute! Everyone thought the little mole was very attractive and admired it very much.

One day, Daisy was playing in the park when a boy named Andy saw the mole. "What's that?" he asked her. Daisy beamed and said, "It's my pet mole".

Andy asked if he could pet the mole, Daisy said yes and Andy gently stroked the mole's head. The mole felt happy and curled up in Daisy's arms and made little squeaky noises.

Andy smiled at Daisy, "Your mole is very attractive," he said. Daisy smiled back and said, "Thank you, Andy". Then, Daisy and Andy played together in the park until it was time to go home. Daisy carefully carried her mole all the way home.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but they have one favorite toy. It is a big gray elephant. The elephant is soft and has a long nose. The twins call him Elly.

One day, Anna and Ben want to play with Elly at the same time. They both grab his nose and pull. Elly makes a loud noise. He does not like it. Anna and Ben struggle. They do not want to share.

"Elly is mine!" Anna says.

"No, Elly is mine!" Ben says.

They pull harder. Elly makes a louder noise. He does not like it more.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the room. She sees Anna and Ben struggle. She sees Elly make noise. She is not happy.

"Anna and Ben, stop!" Mom says. "You are hurting Elly. He is not happy. You have to share. Elly is for both of you."

Anna and Ben look at Mom. They look at Elly. They see his sad eyes. They feel sorry.

"Sorry, Elly," Anna says.

"Sorry, Elly," Ben says.

They let go of his nose. They hug him. Elly makes a happy noise. He likes it.

Mom smiles. She hugs Anna and Ben. She hugs Elly.

"Good job, Anna and Ben," Mom says. "You are very kind. Elly is a famous elephant. He is famous for being soft and nice. He is famous for having two friends who love him."

Tommy was looking for something to play with. He liked to build things and he was very busy. He went over to the furniture and saw an empty glass there. He decided to make it into something special. He took some straws and some cupcake wrappers and made an airplane. He put the airplane on the counter and admired it with a big smile on his face.

Suddenly he heard a voice. "What are you doing?" asked the voice. Tommy turned around and saw another little boy who looked very curious. Tommy said, "I'm building an airplane!" The little boy seemed very interested and asked if he could help too.

Tommy happily said, "Sure!" and the two of them started to work together. They put together the airplane even faster and soon it was finished.

Tommy smiled and said, "Let's have a toast to celebrate our hard work." He then picked up the glass from the furniture and offered it to the other little boy. They both took turns to drink from it and then clicked the glass together. The little boys cheered and laughed.

Tommy was very happy. He had made something special with his new friend and was now feeling very content. He put the glass back on the furniture, said goodbye to his friend and went off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wander around her backyard and explore. One day, she saw a big, angry dog coming towards her. Lily was scared and her knee started to hurt.

Lily's mommy came outside and saw the dog. She quickly picked up Lily and took her inside. Lily's mommy called the dog's owner and they came to get the dog. From that day on, Lily was careful when she wandered around outside.

A few days later, Lily was playing with her toys when she heard a knock at the door. It was the dog's owner! They brought over a big bag of treats for Lily and apologized for their dog scaring her. Lily was happy and her knee felt better, and she learned that sometimes even angry things can have a happy ending.

Molly was a young girl who loved to write. One day she decided to write a story about a jellyfish. She grabbed a piece of paper and a gray crayon. She started writing about how the jellyfish sparkled in the sun. She drew pictures of it in the water with the gray crayon. Molly wanted to write more, so she added that the jellyfish had little tentacles that moved around. When she finished writing, Molly smiled because she had written a wonderful story about a jellyfish.

Simon was a small boy. He looked up at the sky. He admired the roof of the house. There was a tree in the yard. The leaves were all dead. They weren't moving like when the wind blew. Simon didn't understand why.

His dad came outside and said, "When the leaves fall from the tree, it means that it is getting colder outside." Simon looked confused. His dad said, "The leaves get stiff and die, like when you take a rest from running around."

Simon looked up at the roof of the house and then at the leaves on the ground. He wanted to admire the leaves and the roof, but he now knew that they were dead. Maybe someday the leaves would come back. Simon thought that was a wonderful thing to imagine.

Once upon a time there was a patient who tasted an enormous sweet. She was very excited and could not believe how delicious it was.

"Wow," she said. "This sweet tastes sooo good. I want more!"

Her three-year-old daughter heard her and laughed.

"Mommy, can I have some?" she asked.

The patient smiled and said, "Of course you can, sweetheart. Here, you can have half."

The daughter took the enormous sweet and tasted it. Her eyes grew wide and she said, "It tastes yummy!"

She hugged her mom tightly and said, "I love you and your enormous sweets!"

The patient smiled and said, "I love you too, my sweet girl."

Jimmy saw something scary in the woods and wanted to go back home. He started walking, but soon he heard someone call his name. It was his friend, Poppy. She had lots of treasures in her pocket and wanted to trade them with Jimmy. She had a shiny marble and a sparkly car, which looked very exciting.

Jimmy was scared, so he decided to trade. He looked inside his pocket and found some shiny stones, an old toy car, and a feather he found in the park. He handed them to Poppy and she gave him the treasure. They were both happy.

They said goodbye and Jimmy started walking home again, feeling excited with his new treasures. He couldn't wait to show his mom what he traded for.

Once upon a time there was a peanut. It was happy and round, like a ball. But something was wrong. The peanut was smelly. It could smell really bad, like something was wrong.

The peanut was sad, so it decided to go on a journey. It wanted to find out what was making it smell so bad.

The peanut rolled and rolled until it found a smelly river. Something was in the river and it was making it smell. The peanut rolled closer and closer and it saw a fish!

The fish was eating the peanut. It was eating the peanut up bit by bit until it finished. Then the fish swam away and the smelly river became clean again. The peanut was happy the smelly fish had gone.

And that was the end of the peanut's adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a big box in a room. A little boy named Tim saw the box and wanted to know what was inside. He tried to open it, but it was too hard for him. Tim felt sad and decided to wander around the house to find help.

He found his mom in the kitchen. She was very serious because she was making dinner. Tim asked his mom for help with the box. His mom said, "Wait until after dinner, then we can open the box together."

Tim didn't want to wait, so he wandered back to the room with the box. He tried to open it again, but still couldn't. He felt more sad and sat down next to the box. When dinner was ready, Tim went to eat with his family.

After dinner, Tim and his mom went to the room with the box. His mom helped him open it, and inside was a new toy! Tim was very happy and played with his new toy all night. The moral of the story is to be patient and ask for help when you need it.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, John and Jane. Every day they would play together in the warm sun.

One day, they were so excited because they were planning a big celebration. They gathered up their things and went to the woods to find an axe.

John and Jane searched for hours for an axe, but they could not find one. They were sad and did not know what to do.

Then one of the friends had an idea! They decided to build a fort out of sticks they found in the woods. Soon they had built a really big and strong fort!

The two friends were so happy! They celebrated by sitting inside their fort and eating treats. They were warm and happy, and they made a promise to play together forever.

Lily and Max were playing hide and seek in the big house. Lily was the seeker and Max was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then looked for Max. She checked the kitchen, the living room, and the bathroom, but she could not find him.

"Where are you, Max?" she called out. "I give up!"

She heard a giggle from behind a door. She ran to the door and opened it. It was the basement. She saw Max hiding behind a box. He had a playful smile on his face.

"Gotcha!" she said and ran towards him.

But then she saw something else in the basement. It was a big, black spider. It had eight legs and many eyes. It was crawling on the wall. Lily was very scared of spiders. She screamed and ran back to the door.

"Help! Help! Spider!" she cried.

Max heard her scream and saw the spider. He was not scared of spiders. He thought they were cool. He picked up a broom and tried to shoo the spider away.

"Don't worry, Lily, I'll save you!" he said.

But the spider was fast and angry. It jumped from the wall and landed on the broom. Max dropped the broom and backed away. He and Lily both trembled with fear. They wanted to get out of the basement.

"Where is the exit?" Lily asked.

Max looked around and saw a small window. It was high up, but he had an idea. He pushed the box he was hiding behind to the wall. He climbed on the box and reached for the window. He opened it and saw the garden outside.

"Come on, Lily, we can escape through here!" he said.

He helped Lily climb on the box and then through the window. They jumped down and ran to the house. They hugged each other and breathed a sigh of relief.

"That was scary!" Lily said.

"Yeah, but we made it!" Max said.

They decided to play something else. They did not want to go back to the basement. They hoped the spider would not follow them. They were glad they had each other. They were brave and playful friends.

Once upon a time there was a man with a big, bushy mustache. He was very friendly and always smiled a lot.

One day a little girl asked him why he had such a big mustache. The man smiled and replied, "It helps me stay healthy."

The little girl wasn't sure what the man meant, so she asked again. The man explained, "Eating lots of vegetables and keeping active helps me stay fit and healthy."

The little girl smiled and said, "That's so cool! I wish I had a mustache too."

The man replied with a hearty laugh, "No, a mustache isn't necessary for staying healthy. Eating your vegetables and playing outside are all you need."

The little girl smiled and nodded in agreement. She was very relieved because she wasn't sure if having a mustache was a requirement for having a healthy body.

Once upon a time there was a penny. The penny was shiny and was very special. It wanted to do something that would make it honest.

It decided to give to someone who needed it. It looked around and soon found a little girl. Her name was Joy and she was 3 years old. She had no money, so the penny thought she would be a good person to include.

The penny called to Joy, held out in its shiny hand, and said: "Hey Joy, do you want me? I'm honest and I want to help you."

Joy was so happy when she saw the penny! She smiled wide and said: "Oh penny, thank you so much! I will use you to buy candy and treats!"

The penny was so happy to hear that. She knew she did the right thing and now Joy had money to make her happy.

One day, there was a little boy who loved playing outside. He wanted to play in the sun all day long, but his mommy was worried. She wanted to keep him safe, so she warned him about the hot sun.

The boy always obeyed his mommy so he listened to her warning. Instead of playing in the sun, he played in the shade. The little boy was sad that he couldn't play in the sun, but he liked playing in the shade too.

One day, his mommy found a big, noisy fan. She turned it on and it made a lot of wind. Then, she warned her son again to stand away from the fan. The little boy was scared of the fan, but he did as he was told.

The boy's mommy was very worried, so she turned off the fan and hugged the boy. She told him that she only wanted to keep him safe. The little boy smiled, happy that his mommy cared so much about him. He was happy to be safe and warm in his mommy's hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved holidays because she got to play with her friends all day long. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy and daddy. She saw a big orange ball and wanted to play with it. She asked her mommy if she could have the ball, but her mommy said no.

Lily felt sad, but then she saw a boy playing with the same orange ball. She asked the boy if she could play with it too. The boy said yes and they played together for a while. When it was time to go home, Lily didn't want to leave the ball. She asked the boy if she could play with it again tomorrow. The boy said yes and Lily was very happy. She repeated the word "tomorrow" to herself over and over again on the way home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very happy and excited, but she was feeling dizzy. She decided to join a game, but she didn't know what to do.

The game was called 'Under'. The little girl looked under the chair and saw a big surprise - a toy! She was so happy that she couldn't stop smiling. She grabbed the toy and started playing.

The little girl had fun playing with her toy. She played until she got dizzy and felt like she was going to fall down.

So, the little girl stopped playing and lay down. She snuggled her toy and closed her eyes. After a while, she felt better. Then, she got up and joined the game again.

Once upon a time, there was a funny monkey named Max. Max loved to play and swing from tree to tree. One day, he saw a bird flying high in the sky. The bird was speaking a different language that Max didn't understand.

Max wanted to learn the bird's language so he could talk to him. He asked his friends for help, but they didn't know the language either.

hunt in the wood, that his daughter could spin gold out of straw. Now

this king was very fond of money; and when he heard the miller's boast

his greediness was raised, and he sent for the girl to be brought before

him. Then he led her to a chamber in his palace where there was a great

heap of straw, and gave her a spinning-wheel, and said, 'All this must

be spun into gold before morning, as you love your life.' It was in vain

that the poor maiden said that it was only a silly boast of her father,

for that she could do no such thing as spin straw into gold: the chamber

door was locked, and she was left alone.

She sat down in one corner of the room, and began to bewail her hard

fate; when on a sudden the door opened, and a droll-looking little man

hobbled in, and said, 'Good morrow to you, my good lass; what are you

weeping for?' 'Alas!' said she, 'I must spin this straw into gold, and

I know not how.' 'What will you give me,' said the hobgoblin, 'to do it

for you?' 'My necklace,' replied the maiden. He took her at her word,

and sat himself down to the wheel, and whistled and sang:

'Round about, round about,

Lo and behold!

Reel away, reel away,

Straw into gold!'

And round about the wheel went merrily; the work was quickly done, and

the straw was all spun into gold.

When the king came and saw this, he was greatly astonished and pleased;

but his heart grew still more greedy of gain, and he shut up the poor

miller's daughter again with a fresh task. Then she knew not what to do,

and sat down once more to weep; but the dwarf soon opened the door, and

said, 'What will you give me to do your task?' 'The ring on my finger,'

said she. So her little friend took the ring, and began to work at the

wheel again, and whistled and sang:

'Round about, round about,

Lo and behold!

Reel away, reel away,

Straw into gold!'

till, long before morning, all was done again.

The king was greatly delighted to see all this glittering treasure;

but still he had not enough: so he took the miller's daughter to a yet

larger heap, and said, 'All this must be spun tonight; and if it is,

you shall be my queen.' As soon as she was alone that dwarf came in, and

said, 'What will you give me to spin gold for you this third time?'

'I have nothing left,' said she. 'Then say you will give me,' said

the little man, 'the first little child that you may have when you are

queen.' 'That may never be,' thought the miller's daughter: and as she

knew no other way to get her task done, she said she would do what he

asked. Round went the wheel again to the old song, and the manikin once

more spun the heap into gold. The king came in the morning, and, finding

all he wanted, was forced to keep his word; so he married the miller's

daughter, and she really became queen.

At the birth of her first little child she was very glad, and forgot the

dwarf, and what she had said. But one day he came into her room, where

she was sitting playing with her baby, and put her in mind of it. Then

she grieved sorely at her misfortune, and said she would give him all

the wealth of the kingdom if he would let her off, but in vain; till at

last her tears softened him, and he said, 'I will give you three days'

grace, and if during that time you tell me my name, you shall keep your

child.'

Now the queen lay awake all night, thinking of all the odd names that

she had ever heard; and she sent messengers all over the land to find

out new ones. The next day the little man came, and she began with

TIMOTHY, ICHABOD, BENJAMIN, JEREMIAH, and all the names she could

remember; but to all and each of them he said, 'Madam, that is not my

name.'

The second day she began with all the comical names she could hear of,

BANDY-LEGS, HUNCHBACK, CROOK-SHANKS, and so on; but the little gentleman

still said to every one of them, 'Madam, that is not my name.'

The third day one of the messengers came back, and said, 'I have

travelled two days without hearing of any other names; but yesterday, as

I was climbing a high hill, among the trees of the forest where the fox

and the hare bid each other good night, I saw a little hut; and before

the hut burnt a fire; and round about the fire a funny little dwarf was

dancing upon one leg, and singing:

"Merrily the feast I'll make.

Today I'll brew, tomorrow bake;

Merrily I'll dance and sing,

For next day will a stranger bring.

Little does my lady dream

Rumpelstiltskin is my name!"

When the queen heard this she jumped for joy, and as soon as her little

friend came she sat down upon her throne, and called all her court round

to enjoy the fun; and the nurse stood by her side with the baby in her

arms, as if it was quite ready to be given up. Then the little man began

to chuckle at the thought of having the poor child, to take home with

him to his hut in the woods; and he cried out, 'Now, lady, what is my

name?' 'Is it JOHN?' asked she. 'No, madam!' 'Is it TOM?' 'No, madam!'

'Is it JEMMY?' 'It is not.' 'Can your name be RUMPELSTILTSKIN?' said the

lady slyly. 'Some witch told you that!--some witch told you that!' cried

the little man, and dashed his right foot in a rage so deep into the

floor, that he was forced to lay hold of it with both hands to pull it

out.

Then he made the best of his way off, while the nurse laughed and the

baby crowed; and all the court jeered at him for having had so much

trouble for nothing, and said, 'We wish you a very good morning, and a

merry feast, Mr RUMPLESTILTSKIN!'

Once upon a time there was a round dog named Trouble. He was always troubled and couldn't find a place to call home. Everywhere he went, people didn't want him around.

One day, Trouble was walking by the river and he saw a beautiful butterfly. He barked at it and it flew away. All of a sudden, Trouble heard someone shout out, "Hey, don't bite me!"

Trouble shouted back, "I didn't bite you!" He then noticed it was a small gator who was scared of Trouble.

The gator said, "I'm sorry I thought you were going to bite me." Trouble reassured him that he just wanted to be friends and he was now looking for a place to rest.

The small gator said, "You can stay here in my pond if you'd like. I know how it feels to be troubled and alone. I would make a good friend for you, Trouble."

Trouble was overjoyed and thanked the gator for his kind offer. They became the best of friends and lived happily ever after.

Once there was a little boy called Timmy. He was only three years old. He had a problem - he was weak.

One day, Timmy wanted to play with matches. He held one in his hand and shook it. But it didn't light up. He shook it harder, but nothing happened. Timmy was too weak to make it light up.

Then he had an idea. He asked his mum to help. She took the match and shook it hard. Suddenly, the match lit up!

Timmy was so happy and smiled. He thanked his mum for helping him. Now he could have lots of fun with the matches!

Once upon a time there was a boy. His name was Tom. He lived along with his mum. He had no dad, but he had a lot of friends.

One day, Tom saw something very big and scary. It was a big, black dog! The boy was scared, but he still tried to approach it. He said to the dog, "Hi, I'm Tom. Are you my friend?"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved lightning because she thought it was so pretty. Each time she saw it in the sky, she would stop and watch it for a while.

One day, she saw a beautiful lightning bug. She wanted to put it in her pocket but the bug was too fast for her. She tried to catch it, and she even put a tasty cookie as bait, but the bug was too clever!

Suddenly, her big brother came. He picked up the bug and put it in the pocket of his shirt. He said to his little sister, "Now I have it. You can't get it back!".

The little girl was so upset. She said to her brother, "Please put the bug back, it belongs in the sky with all the other lightning bugs. They need to be together".

The big brother smiled at his sister and said, "Ok, I will let it go. I will put it back outside". The little girl was very happy and she ran outside together with her brother to watch the little bug fly away with the lightning.

Once there was a little girl. She was only three years old and very adventurous. One day, the girl's mommy said, "Let's go to the park!"

The little girl was so excited. She jumped up, grabbed her mom and said, "Yippee! I'm ready!"

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong man with a big, strong mustache. He was very proud of his mustache and would comb it every day. One day, he went to the park to play with his friends. He was having so much fun that he didn't notice his mustache had fallen off. He looked and looked but he couldn't find it anywhere. He felt sad because he loved his mustache so much. But then his friends helped him look and they found it in the grass. He was so happy to have his mustache back on his face.

Lily and Max were at the zoo with their mom. They wanted to see the penguins. They liked how they looked in their black and white coats. They followed the signs to the penguin house.

When they got there, they saw a big pool of water with ice and rocks. There were many penguins in the water and on the land. Some of them were swimming and diving. Some of them were standing and flapping their wings. Some of them were marching in a line.

"Look, mom, they are marching!" Lily said. "They look like soldiers!"

"Yes, they do," mom said. "They march to keep warm and to stay together. It is very cold where they live."

Lily and Max started to march like the penguins. They lifted their feet high and swung their arms. They made funny noises with their mouths. They had fun.

But one penguin did not like their marching. He was the leader of the penguin group. He thought they were mocking him and his friends. He felt angry and annoyed. He decided to teach them a lesson.

He jumped out of the water and ran towards Lily and Max. He opened his beak and squawked loudly. He pecked at their shoes and legs.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily and Max cried. "Stop it, stop it, stop it!"

They ran away from the penguin. They were scared and hurt. They ran to their mom and hugged her.

"Mom, mom, mom!" they said. "The penguin is mean! He bit us!"

Mom looked at the penguin. He was still chasing them. He looked angry and proud. She picked up Lily and Max and carried them away from the penguin house.

Lily and Max nodded. They understood. They felt sorry for the penguin. They did not mean to upset him. They just wanted to have fun.

Lily and Max smiled. They liked the monkeys. They hoped they would be nicer than the penguin. They followed their mom to the monkey house. They forgot about the penguin. They were happy again.

Once there was a boy named Jack. He was three years old and he loved playing with his friends. One day, he was walking in the park when he saw a glove on the ground. He picked it up and asked himself, "Whose glove is this?"

He looked around but there was no one in sight. Then he came upon an old man and asked, "Excuse me, sir, can you answer me? Whose glove is this?"

Jack was happy that he solved the mystery of the glove. But then he remembered something. He asked the old man, "Can I have your glove? It's so soft and looks very easy to use."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to eat pears. One day, she went to the market with her mommy and saw a big basket of pears. She was so happy and asked her mommy to buy some for her. Her mommy said yes and bought a big, juicy pear for her.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Emma. Emma had a big goal. She wanted to break a record. She was determined to make her goal come true.

Once upon a time, there was a group of delicate butterflies. They loved to wander around the garden and smell the pretty flowers. One day, they met a little girl named Lily.

Once upon a time, there was a snowman. His name was Bob. He lived in a cold, snow-covered town.

Joe was so curious to see what was inside the envelope. He opened it and found a new toy rabbit. Joe was so happy that he said to the rabbit, "Hi there, I'm Joe! It's nice to meet you!"

The rabbit replied, "It's nice to meet you too! Let's go and play in the garden".

Joe smiled and said, "That's a great idea! Let's go!"

And so, Joe and the rabbit went off to the garden to play together.

One day, Joe and his mommy were walking in the park when they noticed a quiet bird. Joe wanted to mention the bird to his mommy, so he pointed at it and said, "Look, mommy!" His mommy smiled and said, "Yes, that's a very pretty bird."

The bird then started to make some noise, chirping gently. Joe was so excited that he wanted to mention it again. "Hear it, mommy!" he said. His mommy smiled and said, "Yes, I hear it."

As they kept walking, they noticed a guilty-looking puppy sitting by himself, beneath a big tree. The puppy was very quiet, but Joe still wanted to mention it, so he said, "Look at the puppy mommy!" His mommy smiled and said, "That's a sweet little puppy."

Joe and his mommy kept walking, but Joe always remembered the quiet bird and guilty-looking puppy they saw on their walk.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a microscope in their dad's office. They wanted to see what it could do.

"Let's split this leaf and look at it," Ben said. He tore a small piece of green from a plant and put it on a slide.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said. She turned on the light and looked through the eyepiece. "Wow, I see tiny dots and lines. They are so pretty."

Ben took his turn and nodded. "They are. I wonder what they are."

They heard their dad coming and quickly hid the microscope under a pillow. They pretended to read a book.

"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" their dad asked.

"Nothing, dad. Just reading," Lily said.

"Are you calm today?" their dad asked. He smiled and ruffled their hair.

"Yes, dad. We are very calm," Ben said.

Their dad left and they looked at each other. They giggled and took out the microscope again. They wanted to see more things. They split a hair, a feather, and a crumb. They had fun with their new toy.

Polly was a happy girl. She had a lot of energy, so each day she would dance. Everywhere Polly went, she brought her horn with her.

Today she was feeling particularly restless. She wanted to dance even more than usual. Polly went to a big field and shouted, "This is my dance floor!" Then she blew her horn and waved her arms up above her head.

She kept dancing and dancing until her feet got tired. She finally stopped and rested in the cool grass. Polly was exhausted and happily out of breath. But she made sure to keep her horn close.

Polly was happy and content. She cooled down and then, when she was ready, it was time to dance again. And that's what Polly did, until it was time for bed.

Lila and her mom were in the car. They wanted to go to the zoo. Lila loved the zoo. She wanted to see the wild animals. She hoped to see the lions and the monkeys and the giraffes.

But the car was not moving. There were many cars in front of them and behind them. They were stuck in traffic. Lila was sad. She looked out the window and saw the red lights and the honking horns.

"Mom, why are we not moving?" she asked.

"Because there is too much traffic, honey. Sometimes there are too many cars on the road and they make a big jam. We have to wait until the jam clears," mom said.

"How long do we have to wait?" Lila asked.

"I don't know, honey. Maybe a few minutes, maybe a long time. It depends on how fast the cars can move," mom said.

Lila sighed. She did not like waiting. She wanted to go to the zoo. She hoped the traffic would go away soon. She hoped the zoo would not close before they got there. She hoped the wild animals would not be too tired or too hungry to play with her. She hoped they would have fun at the zoo. She hoped, she hoped, she hoped.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Joe.
Joe loved to play in the sun. Every day he ran outside and felt the warmth of the sun on his face.

One day, Joe's mom said, "Joe, remember this is your first day of school. Don't forget to be brave and make new friends."
Joe nodded.

At school, Joe saw some new faces. He was a little scared but he remembered what his mom said. He bravely said hello to the other children and soon he was playing with them in the sun.

The other children didn't have any toys to share, so Joe brought in a little basket of his own toys. The other children were so happy and they quickly became friends.

Joe smiled. He was glad he remembered what his mom said. He remembered that if he was brave and kind, he could make new friends.

Joe thought to himself 'I am happy when I do things with a kind heart.' His mom was right, good things can happen when you are brave and kind.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sue. Sue loved to design pretty pictures. She used soft colors to draw flowers, trees, and animals. Sue wanted to share her pictures with her friend, Tim.

Sue put her picture in the mail for Tim. She was very happy. She thought Tim would love her soft colored picture. Sue waited and waited for Tim to get her mail.

But one day, a big rain came. The rain was so strong that it made the mail wet. Sue's soft colored picture was all wet and messy. Tim never got to see Sue's pretty design. Sue was very sad.

Mama and Jack were very excited. They had just moved into a new house. Jack was only three so he couldn't help much, but he watched as Mama unpacked all their boxes. He saw clothes and toys, books and games. When Mama asked him what he was most excited about, he smiled and said, "I'm excited to make friends here!"

But when they opened up one of the boxes, he saw something strange - it was a stiff, white jacket. Jack was confused. "What is this thing?" he asked.

Mama smiled sadly. "It's a cold jacket," she said.

Jack frowned. "Why's it here?" he asked.

Mama looked at Jack with deep sadness in her eyes. She told him that the jacket had belonged to Daddy, but he had moved on to a better place. She hugged Jack and said, "It's okay to be sad, but Daddy is always with us in our hearts."

Jack looked at the cold jacket and made a silent promise that he would never forget Daddy. He knew that no matter where he moved, he would always remember.

John was walking in the park when he saw a big black raven on the ground. It looked upset, so he went over to help it. He realised that it had been caught in some brambles and so he carefully began to try to free it.

John took a deep breath and carefully began to try to loosen the brambles. As he was pinching the brambles, the raven flapped its wings and flew away!

John was amazed as he watched the raven soar away. He smiled, but then he heard a tiny voice asking him why he had been pinching the raven.

John looked down and saw a little girl of three years old. He smiled and said, "I was trying to help the raven, it was hurt and I wanted to set it free".

The little girl said, "Oh, okay. That's very kind of you". She smiled at him and then ran off, but John was still smiling. He was so pleased that he had helped the poor raven and made the little girl so happy.

A big hot sun was shining in the sky. Two friends saw it and decided to go outside. They wanted to have fun in the warm weather.

The two friends started to play chase and they got very hot. One of the friends found an old rag lying in the grass. He decided to throw it in the air and try to catch it.

His friend got mad and picked up the rag. He wanted to keep it for himself. He started shouting and tried to pull it away from his friend.

This made the other friend very angry. He also wanted the rag and a fight started! They pushed and pulled each other trying to take the rag away.

Eventually one of them got it. Both were so tired that they decided to stop fighting. They took a break and decided to find something else to do.

One day, a magical creature appeared. It had shiny jewelry all over its body. Every time it moved, the jewelry would sparkle and shine.

The creature seemed friendly, so the little girl wanted to get closer. She wanted to touch the beautiful jewelry. But when she got closer, the jewelry suddenly seemed disgusting! It was slimy and smelly.

The little girl was sad and stepped back. The creature smiled and flew away. She never saw it again, but she always remembered its pretty jewelry.

Mummy and Daddy were picking flowers in the garden. Mummy picked a red daisy, Daddy picked a purple thistle and the little girl picked a beautiful lily. The lily was her favorite because it was so fluffy and white and the aroma was heavenly.

Daddy said, "Let's bring this lily inside and put it on the windowsill."

Mummy said, "How about we make it a surprise?"

So the family all went inside and the little girl put the lily on the windowsill.

When she stepped back to admire her work, she noticed a bright yellow butterfly that had landed on the lily. The little girl smiled.

Mummy said, "Oh my, that lily looks so warm and cozy with the butterfly on top."

The little girl nodded, delighted with her surprise. And, from that day on, the warm lily became a happy reminder of the special family day.

Once upon a time there was a pretty fly. It was orange and had big wings. The sun was shining and the fly was happy.

The fly went buzzing around, looking for food. Suddenly he noticed a bright yellow flower. It had lots of yummy nectar!

He flew over to the flower and started drinking the nectar. It was so sweet and delicious! As he drank, he closed his eyes and blinked in content.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was a bee! The bee said: "Hi there, fly! What are you doing here? This flower is mine!"

The fly flew away in a hurry. He was feeling a bit scared. But then he saw something even prettier - a rainbow up in the sky. It was so big and colourful! He just had to go and look closer.

He flew up to the rainbow and sat on a pot of gold. He blinked a few times in amazement. Then he smiled and said: "This is the prettiest place I have ever seen!"

Ben and Mia are twins. They like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They drive them on the floor, on the sofa, on the table. They make noises like vroom, beep, honk.

One day, they find a big black car in the garage. It is their dad's car. It looks shiny and cool. They want to play with it. They open the door and climb inside. They see many buttons and levers. They touch them and pull them. The car makes noises like click, whirr, ding.

"Look, Mia, I can drive!" Ben says. He turns the key in the ignition. The car starts to move. It goes forward and backward. It bumps into the wall and the shelves. It makes noises like crash, bang, screech.

"Stop, Ben, stop!" Mia says. She is scared. She wants to get out. But the door is locked. She cries and screams. She pushes the horn. It makes a loud noise like honk, honk, honk.

Dad hears the noise. He runs to the garage. He sees the car moving and shaking. He sees Ben and Mia inside. He is angry and worried. He opens the door and takes them out. He hugs them and checks if they are hurt. He is glad they are okay. He scolds them and tells them to never play with his car again. He says it is dangerous and not a toy. He says they could have broken the car or hurt themselves or others.

Ben and Mia are sorry. They say they are sorry to dad and to the car. They promise to never do it again. They learn that they should not touch things that are not theirs. They learn that they should listen to dad and be careful. They learn that driving is not a game. They go back to their toy cars. They drive them safely and happily. They make noises like vroom, beep, honk.

Once there was a small girl named Nina. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day, Nina was out walking in the forest all alone. She passed by a huge tree and spotted a funny knob on its bark. She smiled and giggled in delight.

Suddenly, she heard a deep booming laughter. She was surprised and scared. Nina was so lonely and thought no one else was there.
