Then from behind the tree, an old man appeared. He saw Nina, smiled, and said "hey there little one". He had a funny twinkle in his eye. He asked her why she was so lonely and she told him about the knob.

The old man grinned, put his hand on the knob and started to spin it. Suddenly, the knob opened! Inside was a box of chocolates. "For me?" Nina said, amazed.

The old man nodded, and they both laughed together. From that day on, they both went to the tree every day and had lots of fun.

Max had a lot of purple shampoo in his room. He was ready to try it out! He walked over to the mirror and picked up the bottle. It felt a bit heavy in his hands.

Max's mum saw him and smiled. She knew he liked playing with colourful things. She encouraged him to try the shampoo on his own.

Max smiled back. He was a bit scared of getting it in his eyes, but he was brave. He squirted a bit of the purple shampoo in his hand, rubbed it together and put it on his hair. It tickled!

Max's mum watched him in admiration. She thought he did a great job and told him so. He smiled proudly.

Max was so proud of what he'd done. He had tried something new by himself and it worked out great! His mum's encouragement had made him feel even more confident.

Once upon a time, in a small harbor, lived a unique fish named Finny. Finny was not like other fish. He had bright colors and always swam in circles. All the other fish liked to watch Finny swim.

One day, a big fish named Bubbles saw Finny and said, "Finny, why do you always repeat swimming in circles?" Finny replied, "I like it. It's fun and makes me special." Bubbles thought for a moment then said, "Can I try too?" Finny smiled and said, "Of course, Bubbles!"

Bubbles tried to swim in circles like Finny, but he was not very good at it. He got dizzy and bumped into a big rock. Bubbles got hurt and started to cry. Finny felt bad and tried to help Bubbles. But it was too late. Bubbles had to go away and live in another harbor. All the other fish were sad and missed Bubbles. They learned that not everyone can be unique like Finny, and sometimes trying new things can have a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient painter. She was very talented and spent her days creating beautiful pictures. One day a man came to her door and asked her to sign a piece of paper. She gladly accepted, and when she signed, a magic happened! Suddenly, a rainbow appeared in the sky, and the painter was filled with joy and amazement.

The next day, the painter decided to put the rainbow she had created on one of her paintings. She remembered how happy the rainbow had made her and wanted to share that feeling with everyone.

She worked long and hard, carefully brushing each color onto the canvas until the rainbow was just the way she wanted it to be. Everyone who saw it was filled with awe and delight.

Even after all these years, the ancient rainbow still brings joy to the painter and reminds her of the magical moment when she first signed the paper.

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Tom. Tom liked to be organized. He had a shop where he would sell ties. Every day, he would put his ties in nice rows on a table.

One day, a dog named Max came to the shop. Max wanted to buy a tie. Tom showed him all the ties, but Max could not pick one. Tom had an idea. He said, "Come back tomorrow, I will have a new tie for you."

That night, Tom made a special tie just for Max. It was blue, Max's favorite color. The next day, Max came back to the shop. He saw the blue tie and loved it. Tom was happy that he could help Max. From that day on, they were best friends.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She had a special mission; to collect doves. Everyday she would put on her brightly coloured dress and her sparkly shoes and go out collecting. Every morning she would walk to the park and then look to the sky. Then she would spot a dove and try to catch it in her hands.

Today was a sunny day, and the little girl was feeling very sleepy. She found a big tree to sit under as she watched the doves up in the sky. Suddenly she noticed a dove land on a branch close to her. Gently, she reached out to try and catch it. "Coo-Coo!" the dove said.

The little girl was suprised. She had never heard a dove talk before!

"Hi, little dove" the little girl said. "My name's Daisy. And I'm here to collect doves".

"Well, you caught me!" the dove said. "Let's be friends!"

Daisy was so happy. She had found a special friend and could share her dove collecting mission with him.

Together Daisy and her dove friend went on many adventures and caught lots of doves. Every night before bedtime, Daisy would give her doves a big hug before they flew up to the sky.

That was Daisy's life collecting her special doves, and it was just perfect.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Kelly who loved to explore. On one of her adventures she came across a weird pebble in the park. She picked it up and tried to lift it but it was too heavy for her. So she asked her mom for help.

â€œThis pebble is too heavy for me to lift, Mommy! Can you help me?â€

Her mom smiled and said, â€œIf something is too difficult for you, you can always ask for help. You shouldnâ€™t try to do everything on your own.â€

So Kelly and her mom worked together and were able to lift the pebble and set it down safely.

Kelly learnt that itâ€™s always good to ask for help when something is too hard. The moral of the story is that two heads are better than one!

Sara liked to play in the attic. She found many old things there. Some were toys, some were clothes, some were books. She liked to display them on the floor and pretend they were hers.

One day, she found a big box in the corner. She opened it and saw a doll. The doll had long hair, a pretty dress and shiny shoes. Sara was happy. She took the doll out and hugged it. She wanted to display it with her other things.

But the doll was not nice. It had a mean face and sharp teeth. It bit Sara's arm and made her cry. Sara was scared and hurt. She threw the doll back in the box and ran away. She did not want to play in the attic anymore.

She went to her mom and showed her the bite. Her mom was worried and angry. She asked Sara where she got the bite. Sara told her about the doll in the attic. Her mom did not believe her. She thought Sara was lying.

She took Sara to the attic and opened the box. She wanted to see the doll. But the box was empty. There was no doll. Sara was confused and uncomfortable. She did not know where the doll went. She hoped it would not come back.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. Anna was very excited to learn something new. She wanted to learn how to use a fork.

One day, her mommy showed her how to pick up the fork. Anna was so happy and she smiled brightly. She practiced picking up the fork while walking around the kitchen.

But then, something strange happened! Anna started to feel a bit dizzy, as if the room were spinning around her. She bent down and put her head on the table.

Anna's mommy was worried. She rubbed Anna's back, and gave her something to drink. Soon Anna felt better and she was finally able to pick up the fork again.

Anna was so proud of herself for learning how to use a fork! She had felt a bit dizzy, but was very happy she now knew how to do it. She was one step closer to being a big girl.

Once upon a time, there was a big orange cat named Max. Max was very bald, with no fur on his head. One day, Max saw a little mouse and wanted to eat it. But the mouse disagreed and said, "Please don't eat me, Max. I'm just a tiny mouse." Max thought about it and decided not to eat the mouse. Instead, Max and the mouse became friends and played together every day. The end.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to pretend they were animals and make noises. Ben was a lion and Lily was a mouse.

"Roar!" Ben said, jumping out from behind the couch. "I am a big and strong lion. I will catch you, little mouse!"

Lily squeaked and ran away. She hid under the table and looked for something to protect herself. She saw a pin on the floor. It was shiny and sharp.

"Roar!" Ben said again, crawling towards the table. "Where are you, little mouse? I can smell you!"

Lily held the pin in her paw and waited. When Ben poked his head under the table, she jabbed him with the pin.

"Ow!" Ben cried, pulling back his head. "That hurt! What did you do, little mouse?"

Lily came out from under the table and showed him the pin. "I poked you with this. It is a pin. It can make holes in things. You scared me, big lion. You made me frightened."

Ben rubbed his head and looked at the pin. He felt sorry for Lily. He did not want to hurt her or make her frightened. He wanted to play with her and have fun.

"I am sorry, little mouse," he said. "I was only pretending. I did not mean to scare you. Can we be friends?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She gave him the pin and hugged him. "We can be friends, big lion. But no more roaring, okay?"

"Okay," Ben said. "No more roaring. How about we pretend we are something else? Something nice and friendly?"

Lily thought for a moment. Then she said, "How about we pretend we are birds? We can fly and sing and make nests."

Ben liked that idea. He agreed. They put away their toys and flapped their arms. They pretended they were birds and flew and sang and made nests. They had fun and did not frighten each other. They were happy.

Once there was a little girl named Alison. Alison lived with her mom and dad. She loved to dress up in new clothes every day. No matter what she was wearing, she always felt cool.

One day Alison's mom brought her a new dress. It was pretty and sparkly! Alison was so excited that she put it on right away. She asked her mom to take her outside to show off her new dress.

Outside in the front yard, Alison was playing in her dress when it started to rain. Alison shouted out to her mom, but the rain was so loud she couldn't hear. Alison started to run inside, but she was so spoiled that she didn't want to get wet.

So instead of running inside, Alison hid under a cooler. She stayed there until the rain stopped. When the sun came out, she was still dry and could play in her dress again. So Alison removed the cooler, spun around and laughed as she enjoyed her new dress in the sun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside, but it was raining, so he had to stay inside. He was feeling sad and bored.

Timmy's mom noticed how he was feeling and asked, "Do you want to play a game?"

"Yes, please!" Timmy said excitedly.

His mom said, "Let's play hide and seek. You hide and I'll find you."

Timmy ran to the closet to hide. He found a comfortable blanket and decided to wrap himself in it. He felt cozy and warm.

His mom counted to ten and then started looking for him. She searched the whole house, but she couldn't find him. She started to get worried.

Suddenly, Timmy jumped out of the closet and yelled, "Boo! You found me!"

His mom laughed and said, "You scared me! You're a great hider. Let's play again!" They played another round of hide and seek and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time there was an ancient spot in the forest. A little girl named Molly took a trip to the spot to see what it was like. As she looked around, she saw that it was very old and seemed to be magical.

"What is this place?" said Molly to a nearby bird.

The bird chirped and then said, "This is an ancient spot. It has been here for many, many years."

Molly was interested in the spot so she decided to stand right in the center of it. Suddenly, she felt a tingle pass through her body.

"What was that?" said Molly, feeling a bit scared.

The bird said, "That was the magic of this spot. It will give you strength."

Molly was surprised, but also excited. She thanked the bird and then stood in the spot for a few moments more, feeling the strength it gave her. Then she waved goodbye and left the ancient spot.

One morning, Jimmy woke to see snow outside. He hopped out of bed and was so excited. He ran to get his beloved red boots. He put them on and then called out to his mom in the kitchen.

"Mom, can I go outside and play in the snow?"

Jimmy's mom looked out the window. She was a bit worried.

"Jimmy, the walkway is sort of slippery," she said. "Wait and let me get your warm coat, hat and mittens."

Jimmy waited patiently. After a few minutes, he grabbed his coat and hat, and ran out the door. He jumped in the snow and it was so cold and fluffy. He made a snowman and started to sort out a snowball fight with some of his friends.

His mom came and watched from the front window. She was still a bit worried but smiled when she saw Jimmy was having lots of fun.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. Lily wants to go on the slide, but Tom is scared.

"Come on, Tom, it is fun!" Lily says.

"I don't know, Lily, it is high and fast," Tom says.

Lily holds Tom's hand. "We can go together. I will help you. Don't be scared," she says.

Tom thinks for a moment. He wants to be brave, but he is still scared. He looks at Lily. She is his friend. She is honest. She will not hurt him.

"Okay, Lily, I will try," he says.

They climb up the stairs. They sit on the slide. Lily counts to three. They slide down. Tom feels the wind in his hair. He feels the sun on his face. He feels happy.

He realizes he likes the slide. He realizes he is not scared anymore. He realizes he has a new goal. He wants to go on the slide again.

"Wow, that was fun!" he says.

"See, I told you!" Lily says.

They hug each other. They are happy. They are friends. They go on the slide again.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. They were going on a trip to the airport. The mom packed a useful bag with snacks and toys. The dad carried heavy suitcases to the car.

At the airport, they saw big planes in the sky. The little boy was excited to see them. They had to wait in line to check their bags. The mom gave the boy a teddy bear to carry.

Finally, they got on the plane and sat in their seats. The boy was happy to have his teddy bear to play with. The plane took off and they flew high in the sky. When they landed, the dad carried the suitcases again. They had a fun trip and were happy to be home.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his friends in the park. They would run, jump, and have lots of fun.

One day, Spot found a big bag of rice. He thought it would be fun to bury the rice and play a game with his friends. So, he dug a big hole and put the rice in it. Then, he covered it with dirt.

Spot called his friends to play a game of finding the rice. They all looked and looked, but they could not find it. Finally, Spot showed them where the rice was. They all laughed and had a great time. Spot was a very dependable friend.

Once upon a time, in a wild garden, there lived a little ant named Andy. Andy was a hard worker and loved to serve his ant friends. Every day, he would help them find yummy food.

One sunny day, Andy met a big bee named Betty. "Hi, I am Andy," said the ant. "I like to serve my friends. Can I help you find some food?" Betty the bee smiled and said, "Yes, please! I am hungry."

Andy and Betty looked around the wild garden. They found tasty flowers for Betty and sweet crumbs for Andy. They became good friends and loved to play together. From that day on, Andy and Betty always helped each other and served their friends in the wild garden. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a mommy and her little girl. The girl was very brave and loved playing outside in the rain. One day, while they were outside, a very loud thunder clap shook the sky. The little girl was scared, but mommy was so strong. She grabbed the little girl and held her tight, to try to prevent any more thunder.

The mommy sang a song to the little girl about the rain being like magic in the sky. It helped the little girl stop feeling so scared.

They went inside and watched the rain from the window. Mommy told her stories about the clouds and how they work together to create rainbows. The little girl smiled and felt safe. She knew her mommy was strong and could prevent the thunder from scaring her again.

The days went by and the little girl was no longer scared of thunder. She even welcomed the powerful thunderstorms and smiled from the window.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a big bedroom with fancy things in it. She loved her room very much. One day, she saw a small flower in her room. The flower was trying to bloom.

Sue said to the flower, "Hello, little flower! Why are you trying to bloom in my bedroom?" The flower said, "I want to be a fancy flower in your room." Sue liked the idea, but she knew that flowers needed sun and water to grow.

Sue tried to help the flower. She gave it water and put it near the window. But the flower did not get enough sun. It tried very hard to bloom, but it could not. The flower became sad and said, "I am sorry, Sue. I cannot be a fancy flower in your room."

In the end, the flower did not bloom. It stayed small and sad. Sue felt bad for the flower. She wished she could help it more. But she knew that flowers needed sun and water to grow, and her bedroom was not the best place for a flower to live.

Once upon a time, there were two naughty kids. They loved to run and play near a big, tall structure in their backyard. One day, they decided to do something very naughty and climb the structure.

The kids reached the top of it and looked around. They could see far away, but at the same time, they felt scared. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. They looked down and saw their mom coming! They quickly climbed down, one step at a time.

Their mom was angry. She said they should never go near the structure again. She warned them of the danger. But the kids didn't understand.

Time passed and the kids grew up. They started to regret not listening to their mom. They wished they had listened so they wouldn't have gotten in trouble. From then on, they stayed away from the tall structure and never climbed it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had curly hair and loved to explore. Every morning she would go out into her garden and find something new.

One day, while the girl was playing, she saw a big, juicy apple on the ground. She picked it up and wanted to eat it right away. But it was too big! So she ran into the kitchen and asked her mom, "Please can I have a piece of the apple?" Her mom smiled and cut the apple into pieces. The girl took a bite and it was so tasty!

The girl ate her apple and thought of other tasty treats she could make. She asked her mom, "Please, can I make some cookies?" Her mom said yes and the girl got to work. She gathered ingredients and mixed them together. Soon, delicious chocolate chip cookies were in the oven.

The girl smiled as she pulled the cookies out of the oven. They smelled so yummy and tasted even better. She shared them with her mom, who said they were the best cookies she had ever tried.

The little girl was so happy and proud of herself! From that day on she loved to explore her garden and make tasty treats.

Sam and Ben are playing in the park. They have a toy gun that makes a loud noise. Sam likes to pretend he is a cowboy and Ben is a robber. They run and hide behind the trees and the swings.

"Bang, bang, you are dead, robber!" Sam shouts, pointing the gun at Ben.

"No, I am not, cowboy! You missed me!" Ben shouts back, dodging the gun.

They laugh and play some more. But then, a big boy comes and sees the gun. He wants to play with it too. He runs to Sam and grabs the gun from his hand.

"Hey, give me that! It is mine!" Sam says, angry.

"No, it is mine now! You are too small to play with it!" the big boy says, angry too.

He pushes Sam to the ground and runs away with the gun. Sam cries and Ben runs to help him.

"That is not nice! He is a bully!" Ben says, sad.

They look at the big boy, who is playing with the gun by himself. He does not look happy. He looks lonely.

"Maybe he has no friends to play with," Sam says, wiping his tears.

"Maybe we can share the gun with him," Ben says, smiling.

They get up and walk to the big boy. They ask him if he wants to play with them. The big boy is surprised. He does not know what to say.

"Really? You want to play with me?" he says, unsure.

"Yes, we do. We can take turns with the gun. It is more fun to play together," Sam says, friendly.

The big boy smiles. He gives the gun back to Sam and says sorry. He says his name is Tom. They shake hands and become friends. They play cowboys and robbers together. They have a lot of fun. They are not angry anymore. They are happy.

Molly and Jake had their birthday parties at the same time. They were both turning three years old and had invited all their friends over to celebrate. The party was a blast and everyone had a lot of fun.

At the party, Molly noticed how envious Jake was of her special bouncy castle. She wanted to make Jake feel better, so she asked if anyone wanted to come and play with her in the bouncy castle. All of the kids eagerly said yes and went to play with Molly.

To remind Jake of all the fun they had had, Molly gave each of her friends a small toy from the bouncy castle as a party favor. All the kids loved the tokens and thanked Molly.

Jake smiled and thanked Molly too. He was happy that Molly had remembered him and had been so sweet to share the bouncy castle with her friends. He was definitely having the best birthday ever.

Once upon a time, a little girl had a big dream. She wanted to be strong and tough like her big brother. But it was always so hard to be like him!

One day, she got an idea. She would eat broccoli! She knew that broccoli would make her tough like her big brother.

Every day, she ate broccoli. At first, it tasted yucky, but the more she ate, the better she felt. She even started to like it!

Her dream was coming true. With every bite of broccoli, she got a little bit tougher and stronger. Soon, she felt like she could do anything, just like her big brother.

The little girl was so happy to have reached her dream. And she kept eating broccoli every day!

Jim was sad. He had been playing in the park all day and he was really tired. He sat down on the bench and started to complain. He said that the park was too dirty and he didn't like it.

Suddenly, a message floated down from the sky. It said "Hey Jim, why don't you come to the beach? It's clean and beautiful." Jim was excited and jumped up from the bench.

He ran all the way, but when he arrived at the beach, it was just as dirty as the park had been. Jim was even more angry than before and he started to complain again. He said "This beach is just as dirty as the park!"

But then he heard another message coming down from the sky. It said "Jim, just look around. There is so much beauty everywhere! See, there's a pretty tree, some birds and a nice big ocean. Everywhere you look there is love and beauty, you just have to see it!"

Jim looked around and he saw the beauty everywhere. He smiled and he knew that he had been wrong to complain about the dirty park and beach. From then on, he looked for beauty everywhere.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play with trains. Lily had a big train that made steam. Tom had a small train that did not make steam.

One day, they went to the park with their trains. They saw a boy with a shiny new train. His train made steam and noises. It was very fast and fun.

"Wow, look at his train!" Tom said. "I want a train like that!"

Lily felt jealous. She liked her train, but she thought the boy's train was better. She wanted to play with it.

"Can we play with your train?" she asked the boy.

The boy shook his head. "No, this is my train. You can't touch it."

Lily and Tom felt sad. They went back to their trains.

"Your train is nice, Lily," Tom said. "It makes steam. My train does not make steam."

Lily smiled. She had an idea.

"Tom, I have something to tell you. I recommend you to do this. You can make your train make steam too. You just need some water and a straw."

She showed Tom how to put some water in his train and blow through a straw. The water came out as steam.

"Wow, thank you, Lily!" Tom said. "This is so cool! Now my train makes steam too!"

They played with their trains happily. They did not care about the boy's train anymore. They were happy with their own trains. They were best friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lulu. Everyday, she went on a walk with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lulu stumbled upon a shiny object in the grass. It was a microscope! Lulu picked up the microscope and looked through it. She could see tiny bugs and ants up close. She was so excited and proud.

Mommy and Daddy said that the microscope was very safe. Lulu knew that it was very special and she had to take good care of it.

Later that night, Lulu was having dinner with her mommy and daddy. Mommy said to Daddy, "Should we get Lulu her own microscope for her birthday?"

Lulu shouted with glee, "Yes please!"

Everyone laughed at her enthusiasm. Mommy and Daddy said that they would make sure to find a safe microscope for Lulu's birthday present.

Lulu couldn't wait to have her very own microscope!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and her cat, Daisy. Every day, Lily and Daisy would go for a walk down a path near their house. They loved to see the flowers, trees, and birds.

One sunny day, Lily and Daisy met a new friend on the path. It was a tiny ant. The ant said, "Hello, I am Andy the Ant. Can you please help me? I need some water for my family." Lily wanted to be useful, so she said, "Yes, I can help you, Andy."

Lily found a small cup and poured some water from a nearby stream. She carried the cup back to Andy and his family. The ants were very happy and thanked Lily for her help. From that day on, Lily, Daisy, and Andy the Ant became best friends and had many fun adventures together on the path.

Once upon a time there was a hairy monster who lived under a mountain. The monster was so naughty that the other animals were scared of him. One day, the monster wanted to escape from the mountain, so he bit through the stone walls. Suddenly, a jail appeared in front of him. The monster was so scared that he forgot about freedom and ran back inside the mountain.

The next day, the monster saw a mouse walking by. The monster jumped out and said, "Please, mouse, will you help me escape this jail?"

The mouse replied, "If you promise not to bite me, I will try to help you."

The monster agreed and the mouse guided him out of the jail and back to the mountain. From then on, the monster was careful not to bite anyone anymore.

Once upon a time there was a little girl in a clean crib. Every night her mother would pass her a story book and read to her until she fell asleep. Then the little girl would dream about adventures and playing with her friends.

When morning came, the little girl would get out of bed and go play. She loved to visit the beach, collect shells and make castles in the sand. Sometimes she would even pass by a playground and swing on the swings.

At the end of the day, when the sun had gone to sleep, the little girl would go home to her clean crib. After eating a yummy dinner and giving her mom a hug, she would curl up in her comfy crib and be ready for the next day's adventures.

Once there was a bug who liked to twist. Every day the bug would twist and twist, until one day something bad happened. The bug twisted a little too much and he got too tired. He went still and was dead.

The other bugs in the garden were sad. They gathered around their dead friend and missed him.

But then, something amazing happened! The dead bug suddenly twisted back to life! He was very happy to be alive again, and all the other bugs were excited too.

From then on, the bug never twisted too much. He learned that twisting was fun, but knew when it was time to stop. And everyone was happy!

John ran quickly to the mall. As he looked around, he saw so many things. He found a deep pond with lots of fish inside.

â€œWow,â€ John said.

John saw Mommy walking up to him. â€œHi John!â€ she said. â€œLetâ€™s go on a hunt. Can you help me find something?â€

â€œSure!â€ said John. The two of them ran around the mall looking for things. They saw a big deep bird's nest in a tree. They also saw lots of yummy snacks in the mall store.

John saw a playground and got excited. â€œMommy, can we go on the slide?â€ he asked.

Mommy laughed. â€œOf course!â€ She said. They ran to the slide, and soon they were having lots of fun. After a while, it was time to leave. John said goodbye to all the friends he made and ran back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to decorate. She loved to put patterns on things â€" trees, walls, and even the ground. Today, she had decided to decorate her bedroom.

First, she decided to paint the walls. She chose a cool pattern, which she did all by herself. When she finished, it looked beautiful and she was so proud.

Then, she picked out some cool fabric for her bedspread. The fabric had different coloured and patterned shapes on it. The little girl spread it over her bed and it looked so cool.

Finally, she looked for decorations for her dresser. She found a cool mirror and added some pretty coloured flowers to the top. Now her room was complete, and it looked so nice. The little girl was very happy with how it looked.

Once upon a time, a little girl was marching in the dark. She had a big smile on her face. The little girl was so happy that she started to march faster and faster. All of a sudden, her foot stepped on a rock. She felt scared and she stopped marching.

The little girl looked around, there was nothing but the dark all around her. She couldn't see a thing. She was brave, though, and she decided to march on. Even though it was dark, she felt okay because she had a big smile on her face.

The little girl marched through the dark until she suddenly saw a light. Then she could see that the darkness was not so dark after all. She was so happy and she kept on marching until she was out of the darkness and the darkness behind her was left far away.

Now the little girl was out of the dark and she could see. She felt safe and she marched along, with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to watch TV all day long. His mommy said, "Timmy, you need to let the TV rest for a while." But Timmy didn't want to stop watching his favorite show.

One day, the TV started to go slow. Timmy became sad because he couldn't watch his show. He said, "Mommy, why is the TV so slow?" His mommy said, "Maybe it needs a break. Let's turn it off for a bit."

Timmy agreed and turned off the TV. After a while, he turned it back on and it worked perfectly fine. Timmy learned that sometimes it's good to let things rest so they can work better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Abby. She was three years old and she loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, Abby went out to play in the garden. As she walked, she saw a flag blowing in the wind. She had never seen a flag before, so she asked her mummy, "What is that?"

Mummy said, "It's a flag, Abby. It is a symbol that stands for something important." Abby was full of wonder, and she wanted to know more. So, mummy went on to explain, "Flags can mean many things. This one is a symbol of peace - it shows that the people who live around here are gentle and kind."

Abby smiled and said, "I know all about flags now!" She spent the afternoon playing in the sunshine, and she always remembered what mummy taught her about the flag.

Once upon a time there was an old man and an old woman who lived together. Every day the old man would teach the old woman something new. Today, the old man was going to teach the old woman how to use pastels.

The old man put the pastels onto the table and explained to the old woman, â€œYou just need to colour inside the lines.â€ The old woman tried her best but she couldnâ€™t quite colour the way the old man did.

The old man smiled and said, â€œThatâ€™s ok, youâ€™ll get better as you practice.â€ He pointed to one of the pictures on the table and said, â€œLetâ€™s try this one.â€ The old woman picked up the pastels and carefully coloured inside the lines.

After she was finished, the old man praised her effort. â€œThatâ€™s perfect,â€ he said. â€œYouâ€™ve really improved.â€ The old woman smiled and thanked him for teaching her. They both admired her work and then had a cup of tea to celebrate the old womanâ€™s success.

One day, Larry went to the store. He needed to get some lotion. His mom had told him lotion was a dependable thing to receive.

Larry was very excited. He ran to the lotion aisle and saw all kinds of different lotions. He looked at the bottles and read the directions.

Finally he found one that said it was dependable. He brought it to the register and paid for it. When he got back home, his mom hugged him and said, "Thank you for bringing me the lotion. You are very dependable."

Larry was very proud. He was happy to have received something his mom said was dependable. From then on, Larry always received lotion with a dependable attitude.

Paul was feeling very happy. Today he was meeting his old friends from his childhood. Paul was excited to see them again as it had been a long time. When he arrived, he was reminded of all the fun they used to have together.

Paul said, "Do you remember when we used to play together in this park? It was so much fun!" All of his friends nodded and started laughing.

His friends suggested they should keep in touch, so they decided to create a network. This way, they could always stay in touch, no matter where they were in the world. They wanted to make sure that their network was reliable so they exchanged emails, telephone numbers and addresses.

Paul was delighted. "This is a great idea! Now, we always have a way to stay connected". His friends agreed and all of them hugged before saying goodbye. Paul couldn't believe how lucky he was. He was reminded of how wonderful it was to have such reliable friends.

Once upon a time there was an ancient tree. Every day it would grow bigger and bigger. One day, the tree took an special trip. It was so excited!

It flew high in to the sky and looked out over the world below. The tree felt so small compared to everything else around it. Suddenly, the tree grew and grew until it was the tallest tree in the whole world!

The tree looked down and it could see the whole world. It could see all the beautiful places below it. Everywhere the tree looked it could see wonderful things.

The tree was so happy that it took a trip every day. It saw so many wonderful things every day and grew taller and taller. And so, the tree stayed the tallest tree in the world for many years.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Bella. She was very happy. One day she wanted to wear her favourite blouse. Problem was that it was too small for her!

Bella started to cry. Her mum hugged her and said, "Don't cry, sweetie. Let's look for something else to wear." Bella nodded, wiped her tears and was alert.

They soon found a new blouse that fit Bella nicely. She was very happy now and danced around in joy.

Mum said, "It's important to remain alert and see the situation in a positive light."

The moral of the story is to always stay positive and look for solutions!

It was a sunny day and two friends, Lucy and Max, were out for a walk. They got to the street where there was lots of traffic.

"Look Max!" Lucy said. "All the cars make noise!"

Max nodded and looked at the traffic. It was strong.

"Let's go to the park," Lucy said.

The two friends walked to the park together. When they got there, they saw a weak tree.

"Let's make the tree stronger," Lucy said.

Max smiled and ran to get some soil and water. With lots of care and patience, Max and Lucy made the tree strong again.

They were happy and laughed together. The weak tree was now strong and standing tall.

"We did it!" they said together.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. He lived in a wild jungle. Every morning he would roar very loudly. The other animals were scared of him and had to be extra quiet.

One day, the lion found a fireplace in the middle of the jungle. He was so excited! He went over to it and noticed it was very old and original. He made a roaring sound and the fireplace lit up.

Now the lion had a nice warm home. He would spend the evenings by the fireplace, warming his body and keeping himself safe.

Every evening, he would roar and the fireplace would glow brightly. He was so happy in his own special den. He was the king of the jungle!

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim went on a vacation with his family. They went to a big park with lots of trees, flowers, and a big lake. Tim was very happy to play with his ball and run around.

One day, while Tim was playing, he did a stumble on a rock. He fell down and his ball rolled far away. Tim felt a little guilty because he didn't look where he was going. He got up and looked for his ball.

Tim found his ball near a big tree. He was very happy to find it. He hugged the ball and promised to be more careful. Then, he went back to play with his family, having lots of fun on their vacation.

Once upon a time there was a bee called Buzzy. He liked to skip around his hive, which was different from all the other hives in the garden. Every day he would fly from flower to flower collecting nectar, and then skip back to his hive with a smile on his face.

One day, while he was skipping around the garden, he noticed a funny looking hive in the corner. It was shaped differently than his hive and it had some interesting patterns painted on it.

Buzzy was so curious that he decided to fly over to the strange hive. He buzzed around it a few times, and then decided to peek inside. It was full of different kinds of goodies that he'd never seen before!

He smiled and flew back to his own hive with some of the treats. Ever since then, Buzzy has been skipping around the garden with a bit more excitement. He never knows when he'll find a new and exciting hive!

Once there was a little girl, and she was determined to learn how to ride her bike. She was only three, so she was really wobbly when she tried to ride it. Her mom wanted to encourage her, so she showed her how to ride safely. She showed her how to practice on her bike on the white rug in their living room.

The little girl was a bit scared to try it, but with a few gentle words from her mom, she got on the bike and started to pedal. She swerved around, and had lots of falls, but every time she fell, her mom was there, to help her back up and encourage her to keep going.

Pretty soon, the little girl mastered it, and she was so proud! She started to ride around the white rug, pumping the pedals confidently and laughing with joy. Her mom cheered, "Well done!" and she gave her a hug. The little girl was delighted that she had made progress, and now she was ready to try riding on the street, too.

Once there was a girl named Henry. She lived in a child's room and enjoyed painting a lot. One day, Henry wanted to paint a number. She was very anxious to see what it would look like.

When she had finished the painting, she showed it to her parents. But they said it wasn't good enough. Henry felt really bad, but she was determined to make a better painting.

The next day Henry came back with what she thought was a better painting. But her parents weren't impressed, and they said it still wasn't good enough. Henry was so frustrated, she started to cry.

Her mom comforted her and said "Henry, painting is like a journey. It's important to take your time and keep trying. It's not about the final painting, it's about the effort you put in along the way."

Henry was sad, but she tried to take her mom's advice. She kept painting and finally made a picture her parents liked.

The moral of the story is to not be anxious when trying something new and to keep trying, even if something doesn't turn out the way you want.

Once upon a time, there was a small elf named Pixie. She was very good at solving problems. One day, Pixie saw something strange in the sky. She had never seen anything like it before.

Pixie looked closer and saw something moving in the light. "What is this?" she said out loud. She tried to make out what it was.

Suddenly, Pixie remembered that her friends had told her about something called motion. That was when things moved by themselves.

So Pixie decided to solve the mystery. She took out a magnifying glass and looked very carefully. After a long time of looking, Pixie finally saw what it was - a beautiful butterfly!

Pixie was so happy to have solved the mystery. She waved goodbye to the butterfly as it flew away, and smiled to herself.

Little Peter enjoyed playing games with his friends. One of his favourites was 'match'. He would try to find two objects of the same shape or colour and put them together.

One day, Peter had a nightmare in which he was in a room filled with objects and he had to match them all but he was too little to do it. In the nightmare, the room seemed to keep on getting bigger and bigger.

When he awoke, it was morning and he was relieved that it was just a dream. He decided to enjoy his favourite game of 'match' with his friends instead.

So Peter and his friends went outside and played 'match'. They had a lovely time until it was time to go home. Peter was glad to be playing a game so much more fun than his little nightmare.

Ted was walking around the park and he felt shy. He looked around but everyone was busy. He noticed a mug lying on the grass. Ted was curious and he slowly walked towards it.

The mug had been left alone, so Ted picked it up. He ran his hands over the mug and he saw something written on it! It said "Complete me."

Ted was baffled but he decided to give it a try. He started to draw pictures on the mug with a red crayon. He felt happy and proud as he completed the mug.

Suddenly the park was filled with cheers! Everyone was cheering at Ted and he realized that they had been watching him complete the mug! Ted was embarrassed but he was also very happy. This was the best day ever.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely folder. The lonely folder lived in a big box with other folders. The lonely folder was sad because it had no papers inside. The other folders had many papers and they were happy.

One day, a nice person came to supply papers to the lonely folder. The nice person put many pretty papers inside the lonely folder. The lonely folder was so happy and not lonely anymore.

Now, the lonely folder was friends with the other folders. They all had pretty papers inside them. They lived happily in the big box together. And they all were happy folders.

Muffy the bunny hopped over to the park. She was so excited to play. As she arrived, she saw a big, powerful wheel. It was so high, she could hardly reach the top.

Muffy hopped around the wheel with her friends, until one of them said "Let's take a spin!". She was a bit scared, but also excited. She hopped into the middle of the wheel and held tight.

The wheel started to spin much faster than Muffy expected. She spun around and around, faster and faster! She was so happy, she squealed with delight.

After what felt like a long time, the wheel stopped spinning. Muffy hopped off the wheel and welcomed her friends to join her for a ride. Everyone spun around together and had a great time.

Once there was a small bear named Winter. Winter loved to explore in the woods and one day, he discovered a small doorway hidden in a tree.

Excitedly, Winter stepped through and found himself in a new and magical world. He gasped when he saw that flowers glowed in the dark and trees were shaped like animals!

Winter was looking around when he noticed someone standing nearby. It was a small fairy. She said, "Hello, Winter! What is your name?"
Winter smiled and said, "My name is Winter."

The fairy laughed and said, "That's a wonderful name! I'm glad you're here. You can explore and make friends in this magical place!"

Winter was so excited! He thanked the fairy and began exploring. He made many new friends and enjoyed discovering all the wonderful things in the magical world.

Winter will never forget his magical time in the small doorway deep in the woods.

Once there was a boy who hoped for a special treat. He wanted sauce. He asked his mum for it, but she said it was too tough and he wouldn't like it. He hoped it would be different and asked again. His mum saw how much he wanted it and said she would try. She got the sauce, and it was tough. The boy was disappointed. But then his mum said she would put it in the blender and see what happened. She did and the sauce was perfect. The boy happily ate it all up and said it was the best sauce ever! He always hoped for the best.

Once there was a little girl named Hannah. She was three years old. One day she was playing with her toys when something special happened. She found a box in her room. Hannah was so excited! She decided to open the box. Inside she found a beautiful doll.

Hannah was so happy and started to show her doll to her family. But then she realized that the doll didn't have any clothes on. So she began to complain. She said "Why doesn't my doll have any clothes?"

Her family was very patient with her. They said to her "Let's look for some clothes for your doll." So they went to the toy store and found a nice outfit for her doll. Hannah was so glad and gave her doll a big hug. She thanked her family for being so patient with her and showing her how to find the doll's clothes.

Hannah was very happy and went back to playing with her doll. She never complained again about the doll's clothes.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a favorite vest that he loved to wear. It was a pretty vest with many colors. He wore it all the time.

One day, it started to rain when Tim was playing outside. The rain made Tim and his vest very wet. Tim did not like being wet, so he went back inside his house. His mom saw his wet vest and told him to take it off.

Tim took off his wet vest and started to weep. He was sad because his favorite vest was wet. His mom saw him weep and hugged him. She told him not to worry, she would dry the vest. Tim felt better and played with his toys while he waited for his vest to dry.

Once there was a garden. Every day the guard would come to the garden and spray the flowers. Every flower was so proud, standing tall and happy in the sunshine. The guard was proud of his work, he enjoyed making the garden look pretty.

One day a butterfly flew over the garden. It was a big and colourful butterfly, flying gracefully around the flowers. It was so beautiful that the guard just watched in awe. He was very proud that he had made such a lovely garden.

The guard continued to spray the garden every day, taking extra time to make the flowers look even more beautiful. Soon more and more animals came to the garden. Rabbits, birds and butterflies all fluttered around, taking in the beauty of the garden. The guard smiled, he was so proud of his work.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they find a big gray hat in the closet. It is their dad's hat. Ben wants to wear the hat. He puts it on his head. He says, "Look at me! I am a big man!"

Sam wants to wear the hat too. He says, "No, Ben! It is my turn! Give me the hat!" He tries to pull the hat from Ben's head. Ben holds the hat tight. He says, "No, Sam! It is mine! Go away!"

They start to fight. They push and pull and shout. The hat falls to the floor. They both run to get it. They bump their heads. They cry.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the closet. She sees the hat and the boys. She says, "What are you doing? Why are you fighting? This is not your hat. This is dad's hat. You should not take his things without asking. You should share and be nice."

She picks up the hat. She puts it on her head. She says, "Now, I am a big man!" She smiles. The boys stop crying. They laugh. They say, "No, mom! You are a big woman! You are funny!"

Mom hugs the boys. She says, "I love you, Ben and Sam. You are my big boys. But you are still little. You have a lot to learn and gain. Now, let's put the hat back and play something else."

One day, a powerful ant named Tim found an umbrella. He knew this umbrella was special. Tim had a plan. He wanted to show his friends how strong he was. So, he decided to carry the umbrella to the top of a big hill.

Tim started to walk up the hill. It was hard work, but he did not give up. He knew his friends would be very happy to see him at the top. As he walked, he saw a little bug named Sam. Sam was sad because he could not pinch. Tim wanted to help Sam.

Tim said, "Sam, you can use my umbrella to learn how to pinch." Sam was very happy. He tried to pinch the umbrella and after some time, he could do it. Sam thanked Tim for helping him.

Tim continued to walk up the hill. When he reached the top, his friends were waiting. They were so proud of Tim. They clapped and cheered. Tim was happy he could help Sam and show his friends how powerful he was.

From that day on, Tim and Sam were best friends. They played together and helped each other. The umbrella was always with them, reminding them of the day they became friends.

Once upon a time, there was a wrap. It was orange and it was special.

Mommy went to the closet and put the wrap inside. Then she held the wrap up and told me to close my eyes.

When I opened them again, Mommy had put the wrap around me. It was so orange and warm and comfy. I smiled and laughed.

Mommy smiled too. She hugged me and said "You look just like a little present" Then she gave me a kiss.

I was so happy. I was wearing the orange wrap just like I wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jack. He was very excited because he was at the beach with his mom.

The sun was shining and the sea was very calm. Jack saw a big, blue wave rolling in and asked, "Mom, can I go and play?"

Mama nodded, "Yes, be careful. Have fun!"

Jack hopped on the sand and danced, spinning and twirling around on his toes. He laughed as the wind blew through his hair, like a big hug.

Then, he heard something. Jack turned and saw a pretty, pink kite flying above him. He waved at it and shouted, "Hi!"

The kite spun in circles above Jack's head. He smiled and felt so happy, like he was dancing in the sky.

Jack and the kite played together all afternoon. They spun together, over the sea and the smooth sand.

"Bye-bye kite," Jack waved as the sun went down and it was time to go home.

The kite waved back, spinning one last time. Then it flew away, taking all of Jack's happy memories with it.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who loved to play together - Alex and his pet dog, Spot. One day, Alex brought a metal toy car to play with. He put it down and started playing, but Spot got too excited and SNAP - the metal car broke. Alex got worried and started to panic.

"Spot, why did you break my toy?" Alex asked with a sad voice.

Spot whimpered and curled up with his tail between his legs. He knew he had done something wrong.

Alex was still worried, but he knew he had to forgive Spot. He gave his furry friend a big hug and said, "It's ok, I still love you Spot".

Spot was so happy that he started jumping up and down, and the two best friends went back to playing and having fun together.

Jill and Jack were siblings who were often impatient with each other. They were in the park one day, playing together.

Jill saw a swing and she wanted to swing. She asked Jack to push her but he said no. Jill became very impatient and began to cry.

Jack then saw an old car on the other side of the park. He ran over to the car, forgetting all about Jill. But Jill followed him and shouted for him to come back.

Finally Jack got to the car, and he knew he should help Jill. He went back to the swing and started to push Jill. She laughed and smiled.

Jack then saw an old tree nearby. He ran to the tree and started to climb. He asked Jill to climb with him but when she said no, Jack got impatient.

Jack then saw a bush that he wanted to explore. He ran over to the bush and started poking through the leaves. But Jill yelled at him to come back.

Jack came back and he and Jill decided to end their day of play. As they walked home, they held hands and laughed. It was a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play with her toys and her dog, Max. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk in the park. They saw a monster! The monster was big and scary. Lily pointed at the monster and said, "Look, Max! A monster!" Max barked at the monster, but the monster didn't move.

Lily thought about what to do. She remembered that her mom told her to be independent and brave. So, Lily took a deep breath and walked up to the monster. She saw that the monster was sad and lonely. Lily decided to be the monster's friend. She played with the monster and showed him her toys. The monster was happy and no longer scary.

From that day on, Lily and the monster played together in the park. Max also became friends with the monster. Lily learned that sometimes things that seem scary are actually friendly and nice.

Once upon a time, there was a bossy flower. Every day, the flower would stand tall and expect everyone to look at her. She was proud of her beautiful petals, which bloomed in all sorts of colours.

One day, the wind started to blow. The flower felt excited - she loved when the wind blew! Before she knew it, a wave had carried her away. Soon, the flower was floating in the air, high above the ground.

The flower drifted and floated, until finally the wave carried her very far away. Soon, the flower saw a large, sparkling lake. The wave carried her right up to the shore and dropped her softly onto the ground.

The flower was happy to see the lake - it was so pretty! The sun made the water sparkle and she felt like she was in a magical place. From that day on, the flower stayed near the lake, so she could enjoy its beauty.

And every day, the bossy flower would bloom in joy, to show her appreciation for this special place.

Once there was a small fish. It swam in the pond and had a lot of fun. The fish loved to splash and jump out of the water. One day, it saw a square on the surface of the water. It was gentle and it moved around gracefully. The fish was curious, so it jumped out of the water to take a closer look.

When it got close to the square, the fish found out it was actually a big leaf. As the fish was swimming around the leaf, it splashed it with its fins and made it move around. The gentle leaf made waves in the pond and the fish had even more fun.

In the end, the little fish and the leaf became friends. They would splash and play around the pond together every day. It was the best game in the world!

Once there was a boy and his name was Tom. He had a staff that a very special staff. He knew it was special because it could fit anyplace.
Tom went to the park to show off his special staff. While he was there he saw a fake staff. It looked just like his but it was made of plastic. Tom grabbed his staff and said, "That staff is not real! Mine is special and it fits the best!".
Tom showed the other kids how his staff was the best. He could fit it around a tree, he could even fit it through the playground bars! Everyone was amazed by Tom's special staff and that's how he knew it was the best.

Once there was a girl who was three years old. She was scared of the dark, but she wanted to peek at the big tree in the living room. She crept ever so softly so that no one would hear her.

When she reached the tree she looked up and saw a beautiful ornament. It was so shiny and sparkly. She was scared to touch it, but could not resist its beauty. She reached up and grabbed it ever so carefully.

The ornament was so light and felt nice in her hands. Suddenly, the lights turned on and the girl got scared. She quickly put back the ornament and ran out of the living room. She was so scared she never tried to peek at the tree again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a black cat named Midnight. One day, while playing outside, Lily saw a butterfly. "Look, Mommy! I see a butterfly!" she exclaimed.

Her mommy said, "Yes, Lily, it's beautiful. If you catch it, I'll give you a reward."

Lily ran after the butterfly, but it was too fast. She was sad that she couldn't catch it. Midnight saw her sad face and meowed, "Don't worry, Lily. I'll help you catch the butterfly."

Together, Lily and Midnight caught the butterfly and brought it to her mommy. "Good job, Lily and Midnight! You caught the butterfly, so here's your reward," said her mommy, giving her a piece of candy. Lily was happy and hugged Midnight.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Bob. Bob went to check his mailbox and found a big envelope inside. He opened it and saw a letter from the bank. The letter said he owed them a lot of money.

Bob started to panic and didn't know what to do. He went to his friend, Timmy, and showed him the letter. Timmy said, "Don't worry, we can help you. Let's call the bank and ask for help."

Bob felt better and they called the bank. The bank explained everything to them and they made a plan to pay the money back slowly. Bob was happy and thanked Timmy for his help.

Once upon a time, there was a brilliant girl. She had a shiny glove. One day, the glove flew away. So the girl went to rescue it.

The glove flew higher and higher until it was stuck in a tree. The girl was so sad. But then she had an idea! She found a ladder and reached for the glove.

The girl was so brave. She grabbed the glove with one hand and the ladder with the other until she touched the ground. She was so happy and shouted, "I rescued my glove!"

The girl hugged her glove and danced with joy. Everyone around her was so happy to see her rescue. From then on, they called the girl the Brilliant Glove Rescuer!

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Zoom. Zoom loved to go fast. One day, Zoom went to the park to play with his friend, a big tree.

Zoom and the tree liked to play a game. The tree would shake its leaves, and Zoom would try to dry them with his wind. "Zoom, can you dry my leaves today?" the tree asked. "Yes, I can!" said Zoom. So, Zoom went very fast around the tree, making a lot of wind. The leaves became dry, and the tree was happy.

After playing, Zoom was hungry. He saw a delicious apple on the ground. Zoom picked up the apple with his little door and ate it. "Yum, this is delicious!" said Zoom. The tree smiled, happy to see his friend enjoy the apple. And they played together until the sun went down.

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She put her favourite toy bear in her bag and set off.

Then she saw a big mountain and wanted to climb it. She was trying very hard but it was difficult. She felt a bit scared, so she yelled out "Help!"

Suddenly her mummy was there, and the girl was embarrassed that she had made so much noise! Her mummy said it was alright and gave her a hand up the mountain.

The girl made it to the top and when she looked in her bag, she saw her favourite toy bear was gone. She yelled out "No!" and was very sad. But then, she looked down the mountain and saw her mum. She had her bear!

The girl was so happy and waved at her mummy. Together, they went home and the girl never forgot the adventure she had gone on.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go on a trip with her family, so she packed her luggage. Her mom said, "Lily, don't forget to pack your favorite dress."

Lily replied, "I already did, Mommy! Can we go now?"

They went to the airport to catch their flight, but there was a problem. The flight was delayed. Lily got bored and said, "Mommy, can we bake cookies while we wait?"

Her mom said, "That's a great idea, Lily! Let's go buy some cookie dough."

They bought the cookie dough and baked cookies together. They became so popular that other people in the airport wanted to try them too. But they didn't have enough cookies to share with everyone. Lily felt sad that they couldn't share with everyone, but her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can always bake more cookies next time."

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bob and Betty. They were playing hide and seek and Bob was the one counting.

Betty was hiding very well, behind an ancient tree. Suddenly, Bob heard a funny noise coming from behind the tree. He got closer and saw there was an ancient player attached to the tree.

Bob asked: "What is that thing attached to the tree?".

Betty replied: "It's an ancient player. I found it on my walk today and I thought it would be nice to attach it to the tree".

Bob smiled and said: "Cool! Let's play some music".

So, Bob and Betty began to play music from the ancient player, much to the delight of the birds in the trees around them.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny baby who went on a big adventure. He wanted to go on a journey to explore the world and discover something new.

The baby brought with him a few of his toys and headed out. Along the way, he saw an ancient garden. He couldn't believe his eyes! He went into the garden and started to gather the things he found there.

"These are so exciting!" the baby squeaked.

Suddenly, he heard a voice coming from behind him. It was an old, wise owl.

"What are you collecting, little one?" the owl asked.

The baby was so surprised that he dropped his toys.

"I am gathering rocks and sticks," he said, feeling proud.

The wise owl smiled. "That is a very special thing you are doing. You will have lots of fun with those things".

The baby was so happy and thanked the wise owl before packing his treasures and continuing his journey.

As he went along, the baby realised he had learnt something amazing. He had learnt that even the simplest things can be special and ancient!

Jimmy was so lucky! He had a new friend named Sammy. One day they went on a special adventure. Sammy asked to go to the ice cream store. So they went and they had fun choosing flavors.

At the store, Jimmy said, "I want to order vanilla!" So Sammy said, "Okay, let's do it!" They ordered the vanilla ice cream and two spoons.

When they had finished eating, Jimmy said, "You're the best friend ever, Sammy!" Sammy smiled and said, "You're lucky for having such a great friend!"

They both laughed together. It was a lucky day after all!

Once upon a time there was a boy who was very hungry. He looked in his cupboard and saw a cauliflower. He loved cauliflower and he was very happy.

The boy called his mom so she could help him prepare it. Mom came over and boiled the cauliflower. It smelled really nice.

They added cheese and made a yummy dish. The boy was so excited. He gobbled up the cauliflower and it was so tasty.

The boy was no longer hungry, so he went outside to play in the sun with his friends. He called out to them "Come play with me!"

Everyone had so much fun playing together. The boy and his friends went home with big smiles on their faces. The boy was very happy to have eaten a delicious cauliflower dish.

Lily liked to wander in the park. She saw many things: trees, flowers, birds, dogs. She liked to say hello to them. One day, she saw a big tunnel. It was dark and long. She wanted to see what was inside.

She walked into the tunnel. It was cold and quiet. She could not see much. She heard a noise. It was a train. It was coming fast. Lily was scared. She ran out of the tunnel. She looked for her mom.

Her mom was busy. She was talking on the phone. She did not see Lily. Lily cried. She wanted her mom. She did not like the tunnel. She did not like the train. She wanted to go home.

A man saw Lily. He was kind. He asked her what was wrong. He helped her find her mom. He told her not to wander in the tunnel. He said it was dangerous. He said the train could hurt her.

Lily hugged her mom. She was happy. She said sorry. She said she would not wander in the tunnel again. She said she would stay with her mom. Her mom hugged her back. She said she loved her. She said she was glad she was safe. They went home together.

Once upon a time, there was a wise man who loved mysteries. He touched many strange things as he searched for answers. One day, he touched a big rock in the woods and a loud noise came out. The man was scared, so he ran away.

The wise man kept searching, but soon he forgot all about the big rock. He spent weeks searching for new mysteries. He thought he was so clever, but soon he found out he was wrong.

One day, he touched something he shouldn't have touched. It was too late, because all the mysterious things in his life had gone. He looked around, but he couldn't find anymore mysteries. He had touched one too many and it was a bad mistake.

The wise man was sad and lonely, knowing he would never find the mysteries he wanted. He had never felt so foolish in all his life. But there is a lesson in this story: never touch the things that are mysterious!

Tom and Anna are having lunch with Mom and Dad. They have soup and bread and cheese. Tom likes soup, but Anna does not. She makes a face and pushes her bowl away.

"Anna, you have to eat your soup. It is good for you," Mom says.

"I don't like soup. It is hot and wet and yucky," Anna says.

"Look, Anna, you can use your fork to eat the cheese. Cheese is yummy and soft and yellow," Dad says. He shows Anna how to cut the cheese with his fork.

Anna looks at Dad's fork. It is big and shiny and has four teeth. She likes Dad's fork. She reaches for it, but Dad stops her.

"No, Anna, this is my fork. You have your own fork. It is smaller and easier for you to hold," Dad says. He gives Anna her fork. It is not as big or shiny as Dad's fork. It has three teeth and a pink handle.

Anna looks at her fork. She does not like her fork. It is small and dull and has a silly color. She throws her fork on the floor and cries.

"Anna, that is not nice. You have to pick up your fork and say sorry," Mom says.

Anna does not want to pick up her fork or say sorry. She is angry and sad. She wants a big fork like Dad's. She thinks it is not fair.

Tom looks at Anna. He feels sorry for her. He likes his sister, even when she is silly. He has an idea. He picks up his fork and gives it to Anna.

"Here, Anna, you can have my fork. It is big and shiny and has four teeth, like Dad's. I don't mind. I can use my spoon to eat my soup," Tom says.

Anna looks at Tom's fork. She is surprised and happy. She takes Tom's fork and smiles.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. I am sorry I was mean," Anna says.

Mom and Dad look at Tom and Anna. They are proud and happy. They hug their children and praise them.

"That was very kind of you, Tom. You are a good sharer. And that was very nice of you, Anna. You are a good apologizer. We love you both very much," Mom and Dad say.

Tom and Anna hug Mom and Dad back. They love them too. They eat their lunch with their forks and spoons. They are a happy family.

The boy was very glad. He was going for a walk by the creek. He had his recorder with him. He was so excited!

He stopped in one spot and looked around. He heard the birds chirping in the trees and the water lapping against the creek's banks. He listened to the sounds and then started to record them.

He played back the recording to see how it sounded. He couldn't believe how it sounded; it was like he was really there! He recorded some more sounds, and then he decided to walk a little further. He was very glad.

As he walked, he recorded the sounds of the creek, the bird's chirps and the rustling of the leaves in the wind. He was so happy, he kept on recording until his recorder ran out of batteries.

But even after his recorder ran out of power, he still remembered the wonderful sounds of nature. He was so glad that he got to record it all.

Once there was a little girl who went for a walk in the woods. She saw an owl perched on a branch and felt curious. She went closer to the owl and examined it. The owl looked back at her with its big eyes. The girl thought it was so interesting and smiled.

Suddenly, the owl moved and the girl backed away. The owl left a present behind which was something gross and disgusting. The girl wrinkled her nose in disgust.

The girl touched the present with her finger and it made a squishing sound. She quickly wiped her finger on her pants and backed away from the present.

The girl wanted to see the owl again so she kept examining the area where it had been. But the owl was nowhere to be seen.

John was running in the park with his mom. He saw a huge plate. He thought it was very strange. He wondered why there was a plate in the park.

John's mom asked him, "Do you want to touch it?" He shook his head yes and ran over to the plate.

John touched the plate and it made a loud noise. It scared him and he ran back to his mom. His mom laughed and said, "Let's see if something else happened."

John and his mom ran back over to the plate and saw that there was now a big pile of cookies.

John was very excited! He ran over to the plate, and starting eating the cookies. He was so happy he had found such a huge plate of cookies.

Jack was a young kid who enjoyed wild adventures. He dreamed of travelling the world and seeing all the cool places he had read about in his books.

One day, Jack decided he was going to fulfil his dream and go explore the world. He got a map from his mum and loaded his backpack with all the supplies he would need for his journey.
