Once upon a time, there was a big lion. The lion was very powerful and strong. He lived in a jungle with his friends. One day, the lion decided to lead his friends to a new place. They walked and walked until it was noon.

The sun was shining bright and they were all very tired. The lion saw a big tree and told his friends to rest under it. They all sat down and had some food. The lion was happy that he was able to lead his friends to a safe place.

After they rested, the lion led his friends to a river where they could drink water and play. They all had fun and enjoyed their day. From that day on, the lion became the leader of their group and they all followed him wherever he went.

Little Sammy was walking in the garden one day. He noticed a wide sunflower and smiled. He took a deep breath and said to it, "Hello sunflower. I surrender to you." He ran his hands through its petals and admired its beauty.

Suddenly, the sunflower started to move. Sammy's eyes widened in amazement. "What are you doing?" He asked curiously.

The sunflower said, "I'm surrendering right back to you." Sammy laughed and ran around the garden. He was so excited.

Every day Sammy ran to the garden to see the wide sunflower. They shared stories, laughed, and enjoyed each other's company. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old. She loved to explore and dreamed of far off places.

One day, she found an interesting symbol in the grass. She touched it and it glowed a bright yellow. Suddenly, all of Lucyâ€™s dreams felt possible.

Lucy asked her mom, â€œWhat is this?â€ But mom just ignored her and walked away. Lucy felt confused and sad.

So she decided to explore some more. She found a delicious-looking fruit tree. She begged her mom to let her pick one of the tasty fruits. Again, mom ignored her.

That night, Lucy was so sad and lonely. She was also very disappointed that her mom kept on ignoring her and wouldn't let her have the tasty fruit.

The next day, Lucy never mentioned the symbol or the fruit tree again. She learned that no matter how much she wanted something, sometimes her wishes would be ignored.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived an unusual barber. He loved to dress up in funny clothes while he cut hair. The people in the town liked to visit him because he made them laugh.

One day, a little boy came to the barber for a haircut. The barber was wearing a big hat and a long, colorful coat. The boy giggled as the barber danced around while cutting his hair. The boy's mom watched and smiled.

In the end, the boy had a nice haircut, and he and his mom left the barber's shop feeling happy. The unusual barber waved goodbye, and the boy knew he would come back to see him again.

Once there was a bright kitten living in a big family home. Everyone loved the kitten and took care of it.

One day, the family was having lunch together. As they ate, the mother said "This food reminds me of the fun times we all had together.â€

The little boy asked, "What do you mean, Mommy?â€

The mother smiled and said, â€œIt reminds me of the way we all took turns cuddling and playing with the kitten!â€

The little boy smiled and said, â€œOh, thatâ€™s right! We have such a bright and playful kitten!â€

Everyone laughed and enjoyed the reminder of the fun times with their kitten.

Tommy was terrible at sawing wood. Every time he tried to make something with saw, it never looked quite right. He wanted to improve his sawing skills. So he asked Papa to help.

Papa showed Tommy how to carefully hold the saw and make the right shapes. Tommy practiced every day, and soon he was sawing much better.

Tommy was so proud of himself for improving. He started to make lots of different things with his saw. He made wooden dolls and toys. He made little tables and chairs. All his friends and family said how much better his sawing had become.

When Tommy saw what he had created with his saw, he knew that he had improved a lot. It made him feel really happy. He knew he had worked really hard and now everything he made with his saw looked great!

The family was outside playing in the garden. The mother was pushing the father on the swing. The children were running and laughing.

Suddenly, the baby of the family started crying. The father ran to him and picked him up.

The little brother was jealous of all the attention the baby was getting. He started to cry too.

The mother tried to calm the little boy but he was too embarrassed to stop. He knew he was jealous and he didn't want his family to know.

The father asked, "What's wrong, my little one?"
The little brother said softly, "I was jealous of the baby getting so much attention."

The mother smiled and said, "It's okay to be jealous on occasion. What can we do to make you feel better?"

The father looked at the little boy and said, "Let's play a game of hide and seek."

The little boy smiled and nodded. He soon forgot all about his embarrassment and enjoyed playing the game with his family.

"Ready, set, go!" shouted Molly as she climbed the ladder to the top of the slide. She excitedly slid down the slide, giggling along the way.

When she reached the bottom, she looked across the park. The sun was setting, painting the sky pink and orange.

Molly spotted a curious machine near the swing set. She approached it and saw it said "mixer". Molly peered into the bowl and saw many colorful objects. She reached inside and began to play with them.

Suddenly, a voice behind her said, "Careful there, Molly. That mixer can be very clumsy." Molly spun around and saw her Nana standing there. Molly smiled, grabbed a handful of the colorful objects, and scrambled back up the ladder to the top of the slide.

"Ready, set, go!" shouted Molly again as she slid back down the slide for the second time.

Once there was a frog. He loved to sing. He opened his mouth wide every day and sang a green song. Everyone around him would stop and listen.

One morning he woke up feeling extra sleepy. He tried to sing his green song, but all he could do was yawn. He stretched out his arms, but the yawns kept coming!

He gave up trying to sing and instead decided to take a nap. He found a nice spot in the sun and yawned himself to sleep.

When he woke up, he felt much better. He opened his mouth wide and sang his green song with all his heart. Everyone around him was smiling as they sang along.

It was a special moment - one that he would never forget. And he never yawned while singing his green song ever again!

Once, there lived a boy named Alex. He was three years old and he loved to watch cartoons on TV. He felt very glad when he got to watch them.

One day, Alex and his mom decided to go to the park. As they got there, he saw many children playing and having fun. He was excited and asked his mom if he could join them.

His mom said, "Yes, you can join them and use your imagination to play." Alex listened and ran over to the children.

He started playing with everyone else. They were all pretending they were in a cartoon. Alex was so happy to be joining in the game. He used his imagination to pretend he was a character. They all had a great time.

When it was time to go home, Alex was very glad. He hugged his mom and thanked her for taking him to the park. He enjoyed playing with the other children. Alex had lots of fun and made new friends.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toy cars and trucks. They make a lot of noise and pretend they are in traffic.

"Beep beep! Move, move!" Ben says as he pushes his red truck along the floor.

"No, you move! I have a green light!" Anna says as she rolls her blue car next to him.

They both laugh and keep playing. They make turns and stops and honks. They have fun.

But then, they hear a real noise outside. It is loud and scary. They run to the window and look. They see a big fire truck with a siren and a ladder. It is rushing to a house that has smoke.

"Wow! Look at that!" Ben says.

"Is there a fire? Is someone in trouble?" Anna says.

They watch the fire truck stop and the firefighters get out. They see them spray water and climb the ladder. They hope everyone is safe.

They also see something else. Behind the fire truck, there is a small yellow car. It has a cute dog in the back seat. The dog is barking and wagging its tail. It looks happy and friendly.

"Look at the dog! It is so cute!" Anna says.

"I want to pet it! Can we go outside?" Ben says.

They ask their mom if they can go outside. She says yes, but they have to be careful and stay close. They put on their shoes and coats and run outside. They see the dog and wave to it. The dog barks and wags its tail more.

"Hi, doggy! What is your name?" Anna says.

The dog's owner sees them and smiles. She is a nice lady who lives in the house next to the one with the smoke. She says her name is Mrs. Lee and her dog's name is Sunny.

"Sunny is very friendly. Do you want to pet him?" she says.

"Yes, please!" Ben says.

They pet Sunny and he licks their faces. He is soft and warm and fluffy. They giggle and hug him. They make a new friend.

They also see the firefighters put out the fire and save the people in the house. They are brave and strong and helpful. They clap and cheer for them.

They have a big adventure. They see a lot of things. They learn a lot of words. They have a lot of fun.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the farm. One day, they see a new animal in the farm. It is a mule. A mule is like a horse, but with long ears and a different tail.

"Hello, mule!" Tom says. "What is your name?"

The mule does not answer. He looks at Tom and Sue with big eyes. He is shy.

"Can we pet you, mule?" Sue asks. She walks closer to the mule. She wants to touch his soft fur.

The mule does not like that. He kicks his legs and makes a loud noise. He runs away from Sue. He is scared.

"Ouch!" Sue says. She falls on the ground. She hurts her knee. She cries.

Tom runs to Sue. He helps her get up. He hugs her. He is sorry.

"Don't cry, Sue," Tom says. "The mule did not mean to hurt you. He is new here. He does not know us. He needs time to be our friend."

Sue stops crying. She nods. She understands.

"Maybe we can give him some food," Tom says. "Maybe he likes apples or carrots. Then he will see we are nice."

Sue smiles. She agrees.

They go to the barn. They find some apples and carrots. They take them to the mule. They put them on the ground near the mule. They wait.

The mule sees the food. He smells it. He is hungry. He walks to the food. He eats it. He likes it.

Tom and Sue watch the mule. They are happy. They see the mule's ears move. They see his tail wag. They see his eyes glow. He is happy too.

"Look, Sue," Tom says. "The mule is glowing. He likes us. He is not shy anymore."

"Look, Tom," Sue says. "The mule is coming to us. He wants to be petted. He is not scared anymore."

The mule comes to Tom and Sue. He lets them pet him. He makes a soft noise. He is friendly.

Tom and Sue pet the mule. They talk to him. They give him a name. They call him Moe.

Moe is a good mule. He likes Tom and Sue. He likes the farm. He is easy to love.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny. She was very smart and always wanted to learn new things. One day, she heard a strange noise coming from the woods. She decided to go and see what it was.

When she reached the woods, she found a trap. The trap was very big and made of metal. She tried her best to get away but she could not. She tried to run but she couldn't. She pleaded for help but no one answered.

The bunny was very scared and started crying. Suddenly, she heard a voice. The voice said that if she repeated what she heard, she would be free. She listened carefully and repeated the words. To her surprise, the trap opened!

The bunny was so happy and thanked the voice. But then the voice said something even more surprising. The voice said she was too stupid to set herself free! The bunny was very surprised and very sad. She vowed never to make the same mistake again!

Once upon a time there there was a fierce big cat called Max. He liked to take long walks in the wide forest near his home. One day, Max came across a lake. He stopped and looked around, but he couldn't see anything special. Suddenly, a voice came from the lake.

â€œMax, come here,â€ the voice said.

Max was scared and wanted to leave but he was curious, so he stepped closer. Then, he saw another fierce big cat come out of the lake. The cat said, â€œI am Ty the Water Cat. I live underwater. Come with me, Max.â€

Max didn't know what to do. He was not sure if he should take Ty's advice or not.

He thought for a moment and then he decided to take Ty's advice. He followed him into the lake.

Max was amazed by what he saw. There were lots of colourful fishes, coral reefs, and wonderful underwater plants. Ty showed Max all the amazing underwater things. It was a beautiful place, and Max had a great time.

At the end of the day, Ty said goodbye to Max and Max said goodbye. He took the long journey home with a big smile on his face. From then on, Max visited Ty in the wide lake every week.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom was making a cake and asked Lily to polish the silverware.

Lily found it difficult to hold the silverware, but she tried her best. While she was polishing, her mom asked her, "Lily, do you know what season it is outside?"

Lily looked out the window and said, "It's summer!"

"That's right," said her mom. "And in the summer, we like to eat cake with fresh fruit on top. Can you go pick some strawberries from the garden?"

Lily was excited to help and quickly ran outside to pick some strawberries. When she came back inside, her mom had finished the cake and they sat down to eat it together.

"This cake is delicious!" said Lily.

"I'm glad you like it," said her mom. "And thank you for helping me polish the silverware and pick the strawberries. You're such a good helper."

Lily smiled and felt proud of herself for being such a good helper in the kitchen.

Once upon a time, two friends, Tom and Ben, were planning an outing to the opera that evening. Tom was very excited to go and was hopeful to see all the wonderful things the opera had to offer.

Ben wasn't as optimistic as Tom. He said to Tom, "We don't have enough money for the opera. How can we see the show?"

Tom replied, "Don't worry, I have an idea. I hope we can get into the opera. I have a friend who works there. She is a generous person, I'm sure she will help us."

So, Tom and Ben walked over to the opera. When they arrived, they knocked on the door. To their surprise, the door opened and it was Tom' friend. She smiled and said, "Oh, you two wanted to go to the opera. Come in, I think I can help you."

Tom and Ben were very happy to have been welcomed into the opera. Little did they know, it was about to be one of the most incredible nights of their lives!

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max loved to dig in the dirt and play with his ball. One day, Max's owner noticed that he was feeling very tired and weak. She took him to the vet, who said that Max needed more power in his body to feel better.

Max's owner decided to give him special food that would raise his power. She also gave him lots of love and cuddles. After a few days, Max started to feel much better! He had more power to play with his ball and dig in the dirt.

But one day, Max got very dirty from digging in a filthy mud puddle. His owner didn't mind, though. She knew that even though Max was filthy, he was still her lovable dog. And Max was happy, because he got to play in the mud and feel the power of being a dog!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she found a big maze made out of green bushes. She wanted to explore it but didn't know how to get through it.

Suddenly, a modern robot appeared and said, "Hello, little girl. Do you need help getting through the maze?" Lily was surprised but happy to have found a friend. "Yes, please," she said.

The robot led the way and showed Lily how to yield to the right path. They talked and laughed as they made their way through the maze. Finally, they reached the end and Lily said, "Thank you so much, Mr. Robot. You're the best!" The robot replied, "It was my pleasure, Lily. I'm glad I could help." And with that, they said goodbye and went their separate ways.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and loved playing outside. One day, she was walking in her backyard when she heard a loud rustling in the bushes. She looked around and saw a small creature with light fur.

The little girl was excited to see a new animal. She asked, "What are you?"

The animal looked up and replied, "I'm a squirrel. I'd love some corn if you have any."

"I do have some," the little girl mentioned as she grabbed some from the basket. She put some pieces in front of the squirrel. The squirrel quickly grabbed the pieces and quickly munched away.

The little girl and the squirrel sat together, talking and munching on the corn in the warm light of the sun. That's when the little girl noticed something about the squirrel. She said, "You have the softest fur I've ever seen."

The squirrel was happy and thanked the little girl for the corn. Then it happily scampered away into the woods.

Once upon a time there was a dependable bear who loved having fun. He went on many adventures with his friends and each discovery was full of joy and surprise. One day, he found something he could not accept. His friends were scared, but the bear was brave. He thought carefully and tried to find a way to make things fun again. He worked hard and tried many things. Finally, he came up with a dependable way to solve the problem. All of the animals celebrated and had lots of fun! They thanked the bear for his hard work and accepted his solution. They all lived happily ever after. The end.

Mommy was very excited and she said, "Let's unpack!"
Mommy took out some new clothes from the box. First, she took out a new skirt. It was pink and had pretty flowers on it.
Mommy put on the skirt and said, "How do I look?" Her friend said, "You look great!"
But then a naughty boy came up and said, "That skirt looks ugly." Mommy looked very angry and said, "That was very rude!"
Mommy put her hands on her hips and said, "It's time for you to leave!" The naughty boy ran away and Mommy said, "Let's finish unpacking!"
They unpacked some more clothes and they were all happy.

The clever little girl was playing in the park. Suddenly, a boy rushed up to her.

"Hello!" said the boy with a smile.
"My name is Jeff, let's go for a jog!"

The girl gave a broad smile. She liked the idea of jogging together. So the two of them jogged around the park together.

Jeff told the girl about his favourite films. The two of them laughed and enjoyed the jog until they reached the pond. They sat down to take a break and watched the ducks swimming around. Then Jeff suggested that they watch a film together.

The girl thought it was a very clever idea. So they went back to Jeff's place and watched a funny movie together. They both laughed and enjoyed the film.

At the end of the movie, both of them said goodbye and promised to go for a jog together the next day. They were both excited for their new adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy named Spike. Spike was a lucky dinosaur with a big spike on his back. Tim and Spike were best friends. They played together every day.

One sunny day, Tim and Spike went to the park. They saw a little girl crying. Tim wanted to help her. He asked her what was wrong. The girl said she lost her toy. Tim and Spike wanted to make her feel better.

Tim offered to help the girl find her toy. The girl said thank you. Tim, Spike, and the girl looked everywhere. They were lucky because they found the toy under a big tree. The girl was so happy. Tim, Spike, and the girl played together all day long.

Mum and Dad were discussing something very important. Mum and Dad have been married for a while, so they knew all the important topics to talk about.

Dad held one of his fingers up. He was making a point, so he used his finger to explain. Dad was very delicate with his words. He was trying to make sure Mum understood what he was saying.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally loved to draw with her yellow pencil. One day, Sally went to the park to draw pictures of the flowers and trees. She sat on a bench and started to draw.

Suddenly, a boy walked up to Sally and said, "What are you drawing?" Sally said, "I'm drawing a flower. Look!" The boy looked and said, "Wow, that's pretty!" Sally smiled and said, "Thank you. Do you like my yellow pencil?" The boy said, "Yes, it's very bright."

Sally and the boy talked for a little while longer and then said goodbye. Sally continued to draw her pictures with her yellow pencil and was very happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She wanted to be successful, and to make her dream come true she had to build a special engine. The engine was very tricky and it took her a long time to figure it out.

Finally, one day she finished it, and it worked! The engine started to run, and the little girl was very happy. She hopped and danced, and thanked her engine for being so successful.

The engine ran every day and every night, and it kept the little girl's dreams alive. She was so thankful for being so successful, and she thanked her engine every day.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl and her name was Amy. She liked to go on adventures and explore new things. One day, she went outside to play with her toys. She grabbed her favorite red fork and went on her way.

She saw a butterfly and chased it around the garden. She was so happy that she followed it all the way around the tree and up to the swing set. But, just as she was about to get close, the butterfly flew away!

She heard voices coming from the park and decided to go over and see who it was. When she got there, she saw a group of kids playing with a big blue ball. They all said hi to her and asked her to join them. She smiled and said yes.

They played all sorts of fun games and laughed and smiled the whole time. At the end of the day, Amy was so happy, she ran all the way home and hugged her parents. What a fun day!

The little boy wanted to bathe, but he didn't know how. He asked his dad, "Can I bathe?" His dad said, "Yes, but you must be careful. Make sure you stay in the bathtub and don't get too wet."

The boy was excited and he started running towards the bathroom. When he reached the bathroom door, it was closed. He knocked on it and yelled, "Open the door!" His dad walked up to him and said, "No, you must wait. You can't go until I say it's okay."

The boy was disappointed and he stepped away from the door. He started to cry, but then his dad said, "It's okay. We'll take a nice bath together and I will help you."

The little boy was happy again and he ran into the bathroom. He got into the bathtub with his dad and the two of them had a nice time. When the bath was finished, the boy felt all clean and refreshed. He was happy that his dad helped him to have a nice bath.

It was a bright and sunny day, and the little birds were chirping in the trees. Everywhere, animals were waking up and getting ready to start their day.

One little squirrel was particularly excited. It was time to celebrate! He gathered up his family and some of the other animals, and all of them excitedly scampered over to the clearing near the tree.

When they arrived, the squirrels family broke open their acorns and shared them with everyone. They were sweet and delicious, and everyone had a great time eating them.

After everyone was finished, the little squirrels family taught everyone the 'Nut Shuffle'. They showed how to do the dancing steps and everyone followed along. Everyone laughed and cheered as they all danced around in a circle.

When everyone was exhausted from the Nut Shuffle, they all agreed it was one of the best celebrations ever! They had fun playing, eating, and dancing together in the harmless way of nature. All of the animals smiled in awe of the beauty of nature and its celebration of life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily found a shiny coin on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"Look what I got, Timmy! It's a coin!" said Lily.

"Wow, that's so cool! You're so strong for finding it," replied Timmy.

Lily felt proud of herself for being strong and finding the coin. She decided to save it in her piggy bank at home. From that day on, Lily always looked for coins when she played outside with her friends. She wanted to get more coins and become even stronger.

Once there was a teddy bear. He was very hairy with big eyes. He had one special thing: a watch. It was tied around his neck with a red ribbon.

One day, a little girl came over to the teddy bear's home. She saw the watch and wanted it. She tried to lift it up, but it was too heavy. She asked the bear if he could give it to her.

The bear said he was sorry, but he said he could not give it away. He said it was very special to him and he wanted to keep it.

But then the little girl said she just wanted to play with it for a little bit. She asked if he could lift it off his neck and give it to her for a few minutes.

The bear thought about it for a minute, but then he said yes. He lifted the watch off his neck, and the little girl happily took it. She played with it for a few minutes and then gave it back to him.

The little girl said goodbye and thanked the bear. The bear thanked her too, and put his watch back around his neck. He smiled, happy to have his special watch back around his neck again.

Once there was a long gorilla. Every day he loved to sing and make songs. One day he was walking through the forest and he heard two birds chirping by a tree. The gorilla stopped and listened to the birds.

The birds said, "Why don't you sing with us? The forest will be more beautiful with your cheerful songs."

The gorilla smiled and said, "I would love to! Singing is my favorite thing to do." So the three of them sang together in the forest. After a while, the birds said, "Thank you for singing with us, Gorilla. Now we can all make the forest more beautiful together."

The moral of this story is that everyone has something special to contribute, and that by working together we can make the world a brighter place.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful evening with a purple sky. All the animals outside were busy singing and playing in the sun.

However, the purple evening came to an end. As night started to fall, the animals said goodbye and went home. But then something unexpected happened!

In came a purple dragon! Everyone was scared, but the dragon was friendly. He said he was looking for some friends to include him in their games.

The animals all paused to think. Then the little squirrel said, "Let's include him!"

Everyone agreed and they all had a wonderful evening of playing together. The dragon even taught them a new game, and they had so much fun!

When the night ended, the dragon flew away. But the animals always looked forward to having the purple dragon return to their evening fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old, and was playing in her backyard one day. She was so happy and excited to be outside.

Then all of a sudden, Lucy heard a loud noise. She was very worried. She looked up to see a big bird staring at her. Lucy gulped and bowed her head. The bird kept looking at her with its beady eyes.

Lucy got scared. She ran and hid behind a tree. She stayed there for a few minutes until the bird flew away. She was relieved.

She peeked out from her hiding spot and saw something shiny on the ground. She bent down and picked it up. It was a tiny nose!

She put it back where it belonged and smiled. Then she ran inside to tell her mom about her scared, but exciting adventure.

Sara and Tom were friends who liked to play with toys. They had many toys, but they also liked to look at the screen. The screen showed them funny pictures and sounds. Sometimes they laughed and clapped at the screen.

One day, Sara and Tom found a new toy in the toy box. It was a small screen that had buttons and lights. They were curious and wanted to play with it. They took turns to press the buttons and see what happened. The screen made noises and changed colors. They were happy and excited.

But then, Sara and Tom started to argue. Sara wanted to keep the screen for herself. She said, "This is my screen. I found it first. You can't have it." Tom was angry and said, "No, this is our screen. We share it. You are not nice." They pulled and pushed the screen, trying to take it from each other.

The screen did not like this. It did not belong to Sara or Tom. It belonged to someone else. It was a gift from a kind aunt who wanted to surprise them. The screen was sad and scared. It did not want to be broken or lost. It wanted to be loved and cared for.

The screen made a loud beep and flashed a message. It said, "Please stop fighting. I am not your toy. I am a gift. Please give me back to the toy box. Thank you." Sara and Tom were surprised and ashamed. They realized they were wrong. They said sorry to each other and to the screen. They put the screen back in the toy box and hugged. They decided to play with their other toys and be cheerful and kind.

The moral of the story is: Do not fight over things that do not belong to you. Be respectful and grateful for what you have. Share and play nicely with your friends.

"Mike, what are you doing now?" his dad said.

Mike replied, "I'm playing with the lumber, Dad!"

His dad said, "But Mike, that's dangerous! You could get hurt with the saw. There are also other ways to play with the lumber, like building a fort or a house."

Mike looked down, feeling guilty. Then his dad continued, "Let me show you something that can help you play with lumber without the saw."

Mike's dad gathered up some sticks from the lumber pile and put them in a bowl. Then he added some hot water and some drops of food coloring. With a smile, he said, "Mike, watch closely and you'll see something special."

After a few minutes, the sticks began to melt in the bowl. Mike was amazed! He asked his dad, "What happened?"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her dolls and stuffed animals. One day, she found a new toy in her room. It was a bouncy ball with a fun texture. She loved how it felt in her hands.

Lily's little brother, Max, came into the room and saw the ball. He wanted to play with it too. "Can I have a turn?" he asked. Lily said yes and gave the ball to Max. He bounced it too hard and it got stuck on the ceiling. Max felt helpless and didn't know what to do.

Lily saw how sad Max was and wanted to help. She got a chair and climbed up to get the ball down. She was able to reach it and gave it back to Max. "Thank you, Lily!" Max said with a big smile. From that day on, they played with the bouncy ball together and had lots of fun.

One day, Mama took her little boy to the park. He felt so glad! Everywhere he looked he saw so many things to explore. He played on the swings and ran around the grass.

When he got tired, Mama brought out a special lunch for him. It was delicious! He ate it all up and was so content.

Before they left, Mama took her boy for a special shower. The water was warm and it felt so nice. He played and splashed and was so happy.

Finally, after he was fed and washed, they said goodbye to the park. Mama was glad she had such a fun day with her little boy. He smiled and held her hand as they walked home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was outside playing with her toys when she felt very cold. She went to her mom and said, "Mommy, I'm cold."

Her mom said, "Let's go inside and get you a warm blanket."

Lily rubbed her hands together to keep them warm as they walked inside. Once they were inside, her mom wrapped her up in a cozy blanket.

Lily felt much better, but she started to worry about her toys outside in the cold. She said to her mom, "Mommy, my toys are cold too. Can we bring them inside?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, let's go get them." Together, they went outside and brought all of Lily's toys inside where they could be warm and cozy too.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Sarah and Jack.

Sarah and Jack were always happy when they were together. One day, they were having a lovely meal under a big, shady tree. As they enjoyed their meal, Sarah said, "Oh look! There's a charming butterfly!"

Jack wanted to catch the butterfly to keep as a pet. He said, "Let's catch it!"

Sarah replied, "No, it's too beautiful to be locked up in a cage."

The two friends began to quarrel over what to do with the butterfly. Suddenly, a big gust of wind blew the butterfly away.

Sarah and Jack were sad that they couldn't catch the beautiful butterfly, but then they smiled and hugged each other. They both knew that it was best for the butterfly to stay free.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named May. She was a brave, adventurous soul and loved exploring. She had heard stories of a sailor who lived in a small boat on the nearby lake.

So one day, May asked her parents if she could go find the sailor. At first, her parents were unsure and did not allow her to go. But she was persuasive, so they eventually agreed but warned her to be careful.

May excitedly walked to the lake and found the sailor. He was wearing a big coat because it was cold. The sailor welcomed May and let her get into his boat. He told her about his adventures and let her use the oar to try and make the boat sail. Together, May and the sailor sailed around the lake for hours until it got dark.

The sailor sent May home and waved goodbye as she left. May had a wonderful day and thanked her parents for allowing her to go.

Once, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved playing in the rain. One day, when it was raining, Lucy went outside and spun around in the rain. The cool water soaked her and she laughed and twirled around.

But later, the rain stopped and it made Lucy sad. She wanted to keep playing in the rain. So Lucy stomped her feet and said, "Where is the rain?"

Then, Lucy heard a voice speaking. It said, "It's the season for rain, but now it's dull outside. Don't worry, the rains will come again soon."

Lucy smiled and waited for rain. When the rain did come again, she ran outside and spun around again in the rain. She felt so happy when she was soaked in the rain!

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a large dog with brown fur and a red bow on its neck. The dog is friendly and wags its tail.

"Hello, dog!" Anna says. "You are very pretty. Can I pet you?"

The dog nods and licks Anna's hand. Ben is scared of the dog. He hides behind a tree.

"Ben, don't be afraid," Anna says. "The dog is nice. Come and say hi."

Ben shakes his head. He does not want to go near the dog. He sees a shiny purse on the bench. The purse is pink and has flowers on it.

"Look, Anna, a purse!" Ben says. "Maybe it has something inside."

Ben runs to the bench and grabs the purse. He opens it and finds a cookie, a ball, and a whistle.

"Wow, this is a great purse!" Ben says. "I want to keep it."

The dog barks and runs after Ben. The dog wants the purse too. The dog jumps on Ben and knocks him down. The purse falls on the ground and the cookie, the ball, and the whistle roll out.

"Hey, stop it!" Ben cries. "This is my purse!"

The dog picks up the cookie with its mouth and eats it. The dog also plays with the ball and the whistle.

"Bad dog!" Ben says. "Give me back my things!"

Anna comes to help Ben. She sees a lady running towards them. The lady is wearing a blue dress and a hat. The lady is the owner of the dog and the purse.

"Spot, come here!" the lady says. "I'm sorry, kids, he took my purse. He likes to chew on things."

The lady takes the purse and the whistle from the dog. She gives the ball to Ben and the cookie to Anna.

"Here, you can have these," the lady says. "I'm sorry for the trouble. Spot is a good dog, but he is very curious."

The lady puts the bow back on the dog's neck and walks away. The dog wags its tail and says goodbye.

"Bye, dog!" Anna says. "You are very funny. Thank you for the cookie."

Ben is still angry. He does not like the dog. He does not like the ball. He wants the purse.

"Anna, let's go home," Ben says. "I don't want to play here anymore."

Anna nods and follows Ben. She likes the cookie. She likes the dog. She thinks the purse is too big for her. She is happy.

Jimmy was an really busy boy. Every day he was looking for adventure.
One day, he was outside playing when a strange big man appeared from behind a tree. He was bald, with a big red nose and a shiny nail on his finger.
Jimmy was surprised and a little scared, but the man smiled and started to talk to him. He said he was a magical man and could make special things appear just by clicking his nail.
Jimmy was so excited! The man clicked his nail and magcally, a giant ice cream appeared! Jimmy was so happy he ate the whole thing.
The magical man waved goodbye and then he was gone. Jimmy never saw him again, but he always remembered the special day.

One day, a friendly child named Tim went to the park. He saw a big bell there. Tim wanted to make the bell ring.

Tim said to his friend, Sue, "Let's ring the bell together!" Sue smiled and said, "Yes, let's do it!" They both pushed the bell very hard. The bell made a loud "ring" sound.

All the other kids in the park heard the bell ring. They came running over to see what was happening. Tim and Sue were happy to make new friends. They all played together and had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big bear. He was huge! He lived in a dark cave in the forest. One day, he got very hungry and decided to order some food. He called the nearby pizza place and ordered a large pizza with lots of cheese and pepperoni. The pizza arrived quickly and the bear was very happy. He ate the whole pizza and felt very full. After that, he went to sleep in his dark cave. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little green frog. He was happy and funny and he hopped around the meadow all day. Until one day he noticed something strange: a big, green symbol in the sky. He hopped up to get a closer look and shouted out "What's that green thing in the sky?"

Just then, a big, friendly eagle flew down from the clouds. "That's a symbol of power" he said. "It means that you can gain strength if you try hard enough."

The frog cheered excitedly. He wanted to gain strength, so he hopped around the meadow even faster than before. He practiced and practiced, and soon he felt stronger.

The green frog was so proud of himself. He hopped up high into the sky and proudly saw the green symbol still shining brilliantly. He knew he had gained strength!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old. She loved playing outside in the sunshine and running around with her furry cat.

One day, she noticed a big hairy stack of hay in the corner of her garden. She got really excited and rushed over to it. She ran her fingers through the soft hay and shouted with joy.

Then, she decided to make a hideout in the stack. She carefully moved the hay to create little nooks and crannies, and a cozy hiding place. She was so excited when she was done and couldn't wait to go hide inside her hay stack.

Just then, her cat came over and meowed. Lucy called out, "Hi kitty! I made a stack house. Do you want to come inside and play?" The cat darted inside, and Lucy quickly followed. She was so excited to explore her new secret hideaway.

The two of them curled up together in the cozy hay and stayed there for hours, filled with excitement.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jane. They were playing together in the park with their wagon. Jack wanted to pull the wagon and was so excited to play. Jane was happy too, but she said "Wait a minute! Let's delay, we should get a sparkly toy first!"

So, they went to the popular store. When they arrived, the store was full of different kinds of toys. It was so hard for them to choose just one - all the toys looked exciting! But finally, Jack chose a fire truck with red and blue colors. Jane was so excited and said "Can I play with it too?" Jack said "Yes!"

After they bought the toy, they went back to the park with the wagon. They had so much fun playing together. They even got to give their wagon a ride too.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a happy little rabbit called Fluffy. He lived in the woods on a bright, sunny day.

Fluffy loved to dance. He would hop around, spin and twirl and jump in the air. Everyone in the woods thought he was so funny, watching him dance and showing off his moves.

But one day, Fluffy was feeling a bit uncomfortable. He couldn't get his dance just right and he didn't feel happy like he usually did.

So, he decided to take a break. He found a nice, quiet spot in the woods and curled up to have a nap. Suddenly, as he was dozing off, he heard a strange sound! It was a tune and it was coming from nearby.

Fluffy hopped out of his resting spot and followed the music. As he got closer, he saw something amazing! There was a group of other rabbits dancing together!

Fluffy couldn't believe his eyes. He wanted to join in and dance with the others. So, he put on a brave face and joined the fun. He found he was able to do all the moves with the others and had a great time.

The other rabbits were so happy to have Fluffy join them and he never felt uncomfortable again. From then on, every time the sun shone, Fluffy and his new friends would dance in the woods together, having the best time ever!

Once upon a time there was a mom and a child who liked to go for walks together. One day, when they stepped outside, the mom pointed to the sky and said to the child, "Look, can you see the sun up there? It looks so good and warm." The child was amazed and asked, "What is it for?" The mom said, "It is very valuable! It gives us light and warms us. We have to take care of it."

The child was very intrigued and asked again, "What should we do to take care of it?" The mom thought for a moment and said, "We can go outside and play in the sun, it will make us feel good. And we can also cut back on things that harm the environment, so the sun will last forever."

The child smiled and said, "I love the sun!" The mom smiled too and said, "Me too, sweetheart. We must remember to value the sun always."

KING GRISLY-BEARD

A great king of a land far away in the East had a daughter who was very

beautiful, but so proud, and haughty, and conceited, that none of the

princes who came to ask her in marriage was good enough for her, and she

only made sport of them.

Once upon a time the king held a great feast, and asked thither all

her suitors; and they all sat in a row, ranged according to their

rank--kings, and princes, and dukes, and earls, and counts, and barons,

and knights. Then the princess came in, and as she passed by them she

had something spiteful to say to every one. The first was too fat: 'He's

as round as a tub,' said she. The next was too tall: 'What a maypole!'

said she. The next was too short: 'What a dumpling!' said she. The

fourth was too pale, and she called him 'Wallface.' The fifth was too

red, so she called him 'Coxcomb.' The sixth was not straight enough;

so she said he was like a green stick, that had been laid to dry over

a baker's oven. And thus she had some joke to crack upon every one: but

she laughed more than all at a good king who was there. 'Look at

him,' said she; 'his beard is like an old mop; he shall be called

Grisly-beard.' So the king got the nickname of Grisly-beard.

But the old king was very angry when he saw how his daughter behaved,

and how she ill-treated all his guests; and he vowed that, willing or

unwilling, she should marry the first man, be he prince or beggar, that

came to the door.

Two days after there came by a travelling fiddler, who began to play

under the window and beg alms; and when the king heard him, he said,

'Let him come in.' So they brought in a dirty-looking fellow; and when

he had sung before the king and the princess, he begged a boon. Then the

king said, 'You have sung so well, that I will give you my daughter for

your wife.' The princess begged and prayed; but the king said, 'I have

sworn to give you to the first comer, and I will keep my word.' So words

and tears were of no avail; the parson was sent for, and she was married

to the fiddler. When this was over the king said, 'Now get ready to

go--you must not stay here--you must travel on with your husband.'

Then the fiddler went his way, and took her with him, and they soon came

to a great wood. 'Pray,' said she, 'whose is this wood?' 'It belongs

to King Grisly-beard,' answered he; 'hadst thou taken him, all had been

thine.' 'Ah! unlucky wretch that I am!' sighed she; 'would that I had

married King Grisly-beard!' Next they came to some fine meadows. 'Whose

are these beautiful green meadows?' said she. 'They belong to King

Grisly-beard, hadst thou taken him, they had all been thine.' 'Ah!

unlucky wretch that I am!' said she; 'would that I had married King

Grisly-beard!'

Then they came to a great city. 'Whose is this noble city?' said she.

'It belongs to King Grisly-beard; hadst thou taken him, it had all been

thine.' 'Ah! wretch that I am!' sighed she; 'why did I not marry King

Grisly-beard?' 'That is no business of mine,' said the fiddler: 'why

should you wish for another husband? Am not I good enough for you?'

At last they came to a small cottage. 'What a paltry place!' said she;

'to whom does that little dirty hole belong?' Then the fiddler said,

'That is your and my house, where we are to live.' 'Where are your

servants?' cried she. 'What do we want with servants?' said he; 'you

must do for yourself whatever is to be done. Now make the fire, and put

on water and cook my supper, for I am very tired.' But the princess knew

nothing of making fires and cooking, and the fiddler was forced to help

her. When they had eaten a very scanty meal they went to bed; but the

fiddler called her up very early in the morning to clean the house. Thus

they lived for two days: and when they had eaten up all there was in the

cottage, the man said, 'Wife, we can't go on thus, spending money and

earning nothing. You must learn to weave baskets.' Then he went out and

cut willows, and brought them home, and she began to weave; but it made

her fingers very sore. 'I see this work won't do,' said he: 'try and

spin; perhaps you will do that better.' So she sat down and tried to

spin; but the threads cut her tender fingers till the blood ran. 'See

now,' said the fiddler, 'you are good for nothing; you can do no work:

what a bargain I have got! However, I'll try and set up a trade in pots

and pans, and you shall stand in the market and sell them.' 'Alas!'

sighed she, 'if any of my father's court should pass by and see me

standing in the market, how they will laugh at me!'

But her husband did not care for that, and said she must work, if she

did not wish to die of hunger. At first the trade went well; for many

people, seeing such a beautiful woman, went to buy her wares, and paid

their money without thinking of taking away the goods. They lived on

this as long as it lasted; and then her husband bought a fresh lot of

ware, and she sat herself down with it in the corner of the market; but

a drunken soldier soon came by, and rode his horse against her stall,

and broke all her goods into a thousand pieces. Then she began to cry,

and knew not what to do. 'Ah! what will become of me?' said she; 'what

will my husband say?' So she ran home and told him all. 'Who would

have thought you would have been so silly,' said he, 'as to put an

earthenware stall in the corner of the market, where everybody passes?

but let us have no more crying; I see you are not fit for this sort of

work, so I have been to the king's palace, and asked if they did not

want a kitchen-maid; and they say they will take you, and there you will

have plenty to eat.'

Thus the princess became a kitchen-maid, and helped the cook to do all

the dirtiest work; but she was allowed to carry home some of the meat

that was left, and on this they lived.

She had not been there long before she heard that the king's eldest son

was passing by, going to be married; and she went to one of the windows

and looked out. Everything was ready, and all the pomp and brightness of

the court was there. Then she bitterly grieved for the pride and folly

which had brought her so low. And the servants gave her some of the rich

meats, which she put into her basket to take home.

All on a sudden, as she was going out, in came the king's son in golden

clothes; and when he saw a beautiful woman at the door, he took her

by the hand, and said she should be his partner in the dance; but she

trembled for fear, for she saw that it was King Grisly-beard, who was

making sport of her. However, he kept fast hold, and led her in; and the

cover of the basket came off, so that the meats in it fell about. Then

everybody laughed and jeered at her; and she was so abashed, that she

wished herself a thousand feet deep in the earth. She sprang to the

door to run away; but on the steps King Grisly-beard overtook her, and

brought her back and said, 'Fear me not! I am the fiddler who has lived

with you in the hut. I brought you there because I really loved you. I

am also the soldier that overset your stall. I have done all this only

to cure you of your silly pride, and to show you the folly of your

ill-treatment of me. Now all is over: you have learnt wisdom, and it is

time to hold our marriage feast.'

Then the chamberlains came and brought her the most beautiful robes; and

her father and his whole court were there already, and welcomed her home

on her marriage. Joy was in every face and every heart. The feast was

grand; they danced and sang; all were merry; and I only wish that you

and I had been of the party.

THE WILLOW-WREN AND THE BEAR

Once in summer-time the bear and the wolf were walking in the forest,

and the bear heard a bird singing so beautifully that he said: 'Brother

wolf, what bird is it that sings so well?' 'That is the King of birds,'

said the wolf, 'before whom we must bow down.' In reality the bird was

the willow-wren. 'IF that's the case,' said the bear, 'I should very

much like to see his royal palace; come, take me thither.' 'That is not

done quite as you seem to think,' said the wolf; 'you must wait until

the Queen comes,' Soon afterwards, the Queen arrived with some food in

her beak, and the lord King came too, and they began to feed their young

ones. The bear would have liked to go at once, but the wolf held him

back by the sleeve, and said: 'No, you must wait until the lord and lady

Queen have gone away again.' So they took stock of the hole where the

nest lay, and trotted away. The bear, however, could not rest until he

had seen the royal palace, and when a short time had passed, went to it

again. The King and Queen had just flown out, so he peeped in and saw

five or six young ones lying there. 'Is that the royal palace?' cried

the bear; 'it is a wretched palace, and you are not King's children, you

are disreputable children!' When the young wrens heard that, they were

frightfully angry, and screamed: 'No, that we are not! Our parents are

honest people! Bear, you will have to pay for that!'

The bear and the wolf grew uneasy, and turned back and went into their

holes. The young willow-wrens, however, continued to cry and scream, and

when their parents again brought food they said: 'We will not so much as

touch one fly's leg, no, not if we were dying of hunger, until you have

settled whether we are respectable children or not; the bear has been

here and has insulted us!' Then the old King said: 'Be easy, he shall

be punished,' and he at once flew with the Queen to the bear's cave, and

called in: 'Old Growler, why have you insulted my children? You shall

suffer for it--we will punish you by a bloody war.' Thus war was

announced to the Bear, and all four-footed animals were summoned to take

part in it, oxen, asses, cows, deer, and every other animal the earth

contained. And the willow-wren summoned everything which flew in the

air, not only birds, large and small, but midges, and hornets, bees and

flies had to come.

When the time came for the war to begin, the willow-wren sent out spies

to discover who was the enemy's commander-in-chief. The gnat, who was

the most crafty, flew into the forest where the enemy was assembled,

and hid herself beneath a leaf of the tree where the password was to be

announced. There stood the bear, and he called the fox before him

and said: 'Fox, you are the most cunning of all animals, you shall be

general and lead us.' 'Good,' said the fox, 'but what signal shall we

agree upon?' No one knew that, so the fox said: 'I have a fine long

bushy tail, which almost looks like a plume of red feathers. When I lift

my tail up quite high, all is going well, and you must charge; but if I

let it hang down, run away as fast as you can.' When the gnat had heard

that, she flew away again, and revealed everything, down to the minutest

detail, to the willow-wren. When day broke, and the battle was to begin,

all the four-footed animals came running up with such a noise that the

earth trembled. The willow-wren with his army also came flying through

the air with such a humming, and whirring, and swarming that every one

was uneasy and afraid, and on both sides they advanced against each

other. But the willow-wren sent down the hornet, with orders to settle

beneath the fox's tail, and sting with all his might. When the fox felt

the first string, he started so that he lifted one leg, from pain, but

he bore it, and still kept his tail high in the air; at the second

sting, he was forced to put it down for a moment; at the third, he could

hold out no longer, screamed, and put his tail between his legs. When

the animals saw that, they thought all was lost, and began to flee, each

into his hole, and the birds had won the battle.

Then the King and Queen flew home to their children and cried:

'Children, rejoice, eat and drink to your heart's content, we have won

the battle!' But the young wrens said: 'We will not eat yet, the bear

must come to the nest, and beg for pardon and say that we are honourable

children, before we will do that.' Then the willow-wren flew to the

bear's hole and cried: 'Growler, you are to come to the nest to my

children, and beg their pardon, or else every rib of your body shall

be broken.' So the bear crept thither in the greatest fear, and begged

their pardon. And now at last the young wrens were satisfied, and sat

down together and ate and drank, and made merry till quite late into the

night.

"What's in that sack, Mummy?" asked Sarah.

Mummy replied, "It's full of lots of fun things that we can take with us on our trip."

Sarah asked, "Can I take my dolly?"

Mummy replied, "Yes of course, but you will have to pack it into the sack yourself."

Sarah was excited and put her dolly safely into the big sack. She looked up at her mummy and smiled.

On the trip, Sarah met lots of friendly people and things she had not seen before. She was having a wonderful time.

When it was time to go home, Sarah remembered that she had put her dolly in the sack and so she checked to make sure it was still there. It was!

Mummy said to her, "Isn't it nice when things are packed up neatly and safely?"

Sarah nodded and smiled.

The moral of the story is to be careful to always pack up things neatly and safely, which helps us to take care of our possessions.

Once there was a girl who liked to push. She pushed a toy car, she pushed a wagon and she pushed a chair. One day, she saw something that she never saw before. It was a regular symbol on the floor. She went to push it, but it didn't move. She was confused, so she asked her mum. Her mum said, "It's not something you can push, it's a symbol that means something special." She asked, "What does it mean?" Her mum smiled and said, "It's a symbol of friendship, and just passing it makes you feel good." The girl smiled because she knew it was true. She was happy that she found this special symbol of friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a clock in her room that tick-tocked all day long. One day, the clock stopped ticking and Lily didn't know what to do. She asked her mom to fix it, but her mom said it was too old and couldn't be fixed.

Lily was sad because she loved the sound of the clock. But then she had an idea! She took a smooth nap on her bed and dreamed of a new clock that would make her happy. When she woke up, her mom surprised her with a new clock that tick-tocked even louder than the old one. Lily was so happy, she hugged her mom and thanked her for the new clock. From that day on, Lily took a nap every day and dreamed of new adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. He was three years old and he was always very happy.

One day, Joe wanted to go on a big adventure. He decided to take a trip to the tip. Joe was so excited, but he was a little worried too. He was scared that the trip might be a bit boring.

So Joe decided to ask his mum for help. His mum gave him a big bag full of fun toys and she showed him the best way to get to the tip.

When Joe arrived, he was delighted to see so many fun things. There were old toys to play with and piles of cards to make. Joe played there all day and forgot all about his worries. It was the best day of his life!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, Timmy found a little hole in the ground. He looked inside and saw a mole. The mole looked sad and gloomy.

Timmy wanted to help the mole feel better. He tried to talk to the mole, but the mole didn't understand him. So, Timmy decided to open up the hole and let the mole come out. The mole was so happy to be out of the hole and in the sunshine.

Timmy and the mole became friends and played together every day. Timmy was happy to have a new friend and the mole was happy to have someone to play with. From that day on, Timmy always made sure to check on the mole and make sure he was happy.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. But they also liked to search for things. They searched for bugs, flowers and rocks. Sometimes they found something special, like a shiny coin or a feather.

One day, they saw a big hill. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side. They asked their mom if they could go. She said yes, but be careful and come back soon. Ben and Lily ran to the hill and started to climb. They used their hands and feet and helped each other.

When they reached the top, they saw a surprise. There was a big lake with ducks and fish. There was also a boat with a sail. It was red and white and looked powerful. Ben and Lily wanted to go on the boat and sail on the lake. They ran to the boat and jumped in.

"Hello, who are you?" a voice said. Ben and Lily looked around and saw a man. He was sitting on the boat and holding a rope. He looked angry. "This is my boat. You can't just come and take it. Get off now!"

Ben and Lily were scared. They did not know the man was there. They did not mean to take his boat. They just wanted to have fun. They said sorry and tried to get off. But the man was still mad. He pulled the rope and made the sail move. The boat started to move fast on the lake. Ben and Lily screamed.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. They wanted their mom. They wanted to go back to the park. They did not like the boat or the lake or the man. They wished they never climbed the hill. They wished they never saw the surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mia. She had a boo-boo on her hand and it was very sore.

Mia asked her mom for a bandage for her sore hand. Her mom said, "No, you don't need one, sweetie. It will heal on its own".

But Mia kept insisting for a bandage. "Mommy, please? Please can I have a bandage?" she asked her mother.

Finally, her mom gave in. She found a different bandage, much different than the regular ones. It had sparkles and pictures on it.

Mia was so excited and happy. She put the bandage on her sore hand and showed it off to everyone!

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bear. The bear was walking through the woods when he heard a loud snap. He looked around and saw a curtain hanging down from a branch. He was curious, so he went to see what had made the noise. There, he found a little mouse. The poor mouse had gotten its tail caught on a twig and had snapped it off. The bear was very sad, he could tell the mouse was hurt.

He looked around and found a soft leaf to wrap up the mouse's tail. He kept it safe until the mouse felt better. Then, he hung the curtain over a branch to make a cozy home for the mouse. The mouse thanked the bear and said goodbye as he scampered off into the woods. The bear was glad he was able to help the little mouse and make sure it didn't get hurt anymore.
