Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was eager to eat something yummy. The girl's mom told her a story about a very special treat. It was called a cupcake and it was said to taste like the best flavor ever.

The little girl was so eager to taste the cupcake that she begged her mom to make one. So the mom went to the kitchen and started to make the cupcake. Soon the cupcake was ready and the little girl was so excited.

The little girl took a bite of the cupcake and it tasted amazing. She closed her eyes and smiled. When she opened her eyes again, she asked her mom, "Can I have more?" Her mom laughed and said, "Of course! Go have another bite."

The little girl happily took a second bite of the cupcake and smiled. Her mom said, "I'm glad you liked the cupcake and that you enjoyed the story too!" The little girl smiled and snuggled up close to her mom. And the two of them enjoyed the story and the sweet taste of the cupcake.

Once there was a little girl named Molly. She lived in a big park with her parents. Molly was only three years old but she was always looking for something fun to do.

One day, when Molly was walking through the park, she saw something glittering in the grass. When she picked it up, she saw that it was a long chain made of silver. Molly was very excited and ran to show her parents.

Molly's mom was very sad when she saw the chain. She said to Molly, "This chain looks very sharp! You must not touch it, because it could hurt you!" Molly was sad but she didn't pick up the chain again.

Molly learnt an important lesson that day, even though it was a sad one. She was careful from then on when she found something new in the park.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sally who loved to explore. One day, she discovered a special tree that she had never seen before. The tree was covered in bright yellow and orange fruit.

"Wow!" Sally said, staring in amazement. She reached up and grabbed one of the pieces of heavy fruit and held it in her hands. She decided to take it home and tell her mum all about it.

When they got home, Sally showed the fruit to her mum.

"What is it, sweetheart?" her mum asked.

"I don't know," Sally said.

Her mum cut the fruit open and smiled. "It's a mango," she said. "It's a very special fruit. You can eat it."

Sally tasted the mango and it was delicious. She smiled and thanked her mum.

Every day afterwards, Sally would go back to the special tree and tell her mum all about what she found.

Jane had a zebra. She loved it very much. But one day, the zebra had to leave. Jane was sad and she was very embarrassed. She didn't want the zebra to go. She asked her mom why the zebra had to leave. Mom said the zebra was going to a new home, so it could make more friends. Jane felt better knowing the zebra was just going away for a little while. She said goodbye to the zebra, and wished it a safe trip.

Now, Jane remembers the zebra with fondness. She knows that it has found new friends, and is happy in its new home.

Tommy was sad when his mum stopped drying him. His eyes were upset and he wanted to stay warm. When his mum gave him a warm tube, he was happy again. He smiled as he hugged it tightly. He loved how the tube made him feel nice and dry. He felt much better after snuggling with it.

Mum was pleased that Tommy was happy again and she said that he could keep the tube. He hugged it over and over, feeling how warm and soft it was.

Later that night, Tommy was still cuddling his tube. He was having the best time, and he felt so dry! He didn't want anything to upset him again. He always felt safe and happy when he had his tube.

One day, Jack wanted to go for a jog. He put on his shoes and stepped outside. He stretched his body and started running.

He wanted to get to the park to play with his friends. As he ran, he noticed a pale meal on a bench. He stopped to have a look. It looked delicious! He began to eat the meal.

He felt so much stronger, so he continued jogging to the park. Finally, he arrived.

His friends were so excited to see him! They all ran around together, playing and having fun. Jack was so glad he had that tasty pale meal before he arrived. Now he had enough energy to play all day!

Once upon a time, there was a monkey named Max. Max lived on an island all alone. One day, Max saw some other animals playing on a different island. Max felt jealous because he wanted to play too.

Max decided to carry a big banana with him and swim to the other island. When he got there, the animals were surprised to see him. Max shared his banana with them and they all became friends.

From that day on, Max would carry bananas with him every time he swam to the other island to play with his new friends. They were no longer jealous of each other and had lots of fun together.

One sunny day, Jessi went for a walk in the forest. She saw a furry fox and asked it what it was doing. The fox didn't say anything, but it just shrugged. Jessi figured it was looking for food in the soil.

Jessi wanted to help the fox, so she opened her backpack and took out an apple. She held it out to the fox and said, "Here you go!"

The fox didn't move. Jessi wondered why, so she said, "It's okay. You can have it."

The fox still didn't move. So Jessi shrugged and said, "Well, I guess you don't want it."

The fox quickly took the apple from Jessi's hand and ran away. Jessi smiled and waved goodbye. She had made a new furry friend in the forest!

Once upon a time there was a modest building. Inside the building lived a family of four. Mama, Papa, Nick and Nora. One day the family had an argument. Mama and Papa were shouting, and Nick and Nora became very scared.

Nick and Nora felt that they needed to get out of the building. The two split up and ran out of the building. They found a big tree in a nearby park and Nick climbed it, hoping that he could get away from it all. Nora saw him and decided to join him so the two could talk.

As Nick looked around from the tree he realised that the family's argument was like a tiny drop in the world. It seemed so small compared to everything else - the sky, the trees and the sun. He asked Nora, "How can the family's argument be so big and scary when everything else is so big and peaceful?". Nora thought for a moment and then said, "Maybe it's because we are too close to it, and it's hard to see the bigger picture".

The two realised that sometimes it's better to take a few steps back and look at a situation from a broader perspective. This gave them the courage to go back inside the modest building and talk to their family.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She wanted to buy a pretty veil for her doll. She asked her mom for some money to buy it. Her mom said she had to do some chores to earn the money. Lily was persistent and did all her chores. Finally, she had enough money to buy the veil. She went to the store and found the perfect veil for her doll. She was so happy and couldn't wait to show her doll the new veil.

Anna and Ben are twins. They live in a big house in a peaceful country. They have many toys and books and games. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight.

One day, Anna and Ben want to play with the same toy. It is a red car with four wheels and a horn. Anna says, "It is my turn to play with the car. I saw it first." Ben says, "No, it is my turn. I like the car more." They pull the car from each other. They shout and cry.

Mom hears them and comes to the room. She is not happy. She says, "Why are you fighting over the car? You have so many other toys to play with. You should share and be kind to each other. You are lucky to live in a peaceful country. Some children have no toys and no home. They live in war and fear. You should be grateful and not complain."

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We love you and we love each other. We will share the car and play nicely." Mom smiles and hugs them. She says, "That's good. I love you too. Now, why don't you take the car outside and enjoy the sun and the flowers?" Anna and Ben agree. They take the car and go outside. They play with the car and have fun. They are happy and peaceful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly. She wanted to have a really fun day, so she decided to go to the park.

When she got to the park, Molly saw a big tree with lots of leaves. She also saw a letter on the ground. Molly was very excited and ran over to pick up the letter.

Molly opened the letter and saw it was from her friends. They had asked Molly to come and eat lunch with them.

Molly was so happy that her friends had invited her over. She decided to go right away.

When Molly got to her friends' house, it was very noisy. Everyone was laughing and having a good time. They all ate lunch together and had a great time! They even ate some delicious treats for dessert.

Molly had a really fun day at her friends' house. She was very glad that she had found the letter.

Once upon a time, a little birdie flew into a big city. It was very excited to see all the tall buildings and bright lights. But as it was flying, it accidentally hit a wire and got stuck. The birdie tried to fly away, but it couldn't. It was scared and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, a little girl saw the birdie and felt sad for it. She wanted to help the birdie, but she didn't know how. She asked her mom for help, and her mom urged her to be brave and try to free the birdie.

The little girl carefully untangled the birdie from the wire and set it free. The birdie flew away happily, and the little girl felt proud of herself for helping an unknown creature. From that day on, the little girl always looked out for animals in need and helped them whenever she could.

Once upon a time there was a crab named Bob. He lived in a big rock by the sea. One day, Bob was walking along the beach and he saw a little girl playing. The girl looked very happy, so Bob decided to greet her.

Bob said, "Hello!"
The girl smiled and said, "Hi there!"

Bob asked, "What are you doing?"
The girl said, "I'm looking for seashells. They are so pretty, and sweet too!"

Then Bob said, "I know of a place that has lots of seashells, right near my rock home. Would you like to come and see?"
The girl was very excited, so she said, "Yes please!"

So Bob and the girl went to Bob's rock home. Sure enough, the beach was full of pretty and sweet seashells. The girl picked up all the shells she could see and thanked Bob for finding them.

Bob said, "You're welcome! I'm glad you're happy."
The girl smiled and gave Bob a big hug.

They said goodbye and the girl ran off, clutching her shell collection close to her heart. Bob watched her go, feeling a great sense of joy. He was glad he could help make someone so happy.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Timmy. He liked to paint. But one day, something terrible happened. He got red paint on his shirt and it got very filthy.

Timmy started to cry. He was really sad about his shirt. He wanted to know how he could fix it.

Finally, his mommy came and said, "It's ok, Timmy! I can help you. You will just need to feel a bit of pain and then your shirt will be better than before.

So his mommy carefully took the shirt off Timmy and washed it. Then she put a special cleaner on it and scrubbed it until it was good as new.

Once it was all clean, she put a new shirt on Timmy and he was so happy. He was so happy he ran around with a big smile on his face. He felt like he had just painted the world.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max liked to dig holes in the yard and chase squirrels. One day, Max was playing in the yard and he found a bone. He was so excited that he started to chew it.

But then, Max swallowed the bone and it got stuck in his throat. He couldn't breathe and he started to cough. His owner took him to the vet and they did an x-ray. The x-ray showed that the bone was stuck in Max's throat and he needed surgery.

During the surgery, Max's heart stopped and the vet couldn't save him. Everyone felt guilty for not watching Max more closely. They learned that sometimes, things that seem like fun can be dangerous and it's important to stop and think before doing something.

Once upon a time there was a box. Inside it was a little bug. The bug was very anxious. He wanted to explore but he was afraid. One day the bug had an idea. He decided to zip out of the box. He raced up and down, around and around. It was so much fun! He felt so happy and free. He saw lots of things and new friends too. The bug had a wonderful time zipping about. But eventually, he decided to zip back in the box. He felt safe and loved. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was walking on the beach one day when she found a beautiful shell. She picked it up and was admiring it when suddenly a big wave came and washed the shell away.

Lucy was very sad and was about to cry, but then she heard a noise behind her. It was something big and it was coming closer! Lucy was scared.

She turned around and saw a dangerous-looking animal. She had never seen anything like it before. It had a big, sharp claw and it was snapping at her. Lucy was so scared that she ran away as fast as she could.

Luckily, she managed to get away from the dangerous animal. But from that day on, Lucy was careful when she went near the shell on the beach. She didn't want to get scared again!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play games with his friends. One day, they decided to play a game of hide and seek. Timmy was so excited to play. He found a really good hiding spot behind a big tree. He waited and waited until he heard his friends shouting, "Ready or not, here we come!"

Timmy stayed very still and quiet, but he was getting scared because he could hear his friends getting closer. He peeked out from behind the tree and saw one of his friends walking right past him. He held his breath and waited until his friend was gone.

Finally, Timmy's friends gave up looking for him and he jumped out from behind the tree shouting, "Victory!" His friends cheered and they all went to get some ice cream. Later that day, they decided to test their bravery and went on a scary rollercoaster ride. Timmy was a little scared at first, but he loved it and couldn't wait to ride it again.

Once upon a time, there was a brown dog. The dog liked to run and play in the park. One day, the dog saw a telephone on the ground. The dog picked up the telephone and started to chew on it.

Suddenly, the telephone rang and scared the dog. The dog ran away and left the telephone on the ground. A man came to the park and saw the broken telephone. He was very angry and called the police.

The police came and took the broken telephone away. The man was sad because the telephone was very important to him. The dog never came back to the park again. The end.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They were both happy and liked to play together. One day they wanted to do something special so they invited their friends to join them. Soon, a big group of happy friends had gathered.

The friends liked to hug and they all gave each other big hugs. The group was so happy. But then they noticed someone far away looking lonely. They wanted to make the person feel better so they decided to give him a big hug too.

They all ran towards him and hugged him. He was very surprised and began to smile. He felt so happy to be part of the group.

From that day on, the group was even closer and happier. They would always remember to reach out to the people who felt distant and offer them a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very obedient. Every day she would do her chores and always listen to her mum. One day, the little girl saw two boys fighting over an object. The boys were very angry and shouting at each other. She felt sad for them and wanted them to stop fighting. So, she took the object from them, and showed it to the boys. The object was very special and the boys wanted to keep it. But instead of fighting, they decided to share it. Seeing this, the little girl smiled and was very proud of them. The boys thanked her and they all went home, happy and content. The end.

Once upon a time, there were two friends - a kitten and a puppy. They were playing in the park together when the puppy stopped suddenly. He said to the kitten, "Look, do you see this perfect tree?" The kitten looked up and saw a tall tree with leaves of many colours. He nodded his head. He agreed with the puppy, the tree was perfect.

The puppy then jumped and said in a loud voice, "Let's climb the tree!" The kitten starred at the puppy and shook his head. He had never climbed a tree before and didn't think it was a good idea. But then, the puppy smiled and said, "It's be fun! I'll show you how." So, the two friends started climbing the tree together.

It was hard work, but with the puppy's help, the kitten made it to the top of the tree. He was so proud of himself and looked out over the park. He turned to the puppy and smiled. Then, they both nodded their heads in agreement - it was the perfect view.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and her dog, Max. One day, Lily and Max went to the park to play.

At the park, they saw some children playing with a ball. Lily wanted to join in, but the children said, "No, you can't play with us." Lily was sad and went to sit on a bench.

Just then, a police officer came over and asked, "What's wrong, little girl?" Lily told the police officer what happened. The police officer said, "Don't worry, I'll talk to the children."

The police officer went over to the children and spoke to them. Soon, the children invited Lily to play with them. Lily was so happy and said, "I win!" The police officer smiled and said, "That's lovely."

From that day on, Lily and Max went to the park every day to play with their new friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a proud boat. It was made of velvet, and it was very nice. One day, the boat wanted to sail. It sailed off into the seas and went on a grand adventure. It saw lots of different creatures, and went through stormy weather. It was strong, and nothing could stop it. Finally, the proud boat finished its voyage and returned to where it began, safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers who lived in the same house. The oldest brother was named Jack, and he was very proud of that. His younger brother, Jason, was a bit jealous.

One day, Jack found a funny root in the garden. He thought it looked like a face and it made him laugh. He showed it to Jason and soon both of them were laughing and having fun together.

After a while, Jason wanted the funny root for himself. He wanted it because Jack had found it first and he was jealous. Jack could see that Jason wanted the root and he decided to let him have it.

The little brothers hugged each other when Jack gave Jason the funny root, and they both laughed and laughed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with clay and create things with her hands. She would spend hours molding and shaping the clay into different shapes and objects.

One day, Lily decided to make a vase. She worked hard on it, making sure it was just the right size and shape. When she was finished, she put it in the oven to bake.

After it was done, Lily took the vase out of the oven and admired her creation. But as she looked at it, she noticed that it was very dark inside. She couldn't see the bottom of the vase at all.

Lily decided to put some flowers in the vase to brighten it up. But when she did, she realized that the dark inside of the vase made the flowers look even more beautiful. From that day on, Lily loved to create vases with dark insides, because they made everything inside them look even more special.

Sam and Lily were playing soccer in the park. They liked to kick the ball and run after it. Sometimes they would pass the ball to each other and try to score a goal.

"Pass me the ball, Lily!" Sam shouted. He was near the goal and wanted to try a shot.

Lily kicked the ball hard to Sam. But the ball was too fast and went over his head. It landed near a big tree, where a boy was sitting and reading a book.

"Hey, that's our ball!" Sam said. He ran to the tree and tried to get the ball back. But the boy did not let him. He held the ball in his arms and said, "No, this is my ball now. I found it."

"That's not fair!" Lily said. She ran to the tree too and tried to help Sam. "You did not find it, you took it. Give it back to us!"

The boy shook his head and said, "No, this is a brilliant ball. It is shiny and round and bouncy. I like it. It is mine."

Sam and Lily did not know what to do. They wanted their ball back, but the boy was bigger and stronger than them. They looked at each other and had an idea.

They both kneeled on the ground and pretended to cry. They made loud and sad noises. They said, "Please, please, give us our ball back. We love our ball. It is our favorite toy. We have nothing else to play with. Please, please, don't be mean."

The boy heard them and felt sorry for them. He did not like to see them cry. He said, "OK, OK, stop crying. Here, take your ball back. But you have to let me play with you. I have no friends to play with. Please, please, don't be mean."

Sam and Lily stopped crying and smiled. They said, "OK, OK, you can play with us. But you have to be nice and share the ball. We can all have fun together. Please, please, don't be mean."

The boy nodded and smiled too. He gave them the ball back and joined them. They all kicked the ball and ran after it. Sometimes they would pass the ball to each other and try to score a goal. They had a brilliant time.

Once there was a man called Bob. Bob liked to do naughty things. He did not listen to the rules. He sometimes skipped school and stole toys from other kids.

One day, Bob did something very naughty. He stole a car and drove it away. The police caught him and put him in jail.

In jail, Bob felt very uncomfortable. He had to stay there all day and night. He was not allowed outside and he couldn't do any of his silly activities.

But one day, Bob changed his ways. He stopped doing naughty things and followed the rules. He said sorry to everyone he had hurt.

The police were very happy with this. They agreed to set him free from jail and make his life more comfortable. They bought Bob a new house and gave him a new job.

Bob finally felt comfortable again. He made sure he followed the rules and thanked the police for helping him. He was very relieved to not have to go back to jail ever again.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys in their room. Tom is very organized. He puts his toys in boxes and labels them. He has a box for cars, a box for animals, a box for blocks and a box for ties. He likes to wear ties when he pretends to be a teacher or a doctor. Sam is not very organized. He throws his toys everywhere and mixes them up. He does not like to wear ties. He thinks they are boring and itchy.

One day, Tom and Sam are playing in their room. Tom is teaching his animals with a tie around his neck. Sam is building a tower with blocks and cars. Sam sees Tom's tie and thinks it is funny. He wants to play with it. He grabs the tie from Tom's neck and runs away. Tom is angry. He says, "That is my tie! Give it back! It belongs to me!" Sam says, "No, it is mine now! I want to play with it!" He wraps the tie around his tower and makes it look like a flag.

Tom and Sam start to fight. They pull and tug on the tie. They yell and cry. They knock over their toys and make a big mess. Their mom hears the noise and comes to their room. She sees the chaos and is not happy. She says, "What is going on here? Why are you fighting over a tie? You have so many toys to share and enjoy. You need to learn to respect each other's things and feelings. You are brothers and you should love each other." She takes the tie from them and puts it back in Tom's box. She makes them clean up their room and hug each other. She says, "Now, say you are sorry and play nicely." Tom and Sam say they are sorry and play nicely. They learn to take turns and ask before they borrow. They have fun with their toys and their ties. They are happy and so is their mom.

One day, there was a girl who wanted to play in her room. She had a big, soft carpet which was perfect for playing. She was happy.

Suddenly, she had an idea and started running around the carpet. She was having lots of fun.

As she ran around, she accidentally splashed water on the carpet. She felt embarrassed.

The girl was worried, but then she remembered something. She ran to the kitchen, grabbed a towel and started to dry the carpet.

Soon, it was all dry and she was happy again. She had learned her lesson and promised to be careful the next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little car. It was very excited for the race about to start. The car had made sure to get up early to get ready.

The car was just about to start when it saw another car. This car was very slow and kept delaying the start of the race. The slow car was only able to inch forward.

The little car was getting very impatient with the slow car. It wanted to start the race right away, but it had to be patient because the slow car could not go any faster.

Eventually, the little car and the slow car were ready, and the race began. The little car was finally able to drive as fast as it wanted and crossed the finish line first! It had been worth the delay!

Bob and Maddy were outside in the park. Bob looked up in the sky and said, "Look! Something is changing in the sky!"
Maddy looked up and said, "Wow, what is it?"
Bob said, "It looks like an opera! It is so beautiful!"
Maddy replied, "Can we get closer to it so I can see it better?"
Bob smiled and said, "Yes! Let's go. I think there are some available seats."

They ran to the opera house and found two good seats. As they watched the opera, Maddy thought it was the most wonderful thing she had ever seen. She could feel all the beautiful colours and music change as the story progressed. Bob and Maddy were both mesmerized and stayed until the end. When it was finished, they both felt so happy and thankful to have experienced it. By the time they got home, Bob and Maddy knew the opera had changed them in some special way.

Once upon a time, there was a dragon who was very shy. He lived in a deep dark cave, far away from the rest of the world. He did not like it when people came too close, so he hid away in his cave.

One day, the dragon heard something from outside. It was the sound of counting. He poked his head out of the cave to see what was happening. There was a little girl counting numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and so on!

The dragon liked the sound of the numbers, so he grew a bit braver and slowly crept out of his cave, step by step. He saw the girl and went closer. The little girl was so happy to meet the dragon, but he was still very shy.

But the dragon eventually got used to the little girl, and they became friends. Every day, the little girl would come to the cave and they would play counting numbers together. The dragon was no longer shy, and they were happy friends.

The End

On Tuesday, Tom had to dress in his best clothes. He did not like his best clothes. They were too tight and too scratchy. He wanted to wear his blue shirt and his green pants. But his mom said no. She said they had to go to a big place with many people. She said it was important.

Tom did not want to go to the big place. He wanted to stay home and play with his toys. He liked his toys. They were fun and colorful. They made him happy. But his mom said no. She said they had to go to the big place. She said it was for his dad.

Tom did not understand. He asked his mom where his dad was. He missed his dad. He had not seen him for many days. He wanted to hug him and hear his voice. But his mom said nothing. She just hugged him and cried.

They went to the big place. It was a church. There were many people. They were all dressed in black. They looked sad and quiet. Tom did not know them. He felt lonely and scared. He held his mom's hand.

They walked to the front of the church. There was a big box. It was covered with flowers. Tom saw a picture of his dad on the box. He remembered his dad. He loved his dad. He wanted to see his dad. He ran to the box. He tried to open it. He shouted, "Dad, dad, where are you?"

But the box did not open. The people gasped. The mom screamed. The priest stopped. Tom cried. He did not know. He did not know that his dad was gone. He did not know that it was his dad's funeral. He did not know that he would never see his dad again.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tom. He was young and liked to explore the world around him. Today he decided to go for a walk in the countryside. So he asked his mom if he could go outside and she said yes.

Tom began running and soon found a bush. It was quite big and it looked a bit rough. He wanted to hurry over to the bush and explore it. He ran as fast as he could and made it to the bush in no time.

Excitedly, Tom started to look around the bush. He found lots of interesting things to see. He found caterpillars and bugs, stones and leaves. But most of all he saw lots of tiny flowers in the bush.

Tom was having great fun, but soon it started getting dark. So he had to hurry back home before it got too late. He ran and ran, but eventually made it back safely.

And so Tom had a wonderful day, having explored the rough bush and seen lots of exciting things!

Once there was a farmer and a horse. The farmer wanted to weigh the horse so he could understand how much it weighed.

The farmer put the horse on the scale and it zoomed up. He was so excited to see how heavy the horse was. But then he realised the scale wasn't honest.

The farmer was sad because he couldn't trust the results. He wished he had weighed the horse properly.

The farmer was disappointed, as he will never be able to find out how much the horse weighs. He will never know if the horse is light or heavy!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. He was three years old and liked to explore outside with his parents.

When Tom opened the drain, he spotted a little gray mouse. He was so excited and wanted to get closer. He asked his mothers if he could pick the mouse up, but his mothers insisted he shouldn't and left the park with Tom.

Tom was sad, but he knew his mothers were right - it was too dangerous and it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big, pink blanket that she loved very much. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to fold the blanket and put it away in the closet. Lily didn't know how to fold it, but her mommy showed her how to do it step by step.

She felt dizzy and fell down on the carpet. Her mommy came to check on her and asked if she was okay. Lily giggled and said, "I'm okay, Mommy. I just got dizzy from spinning too much!"

Once there was a little girl named Mia. She was feeling very anxious because she saw something strange in her backyard - a tunnel!
Mia wanted to fix it and make it better.

She walked up to the tunnel and said "Let's fix it together!"

Mia started to fill up the tunnel with dirt, using her hands and a shovel. She worked really hard and was very careful not to cover up any creatures that were living there.

After she filled the tunnel up all the way, Mia stepped back and looked at her work. The tunnel was fixed! She was so proud of herself and smiled with joy.

Mia had made a big difference and was very happy. From then on, she always tried to fix things that needed help.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Pam. She was very shy and never liked to be around a lot of people.

So each day, Pam would take a walk in a special place, a field near her home. Every day when she walked in this field, she'd take a sack with her.

One day, as Pam was walking in the field, she heard something strange. It was like a horn calling out - faint noises coming from a far distance. After a while, Pam recognised the sound; it was her pet donkey, Jack.

Pam was very excited - she had been looking for Jack since the morning! She quickened her pace and soon she could see him, running and jumping in the meadow. She ran towards him and hugged him.

"You're finally here!" Pam said, relieved and happy. "Where have you been? You fit quite well in this field!"

Jack smiled and looked content. Pam was sure that from now on, this would be his favorite spot in the world!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue. They were brother and sister. They liked to play with their toys and watch television. But one day, the television was very boring. There was nothing fun to watch.

Mom told Tim and Sue to stop the quarrel. She said they could play with both the toy car and the toy doll. Tim and Sue stopped fighting and started to play together. They had fun and forgot about the boring television. They learned to share and be happy together.

Once upon a time there was a jolly little girl. She had pretty green eyes that liked to blink a lot. One day her mama said, â€œWeâ€™re going to the university today!â€ The little girl was excited and couldnâ€™t wait.

Max and his mom were walking together in the cold park. Max was balancing a stick in his hands. He was very proud of himself! His mom was impressed too.

"Wow," said Mom. "That's very impressive Max! You look so strong, balancing that stick across your body."

Max smiled, feeling proud of his skills. He wanted to show her more, so he began to balance on one foot. As he tried to steady himself, his foot slipped, and his body wobbled from side to side.

"Don't worry, Max," Mom said. "Balance takes time. You just need to practice more."

Max nodded, determined to get better. He kept practicing, and slowly his balance improved. Soon, his mom said it was time to go back home.

"Good job, Max. You are getting better and better at balancing. Keep up the good work!"

Lila and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Sometimes they found worms, or ants, or beetles. They put them in a jar and watched them.

One day, they found something different. It was gray and hard and had many legs. It did not move or make any sound. Lila and Ben thought it was dead. They put it in the jar with the other bugs.

That night, Lila and Ben left the jar on the window sill. They went to bed and dreamed of bugs. But the gray thing was not dead. It was sleeping. And when the moon came out, it woke up. It was a firefly. It had a light in its belly that could glow.

The firefly saw the other bugs in the jar. They were scared and sad. They wanted to go out and be free. The firefly felt sorry for them. It used its light to make a hole in the lid of the jar. Then it flew out and helped the other bugs escape.

Lila and Ben woke up in the morning. They looked at the jar. It was empty. They saw a hole in the lid. They wondered what happened. They looked out the window. They saw the firefly and the other bugs flying away. They saw the firefly's light glow in the sun. They smiled and waved goodbye. They learned that some bugs are not dead, but magic.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and very hot. She was so hot she had to take medicine.

The medicine made her feel better. She did not mind taking it at all. She started to feel cool and happy.

She went outside to play with her friends. They laughed and talked and had a good time. They played hide and seek and chased each other around.

Then it began to get hot again. She knew it was time to take more medicine. She did not mind at all, she was happy to take the medicine.

The medicine made her feel cool and happy again. She went out to play with her friends and have fun. She was so glad she had the medicine to keep her cool.

The End

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little girl called Daisy. Daisy loved her mummy and daddy very much, and she spent every day playing with them.

One day, Daisy went to play in the garden. While she was there, she found a beautiful crystal lying in the grass. It glittered in the sunshine and Daisy thought it was magical. She wanted to keep it for herself.

Daisy put it in her pocket and ran back to the house to show mummy and daddy. But when she got there, she saw that someone had disturbed the living room. Everything was in a mess and her parents were nowhere to be seen.

Poor Daisy started to cry. She was scared and she didn't know what had happened. She was so upset that she dropped the crystal and it made a loud noise when it hit the ground.

At that moment, the bad robbers returned to the house. The crystal made them angry and they chased Daisy out of the house.

They never saw Daisy again. Her parents were so sad that she was gone. Daisy's chubby little face never returned to the house again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fancy house. It had a big, fancy window and a big, fancy door.

One day, Johnny and his mommy were outside the house, admiring the window. Johnny's mommy said, "Johnny, how do you think we could reach the window?"

Johnny noticed a ladder, standing against the house. He pointed at it and said, "Look mommy, there's a ladder!"

So Johnny's mommy got the ladder and Johnny helped her to stand it up against the house. Then, Johnny climbed the ladder all the way to the window.

From the top of the ladder, Johnny could wave to all the people inside the house. Everyone in the house was so excited, especially when Johnny shouted out, "I can see you!"

Johnny and his mommy had a lot of fun. The fancy window stood tall, and their smiles were even higher.

Once there was a little girl named Jill. She loved to explore and find fun things. One day she was playing in the garden and came across a funny knob. She twisted and twisted the knob, not knowing what it would do.

Suddenly, her mom came out and saw her. She said, "Jill, what are you doing?" Jill replied, "I'm twisting the knob, Mommy. It's so fun!"

Her mom smiled and said, "Well, it looks like that knob is connected to the hose. Let's see what happens when you twist it!"

So, Jill twisted the knob and the hose began spraying water all over the yard! She laughed and ran around, playing in the wet grass. Her mom laughed too and declared that it was the funnest day ever!

Tim likes trains. He has many trains at home. He plays with them every day. He makes them go fast and slow. He makes them stop and go. He makes them say choo-choo.

One day, Tim goes to the park with his mom. He sees a big train on the tracks. He wants to ride the train. He asks his mom, "Can we ride the train, please?"

His mom says, "Yes, we can. But we have to wait. The train is not available now. It is busy. It will come back soon. Then we can ride it."

Tim waits with his mom. He is excited. He watches the train go by. He counts the cars. He waves to the people. He hears the whistle.

After a while, the train comes back. It stops at the station. The conductor says, "All aboard! The train is available now. Come and ride with us!"

Tim and his mom bring their tickets. They get on the train. They find a seat. They look out the window. They see the trees, the flowers, the animals, and the other trains. They enjoy the ride. Tim is happy. He loves trains.

Once upon a time, there was a big world. It was so big that nobody could see the end of it. One day, the sun came up and it was very brilliant. The trees and flowers were happy and danced in the wind.

But then, a mean dragon came and started to breathe fire. The world became dark and scary. The people were afraid and didn't know what to do. They tried to fight the dragon but it was too strong.

Just when they thought it was the end, a brave knight came and defeated the dragon. The world became bright again and everyone was happy. They thanked the knight for saving them and the world. The end.

Once upon a time there was an icy faucet. The faucet was special. Every day it splashed and giggled and sang!

One day, a little girl named Lily came to see the faucet. She had a big smile on her face.

She said to the faucet, "Hello Faucet! Let's play!"

The faucet was happy and said, "Let's do it!"

Lily and the faucet played all day, splashing and giggling and singing.

But then, something happened. Lily started to tease the faucet. She would splash him with cold water or tickle him with her fingers.

The faucet started to feel hurt and sad. He said to Lily, "Stop please! That's too icy for me!"

Lily felt sorry for making the faucet sad. She hugged the faucet and said, "I'm sorry. I won't tease you anymore."

The faucet was happy again, and from then on Lily and the faucet played gently, singing, splashing and giggling.

Sam and Sara were playing with their scooter. They raced each other around the park, laughing and having lots of fun.

"Let's go to the lake," Sam said.

So they went to the lake and Sam said, "Let's have a swim."

Sara was ready to jump in, but Sam noticed something in the water.

He said, "Look Sara, there is a big snake in the water. We can't bathe until it's gone!"

Sara was scared, but Sam knew what to do. He grabbed a stick and shouted at the snake to scare it away. The snake disappeared, but it was too late.

Sara and Sam were tired and wet and had to go home without a bath.

One day, a small boy named Tim found a penny. This penny was not like other pennies. It was unusual. It was big and shiny. Tim was very happy. He put the penny in his pocket and went to play.

While Tim was playing, he saw a big dog. The dog was nice, but it started to tremble. It was scared of something. Tim didn't know why the dog was scared. He wanted to help the dog.

Tim remembered his unusual penny. He took it out of his pocket. The dog saw the penny and stopped trembling. The dog was not scared anymore. It was happy. Tim and the dog played together all day. The unusual penny had made a new friend for Tim.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy girl called Lily. She was three years old and liked to complain about everything.

Her parents decided to buy her a violin to help her learn something new and have fun. On eager Saturday morning they presented it to her. When Lily saw it, she scowled. The violin was filthy with scratches. Lily complained and said it was useless.

Lily's parents reassured her it was an old violin and that she could repair and make it shine. They showed her how to clean it, so she started rubbing it vigorously with a cloth.

After a few minutes of hard work, the violin began to look better. Lily gasped in delight and ran to the living room to make some music. From that day on Lily learned the beautiful melodies of the violin and she was never grumpy again.

Mia was a thin girl who liked to go to the gym. One day, at the gym, she saw someone teasing her. The teasing made her very sad. She didn't know what to do.

Thanks to one of her friends, Mia found the courage to stand up and speak to the person who had teased her. She looked them in the eyes and said firmly, "Teasing is not nice".

Her words made the teasier feel ashamed. From that day on, the person stopped teasing Mia and instead hugged her and said sorry. Mia was glad that she now felt safe at the gym.

Mia's experience taught her that it's important to stand up for yourself when someone teases you.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint with her fingers and make beautiful pictures. One day, she painted a big yellow sun with a smiley face in the sky.

After painting, Lily's mommy made her some yummy toast with butter. The toast was warm and crunchy, and Lily ate it all up.

Later that day, Lily went outside to play with her friends. She saw a yellow butterfly fluttering by and tried to catch it. But the butterfly flew away, leaving Lily feeling a little sad. So, she painted a picture of the yellow butterfly to make herself feel better.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lola. She was very happy, but she was also worried. She had a bad skin rash, and it made her feel sad.

One day, Lola's mommy said she had something special for her. It was a nice smelling lotion! Lola smiled when she saw it and said "Thank you mommy!"

Lola's mommy showed her how to rub the lotion on her skin to make it feel better. She rubbed it on her red, itchy skin and it felt nice and cool.

When all the lotion was gone, Lola felt much better. She looked at her mommy and said "Thank you mommy!" again. With the lotion, she wasn't so worried anymore and she could go out and play in the sunshine.

The sun was shining in the city as Jack and his parents went for a walk. Jack laughed and smiled as he saw all the different things the city had to offer. Suddenly, his parents split up and Jack froze in shock. He was scared he wouldn't be able to find them again.

"Mommy," Jack said, his voice shaking a little.
"It's okay, Jack" his mom replied. "You can trust me." Jack and his father smiled reassuringly at him, and Jack smiled back.

Suddenly, Jack and his parents passed a big park, with lots of swings and slides. Jack wanted to have a go, but his father said they had to keep walking. Jack began to cry, not understanding why he couldn't have a go.

"I'm sorry, Jack," his father said, holding back a smile. "But we have to be careful here, okay? It's best if we just keep walking."

Jack felt sad, but he knew that his parents were looking out for him. He nodded and held on tight to his mom and dad's hands as they walked through the city. Jack felt safe knowing that he could trust his parents to watch out for him.

Once there was a little rabbit called Mary. Mary loved to play at the park every day. One day, Mary wanted to show everyone her new toy. It was a perfect yellow zipper that she had gotten the day before.

So, Mary started running to the park to show everyone her new toy. When she got there, everyone was really excited to see it. They even asked her to show them how it worked.

Mary smiled and said, "Watch this! It's so easy! All you have to do is pull the zipper."

Mary carefully pulled the zipper open and everyone was so impressed. "Wow, that's perfect!" they said.

Mary felt so proud of her zipper. She knew that it was the perfect toy to show off at the park.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Every day, her mommy would ask her to test her knowledge by asking her some questions.

Every day, Mommy would test Jane and Jane kept getting smarter and smarter. They would spend the evenings talking about the questions and the answers. It became a fun game for them and Jane would always be happy when she got the right answer.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers that had many colors and smells. They liked to touch the soft petals and the green leaves. They liked to pretend they were bees and butterflies.

One day, they saw a new flower that they had never seen before. It was big and white and had a long stem. It looked like a bell. Lily and Ben wanted to see it closer. They ran to the flower and bent down to smell it.

"Wow, it smells so sweet!" Lily said. "I wonder what it is."

"Maybe it is a magic flower," Ben said. "Maybe it can make wishes come true."

They both closed their eyes and made a wish. Lily wished for a new doll. Ben wished for a new bike. They opened their eyes and waited for their wishes to come true.

But nothing happened. The flower did not change. It did not give them anything. It only made a loud noise. It was not a flower at all. It was a trap. It was a snake that looked like a flower. It had been waiting for someone to come close. It had been waiting to bite.

The snake bit Lily and Ben on their arms. It hurt a lot. They screamed and cried. They tried to run away, but they were too slow. The snake bit them again and again. It had poison in its teeth. The poison made them feel sick and sleepy. They fell to the ground and did not get up.

The garden became gloomy. The sun hid behind the clouds. The wind blew the petals away. The other flowers did not bloom. They closed their buds and waited for the night. They were sad and scared. They had lost their friends. They had been fooled by the snake. They wished they had never seen the white flower. They wished they had never made a wish.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She decided to visit a hotel.

When she arrived, she knew something was wrong. The hotel was very disgusting. Everything was old and broken, and it smelled bad.

When she was finished, she felt much better! She then ran out of the hotel and took her adventure somewhere else.

One day, a young girl called Sarah was feeling down. She was sad that she couldn't understand all the big words in school. Her parents came to help. They said, "We will support you, Sarah".

One day, Sarah wanted to show off her new words to her friends. She took the dictionary and went to school.

When Sarah arrived to school, she noticed her friends were playing with a ball. She asked to join in. Sarah didn't know that her friends were using some of the big words she had learnt. But when the teacher heard Sarah's words, he shouted at her and told Sarah off.

Sarah was very upset. She ran away and never returned to school. The dictionary was never seen again.

Once there was an adorable little girl called Lizzie. She liked to perform different tricks and entertain her family. One day, her mom asked her to help with the chores in the kitchen. Lizzie was so excited and she ran to the dishwasher.

Lizzie jumped into the dishwasher and began to perform there. She enjoyed dancing and singing in it. But accidentally, she pressed the wrong button and suddenly, the dishwasher started spinning really fast! Lizzie was so scared that she screamed for help.

Her mom came running to the kitchen and quickly stopped the machine. She pulled out an exhausted and dizzy Lizzie. Thankfully, Lizzie was alright, but sad because she had not finished her performance.

Sara was a gifted girl who liked to paint. She had many colors and brushes and papers. She painted flowers and trees and animals and people. She was happy when she painted.

Lily and Ben were playing in the yard. They saw a big box under a tree. They ran to the box and opened it. Inside, they found many pretty things. There were dolls, cars, books, and hats.

Once there was a brave bunny who always wanted to hop higher and higher. He hopped over a large log and kept on going until he came to a tall, green hill. The bunny felt an urge to reach the top of the hill, so he hopped as fast as he could. He hopped, and hopped, and hopped some more until he reached the very peak of the hill. Then his hopped ever so slowly back down the hill until he reached the bottom. He had done it! He felt so proud and happy at what he had achieved. He knew that if he set his mind to it, he could do anything. He hopped off again into the distance, ready for his next adventure.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Youth. He was only three years old and had soft, curly hair. One day, Youth decided to go exploring. He touched every flower he came across. He touched the leaves on the trees and even the rocks he found.

Youth was so intrigued by the different textures he found. He touched the birds too, but they flew away! He saw a beautiful butterfly and he wanted to touch it's soft wings, but it was so quick that it flew away before he could catch it.

Youth kept going and eventually he found a lake. He touched the water and it felt wonderful, cool and so soft. After his long journey, Youth was tired and he fell asleep by the lake side. He dreamt about touching the butterfly and followed it all the way up to the sky.

When Youth woke up, it was already dark. He went back home and thought to himself, "Tomorrow I will come back and touch the sky!"

As she was playing, Lily saw a big field of wheat. The wheat was tall and golden. Lily wanted to touch it, so she ran towards the field. When she got there, she felt the wheat with her hands. It was smooth and soft.

Suddenly, Lily heard her dad calling her name. "Lily, it's time for dinner!" he shouted. Lily said goodbye to the wheat and ran back to her house. At dinner, Lily told her parents all about the smooth wheat she had touched. They smiled and listened to her story.

He collapsed on his bed with a big yawn. Suddenly he heard a knock on his door. He opened the door slowly and was surprised to see a young boy standing there.

Once upon a time there was a spider who wanted to join the club. The spider had heard of the club and was very excited to take part.

The spider asked the other members of the club how he could join.

Liz was a brave little girl. But today, she had a big task to do and it made her hands feel funny. They tremble, said her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy brought home a new puppy named Max. Lily was so happy to welcome Max into their family. Max was so cute and playful!

Later that day, Lily's mommy made her favorite cookies. But Lily was being naughty and didn't finish her dinner. Her mommy told her that she couldn't have any cookies because she spoiled her dinner. Lily was sad but she knew she needed to listen to her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a peaceful village where everyone was friends. They played together and helped each other. One day, a big monster came to the village. The monster was very angry and wanted to destroy everything.

The villagers were scared and didn't know what to do. But then, a little girl had an idea. She remembered that her friend had a special power to defeat monsters. So, she went to find her friend and asked for help.

Her friend agreed to help and together they went to the monster. The monster was very strong, but the girl's friend was stronger. She used her power to destroy the monster and save the village.

After the monster was gone, the villagers were happy again. They thanked the little girl and her friend for saving them. From that day on, the village was even more peaceful and everyone was even better friends.

Bella and Ben were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to make vroom and beep sounds as they drove them around. Bella had a red car and Ben had a blue one. They pretended they were racing on a big road.

But then, Ben saw something shiny on the shelf. It was a can of fuel that Dad used for his lawn mower. Ben wondered what it would do to his car. He climbed on a chair and reached for the can. He opened it and smelled it. It was strong and bad.

"Bella, look what I found!" he said. "It's fuel for cars. Maybe it will make them go faster."

Bella looked up and saw Ben with the can. She felt scared. She knew fuel was not for playing. It was dangerous. She remembered Dad telling them to never touch it.

"Ben, no!" she shouted. "Put it back! It's not for cars. It's for mowers. It can hurt you and the cars. And Mom and Dad will be mad."

But Ben did not listen. He poured some fuel on his car and on the floor. He thought it would be fun. He did not see the spark from the lamp that was near him.

Suddenly, there was a big boom and a fire. The fuel caught on fire and spread quickly. Ben and Bella screamed. They dropped their cars and ran away. The fire alarm went off and Mom and Dad came running.

They saw the fire and the can and the cars. They grabbed Ben and Bella and took them outside. They called the firemen to put out the fire. They were glad that Ben and Bella were not hurt. But they were also very angry and sad.

Ben felt guilty. He knew he had done a bad thing. He had poked the can and made a mess. He had scared Bella and Mom and Dad. He had ruined his car and the living room. He wished he had listened to Bella. He said he was sorry and hugged them. He hoped they would forgive him. He learned his lesson. He would never play with fuel again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, she found a big box and decided to hide inside it. She felt safe and happy inside her hiding spot.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom was very curious and ran around the garden with his friends. One day, Tom saw something in the garden that made him stop. It was a ghost! Tom and his friends were scared but they thought it was fun.

Clarissa was feeling very grumpy as she watched the soldiers walk by. "What's wrong?" Her mother asked. "Why don't you play with them in the garden?"

Clarissa shook her head, "No. I don't like the soldiers." But her mother smiled and said, "Maybe you'll change your mind. Come and play with them in the garden".

So Clarissa went outside. She thought about running away but everything inside her was telling her to give them a chance. As she stepped out of the house, the soldiers saw her and called her name.

Clarissa was still feeling grumpy so instead of walking toward them, she ran away and started to weep. The soldiers were startled by her reaction but they followed her anyway and finally caught up to her.

"What's wrong?" Asked one of the soldiers. Clarissa wiped her eyes and said, "I was just thinking that sometimes you have to give people a chance". And with that, the soldiers welcomed her as a friend and she learned that soldiers were not so scary after all.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was very tired and she wanted to have a nice sleep. But as she looked out of the window, she saw a lot of smoke in the sky. It was red and when she looked closer, she realised it was coming from a fire. She got very scared.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy who loved to explore. One day, he was in his garden and noticed something strange. He saw a little fuzzy creature, and the creature's voice caught his attention. The boy was so eager that he wanted to get closer to it, so he took a few steps forward.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to climb. One day, he decided to climb to the top of a mountain to get a better view. When he reached the peak, he saw a lake below him. It looked so inviting, so he decided to climb back down to the lake.

As soon as the boy got to the lake, he noticed a boat on the shore. He asked the boat, "Are you available?" The boat replied, "Yes, I am available for you to use." The boy was so excited! He couldn't wait to jump into the boat and go for a ride on the lake.

The boy took the boat out on the lake and had a wonderful time. But when he finished his ride, he noticed a sign near the shore. It said, "Take care of the boat; treat it with respect". The boy realized that it was not just available, it had been given to him to use with respect.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly and sing all day long. One day, Tweety saw a big and delicious worm on the ground. Tweety tried to catch it, but it was too fast. Tweety tried again and again, but the worm was persistent and kept escaping.

Tweety was sad and hungry, but then a wise old owl came and said, "Tweety, don't give up yet. Keep trying and you will catch the worm." Tweety gazed at the owl, and decided to follow the advice. Tweety tried again and again, and finally caught the worm!

From then on, Tweety learned that if you keep trying, you can achieve what you want. The moral of the story is to never give up and always keep trying.

Once there was an old man. He was cool. Every day he would bow down to the ground. He would bow and bow and bow. Even when he was tired, he would still bow.

Once upon a time there was a small girl named Mimi. Mimi was very brave and she wanted to do fun things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily heard a loud noise outside. She wondered what it could be.

Jill had a microphone. It belonged to her, and she could use it whenever she wanted. She liked talking into it and singing into it. She asked her mom if they could go somewhere special to use the microphone.

Tom and Anna were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with many trees. They wanted to see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Tom!" Anna said. "Maybe we can discover something new!"

They told their mom and dad what they discovered. Their mom and dad smiled and hugged them. They said they were very brave and clever. They said they had a wonderful imagination. They said they loved them very much.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Alice. Alice loved to have fun. One day, she was playing in the garden when she saw a treat fall from the sky. She couldn't believe her eyes. She ran over and picked it up.

John was out at the park with his family. He wanted to act brave, so he ran and jumped across the wooden bridge. But when he reached the other side, he felt a bit dizzy. He decided to sit and watch his brothers and sisters play. He heard his dad say something about a surprise.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Emily. She was three years old. Emily had a black microphone that she loved to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his ball, and he would roll it all around the yard. One day, Timmy's mom said to him, "Timmy, I have a surprise for you!" Timmy was so excited to hear this, he couldn't wait to find out what it was.

Mama and Papa were out walking when they saw a very tall tower. They thought it looked so tall that they couldn't even see the top. They asked a man who was bald to tell them how tall it was.

Once upon a time, there was a mysterious girl who lived in a forest. Every day she would go for long walks and discover amazing things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a big wish. She wanted to explore the ocean. She jumped up and down, and asked her mom if they could go. Her mom said yes, so they got onto a boat and sailed away.

Jack woke up feeling very restless. He was itching to go outside and explore. He pulled on his coat and ran to the door. Suddenly he saw something glowing on the ground - it was a pin! Once upon a time there was a boy named Billy. Billy was a very stubborn boy who always wanted things to go his way. He was playing in his backyard one day when he decided he wanted to build a treehouse.

Billy worked very hard. He gathered the wood and nails, and began hammering the pieces together. He kept going, even when it got tough.

Suddenly, Billy stopped. He looked at the treehouse and then at his tools. His hard work had not resulted in a treehouse.

Billy stamped his feet and said, "I'm not giving up!" He was frustrated and very stubborn.

Then he heard a voice from behind him. "Maybe I can help you." It was his dad.

Billy's dad showed him how to build a treehouse. With a few more pieces of wood and nails, they worked together and the result was a beautiful treehouse.

Billy was so proud of his treehouse and he knew that it was his hard work and stubbornness that led to the result.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max loved to eat pasta. One day, Max's friend, a little cat named Lily, came to visit him.

"Max, I want to weigh the pasta," said Lily. Max looked at her and felt ashamed. He had eaten all the pasta!

"Sorry, Lily. I ate all the pasta," Max said. Lily looked sad, but she understood. Max was a big dog and needed lots of food.

Max and Lily decided to go to the store to buy more pasta. They walked together, and Max promised not to eat all the pasta again. They bought the pasta and went back home. Max and Lily weighed the pasta and shared it. They were happy and full.

SECOND STORY

When old Mr Fox was dead, the wolf came as a suitor, and knocked at the

door, and the cat who was servant to Mrs Fox, opened it for him. The

wolf greeted her, and said:

'Good day, Mrs Cat of Kehrewit,

How comes it that alone you sit?

What are you making good?'

The cat replied:

'In milk I'm breaking bread so sweet,

Will you be my guest, and eat?'

'No, thank you, Mrs Cat,' answered the wolf. 'Is Mrs Fox not at home?'

The cat said:

'She sits upstairs in her room,

Bewailing her sorrowful doom,

Bewailing her trouble so sore,

For old Mr Fox is no more.'

The wolf answered:

'If she's in want of a husband now,

Then will it please her to step below?'

The cat runs quickly up the stair,

And lets her tail fly here and there,

Until she comes to the parlour door.

With her five gold rings at the door she knocks:

'Are you within, good Mistress Fox?

If you're in want of a husband now,

Then will it please you to step below?

Mrs Fox asked: 'Has the gentleman red stockings on, and has he a pointed

mouth?' 'No,' answered the cat. 'Then he won't do for me.'

When the wolf was gone, came a dog, a stag, a hare, a bear, a lion, and

all the beasts of the forest, one after the other. But one of the good

qualities which old Mr Fox had possessed, was always lacking, and the

cat had continually to send the suitors away. At length came a young

fox. Then Mrs Fox said: 'Has the gentleman red stockings on, and has a

little pointed mouth?' 'Yes,' said the cat, 'he has.' 'Then let him come

upstairs,' said Mrs Fox, and ordered the servant to prepare the wedding

feast.

'Sweep me the room as clean as you can,

Up with the window, fling out my old man!

For many a fine fat mouse he brought,

Yet of his wife he never thought,

But ate up every one he caught.'

Then the wedding was solemnized with young Mr Fox, and there was much

rejoicing and dancing; and if they have not left off, they are dancing

still.

One day, a little girl was walking in the park with her mom. She saw a big, round balloon in the sky. It was so blue and sparkly that she got so excited! She ran over to it without thinking twice. But then, she saw that the balloon was stuck in the tree. She frowned and looked up in frustration.

Mom saw how upset the little girl was and knew she wanted the balloon. She climbed up the tree and carefully grabbed the balloon. She gave it to her daughter. The little girl smiled, her eyes sparkling with joy. She hugged the balloon and started running in circles around the park, laughing and singing.

The little girl was having so much fun that she forgot about the balloon. Suddenly, it popped and flew away. She frowned again and watched it go away, until it became a little blue dot in the sky. She smiled and turned to her mom. She was so happy, no balloon was needed!

Lily and Tom were playing dress-up in their room. They had many clothes and hats and shoes to try on. They liked to pretend they were different people and animals. Lily put on a red dress and a big hat. She said, "I am a queen. You have to do what I say." Tom put on a blue shirt and a tie. He said, "I am a teacher. You have to learn what I teach."

They played for a long time, but then they heard their mom call them for dinner. They had to end their game and go downstairs. They started to take off their clothes and put them back in the closet. But Lily wanted to keep her hat. She said, "This is my hat. I want to wear it for dinner." Tom said, "No, you have to put it back. It is not yours. It is mom's hat. She will be mad if you take it."

They began to fight over the hat. They pulled and tugged and shouted. The hat fell to the floor. They both reached for it, but they knocked over a hanger. The hanger hit the lamp and the lamp fell down. It made a loud noise and broke. They both stopped and looked at the mess. They were scared and sorry.

Mom heard the noise and came upstairs. She saw the broken lamp and the clothes and the hat. She was not happy. She said, "What happened here? Why did you make such a mess? Why did you fight over the hat?" Lily and Tom hung their heads. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were playing dress-up and we did not want to end. We both liked the hat and we did not share. We did not mean to break the lamp."

Mom sighed and said, "I understand you were having fun, but you have to be careful and respectful. The hat is mine and you have to ask me before you use it. The lamp is ours and you have to be gentle with it. The clothes are yours and you have to put them away. Now, help me clean up this mess and then we can go for dinner. And no more fighting, okay?"

Lily and Tom nodded and said, "Okay, mom. We are sorry. We will help you. We will not fight." They picked up the clothes and the hat and the hanger. They helped mom sweep the glass and fix the lamp. They hugged mom and said, "We love you, mom. You are the best." Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily and Tom. You are the best too. Now, let's go and eat. I made your favorite soup." They went downstairs and ate their soup. They were calm and happy. They ended their day with a good night kiss.

Once there was a girl. She wanted to see the garden. She was very impatient and kept asking her mum if they could go.

One day her mum finally agreed, and the girl was so excited. She quickly put on her shoes and ran out of the house.

When she arrived in the garden, she was amazed by all the different colours. She saw bright flowers and funny insects. She even spotted a squirrel!

But the girl was so impatient that she couldn't stay in one spot for too long. She ran around, trying to explore as much of the garden as she as she could.

Finally, her mum called her back. The girl replied "Just five more minutes, please!" Her mum smiled and said "Yes, but only five!" The girl smiled and ran off to explore some more.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she was picking flowers when she saw a big, scary dog. She was very frightened and ran back to her house. Her mom asked her what was wrong and Lily told her about the dog.

Lily's mom took her outside to show her that the dog was friendly and just wanted to play. They went to the park and played with the dog. Lily was happy and not scared anymore. They played for a long time until it was time to go home. Lily's mom said, "We have to finish playing now and go home." They packed up their basket and went back to their house. Lily was happy and not scared anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a baby leopard who was afraid. He was scared of the big and mean lion that lived in the forest. He wanted to run far away and hide, but he knew he would never be able to outrun the lion. He lay down in the grass and closed his eyes, hoping the lion would go away.

Suddenly, the baby leopard felt something very hard poking him in his side; it was the lion! He opened his eyes to see the lion standing over him, and he was so scared he didn't move. The lion smiled and said, "Let me show you how strong my muscles are!" The baby leopard watched in amazement as the lion flexed his muscles and roared.

But then, something disgusting happened. The lion sat down next to the baby leopard and let out a huge belch! The baby leopard was so surprised and disgusted that he ran away as fast as he could! From then on, the baby leopard always remembered the lion's strong muscles... and his disgusting belch!

Mummy and Timmy were in the closet, looking for something. Mummy asked Timmy to pass her a hanger. Timmy refused because he wanted to pick it himself. Mummy told him that she needed the hanger, but Timmy shook his head and said no. He was being very rude.

Mummy was getting angry now. She told Timmy, "If you don't give me the hanger, you won't get any ice cream." Timmy still refused and said he wanted to pick it himself. He stomped his feet on the floor.

Mummy scolded Timmy and said, "That's not nice behaviour. You have to be polite. Give me the hanger please." Timmy looked at Mummy and said, "Okay." He reached up to the shelf, grabbed the hanger, and handed it to Mummy. Mummy smiled and gave Timmy a hug. "Thank you, my love."

Once there was a hungry bunny. He was hopping through the woods in search of something to eat. Suddenly, he stopped. He sniffed the air with his nose. What was that delicious smell?

The bunny hopped through some bushes and discovered a patch of juicy carrots! He munched on a few of the carrots and felt very happy. He hopped around the carrots and found more surprises.

The bunny discovered a juicy apple and he hopped around it, excitedly. He was so happy and so hungry, he ate the apple in a few bites. Yum!

After that, he hopped a little further. He sniffed the air with his nose and discovered a big, juicy strawberry! He hopped over to it and with one bite, he slurped it all up.

It was a great day for the hungry bunny. He had discovered lots of tasty treats and was very full. He hopped away, feeling happy and content.

One day, Alex went to the kitchen. His eyes lit up with enthusiasm when he saw a big cup of juice. Alex stared at it in delight and smiled. Then he drank some. He liked it so much he wanted some more. He asked his mom if he could have some more, and she agreed. So Alex had an even bigger cup of juice.

He was really enjoying it. His excitement increased as he drank the second cup. He finished the second cup and wanted more. Alex's mom said no, but he was so enthusiastic she could not resist his pleading. So she gave Alex a third cup of juice.

Alex was so happy he was jumping up and down with joy. He felt full after drinking three big cups of juice. He thanked his mom and went off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy mole who lived in a big field. He was a very clumsy mole, and he was always tripping over his feet.

One day, the mole's best friend, a squirrel, came over for a visit. The mole was excited and asked his friend, "What should we do?"

The squirrel answered, "Let's cover things with leaves!"

The mole thought it was a great idea, so they spent the day covering things like rocks, trees, and even a hole in the ground with colorful leaves.

When they were done, the mole was tired and said, "This is fun! Let's do it again!"

The squirrel laughed and said, "Sure, let's do it tomorrow!"

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat tuna sandwiches for lunch. One day, her mom made her a tuna sandwich, but it was cold. Lily didn't like it when her sandwich was cold because it didn't taste as good.

Her mom asked her if she understood why the sandwich was cold. Lily said "yes, it was in the fridge". Her mom smiled and said "that's right, Lily. It's important to keep our food in the fridge so it stays fresh and safe to eat."

Lily learned that sometimes her food might be cold, but it's for a good reason. From that day on, she always made sure to ask her mom if her sandwich was cold or not before taking a bite.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy. He loved to go outside and explore. One day, he was walking through a field when he spotted a point. He was very curious, so he picked it up. But when he touched it, the point started to burn! The fire was too hot and he dropped it. The point caused a big fire that spread all over the field.

The fire burned for many hours and it was hard to put out. By the time it was gone, the whole field was ruined. There was nothing left but charred earth. The boy was very sad, but he had learned an important lesson - never touch a small point if you don't know what it is.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tyler. One day, Tyler wanted to have some ice cream. So he asked his mom for some. His mom said, "Yes, you can have some ice cream!"

Tyler was so happy that he set off running to the store to buy the ice cream. His mom had to run after him!

At the store, Tyler chose the best-looking ice cream, with all the colors of the rainbow. Then he set it on the counter and waited for his mom to pay.

When they got home, Tyler was so excited to eat his ice cream. But as soon as he took a lick of it, he made a funny face - it was uncomfortable! He said, "Mom, why did you buy this?"

His mom laughed and said, "It's called frozen yogurt, not ice cream. It's good for you!" Tyler couldn't help but giggle too. Then he set the frozen yogurt off to the side and decided to wait for some real ice cream.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big ear that he liked to wiggle. One day, Timmy went to the store to sell some toys. He wanted to buy a new toy that was reliable and would make him happy.

At the store, Timmy met a nice man who wanted to buy his toys. The man said he was reliable and would always be fair. Timmy was happy because he could sell his toys and buy a new one.

As Timmy left the store, he wiggled his big ear and smiled. He was excited to play with his new toy and knew he could always trust the reliable man at the store. The end.

Once there was an angel who wanted to relax. She found a nice quiet spot, but it was very hard to find silence. Everywhere was so noisy! She tried very hard to relax and finally she closed her eyes and started to drift off.

But just then, she heard a voice.

"Are you an angel?", it said.

Startled, the angel opened her eyes and saw a little boy. He was only 3 years old, but he was smiling brightly.

The angel was curious, so she asked, "What made you think I was an angel?"

"Because," the little boy said, "angels come to make people relax. That's what my mommy tells me. When I am feeling noisy and upset, she tells me to think of an angel."

The angel smiled. "That's a good idea," she said. "When you need help to relax, just think of an angel. That will help."

The little boy nodded and said, "Thank you! Bye!." The angel waved and watched as the little boy scampered away, then she closed her eyes and relaxed.

Once upon a time, there was a big, old house with a tall chimney. The chimney was very ancient and had been there for a long time. One day, a bird flew into the chimney and got stuck inside. The bird was very scared and didn't know what to do.

Luckily, a kind man came to help the bird. He climbed up the roof and carefully released the bird from the chimney. The bird was very happy and flew away into the blue sky. The man felt proud of himself for helping the little bird and went back inside the house with a smile on his face.

Once there was a person who didn't like anything. She hated the way people looked and the way they talked. She even hated the way food tasted. It was like nothing was good enough for her.

One day she had to go somewhere fancy. She was so unhappy, she wore dark clothing and had a frown on her face. When she got there she saw that everyone was having a wonderful time. They were all dressed nicely and laughing with each other.

The person looked around at all the fancy decorations and felt even more angry. She couldn't stand it anymore and shouted, "I hate this place!"

Everyone stopped and stared at her. No one had ever seen anyone act so unpleasantly in this place. They were all a bit shocked and some of the children began to cry. The person felt a little bit bad, but still didn't want to stay. So she quickly left and never came back.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She was so excited because it was a sunny day. She raced outside to play in the sun.

The little girl saw the ice on the ground. She touched it and noticed how cold and slippery it was. She wanted to have fun with it so she decided to slide.

She said to herself, "I must be careful, I don't want to fall down." The sun shone brightly in the sky and it was so warm and inviting.
