She planted her feet firmly on the ground and pushed off. She slid on the ice and laughed with joy. She felt so happy. Her mom came out from the house and said, "Be careful my darling, you don't want to get hurt!"

The little girl smiled and said, "I am careful, look how much fun I'm having!" Then she kept on playing in the sun and sliding on the ice as the sun shone brighter and brighter.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy called Max. He loved to explore the world around him. One day, he found a mysterious match and decided to take it with him on his exploration.

Along the way, Max saw a small rabbit and asked, "Excuse me, have you seen my match?" The Rabbit replied, "No I haven't, but I could help you find it. I know a powerful wizard who could deliver it to you!"

So the Rabbit took Max to the Wizard who said, "I can help you, but first there's something I want from you" Max asked, "What is it?" The Wizard replied, "I want you to help someone in need."

Max thought about it for a moment and then decided to help a poor old woman. He helped her sweep her yard and collect firewood for the cold night ahead.

At the end of the day, Max thanked the Wizard as he handed him his match. The Wizard smiled and said, "Remember, always be kind to others and you will be rewarded. Helping those who need it is the most mysterious match of all."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old and very curious. She wanted to explore the world around her.

One day, Anna was walking through the forest when she came across an old oak tree. She stopped to look at it and noticed that the base of the tree was empty. Anna decided to take a closer look and curiously stepped inside.

She was amazed to discover that the hollow tree was filled with twinkling lights which displayed colourful images. She gasped in delight and called out to her mum, who had been walking just behind Anna.

"Mummy! Come and look!" Anna exclaimed, stretching her arm out to point to the beautiful display.

Mummy smiled, "Oh Anna, you have found a magical tree!"

Mummy had a big jar of jam. It was big and messy. Little Jack wanted the jam. He asked mum, she said no but he didn't listen. He tried to carry the jam to his bedroom but he was too little and he dropped it. The jam went everywhere. It was a big, messy mess!

Mummy was very mad. She said no more jam for Jack. Jack was very sad, but he understood why mummy was mad.

So mummy cleaned up the mess and gave Jack a big hug. She said if Jack ever wanted jam again he had to ask first. Jack said he would never try to carry the jam on his own again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie lived in a treehouse with a red roof. One day, Tweetie decided to fly to the park to play with his friends.

When Tweetie arrived at the park, he saw his friends playing on the swings. Tweetie wanted to join them, but he was afraid. "I don't know how to swing," said Tweetie. "Don't worry," said his friend, "I'll teach you how to swing gracefully."

Tweetie tried and tried, but he couldn't swing gracefully like his friend. He felt sad and wanted to quit. "I can't do it," said Tweetie. "Don't quit," said his friend, "just keep trying and you'll get better."

Tweetie listened to his friend and didn't quit. He kept trying and eventually, he learned how to swing gracefully. From that day on, Tweetie felt proud of himself and enjoyed playing with his friends at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely bear called Tabby. Tabby had no friends and felt very sad.

Every day, Tabby looked out of her chamber wishing she could find some friends to play with. One day, as Tabby was looking out at the forest, she spotted a rabbit. Tabby was so excited and quickly hopped out of her chamber. She raced up to the rabbit and asked if they could be friends.

The rabbit didn't like Tabby, so they started to tease her. Tabby felt embarrassed and ran away. She ran through the forest until she couldn't run any further.

Tabby hid in a cave and stayed there for a long time. She was so lonely. Tabby missed her chamber and wanted to go home, but she was too scared of seeing the rabbit again.

Eventually, Tabby knew she had to face the rabbit. So she bravely returned to her chamber. But the rabbit was still there. Tabby was very scared and the rabbit kept on teasing her.

Tabby was so sad and lonely, she never went back out of her chamber again.

Once there was an egg that was not happy. He argued about everything and was very disagreeable. Everyone shook their heads and said he was crazy.

One day the egg decided to take a walk around the farm. It was sunny and he felt brave. As he looked around, he saw a little goat playing in a field and he smiled. He went over to introduce himself but the goat didn't want to talk. He just frowned and disagreed with everything the egg said.

The egg became angry and yelled at the little goat, who just looked away. Then, the egg grabbed the goat and tried to shake him. The goat was frightened and began to run away. Suddenly, the egg jumped and was knocked over by a tree branch.

The poor egg lay there, motionless. Everyone ran to help him but it was too late. The crazy egg had died. The goat, feeling a little guilty but also a little relieved, ran away never to be seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little baby named Max. Max was very restless and couldn't stay still for too long. One day, Max's mom put him on the floor to play, but Max wanted to move. He started to crawl around the room, exploring every corner.

Suddenly, Max saw something shiny on the other side of the room. He wanted to see what it was, so he crawled faster and faster until he reached it. It was a toy car! Max was so happy to have found it. He played with the car for a while, but then he started to feel tired.

Max crawled back to his mom and rested in her arms. He felt safe and warm, and soon he fell asleep. From that day on, Max crawled and explored every day, always starting new adventures and discovering new things.

Sara liked to play with her dolls in the park. She had many dolls and she gave them names and clothes. She was happy when she played with her dolls.

One day, a boy came to the park. He had a big truck and he made loud noises. He said, "Vroom, vroom, crash, bang!" He drove his truck near Sara and her dolls. He did not see them and he hit them with his truck. Sara's dolls fell down and some of their clothes came off.

Sara was sad and angry. She said, "Hey, you are bad! You hurt my dolls! Go away!" The boy stopped his truck and looked at Sara. He said, "Sorry, I did not see your dolls. I like to play with my truck. It is fun and loud."

Sara said, "But your truck is not fun for me. It is loud and scary. It makes me and my dolls unhappy. You should play somewhere else." The boy said, "But I like this park. It has grass and trees and flowers. And I want to play with you. You have many dolls. They are pretty and soft. Can I play with you and your dolls?"

Sara thought for a moment. She did not like the boy's truck, but she liked the park too. And she liked to play with other children. She said, "OK, you can play with me and my dolls. But you have to be careful and gentle. And you have to be quiet. No more loud noises. Do you understand?" The boy nodded and smiled. He said, "OK, I understand. I will be careful and gentle and quiet. Thank you for letting me play with you and your dolls."

Sara and the boy played together in the park. They shared their toys and they talked and laughed. They became friends and they had fun. They learned to respect each other's feelings and preferences. They learned that playing together is better than playing alone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sabina. She loved going to the park to play with her friends. She brought her teddy bear along too.

One day, when Sabina was at the park, she saw a huge poppy in the grass. It was a beautiful poppy, with bright petals and a soft, brown centre. Sabina couldn't resist picking it.

Suddenly, a voice called out, "Don't pick that poppy! It's mine!"

Sabina looked up to see a boy standing nearby. He was holding a big basket. "That poppy belongs to me. I'm collecting poppies to make a bouquet," he said.

Sabina felt sad. She apologised to the boy and put the poppy back in the grass. "Don't worry," said the boy. "I can give you one of my poppies." He carefully tore a poppy off the stem, put it in Sabina's hand and smiled.

Sabina smiled back and thanked the boy. She ran away, clutching the brown poppy in her hand. She knew she'd treasure it forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very hungry. She saw a big stone in the middle of the playground. She wanted to eat it so she tried to pick it up. But it was too heavy.

The girl's mom saw her trying to lift the stone and ran over to prevent her from picking it up. She said, "No, don't touch it. You can't eat it, sweetheart."

The girl sulked. She was still hungry. But her mom said, "Let's go get something yummy to eat."

The little girl smiled and the two of them walked away. They went to the store and bought something delicious. The girl was happy to have something to eat.

Now she knew that big stones are too heavy to pick up and that it's not okay to eat them. She was glad her mom had been there to prevent her from trying.

Once upon a time there was a generous lady called Lola. One day, Lola went to the beach to measure the waves that were crashing against the shore. She took her measuring tape and carefully stretched it along the sand.

When Lola finished, she looked up and saw a small fish hiding under a rock nearby. She said, â€œHello there! Are you measuring the waves too?â€ The fish nodded in agreement, so Lola asked if it needed any help.

The fish replied, â€œYes, please! I'm trying to measure how far the waves go under this rock.â€ So Lola took out her measuring tape and showed the fish how to use it. Soon the fish was able to measure the waves accurately.

Lola smiled. â€œThank you for being so generous with your help,â€ she said. The fish nodded and swam away.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was three years old and loved sausages. She would always ask her Mommy for sausages for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

One day, she asked her Mommy for sausages again, but her Mom reminded her very softly that she couldn't always eat sausages for every meal. Daisy became very upset and started to cry.

Her Mommy hugged her tight and said, "You can still have sausages sometimes. Just remind me next time and I'll get you some from the store."

Daisy smiled, because she knew that even though she couldn't always eat sausages, she would still get her favourite food from time to time. So Daisy asked her Mommy for sausages every week!

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She loved going outside to play in the sun. One day, the sun was shining so brightly and everything was so warm.

The little girl excitedly started to run around. She ran so fast she got dizzy, then fell to the ground.

But then, to her surprise, she felt something cold. She looked down and saw the ground was covered in snow. The little girl gasped.

She quickly ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, there's snow outside! Can we go play?"

Her mom chuckled and said, "Yes, but we have to grab a sack first."

So they went outside and gathered up the snow in a sack. The little girl was so excited that she twirled around and around, making a mini snow storm.

They took the sack home and put it near the fireplace. The little girl wanted to play with the snow all day, and her mom said she could do just that.

So the little girl spent the day playing with the snow until the sack was empty. It was cold but still so much fun!

Once upon a time there was a very quiet girl. Her name was Lisa. She liked playing with her dolls and playing make believe. She also liked playing with makeup. One day she decided to give her makeup to her best friend, Debby.

When Lisa gave Debby the makeup, she hugged her and said, "Thank you for this gift!"

Lisa was so happy to see the look of surprise and joy on Debby's face. Her friend valued her gift so much.

Then the two girls sat and talked together in the quiet room. The soft light from the sun shone through the window and surrounded them.

Suddenly Lisa and Debby both smiled. They both knew that their friendship was something special and something to be valued.

John had a twin brother, Adam. They loved to play together every day and they always shared their toys. John was a generous twin and always let Adam have the first turn. One day, they went to the park and Adam had an idea. He said, "Let's play a game! We'll find something to stare at and then see who can stare the longest." John agreed and they each looked around the park until they found something to stare at.

Adam spotted a bird and chose the bird as their target. They both started to stare. Adam thought he was winning, but John was determined to be the winner. He kept on his focusing. He didn't blink once. Finally, after what felt like hours, Adam looked away and gave up. John had won the game! Adam was surprised and clapped for his brother in admiration. He said, "You won because you were generous with me. Thank you for sharing this game with me, John." John and Adam hugged and headed off home after a fun day.

One day, a boy and his mom lay together on a beach. They watched as big white sails floated on the light blue ocean. They watched the sails all day and had lots of fun.
The boy said, "Mom, can I go sailing?" Mom said, "Yes, you can go sailing."
So, the boy went out. He walked down to a boat and saw a light sail. It was so light that he could lift it up by himself! He put the sail in the boat and jumped in too.

The boy pushed the boat out and got into it. He grabbed the sail, and it floated him away. He watched the light sky above, the sail flapping in the wind. Then, he sailed around the ocean all day long.

When the day was over, the boy and his sail were back on the beach, where he had first begun. Mom was waiting, and she hugged him tight. She said, "I am glad you had a fun day of sailing." The boy smiled and said, "Yes, it was light and fun!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom had a dog named Spot. They loved to play together in the park. One day, while they were playing, Tom saw some waste on the ground. He knew it was important to keep the park clean.

Tom said to Spot, "We need to pick up this waste, it's important for the park." Spot barked and wagged his tail. He wanted to help Tom. So, Tom picked up the waste and put it in a bag.

Tom decided to lead Spot around the park to find more waste. They found some more and picked it up. After they were done, the park was clean and beautiful. Tom and Spot felt happy and proud. They knew that keeping the park clean was important for everyone.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary parent. They had a special job - to permit things. The parent said â€˜yesâ€™ when it was safe, and â€˜noâ€™ when it was not.

One day the parent thought their job was too easy. So they asked their child to help. The child said 'yes' to lots of things - like playing, running, and eating ice cream.

Soon, the parent was very busy. They said 'yes' and 'no' all day. But the child was very happy.

At the end of the day, the parent hugged their child and said 'thank you.' The child smiled and said, 'it was fun to help'.

The parent agreed and said that they were glad the child was there to help. They knew the job wouldnâ€™t be so easy without the childâ€™s help.

From then on, the parent and child worked together to permit all the wonderful things in life.

Mia was a small girl who always wanted to help others. One morning, Mia saw a grumpy model walking down the street. She asked the model, "Are you ok?" The model just grumbled and kept on walking. Mia knew she wanted to help.

Mia ran after the model and said, "Please let me help you!" The model stopped and looked at Mia. She could see the concern in Mia's eyes. She sighed and said, "Ok then, what can you do to help me?"

Mia thought for a moment and said, "I can make you smile!" She jumped up and down, clapped her hands and smiled a big smile. The model couldn't help but laugh a little.

The model thanked Mia and said, "You really did help me! That was very kind of you!" Mia smiled and said, "You're welcome!" Then she ran off to help someone else.

Jack and Jill were playing in the park one day. Jack saw a big pile of sugar on the ground and started to reach for it. Jill saw this and quickly warned Jack, "No! That sugar will make you sick! Don't touch it".

Jack listened to Jill and didn't touch the sugar. He asked, "What CAN I touch, then?"

Jill thought for a moment and then said, "You can touch the flowers, the slide and the swings. They are all useful and good for you!"

So, Jack and Jill spent the afternoon playing on the swings, going down the slide and smelling the flowers. They had lots of fun, and Jack remembered never to touch the sugar!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Mandy. She was three years old and loved playing in the park. Her mommy had a phone that she would always talk on.

One day at the park, Mandy said, "Mommy, when I'm bigger, I'm going to marry someone!" Her mommy smiled and said, "Okay, Mandy."

A few years passed and one day, Mandy came home from school very upset. She said, "Mommy, I asked Jimmy to marry me at school but he said 'no' and it made me feel bad!" Her mommy hugged her and said, "Honey, don't worry. It's okay to marry someone when you're grown up. But not now."

Mandy thought about that for a minute and then smiled. She said, "Well, I think Jimmy is a bad idea anyway!"

Mandy and her mommy laughed and hugged. Then Mandy went back outside to play, while her mommy went back to talking on the phone.

Once upon a time there was a wise old man who wanted to organize his day. He had many things to do, but he was determined to get everything done. First, he started with a big smile on his face. He was excited to start his day. He made a plan and set out to do his tasks one by one with determination.

After he finished all his tasks he felt very satisfied. He looked at his face in the mirror and saw that the smile was still there. He was happy that he was able to organize his day so well. He was able to get a lot done and still have some time to relax and enjoy the day.

He knew that being wise, organized and having a smile on his face was the key to having a successful day. He was proud of himself for proving just how wise and organized he could be. He knew that he had made a wise decision by taking the time to organize his day. He smiled a big smile and went off to enjoy the rest of his day.

Jimmy was swinging in the playground. He loved being high up in the air and how it made him feel so light. His friends were there too and everyone was having a great time.

Suddenly, Jimmy heard a loud noise. He stopped swinging and looked around. He saw a jar lying on the ground near the swing. He ran to it and picked it up. The jar had a gentle pattern, with blue and yellow flowers.

Jimmy brought the jar closer to his eyes and saw a ladybug crawling around inside. It was really tiny. He smiled and called his friends.

"Look what I found!" he said.

His friends gathered around him and all looked at the little lady bug. They oohed and ahhed and said it was so cute.

Then the lady bug stopped and Jimmy decided to set it free. He opened the jar's lid and gently turned it upside down. The lady bug hopped out and flew off into the sky, free to explore its new world.

Jimmy smiled and watched until it was out of sight. Then he went back to swing with his friends. That had been an exciting find and he couldn't wait to tell his mom about it when he got home!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted to eat some cookies. She went to the kitchen and saw a plate on the table. She took the plate and laid it on the floor. Then she opened the cookie jar and took out a cookie. But, to her surprise, the cookie was bitter and she didn't like it. So, she put the cookie back on the plate and went to her mom to ask for a new one.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore. One day, he found a cactus in his backyard. It was very interesting and had lots of prickly needles.

Timmy's mom came outside and asked him what he found. "Mommy, look! I found an interesting cactus!" Timmy said.

His mom was happy he found something new to explore. "That's very cool, Timmy. Why don't you give me the cactus so we can put it in a pot and take care of it?" she said.

Timmy gave the cactus to his mom and they went inside to find a pot. They found a big pot and put the cactus inside. Timmy was happy he found something interesting and his mom was happy they could take care of it together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Thomas. He was three years old and loved to explore. One day, he went on a big adventure to a far away oasis.

On his way, he found a broken tree branch. He decided to touch it, but quickly pulled his hand away as it was too sharp.

As Thomas continued his journey, he pondered why the branch was so broken. He soon came across a little river that was flowing down the side of the oasis. He remembered the branch and wondered if the river had something to do with it.

The little boy arrived at the oasis and he was in awe. He ran to the edge of the water and started to touch it. As soon as he did, the river started to swell and the current quickly became stronger. Thomas quickly pulled his hand away.

The little boy realized that the branch had broken from the rapidly rising waters. Thomas now understood why the branch was so broken and he was careful not to touch it again.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Larry and Sue. They went to the park together one day. When they got there, they saw a big band playing some music. It was very loud and they could see the people dancing. Larry and Sue stopped to observe. The music sounded like jazz and it made Larry and Sue laugh. The dancers looked silly and Larry and Sue couldn't believe their eyes! They hopped around the park, enjoying the music and watching the silly people. Later on when they left, Larry and Sue said that it was the most fun they ever had.

One day, Lily was walking in the park. Suddenly, she saw a thing with spikes. It was huge and very scary. "Oh no! What's that?" Lily shouted.

Lily's mom came running to help. When she saw the spikey creature, she said "That's a porcupine. Don't worry Lily, it won't hurt you."

But Lily was still scared. She was so scared, she shouted "I don't like the porcupine. It looks terrible!" Her brave mom just smiled and said "Let's go back home now. Everything's ok."

Lily was relieved they could go home, but she still thought the porcupine was very scary. That was one of the most terrible things she had ever seen!

Once upon a time there was a big old tree. It was so big that it touched the clouds. Every day lots of birds and animals came to the tree and they all supported each other.

One day a little mouse called Sally decided to climb the tree. She kept going higher and higher and soon she was so high that she could see the whole world. Then she heard a loud noise and quickly climbed down.

When Sally got back to the ground she saw a bright yellow bulldozer. An old man with big glasses was driving the bulldozer and wanted to cut the tree down.

Sally shook her head and shouted, "No! This tree supports us all. You can't cut it down!"

The old man looked surprised and smiled at Sally, "You are right my little friend. I'm so sorry."

Sally smiled and the old man turned his bulldozer away. The animals, birds and everyone else cheered for Sally and thanked her for protecting their big old tree.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly little girl. She liked to explore and see new things. One day, she decided to take a walk. As she was walking, she saw a strange symbol in the grass. She stopped to take a closer look.

The symbol was a friendly shape which made the little girl smile. She reached down and held the symbol in her hand. She kept it safe and kept on walking.

The symbol made the little girl feel happy and excited. She couldn't wait to tell her mom about it. When she got back home, she showed her mom the symbol. Her mom was really surprised!

The symbol was special to the little girl and her mom. It was like a reminder that they were both very friendly. The little girl still has the symbol and holds onto it tight. Whenever she looks at it, she remembers her special day.

Once there was a boy named Joe. He was only three years old but he loved to explore.

One day, Joe went to the park with his mom. He decided to explore by himself. Joe saw a big tree and wanted to see what was on top of it. So, he started to climb the tree, but he didn't watch where he was stepping. His foot slipped and he fell down, breaking one of the tree's branches.

Joe was scared. But his mom came to give him a big hug. Then, Joe noticed a big, pink bubble gum at the base of the tree! He was so happy, he quickly forgot about the branch he had broken.

But just as Joe was about to grab the gum, he heard a loud voice. It was the park keeper! He had seen Joe break the branch and he was not happy. He scolded Joe and said that he shouldn't climb so high. Joe was sad, he didn't get the gum.

Joe went back home with his mom and learned an important lesson that day. He knew that it was not okay to break things. Joe knew he shouldn't climb too high again.

Once upon a time, there was a family who had a special theatre. Every week, the family would perform plays for their friends and family. One day, the mother decided to gather special costumes for the theatre. She found a velvet dress that sparkled in the light. As she looked closer, she realised it was fake. She laughed, and put the dress back down.

The next week, it was time for the family to perform in the theatre. They dressed up in their costumes and put on the play. The mother wore the velvet dress and everyone's faces lit up when they saw it. It looked so beautiful and sparkled like no other dress.

At the end of the show, everyone was clapping and cheering. Even the baby clapped and laughed in delight. Everyone was so proud of the family for performing a great show.

The mother wore the velvet dress for many of the shows. The audience was never able to tell it was fake.

One day, a pink car named Speedy liked to go fast. Speedy loved to race with his friends. He was very good at it. All the other cars wanted to be like him.

One day, a new car came to town. His name was Slowly. Slowly was not fast like Speedy. He had no money to make him go fast. The other cars did not want to play with Slowly. This made Slowly very sad.

Speedy saw Slowly and said, "Why are you so sad?" Slowly told Speedy that he had no money to be fast like him. Speedy wanted to help. He gave Slowly some of his money to make him go fast.

Now, Slowly was fast like Speedy. They raced together and had lots of fun. All the other cars wanted to play with them too. Speedy and Slowly became best friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was an orange elephant. He really liked to wave to his friends. The elephant would wave to the animals in the zoo when he walked by them. One day, a little girl came up to the elephant and said, â€œHi!â€ The elephant was so happy he started waving to the girl. He waved his trunk in the air and made the girl giggle.

The little girl waved back and smiled. She asked the elephant if he wanted to go for a walk with her. He happily shook his head yes. So the two of them went for a walk around the zoo. Everywhere they went, the orange elephant would wave hello to his friends. The girl was so happy and even started waving to everyone too.

At the end of the day, the girl had to go home. The elephant was sad to say goodbye, so he gave the girl one final wave before she left. The little girl waved back. She knew she had made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat yummy food. One day, her mommy made her a tasty sandwich. Lily ate it all up and her tummy was happy.

Later that day, Lily went to the park to play. She met a new friend named Timmy. Timmy had a cool body because he could climb really high. Lily was impressed and wanted to speak to him. She said, "Hi Timmy, you have a cool body. Do you want to play with me?" Timmy said yes and they had lots of fun together.

At the end of the day, Lily went home and told her mommy about her new friend. She also told her mommy about the tasty sandwich she had for lunch. Her mommy was happy that Lily had a fun day and enjoyed her food. The end.

Once upon a time there was a hammer. It was very boring and it never moved. One day it got tired of being so still, so it asked for help.

The hammer saw a burning fire and it shouted out, "Can you help me?" Right away, the fire said, "Yes! I can burn you so you can move."

The hammer was excited but also a little scared. But the fire was very gentle, and soon it was burning the hammer in a nice and warm way.

Soon enough, the hammer was moving and it was having lots of fun. As it danced around the fire, it realized the fire had given it a magical power.

Suddenly, the hammer had the power to make all sorts of things out of wood and metal. From chairs to toys and even hammers - all made with its own special burning power.

The hammer was so pleased with its new life. It finally had something to do, instead of just sitting around being boring!

Once upon a time there was a kid named Todd. He was three years old and loved adventure. One day, he decided to sail out to sea on a homemade raft.

Todd hoisted up the sail and it bellowed in the wind. He was scared at first but then he smiled with delight. The sun was shining, the water was glimmering, and he felt like he was on top of the world.

He said loudly to the sea, "This is the best day of my life!"

Suddenly, a giant fish jumped out of the water. "Wow!" Todd called. "It looks like it's trying to play with me."

The fish kept jumping in the air and making loud noises. He jumped and laughed until he was so tired he could barely keep his eyes open. Todd waved goodbye to the giant fish and sailed back to shore.

He thought to himself, "I can't wait for the next time I can sail."

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named John who lived in a happy house. He had a phone that was hidden away in his room, but he loved it.

One day, John had a brilliant idea. He decided to wrap the phone in a big, colorful blanket. Then, he put it in the corner of his room.

John was so proud of his work, he wanted to show everyone. He ran downstairs and shouted, "Mom, come and see what I did! I wrapped up the telephone with a pretty cloth!

Mom came running and said, "John, that's amazing! Where did the telephone go?"

John pointed to the corner of his room and said, "It's hidden there, under the blanket. Mom smiled and said, "Well done, John! You are so clever!"
John was very proud of himself and he couldn't wait to show his friends.

Once upon a time there was a mummy and a daddy. Every day, mummy and daddy went to their job and worked hard all day long. After they were done with their job, they would come home and mummy would feed the little one their dinner.

The mummy and daddy loved the little one very much and they were very proud of their job. One day mummy and daddy were surprised when they came home to a rare sight. The little one had prepared dinner for them!

The little one had a bowl full of rice with some vegetables and a big smile on its face. Mummy and daddy were so pleased that they gave the little one a big hug.

Mummy then said to the little one, "Thank you for feeding us, we are so proud of you!"

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Bun Bun. Bun Bun woke up one morning and saw the sun shining bright outside. He wanted to go play with his friends, but he was feeling very hungry. So, he went to get some carrots from the garden.

But when he got there, he saw that the carrots were very deep in the ground. He tried to pull them out, but he couldn't. "I am struggling," he said to himself.

Just then, his friend, Squirrel, came by. "What's wrong, Bun Bun?" Squirrel asked. "I can't get these carrots out of the ground," Bun Bun replied. "I will help you," Squirrel said. Together, they pulled and pulled until they finally got the carrots out. "Thank you, Squirrel," Bun Bun said. They both enjoyed a tasty snack and played together all day long.

Anna and Ben are playing with their baby brother, Sam. Sam is very small and cute, but he is also very persistent. He wants to grab everything he sees, even if it is not his.

"Look, Sam, this is a ball. You can roll it and bounce it," Anna says, showing him a red ball. She rolls it to him gently, and he smiles and tries to catch it.

"No, Sam, this is a book. You can read it and learn new words," Ben says, holding a colorful book. He opens it and points to a picture of a dog. "This is a dog. It says woof-woof."

Sam reaches for the book, but Ben pulls it away. "No, Sam, this is mine. You have the ball."

Sam frowns and starts to cry. He does not want the ball. He wants the book.

"Ben, don't be mean. Share with Sam. He is just curious," Anna says, taking the book from Ben. She gives it to Sam, who stops crying and laughs. He likes the book.

"Fine, I don't care. I have the ball," Ben says, rolling the ball away. He pretends he is not interested in the book.

But Sam is persistent. He crawls after Ben, dragging the book with him. He wants to share the book with Ben. He thinks Ben will like it too.

"Sam, leave me alone. I don't want the book. I want the ball," Ben says, pushing Sam away.

Sam does not give up. He keeps crawling and laughing. He thinks it is a game.

"Sam, stop it. You are annoying me," Ben says, getting angry.

Anna watches them and laughs too. She thinks they are funny. She loves her baby brother and her big brother. She knows they love each other too, even if they fight sometimes. She decides to join them and play with the ball and the book. She thinks they will have more fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a tutor named Tom. Tom was very good at teaching kids. He had a perfect way to make learning fun. He liked to whistle while he worked.

One day, a little girl named Sue came to Tom for help. Sue wanted to learn how to whistle too. Tom said, "I will teach you how to whistle, Sue. It is easy and fun!"

Tom showed Sue how to put her lips together and blow. Sue tried and tried, but she could not whistle. Tom said, "Do not worry, Sue. Keep trying and you will get it." Sue practiced every day with Tom.

One day, Sue finally learned how to whistle. She was so happy! Sue said, "Thank you, Tom! You are the best tutor ever!" Tom smiled and said, "You did a great job, Sue. Now we can whistle together!"

From that day on, Sue and Tom would whistle while they learned. They had lots of fun and became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a house. It was a normal house with a roof and walls. In the front yard, there was a garden with many flowers. One day, a little seed was planted in the garden. The sun shone and the rain fell and soon the little seed began to grow.

Every day, the little plant grew taller and taller. It had green leaves and a long stem. Then one day, the plant began to bloom. Beautiful flowers in all colors grew on the stem. The flowers were so pretty that the people who walked by the house stopped to look at them.

The little plant grew bigger and bigger until it was as tall as the house. The house was still a normal house, but now it had a big, beautiful plant growing in the garden. And every day, the flowers continued to bloom and bring joy to everyone who saw them.

Once there was a humble bird. This bird wanted to fly very high. One day, the bird flapped its wings and soared up, up and away. The bird felt so free as it flew!

Suddenly, the bird realized it only had one problem - it had no gas. Without gas, it wouldn't be able to keep soaring. The bird looked around to find some, but couldn't see any.

Just then, the bird heard a friendly voice. It was a friendly bee. The bee said that it had lots of gas and would share it with the bird. The bird was so happy!

The bee filled the bird's wings with gas. The bird thanked the bee and flew away. As it soared around, it had the biggest smile. The bird was so proud that it could fly so high and far, thanks to the bee's generous gift!

Mommy and Jimmy were walking down a path one night. It was dark, and their shadows were long.
Jimmy said, "Mommy, look at my shadow. I want to let it run faster than any other shadow".
"Oh no, Jimmy," Mommy said, "It's too dark outside. Let's just take a look at the shadows for now".
Jimmy said, "Okay, Mommy. Let's see how our shadows look like."
Mommy and Jimmy watched their shadows stretch across the path. They were long and thin like two dark lines in the night.
Jimmy said, "Mommy, look, I can make my shadow go on a walk. It's so fun!"
Mommy smiled at Jimmy and said, "Let your shadow go on a walk. I'm sure it will have so much fun!"
Jimmy smiled and with a little skip and a jump, his shadow went on its way. What fun they had that night!

Anna and Ben were playing with paper and scissors. They wanted to make snowflakes and stars. Anna cut many shapes and showed them to Ben. "Look, I made a big snowflake! And a star with six points! And a heart!" she said.

Ben tried to cut his paper too, but it was hard. His scissors were dull and his hands were small. He could not make any shapes. He felt sad and angry. He looked at Anna's shapes and wanted them. He said to Anna, "Give me your shapes! They are mine!"

Anna was surprised and hurt. She said, "No, they are not yours! I made them with my scissors and my paper. You are selfish, Ben! You can't have everything you want!"

Ben did not listen. He grabbed Anna's shapes and ran away. Anna cried and chased him. She wanted her shapes back. They ran around the room, knocking over toys and books. Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong.

She saw Anna and Ben fighting over the paper shapes. She was not happy. She said, "Stop, both of you! What are you doing? Why are you fighting over paper shapes?"

Anna and Ben stopped and looked at their mom. They both tried to explain. Anna said, "Ben took my shapes! He is selfish!" Ben said, "Anna has too many shapes! She won't share!"

Their mom shook her head. She said, "You are both wrong. Anna, you should share your shapes with Ben. He is your brother and he wants to play with you. Ben, you should not take Anna's shapes. She worked hard to make them. You should ask her nicely if you can have some. And you should use your own scissors and paper to make your own shapes. You can both succeed if you try."

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We are sorry, Anna. We are sorry, Ben." They hugged each other and their mom. They gave back the shapes they took and shared them. They also used their own scissors and paper to make more shapes. They had fun and learned to be kind and fair.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emily. Emily loved flowers, especially colorful ones. One day, she went to the store with her mom to buy some bulbs to plant in their garden.

Emily saw many different bulbs at the store. She pointed to a yellow one and said, "Mommy, I want this one!" Her mom said, "Okay, let's order it." Emily was excited to plant her new bulb in the garden.

When they got home, Emily's dad helped her dig a hole in the ground for the bulb. Emily carefully placed the bulb in the hole and covered it with dirt. She watered it and waited patiently for it to grow.

Days passed and Emily checked on her bulb every day. One morning, she saw something different. A green stem was growing out of the ground! She ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, look! My bulb is growing!" Her mom smiled and said, "I'm so happy for you, Emily."

One day, a hunter was walking through the forest. He was looking for something to bring back home. Suddenly, he heard a noise in the bushes. He stopped to listen. It sounded like something was in trouble.

The hunter saw a little bunny tangled in a bush. He carefully took the bunny out of the bush and held it in his hands. The bunny was embarrassed, but the hunter was very kind. He talked to the bunny and made it feel safe.

The hunter brought the bunny back home with him. He hugged the bunny tight and got it some food. He made sure it was happy and comfortable. The bunny was so grateful that the hunter came along and saved it.

After that, the hunter and the bunny were best friends. The hunter would often bring food for the bunny and take long walks together. They were never embarrassed when they were together. They were happy to be friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Kitty. Kitty lived in a small house with a nice family. One day, Kitty saw a big red ambulance outside her house. The ambulance had bright lights and made a loud noise. Kitty was curious and wanted to see what was happening.

Kitty went outside and saw a man lying on the ground. He couldn't move, so the ambulance came to help him. The people from the ambulance put the man on a bed with wheels and took him inside the ambulance. Kitty wanted to help, so she followed them.

Inside the ambulance, Kitty saw the man start to feel better. He looked at Kitty and said, "Thank you for coming with me, Kitty. You made me feel less scared." Kitty felt happy that she could help the man. Soon, the ambulance took the man to a place where he could get better, and Kitty went back to her small house with her nice family.

Once upon a time, there was a team of animals who loved to play together. One day, they found an unusual object in the forest. It was big and shiny, but they didn't know what it was.

The bear said, "What is this thing? Can someone explain it to me?"

The rabbit replied, "I don't know, but it looks like it could be fun to play with."

The team decided to try and figure out what the object was. They worked together to push and pull it, but it wouldn't budge.

Finally, the wise old owl flew down and said, "I know what this is. It's a giant mirror. It reflects everything around it."

The team was amazed and had fun looking at themselves in the mirror. They were happy they had worked together to solve the mystery of the unusual object.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play games with his friends. One day, they played a game and Timmy won! He was so happy and excited.

After playing, Timmy needed to go to the toilet. He went to the bathroom and sat on the toilet. While he was sitting there, he thought about how he won the game earlier. He felt proud of himself.

Timmy went back to his friends and told them about how he won the game. They all cheered and clapped for him. Timmy felt famous! He was happy that his friends were happy for him. From that day on, Timmy always tried his best to win games and make his friends proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was being tucked into bed by her mom. Every night, the mom would show her a sweet hug and kiss before she said good night and turned off the light.

One night, the little girl couldn't sleep. She was having a nightmare, and it was making her scared. Her mom came in to check on her and noticed that she was shaking and didn't feel very warm.

So, Mom got in bed with the little girl and showed her a hug that made the little girl feel safe. She started to feel warm and the nightmare went away. Eventually, the little girl drifted off to sleep, feeling secure and warm all night long.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond with her friends. One day, Ducky saw a big, graceful swan swimming in the pond. Ducky wanted to be as big and graceful as the swan, so she asked her mommy how she could grow big like the swan.

Mommy duck told Ducky that she needed to eat lots of healthy food and exercise every day. So, Ducky started eating lots of vegetables and swimming every day. But, there was a problem. The pond was getting too small for all the ducks and swans. They needed more space to swim.

One day, Ducky and her friends saw a big subway being built near the pond. They were worried that the subway would take up all the space and they wouldn't have anywhere to swim. Ducky went to talk to the construction workers and asked them if they could leave some space for the pond. The workers listened to Ducky and left a big space for the pond to grow.

Now, Ducky and her friends had more space to swim and grow big and strong. They were happy and grateful to the construction workers for listening to them. And Ducky kept eating healthy and exercising every day, growing bigger and more graceful, just like the swan. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. She was always excited to go out with her mom to catch yummy treats.

One day, Emma asked her mom, "Where are we going?" Her mom said, "We are going out to catch something special today. I'm sure you'll like it."

Emma said, "What is it? Can I help?" Her mom said, "Yes, we're going to catch a pie!" Emma liked the sound of that and was excited to go.

When they got to the shop, Emma saw a big, round pie sitting on the counter. She wanted to catch it, but it was too big. So they asked the shopkeeper if they could have a little pie.

The shopkeeper served them a little pie and Emma caught it with her little hands. She was so delighted that she jumped for joy! The little girl and her mom were so happy about catching the pie!

Once, there was a boy named Jack and he loved to go on adventures. He decided to take a walk outside to see what he could find. He stepped on the grass and found a piece of cloth with different colors and shapes on it.

Jack was very excited to find this cloth. He asked his mom what it was and she told him it was a quilt. Jack asked his mom if he could take it home, and she said yes.

Back home, Jack wanted to show his friends the quilt. He stepped into his room where his friends were waiting for him.

When Jackâ€™s friends saw the quilt, they were excited. Each of them wanted to touch it because it was so different from any other cloth they had ever seen.

All of his friends were happy because Jack found something special. They all agreed that his quilt was the most interesting thing Jack has ever brought home.

Once upon a time there was a very charming lab named Rosie. Every morning she would speak to the birds, telling them about her day. She loved to chat with them and would always greet them with a happy bark.

One day, Rosie was feeling particularly adventurous. She decided that she would go explore the woods near her house. She set off on her own and soon stumbled upon a small creek. It was so peaceful and still that Rosie was mesmerized. She decided to take a little dip in the water and played in it for a while.

After her swim, Rosie climbed out of the creek and started walking along the path. Not long after, she came across a tiny log cabin. Rosie peered inside and saw a small family sitting around the table chatting. She barked to get their attention and the family immediately lit up with delight. They invited Rosie into the cabin and the three year old child was thrilled to have her around.

The child spoke sweetly with Rosie and enjoyed scratching behind her ears. Rosie was just as enchanted by the child and the two of them spent the whole day playing. The family thanked Rosie for being so charming and invited her back again soon. Rosie happily accepted and ran off back home, feeling very content and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a festival with lots of fun things happening. There were lots of games for children to play and goodies to munch on.

The best part was when everyone joined together to freeze. Everyone stopped what they were doing and stood still like a statue! It was so funny, everyone looked like a frozen bunch of robots! After a minute, all the children cheered and started playing again.

That night, they all had a delicious festival feast. They ate, sang, and danced. It was supposed to be the best day ever.

But when it was time to go home, everyone was sad. They wanted to keep on freezing and playing together. Soon, they all waved goodbye and promised to have lots more fun together again soon.

Tim and Kim are twins who like to play with toys. They have many toys, but they want more. They see a big box in the living room. It is a gift for their dad. It has a tag that says "Do not open until his birthday".

Tim and Kim are curious. They want to know what is inside the box. They think of a creative plan. They poke a small hole in the box with a pencil. They peek through the hole. They see something shiny and round. They think it is a ball.

They poke another hole in the box. They see something long and thin. They think it is a stick. They poke more holes in the box. They see something black and square. They think it is a book. They are happy. They think they have found many toys for themselves.

But they are wrong. The shiny and round thing is a watch. The long and thin thing is a tie. The black and square thing is a wallet. They are not toys. They are things for their dad. They are his birthday gift.

Their mom comes in the living room. She sees the box with many holes. She is angry. She asks Tim and Kim what they have done. They are scared. They tell her the truth. They say they are sorry.

Their mom tells them they have broken the law. The law is a rule that everyone must follow. The law says you must not open other people's gifts. The law says you must respect other people's things. The law says you must be honest and kind.

Tim and Kim feel bad. They have learned a lesson. They say they will not break the law again. They say they will wait until their dad's birthday to see his gift. They say they will hug him and say happy birthday. They say they will play with their own toys and share them with each other. They say they will be good twins. Their mom smiles. She forgives them. She hugs them and says she loves them.

Once upon a time there was a big elephant. He wanted to know how much he weighed, so he asked the wise old animal doctor.
The animal doctor said he needed something to weigh the elephant, so they found a reliable wooden box. The elephant carefully stepped into the box and the animal doctor carefully weighed the box.

The animal doctor said, "You weigh a lot! You're the biggest elephant I've ever seen!"
The elephant was so happy and jumped up and down, but then he slipped and fell on his knee. He was very sad and began to cry.

But the animal doctor promised the elephant he would always be there to help him. The elephant was so relieved to know that the animal doctor was reliable.
From then on, the animal doctor weighed the elephant every week, and the elephant's knee was never hurt again!

Linda was walking in the forest when she saw something mysterious. She had to take a closer look. She slowly approached it, and realized it was a bulb. She was very excited, she wanted to grab it, and take it with her.

Suddenly a voice shouted, "Hey! Don't grab it!" Linda jumped back in shock. A mysterious figure was standing there, she had never seen anything like it before. He asked her, "Do you know what this is?".

She shook her head, and he said, "That to me is a precious bulb. It's not an ordinary bulb, you know, it can perform magical tricks". Linda's eyes lit up with curiosity, she couldn't take her eyes off it.

The figure said, "If you want, You can take it with you". Linda was very excited, she grabbed the bulb and hugged it. She thanked the figure and ran home. She knew this was going to be a fun adventure.

At home, Linda started exploring the bulb. She played with it and tried to figure out how to make it work. She closed her eyes, concentrated and presto! The bulb suddenly glowed and started performing magical tricks! Linda was amazed, she had never before seen something so mysterious.

Toby was a little boy who wanted to play with the other children. However, all the children were too busy to remember to include Toby. Toby was getting very jealous.

Finally, when Toby was walking by, he saw the other children playing a game. He asked if he could join in, but all the kids just looked away. Toby was so sad.

Just then, Toby noticed that the other boys were pinching each other on their left arms. He ran up to them, and asked if he could join in too.

The other boys looked at each other. "You can join if you pinch the left arm of each of us," they said.

Toby smiled and said, "Yes!" He pinched each of the boys on the left arm and they all laughed. From then on, Toby was welcomed in the group and everyone was very happy.

John wanted to do something special. He kneeled down on the ground in the bright sunshine and closed his eyes. He reached out to the ground and felt around until he found a smooth lemon. He held it carefully in his hand and was amazed by how heavy it was. He smelled it, feeling the sweet and tart scent enter his nose.

John wanted to share the lemon with his family and he ran inside to show them. Inside, he found his mom and dad. He offered his lemon to them with a big smile. They both laughed, but felt excited about what John had done. It was not normal for a three-year-old child to find a lemon in someone's backyard.

John was happy he found the lemon and felt proud he could share it with his family. Everyone gathered around and they enjoyed the crunchy and juicy lemon.

Once there was a bunny who loved to hop. He liked hopping all around, especially in the sunshine. One day, while he was hopping, he saw a harmless pear nearby. He had never seen one before, so he hopped over to take a closer look.

He stood up on his hind legs and sniffed the pear. It smelled sweet and yummy. He wanted to take a bite, but he was a little bit scared. He called out to his friend, a bird named Chirpy, who was sitting near by in a tree.

"Chirpy, do you think this pear is harmless?" the bunny asked.

"Yes, I think it is!" Chirpy said. "You should take a bite!"

So the bunny hopped over to the pear and took a big bite. It was the best thing he had ever tasted! He hopped in circles, as he was so happy.

After that day, the bunny hopped over to that pear tree every day. It always had new, delicious pears to try. He felt so lucky to have such a harmless and tasty snack.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin lived in the big sea with his family. They had a small home near some rocks. One day, Fin saw a big fish and wanted to become big like it.

Fin asked his mom, "Mom, how can I become big like that fish?" His mom said, "Fin, you will become big when you grow up. Just eat your food and play with your friends."

But Fin didn't want to wait. He swam far away from his home to find a way to become big. He saw a big, dark cave and went inside. In the cave, he found a magic rock that could make him big.

Fin touched the rock and said, "I want to become big now!" Suddenly, he became very big. He was happy, but he didn't know that the rock was bad. As he swam back home, he was so big that he broke his family's home by accident. His family was sad and had no place to live. Fin wished he had listened to his mom and waited to become big.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Ann. She was three years old and she liked to play in the mist. One day, Ann was playing in her garden and she saw a big mist rolling in. She was so happy!

Ann shouted, "I'm gonna play in the mist!" so she quickly ran outside.

Ann twirled around in the mist and it felt like she was dancing. She spun and smiled and laughed so much. Suddenly, Ann heard a funny noise coming from the mist.

Ann said, "What's that noise?"

The mist replied, "It's me, I'm singing! Do you wanna dance with me?"

Ann smiled and said, "Yes please!"

Then, the mist and Ann started dancing and singing together. They danced and laughed and had lots of fun. Ann be so happy!

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a soft clown living in the park. Every day, he would jump and laugh while the sun shone and glowed in the sky.

One day, a little girl came to visit the park. She was only three years old and she loved to watch the clown jump.

The girl called out to the clown, "Hey! Clown, why do you jump so much?"

The clown stopped his bouncing and looked down at the little girl. He smiled and said, "I jump because it makes me happy and it makes the sun glow brighter!"

The little girl smiled and said, "I like your smile, Clown! Will you play with me?"

The clown was delighted. He nodded and said, "Let's play catch! The sun will love to watch us play!" Thus, the girl and the clown played catch together while the sun shone and glowed in the sky.

Once upon a time there was a nosy cow named Lucy. Every day Lucy liked to go for walks around the farm. While she was walking one day, she saw something strange in the barn.

Lucy got closer to the barn to investigate and saw the farmer trying to prevent something from escaping. She was so nosy that she couldn't help but moo at the farmer to ask what was going on.

"Go away cow," yelled the farmer. "You can't come in here. I'm trying to keep this nasty fox locked up so it can't get out and hurt the other animals."

But Lucy was too nosy and kept trying to sneak into the barn. The farmer finally got so annoyed that he opened the door and let the fox out. The fox ran outdoors and started chasing Lucy.

Lucy was so scared that she ran and ran until she was too tired to go any further. When the farmer finally caught up to her, the fox had already chased her off of the farm.

Lucy was never seen again. The nosy cow hadn't listened to the farmer and that prevented her from ever returning to the farm.

Molly was playing in her backyard when she heard a fierce noise. She looked up and saw a missile shooting through the sky. Molly jumped into a puddle and started to splash.

"What are you doing?" said her mom.

"I'm splashing!" yelled Molly. "The missile was fierce so I wanted to be safe!"

Mom laughed and said, "That's a good idea, but I think the missile is gone now."

Molly peeked out of the puddle and looked around. The sky was clear, so she stopped splashing and came out of the puddle.

"I'm glad the missile is gone," she said.

"Me too," said Mom. She gave Molly a big hug and said, "Let's go back inside now."

Molly and Mom went inside, and Molly stopped worrying about the fierce missile.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Susie. Jack had a big, warm, cozy sweater, which he wore every day. Susie was so envious of Jack's sweater, so one day, she asked him:

Susie: "Jack, can I have your sweater?"

Jack: "No, I like my sweater very much. Why don't you make your own?"

Susie thought of a great idea. She found wool and needles and started to make her own sweater. She tried and tried, and with Jack's help she improved it little by little.

At last, Susie had herself a very nice sweater, which Jack thought looked even better than his. Susie was so happy and Jack was so proud of her!

The End

Molly was so excited to go for a walk. She had put on her shiny pink coat and was pulling on her mittens. She had asked her mom if she could bring along her favourite squeaky toy and her mom said yes.

Molly ran ahead, her tiny shoes slapping with every step down the path. Mom called out, "Wait for me, Molly!"

Molly stopped and looked back. Her mom had not tied her shoes yet and was trying to catch up. "Come on, let's get your shoes tied."

Molly waited impatiently as her mom prepared her shoes with the tight knots. Finally, Mom tied the second heel and said, "Good, now we're ready to go."

Molly was so happy, she held up her squeaky toy and ran ahead again. She laughed, happy to be out for a walk with her mom.

Jimmy was a little boy. He really liked to jog. Every day he would go to the park with his dad and jog along the path.

Jimmy's dad liked to play the guitar. Every day when Jimmy and his dad went to the park, his dad brought his guitar and would play it while Jimmy jogged.

At the park there was a fat cat. Jimmy really liked the cat and liked to talk to it when he was taking a break from jogging. One day the cat even chased Jimmy when he jogged past it!

The cat made Jimmy laugh. Jimmy and his dad would go to the park every day and Jimmy would jog while his dad played the guitar. It was always so much fun.

A little boy named John was walking down a street one day. He saw a big barrel near the side of the street. He wondered what was inside the barrel.

John peeked inside and discovered that it was full of sour fruit! He was so excited to find the barrel. He went to find his mum.

When he showed her the barrel, she was very happy. She smiled and said that the barrel would provide lots of yummy snacks for their family.

John and his mum took some of the sour fruit from the barrel and made yummy treats. Then they shared them with their family and everyone enjoyed them a lot.

John was so pleased that he had found the barrel. He was happy to know it could provide tasty snacks for his family.

Once there was a baby bear named Benny. He was glad he was out in the woods with his mom and dad. His mom and dad told him a story of how their family had been around for a long time. Benny loved the story!

But then one day, Benny noticed something was strange. He saw a bunny hop away with one of his mom's favourite blankets! Benny was so surprised that he had been so soft and sneakily stolen it.

He told his mom and dad what he had saw. "That bunny was so naughty!" his dad said. Mom agreed and said, "We should go look for our blanket." They all agreed and went searching for it.

After looking around for a little bit, Benny finally spotted the bunny with his blanket! He told his mom and dad, "There it is!" They saw the bunny and chased after it. Finally after a lot of running, they caught the bunny and got their blanket back!

"Now that bunny won't steal anything else," Mom said. Benny smiled and was glad the story had a happy ending!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sam. She loved to wear her favorite dress, which was blue with a big pink bow.

One day, Sam went for a walk in the woods with her mom. Suddenly, they heard a noise. "What was that?" Sam asked.

"I'm not sure," her mom replied. "But stay close to me!"

The noise got louder, until they saw a man walking towards them. He was wearing a terrifying mask and carrying a big weapon.

"Oh no!" Sam's mom said. "Let's go!" She grabbed Sam and they ran away, but the man chased after them.

Finally, they reached a big house. Sam's mom opened the door and they quickly ran inside. The man stopped outside and shouted, "You can't escape! I'll get you!"

Sam and her mom were so scared. They hid behind the couch and waited for a long time.

Finally, the noise stopped. Sam's mom peeked outside, but the man was gone.

"We are safe now," Sam's mom said. She hugged Sam tightly. "Let's never go for a walk in the woods again."

Sam nodded. She never wanted to experience something so terrible again.

Once there was a girl who liked to explore dark places. She was very brave. She decided to explore a nearby cave, so she got a flashlight. She brought the flashlight with her and planned to explore the cave.

But the cave was very dark. She needed more light, so she asked her brother for help. He had a much brighter flashlight, so she took it.

She entered the cave, with the bright flashlight. She shined it all around the cave and saw all sorts of interesting things. But then something stupid happened - she dropped the flashlight and it broke. Now she was very sad because she couldn't explore anymore.

But then she remembered that she still had her first flashlight. She quickly found it and it still worked. She was so happy and she used her first flashlight to finish exploring the cave. It wasn't as bright as the other one, but it finally worked.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a chest that he loved very much. He kept all his toys and treasures inside it. One day, Timmy went to open his chest, but it was tight shut. He tried and tried, but he couldn't open it.

Timmy was sad because he couldn't play with his toys. He sat down and thought about what to do. Suddenly, he heard a ringing sound coming from inside the chest. He knew he had to get it open to see what was making the noise.

Timmy pushed and pulled with all his might, and finally, the chest opened. Inside, he found a shiny bell that was ringing. He was so happy that he could play with his toys again and listen to the bell ring. From that day on, Timmy always made sure to keep his chest unlocked so he could play with his toys anytime he wanted.

Once there was an ant who wanted to be powerful. He asked all of the animals in the forest how he could be powerful. A fox told him that he could act. The ant asked the fox what he meant by act. The fox said, "Acting is when you pretend to be something else but you don't really change."

The ant was excited. He decided to try it out. He pretended to be a lion. He widened his eyes, put his hands on his hips, and roared like a lion. All of the animals were scared. The ant was proud that he made them all scared.

"I am powerful!" the ant exclaimed. He continued to act like a lion and strutted around the forest. All of the animals kept their distance. The ant was very proud of himself and laughed and smiled.

He had learned that by acting, he could be powerful. He was so happy that he decided to act like a lion every day. Whenever he got scared, he acted like a lion and all the animals in the forest were scared too.

Sam and Jane were playing in the park. It was a warm day and they were having fun. Suddenly, Sam saw something shining in the grass. "What is it?" he asked.

Jane said, "Let's find out." She bent down and opened her hand. Inside her hand was a shiny gold ring.

"Wow," said Sam. He reached out his finger to take it. It felt warm against his skin.

Suddenly, a woman ran up to them. "That's my ring!" she shouted. "Give it back to me at once!"

Sam and Jane were so scared, they dropped the ring and ran away.

The woman picked up the ring and smiled cruelly. "It's too late," she said. "You'll never get it back now."

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to explore the world. One day she decided to go for a walk and explore a new space for the first time. The space was a large park filled with delicate flowers and brightly coloured butterflies. She quickly noticed a man and a woman picking flowers from the bushes and she approached them with curiosity.

The little girl asked "What are you doing?".
The man replied "We are picking these flowers to include them in our garden, so we can enjoy them for a long time".
The little girl thought about the man's words and said "I like exploring different spaces and I think it is important to be careful with the things we pick, so we can enjoy them for a long time".

The couple thanked the little girl for her words as they had never thought of this before. From then on they carefully picked the delicate flowers and decided to explore more spaces and appreciate the beauty around them.

The moral of the story is to always appreciate what we have and to be careful not to damage delicate things when exploring new spaces.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. The bear liked to go to the shop to buy honey. But one day, the shop was closed. The bear didn't like that. He got mad and started to fight with the door. The door didn't move, but the bear kept trying. After a while, the bear got tired and went back to his cave. But on the way, he smelled something smelly. It was a skunk! The bear didn't like the smell, so he ran away as fast as he could. From that day on, the bear made sure to check if the shop was open before going there.

CLEVER ELSIE

There was once a man who had a daughter who was called Clever Elsie. And

when she had grown up her father said: 'We will get her married.' 'Yes,'

said the mother, 'if only someone would come who would have her.' At

length a man came from a distance and wooed her, who was called Hans;

but he stipulated that Clever Elsie should be really smart. 'Oh,' said

the father, 'she has plenty of good sense'; and the mother said: 'Oh,

she can see the wind coming up the street, and hear the flies coughing.'

'Well,' said Hans, 'if she is not really smart, I won't have her.' When

they were sitting at dinner and had eaten, the mother said: 'Elsie, go

into the cellar and fetch some beer.' Then Clever Elsie took the pitcher

from the wall, went into the cellar, and tapped the lid briskly as she

went, so that the time might not appear long. When she was below she

fetched herself a chair, and set it before the barrel so that she had

no need to stoop, and did not hurt her back or do herself any unexpected

injury. Then she placed the can before her, and turned the tap, and

while the beer was running she would not let her eyes be idle, but

looked up at the wall, and after much peering here and there, saw a

pick-axe exactly above her, which the masons had accidentally left

there.

Then Clever Elsie began to weep and said: 'If I get Hans, and we have

a child, and he grows big, and we send him into the cellar here to draw

beer, then the pick-axe will fall on his head and kill him.' Then she

sat and wept and screamed with all the strength of her body, over the

misfortune which lay before her. Those upstairs waited for the drink,

but Clever Elsie still did not come. Then the woman said to the servant:

'Just go down into the cellar and see where Elsie is.' The maid went and

found her sitting in front of the barrel, screaming loudly. 'Elsie why

do you weep?' asked the maid. 'Ah,' she answered, 'have I not reason to

weep? If I get Hans, and we have a child, and he grows big, and has to

draw beer here, the pick-axe will perhaps fall on his head, and kill

him.' Then said the maid: 'What a clever Elsie we have!' and sat down

beside her and began loudly to weep over the misfortune. After a while,

as the maid did not come back, and those upstairs were thirsty for the

beer, the man said to the boy: 'Just go down into the cellar and see

where Elsie and the girl are.' The boy went down, and there sat Clever

Elsie and the girl both weeping together. Then he asked: 'Why are you

weeping?' 'Ah,' said Elsie, 'have I not reason to weep? If I get Hans,

and we have a child, and he grows big, and has to draw beer here, the

pick-axe will fall on his head and kill him.' Then said the boy: 'What

a clever Elsie we have!' and sat down by her, and likewise began to

howl loudly. Upstairs they waited for the boy, but as he still did not

return, the man said to the woman: 'Just go down into the cellar and see

where Elsie is!' The woman went down, and found all three in the midst

of their lamentations, and inquired what was the cause; then Elsie told

her also that her future child was to be killed by the pick-axe, when it

grew big and had to draw beer, and the pick-axe fell down. Then said the

mother likewise: 'What a clever Elsie we have!' and sat down and wept

with them. The man upstairs waited a short time, but as his wife did not

come back and his thirst grew ever greater, he said: 'I must go into the

cellar myself and see where Elsie is.' But when he got into the cellar,

and they were all sitting together crying, and he heard the reason, and

that Elsie's child was the cause, and the Elsie might perhaps bring one

into the world some day, and that he might be killed by the pick-axe, if

he should happen to be sitting beneath it, drawing beer just at the very

time when it fell down, he cried: 'Oh, what a clever Elsie!' and sat

down, and likewise wept with them. The bridegroom stayed upstairs alone

for a long time; then as no one would come back he thought: 'They must be

waiting for me below: I too must go there and see what they are about.'

When he got down, the five of them were sitting screaming and lamenting

quite piteously, each out-doing the other. 'What misfortune has happened

then?' asked he. 'Ah, dear Hans,' said Elsie, 'if we marry each other

and have a child, and he is big, and we perhaps send him here to draw

something to drink, then the pick-axe which has been left up there might

dash his brains out if it were to fall down, so have we not reason to

weep?' 'Come,' said Hans, 'more understanding than that is not needed

for my household, as you are such a clever Elsie, I will have you,' and

seized her hand, took her upstairs with him, and married her.

After Hans had had her some time, he said: 'Wife, I am going out to work

and earn some money for us; go into the field and cut the corn that we

may have some bread.' 'Yes, dear Hans, I will do that.' After Hans had

gone away, she cooked herself some good broth and took it into the field

with her. When she came to the field she said to herself: 'What shall I

do; shall I cut first, or shall I eat first? Oh, I will eat first.' Then

she drank her cup of broth and when she was fully satisfied, she once

more said: 'What shall I do? Shall I cut first, or shall I sleep first?

I will sleep first.' Then she lay down among the corn and fell asleep.

Hans had been at home for a long time, but Elsie did not come; then said

he: 'What a clever Elsie I have; she is so industrious that she does not

even come home to eat.' But when evening came and she still stayed away,

Hans went out to see what she had cut, but nothing was cut, and she

was lying among the corn asleep. Then Hans hastened home and brought

a fowler's net with little bells and hung it round about her, and she

still went on sleeping. Then he ran home, shut the house-door, and sat

down in his chair and worked. At length, when it was quite dark, Clever

Elsie awoke and when she got up there was a jingling all round about

her, and the bells rang at each step which she took. Then she was

alarmed, and became uncertain whether she really was Clever Elsie or

not, and said: 'Is it I, or is it not I?' But she knew not what answer

to make to this, and stood for a time in doubt; at length she thought:

'I will go home and ask if it be I, or if it be not I, they will be sure

to know.' She ran to the door of her own house, but it was shut; then

she knocked at the window and cried: 'Hans, is Elsie within?' 'Yes,'

answered Hans, 'she is within.' Hereupon she was terrified, and said:

'Ah, heavens! Then it is not I,' and went to another door; but when the

people heard the jingling of the bells they would not open it, and she

could get in nowhere. Then she ran out of the village, and no one has

seen her since.

One day, Timmy went to the store. He saw something he wanted, so he asked his mom if he could please have it. His mom said yes, and they went home with the special thing. It was a big roll of colorful tape!

Timmy was so lucky! Tape was so much fun! He wrapped presents for his friends, and he even taped pictures to his wall.

But then, Timmy wanted to use all his tape. He started to get sad. He wanted more colored tape! So he asked his mom if he could please have some more tape.

Mom smiled and said yes. She took Timmy back to the store, and they bought lots of colorful tape. Now Timmy can have fun and make things with tape for years and years to come. He is so lucky!

Once upon a time, there was an ugly basket. Nobody wanted the basket and so it was very sad.

One day it decided to settle in the forest. One by one, animals began to come by and take the basket in. A rabbit brought it a nice, soft blanket. A deer gave it a pillow. And a fox found some pretty flowers for the basket.

Soon, the basket became very cozy. All the animals settled there at night, listening to the frog's songs and feeling the warmth of the fireflies.

The animals loved the basket and so did the basket. It felt like home and it couldn't have been any happier.

One day, mommy and daddy took Tom to the park. Tom was very happy. He saw some birds flying in the sky and some squirrels running around. Then he saw something shiny on the ground. It was a copper penny! Tom shouted with delight and ran to pick it up.

Mommy smiled at him and said, "Let's organize your penny with the others!"

Tom ran back over to where his parents were sitting. They had a jar there with other pennies in it. Tom carefully put his penny in the jar and Daddy said, "Let's add another penny to it every day and by the end of the year, we'll have a nice collection. We can be happy together!"

Tom smiled and hugged his parents. He was so lucky to have such a great family. He couldn't wait to organize more pennies with them!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bike. He had a red bike that he rode every day. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play.

"Hi Timmy, can we ride bikes?" asked Billy.

"Sure!" said Timmy.

They both got on their bikes and started to ride around. Timmy's bike was very reliable, but Billy's bike was old and slow.

"Timmy, your bike is so fast!" said Billy.

"Yeah, it's my favorite bike," said Timmy.

They rode around for a while until they got tired. They stopped and put their bikes down. Timmy put his hand on his chest and said, "I'm tired."

Billy said, "Me too. Your bike is so fast. I wish mine was like yours."

Timmy smiled and said, "Maybe we can race next time. Then your bike can speed up too!"

Once upon a time there was a girl called Donna. She was very anxious because she had to clean her vehicle. Every day when she woke up, she looked at her vehicle and her heart beat faster. She was so worried.

One day, Donna decided she could not wait any longer. She had to clean her vehicle. She went outside and got a bucket, a cloth and some soapy water.

Donna started washing the vehicle. She scrubbed with the cloth and used the soapy water to get rid of all the nasty dirt. She worked hard and after a long time, the vehicle was clean. Donna was so happy.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her favorite blue ink pen. Her mommy always told her to keep her desk tidy, so she made sure to put the cap back on the pen when she was finished.

One day, Lily entered a drawing contest at school. She worked very hard on her drawing and was proud of it. When the judges announced the winner, Lily's name was called! Everyone applauded and cheered for her.

Later that day, Lily's mommy asked her how she won the contest. Lily replied, "I made sure to keep my desk tidy, so I could find my ink pen quickly. And when I drew my picture, I tried my best and didn't give up. That's why I won!" Her mommy smiled and gave her a big hug.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play with cards. They have many cards with animals and colors. They make piles and match the cards.

One day, Sara finds a card that is torn. It is a card with a big lion. She likes the lion card. She is sad. She shows the card to Ben.

"Oh no, your card is broken!" Ben says. "Do you want to fix it?"

"Yes, please. How can we fix it?" Sara asks.

Ben thinks. He has an idea. He gets some tape from his backpack. He puts the tape on the card. He sticks the two pieces together.
