"There, your card is fixed!" Ben says. He gives the card to Sara.

Sara smiles. She looks at the card. The lion is still there. The tape is shiny. She thinks the card is amazing.

"Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. You made my card amazing!" Sara says.

Ben smiles too. He is happy. He likes to help Sara. They hug. They play with the cards again. They have fun.

"Are you ready to go to the park?" Mommy asked.

"No," said little John. He was playing with his yellow trucks on the rug.

"We need to leave now," said Mommy.

John shook his head. He didn't want to go.

Mommy sighed. "John, if we delay any more, it will be morning."

Little John looked out the window at the bright yellow sunshine. He smiled and said, "Okay, Mommy. Let's go!"

Jane was very tired. She wanted to take a nap. She asked her mom, "Will you take me to the cliff to sleep?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes of course!"

When they arrived at the cliff, Jane looked out at the beautiful view. It was so fair. Jane was so excited. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for taking me here!"

They lay down together on the grass. The sun was setting in the sky. Jane started to feel sleepy. Her mom said, "We should go to sleep now. The night is coming."

So, Jane and her mom closed their eyes and fell asleep at the cliff. Jane dreamed of the beautiful fair view from the cliff and of running through the grass. When Jane's mom woke up, she carried Jane back home feeling happy.

Once upon a time there was a dark cane. It was special and it wanted to find a perfect match. It looked in the sky and down the street but could not seem to find one. So it decided to take a walk.

It went to the park and saw a lot of different things but still could not find its match. Then, it heard a happy voice! It was a three year old boy. He had a cane, too, and it shone brightly in the sunshine. The dark cane and the boyâ€™s cane looked very similar.

The dark cane was so happy that it had finally found its match. The two canes spent the day walking and playing together. They laughed and had lots of fun.

At the end of the day, when the sun began to set, the boy said goodbye and gave his cane to the dark cane. Now, the dark cane was never lonely. It always had its perfect match by its side.

Once upon a time, there was a famous wall. Everyone knew it was very important. One day, a group of three children wanted to take a closer look. The oldest, who was three-years-old, was so brave that he stepped up to the wall first. He thought the wall looked so tall and strong, he was sure he could climb it. Taking a deep breath, the brave little three-year-old started climbing. He made it all the way to the top and was so proud of himself. He waved from up on the wall to his friends below and smiled. THE QUEEN BEE

Two kings' sons once upon a time went into the world to seek their

fortunes; but they soon fell into a wasteful foolish way of living, so

that they could not return home again. Then their brother, who was a

little insignificant dwarf, went out to seek for his brothers: but when

he had found them they only laughed at him, to think that he, who was so

young and simple, should try to travel through the world, when they, who

were so much wiser, had been unable to get on. However, they all set

out on their journey together, and came at last to an ant-hill. The two

elder brothers would have pulled it down, in order to see how the poor

ants in their fright would run about and carry off their eggs. But the

little dwarf said, 'Let the poor things enjoy themselves, I will not

suffer you to trouble them.'

So on they went, and came to a lake where many many ducks were swimming

about. The two brothers wanted to catch two, and roast them. But the

dwarf said, 'Let the poor things enjoy themselves, you shall not kill

them.' Next they came to a bees'-nest in a hollow tree, and there was

so much honey that it ran down the trunk; and the two brothers wanted to

light a fire under the tree and kill the bees, so as to get their honey.

But the dwarf held them back, and said, 'Let the pretty insects enjoy

themselves, I cannot let you burn them.'

At length the three brothers came to a castle: and as they passed by the

stables they saw fine horses standing there, but all were of marble, and

no man was to be seen. Then they went through all the rooms, till they

came to a door on which were three locks: but in the middle of the door

was a wicket, so that they could look into the next room. There they saw

a little grey old man sitting at a table; and they called to him once or

twice, but he did not hear: however, they called a third time, and then

he rose and came out to them.

He said nothing, but took hold of them and led them to a beautiful

table covered with all sorts of good things: and when they had eaten and

drunk, he showed each of them to a bed-chamber.

The next morning he came to the eldest and took him to a marble table,

where there were three tablets, containing an account of the means by

which the castle might be disenchanted. The first tablet said: 'In the

wood, under the moss, lie the thousand pearls belonging to the king's

daughter; they must all be found: and if one be missing by set of sun,

he who seeks them will be turned into marble.'

The eldest brother set out, and sought for the pearls the whole day:

but the evening came, and he had not found the first hundred: so he was

turned into stone as the tablet had foretold.

The next day the second brother undertook the task; but he succeeded no

better than the first; for he could only find the second hundred of the

pearls; and therefore he too was turned into stone.

At last came the little dwarf's turn; and he looked in the moss; but it

was so hard to find the pearls, and the job was so tiresome!--so he sat

down upon a stone and cried. And as he sat there, the king of the ants

(whose life he had saved) came to help him, with five thousand ants; and

it was not long before they had found all the pearls and laid them in a

heap.

The second tablet said: 'The key of the princess's bed-chamber must be

fished up out of the lake.' And as the dwarf came to the brink of it,

he saw the two ducks whose lives he had saved swimming about; and they

dived down and soon brought in the key from the bottom.

The third task was the hardest. It was to choose out the youngest and

the best of the king's three daughters. Now they were all beautiful, and

all exactly alike: but he was told that the eldest had eaten a piece of

sugar, the next some sweet syrup, and the youngest a spoonful of honey;

so he was to guess which it was that had eaten the honey.

Then came the queen of the bees, who had been saved by the little dwarf

from the fire, and she tried the lips of all three; but at last she sat

upon the lips of the one that had eaten the honey: and so the dwarf knew

which was the youngest. Thus the spell was broken, and all who had been

turned into stones awoke, and took their proper forms. And the dwarf

married the youngest and the best of the princesses, and was king after

her father's death; but his two brothers married the other two sisters.

The boy was a bit wary at first but decided to accept the offer. He stepped forward and gave the voice a hug. As soon as he did, the voice revealed itself to be an old sparrow. The sparrow gave him the key and said: "Go ahead and explore the hut. I'm sure you'll find something interesting inside!"

The boy thanked the sparrow and used the key to unlock the door of the hut. After a few moments of exploring inside, he found a beautiful old desk that was covered in dust. He was amazed by his find, and smiled as he closed the door and locked it again with the key. He was sure he would come back to explore the hut again soon.

Ben and Sam were best friends. They liked to play outside and go on adventures. One day, they saw a kayak by the lake. It was red and shiny and looked like fun.

"Wow, look at that kayak!" Ben said. "Can we try it?"

"I don't know," Sam said. "It's not ours. Maybe someone left it here."

"Or maybe they don't want it anymore," Ben said. "Let's go and see."

They ran to the kayak and touched it. It was smooth and hard. They looked inside and saw two paddles.

"Let's go for a ride," Ben said. "It will be fun."

"But what if someone comes back and gets angry?" Sam said. "We should ask first."

"Who are we going to ask?" Ben said. "There's no one here. Come on, don't be scared."

Ben climbed into the kayak and grabbed a paddle. He waited for Sam to join him.

Sam looked around. He felt bad. He knew it was wrong to take something that was not theirs. He wanted to have fun, but he also wanted to be good.

"Ben, I don't think we should do this," Sam said. "It's not nice. Let's go and play something else."

Ben frowned. He was annoyed. He wanted to go on the kayak. He thought Sam was being silly.

"Fine, be a baby," Ben said. "I'm going without you."

He pushed the kayak into the water and started to paddle. He felt happy and free. He didn't care about Sam.

Sam watched Ben go. He felt sad and lonely. He wished Ben would listen to him. He hoped Ben would be safe.

Soon, Ben was far away from the shore. He looked around and saw the lake was big and beautiful. He saw fish and birds and trees. He smiled and paddled faster.

But then, he heard a loud voice.

"Hey, you! Get out of my kayak!"

Ben turned and saw a man on the shore. He was big and angry. He was waving his arms and shouting.

Ben felt scared. He realized he had made a mistake. He had taken someone else's kayak. He had been bad.

He tried to paddle back, but it was hard. The wind was blowing and the water was choppy. He felt tired and sorry.

The man ran into the water and swam towards Ben. He reached the kayak and grabbed it. He pulled Ben out and dragged him to the shore.

He was very mad. He yelled at Ben and asked him why he had taken his kayak. He said he had been generous and let other people use his kayak, but only if they asked first. He said Ben had been rude and selfish.

Ben felt ashamed. He didn't know what to say. He wished he had listened to Sam. He wished he had been good.

He looked at Sam, who was still on the shore. Sam looked at him with pity and concern. He walked over to Ben and the man.

He said he was sorry for what Ben had done. He said they were friends and they had seen the kayak and wanted to try it. He said Ben had not listened to him and had gone without asking. He said he had tried to stop him and had stayed behind.

He said they had learned their lesson and they would never do it again. He said they were sorry and they hoped the man would forgive them.

The man looked at Sam and Ben. He saw they were young and scared. He saw they had made a mistake and they were sorry. He felt his anger fade.

He said he was glad Sam had been honest and brave. He said he was glad Ben had come back and had apologized. He said he would forgive them, but only if they promised to be good and to respect other people's things.

He said he would be generous and let them use his kayak, but only if they asked first and followed his rules. He said he would teach them how to paddle and how to be safe on the water.

He said he hoped they would enjoy the kayak and the lake, but also learn to be good and kind.

Sam and Ben nodded. They said they were sorry and they thanked the man. They said they would be good and they would respect his kayak. They said they would like to learn from him and have fun with him.

They hugged each other and smiled. They felt happy and relieved. They had made a new friend and they had learned a valuable lesson.

They had learned to be good and generous.

Molly didn't know what to do. She was so sad that she couldn't get her cocoa. Then, her mom came in and said "Let me try." She reached up, and with one big stretch, she got the cocoa.

Molly was so happy and said "Thank you, Mom!" as she enjoyed her cocoa. Next time, Molly thought, she would ask for help if she wanted cocoa. She had learned her lesson!

Once upon a time there were two friends named Joe and Ben. Joe and Ben were always playing together. One day Joe said to Ben, "Let's play hide and seek!"
Ben was anxious, but he agreed to play. They counted together to a big number and then Joe hid.
Joe hid in the tallest tree he could find. Ben started counting and looking for Joe. He checked every bush and tree, but he couldn't find Joe anywhere. Suddenly, Ben had a great idea. He knew Joe often hid in the tallest tree.
He ran over to the tree, and sure enough, there was Joe!
Ben said, "I found you! Now, it's your turn to hideâ€.
Joe smiled and the two friends counted again to a big number and then Joe went to hide. Joe included himself in the game and was excited to hide.
Ben anxiously searched but he was sure that Joe would be the hardest to find. After what seemed like a long search, Ben found Joe and they both laughed. Joe and Ben continued to include each other in their fun game of hide and seek.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden where she had a big cactus. One day, Lily's friend came to her garden to play. Her friend accidentally touched the cactus and got hurt. Lily's friend started crying and Lily felt sorry for her.

Lily's mother came to see what happened and saw that her friend was hurt. She asked Lily what happened and Lily told her that her friend touched the cactus and got hurt. Lily's mother wrapped a bandage around her friend's finger and told her that she will be okay.

Lily's friend stopped crying and thanked Lily's mother for helping her. Lily felt happy that her friend was okay and they continued to play in the garden. From that day on, Lily made sure to tell her friends to be careful around the cactus.

Once upon a time there was an old man who was very foolish. One day he was walking in the countryside and he saw a bottle lying on the ground. He picked it up and he understood that it had belonged to someone else. He was so excited that he started jumping up and down.

He ran back to his room and held the bottle close while he examined it. It was sparkling and it was so beautiful that it almost seemed magical. He thought that if he drank from it he would feel happy and powerful. But he was a foolish old man and he could not understand this.

So instead, he took the bottle and put it carefully in a special box. He told everyone that he had found a special magical bottle and he showed it off whenever he could. But no one understood the true power of the bottle and they just laughed at the foolish old man.

The end.

Mama was in the kitchen making a new meal. She had all the ingredients mixed together in a pot. They were spicy. She opened the pot and added some soap. Then she stirred it all together and closed the lid.

The soup smelled delicious! Mama put a big bowl on the table and the family gathered around to enjoy it. They all ate it with big spoons. The soup was nice and hot and a little spicy.

When everyone had finished eating, Mama filled the bowl with warm soapy water. She passed it around the table and everyone took turns washing their spoons.

When they had all rinsed their spoons off, Mama closed the bowl and put it away. Everyone praised her for her delicious spicy soup. The family all had a special moment and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot loved to go for walks with his owner. One day, Spot and his owner went to the park. Spot saw a big tree and ran over to it. He shook his body and a bunch of leaves fell on him.

After playing in the leaves, Spot's owner said it was time for some exercise. They started running around the park. Spot loved to run and jump. He felt very happy and healthy.

When they finished exercising, Spot's owner gave him a fancy treat. It was a big bone covered in yummy sauce. Spot licked his lips and ate it all up. He was very happy and felt like a fancy dog. The end.

Lily and Tom were playing with bubbles in the park. They had a big bottle of soap and a wand to make the bubbles. They were very jolly and laughed as they chased the bubbles in the air.

"Look, Lily, I can make a big bubble!" Tom said, as he blew hard on the wand. A huge bubble came out and floated in the wind.

"Wow, Tom, that's amazing!" Lily said, clapping her hands. "Can I try?"

"Sure, Lily, here you go." Tom handed her the wand and the bottle. "But be careful, don't spill the soap."

Lily took the wand and dipped it in the bottle. She tried to blow a big bubble, but she blew too hard and the soap splashed on her face. She felt a sting in her eyes and started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow, it hurts!" Lily wailed, rubbing her eyes.

Tom felt sorry for Lily and ran to help her. He grabbed a tissue from his pocket and tried to wipe her face. But he was not gentle and he pushed the tissue too hard on her eyes. Lily felt more pain and cried louder.

"Stop, stop, stop, you're hurting me!" Lily screamed, pushing Tom away.

Tom was shocked and hurt by Lily's push. He dropped the tissue and the bottle and the wand. He felt angry and sad. He picked up a rock and threw it at Lily. The rock hit Lily on the head and made a big bump. Lily fell to the ground and fainted.

Tom realized what he had done and felt scared and sorry. He ran to Lily and tried to wake her up. But Lily did not move or talk. Tom cried and cried and cried.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on tours with her family. One day, they went on a tour to a beautiful beach. Lily was so excited to play in the sand and swim in the water.

But when they arrived, Lily saw that the beach was very dirty. There was trash everywhere! Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. Then, her mom told her that they could help clean up the beach. So, Lily and her family picked up all the trash and made the beach clean again.

After they finished, Lily felt happy and relaxed. She learned that it's important to take care of the environment and keep it clean. From that day on, whenever she went on a tour, she made sure to leave the place better than she found it.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Annie. She was three years old and loved to play. One day she was playing in the garden with her pet dog. Suddenly, the pet dog jumped onto the grass and Annie heard a pop. When she looked around, she saw that her shoe was gone!

Annie was very sad and started to cry. Her mom came out to see what was wrong and Annie told her about the shoe. Mom knew Annie needed a new shoe so she said it was time to go to the store.

At the store, Mom told Annie to pick out the shoes she liked. Annie looked around and saw all of the different shoes. Eventually, she chose a serious looking pair of black shoes.

Once the shoe was on, Annie felt so much better. She thanked her mom for helping her find the right shoe and said she was ready to play again. Mom smiled and they both went back into the garden to continue their fun time.

The end.

One day, a big whale was swimming in the deep blue sea. The whale was very mysterious. It had a big smile on its face and liked to play with the little fish.

The mysterious whale loved to relax in the warm water. It would lay on its back and let the waves rock it like a baby. The little fish would swim around the whale, and they all felt happy and safe.

One day, the mysterious whale and the little fish found a beautiful place to relax. It was a quiet spot with lots of colorful plants and pretty shells. They all had a fun day, playing and relaxing together in their new secret place.

Once upon a time, there were three little animals: a cat, a dog, and a mouse. They were all friends, but sometimes the cat was bossy and told the others what to do. One day, they wanted to have a picnic, but they couldn't decide what to eat. The cat said they should eat fish, the dog said they should eat bones, and the mouse said they should eat cheese.

They argued and argued until they realized that they were all hungry and didn't want to fight anymore. So, they decided to unite and make a menu together. The cat brought some fish, the dog brought some bones, and the mouse brought some cheese. They all shared and had a great time together.

After the picnic, they realized that it was much better to work together and share than to argue and be bossy. They learned that everyone has good ideas and that it's important to listen to each other. From that day on, they always made their menus together and had lots of fun. The moral of the story is that it's better to work together and be friends than to be bossy and argue.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her favorite toy, a shiny red ball. One day, Lily was playing with her ball outside when she accidentally threw it too hard and it broke into pieces. She was very sad.

Lily's mom saw how sad she was and gave her a big hug. She told Lily that sometimes things break, but that's okay because we can always fix them or get new ones. Lily felt a little better, but she still missed her ball.

The next day, Lily's mom took her to the park. They went on a big swing and Lily felt like she was flying. She took a big breath of air and her mom told her that she was breathing in oxygen. Lily didn't know what oxygen was, but it sounded important.

As they were leaving the park, Lily saw a boy playing with a shiny red ball just like hers. She ran over to him and asked if she could play too. The boy said yes and they had so much fun together. Lily realized that even though her ball broke, she could still have fun and be independent by making new friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old and loved playing outdoors. One day, Jane decided to explore the fields near her home.

As she roamed around, Jane found a promise rock. On the rock was written something special. She couldn't read it, so she turned around.

Suddenly, Jane noticed a rough-looking man walking towards her. She started to feel scared and hid behind the bush.

The man started to talk. He said, "I want you to cover the promise rock. If you don't, I'll take away something you love."

Jane was too frightened to move. She thought for a moment and then decided to stand up and face the man. She said, "I will not cover the promise rock. I don't have to do what you say!"

The man thought for a moment and then he smiled. He said, "I can see you're brave. I won't make you do anything, but please remember this. Promises should always be kept."

With that, the man walked away. Jane was relieved and happily continued her journey, keeping her promise to never forget the promise rock.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Tom and Tim. Tom and Tim were playing in the park.

Tim said to Tom, "Let's play hide and seek!"
Tom was so excited and they started to look for a good hiding spot.

Tom found a secret spot behind the big tree. It was very attractive, with lots of colorful flowers. Tim counted to three and Tom hid behind the tree.

Tom waited and waited, but Tim couldn't find him. Tom started to giggle. Finally, Tim found Tom and said, "You found a secret place! It's so attractive!"

Tom beamed with pride and said, "I did! Let's see who can find the best secret spot next time!"

Tom and Tim laughed and continued to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who had a very special stuffed bear named Teddy. Teddy was always with Lily, and she loved him very much. One day, Lily and her family went on a trip to the beach. While they were playing in the sand, Lily accidentally dropped Teddy and he got lost in the waves.

Lily was very sad and cried for Teddy. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we'll find him." But Lily was worried that they would never find Teddy and he would be wasted in the ocean forever.

A kind man saw Lily crying and asked what was wrong. Lily told him about Teddy and how she missed him very much. The man promised to help find Teddy and said he was a reliable friend. After searching for a while, they found Teddy washed up on the shore. Lily was so happy and hugged Teddy tightly. "Thank you for helping me find Teddy," she said to the man. "You're a reliable friend too!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very intelligent. She went to the store with her mom and bought a new toy. The toy had lots of little nails in it, and the little girl wanted to remember where each nail went. She used her intelligent mind to remember where to place each nail and at the end of the day she finished her toy. She was so proud of her work! When her mom came home, the little girl showed her the finished toy, and her mom clapped with joy. The little girl was very proud of her accomplishment, and promised to always remember how intelligent she was.

Once there was a boy called Jake. Jake loved to play in the park with his friends. One day, he was playing in the park when he fell. He was so scared and he didn't know what to do. He started to worry.

His mom saw him from the other side of the park and ran over to help. Jake was still scared but when he saw his mom everything felt normal. She picked him up and hugged him.

Jake's mom kissed him on the forehead. She smiled and said "it's ok, these things happen". Jake felt better now and wasn't worried anymore. He hugged his mom and they started to play together in the park.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Lily and Max. They were playing in the garden outside of Lily's house. Lily's garden was so rich and colorful, with big green trees and red, yellow, and orange flowers.

Max looked around and noticed something. He asked Lily, "Do you recognize that thing in the garden?" Lily wasn't sure what he was talking about. Max pointed to a spot in the garden and said, "That big yellow thing is special."

Lily walked closer and then she recognized it! It was a huge yellow butterfly! She said, "Wow! It looks so pretty." The butterfly flew over to a nearby flower and started to drink the nectar.

Max and Lily watched the butterfly for a long time. Eventually, the butterfly flew away but Max and Lily never forgot about it. They will always remember their special moment in the rich garden.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Peter. One day Peter went for a walk in the countryside. He walked and walked and soon he saw something strange. There were lots of peppers growing on a bush! So Peter decided to pick some and he filled his pockets with as many as he could.

On his way home he heard a noise. It was a strange sound and it made Peter panic. He started to run but the peppers kept bouncing out of his pockets. Before long he had lost them all!

Peter was very sad that he had lost his peppers but then he noticed something useful. There were lots of pepper plants growing near where the peppers had bounced out of his pocket. Peter was very happy! He picked some more peppers and made his way home with a pocket full of peppers.

He was so relieved he had found more peppers, he never wanted to panic like that again! So from then on, he always remembered to be careful when he was picking peppers.

Lila and Tom were playing with paper. They liked to fold it and make shapes. Lila made a paper horse. She was proud of it. She showed it to Tom.

"Look, I made a horse!" she said.

Tom looked at the paper horse. He did not like it. He wanted to make a better horse. He took Lila's paper horse and tore it.

"That's not a horse, that's a mess!" he said.

Lila was sad and angry. She cried. She wanted her paper horse back.

"Why did you do that?" she asked Tom.

Tom was not sorry. He was mean. He laughed at Lila.

"Because I can make a better horse than you!" he said.

He folded another paper and made a horse. He showed it to Lila.

"See, this is a horse!" he said.

Lila looked at Tom's paper horse. It was not a better horse. It was a big and ugly horse. It had too many legs and a long nose. It looked like a monster.

"That's not a horse, that's a monster!" she said.

Tom was surprised. He did not like Lila's words. He felt ashamed. He realized he was wrong.

"Maybe you're right, maybe it's a monster," he said.

He looked at Lila's paper horse. It was a modest horse. It had four legs and a short nose. It looked like a real horse.

"Maybe your horse was better than mine," he said.

He felt sorry. He wanted to be nice. He gave Lila his paper horse.

"Here, you can have my horse. I'm sorry I tore your horse," he said.

Lila was happy. She liked Tom's paper horse. She forgave Tom.

"Thank you, Tom. I like your horse. It's a funny horse," she said.

She gave Tom a hug. They became friends. They played with paper horses. They had fun.

Lily and Anna were best friends. They liked to play with dolls and dress up. One day, they found a pretty box under Lily's bed. It had a lock and a key.

"What is in the box?" Anna asked.

"I don't know. It is a secret," Lily said. She took the key and opened the box. Inside, there were many shiny things. There were rings, necklaces, bracelets, and earrings.

"Wow, they are so pretty!" Anna said. She reached for a ring.

"Stop! Don't touch them!" Lily said. She pulled the box away from Anna. "They are mine! They are from my grandma. She gave them to me before she went away. She said they are very special and I have to keep them safe."

"But I just want to look at them. Please, can I try one on?" Anna said. She felt sad and angry. She thought Lily was being mean and selfish.

"No, you can't! They are not for you. They are only for me. Go away!" Lily said. She closed the box and put it back under the bed. She turned her back to Anna.

Anna felt tears in her eyes. She did not want to play with Lily anymore. She got up and ran out of the room. She did not say goodbye.

Lily heard Anna leave. She felt lonely and sorry. She did not mean to hurt Anna. She loved her friend. She wanted to share her pretty things with her. But she was afraid to lose them. She remembered how her grandma hugged her and told her to take good care of them. She missed her grandma very much.

She got the box out again and opened it. She looked at the shiny things. They were pretty, but they did not make her happy. She wished Anna was there with her. She wanted to say sorry and give her a hug. She wanted to tell her the secret of the box. She wanted to play with her again.

She took the key and ran after Anna. She hoped she would find her and make up with her. She hoped Anna would still be her friend. She hoped they could seat together and look at the pretty things and smile.

Once there was a brave little girl. She loved exploring the world around her.

One day, she went on a walk in the woods. She found an apple tree and decided to pick one of the big apples for her snack. As she was enjoying the sweet apple, she grew tired. She decided to have a nap under the apple tree.

The sun was warm and the breeze was gentle, so she curled up and fell fast asleep. She dreamed of all the brave adventures she would have in the future.

When she woke up, she felt refreshed. She climbed down from the apple tree and went off to explore new paths. She was ready for more brave adventures!

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a girl named Lily. She loved to eat pastry. One day, her mom made a big pastry for her. Lily was very happy.

But, Lily was worried. It was a rainy day, and she wanted to eat the pastry outside. She did not want the pastry to get wet. So, she waited for the rain to stop.

After a while, the rain stopped. The sun came out and it was dry outside. Lily took her pastry and went to the park. She sat under a big tree and ate her yummy pastry. She was not worried anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Bob. Bob wanted a pet to play with, so his mommy showed him a plate with a little kitten. The kitten was so gentle and soft. Bob's mommy asked him, "Do you like the little kitty?"

Bob couldn't help but smile and nod his head in excitement. "Yes!" he said.

Bob's mommy smiled and said, "Ok, then it's yours. What are you going to name it?"

Bob thought for a moment and said, "Fluffy!"

Bob and Fluffy became best friends. Bob would show his friend all his toys and Fluffy would sleep in Bob's bed, purring softly. Every day, Bob would show Fluffy how much he loved him by stroking his fur gently.

Bob and Fluffy were happy together, and Bob's mommy was happy too.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emily. Emily was a very independent girl and she loved to go outside and do things by herself. One day she was feeling happy and decided to go skipping. She skipped through the long grass and sang a song. Soon she came to a big garden full of different plants and flowers.

But what caught Emily's eye was the strange little trees growing in the garden. She couldn't believe her eyes! They were broccoli trees! She skipped over to the trees and looked closely at the broccoli. It was so delicious and juicy.

Emily started picking the broccoli and putting it in the basket she was carrying. Then she skipped off happily to deliver the broccoli to her family. From that day on, Emily was so proud of herself for being so independent and she never forgot her broccoli picking adventures.

Once upon a time there were two friends. One was a horse and one was a boy. They had known each other since they were young.

One sunny day the boy came to the stable to visit the horse. He called out to the horse, "Hello! Fancy seeing you here!" The horse replied excitedly, "Come on in! I have something to show you!"

The boy followed the horse into the stable. He saw lots of fancy things in there. The horse said, "This is what I wanted to show you. It's a skipping rope!"

The boy was delighted. He tied the rope to a post and began skipping glee. The horse watched him and smiled.

They spent the rest of the afternoon together, enjoying the sunshine and playing skipping. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a mummy and a daddy. They had a little boy called Jack. Every day, mummy and daddy would prepare Jack's breakfast. Today was special. He was getting ready to go to the park.

Daddy said to Jack, "Let's go get ready for the park! What do you want to bring?" Jack said he wanted to bring his toy. He had a very special toy - a blue car. Daddy said, "Let's go."

Jack, Mummy, and Daddy got ready and went to the park. Jack ran around and explored. He saw a lot of colourful flowers, so he picked some for Mummy. Mummy thanked him with a big hug.

Jack and his family spent a peaceful afternoon in the park. Jack played with his toy and ran around and laughed. He felt very happy! When the sun started to set, they prepared to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He had an adorable pet cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to play with Tom, and they would race around the house all day long.

One day, Tom found a big ball of string. He thought it would be fun to play with Kitty. So, he threw the ball, and Kitty raced after it. As Kitty played, the string made a big knot. Tom laughed as he watched Kitty try to untangle the knot.

In the end, Tom helped Kitty untangle the knot. They were both very happy. They continued to race and play together, and they lived happily ever after.

Jimmy was new in town and he wanted to make friends. He saw a group of children playing and decided to join them. When Jimmy asked if he could join, the group said yes. But he didn't fit in. Everyone stared at him, and he felt uncomfortable. He tried hard to be part of the group, but it didn't work. He asked the group if everything was okay, but they just kept looking at him.

Jimmy started to feel very sad. He asked if he could still stay in the group, but the kids said no. They said he was too different and made the group uncomfortable. So, Jimmy left the group and started to walk away. He felt sad and alone.

Jimmy kept his head down and walked home. He wished he hadn't asked to join the group. He didn't feel like he belonged.

Once upon a time, there was a doggy who lived in a house with his family. The doggy was very happy and loved to play with his family. One day, he was given a thick bone. The doggy was very excited. He wanted to show the bone to his family, so he picked it up with his mouth and bit it. But he bit it too hard. His teeth went right through it. Now he had no bone!

The doggy was very sad. He went outside to see if he could find another bone. He ran around and around until he found another bone. It was not as thick as before, but the doggy was excited. He grabbed the bone and put it in his mouth. He bit it, and it broke too. Now he had no bone again.

The doggy was very frustrated and this time, he was angry too. He looked all around for a bone, but every bone he found was too thin and he had to leave it behind. Eventually, he got tired and went back home. When he arrived, he was sad because he had no bone to show his family. He would have to go without a bone.

The bad ending of the doggy's story teaches us that sometimes even if we try, we don't always get what we want. It can be sad, but remember: it's okay to not always get what you want!

Once upon a time, there was a stubborn little girl. She lived in a small village. Every day she was in a hurry to do her chores. She raced around, trying to get them all done. One day, she was hurrying so much that she almost ran into a wall! Luckily, she stopped in time to avoid a crash. From then on, she ran around a little less quickly. After that, she always remembered to take the time to enjoy her village and the people around her.

Once upon a time, there was a modern band. The band made really cool music. All of the people in the town enjoyed listening to the band's music.

One day, while everyone was listening to the band at a concert, a giant bellowing noise filled the air. Everyone looked up and noticed a huge animal in the sky, and it was getting closer and closer!

Suddenly, the band stopped playing, and all of the people started to worry and scream. Then, one brave band member stepped forward and said that he had a plan. He said that he was going to try to rescue the animal!

He asked everyone to clap as loud as they could, so he could find the animal in the sky and bring it down safely. Everyone clapped, and the band member flew up in the air and grabbed the animal. The animal was so happy.

The band member brought the animal down to the ground, and everyone cheered. The band started to play again, and everyone celebrated. The band member was a hero and the modern band was very proud.

Once there was a package. It was very attractive and hung from the wall. Inside the package was a mysterious gift.

Every day, a little girl would come to the package and try to open it. It didn't matter how hard she tried, it was too hard to open.

One day, the package spoke to the little girl. It said, "I have a special surprise inside for you. Hang me at a safe place and the surprise will be revealed."

The little girl was so excited that she found the perfect spot and hung the package there. Then, she stepped back and opened the package. Inside was a beautiful toy doll! The little girl was so happy that she hugged the package and thanked it for the wonderful surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow house. In the house, there was a girl named Sally. Sally loved to paint. She had a lot of fun making pretty pictures.

One day, Sally's friend Timmy came over to play. They decided to paint together. Timmy said, "Sally, let's paint a big, yellow sun!" Sally agreed, and they started to paint the sun on a big piece of paper.

While they were painting, the telephone rang. Sally picked it up and said, "Hello?" It was her grandma on the other side. Grandma said, "Hi Sally! I miss you. Can I come visit you today?" Sally was very happy and said, "Yes, Grandma! Please come. We are painting a big, yellow sun!"

Grandma came over, and they all painted together. They had a great time, and the big, yellow sun was very pretty. At the end of the day, they hung the painting on the wall, and it made everyone smile.

Mommy and Lucy were in their garden. Mommy showed Lucy a flower pot and said, "Look Lucy! This wire is coming out of the ground. It's very ugly." Lucy was so excited to see it.

Mommy said, "Let's take this wire away. It's not very nice." So Mommy got a shovel and started to dig around the wire. Lucy watched and helped.

Mommy said, "Now we will spray this flower pot to make it look better!" Lucy liked the idea and ran to the kitchen to get the sprayer.

Mommy and Lucy sprayed the pot together. When they finished, the pot was even prettier than before. Mommy smiled and said, "See how much nicer it looks!"

Lucy was proud of what she had done. She smiled and said, "I helped make it pretty!"

Mommy ruffled Lucy's hair and said, "Yes you did, honey! Now let's go inside for some ice cream."

Lucy was so happy. She'd helped Mommy and made the ugly flower pot pretty again.

One day, a little girl named Sue and her mom were talking. Sue said, "Mom, I want a holiday." Mom smiled and said, "We can plan a fun trip, but not too expensive."

They looked at a big book with pictures of places. Sue saw a picture of a beach. She said, "I want to go here!" Mom said, "That's a nice beach. Let's save money for our trip."

Sue helped Mom save money. She put coins in a jar. One day, the jar was full. Mom said, "We have enough money for our holiday!"

They went to the beach. Sue played in the sand and swam in the water. She was very happy. At the end of the day, Sue said, "Thank you, Mom, for our fun holiday!"

One day, a little girl named Sarah went outside to play in her backyard. She saw a soccer ball sitting there and she was really excited. She picked it up, and it felt fit in her hands.

She began to kick the soccer ball. She kicked it hard across the backyard. She kicked it so hard that it went over the fence and she couldn't find it.

Sarah was upset. She wanted her soccer ball back. She called her mom to help her find it. Mom looked over the fence and saw the soccer ball. She then pulled it back over the fence to Sarah.

Sarah was so happy. She hugged her mom, thanked her, and went right back to kicking the soccer ball around in the backyard. She was having so much fun.

Lila and Ben are friends. They live in a small town. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big balloon in the sky. It is red and yellow and blue.

"Wow, look at that balloon!" Lila says. "It is so big and pretty!"

"Maybe it is a magic balloon," Ben says. "Maybe it can take us to a faraway place."

Lila and Ben run to the balloon. They want to touch it. But the balloon is too high. They cannot reach it.

"Maybe we can climb a tree," Lila says. "Maybe then we can get the balloon."

They find a thin tree near the balloon. They try to climb it. But the tree is too thin. It bends and shakes. Lila and Ben fall down.

"Ouch, that hurt!" Lila says. "The tree is too thin. It cannot hold us."

"Maybe we can ask someone for help," Ben says. "Maybe someone has a ladder or a rope."

They look around. They see a man with a big hat. He is holding a string. The string is tied to the balloon.

"Excuse me, sir," Lila says. "Can we have your balloon? We like it very much."

The man smiles. He says, "Sure, you can have my balloon. But you have to do something for me first."

"What do we have to do?" Ben asks.

"You have to believe," the man says. "You have to believe that the balloon is magic. You have to believe that it can take you to a faraway place. You have to believe that anything is possible."

Lila and Ben nod. They say, "We believe. We believe in the magic balloon."

The man gives them the string. He says, "Hold on tight. And don't let go."

Lila and Ben hold the string. They feel the balloon lift them up. They see the town below them. They see the park, the houses, the cars, the people. They see the clouds, the sun, the birds, the stars. They see a faraway place. They see a magic place.

They smile. They say, "Thank you, sir. Thank you for the magic balloon."

The man waves. He says, "You're welcome, kids. Have fun. And keep believing."

Once upon a time, in a big, green forest, there was a chubby, little bunny. This bunny loved to play with his friends. They would run, jump, and make lots of noise while playing.

One day, while they were playing, a big, kind bear came to the forest. The bear could do a funny trick. He would bow to the trees and the trees would bow back. The chubby bunny and his friends were very happy to see this.

So, the chubby bunny asked the big bear to teach them how to bow. The bear said, "Yes, I will help you." They all tried to bow to the trees, and the trees bowed back. They made a lot of noise, laughing and clapping. From that day on, the chubby bunny and his friends would always bow to the trees, and the trees would bow back. They had so much fun playing together in the big, green forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jimmy. He lived in a small village with his mama. Every day he would explore and have lots of fun.

One day, Jimmy found a broken toy on the ground. He was so excited! He knew his mama could repair it.

Jimmy quickly ran back home and asked his mama if she could repair the toy. But his mama said she was very busy and had lots of work to do. Jimmy was disappointed and walked away sadly.

The next day Jimmy asked his mama again, but she was still too busy. Jimmy was sad, but he thought of an idea. He searched the village and asked all his friends if any of them could repair the toy.

Finally, Jimmy found his best friend, Ben. Ben said he could do the repair. Jimmy was so excited! They worked together to repair the toy.

When they were finished, the toy was like new and looked so cool! Jimmy was so happy. He thanked Ben for the repair. Jimmy and Ben had lots of fun playing with the toy.

Jimmy was so glad he had thought of the idea to ask his friends for help. He promised himself to always be brave and never give up.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her pillow every night before bed. Her pillow was soft and fluffy, and she loved to hug it tight.

One day, Lily's mom became very harsh with her. She scolded Lily for not cleaning up her toys. Lily felt very sad and cried herself to sleep that night.

The next day, Lily's pillow became very hard and uncomfortable. She couldn't sleep well and felt very tired the next day. She realized that her sadness and tears had made her pillow change.

Lily learned that being sad and crying can make things become worse. She promised herself to always try to be happy, even when things are hard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, Lily's mom asked her to put the dishes in the dishwasher. Lily was very cheerful and happy to help her mom.

As she was putting the dishes away, Lily accidentally dropped a plate and it broke into many pieces. She started to cry because she was worried that her mom would be angry with her.

Lily's mom heard her crying and came into the kitchen. She saw the broken plate and asked Lily what happened. Lily told her what had happened and apologized for breaking the plate. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, accidents happen. The most important thing is that you tried to help me."

From that day on, Lily learned that it's okay to make mistakes and that it's important to always try your best. She also learned that it's important to ask for help when you need it.

John was walking down the street, thinking about what he needed to buy. Then he saw it: a vendor selling fresh fruits and vegetables. He thought that this was a great place to buy food, so he slowly walked over. But when he got closer, he realized something was wrong. The vendor's stand was filthy, and John hesitated to buy anything. He thought that maybe he should look for something else, but then again he thought about how hungry he was. So he decided to take the risk and went to the vendor and bought an apple.

When he took a bite, he found that it was delicious! He quickly realized that the vendor was selling great food, despite the place being so dirty. John thought it was funny how, with a little patience and trust, he found the yummiest apple and it was worth the extra effort.

John was feeling brave, so he dared to go outside to explore. He saw a lot of different things as he looked around. He noticed an area behind a giant bush that looked like it had some space. He cautiously ventured closer, and to his surprise, he found a sandy path that seemed to fit perfectly in the space. Fearful of what might be hidden there, he froze for a moment. Taking a deep breath, he stepped into the space and followed the sandy path. The path suddenly stopped at the edge of the river. John quickly scanned the riverbank to see if anything was there. He saw something glistening in the water and wondered what it was. Taking all his courage, he slowly walked into the river to take a closer look. He looked down and saw some shining, glistening stones. He had found a treasure! He was too small to carry it, so he had to be creative and come up with a plan. He gently gathered the stones and placed them in his pocket. With a huge smile, he ran back home with the treasure tucked away in his pocket.

Once upon a time, there was a huge musician. He wanted to take a walk in the park and play some music. He grabbed his guitar and headed off. As he walked, he saw lots of animals. He waved to a cow, high-fived a sheep and gave some breadcrumbs to a hungry duck. Soon he came to a big tree in the middle of the park. He decided to take a seat there and strum his guitar.

Before long, a group of children came to join him. They were very excited to hear the music. The musician strummed away and the children clapped along. It was so much fun! After a few songs, the children took out a jump rope and started to play. The huge musician jumped in and started to skip too. He was having a great time!

Soon all the animals gathered round to watch. The cow mooed, the sheep baaed and the duck quacked. The huge musician felt so happy. He was making lots of new friends. Everyone said goodbye to the musician as the sun began to set. He bid them all farewell and took his guitar off home.

Lila and Max were best friends. They liked to play together at the park. One day, they saw a big tree with green balls on it. They wondered what they were.

"Let's pick one and see," Max said. He climbed the tree and grabbed a green ball. He threw it to Lila. She caught it and looked at it. It was hard and bumpy.

"What is this?" Lila asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it's a toy," Max said.

They tried to roll it, bounce it, and kick it. But it was not fun. It was too heavy and dull.

"Maybe we can open it," Lila said. She found a rock and hit the green ball with it. It cracked and showed a soft green inside and a big brown seed.

"Wow, look at that!" Max said. He climbed down and joined Lila. They touched the green inside. It was creamy and smooth.

"Can we eat it?" Lila asked.

"I don't know. Maybe we should ask someone," Max said.

They saw a lady walking by with a dog. They ran to her and showed her the green ball.

"Excuse me, miss. What is this?" Max asked.

The lady smiled and said, "That's an avocado. It's a fruit. You can eat it. It's very good for you. And very popular too. Many people like it."

"Really? Can we try it?" Lila asked.

"Sure, why not. But you have to share it. And don't eat the seed. It's too hard," the lady said.

She gave them a spoon and helped them scoop out the green inside. They tasted it. It was mild and buttery.

"Mmm, this is yummy," Lila said.

"I like it too," Max said.

They ate the avocado and thanked the lady. They felt happy and full.

They decided to keep the seed and plant it in the park. Maybe they could grow more avocados and share them with their friends.

They settled on a spot near the tree and dug a hole. They put the seed in the hole and covered it with dirt. They watered it with their water bottles.

"Maybe one day, we'll have our own avocado tree," Lila said.

"That would be awesome," Max said.

They hugged and smiled. They were best friends. And they loved avocados.

Once, there was an otter who lived near a big river. She was very dry, so she decided to take a swim. But when she stepped in the water, she noticed that she was much heavier! She thought something was wrong, so she asked the other animals.

The birds told her that when something is dry, it weighs more. The otter was so happy to find out why she felt so heavy. She took another swim and felt much lighter!

From then on, the otter was very careful to stay nice and wet when she swam. She even taught her otter friends, so they didn't weigh as much as they did before.

The river is now full of happy and light otters, thanks to the knowledge she passed on.

Once upon a time, there was a clever mouse who lived in the countryside. One day, the mouse was out exploring when it saw a pile of corn. The mouse was so excited and quickly began to eat it. Suddenly, something underneath the pile of corn revealed itself. It was a tiny door!

The mouse cautiously approached the door and carefully knocked on it. A small voice called out from behind the door, "Who is it?"

The mouse was so surprised. He answered, "It's a mouse. I'm looking for a place to live."

The little voice said, "Come inside! I'm a squirrel, and I'm looking for a friend too!"

The mouse joyfully opened the door, and there was the squirrel, wearing a big smile on its face.

The mouse and the squirrel became great friends. They played all day and bought lots of corn to share. The clever mouse was excited they were now best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Sally. She was only three years old, but already knew how to do so many things. One day, her mom asked her if she wanted to watch a film. Sally said, "Yes!" So they put on a film in their living room and Sally listened to all the sounds coming from the TV.

The film was about a normal family who lived in a cute little house. Sally watched as the family went on fun adventures and she smiled in delight. Sally was especially thrilled when they went to the zoo and saw so many animals! She loved listening to the chirps and roars of the creatures.

After the film was done, Sally said, "Can we watch it again?" Her mom said, "Yes, but later. We must do something else now." So Sally put her feet on the floor and dashed off to play. She knew it would only be a short while before she got to listen to the film again.

Sara was a little girl who loved to hug. She hugged her mom, her dad, her brother, her dog, and her toys. She hugged everyone and everything she saw. But there was one thing she was not allowed to hug: the queen.

The queen was a very important lady who lived in a big castle. She wore a shiny crown and a long dress. She came to visit Sara's town once a year, and everyone had to be very polite and quiet. Sara's mom told her, "You can wave to the queen, but you can't hug her. She doesn't like hugs. It's a rule."

Sara nodded, but she was curious. Why didn't the queen like hugs? Hugs were nice and warm and made people happy. Sara wanted to make the queen happy. She wanted to hug her.

The day came when the queen arrived in her carriage. Sara and her mom stood in the crowd, waiting to see her. Sara saw the queen's face. She looked sad and lonely. Sara felt sorry for her. She thought, maybe the queen needs a hug.

Sara waited for the right moment. When the queen was close enough, Sara ran out of the crowd and hugged her. She hugged her tight and said, "I love you, queen. You are beautiful."

The queen was shocked. She gasped and dropped her purse. The guards shouted and ran to Sara. Sara's mom screamed and ran after her. The crowd gasped and whispered. Sara felt guilty. She knew she had done something bad.

But then, something amazing happened. The queen smiled. She smiled a big, bright smile. She hugged Sara back. She said, "Thank you, little girl. You are brave and kind. You made me happy."

The guards stopped. Sara's mom stopped. The crowd stopped. Everyone was surprised. The queen broke the rule. She hugged Sara.

The queen picked up her purse and waved to the crowd. She said, "This is Sara. She is my friend. She taught me something today. Hugs are good. Hugs are not a rule. Hugs are a gift."

Everyone cheered. Sara cheered. The queen cheered. They hugged again. Sara was happy. She had made a new friend. She had made the queen happy. She was not guilty. She was a hero.

Jack and Jill were playing chase in the hall. Jack was running and jumping and having lots of fun. Jill got a bit careless and tipped over a flower pot. It made a crash and a mess!

Suddenly, Jill felt scared and started to cry. Jack stopped playing and went to her. He said, â€œItâ€™s ok Jill, letâ€™s clean it up.â€ He helped her clean the mess and then gave her a hug.

Jill felt better. She accepted Jackâ€™s help and the two of them were soon playing again. They were even more careful with the flower pots, so no more accidents happened.

Jack and Jill were best friends now and they played together in the hall every day. They accepted each otherâ€™s mistakes, laughed a lot and never got careless again.

Once upon a time, there was a leaf. The leaf wanted to rise up high in the sky, like a kite. It tried to flap its edges, but the wind was too slow.

So the leaf found an idea. It decided to find something sour. It saw a lemon and asked it for a little bit of help. The lemon was sour and strong enough that it could help the leaf rise up high. The leaf felt the sour lemon push it up and up until it was higher than the clouds!

The leaf was so happy that it was flying. It spread its edges to go even higher. It flew over the trees, houses, and even the ocean!

Finally, after a long journey, the leaf had to come down. But it had made its dream come true, and it had risen higher than it ever thought possible!

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny. The bunny liked to hop all around the garden. One day, the bunny saw a big sunflower. It was so tall! The bunny hopped over to the sunflower and looked up at it.

Suddenly, the bunny heard a serious voice. It was the sunflower talking! The sunflower said, "Little bunny, please be careful. Don't hop on my petals." The bunny was surprised that the sunflower could talk. The bunny said, "I'm sorry, Mr. Sunflower. I didn't mean to hop on your petals."

From that day on, the bunny and the sunflower became friends. The bunny would hop around the garden and visit the sunflower every day. The sunflower was always very serious, but the bunny liked to make the sunflower laugh by hopping around and doing silly tricks. They had lots of fun together in the garden. The end.

One day, Lily and Tom went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers, birds and bugs. Lily liked to gather flowers and make a crown. Tom liked to gather bugs and put them in a jar.

"Look, mom, I found a beetle!" Tom said, showing his jar. "It is big and shiny and has spots."

Mom smiled and said, "That is a nice beetle, Tom. But do you think the beetle is happy in the jar?"

Tom thought for a moment. He looked at the beetle, who was crawling and tapping on the glass. He said, "No, I think the beetle is sad. He wants to be free and play with his friends."

Mom nodded and said, "That is right, Tom. Bugs are living things, just like us. They have feelings and needs. They like to explore and have fun. How would you feel if someone put you in a jar?"

Tom said, "I would feel scared and lonely and bored. I would not like that at all."

Mom said, "Then you should let the beetle go, Tom. He will be happier in his home, and you can still watch him from a distance. Maybe you can find another way to enjoy bugs, like drawing them or reading about them."

Tom agreed and opened the jar. He gently placed the beetle on a leaf and said, "Bye, beetle. I am sorry I made you sad. You are adorable and I hope you have a good day."

The beetle waved his antennae and scurried away. Tom felt happy and proud. He learned to respect and care for bugs. He gathered his crayons and paper and started to draw the beetle and his friends. Lily joined him and they had fun together. Mom hugged them and said, "I am proud of you, Tom and Lily. You are kind and curious and creative. You make the world a better place."

Lily and Ben were playing hide and seek in the park. Lily was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Ben ran to a big tree and hid behind it. He saw a rope hanging from a branch. He wanted to swing on the rope like a monkey. He grabbed the rope and tried to swing, but he was clumsy. He slipped and got tangled in the rope. He felt a knot around his leg. He could not move. He was scared.

Lily counted to ten and opened her eyes. She looked for Ben. She did not see him. She called his name. "Ben, where are you? I'm coming to find you!" She walked around the park. She saw the big tree. She heard a whisper. "Lily, help me!" She went to the tree and saw Ben. He was hanging from the rope. He looked sad. She ran to him. "Ben, what happened? Are you okay?" She asked.

Ben told her what happened. He said he was sorry. He said he was silly. He asked her to help him. Lily saw the knot. She tried to untie it, but it was hard. She pulled and twisted the rope, but it did not work. She said, "Don't worry, Ben. I will help you. I will get someone to help us." She looked around. She saw a man walking his dog. She waved and shouted. "Mister, mister, please help us! My friend is stuck in the rope!" The man heard her and came to the tree. He saw Ben. He said, "Oh dear, how did this happen? Don't worry, I will get you down." He climbed the tree and untied the knot. He lifted Ben and brought him down. He checked his leg. He said, "You are lucky. You are not hurt. Just a little bruise. Be careful next time." He smiled and gave him a hug.

Lily and Ben thanked the man. They said they were sorry for the trouble. The man said it was no trouble. He said he was glad they were okay. He said he had to go. He said goodbye and walked away with his dog. Lily and Ben hugged each other. They said they were happy they were friends. They said they would play hide and seek again, but not with the rope. They laughed and ran to the swings. They had fun. They were happy.

John was playing when he saw something hidden under a tree. He wished he knew what it was so he ran over and started digging. After a few moments, he found a magical wish cave! He was so excited and he went inside to explore.

John saw lots of things, including a big wishing well. He closed his eyes and made a wish. He wished for heaps of toys and sweets and before he knew it all the toys were in the cave!

John started playing with all the toys. He was having so much fun! When he got tired he lay down and had a nap. Suddenly he heard a loud noise and he woke up to find that the wish cave was gone and he was home again.

John had a fantastic adventure. He smiled and knew it was a hidden wish come true!

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue sea. One day, Nemo saw a shiny purse at the bottom of the sea. He was curious and wanted to know what was inside the purse. So, he got ready and took a deep breath. He dived into the water and swam towards the purse. When he reached the purse, he opened it and found a shiny pearl. Nemo was so happy and swam back to his home with the pearl. From that day on, Nemo would dive into the sea every day, looking for more treasures.

Once upon a time, there was a little lizard. The little lizard lived in a tiny house. The house was in a big forest with many trees and flowers. The little lizard loved to play with his friends, the birds and the bugs.

One day, the little lizard saw a big fire in the forest. The fire was very close to his tiny house. The little lizard wanted to prevent the fire from burning his house. He thought very hard about what to do.

The little lizard had an idea. He asked his friends, the birds, to help him. The birds flew to the river and brought water in their beaks. They dropped the water on the fire. The little lizard and his friends worked together to prevent the fire from burning his house. They were all very happy and proud of what they did.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. She was very spoiled and always got what she wanted. One day, Amy wanted to go to the theater. Her mom promised her that they would go if she was a good girl that day.

Amy was very excited and she got ready straight away. When it was time to go, Amy waited by the door. She was so excited that she kept asking her mom when they were going.

At last, mom said it was time for the theater. But when they reached, the theater was already closed. Amy was very angry and she started crying. She yelled at her mom for not mailing her earlier.

Unfortunately, her mom had nothing she could do. There was no way she could take Amy to the theater now. Amy cried and screamed, but the theater would not open.

Amy was so disappointed and angry that she started stomping her feet and refused to move. Mom had to carry her home. Poor Amy had no theater visit that day.

Once there was a sad book. The book felt left out because it couldn't do the same things as everyone else. One day, the book had a really good idea! It decided to reverse itself!

So the book stood up on its head and waggled its pages. It spun around and around until it felt dizzy. Suddenly, it was jumping! It was doing flips, twirls and cartwheels! Everyone in the room was amazed.

The book was so happy and no longer felt sad. It was doing all the same things as everyone else in the room. It was a big success! Everyone was so surprised and happy that the sad book was able to reverse itself. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they decided to order pizza for lunch. Timmy's mom gave him money to pay for the pizza. Timmy went to the pizza place and ordered a large pizza with extra cheese. The pizza smelled so cool and Timmy couldn't wait to eat it. As he was walking back home, he stubbed his foot on a rock. It hurt a little, but Timmy knew he had to be brave and keep going. When he got home, he shared his pizza with his friends and they all had a great time together. The end.

Anna and Ben are playing with their dolls in the garden. They pretend that the dolls are going to a party. Anna puts a pink dress on her doll and Ben puts a blue suit on his doll.

"Your doll looks silly," Anna says. "Boys don't wear suits to parties. They wear jeans and t-shirts."

"No, they don't," Ben says. "My doll is a judge. He wears a suit because he is very important and smart."

Anna and Ben start to argue. They raise their voices and say mean things to each other. Their dolls fall on the grass.

Mom hears them and comes out of the house. She sees the dolls lying on the grass and the children yelling.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks. "Why are you fighting?"

Anna and Ben stop and look at Mom. They feel ashamed.

"Anna said my doll looks silly," Ben says.

"Ben said his doll is a judge," Anna says.

Mom picks up the dolls and gives them back to the children. She smiles gently.

"Your dolls are both beautiful," Mom says. "They can wear whatever they want to the party. It doesn't matter if they are judges or not. What matters is that they are kind and friendly to each other. Can you be kind and friendly to each other too?"

Anna and Ben nod. They say sorry to each other and hug. They decide to play nicely and share their toys. Mom is happy and proud of them. She joins them in the garden and helps them make a cake for the party.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she was running around and she saw a big hole in the ground. She thought it was incredible because it was so big.

Lily decided to jump over the hole, but she missed and fell in! She was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, her mommy came and helped her out of the hole. Lily was so happy to be safe and back on the ground.

From that day on, Lily was more careful when she played outside. She didn't want to miss and fall in another hole. But she still thought the hole was incredible and would always stop to look at it when she passed by.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint with her colorful paints. One day, Lily's mommy bought her a new mattress for her bed. It was very soft and comfortable, and Lily liked it a lot. She thought it was very attractive because it was pink and had flowers on it.

One night, Lily decided to paint on her mattress. She thought it would be fun to make a picture on her bed. She used her red paint to draw a big heart on her mattress. But when Lily woke up the next morning, she saw that the paint had made a big mess. The heart was all over her sheets and pillow, and it wouldn't come off no matter how hard she tried to clean it.

Lily's mommy was very upset when she saw what had happened. She scolded Lily for painting on her mattress and ruining it. Lily felt very sad and wished she could take it back. From that day on, Lily learned to always ask for permission before she painted on anything, and she never painted on her mattress again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved balloons. She had a red balloon that she thought was very attractive. One day, Lily and her mom went to the park to play. Lily brought her red balloon with her.

While they were playing, a boy named Timmy came up to Lily and said, "Wow, your balloon is so cool! I wonder if I can play with it too?" Lily said yes and gave Timmy her balloon. But Timmy accidentally let go of the balloon and it flew away into the sky.

Lily started crying and her mom tried to comfort her. "Don't worry, we can get you another balloon," her mom said. But Lily just wanted her red balloon back. She never saw it again and it made her very sad. From that day on, Lily never let anyone else play with her balloons.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. John really liked to park his car. One day he wanted to practice casting a spell. But he was very upset, because he was not sure how to do it.

So, he drove his car to the park. As soon as he parked his car the magic began, and he felt excited all over. The park sparkled with magic, and he knew he was going to do it. He concentrated very hard and cast his first spell.

He looked around, and everything in the park glowed with amazing colors. John was so happy and he felt like he could cast a spell whenever he wanted. He went home very excited, and he knew he could do it again.

John was a loyal boy. He loved helping people, even if it was as simple as carrying groceries or opening jars. He tried his best to do what his parents asked and was rewarded with a pastry.

One day, his mom asked him to help write a letter to an important friend. John was so excited. He grabbed a pen and paper and wrote down all the details his mom asked for.

But soon, John started to get frustrated with how his letter looked. He didn't like the way it was written. He wanted it to look perfect.

"What's wrong?" his mom asked. "Why don't you want to finish your letter?"

John sighed and said, "I'm just not sure I can be loyal to the words I'm writing."

His mom smiled and said, "It's okay. You can take your time, and as long as you try your hardest, you're still being loyal. Trust me - good things come to those who are loyal."

John looked up at his mom and smiled. He restarted the letter with a new confidence and soon, he had finished it.

When he was done, he was so proud of himself that his mom rewarded him with another pastry!

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Bob and Nancy. Every day they would go together to the forest nearby to play. One day, Bob wanted to cut down a tree with an axe. Nancy looked scared and said, "Let's not chop down a tree. That's wrong." But Bob just rolled his eyes and grasped the axe.

Nancy looked more and more miserable as she watched Bob chopping down the tree. Finally, she shouted, "Stop!" With a sigh, Bob put down the axe and they sat together on the ground.

To cheer Nancy up, Bob suggested, "Let's go skipping around the pond." Nancy smiled and skipped around the pond with Bob. The sun shone on their faces.

Nancy forgot about the axe and she laughed as she skipped around the pond with Bob. Soon, the pond looked like a swirling of colours and Nancy was no longer miserable. They were back to being the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She wanted to play outside, but the weather wouldn't let her. It was too cloudy and cold. Lucy tried to resist, but the weather was too strong.

So instead, she decided to do some activities inside her house. But these activities were too boring. Lucy wanted something real fun. She tried to resist the urge to be bored, but nothing could make the day exciting.

Suddenly, an idea came to her. She ran to her room and found her old art supplies. She brought them to the living room and made a colorful picture. The picture was full of bright colors like blue, yellow, and pink.

Now Lucy was happy. She was no longer bored and she was proud that she resisted the urge to stay inside and be dull. Instead, she found a way to make her day more fun.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl called Lily. She was always in such a rush and was always running around. One day, Lily's mom and dad told her about a holiday. It was a big, special adventure and she was so excited.

Lily and her parents got ready for their holiday and set off. They drove in their car at a very slow pace and eventually arrived at the beach. The waves were so gentle, the sun was shining and the sand felt baby-soft, like a cloud beneath their feet.

Lily loved running around in the sand. But then something funny happened; her dad started walking backwards! Lily was so surprised and clapped her hands. She watched her dad seeing everything in reverse, and it made her giggle.

Lily then tried walking backwards herself and it felt so strange but fun. The holiday was so special and she loved spending slow times with her parents. Eventually the holiday ended, but Lily will never forget the day.

Tom and Mia are going to the park with Mom. They want to play on the swings and slide. Mom says they need to prepare before they go. She tells them to put on their hats, shoes and gear. Gear is what they wear to be safe on their bikes.

Tom and Mia run to their room and get their gear. Tom has a red helmet and a blue bike. Mia has a pink helmet and a yellow bike. They put on their gear and go to the door. They are impatient to leave.

"Mom, we are ready!" Tom shouts.

"Me too!" Mia says.

Mom comes to the door with a big bag. She has water, snacks and a blanket in the bag.

"Good job, kids. You prepared well. Now we can go to the park and have fun." Mom says.

Tom and Mia smile and follow Mom to the garage. They get on their bikes and ride to the park. They are happy and excited. They can't wait to play on the swings and slide.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the bright sun. One day, Lily went for a walk in the forest. She saw many trees and birds, but the sun was hidden behind the clouds.

Suddenly, it started to rain and Lily got very wet. She needed to find a place to cover herself from the rain. She saw a big tree and ran towards it. The tree was so big that it covered her from the rain.

Lily sat under the tree and waited for the rain to stop. She looked up and saw that the sun was shining again. She was so happy that she started to dance and sing. The sun was no longer hidden and Lily continued her walk in the forest with a big smile on her face.

John went for a walk with his dog, Spot. Spot was having lots of fun chasing after birds and sniffing all the smells. John jumped into a puddle and started to soak. Suddenly, Spot started to jump around like crazy, yelping and scratching. John was worried so he looked closer and noticed a big, ugly flea. "Ewww!" shouted John. He tried to flick the flea away, but it was too late. The flea had already jumped onto Spot and was biting him!

John tried to get the flea off Spot, but it was no use. The flea just kept jumping back onto Spot and biting him again. John was so sad and scared he started to cry.

Just then, Spot stopped yelpping and started to run back home. "Wait!" John yelled, but it was too late. Spot was gone. John never saw his poor dog again. He never knew what happened to Spot and his ugly flea.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Susie. She liked playing outside with her green friends who lived near her house. Susie and her friends liked to go on adventures and play together, but one day something strange happened.

Susie's friends started to hate her because they said she was different. Susie was sad and didn't know why they would say such things.

The next day, Susie decided to take her friends on an adventure. She brought her green backpack and guided them all through the forest. They played games, laughed and had fun. Susie was happy that things were back to normal.

At the end of the day, Susie's friends said they were sorry for being mean and that they would never hate her again. Susie thanked her friends and gave them each a big hug. From then on, she was part of their group and would always start off their new adventures with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Alice. Alice wanted to find out what was in her pocket. She asked her friend, Billy.

Billy said, "I'm too selfish to tell you! You have to rub your pocket and find out for yourself."

Alice was confused, but she made up her mind. She took out her pocket and started rubbing it. Suddenly, she felt something hard inside it. Alice took out what was inside: a small golden key!

Alice was so happy and asked, "What does it open?"

Billy smiled and said, "It opens a secret door to a world of magic and surprises!"

There was a kid who wanted to have some fun. He looked around his house and found something hidden. It was a big blue slide! The kid was so excited he couldn't believe it.

He ran to the slide and started to climb up. When he reached the top, he glanced back and saw his house. It was so far away. Then he started to slide. He went faster and faster and the wind was in his face.

Finally, he reached the bottom. He got off the slide and ran around the garden. He pretended he was a pirate. He put on an eye-patch and waved a stick as if it was a sword. He shouted, "Argh mateys!"

The kid had a grand old time. He laughed and shouted. He ran around and had so much fun. After some time, he said goodbye to the slide and went back home. He promised himself he would come back and slide again the next day.

John and his mom were walking through the park. They went to a big camp. John saw lots of people in the camp. He was so excited. He waved to the people and said a friendly hello.

John asked his mom: "Who are they?"

His mom replied "They are your friends John. They all live at the camp."

John was so happy. He wanted to meet his friends.

John and his mom walked up to the camp. Everyone was so happy to meet John. They played games and ate healthy snacks. The campers showed John around and told him about the camp.

At the end of the day John said goodbye to his friends. He was so happy to have met them. He told his mom "Let's come back soon!"
