Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to build structures with his toy blocks. One day, Tim built a big structure that he was very proud of. He wanted to show his friend, Sam.

But then, Sam came over and accidentally knocked down Tim's structure. Tim was very sad and said, "Please be careful, Sam! My structure is dead now." Sam felt bad and wanted to make Tim happy again.

So, Sam said, "Please, let me help you build a new structure, Tim." Together, they built an even bigger and better structure than before. Tim was happy again, and they played with the new structure all day long.

Sara likes to read books. She has many books in her room. She reads them every day. She reads about animals, and cars, and stars.

One day, Sara finds a new book in her room. It is a big book with a shiny cover. She opens it and sees many pictures. She sees a picture of a chain. A chain is a long thing with many round parts. She reads the words under the picture. The words say: "A chain can be used to pull, to lock, or to make noise."

Sara wants to try the chain. She looks around her room. She sees her toy box. She sees a lock on her toy box. She thinks: "Maybe I can use the chain to open the lock." She takes the chain and puts it around the lock. She pulls the chain hard. The lock does not open. She pulls harder. The lock still does not open. She pulls harder and harder. The chain breaks. The lock falls to the floor. Sara is sad. She says: "Oh no, I broke the chain. Now I can't read the book anymore."

Sara hears a noise. She turns around. She sees her mom. Her mom is smiling. She says: "Sara, what are you doing? I brought you a new book. It is a book about chains. I thought you would like it." Sara is surprised. She says: "Mom, this is the book I was reading. I found it in my room. I tried to use the chain to open the lock, but I broke the chain. I'm sorry, mom." Her mom hugs her. She says: "It's okay, Sara. The chain was old and weak. It was not a good chain. I have a new chain for you. It is a strong chain. You can use it to play, but not to open locks. And you can still read the book. The book is not broken. It is a good book. I love you, Sara." Sara smiles. She says: "I love you too, mom. Thank you for the book and the chain. Can we read the book together?" Her mom says: "Of course, Sara. Let's read the book together. It is a warm day. We can read the book in the garden. Come on, Sara. Let's go." Sara takes the book and the chain. She follows her mom. She is happy. She likes to read books. She likes to learn new things. She likes to be with her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She liked to help her mom cook food in the kitchen. One day, while her mom was away, Amy wanted to make a spicy soup for her family.

Amy went to the cabinet to find the spicy red pepper. She put a little bit in the soup, but she wanted the spicy taste to increase. So, she put more and more red pepper in the soup. The soup became very red and spicy.

When her mom came back, she saw the spicy soup and tasted it. "Wow, this is very spicy!" she said. Amy was happy that her mom liked the soup. From that day on, Amy always helped her mom in the kitchen and learned how to make many different kinds of food.

Once upon a time there was a boat called Sunny. It sailed out on the ocean. One day it sailed to a new place and a new person got on board.

The person said, "I am here to keep the ocean safe from danger." Everyone on board was happy because they thought the new person would take care of the ocean.

The new person was on the boat for a long time. He kept things away from the ocean and stopped bad things from happening.

One day he said, "I have to leave now." Everyone on board was sad. But no one could stop him from leaving.

The boat sailed back out on the ocean, but something was different. Now there was no one to keep the ocean safe anymore. The ocean was in trouble and there was no one left to help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the morning when the mist was still around. She would run around and laugh, but one day she fell and hurt her knee. It was uncomfortable and she started to cry.

Her mom came outside and saw her crying. "What happened, Lily?" she asked.

"I fell and my knee hurts," Lily said.

Her mom kneeled down and looked at her knee. "It's just a little scrape. Let's clean it up and put a bandage on it," she said.

Lily felt better after her mom helped her. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for making me feel better." They continued to play outside in the mist and had a fun day together.

Once upon a time there was a small boy who wanted to go on an adventure. He decided to take a boat out to sea. After a few hours, the boat sailed onto a big, beautiful island.

The island was so nice that the boy wanted to explore it. He jumped out of the boat into the water and started to swim towards the island. There was a mild breeze that kept him cool as he swam.

The boy arrived on the shore of the island. He looked around and noticed a small hut. He stood up and walked towards it. When he arrived, he heard a voice say, "Hello! Who are you?"

The boy was surprised. He looked around and saw an old man standing nearby. The old man said, "I'm the island's caretaker. My name is John. What's your name?"

The boy smiled and said his name. Then he asked if he could explore the island. John said to him, "Of course you can. Just be careful - some of the island can be a bit wild. I'll stay here and make sure you're safe."

So the boy explored the island with John. They walked around the beach and swam in the mild ocean. Then, when it was time to go back, the boy thanked John for showing him the island and waved goodbye.

The boy sailed back to the shore with lots of great memories of the island. He

Once upon a time, there were two boys who were very brave. They often went on adventures together. One day, the boys dared each other to go into a dark cave. They went together, but they were scared.

The boys made it to the cave's entrance and paused. They looked at each other and the taller boy said, "We have to go in there? That is a difficult fight!"

The smaller boy nodded, but neither of them wanted to take a step forward. They both knew something was waiting on the other side of the cave.

Suddenly, the smaller boy stumbled and fell into the cave. He screamed and the taller boy had to help him. Then they knew they had to go forward.

The smaller boy was afraid and begged not to go, but the taller boy had no choice. He had to help his friend. So, the boys continued further into the dark cave, looking for the scary thing that was waiting for them.

When they made it to the other side, they were faced with two large dragons. The boys tried to fight their way out, but it was too difficult. The dragons defeated them and the boys knew they had lost the fight.

The boys never returned from the dark cave again.

Moral of the story: It is important to think before rushing into something you are afraid of.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty river. Everyday, lots of traffic would come over the river. Boats, cars, planes. All sorts of things!

But one day, a strange thing happened. The boats, cars and planes began to vanish. One by one they all disappeared in a flash!

The people were so surprised. Where did they go? Where had they all gone?

Nobody could figure it out. Until one night, they saw a bright light over the river. It was so bright that it lit up the sky. As the people watched, they saw all the boats, cars and planes flying back over the river!

They were so relieved, and they were so happy. All their traffic had come back! The people celebrated and cheered, and the mighty river was flowing again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to travel. She looked up at the tall vine growing over her head and decided to climb it. She grabbed onto the vine and began to climb. As she got higher and higher, an old man noticed her and called out to her.

"Where are you going, child?" he asked.

The little girl grinned. "Up!" she said and kept on climbing.

The old man chuckled. "You can't reach the sky," he said. "But if you keep going, you'll reach the end of the vine."

So the little girl kept climbing and eventually reached the top of the tall vine. As she looked around, she felt so happy and proud of herself. She took in a deep breath of fresh air and said, "I did it! I traveled the tall vine!"

As she looked around, she knew it was time to go home. She carefully made her way back down the vine until she felt safe to jump down.

The old man was waiting for her with a smile on his face. "You travelled the tall vine bravely," he said.

She smiled and said, "Yep, I did it! It was so fun!"

The old man said, "That's what adventure is all about. Keep exploring and never stop travelling!"

One day, Mommy and Johnny went to the park. They saw a tall grass and Mommy decided to cook it. Johnny was so excited and watched as Mommy picked the grass.

Mommy found a mysterious pot and put the grass in it. Then she added a few unknown ingredients. Johnny stared in amazement as it smelled so good.

Mommy lit the fire and stirred the pot. She continued to stir and stir until the grass was cooked. Johnny was so excited!

Mommy served the tasty grass for dinner and both Mommy and Johnny loved it. They laughed and smiled as they enjoyed their yummy dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy named Max. Max loved to play with his ball and chew on his bone. One day, Max saw a big dog in the park and got very scared. He ran away and hid behind a tree.

Max's friend, a little girl named Lily, saw him hiding and asked, "What's wrong, Max?"

"I saw a big dog and it scared me," Max replied.

"Don't be scared," Lily said. "That dog is friendly. He just wants to play with you."

Max wasn't sure, but Lily's words excited him. He slowly came out from behind the tree and saw that the big dog was wagging his tail and smiling.

Max and the big dog played together and Max even shared his bone with him. From that day on, Max wasn't scared of big dogs anymore. He was excited to make new friends.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They liked to play together every day in the park.

One day, Jack wanted to eat beef for his lunch. But Jill wanted to eat something else.

Jack said to Jill, "Let's eat beef, it's yummy!"

Jill said, "No, I want to eat something pink."

Jack was not happy and they started to play a game of tag. Suddenly, Jack had an idea. He said, "Let's go to the store and buy a pink beef!"

Jill was excited and they ran to the store. They found a delicious pink beef, and Jack bought it for Jill. Jill was so happy, and they both enjoyed eating the pink beef together.

The friends kept playing in the park and enjoyed their lunch of pink beef. From that day on, Jack and Jill enjoyed playing together and eating pink beef for lunch.

Lily was scared of the dark. She did not like to sleep in her big bed alone. She heard noises at night that made her feel cold and shiver. She wanted to be with her mum and dad, but they said she was a big girl and had to sleep in her own room.

One night, Lily had a bad dream. She dreamed that a big monster was under her bed and wanted to eat her. She woke up and screamed. She ran out of her bed and looked for a place to hide. She saw her wardrobe and opened the door. She crawled inside and closed the door behind her. She felt safe in the wardrobe. It was warm and cozy and smelled like her clothes.

"Mum! Dad! Where are you?" she heard a voice outside. It was her dad. He had heard her scream and came to check on her. He turned on the light and looked around the room. He saw her bed was empty and her blanket was on the floor. He was worried. He called her name again.

Lily heard her dad's voice and felt happy. She wanted to see him and hug him. She opened the wardrobe door and peeked out. She saw her dad standing by her bed. He looked at her and smiled.

"Lily, there you are! What are you doing in the wardrobe?" he asked.

Lily came out of the wardrobe and ran to her dad. She wrapped her arms around him and said, "Dad, I had a bad dream. There was a monster under my bed. I was scared. I hid in the wardrobe. I felt safe in the wardrobe."

Dad hugged her back and said, "Oh, Lily, I'm sorry you had a bad dream. There is no monster under your bed. It was just a dream. You are safe with me. Do you want to sleep with me and mum tonight?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. I love you, dad."

Dad picked her up and said, "I love you too, Lily. Come on, let's go to our bed. You can sleep with us and we will keep you warm and safe."

He carried her to his room and tucked her in between him and mum. Lily felt happy and safe. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She did not have any more bad dreams.

"Mommy, can I dress up?" asked the little girl.

"Of course," her mom said.

The girl went to her room and got out her favorite dress. She put it on and twirled around in it.

She then asked, "Mommy, can I use your microphone?"

"That's a good idea," mom said.

The girl grabbed the microphone and pretended to be a singer. She sang her favorite song at the top of her lungs.

Mom said, "You are so interesting and creative. I'm so proud of you!"

The girl smiled and thanked mom. She then put the microphone away, and the two hugged.

Bobby was having a rough day. He missed the bus to school and now he was going to be late. His mom noticed the worry on his face and said, "Don't worry, I will call your tutor and you won't get in trouble."

Bobby sighed in relief as he heard his mom's words. He thought, "A tutor can help me with the work I missed while I'm late, so I can catch up."

Mom did call Bobby's tutor, Mrs. Johnson. She was very harsh with Bobby's mom and said, "No delay, he needs to come right away."

Bobby was scared. He didn't know what to do as he rode in the car to the tutor's house. He had never had a tutor before and he was sure Mrs. Johnson was going to be angry.

They arrived at Mrs. Johnson's house and Bobby was surprised to find her welcoming and kind. She even gave Bobby some snacks and asked him to tell her about his day.

Bobby happily talked to Mrs. Johnson about how he missed the bus and how he felt worried that he had delayed. Mrs. Johnson listened to Bobby and told him it was okay to make mistakes, but it was important to stay on track.

Bobby was thankful for Mrs. Johnson's kind words. He soon realized that having a tutor was not as harsh as he thought it would be. In

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to make them zoom on the grass and the dirt. They had many cars of different colors and sizes.

"Look at my orange car!" Ben said. "It is very fast and loud. Zoom, zoom, zoom!"

Lily looked at Ben's car and wanted to play with it. She reached out her hand and grabbed it. "I want to play with the orange car!" she said.

Ben was angry. He did not like to share his car. He pulled it back and shouted. "No, it is my car! You have your own car. Give it back!"

Lily was angry too. She did not want to give back the car. She held it tight and cried. "No, it is mine now! You have many cars. I only have one!"

They both started to tug and yell. They did not hear their mom calling them from the house.

"Ben, Lily, what is going on?" mom said. She came to the garden and saw them fighting over the car. She was not happy. She took the car from them and put it on the table. "You two need to learn to share and be nice. No one can play with the car until you say sorry to each other."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They felt bad for making mom angry and for hurting each other. They said sorry and hugged. Mom smiled and gave them a hug too. She gave them each a cookie and a glass of milk. She said they could play with the car together if they promised to take turns and be kind.

Ben and Lily agreed. They thanked mom and went back to the garden. They played with the car and their other toys. They made them zoom and laugh. They were happy and had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a pirate named Jack. He loved to sail on his big pirate ship with his friends. They would look for treasure on different islands.

One day, Jack and his friends found a treasure map. They were so excited to find the treasure. They had to count the steps and follow the map to find it. They were very competitive and wanted to be the first to find the treasure.

After a long journey, they finally found the treasure. It was a big chest full of gold coins and precious jewels. They were very happy and celebrated together. From that day on, they were known as the best pirate crew ever.

Once upon a time, there was a poor bulb. It felt so sad and alone. It was dark and lonely and nothing made it happy.

One day, something magical happened. A kind person came and picked the bulb up. They brought it to a special place and made it shine again.

The person used magic to restore the poor bulb. They brushed away all the dust and dirt and replaced it with special stuff that made it shine. The bulb was restored to its beautiful, bright state!

From then on, the bulb was so happy and bright. And each day, it thought of the kind person who had restored it. It thought they were amazing, and it was so thankful to have been chosen.

The bulb thanked its lucky stars, and was grateful for the kindness it had been shown.

Sara loved to play with her mom's purse. It had many things inside that seemed fun and pretty. She liked to take out the lipstick, the keys, the coins, and the sunglasses and pretend she was a grown-up lady.

One day, Sara saw her mom's purse on the table. She thought her mom was busy in the kitchen and would not mind if she played with it for a little while. She grabbed the purse and ran to her room. She opened the purse and started to take out the things inside.

She put on the lipstick and made a funny face in the mirror. She jingled the keys and imagined she was driving a car. She counted the coins and thought she was rich. She put on the sunglasses and felt very cool.

She was having so much fun that she did not hear her mom calling her name. She did not notice that one of the things she took out of the purse was a small envelope. She did not see that the envelope had a sticker that said "Do not open until your birthday".

Her mom came to her room and saw Sara playing with her purse. She was not angry, but she was surprised. She said, "Sara, what are you doing with my purse? You know you are not supposed to touch it without asking me."

Sara looked at her mom and smiled. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to play with your things. They are so charming. Look, I have lipstick, keys, coins, and sunglasses. And I have this envelope too. What is inside?"

Her mom gasped and took the envelope from Sara. She said, "Oh, Sara, this is a special envelope. It is a gift for you. But you are not supposed to open it until your birthday. It is a surprise."

Sara's eyes widened and she said, "A gift for me? A surprise? What is it, mom? Can I open it now? Please, please, please?"

Her mom shook her head and said, "No, Sara, you have to wait. It is only a few days until your birthday. Then you can open it and see what it is. I promise you, it is something very wonderful. Something you will love."

Sara pouted and said, "But I want to see it now. I can't wait. Please, mom, just a little peek."

Her mom hugged her and said, "No, Sara, you have to be patient. Trust me, it will be worth it. Now, let's put everything back in my purse and go to the kitchen. I have a treat for you. Some cookies and milk. How does that sound?"

Sara nodded and said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry I played with your purse. I love you. And I love your gift. Even if I don't know what it is."

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Sara. And I'm glad you love your gift. But you have to wait until your birthday to open it. It is a secret. A very special secret."

Once upon a time there was a gray mouse. The mouse really wanted to stay in his cozy hole, but he just couldn't stay there forever. He wanted to explore the world!

The mouse asked his mom if he could go outside. She said "yes, but only if you promise to come back in a few hours." She gave him a permit to go out and explore.

The mouse was thrilled. He had never been allowed to go outside by himself before. He walked and walked, and saw so many interesting things. But he always remembered the promise he had made to his mom, so he eventually came back home.

His mom was very happy to see him back safe and sound. She said "My brave little mouse! You were allowed out today but always remember to abide by my rules and get a permit before you go exploring again!â€ The mouse nodded and snuggled into his cozy hole to stay.

Once upon a time, there was a sheep who had been getting a bit dull and grey. She was called Pat, and her wool was not as soft and fluffy as it used to be. She was feeling rather sad, and wasn't sure how to make things better.

One day, she decided to take a walk to ask someone for help. As she passed a field of tiny lambs, one of them stopped, looking up at Pat with their bright eyes. Pat explained how she was feeling dull and grey, and the lamb said "I think I know what you need! A bit of sun will help you sparkle up again. It will increase your energy!"

Pat was excited! She took a nap in a spot she felt sure was full of sunlight for the rest of the day. She woke feeling energized and her wool was soft and fluffy again. From that day forward, Pat made sure to take a sunbathing break each day, so her wool would never go dull again.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the world around her. One day, she found a tiny bug on the ground. She wanted to see it up close, so she asked her mom for her microscope.

Her mom helped her set it up and Lily carefully put the bug under the microscope. She examined it closely and saw all the little details she couldn't see before. It was so cool!

Later that day, Lily's mom gave her a cookie. But when she took a bite, she realized it was spoiled. She didn't like it at all and told her mom. Her mom said sorry and gave her a fresh cookie instead. Lily was happy again and went back to examining the world around her.

Jill likes to skip. She skips to school, she skips in the park, she skips at home. She is happy when she skips. She thinks skipping is fun.

One day, Jill skips to the farm. She sees a big horse. She wants to skip with the horse. She goes near the horse and says, "Hello, horse. Do you want to skip with me?" The horse looks at Jill and shakes his head. He says, "No, thank you. I do not skip. I run. Skipping is for little girls, not for big horses."

Jill feels sad. She thinks the horse is not nice. She says, "But skipping is fun. You should try it. It will make you happy." The horse says, "No, I do not need to try it. I know what I like. I like to run. Running is fun. It makes me happy."

Jill does not give up. She says, "Please, horse. Just try it once. Maybe you will like it. Please, please, please." The horse sighs. He says, "Fine. I will try it once. But only once. And then you will leave me alone."

Jill is happy. She says, "Thank you, horse. You are nice. Come on, let's skip." She holds the horse's mane and starts to skip. The horse tries to skip too. But he does not like it. He feels silly and awkward. He trips and falls. He hurts his leg. He says, "Ow, ow, ow. This is not fun. This is bad. I do not like skipping. I like running. Why did you make me skip?"

Jill is sorry. She says, "I am sorry, horse. I did not mean to make you fall. I just wanted to share my fun with you. I thought you would like skipping too. But I see now that you have your own fun. And that is okay. We can have different fun. We can still be friends."

The horse says, "It is okay, Jill. I am sorry too. I was not nice to you. I should have been more polite. I see now that you have your own fun too. And that is okay. We can have different fun. We can still be friends."

Jill and the horse hug. They say, "We are sorry. We are friends. We are nice." Then they see a farmer. He has a bucket of oats. He says, "Hello, Jill. Hello, horse. Are you hungry? Do you want some oats?" Jill and the horse say, "Yes, please. We are hungry. We want some oats." They eat the oats. They are yummy. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: We can have different fun. We can still be friends. We can be nice.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who was very sick. He had a bad cough and felt so tired all the time. He was so sad.

One day, his mommy took him for a special visit to the doctor. The doctor gave him a strange-looking drink that tasted yucky. The doctor said that it was a special herb, and it would help him to feel better.

At first, the little boy didn't want to drink it. It made him feel icky inside. But he knew it would help him, so he drank it.

The little boy had to suffer for a few days while the herb helped him to heal. But soon, he felt better and was happy again. The disgusting herb medicine had done its job.

Lily was a shy girl who liked to play with puzzles. She had many puzzles with animals, cars, and flowers. She could solve them very fast and make nice pictures.

One day, she got a new puzzle from her grandma. It was a big puzzle with a zoom. A zoom was a thing that could fly in the sky and make loud noises. Lily had never seen a zoom before. She was curious and excited.

She opened the box and took out the pieces. She tried to find the corners and the edges. She looked at the picture on the box. It was a zoom with red and blue stripes. It had wings and a tail and a nose.

Lily started to solve the puzzle. She found the pieces that matched the colors and the shapes. She worked hard and had fun. She did not notice that her brother Max came into the room.

Max was not shy. He liked to play with balls and cars and trucks. He saw Lily's puzzle and wanted to play too. He grabbed some pieces and tried to fit them in. He did not look at the picture. He did not care about the zoom.

Lily was angry. She said, "No, Max, that is not right. You are messing up my puzzle. Go away and play with your own toys."

Max did not listen. He said, "I want to play with the zoom. It is cool. Let me help you."

He pushed some pieces and broke the puzzle. Lily cried. She said, "You are mean, Max. You ruined my puzzle. I don't want to play with you."

Max felt sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to hurt you. I just wanted to play with you. Can we fix the puzzle together?"

Lily stopped crying. She said, "OK, Max, but you have to be careful and follow the picture. The zoom is not easy to solve. It has many pieces and details."

Max nodded. He said, "OK, Lily, I will be careful and follow the picture. The zoom is hard to solve. But it is also fun and pretty."

They hugged and smiled. They worked together and solved the puzzle. They made the zoom fly in the sky and make loud noises. They were happy and proud. They showed their puzzle to their grandma and said, "Look, grandma, we solved the zoom. It is a gift from you. Thank you, grandma."

Grandma smiled and said, "You are welcome, my dears. You did a great job. I'm glad you solved the zoom. And I'm glad you played together. You are a good team."

Once upon a time there was a wealthy princess. She was always in a hurry to go out and have fun.

One day, she asked her maid for some special makeup. "I want to look really pretty," she said.

The maid smiled. "Yes, Princess. I'll hurry and get the makeup for you," she said.

The maid quickly ran away to find the special makeup. Soon enough, she returned with a beautiful makeup set.

The princess put on the makeup to make herself even prettier. She smiled and thanked the maid for helping her.

With that, the princess waved goodbye as she hurried off to go outside and enjoy her day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys, especially his toy cars. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy had a toy weapon that he wanted to show Timmy. Timmy got nervous when he saw the weapon because he didn't like scary things.

Billy noticed that Timmy was nervous, so he put the weapon away and they decided to play with Timmy's toy cars instead. THE TWELVE DANCING PRINCESSES

There was a king who had twelve beautiful daughters. They slept in

twelve beds all in one room; and when they went to bed, the doors were

shut and locked up; but every morning their shoes were found to be quite

worn through as if they had been danced in all night; and yet nobody

could find out how it happened, or where they had been.

Then the king made it known to all the land, that if any person could

discover the secret, and find out where it was that the princesses

danced in the night, he should have the one he liked best for his

wife, and should be king after his death; but whoever tried and did not

succeed, after three days and nights, should be put to death.

A king's son soon came. He was well entertained, and in the evening was

taken to the chamber next to the one where the princesses lay in their

twelve beds. There he was to sit and watch where they went to dance;

and, in order that nothing might pass without his hearing it, the door

of his chamber was left open. But the king's son soon fell asleep; and

when he awoke in the morning he found that the princesses had all been

dancing, for the soles of their shoes were full of holes. The same thing

happened the second and third night: so the king ordered his head to be

cut off. After him came several others; but they had all the same luck,

and all lost their lives in the same manner.

Now it chanced that an old soldier, who had been wounded in battle

and could fight no longer, passed through the country where this king

reigned: and as he was travelling through a wood, he met an old woman,

who asked him where he was going. 'I hardly know where I am going, or

what I had better do,' said the soldier; 'but I think I should like very

well to find out where it is that the princesses dance, and then in time

I might be a king.' 'Well,' said the old dame, 'that is no very hard

task: only take care not to drink any of the wine which one of the

princesses will bring to you in the evening; and as soon as she leaves

you pretend to be fast asleep.'

Then she gave him a cloak, and said, 'As soon as you put that on

you will become invisible, and you will then be able to follow the

princesses wherever they go.' When the soldier heard all this good

counsel, he determined to try his luck: so he went to the king, and said

he was willing to undertake the task.

He was as well received as the others had been, and the king ordered

fine royal robes to be given him; and when the evening came he was led

to the outer chamber. Just as he was going to lie down, the eldest of

the princesses brought him a cup of wine; but the soldier threw it all

away secretly, taking care not to drink a drop. Then he laid himself

down on his bed, and in a little while began to snore very loud as if

he was fast asleep. When the twelve princesses heard this they laughed

heartily; and the eldest said, 'This fellow too might have done a wiser

thing than lose his life in this way!' Then they rose up and opened

their drawers and boxes, and took out all their fine clothes, and

dressed themselves at the glass, and skipped about as if they were eager

to begin dancing. But the youngest said, 'I don't know how it is, while

you are so happy I feel very uneasy; I am sure some mischance will

befall us.' 'You simpleton,' said the eldest, 'you are always afraid;

have you forgotten how many kings' sons have already watched in vain?

And as for this soldier, even if I had not given him his sleeping

draught, he would have slept soundly enough.'

When they were all ready, they went and looked at the soldier; but he

snored on, and did not stir hand or foot: so they thought they were

quite safe; and the eldest went up to her own bed and clapped her hands,

and the bed sank into the floor and a trap-door flew open. The soldier

saw them going down through the trap-door one after another, the eldest

leading the way; and thinking he had no time to lose, he jumped up, put

on the cloak which the old woman had given him, and followed them;

but in the middle of the stairs he trod on the gown of the youngest

princess, and she cried out to her sisters, 'All is not right; someone

took hold of my gown.' 'You silly creature!' said the eldest, 'it is

nothing but a nail in the wall.' Then down they all went, and at the

bottom they found themselves in a most delightful grove of trees; and

the leaves were all of silver, and glittered and sparkled beautifully.

The soldier wished to take away some token of the place; so he broke

off a little branch, and there came a loud noise from the tree. Then the

youngest daughter said again, 'I am sure all is not right--did not you

hear that noise? That never happened before.' But the eldest said, 'It

is only our princes, who are shouting for joy at our approach.'

Then they came to another grove of trees, where all the leaves were of

gold; and afterwards to a third, where the leaves were all glittering

diamonds. And the soldier broke a branch from each; and every time there

was a loud noise, which made the youngest sister tremble with fear; but

the eldest still said, it was only the princes, who were crying for joy.

So they went on till they came to a great lake; and at the side of the

lake there lay twelve little boats with twelve handsome princes in them,

who seemed to be waiting there for the princesses.

One of the princesses went into each boat, and the soldier stepped into

the same boat with the youngest. As they were rowing over the lake, the

prince who was in the boat with the youngest princess and the soldier

said, 'I do not know why it is, but though I am rowing with all my might

we do not get on so fast as usual, and I am quite tired: the boat

seems very heavy today.' 'It is only the heat of the weather,' said the

princess: 'I feel it very warm too.'

On the other side of the lake stood a fine illuminated castle, from

which came the merry music of horns and trumpets. There they all landed,

and went into the castle, and each prince danced with his princess; and

the soldier, who was all the time invisible, danced with them too; and

when any of the princesses had a cup of wine set by her, he drank it

all up, so that when she put the cup to her mouth it was empty. At this,

too, the youngest sister was terribly frightened, but the eldest always

silenced her. They danced on till three o'clock in the morning, and then

all their shoes were worn out, so that they were obliged to leave off.

The princes rowed them back again over the lake (but this time the

soldier placed himself in the boat with the eldest princess); and on the

opposite shore they took leave of each other, the princesses promising

to come again the next night.

When they came to the stairs, the soldier ran on before the princesses,

and laid himself down; and as the twelve sisters slowly came up very

much tired, they heard him snoring in his bed; so they said, 'Now all

is quite safe'; then they undressed themselves, put away their fine

clothes, pulled off their shoes, and went to bed. In the morning the

soldier said nothing about what had happened, but determined to see more

of this strange adventure, and went again the second and third night;

and every thing happened just as before; the princesses danced each time

till their shoes were worn to pieces, and then returned home. However,

on the third night the soldier carried away one of the golden cups as a

token of where he had been.

As soon as the time came when he was to declare the secret, he was taken

before the king with the three branches and the golden cup; and the

twelve princesses stood listening behind the door to hear what he would

say. And when the king asked him. 'Where do my twelve daughters dance at

night?' he answered, 'With twelve princes in a castle under ground.' And

then he told the king all that had happened, and showed him the three

branches and the golden cup which he had brought with him. Then the king

called for the princesses, and asked them whether what the soldier said

was true: and when they saw that they were discovered, and that it was

of no use to deny what had happened, they confessed it all. And the king

asked the soldier which of them he would choose for his wife; and he

answered, 'I am not very young, so I will have the eldest.'--And they

were married that very day, and the soldier was chosen to be the king's

heir.

Alice and her mom were standing outside, looking up at the sky. "Mom, why isn't the sun shining?", asked Alice.

"Because it's raining outside, and it's making it miserable," her mom replied.

Alice saw fat drops of rain falling from the sky. "What makes rain?", she asked her mom.

"Well," her mom said, "rain is made when clouds in the sky get filled with water and then it falls down from the sky".

Alice was fascinated! She thought it was amazing how the clouds could make rain.

They watched the rain and how it made puddles on the ground. "Let's go in," said her mom. "It's too cold and miserable out here."

Alice agreed and they ran inside, with the sound of the rain following them.

One day, John wanted to go slide. He ran off to the playground with his diary.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to climb mountains with her parents. One day, they found a very ugly mountain. It was covered in brown rocks and had no trees or flowers. Lily's parents wanted to climb it, but Lily refused. She said it was too ugly and scary.

Her parents tried to convince her, but she wouldn't budge. So they left her with a babysitter and went to climb the mountain without her. Unfortunately, they got lost and never came back. Lily was very sad and missed them a lot. She wished she had gone with them, even if the mountain was ugly.

From that day on, Lily never refused to do something her parents wanted to do. She learned that spending time with them was more important than how things looked. She still loved climbing mountains, but she never forgot the lesson she learned from the ugly mountain.

They sipped their juice and nibbled their crackers. They felt better.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Anna said. "These are not for us. These are for my dad. He likes spicy things."

Ben looked at the jam. He was hungry too. And he wanted to make Mia happy. He was a loyal friend. He decided to try to open the jar.

"Ow! It's too hard. I can't open it," he said.

"Let me try," Mia said. She took the jar from Ben and twisted the lid. But she was too weak. She could not open it either.

They looked at each other. They were sad. They wanted the jam so much.

Once there was a boy named Bob. He loved to look at the big bright blue sky. One day, he decided to go for a walk in the park.

He looked around and noticed a pond. As he walked closer, he could see a big fish swimming around. He was so excited, he had never seen anything like it before!

The fish was very gentle and the boy could tell that it was a tuna. Bob looked into the water and watched the tuna swim around. It was so beautiful!

Bob suddenly noticed a bird flying above the pond. He looked up and watched as the bird circled around. Then it swooped down and landed right next to the tuna!

Bob was so surprised that he didn't even move. The bird looked around and then flew away with the tuna still in its beak.

Bob was amazed. He could hardly believe that he had just seen a bird with a tuna in its beak! He couldn't wait to tell everyone about his adventure.

Lila liked to play with her dolls. She had a pink dress for her doll, and a pink crown. She pretended her doll was a princess, and she was a prince. She lifted her doll and said, "You are my princess. I will take you to the castle."

But Tom, her brother, did not like her game. He wanted to play with his cars. He saw Lila's doll and said, "That is not a princess. That is a silly doll. Give it to me." He grabbed the doll from Lila and threw it on the floor.

Lila was very sad and angry. She cried and said, "No, Tom! That is my doll. You are mean. Give it back to me." She ran to the floor and picked up her doll. She hugged it and checked if it was hurt.

Tom laughed and said, "You are a baby. You cry for a doll. Dolls are for girls. I have cars. Cars are for boys. They are fast and cool." He zoomed his car on the table and made loud noises.

Lila did not care what Tom said. She loved her doll and her pink dress and her pink crown. She said, "You are wrong, Tom. Dolls are not for girls only. And cars are not for boys only. I can play with both. And I can be a prince if I want to. You are not the boss of me." She lifted her doll again and said, "Come on, princess. Let's go to the castle. We don't need Tom." She walked away with her doll and left Tom alone.

Once upon a time, there was a black chicken named Jack. Jack lived on a farm with his friends, the cows and the pigs. One day, Jack saw a big, juicy worm in the dirt. He wanted to eat it, but it was too long.

Jack asked his cow friend, "Can you help me part this worm?"

The cow replied, "Sure, I can help. Let me use my strong teeth to part it in half."

Jack was very happy and ate his half of the worm. He thanked his cow friend and they continued to play together on the farm.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play and sing. One day, they find a big hat and a long scarf in Mom's closet. They put them on and pretend to be opera singers.

"Hello, I am Sara, the best opera singer in the world!" Sara says in a loud voice.

"And I am Ben, the most handsome opera singer in the world!" Ben says in a loud voice.

They start to sing a song they make up. They sing very high and very low. They sing very fast and very slow. They sing very loud and very soft. They make funny faces and gestures.

Mom hears them and comes to see what they are doing. She sees them in the hat and the scarf, singing their silly song. She smiles and claps her hands.

"Bravo, bravo, you are wonderful opera singers!" Mom says in a kind voice.

Sara and Ben stop singing and bow. They are happy that Mom likes their show. They run to hug her and say thank you.

Mom is compassionate. She loves Sara and Ben very much. She laughs with them and tells them they are very creative and funny. She says they can keep the hat and the scarf and play opera anytime they want. Sara and Ben are very happy. They love Mom very much. They laugh with her and tell her they love her too.

MOTHER HOLLE

Once upon a time there was a widow who had two daughters; one of them

was beautiful and industrious, the other ugly and lazy. The mother,

however, loved the ugly and lazy one best, because she was her own

daughter, and so the other, who was only her stepdaughter, was made

to do all the work of the house, and was quite the Cinderella of the

family. Her stepmother sent her out every day to sit by the well in

the high road, there to spin until she made her fingers bleed. Now it

chanced one day that some blood fell on to the spindle, and as the girl

stopped over the well to wash it off, the spindle suddenly sprang out

of her hand and fell into the well. She ran home crying to tell of her

misfortune, but her stepmother spoke harshly to her, and after giving

her a violent scolding, said unkindly, 'As you have let the spindle fall

into the well you may go yourself and fetch it out.'

The girl went back to the well not knowing what to do, and at last in

her distress she jumped into the water after the spindle.

She remembered nothing more until she awoke and found herself in a

beautiful meadow, full of sunshine, and with countless flowers blooming

in every direction.

She walked over the meadow, and presently she came upon a baker's oven

full of bread, and the loaves cried out to her, 'Take us out, take us

out, or alas! we shall be burnt to a cinder; we were baked through long

ago.' So she took the bread-shovel and drew them all out.

She went on a little farther, till she came to a tree full of apples.

'Shake me, shake me, I pray,' cried the tree; 'my apples, one and all,

are ripe.' So she shook the tree, and the apples came falling down upon

her like rain; but she continued shaking until there was not a single

apple left upon it. Then she carefully gathered the apples together in a

heap and walked on again.

The next thing she came to was a little house, and there she saw an old

woman looking out, with such large teeth, that she was terrified, and

turned to run away. But the old woman called after her, 'What are you

afraid of, dear child? Stay with me; if you will do the work of my house

properly for me, I will make you very happy. You must be very careful,

however, to make my bed in the right way, for I wish you always to shake

it thoroughly, so that the feathers fly about; then they say, down there

in the world, that it is snowing; for I am Mother Holle.' The old woman

spoke so kindly, that the girl summoned up courage and agreed to enter

into her service.

She took care to do everything according to the old woman's bidding and

every time she made the bed she shook it with all her might, so that the

feathers flew about like so many snowflakes. The old woman was as good

as her word: she never spoke angrily to her, and gave her roast and

boiled meats every day.

So she stayed on with Mother Holle for some time, and then she began

to grow unhappy. She could not at first tell why she felt sad, but she

became conscious at last of great longing to go home; then she knew she

was homesick, although she was a thousand times better off with Mother

Holle than with her mother and sister. After waiting awhile, she went

to Mother Holle and said, 'I am so homesick, that I cannot stay with

you any longer, for although I am so happy here, I must return to my own

people.'

Then Mother Holle said, 'I am pleased that you should want to go back

to your own people, and as you have served me so well and faithfully, I

will take you home myself.'

Thereupon she led the girl by the hand up to a broad gateway. The gate

was opened, and as the girl passed through, a shower of gold fell upon

her, and the gold clung to her, so that she was covered with it from

head to foot.

'That is a reward for your industry,' said Mother Holle, and as she

spoke she handed her the spindle which she had dropped into the well.

The gate was then closed, and the girl found herself back in the old

world close to her mother's house. As she entered the courtyard, the

cock who was perched on the well, called out:

'Cock-a-doodle-doo!

Your golden daughter's come back to you.'

Then she went in to her mother and sister, and as she was so richly

covered with gold, they gave her a warm welcome. She related to them

all that had happened, and when the mother heard how she had come by her

great riches, she thought she should like her ugly, lazy daughter to go

and try her fortune. So she made the sister go and sit by the well

and spin, and the girl pricked her finger and thrust her hand into a

thorn-bush, so that she might drop some blood on to the spindle; then

she threw it into the well, and jumped in herself.

Like her sister she awoke in the beautiful meadow, and walked over it

till she came to the oven. 'Take us out, take us out, or alas! we shall

be burnt to a cinder; we were baked through long ago,' cried the loaves

as before. But the lazy girl answered, 'Do you think I am going to dirty

my hands for you?' and walked on.

Presently she came to the apple-tree. 'Shake me, shake me, I pray; my

apples, one and all, are ripe,' it cried. But she only answered, 'A nice

thing to ask me to do, one of the apples might fall on my head,' and

passed on.

At last she came to Mother Holle's house, and as she had heard all about

the large teeth from her sister, she was not afraid of them, and engaged

herself without delay to the old woman.

The first day she was very obedient and industrious, and exerted herself

to please Mother Holle, for she thought of the gold she should get in

return. The next day, however, she began to dawdle over her work, and

the third day she was more idle still; then she began to lie in bed in

the mornings and refused to get up. Worse still, she neglected to

make the old woman's bed properly, and forgot to shake it so that the

feathers might fly about. So Mother Holle very soon got tired of her,

and told her she might go. The lazy girl was delighted at this, and

thought to herself, 'The gold will soon be mine.' Mother Holle led her,

as she had led her sister, to the broad gateway; but as she was passing

through, instead of the shower of gold, a great bucketful of pitch came

pouring over her.

'That is in return for your services,' said the old woman, and she shut

the gate.

So the lazy girl had to go home covered with pitch, and the cock on the

well called out as she saw her:

'Cock-a-doodle-doo!

Your dirty daughter's come back to you.'

But, try what she would, she could not get the pitch off and it stuck to

her as long as she lived.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the fields. One day, he saw a big, strong bull in the distance. The bull was very scary and Timmy was afraid.

But then, Timmy had an idea. He decided to peek at the bull from behind a big rock. He was very careful not to make a sound. To his surprise, the bull was not scary at all. In fact, the bull was very modest and shy.

From that day on, Timmy visited the bull every day. He would bring him fresh grass and water. The bull was very grateful and they became good friends. Timmy learned that sometimes things that seem scary aren't really that bad.

Once upon a time, there were two little boys in the town. One of them was Jack, who was three years old. He went to the dock early every morning with his father. Today, dad had given Jack an important task.

"Jack," said dad, "It's your turn to load up the boat with the fish."

Jack was excited. He grabbed the net and started to load the boat. With each fish, his score improved.

But suddenly, he heard a loud noise.

"Oh no," said Jack.

The noise was coming from inside the boat - it was his dad! He had fallen on the fish and was now miserable.

Jack ran over to help. He tried to help his dad but it was too late. Dad had broken his arm and needed to go to the hospital immediately.

Jack was sad. He had to go home without his dad. His score was low, and his dad was in pain. It was a miserable ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. She was going to the park with her mom and dad. When they got there, Daisy saw lots of fun things to do.

She saw a big brown club laying on the ground. Dad said it must belong to the playground! Daisy was so excited. She offered to play with the club.

Dad said that was a great idea. Together, they began to hit the ball with the club. Daisy laughed and had so much fun. Dad said she was really good at it!

They played with the club until it was time to go home. Dad offered to take it with them, but Daisy said no. She wanted to leave it in the playground for someone else to find and play with.

Once upon a time, there was a soldier named Tim. He was a very bad soldier because he didn't listen to his captain. One day, Tim went to the store to buy some new boots.

At the store, he met a little boy named Jack. Jack said, "Hi, soldier! Can you tie my shoe?" Tim said, "Sure, I can tie your shoe." So, Tim tied Jack's shoe and they became friends.

But then, Tim's captain came to the store and saw Tim talking to Jack. The captain said, "Tim, you are a bad soldier! You should be training, not playing with children." Tim felt sad and said, "I'm sorry, captain. I will go back to training now." But Jack said, "Don't worry, soldier. You can still be my friend." And Tim felt happy again. The end.

Once upon a time there was a dog called Max. Max was very serious but he really loved to play. One day, Max was running around the park with his friends, when he suddenly noticed something special. It was a buckle! Max was so excited! He wanted to try it on his coat. But when he tried, the buckle was facing the wrong way. Max didn't know what to do.

So, he called for help. His friends came to help him. They saw the buckle and all said 'Let's reverse it!'. So, they did! They figured out how to turn the buckle around and, soon enough, Max had his buckle on the right way. He was so happy!

Max showed off his new buckle and all his friends were very impressed. Max was very proud of himself and couldn't help but smile. He had learned an important lesson - that with a bit of help and a bit of work, you can find a way to make something right even when it's not the way you wanted it to be in the first place.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She loved to eat apples and would pick them from the tree in her backyard. One day, she went for a walk in the forest and got lost. She didn't know which way to go.

Lily saw a man walking by and asked him for help. He was compassionate and gave her a compass to help her find her way back home. Lily followed the compass and guessed which way to go. After a while, she found her way back home and was happy to eat her apples again.

From that day on, Lily always carried a compass with her whenever she went for a walk in the forest. She knew that if she ever got lost again, she could use it to find her way back home.

John was a busy little three-year-old. He loved to explore and asked lots of questions. One day, he asked his mom all about the ceiling. She told him that the ceiling was like an open lid on their home. She said that it owned the room, keeping them safe and sheltered.

John was so intrigued by the ceiling that he decided to give it a try himself. He slowly reached up and touched the open ceiling with his little hand. It felt strange and smooth! He giggled and laughed.

John's mom saw how excited he was about the ceiling and asked if he wanted to explore some more. He shouted out yes! So, she picked him up so he could see the ceiling from above.

John was in awe. He pointed out the lights and decorations on the ceiling. He also noticed how the ceiling was really big and how it owned the whole house!

After their exploration, John felt so happy. He had learned a lot about the ceiling and now he owned the knowledge.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and sing. One day, she went to a dance class with her friends. She was so excited to learn new moves.

During the class, the teacher showed them a special tap dance. Lily had never tapped before, but she wanted to try. She put on her tap shoes and started to dance.

At first, she was a little unsure, but then she started to believe in herself. She tapped her feet to the beat of the music and it sounded so good! Her friends cheered her on and she felt very happy. From that day on, Lily loved tap dancing and believed in herself.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a wide bench near the slide. They run to the bench and sit on it.

"Look, a bird!" Mia says. She points to a small bird on the grass. The bird has a red head and a yellow belly.

"Wow, it is pretty!" Tom says. He wants to see the bird better. He gets off the bench and walks to the bird.

"Tom, be careful!" Mia says. She knows the bird is shy. She stays on the bench and watches Tom.

Tom is very quiet. He moves slowly to the bird. He reaches out his hand. He wants to touch the bird. He pokes the bird with his finger.

"Tweet!" The bird is scared. It flies away. It goes to a tree.

"Tom, you made the bird go away!" Mia says. She is sad. She likes the bird.

"Sorry, Mia. I just wanted to say hello to the bird." Tom says. He is sorry too. He goes back to the bench.

"It is okay, Tom. Maybe the bird will come back later." Mia says. She smiles at Tom. They are still friends.

They sit on the bench and wait for the bird. They see other things in the park. They see a dog, a ball, and a flower. They have fun. They are happy.

Bob was out for a walk in the forest. Suddenly he saw something shiny in the leaves. He bent down to take a closer look. What he found was a berry that was so juicy and yummy looking! He couldn't resist picking it up and eating it.

But the berry was not alone. He looked around and saw many more. Bob was so excited. He gathered as many of these tasty berries as he could and started to put them in his basket.

Suddenly, he heard a voice, "What do you think you're doing?" He looked around and saw a little girl. She was very messy with leaves and dirt all over her clothes. She asked him "Why are you picking my berries?"

Bob replied, "I'm sorry I didn't know they were yours. I just thought I'd find some yummy berries!".

The little girl smiled. "That's ok, I'm happy to share. Just make sure you don't make a mess. Choose the berries carefully."

Bob gave her a big smile. He thanked her and continued to hunt for berries. He picked the biggest and juiciest ones he could find and eventually filled his basket. He had fun and made sure he didn't leave a messy trail. The little girl even gave him an extra berry for being so careful. Bob was happy to have found so many delicious berries, and to have made a new friend.

Lily liked balloons. She liked to blow them up and tie them. She liked to make them fly and bounce. She liked to play with them with her friends.

But Max did not like balloons. He was scared of them. He thought they were loud and mean. He did not like to see them or touch them. He hated when Lily played with them.

One day, Lily brought a big red balloon to school. She was very happy. She showed it to her friends and they smiled. But Max saw the balloon and he was very worried. He wanted the balloon to go away.

He had an idea. He found a sharp stick and he hid it in his hand. He walked up to Lily and her friends. He pretended to be nice. He said hello and asked to see the balloon.

Lily was surprised. She did not know Max wanted to play. She was kind and she gave him the balloon. She hoped he would like it.

But Max did not like it. He held the balloon and he poked it with the stick. The balloon popped with a loud bang. Lily and her friends screamed and jumped. Max laughed and ran away.

Lily was very sad. She liked her balloon and she wanted to play with it. She did not understand why Max did that. She felt angry and hurt. She cried and hugged her friends.

Max was not happy. He thought he would feel better after he popped the balloon. But he did not. He felt guilty and mean. He saw Lily crying and he felt sorry. He wished he did not poke the balloon. He wished he was nice.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a big red car. She loved to put things in the car boot. One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. Before they left, Lily put her toys in the boot. But she was careless and did not shut the boot all the way.

At the park, Lily had so much fun. She played with her ball and her doll. She ran and laughed all day. The sun began to set and it was time to go home. Lily and her parents walked back to the car.

When they got to the car, they saw that the boot was open. Lily's toys were gone! She was very sad. Her mom and dad told her it was important to shut the boot next time. From that day on, Lily was never careless with the boot again. She always made sure to shut it tight, so her toys would be safe.

One day, a little girl named Lucy found a jar of jam. It was her favorite, red and sweet. She wanted to eat it all. But the jar was tough to open. She tried and tried, but it just would not open.

Lucy asked her big brother Tom for help. "Tom, can you open this tough jar for me?" Tom was strong and opened the jar easily. But as he opened it, he accidentally cut his finger on the jar's lid. It hurt a lot.

Lucy felt bad and wanted to help Tom. She knew that hugs could heal. So, she hugged Tom tight and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I hope your finger heals fast." Tom smiled and thanked Lucy for her hug. They both enjoyed the sweet jam together, and soon, Tom's finger healed.

Once there was a little girl called Lilly. Lilly was three years old and loved adventures. But one night Lilly had a nightmare. She was scared and started to cry. She ran to her parents and knelt down beside her mum and dad.

Her mum said, "Don't worry Lilly, we're here to look after you."

Lilly felt much better but she was still scared of the nightmare. So she decided to take matters into her own hands. She ran to her dad and said, "Let's make a nightmare catcher!â€

Her dad got some thin sticks and bent them into an arch. Then he tied them together with some string. He said, â€œThis will catch any nightmares that come too close to you.â€

Together they hung the nightmare catcher over Lilly's bed and with a smile she said, "Goodnight."

Lilly felt much better and brave enough to go to sleep. She fell asleep safe in the knowledge that any nightmare that tried to enter her room would be caught up in the nightmare catcher.

Once upon a time, there was a good girl with lots of friends. One day, she wanted to unite all of her friends together in one place. So, she took a photo and invited all of her friends to gather around. They all smiled big and posed for the special photo. Everyone was so happy to be together in one place.

When the photo was taken, the girl was so excited to show it to all of her friends. She passed around the photo, and everyone was so happy to see the good photo that had captured the moment they all shared together.

The girl always kept the photo with her, so that she could always remember the special moment they shared and how they had all united together.

The end.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play with sand. They had a big bucket and a small shovel. They wanted to make an island with sand. They filled the bucket with sand and turned it over on the ground. They made a round hill of sand.

"Look, we made an island!" Lily said. "But it needs something more."

"Maybe we can make a palm tree with leaves and a coconut," Tom said. He found a stick and some green paper. He cut the paper into leaf shapes and stuck them on the stick. He also found a brown ball and put it on the stick. He pushed the stick into the sand hill.

"Wow, that looks like a real palm tree!" Lily said. "But how can we get the coconut?"

Tom had an idea. He climbed on the sand hill and reached for the ball. He pulled it off the stick and held it in his hands. He squeezed the ball hard.

"Crack!" The ball broke into two pieces. Inside, there was white stuff and water.

"Look, it's a real coconut!" Tom said. He gave one piece to Lily and kept the other. They drank the water and ate the white stuff.

"Mmm, this is yummy!" Lily said. "We are successful island makers!"

They smiled and hugged each other. They were happy and proud of their island. They played with sand until it was time to go home.

One day, Sammy the elephant marched out into the sun. He felt so jolly. He shouted "hello!" to everybody as he marched along.

Then he noticed something fun: a big, colourful cage with a door wide open. "Where are the animals?" he wondered. He heard something coming from inside.

He stepped closer and looked in. He saw three little bears playing joyfully together. "Hi!" he said, making them all jump. They smiled and waved back at him.

The little bears said, "Come in and join us!" Sammy felt so excited. He stepped into the cage and they all began to march around together, laughing and singing happily, while the sun shone brightly above.

Once upon a time, there was a small squirrel. The squirrel lived in a big oak tree. The oak tree was in a pretty park. The squirrel had a lot of friends in the park.

One sunny day, the squirrel and his friends played a fun game. They would shoot acorns with their tails. The acorns flew high into the sky. All the animals laughed and clapped.

At the end of the day, the small squirrel went back to his oak tree. He was happy and tired. He curled up in his cozy nest and went to sleep. The squirrel had a good day with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a happy little three year old girl. Her name was Jane. Jane loved to play and explore. One day Jane stumbled upon a huge and mysterious maze. She was excited to explore it. She wandered the paths and around the corners for hours, looking for a way out. Along the way, she met a humble old man and room full of animals.

The old man smiled and said: "Little one, the way out of the maze is the way you came. Look for it." Jane was confused and asked the old man: "How can I find my way out?"

The old man replied: "Be patient, follow your heart and trust in yourself. You will find the way out. Look carefully at the paths and be humble". Jane was determined and brave, she searched the maze and finally found the way out! She was so proud of her little humble self. Jane would never forget her adventure in the maze.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a long hair and loved to wear matching clothes. One day, she went to the store with her mom to buy a new dress. There were many pretty dresses, but Lily couldn't choose which one she wanted. Her mom helped her and they found a dress that matched her shoes. Lily was very happy and wore her new dress to a party. All her friends loved it too!

Once upon a time, there was a perfect church. It was so pretty that people from far away would often come to peek at it. Every day, the church looked more perfect.

One day, a little girl came to peek at the church. She was only three years old, but something about the church looked so magical. She wanted to explore it.

The little girl slowly opened the big door of the church and peeped inside. It was like a dream come true! Everything looked so perfect. From the big windows to the tall columns.

The little girl stayed and peeked around until she was too tired to stay. Then she left, happy to have found the perfect church.

Once there was a little girl called Lisa. She was three years old and she loved making new friends. One day she was in the park playing with her toys, when suddenly she saw something unusual. It was a needle! The needle was very shiny. Lisa knew she shouldn't touch it, so she decided to ask an adult for help.

She went to an old man and asked, "Please, could you help me?" The old man smiled and said, "Yes, I can help. What do you need?" Lisa told him about the needel, and the old man recommended she tell her mummy.

So Lisa ran home and found her mummy. She told her all about the needle she had seen and her mummy said, "That's not a plaything, Lisa! You must never touch one of those." Her mummy recommended she stay away from needles and the old man had saved her from harm.

One day there was a scary laser. No one knew what it was for. Everyone was scared because it was so big and loud.

The people wanted to sort the laser out, but they didn't know how. They asked the children to help them.

The children were brave and wanted to help. One of them named John said, "I know how to play with the laser." He showed them how to make the laser move around like a toy.

Everyone was happy that the laser was sorted out. They had fun playing with it. The people were very thankful for John's help. John became a hero that day!

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to help their mom bake pies. One day, mom made a big apple pie and put it on the table to cool. She told Lily and Ben not to touch the pie until it was ready.

But Lily and Ben were very hungry and curious. They wanted to taste the pie. They waited until mom went to the garden and then they tiptoed to the table. Lily reached for the pie and lifted it with both hands. It was heavy and hot.

"Be careful, Lily!" Ben whispered. "Don't drop the pie!"

But Lily was not careful. She lost her balance and the pie slipped from her hands. It fell on the floor with a loud thud. The pie broke into pieces and made a big mess.

"Oh no!" Lily cried. "We dropped the pie!"

Mom heard the noise and came back to the kitchen. She saw the pie on the floor and Lily and Ben with sad faces.

"What happened here?" mom asked.

"We're sorry, mom," Lily and Ben said. "We wanted to try the pie and we dropped it."

Mom was not happy, but she was not angry either. She hugged Lily and Ben and said, "It's okay, my lively twins. I know you didn't mean to drop the pie. But next time, please listen to me and wait until the pie is cool. Now let's clean up this mess and make a new pie together."

One day, a cute little girl named Lily went to her garden. She had a small bag of beans. She wanted to grow big bean plants. Lily dug a hole in the ground and put a bean in it. She covered the bean with dirt and gave it some water. "Grow big and strong, little bean," she said.

The next day, Lily saw a small bird in her garden. The bird looked at the place where Lily put the bean. "Are you looking for my bean?" Lily asked the bird. The bird nodded its head. Lily thought the bird was hungry, so she gave it some seeds to eat. "You can visit my bean, but don't eat it, okay?" The bird nodded again and flew away.

Days went by, and Lily took care of her bean every day. The bird came back to visit, too. One day, the bean started to grow into a big, strong plant. Lily was so happy! The bird came back and saw the big bean plant. It nodded its head and flew away. Lily knew that the bird was happy for her and her big bean plant.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tom. Tom liked to play outside but sometimes he got tired and wanted to rest. One day, Tom was sitting in his garden and saw something he wanted - a nice, red stamp. It was beautiful and Tom knew he needed it.

Once there was a little girl who was very curious. She wanted to see what was beneath the blue sea. So she asked her brother if she could borrow his boat. But her brother said she must not go alone. He told her she could come if she was brave enough.

Once upon a time, there was a big swamp. In the swamp, there lived an elderly frog. The elderly frog had many friends.

Once there was a cool spider who lived in a nice cave. Every day she would explore the cave, looking for something new to find. But sometimes the spider found that other creatures would ignore her.

Once upon a time, there was a light beetle. He had never been outside and wanted to see the world.

The bird took the beetle to the ant, who said she could help. She pulled and tugged, and the beetle worked his way around the branch, until he was finally free.

The beetle thanked the bird and ant, before flying off into the light. He had seen the world and was now ready for a real adventure!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Star. Star was three and loved helping the people in her family prepare dinners.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play and have fun. They are very happy because they are going on holiday with Mum and Dad. They pack their bags and toys and get in the car.

The car goes very fast on the road. Lily and Tom look out the window and see many things. They see cows and sheep and trees and houses. They tell each other what they see and make up stories. They sing songs and laugh.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play in the garden. They liked to smell the herbs that grew there, like mint and rosemary. They liked to see the sun shine on the flowers and the bees. They liked to hear the birds sing and the wind blow.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a new herb in the garden. It was tall and green, with purple flowers. It smelled sweet and spicy. They wanted to touch it and taste it, but they did not know what it was.

"Let's ask Mom," Tom said.

Lily picked a leaf and put it in her mouth. She made a face and spat it out. "Yuck! It's bitter and hot!"

Lily felt angry and sad. She wanted to make Tom feel bad too. She saw a shiny red berry on the herb. She picked it and gave it to Tom. "Here, try this. It's sweet and juicy."

Tom trusted Lily. He took the berry and bit it. He felt a pain in his mouth and his throat. He dropped the berry and cried. "Ow! Ow! It hurts! It burns!"

Lily saw Tom cry and felt scared. She did not mean to hurt him. She wanted to help him, but she did not know how. She ran to the house and called Mom.

Mom came and saw Tom. She saw the herb and the berry. She knew what they were. They were poison. She was very angry and very worried. She took Tom to the car and drove to the hospital.

Lily stayed in the garden. She felt lonely and sorry. She wished she had not given Tom the berry. She wished she had listened to him. She wished they were still friends. She cried and cried. The sun did not shine for her anymore.

One day, Jack went fishing with his dad. Jack loved to go fishing. His dad gave him a gentle fishing rod and told him to stir the water with it. Once there were two friends, Ben and Jake. Ben had a net that he used to shoot things with. One day, Jake said, "Let me have a go at shooting things with the net."

Once upon a time there was a mechanic. He had a long day because he had to fix a lot of cars. He was so tired, he decided to take a break. So he went outside and dug a hole in the ground. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Amy. She was always curious and wanted to explore the world. One day, while exploring her garden, she stumbled across a little puppy. The puppy was so attractive and eager to play, so Amy decided to take the puppy home and protect it.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Elly. Elly lived in a warm, sunny place with her family. They liked to play and eat together. Elly was a very happy elephant.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Timmy. Timmy loved to race with his friends on the beach. One day, Timmy saw a shiny oyster on the sand. He wanted to show it to his friends, but a seagull swooped down and snatched it away. Timmy was sad and angry.

Once upon a time there was a family who loved to study. They would read books, learn about numbers and practice their words every day.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty mouse. It was always so clever and brave. One day, it was playing in the garden when it saw a big bucket of paint. It wanted to have fun and paint the garden, but it knew it mustn't. The mouse ran away to prevent the paint from spilling.

Lily and Ben love to play with their toy instruments. Lily has a small drum and Ben has a tiny guitar. They pretend to be musicians and make loud noises. Sometimes they sing along, too.

John replied, "I'm gonna see the duck!"
