John raced back to the lake wearing his sunglasses. He saw the duck and it looked even bigger than before. It was amazing! He wanted to get closer so he crept slowly towards it. Suddenly, the duck started swimming away.

John was sad but he kept watching it until it disappeared. He felt mighty as he walked home. He knew the sunglasses had helped him see the wonderful duck.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sue. She was only 3 and liked exploring outside.

One day Sue was playing in her garden when she saw something wet and unusual. She came closer and leaned down to take a look. Suddenly she heard a whisper! She felt scared but called out bravely 'Who's there?'.

From the wet and unusual thing stepped out a friendly frog. His voice was soft and kind as he said 'Hello Sue, I'm Henry.' Sue was so happy to meet someone new and laughed as the frog hopped away.

The next day Sue and Henry became best friends. They played in the garden and went for adventures. Every time they went out Henry would whisper 'Let's explore!'. Sue couldn't believe that she had found such an unusual new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Cindy. She was very special because she could grow things with her magical spell. Wherever she went she would cast her spell and flowers would grow out of the ground. Even bees and butterflies followed her around! Everyone was so impressed by her magic.

Every day, Cindy would explore and find new places to grow things. She would use her impressive spell and make trees bloom and fruits sprout out of the ground. Birds would then come to eat the fruits that Cindy created. It was very cool!

One day, Cindy wanted to make something really special. She closed her eyes, held her hands to her chest, and said her magical spell. When she opened her eyes, she couldn't believe what she saw! A big, beautiful castle had appeared out of nowhere. It was so impressive!

From that day on, Cindy's magical spell was known all over the world. People admired her special talent and she was able to create even more amazing things!

Once there was a girl named Liz. She wanted to go to the playground, but her mom wanted her to go on the subway. Liz was scared because she had never been on the subway before. When they got to the station, the subway car was a deep purple color.

But when Liz got inside the train, she started to suffer. The car was loud and it made her feel very scared. She started to cry and her mom hugged her tightly. The other passengers looked at Liz sympathetically.

After a while, the subway car stopped and Liz was so happy. She was relieved to get off and never wanted to ride the subway again. Instead, she and her mom took the bus to the playground.

Liz had an amazing time playing there and she forgot all about her suffering on the subway. She was so happy that the day turned out to be great.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, John and Alex. They were playing in the park together.

Suddenly, they heard a loud leak coming from the playground. They both looked around to see where it was coming from.

Alex said, "What's that noise?"

John answered, "I think it's a leak!"

They both went over to take a closer look. Sure enough, there was water pouring out of the slide. It was a funny sight!

John and Alex decided to try and fix the leak. After a few minutes of brainstorming, they had the perfect solution. They took some sand from the sandbox and put it in the hole where the leak was coming from.

The leak was fixed and John and Alex were both very proud of their work. The park was much better now, and it was finally time for them to go home.

They had had so much fun, that they promised each other that they would come back to the park as soon as possible.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lily, and she loved to play outside. She found the most joy in chasing the sunset as it drifted across the sky.

One day, her big brother asked her if she wanted to join him in playing a game of kick-ball. Lily was so excited! She had never kicked a ball before, but she was eager to try.

They made their way to the grassy patch in the park, and Lily's brother showed her how to kick. It was so much fun! In no time, the sun began to fall, causing a beautiful sunset.

Lily and her brother were so grateful to be able to watch the sunset together. Suddenly, Lily remembered something and quickly ran off.

Her brother asked, "Where are you going?"

Lily replied, "To catch the sunset!" And with a giggle she ran off laughing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to dress. Each morning, she chose the prettiest dress for that day. Today, she chose a dress with lots of pink and purple stripes.

On the way to school, she saw a matching hat. She was so excited that she dressed it on her head. She especially liked how it made her look very pretty.

When she arrived at school, she showed her friends her matching hat. She twirled and danced, feeling so excited about her new look.

Unfortunately, the day was a bit rough. It started to rain and the wind was so strong. Her pretty dress and matching hat were both ruined.

The little girl was very sad. But then she looked up at the sky and saw a beautiful rainbow. She soon forgot all her worries and started to dream of her next dress to dress.

Once upon a time there was a little boat. It liked to pass the harbor. Every day it sailed by, looking out for its friends.

One day it noticed something unusual. Another boat was in the harbor. It was a bigger boat and it was very restless. The little boat was worried.

Suddenly the little boat had an idea! It went closer to the harbor and waved hello to the bigger boat. The bigger boat looked surprised and waved back. The two boats started to have a chat.

The bigger boat was going on a long journey and it was feeling lonely. The little boat was happy to help and offered to pass by the harbor every day to keep the bigger boat company. The bigger boat accepted the offer and was very happy.

The two boats became good friends and looked forward to seeing each other every day while they both passed the harbor. They were very content with the arrangement.

One day, a restless little dog named Spot was playing outside. The sun was hot, and the heat made Spot very warm. Spot wanted to find a friend to play with.

Spot saw a big tree and heard a bird singing. "Do you want to play with me?" asked Spot. The bird said, "Yes, let's play!" They decided to play a game called "Clap and Hop". Spot would clap his paws, and the bird would hop from branch to branch.

They played and played until they were tired. Spot and the bird sat under the tree to rest. "That was fun!" said Spot. The bird agreed, and they both took a nap in the shade.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and paint. One day, her mommy bought her a big blackboard to display her art. Lily was very happy and started drawing right away.

But one day, Lily's little brother came and scribbled all over her beautiful drawing. Lily was very upset and started crying. Her mommy came and saw what happened. She told Lily's brother that he should be sorry for what he did.

Lily's brother felt bad and said sorry to Lily. Lily forgave him and they both started drawing together on the blackboard. They learned that it's important to be kind to each other and respect other people's things. From that day on, they always shared the blackboard and drew together happily ever after.

There was a girl called Lila and she wanted to go to the city. She had never been there before, so it was so exciting! Lila put on her shoes and started to skip. As she skipped along the road, she saw the city in the distance.

The closer she got, the more miserable she felt. Everywhere she looked, there were tall buildings and grey sky's. She wanted to turn back, but she couldn't make herself do it. She walked closer, then started to skip again.

Finally, Lila reached the city. It was so much different than she imagined. It was loud and busy. She felt like a stranger in a strange place. She put her hands over her ears, but it still felt so loud.

Lila was miserable. She was so glad when she got back home. She vowed never to skip to the city again. From now on, she'll just have to stay in her own town.

Once there was a daddy and a daughter. The daddy loved coffee. Every morning he would make coffee. But one day, he spilled coffee all over the couch while he was making it. The daughter was very angry and she shouted at the daddy. She said, "Daddy, why did you do that?" The daddy got very hurt and he began to cry.

The daughter realised that she had been unkind and she felt sorry. She hugged her daddy and said, "I forgive you, Daddy". But instead of forgiving her, the daddy said, "You should not be so unkind. You should always be nice and be kind to others."

The moral of the story is that we should always remember to be kind and gentle to all, even when we are hurt. Even when we make mistakes, we should forgive and always be kind.

One day, a little child was walking in the park and came across another child. The other child was very bossy and kept telling the first child what to do. The first child didn't like this very much. So they kicked the bossy child and ran away.

The bossy child chased after the first child, but the first child was faster. They ran and ran and eventually stopped in a grassy field. When the bossy child caught up, the first child was ready. They kicked again and the bossy child ran away!

The first child was happy, but then they heard a cooing sound. It was a baby bird! The first child carefully kicked the ground in front of it, and the little bird flew away out of the field.

The child watched it go, feeling glad they had helped. They felt proud and ready to do more good deeds.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a nosy dragon named Dina. Dina loved to act silly and make everyone laugh. She wanted her friends to have fun!

One day, Dina found a computer in the forest. She was so excited!

"What does this do?" Dina asked.

A fairy replied, "I'm not sure, let's try it!"

The fairy and Dina acted out pushing the buttons on the computer. All of a sudden, music started to play and they jumped with excitement.

"Let's keep trying different things," said the fairy.

Dina was busy acting and pushing every button she could find. Suddenly, the computer started to make funny noises. "It's so funny!" laughed Dina.

The nosy dragon had so much fun with the computer in the forest. She learned how to act and how to make funny noises. Now she was the star of the show!

Once upon a time there was a little ship. It was an independent ship, so it could go wherever it wanted. One day, it decided to go on an adventure. It sailed and sailed and sailed until it reached a far away island. The island looked like a paradise, so the ship was excited to explore it.

But when the little ship approached the shore, it couldn't quite reach it. The water was too deep and the ship was too small. It was sad and disappointed, so it sailed back out to sea.

The ship was determined to reach the island, so it kept thinking and searching. Finally, it found a solution. Some friendly dolphins helped the ship travel close enough to the shore that it could just touch it with its front fin. But the ship was still too small to land on the beach.

The little ship was brave and independent. On its own, it figured out how to get close to the island, using its imagination and resourcefulness. And from then on and whenever it wanted, the little ship could go back to the island and explore it.

Once upon a time, there lived a happy little girl named Tina. She had a bouncing ball that she loved to play with. Every day, she would take her bouncing ball to the park and roll it down the trail. She would watch it as it rolled far away, and followed it with her eyes until a new adventure began.

One cold and chilly day, Tina found that her bouncing ball had suddenly disappeared down a deep dark hole! She looked around to see what she could do and spotted a tall man standing near her. "Can you help me find my bouncing ball?" she asked the tall man.

The tall man smiled and replied, "Yes I can! Follow me! I know the exact spot where your bouncing ball is." So, Tina followed the tall man on a new trail. After walking for a while, they finally arrived at the deep dark hole where Tina's bouncing ball was hidden! The tall man retrieved the bouncing ball, and returned it with a smile.

Tina was so happy to have her bouncing ball back! She thanked the tall man for his help and ran back home to play with her bouncing ball.

Once upon a time, there was a horse. He was very heavy. He liked to travel far and wide. Every day, his owners would remind him to stay safe and not wander too far away.

One day, the horse got so excited despite his heavy legs and he ran off away from his owners. He ran and ran and ran, until he reached a meadow. The grass was so green and soft. He decided to stay a while.

The owners were worried but they didn't know what happened to the horse. They searched for days and days until one day, they remembered the meadow. They went to the meadow and found the horse grazing peacefully.

From then on, his owners would remind him to be careful when playing and always stay close. He also reminded himself to always stay close to his owners, so he could continue to enjoy his freedom.

Once upon a time there was a powerful jellyfish called Louie. He swam in the sea and he loved to listen to the waves.

One day, Louie heard something different. It was a voice, calling out to him. "Louie, I need help," it said.

Louie was scared at first but then he decided to listen. He swam as close as he could and he saw a little girl.

"My kite is stuck in the tree. Will you help me get it back?" asked the girl.

Louie was powerful and brave, so he said yes. He swam as fast as he could to help the little girl. He used all his power to move the kite down from the tree.

The little girl was so happy that she gave Louie a big hug. Louie was so grateful and thanked her kindly. They said goodbye and Louie swam away, happy that he had helped.

Once there was a little girl called Mia who was three years old. She was excited to go to the beach with her Mummy and Daddy. When they arrived, they put down their towel and Mia explored the beach. She saw some little fishes swimming in the sea.

Mia's Mummy said, "Mia, do you want to swim too?"
Mia got very excited and ran to the sea.

Mummy gave Mia a watch to wear on her wrist. She was worried about the sea being too deep for Mia, but the watch would help.

Mia had a lot of fun. She swam and laughed, exploring the water. After an hour, Daddy said it was time to go back. Mia was a bit worried because she was having so much fun.

Mummy and Daddy hugged her and said that it was OK to be worried about leaving the beach. They promised that they would come back another day for Mia to swim again.

Mia knew that everything was all right. She was relieved and happy that she'd be able to swim again soon. The watch that Mummy had given her was still on her wrist and she was sure that it would remind her of the joy of swimming.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to tear things. One day she saw an envelope lying on the floor. She thought it was so fun to tear, so with a loud tear, she ripped it open. When she opened it, there were lots of colourful pieces of paper inside. She was so happy, that she started picking up the pieces and tearing them up until they were tiny. She kept tearing all the pieces until she could tear no more. Afterwards she felt all giggly and happy, so she laughed out loud. And they all lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Pete. Pete loved to play with his friends in the snow. One day, they decided to go on an adventure to find some fish.

As they were walking, Pete saw a big iceberg with a sign that said "Danger! Icy waters ahead!" Pete knew that meant the water was very cold and could hurt them. He wanted to teach his friends about the danger, but they didn't listen.

Soon, they came across a river with a strong current. Pete tried to warn his friends to go left, but they went right and got swept away. Pete quickly went left and found a safe spot to cross. He was sad that his friends didn't listen, but he knew it was important to always be safe and listen to warnings.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Freddy. Freddy was feeling very cold and didn't know what to do. He asked his friend, a bird named Benny, what he should do. Benny recommended that Freddy should find a warm place to stay.

Freddy hopped around looking for a warm place, but he couldn't find one. He saw a big rock and thought it would be warm, but when he hopped on it, it was still cold. He asked a mouse if she knew of any warm places, but she didn't know what to recommend.

Finally, Freddy saw a big, cozy-looking leaf. He hopped on it and it was warm! He was so happy that he thanked Benny for recommending he find a warm place. Freddy snuggled up on the leaf and fell asleep feeling warm and happy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was so excited to go on a special trip. She was going to meet a deep statue.

The next morning Lucyâ€™s mom drove her to the park. When they arrived, the statue was so tall. It was so deep, Lucy was scared. But then she said to herself, â€œItâ€™s okay, I can do this!â€

She slowly and carefully walked up to the statue. She was so close! She reached out and touched the statue. It felt so cold and wet.

Lucy was so proud that she had met the deep statue. She shouted and jumped for joy. She looked up to the sky and whispered a thank you to the statue.

Lucy felt so brave, she knew she could do anything! She hugged her mom and skipped off home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who wanted to swim. She had an ordinary helmet and it was bright red. She put the helmet on her head, smiled and jumped into the pool.

The water was cool and felt very nice. She practiced her swimming strokes and quickly became a very good swimmer. She was so happy in the pool that she swam around and around.

Time passed by and soon it was time to go home. She got out of the pool and took off her helmet. She smiled and waved goodbye to the pool before she walked home.

The girl was so proud of her swimming skills. Swimming always made her happy. She knew that she wanted to swim again soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play with her friends. They were having so much fun, but then Lily saw a drain. She wanted to study it, so she went closer to look. Suddenly, her ball fell into the drain!

Lily was very sad because she thought her ball was dead. She asked her friends what to do, but they didn't know. Just then, a kind man walked by and asked what happened. Lily told him about her ball, and he said he could help. He got a long stick and fished the ball out of the drain.

Lily was so happy and thanked the man. She learned that she should be careful around drains and that there are always kind people who can help. She went home and told her mom all about her adventure. Her mom was proud of her for being brave and for learning something new.

Once upon a time there was a brilliant car. It was so shiny and new. One day, the car drove off on an adventure! Along the way, it drove through a forest.

Suddenly, the car spotted a big tree branch in the road. It tried to swerve away but it was too late. The branch got stuck in the car's wheel!

The car was stuck, so it honked and honked for help. Suddenly, a big giant came out of the forest. The giant was so strong he could squeeze the branch away from the car's wheel!

So the giant grabbed the branch and gave it one big squeeze. The branch flew away and the car was Good As New. The car cheered and the giant cheered too.

The car drove away and thanked the giant for his help. The car never forgot the giant's brilliant squeeze!

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Mia. Mia loved to bake. She often went to her kitchen to mix and stir ingredients for her tasty treats.

One day, when she was in the kitchen, Mia found a big book. It was a novel, and Mia was so excited. She decided to sit down and read it.

But when Mia tried to read the book, the words sounded strange. She couldn't understand what they meant. Mia became deaf. She couldn't hear a thing.

Mia was so sad. She wondered if there was a way that she could hear the stories in the novel. Then, she had an idea. She grabbed her mixer, and mixed a bit of flour, sugar and milk. She put the dough in an oven and baked a jolly cake.

When Mia took the cake out of the oven, she heard music and noise. Mia smiled as she ate her cake. She knew that as long as she kept baking, she would never have to be deaf again.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. Ellie loved to decorate her house with pretty flowers and colorful balloons. One day, Ellie wanted to decorate her house for a big party. She asked her friend, a little mouse named Mickey, to help her decorate.

Mickey was so excited to help Ellie. "What can I do to help?" Mickey asked. "Can I blow the trumpet?" he added.

Ellie smiled and said, "Of course, you can blow the trumpet! It will make the party more fun!" Mickey was happy and started to blow the trumpet. It was an enormous trumpet, almost as big as Mickey himself! Everyone in the jungle heard the sound and came to join the party. Ellie and Mickey were very happy that their decorations and the enormous trumpet made the party so much fun.

Once upon a time, there was a curious cow who was always looking for something new. One day the cow decided to explore beyond its usual boundaries. But what the cow didn't know was that the new path ahead would separate it from the other cows for a very long time.

The cow kept going, more curious than ever before. As it walked further away, the other cows noticed and started to call out. But the cow kept walking and eventually the sound of the other cows faded away.

Everything seemed unfamiliar, but the cow was determined to keep going. Unfortunately, the cow didn't realize how far it had gone and before long it was completely lost.

The cow looked around, but all the scenery seemed strange and unfamiliar. Then, just as the cow started to worry, it heard the sound of the other cows again. The cow followed the sound and eventually it found its way back to where it had started.

The cow was relieved to be back with the other cows and it never ventured that far away again. However, it did remain curious about what was out there beyond its familiar boundaries.

Once there was a little girl called Alice. She was very intelligent and loved stories. One day, Alice read the most amazing story about a prince saving a princess from a giant dragon.

Alice was so excited about the story that she decided to go and find a giant dragon of her own! She travelled far and wide, but alas, she could not find one.

Alice was about to turn back and go home when she spotted a giant dragon in the distance. She was so excited and ran towards it. The dragon saw Alice coming and opened its mouth wide, ready to eat her!

Alice was so scared, but it was too late. The dragon ate her and the story had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in his backyard. He had a big hedge that he liked to hide behind. One day, Timmy accidentally broke a toy while playing. He was sad, but he knew he could fix it.

As he was fixing his toy, he noticed something strange. There was a mysterious hole in the hedge. Timmy was curious, so he peeked through the hole. On the other side of the hedge, he saw a beautiful garden with colorful flowers and butterflies.

Timmy was amazed by the mysterious garden. He wanted to go inside and explore, but he didn't know how to get there. He tried to break a hole in the hedge, but it was too strong. Timmy realized he needed help, so he went to ask his mom. Together, they found a way to go around the hedge and into the mysterious garden. Timmy was so happy to have discovered something new and exciting.

John was playing hockey in the park. He was whacking the puck around and having a lot of fun. But then he noticed it was getting gloomy outside, and he got a bit sad. He sighed and put away his hockey stick and skates, and went home.

On the way home John saw some kids playing a game of tag. He wanted to play too, but he didn't feel like it. He continued home, sighing.

When he got home, his mom asked him why he was so sad. John didn't know how to explain, so he said he was just tired. His mom hugged him and said that would be alright. He smiled and kept on walking.

John eventually forgot his sadness and he remembered the fun he had playing hockey. He smiled as he remembered what happened in the park and he was glad he was home.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Pete. One day, Pete decided to go for a bounce around his garden. He jumped and jumped and jumped, until he eventually bounced so high that he made it up to the sky!

Pete was so excited to reach the sky and he couldn't wait to explore. He bounced around and soon saw the whole world! The world looked so big and Pete felt so small. Suddenly, Pete felt a bit ashamed. What would the world think of him, so small and tiny?

Just then, Pete saw a beautiful blue bird. It flew up to him and said "Hi Pete, donâ€™t be ashamed. You can explore the world if you like!"

Pete smiled and said "Thank you bird. I will!" And with that, he bounced off to explore the world. He went everywhere, and had lots of fun adventures!

Jack was three years old and loved playing in the park. One day, while he was swinging he felt the earth shake. Jack started to cry. His dad quickly came to his side and asked him what was wrong.

Jack said, "The ground is moving!"

His dad calmly said, "That was an earthquake. But you don't need to be scared, I'm here to comfort you." His dad put his arms around Jack and hugged him tightly.

Jack looked out the window. He saw the sky was a gray color and he was scared. His dad said, "It's okay Jack. Everything is gonna be alright. It's just a little earthquake, nothing we can't handle together."

Jack smiled and his dad gave him one more hug. Jack felt like he was safe now, so he went back outside to play.

The curtains were hanging cleanly in the windows of the little room. Every day, the girl would run in and whisper secrets to them. She hadn't noticed it before, but today, when she was talking in her very quietest voice, the curtains rustled as if in response. Her eyes grew wider as she heard what sounded like an echo of her own whisper.

Curious, she asked the curtains, "Can you understand me?". The curtains didn't move. She whispered the question again and waited. She heard a faint whispering in response, but it wasn't the same as if she were speaking. This whisper felt different somehow.

The girl waited and listened. Suddenly, the curtains moved again. This time they were pushing back, inviting her closer. As the girl looked closer, she saw a crack in the window and she could now hear more clearly the voice she had heard earlier. "Come here," it said.

The girl took a deep breath, trembling with anticipation and excitement. She stepped closer and the curtain parted. Behind it was a secret garden. Everything was clean and vibrant and the girl felt more alive than she had ever felt before. She was finally on an adventure of her own.

The girl and the whisper from the curtains had a lot more to share.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy was playing with his toy truck when he heard his mom calling him for dinner.

Timmy ran inside and sat down at the table with his family. His mom had made spaghetti, Timmy's favorite. As Timmy was eating, he accidentally spilled some sauce on his shirt.

Timmy's older sister, Sarah, started to laugh and said, "Ha ha, Timmy, you look silly with sauce on your shirt!" Timmy felt embarrassed and didn't want to eat anymore.

His mom saw that Timmy was upset and said, "It's okay, Timmy. It's just a mild stain. We can wash it out." Timmy felt better and finished his dinner.

After dinner, Timmy's mom sat him down and said, "Timmy, it's not nice to laugh at someone when they make a mistake. We should always be kind to others." Timmy nodded his head and promised to be kind to others from now on.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big doll and Ben had a small car. Lily liked her doll very much, but she wished she had a car too. She asked Ben if she could play with his car for a while.

"No, this is my car. You have your doll. Go away!" Ben said. He was not very friendly.

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to have a car too. She thought of a plan. She saw a bottle on the table. It had a label that said "shrink". She did not know what that word meant, but she thought it might make things smaller. She took the bottle and sprayed some of it on Ben's car.

Ben saw what Lily did and shouted. "Hey, what are you doing? Stop it! You are making my car shrink!"

Lily laughed. She thought it was funny to see Ben's car get smaller and smaller. She picked up the tiny car and put it in her pocket. She said, "Now I have a car too. And you have nothing. Ha ha!"

Ben was very upset. He cried and ran to his mom. He told her what Lily did. Mom was not happy. She scolded Lily and made her give back the car. She said, "Lily, that was not nice. You should not take things that are not yours. And you should not use things that you do not understand. You could have hurt Ben or yourself. You need to say sorry to Ben and share your toys."

Lily felt sorry. She realized she was wrong. She gave back the car to Ben and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was mean. I should not have sprayed your car. Can we be friends again?"

Ben was still sad, but he forgave Lily. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry too. I should have been more friendly. Can we play together?"

Lily and Ben hugged and smiled. They decided to play together and share their toys. They learned a lesson. They wished they would never fight again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack. He was always very creative and loved trying to find new ways of doing things.

One day, Jack wanted to get a fancy new name. He was tired of the same old name, Jack. He wanted something a bit more creative!

So Jack asked his mum, "Mum, can I get a new name?" His mum said kindly, "Hmmm... I don't know, Jack. What kind of name do you want?"

Jack thought long and hard, and then replied, "I want something special, something creative!"

His mum said, "Well okay, why don't we try out some new names and see what fits?" She thought and then said, "How about 'James'?"

Jack liked it. He grinned and said, "James! That's a perfect name for me. Can I get it please, mum?"

His mum nodded and smiled. She said, "Of course you can, Jack. From now on, you shall be known as James!"

And so, Jack became James! He was so happy with his new, creative name.

Once upon a time there was a dependable little girl named Jemma. She enjoyed playing outside and loved her toys the most. She always wanted to be good and do what she was supposed to do. Every day she would brush her teeth with her special brush.

One day Jemma was given a special task. She was told to remember three numbers. She was very excited and was determined to do a good job. She used her brush to help her remember each number. She wrote one number on each of the three bristles of the brush. Then she looked in the mirror, closed her eyes and tried to remember.

Jemma was so proud of herself after she remembered each of the numbers. She kept her brush close so she could always remember the numbers too. Every day she was dependable and remembered the numbers like she was told. Jemma's brush was her helpful reminder.

Once upon a time, there was an old man walking in a park. He was whistling and singing a happy tune!

Little John was in the park too, playing with his friends. He saw the old man walking and he stopped to watch him. Little John was very thoughtful and he wondered why the man was so happy.

Suddenly, the old man stopped whistling and looked over at Little John. He said, â€œWhy donâ€™t you come and join me in a sing-along?â€ Little John was so excited! He quickly ran over to the man and started singing along with him.

The old man and Little John whistled and sang together for hours. Everywhere they went, people could be heard clapping and cheering for them. Little John had never been so happy before!

That day, Little John learned an important lesson - that being thoughtful and kind can make other people happy too.

Once upon a time, in a small park, there was a broken swing. It was sad because no one could play on it. The swing wanted to be fixed so kids could have fun again.

One day, a little boy saw the broken swing. He had an idea! He went home and found a big piece of cardboard. The boy brought the cardboard to the park and put it on the broken swing.

Now, kids could sit on the cardboard and swing! They were so happy to play on the swing again. The broken swing was not sad anymore. It was happy to see the kids having fun. And they all played on the swing every day.

One day, Mommy decided to take Susie to the park. Susie was very excited! She put on her shirt, shoes, and hat and ran outside with Mommy.

When they got to the park, they saw lots of people playing. Mommy said, "Susie, you can play over there, but remember to stay close to me."

Susie thanked Mommy and ran off to the playground. She saw some boys playing with a ball. She asked them if she could join, but they said no. Susie was sad.

But then Mommy called Susie over. She said, "Susie, it's OK. I will permit you to play with them." Susie was happy and ran to the boys. The boys said she could join, but at one point, the ball bounced and rolled into a dirty bush.

The boys were scared to go in! But Susie was brave. She reached into the bush and found the ball. She came out holding the ball with a huge smile on her face. The boys thanked Susie, and they all continued playing.

At the end of the day, Mommy and Susie said goodbye to the boys and went home. Susie was very happy; she had a great day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the sun with her friends. One day, they decided to play a game of tag. Lily was running so fast that she didn't see a rock in her way. She tripped and fell, ripping her favorite dress.

Lily was sad because her dress was torn. Her friend Sarah saw that Lily was upset and offered her a cloth to wipe away her tears. Lily was grateful for her friend's kindness and felt better.

Later, Lily's mom asked her what happened to her dress. Lily told her the truth and said, "I tripped and fell." Her mom was proud of her for being honest and said, "It's okay to make mistakes. The important thing is to learn from them and step forward."

Lily learned that it's important to be honest and grateful for the kindness of others. She also learned that it's okay to make mistakes and to keep moving forward.

Once upon a time there were two humans. One was very alert, and the other was sleepy. The alert human said, "Let's go for a walk." But the sleepy human just stayed in the same spot.

The alert human said, "Come on! Let's walk into the forest." But the sleepy one just shrugged and said, "No."

"Oh, come on!" said the alert human. "It'll be fun!"

Finally, the sleepy human agreed and they started walking into the forest. But when they got there, they got separated. The alert human kept walking and calling out the sleepy one's name, but he couldn't find him. He was all alone.

Finally, he heard someone call out his name. He looked up and there was the sleepy human! He had found him!

The alert human breathed a sigh of relief and said, "Let's go home together!"

And so that's what they did. They always stayed together from then on!

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Benny. Benny loved to sit under the big oak tree in the forest. One day, Benny made a promise to his friend, the rabbit. Benny promised to share his honey with the rabbit.

But one day, when Benny went to get the honey, he found that it had gone bad. The honey was bitter and not good to eat. Benny was very sad because he couldn't keep his promise to his friend.

The rabbit came to visit Benny and asked for the honey. Benny had to tell the truth and said that the honey was not good. The rabbit was very upset and didn't want to be friends with Benny anymore. Benny felt very alone and sad, wishing he could make it up to his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was only 3 years old. She was playing in a huge park with lots of other kids, when she saw a big path up ahead. The path was huge and meandered through the park and across the grassy fields.

The little girl wanted to follow the path, so she started walking along it. As she followed the path, she saw a big crack in the ground. The crack was so big that it made the path impossible to cross.

The little girl became very angry and sad. She asked her mom, "Mom, can you help me fix the crack in the path?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course I can help. I'll get your dad and he can help us fix it."

Mom and Dad brought shovels from home and started digging around the edges of the crack. After a lot of work, the crack was filled and the path was fixed.

The little girl was so happy and excited! She smiled and ran back to her friends to tell them that the path was fixed. They all rejoiced and ran along the huge path together.

The End.

One day, a fast dog named Spot and a slow turtle named Tim were friends. They liked to play together. They wanted to send a letter to their friend, Cat. But they needed a stamp to send the letter.

Spot said, "I will go to the store to get a stamp. I am fast." Tim said, "I will support you, Spot. I will wait here."

Spot ran to the store very fast. But there was a big rock in the way. Spot could not jump over the rock. He was sad. Tim came and saw Spot was sad.

Tim said, "I will help you, Spot. We can go around the rock together." Spot said, "Thank you, Tim." They went around the rock and got the stamp. They sent the letter to Cat. They were happy friends.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her. One day, she was out looking for an adventure. Suddenly, she heard a loud, noisy noise coming from the top of a hill. She hopped up the hill and saw a bird with a long neck. The bird kept sorting through the leaves on the ground.

"What are you looking for, Mr. Bird?" asked Lucy excitedly.

The bird turned around and said "I'm looking for a spider to eat. Have you seen one?"

Lucy thought for a minute and said, "I haven't seen any spiders, but I could help you sort through the leaves to find one!"

The bird smiled, and said, "That would be great!"

So, Lucy and the bird worked together and sorted through the leaves. Soon enough, they spotted a small, black spider. The bird picked it up and thanked Lucy.

"Thank you for helping me find my lunch, Lucy!" said the bird.

Lucys smiled and said, "You're welcome! It was fun helping you sort!"

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She had a cup that was blue. Every morning she would get out of bed and drink from the cup. This made her very happy.

One day, Jane asked her parents for something special. They told her that if she waited until bedtime, something good would happen. Jane was happy and couldn't wait.

When bedtime came, Jane was so excited. But something seemed strange. Her parents had a surprise for her, but it didn't look like anything she had expected.

Her parents offered her a new cup - one that was even bluer than her old cup. She was so excited. The cup seemed magical, and it sparkled in the light. Jane knew that this cup was special and it would make her happy.

Once, there was a very old shape. It was round and had nine sides. It liked to tell stories to the other shapes.

One day, it told a story about a snake and a tiger. But a square shape didn't like this. It wanted the old shape to tell stories about a snail and a ladybug instead.

But the old shape didn't want to change its story. So, it kept telling the story about the snake and the tiger.

The square shape was very angry. It shouted and shouted, but the old shape still wouldn't listen.

Then another shape stepped in. It was a triangle shape and it was very wise. It explained to the square shape that everyone has different stories to tell.

The square shape understood and it smiled. Everyone was happy and the old shape carried on telling its story.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and collect pebbles. One day, she found a shiny pebble that she wanted to give to her friend, Max. So, she put it in a small box and asked her mom to deliver it to Max's house.

But when Max received the box, he was angry because he thought it was a prank from Lily. He threw the box on the ground and the pebble fell out. Lily's mom saw what happened and explained that Lily just wanted to give him a present. Max felt bad and went to apologize to Lily.

From that day on, Lily and Max played together every day and collected pebbles together. They never got angry at each other again.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim went to school. His teacher, Miss Kate, was very nice. Tim had many friends who were pupils too. They played and learned together. One day, Tim saw a big, shiny toy car in a shop. It was very expensive, but he wanted it so much.

Tim asked his mom, "Can I have the expensive toy car, please?" His mom said, "No, it is too much money. We cannot buy it." Tim was sad, but he had an idea. He thought he could take the toy car without his mom knowing.

The next day, Tim went to the shop and took the toy car. He hid it in his bag and went to school. When he got to school, he showed his friends the toy car. They all wanted to play with it. Tim let them play with the car, but he didn't tell them he took it from the shop.

Miss Kate saw the pupils playing with the expensive toy car. She knew it was not Tim's car. She asked Tim, "Where did you get this car?" Tim didn't want to tell the truth. He lied and said, "My mom bought it for me." Miss Kate knew Tim was not telling the truth. She called his mom and found out he took the car from the shop.

Tim got in big trouble. His mom was very sad and angry. She made Tim return the toy car to the shop and say sorry. Tim learned that taking things without asking is wrong. He felt bad and promised never to do it again. But because he lied, his friends and Miss Kate did not trust him anymore. Tim was very sad and lonely.

Mummy and John were in the park. John was eating his ice-cream, while Mummy was talking to a friend. Suddenly, John felt embarrassed as he saw everyone around them staring at him. He quickly tried to hide the ice-cream behind his back.

Mummy noticed his embarrassment and asked, "What's wrong, John?"

John replied, "They are all looking at me."

Mummy smiled and said, "That's normal, the ice-cream is yummy, why don't you show it to them?"

John reluctantly put the ice-cream back in his hand and tried to smile, but the other children kept staring at him. He felt even more embarrassed and started to cry.

Mummy hugged him and said, "That's ok, everyone makes mistakes. Let's go home now."

John sadly nodded and Mummy took him home. The ice-cream was all gone, but the embarrassment he felt was not.

One day, a humble alligator went for a walk. He saw a little bird sitting on a tree. The alligator wanted to be friends with the bird.

"Hello, bird," said the alligator. "Can we be friends?"

The bird looked at the alligator and said, "Yes, we can be friends."

They played together all day. They had so much fun. The alligator and the bird were very happy to be friends.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy boy. He lived next to a deep, dark well. He was always curious and one day he decided to come closer to the well to take a peek inside. His dad was very worried and told him: "Don't come close to the well! You can hurt yourself!â€ But the boy ignored him and came closer. Suddenly, he lost balance and fell inside the well.

The boy leaned against the walls of the well and started to cry. Then he heard a voice from above: â€œDo not worry! I am here to help youâ€. He looked up and saw a beautiful angel right above the well. The angel asked: â€œDo you remember what your dad said? If you do as your dad tells you, you can prevent yourself from getting into dangerous situations."

The angel flew away, while the boy felt really grateful. He decided that he would always listen to what his dad said. From that day on, he would never be clumsy around the well again!

The moral of the story is that it is important to listen to your parents' advice. They know what is best for you, even if it may seem unimportant or uncomfortable at the time.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Sarah. Jack was a brave player and Sarah was a shy designer.

One day, Jack said to Sarah, "Let's make something special today". Sarah was very shy, so she hesitated and shook her head no.

But Jack didn't give up. "Let's make a big house," he said. "It will be so fun!"

Finally, Sarah agreed. She started to design while Jack ran to the store to get supplies. When Jack returned, Sarah showed him her plan.

Jack was very impressed. With Sarah's help, he began to build the house. They worked together all day, and eventually, the house was done.

Jack and Sarah beamed with pride. Sarah had overcome her shyness, and together they had made something amazing.

Jessie had a thin guitar. It made him happy to play it. Every day, he would strum the strings and pluck little tunes. One day, however, something strange happened. He felt a tickle in his nose. He paused his playing and then he sneezed! His guitar made a funny noise when he sneezed. He smiled and continued playing, with the guitar sounding slightly different after the sneeze. Jessie kept playing and eventually the strange sound went away. Jessie kept his guitar thin and kept playing delicious melodies every day.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fat cat named Tom. Tom lived in a cozy house with his owner, Lily. One day, Tom met a beautiful cat named Bella. They fell in love and decided to get married.

Lily was happy for them and asked, "Tom, are you sure you want to marry Bella?" Tom replied, "Yes, I love her spirit and she loves mine."

The wedding was held in the garden and all the cats in the neighborhood came to celebrate. They danced and sang all night long. Tom and Bella were very happy together and lived happily ever after.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to watch his favorite show on the television. Tim was very calm as he sat on the floor in front of the television. He waited for his show to start.

His mom walked into the room and said, "Tim, please stand up and turn on the television." Tim stood up and pushed the button on the television. The screen lit up, and his show began to play.

As Tim watched his show, a friendly dog named Spot came into the room. Spot sat down next to Tim and watched the television too. They both enjoyed the show and were very calm and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little ant named Andy. He loved to crawl around and explore the world. One day, he met a friendly ladybug named Lily.

"Hi there, Andy!" said Lily. "What are you up to today?"

"Just crawling around, looking for something special," replied Andy.

As they continued on their way, they saw a big, juicy strawberry in the distance.

"That looks like an ordinary strawberry," said Lily.

But Andy had a feeling that it was anything but ordinary. He crawled closer and closer until he was right next to the strawberry. Suddenly, he saw something shiny and sparkly inside the strawberry!

"Look, Lily!" he exclaimed. "It's a treasure!"

Together, they carefully dug out the treasure and found a beautiful diamond. From that day on, Andy and Lily crawled around together, looking for more treasures to discover.

Jimmy and Alice were best friends. They liked to race each other every day.

One day, they saw a group of people on the other side of the park.

Alice said, "Let's go clap for them."
Jimmy shook his head. He was too sleepy.

Alice said, "Come on. I don't want to go alone. Please?

Jimmy sighed. He reluctantly followed Alice across the park.

When they reached the group of people, Alice started to clap. But Jimmy just stood there, feeling too tired to move.

Alice, who was getting angry, poked Jimmy in the side. She said, "Clap! Clap!"

Jimmy, who was getting scared, pushed Alice away.

The group of people stopped what they were doing and watched. They looked angry.

Alice started to cry. She said, "Jimmy, why did you do that?!"

Jimmy, who felt sad and scared, couldn't find any words.

The group of people started to move towards Jimmy and Alice. Jimmy and Alice ran away as fast as they could. They were very scared and they never raced each other again.

Tom and Mia were playing with a balloon in the park. They liked to toss it to each other and watch it float in the air. Sometimes, they would try to catch it with their palms, but it was slippery and bouncy.

"Look, Tom, I can hold it with one hand!" Mia said, as she squeezed the balloon with her fingers.

"Wow, you are great, Mia!" Tom said, as he clapped his hands. "Can I try?"

"Sure, here you go!" Mia said, as she released the balloon and threw it to Tom.

Tom reached out his palm and tried to grab the balloon, but he missed. The balloon flew away from him and towards a big tree.

"Oh no, the balloon!" Tom said, as he ran after it.

Mia followed him, but they were too late. The balloon got stuck on a branch and popped.

"Pop!" They heard a loud noise and saw the balloon burst into pieces.

They stopped and looked at each other. They felt sad and disappointed.

"I'm sorry, Tom, it was my fault," Mia said, as she hugged him.

"No, it's okay, Mia, it was an accident," Tom said, as he hugged her back.

They decided to go back to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a bench nearby. They told them what happened and asked for another balloon.

Mom and dad smiled and gave them a new balloon. They said they were proud of them for being kind and sharing.

Tom and Mia thanked them and went back to playing. They were happy again and forgot about the popped balloon. They had fun with their new balloon and each other.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Max. Max was very loyal to his owner, a little girl named Lily. Max loved to play with Lily and go on walks with her.

One day, Lily and Max went to the park to play. They played fetch and ran around together. Suddenly, a big bird flew overhead. Lily looked up and said, "Wow, that bird can fly really high!" Max barked and wagged his tail.

Later that day, Lily and Max were walking home when they saw the bird again. This time, the bird swooped down and grabbed Max with its claws. Lily screamed and tried to save Max, but it was too late. The bird flew away with Max and Lily never saw her loyal friend again.

Before the bird took Max away, Lily had a bad feeling in her stomach. She knew something bad was going to happen, but she didn't listen to her instincts. Now, she was very sad and missed Max very much.

Jack and Jane were playing a game. They were running around trying to catch each other. They were laughing and having fun. Suddenly, Jack stumbled and fell down.

Jack looked a little sad. Jane quickly said, "It's ok! Don't worry."

"What kind of game do you want to play next?" she asked.

Jack thought for a bit and then he said, "Let's play hide-and-seek. That's an easy game and I like it."

So, they started to play hide-and-seek. Jane hid first, but then Jack couldn't find her. He stumbled all around the house, trying to find Jane, but he couldn't locate her.

Finally, Jane jumped out from behind the sofa and yelled, "I'm here!"

Jack started laughing. Jane said, "Let's play again. We can play it as many times as you want!"

Jack smiled and then shouted, "Yes! Let's do it!"

They had lots of fun playing hide-and-seek and then playing even more games. Jack and Jane had a happy day together.

Once upon a time, there was a big truck. The truck was very loud and had many wheels. It was a vehicle that helped move things from one place to another.

One day, a little bird was flying above the truck. The bird was very graceful and flew with ease. The bird wanted to measure how big the truck was, so it flew down and landed on the hood.

The bird looked at the truck and saw that it was very long and tall. It was too big for the little bird to measure, but it was still very impressive. The bird flew away, feeling happy to have seen such a big and powerful vehicle.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. They saw a bird flying in the sky. Lily asked her mom, "Can I fly like a bird today?" Her mom said, "No, Lily. We can't fly like birds because we don't have wings. But we can watch them from a distant."

Lily saw a boy playing with a ball. She asked her mom, "Can I play with him?" Her mom said, "Yes, you may. But you must ask him if he will permit you to play with him." Lily went to the boy and asked him, "Can I play with you?" The boy said, "Yes, you may. Let's play together!"

They played together for a long time. Lily had so much fun with the boy. When it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to the boy and thanked him for playing with her. She told her mom, "Today was a great day at the park!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived on a ranch. Every morning, she would go outside and see the wild horses. She loved them, especially the pink one! She wished she could become a horse, so she could run in the fields with them.

One day, while playing in the fields, the little girl found a magical necklace. It was beautiful, with a single pink gem in the center. She wore it around her neck and suddenly she became a horse! She was so excited that she ran with the wild horses, as fast as she could!

The little girl and the wild horses explored their ranch together, prancing through the meadows and playing in the streams. They even galloped beneath the stars at night!

The next morning, the little girl found the necklace again. She put it on, and she became a little girl once more. But she never forgot her adventure on the ranch with the wild horses - especially the pink one!

Once there was a comfortable seat in the park. It was brown and furry and looked like a lion. One day a little boy saw the seat and wanted to sit on it. So he walked over to it and hopped on. He was very surprised to see that the seat has a tail! He giggled. Then, without warning, the seat started to move and roar! The boy was so scared that he jumped off and ran away. After the boy left, the seat changed back into a lion. It looked around the park, yawned and then walked away.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was very excited, because her mom had just given her a surprise. It was a special presentâ€"a red pedal car! She could go anywhere she wanted with it. Her mom also said she had to be organized when driving it.

The girl was a bit scared at first, but then she felt brave. She thought it looked fun, so she asked her mom if she could go for a drive. Her mom said yes and gave her a permit to be in the streets.

The girl put on her helmet and safety vest, then she hopped into her pedal car. She started pedaling as soon as she could. She was so happy and excited to explore the world and feel the wind in her face.

She drove around the town, meeting all kinds of people. She went over the hills, up and down the roads, and everywhere felt different. Everyone said hello and waved to her, and it made her smile.

By the end of the day, the girl felt so proud. She drove the pedal car so well, and it was all because her mom had taught her how to be organized. She thanked her mom for the special present and promised to be careful when outside in the streets.

The girl then grabbed her permit and her special pedal car, hopped in, and drove off into the sunset.

One day, a young girl named Betty wanted to go explore outside. She put on her shoes, grabbed her favorite teddy bear, and set off to find something exciting.

Betty walked and walked until she stumbled upon an unusual stone. It was big, round, and sparkly. She had never seen a stone like this before! She decided to stay with the stone and see what it did.

Betty spent the whole day playing with the stone. She threw it in the air, put it in her pocket, and even gave it a hug. Then the sun began to go down and it was time to go home.

Betty said goodbye to the stone and ran to her house. From that day on, she always stayed near the unusual stone whenever she went exploring - because it was her special friend.

Once upon a time, there was a rich jewel. It was the most beautiful thing in the world and people said it was magical. Everyone wanted it, but no one could find it. Then one day a little girl came running to the village. She said she knew where the jewel was!

Everyone was excited and followed the girl. She brought them to the edge of a big lake. On the other side was a little castle. The girl said the jewel was hidden inside.

The brave villagers crossed the lake and came to the castle. They looked everywhere but could not find the jewel. Then, one of them saw a hole in the wall. Inside was the rich jewel!

The villagers were so happy! They took the jewel back to the village and showed it to everyone. They decided to keep it for safe keeping. They all said it was the best thing ever!

George was so excited. Today was the day of the Lively Clown show! He had waited all week and now it was almost time. Getting ready, George went to the bathroom and wiped his face. He made sure he looked his best so he could meet the Lively Clown.

When George arrived, the show had already started. He saw that the Lively Clown was dancing and smiling at the audience. Everyone was having so much fun!

George watched the Lively Clown with awe. When it was finally his turn to meet the clown, he started to feel a little bit nervous.

The Lively Clown was now standing right in front of him. George was so excited he forgot to say hello! The clown waved its hand in the air and asked, "Well, hello there! What do you want from me today?".

George smiled and said, "I want a big hug from the Lively Clown".

The clown laughed and gave George a big, warm hug. With a big smile, the clown said goodbye and waved goodbye to the audience.

George was still smiling when he returned home. He decided that he would always remember the Lively Clown and the wonderful hug.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the park. They saw a big crane lifting heavy things. They wanted to know how it worked.

"Let's go and ask the man who drives the crane," Ben said.

"OK, but be careful," Anna said.

They ran to the crane and saw a man sitting inside. He was wearing a helmet and a vest.

"Hello, sir," Ben said. "Can you tell us how you make the crane move?"

The man smiled and opened the door. He invited them to sit with him.

"Sure, I can tell you," he said. "The crane has a motor and a cable. The motor makes the cable go up and down. The cable has a hook at the end. I use a joystick to control the hook. I can lift and lower things with the hook."

"Wow, that's amazing," Anna said. "You must be very intelligent to do that."

The man laughed and said, "Thank you, but I'm not the only one who is intelligent. The crane is also intelligent. It has sensors and computers that help me. They tell me how much weight I can lift and how far I can move. They also warn me if there is any danger or problem."

"Really? How do they do that?" Ben asked.

The man showed them a screen and some buttons. He explained how the sensors and computers worked. He also told them some rules and safety tips for using the crane.

Anna and Ben learned a lot from the man. They thanked him and said goodbye. They went back to their toys and pretended to be crane drivers.

They had fun and also learned something new. They realized that the crane was not just a big toy, but a useful and intelligent machine. They also realized that the man was not just a driver, but a teacher and a friend. They learned to be curious, respectful, and grateful.

Once upon a time there was a baby tortoise called Mike. Mike was very tough, unlike most other tortoises. He wanted to go to the market, but was too small.

So Mike decided to take a nap. He curled up and closed his eyes, dreaming about the things he would see when he was big enough to go to the market.

When Mike woke up from his nap, he had grown! He was now big enough to go out and explore the market. So Mike set off, determined to take in all the sights and sounds of the market.

As he walked around, he noticed all kinds of interesting things, like piles of bright fruit and vegetables, and lively music playing. Mike was very delighted, he had never seen anything like it before.

Mike stayed in the market all day, exploring until the evening. He was so happy he had taken a nap and had the chance to see the market.

The next day, he set off for another adventure, knowing that if he ever wanted to see the market again, he would need to take a nap and grow big and tough.

It was a hot day and Sandy and her mommy were at the park. Sandy blinked in the bright sunlight and looked around. Everything was so much fun.

Suddenly, Sandy saw a butterfly fluttering in the sky. She was mesmerized. She started to walk towards it when her mommy yelled "wait, Sandy!"

Sandy stopped and looked back at her mommy. Her mommy blinked and smiled. "Let's go and have a picnic," she said.

So they spread a blanket on the grass and unpacked the food. While they ate, the butterfly flew down and landed on Sandy's shoulder. Sandy gasped in surprise and smiled. She closed her eyes and blinked slowly. She felt so happy.

Afterwards, Sandy and her mommy packed everything away and headed home. Sandy couldn't stop smiling. She promised herself that she would always remember that special day at the park.

Once upon a time there was a boy who looked for an adventure. He ran down to the beach, hoping to find something fun.

He looked around the shore and saw a large octopus in the sand. The boy wanted to catch it. He waited and waited, but the octopus kept running away from him.

Finally, the octopus got stuck in the sand. The boy ran so fast and caught the octopus. It felt slippery and slimy.

The octopus tried to get out of the boy's hands, but he was strong and held tightly. Suddenly, the octopus made a bad sound. It made the boy jump and he dropped the octopus.

The octopus swam away, leaving the boy by himself. He was happy that he got to catch the octopus, even though it was bad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the rain and jump in the puddles. One day, she went outside and it started to rain. She ran around and got very wet. Her clothes were soaked and her hair was dripping.

As she was walking back to her house, she saw a big rainbow in the sky. She wondered how it got there and why it was so pretty. She felt happy and excited to see something so wonderful.

When she got inside, her mom made her a cup of hot chocolate. Lily took a sip and made a funny face because it tasted bitter. Her mom added some sugar and stirred it until it tasted sweet. Lily smiled and felt warm inside.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl. She had a special weapon. It made her feel very brave.
One day, the girl had a hard task. She needed to manage this task all by herself. She was very scared, but she tried her best.
The brave girl was able to manage it. She was so proud of herself.
Suddenly, she noticed the dead animal in front of her. It had been hurt by a dangerous weapon. The brave girl was sad.
She knew it would be hard, but she managed to take care of the animal. With help from her special weapon, she was able to make it better again.
The brave girl was very happy. She was proud that she had managed to help the animal.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a black cat named Mittens. One day, Lily was playing with Mittens and she dropped her toy. Mittens went to get it for her, but he got into trouble. He accidentally knocked over a vase and it broke into many pieces. Lily's mom was not happy, but Lily told her it was her fault because she dropped her toy. Lily's mom forgave her and they all played together with Mittens.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. He loved gum. One day, he found a thin piece of gum on the ground. He thought it was very special. He put the gum in his pocket to save it for later.

Tom went to play with his friend, Sam. They played a game where they had to escape from a pretend monster. They ran and hid, but the monster always found them. Tom felt scared, but he remembered his special gum. He thought it could help them win the game.

Tom took out the thin gum and shared it with Sam. They both chewed the gum and started to run from the monster again. But this time, they did not escape. The gum made them feel sick and slow. The monster caught them, and they lost the game. Tom and Sam were very sad. They learned never to pick up gum from the ground again.

There was once upon a time a soldier who for many years had served the

king faithfully, but when the war came to an end could serve no longer

because of the many wounds which he had received. The king said to him:

'You may return to your home, I need you no longer, and you will not

receive any more money, for he only receives wages who renders me

service for them.' Then the soldier did not know how to earn a living,

went away greatly troubled, and walked the whole day, until in the

evening he entered a forest. When darkness came on, he saw a light,

which he went up to, and came to a house wherein lived a witch. 'Do give

me one night's lodging, and a little to eat and drink,' said he to

her, 'or I shall starve.' 'Oho!' she answered, 'who gives anything to a

run-away soldier? Yet will I be compassionate, and take you in, if you

will do what I wish.' 'What do you wish?' said the soldier. 'That you

should dig all round my garden for me, tomorrow.' The soldier consented,

and next day laboured with all his strength, but could not finish it by

the evening. 'I see well enough,' said the witch, 'that you can do no

more today, but I will keep you yet another night, in payment for

which you must tomorrow chop me a load of wood, and chop it small.' The

soldier spent the whole day in doing it, and in the evening the witch

proposed that he should stay one night more. 'Tomorrow, you shall only

do me a very trifling piece of work. Behind my house, there is an old

dry well, into which my light has fallen, it burns blue, and never goes

out, and you shall bring it up again.' Next day the old woman took him

to the well, and let him down in a basket. He found the blue light, and

made her a signal to draw him up again. She did draw him up, but when he

came near the edge, she stretched down her hand and wanted to take the

blue light away from him. 'No,' said he, perceiving her evil intention,

'I will not give you the light until I am standing with both feet upon

the ground.' The witch fell into a passion, let him fall again into the

well, and went away.

The poor soldier fell without injury on the moist ground, and the blue

light went on burning, but of what use was that to him? He saw very well

that he could not escape death. He sat for a while very sorrowfully,

then suddenly he felt in his pocket and found his tobacco pipe, which

was still half full. 'This shall be my last pleasure,' thought he,

pulled it out, lit it at the blue light and began to smoke. When the

smoke had circled about the cavern, suddenly a little black dwarf stood

before him, and said: 'Lord, what are your commands?' 'What my commands

are?' replied the soldier, quite astonished. 'I must do everything you

bid me,' said the little man. 'Good,' said the soldier; 'then in the

first place help me out of this well.' The little man took him by the

hand, and led him through an underground passage, but he did not forget

to take the blue light with him. On the way the dwarf showed him the

treasures which the witch had collected and hidden there, and the

soldier took as much gold as he could carry. When he was above, he said

to the little man: 'Now go and bind the old witch, and carry her before

the judge.' In a short time she came by like the wind, riding on a wild

tom-cat and screaming frightfully. Nor was it long before the little man

reappeared. 'It is all done,' said he, 'and the witch is already hanging

on the gallows. What further commands has my lord?' inquired the dwarf.

'At this moment, none,' answered the soldier; 'you can return home, only

be at hand immediately, if I summon you.' 'Nothing more is needed than

that you should light your pipe at the blue light, and I will appear

before you at once.' Thereupon he vanished from his sight.

The soldier returned to the town from which he came. He went to the

best inn, ordered himself handsome clothes, and then bade the landlord

furnish him a room as handsome as possible. When it was ready and the

soldier had taken possession of it, he summoned the little black manikin

and said: 'I have served the king faithfully, but he has dismissed me,

and left me to hunger, and now I want to take my revenge.' 'What am I to

do?' asked the little man. 'Late at night, when the king's daughter is

in bed, bring her here in her sleep, she shall do servant's work for

me.' The manikin said: 'That is an easy thing for me to do, but a very

dangerous thing for you, for if it is discovered, you will fare ill.'

When twelve o'clock had struck, the door sprang open, and the manikin

carried in the princess. 'Aha! are you there?' cried the soldier, 'get

to your work at once! Fetch the broom and sweep the chamber.' When

she had done this, he ordered her to come to his chair, and then he

stretched out his feet and said: 'Pull off my boots,' and then he

threw them in her face, and made her pick them up again, and clean

and brighten them. She, however, did everything he bade her, without

opposition, silently and with half-shut eyes. When the first cock

crowed, the manikin carried her back to the royal palace, and laid her

in her bed.

Next morning when the princess arose she went to her father, and told

him that she had had a very strange dream. 'I was carried through the

streets with the rapidity of lightning,' said she, 'and taken into a

soldier's room, and I had to wait upon him like a servant, sweep his

room, clean his boots, and do all kinds of menial work. It was only a

dream, and yet I am just as tired as if I really had done everything.'

'The dream may have been true,' said the king. 'I will give you a piece

of advice. Fill your pocket full of peas, and make a small hole in the

pocket, and then if you are carried away again, they will fall out and

leave a track in the streets.' But unseen by the king, the manikin was

standing beside him when he said that, and heard all. At night when

the sleeping princess was again carried through the streets, some peas

certainly did fall out of her pocket, but they made no track, for the

crafty manikin had just before scattered peas in every street there

was. And again the princess was compelled to do servant's work until

cock-crow.

Next morning the king sent his people out to seek the track, but it was

all in vain, for in every street poor children were sitting, picking up

peas, and saying: 'It must have rained peas, last night.' 'We must think

of something else,' said the king; 'keep your shoes on when you go to

bed, and before you come back from the place where you are taken, hide

one of them there, I will soon contrive to find it.' The black manikin

heard this plot, and at night when the soldier again ordered him to

bring the princess, revealed it to him, and told him that he knew of no

expedient to counteract this stratagem, and that if the shoe were found

in the soldier's house it would go badly with him. 'Do what I bid you,'

replied the soldier, and again this third night the princess was obliged

to work like a servant, but before she went away, she hid her shoe under

the bed.

Next morning the king had the entire town searched for his daughter's

shoe. It was found at the soldier's, and the soldier himself, who at the

entreaty of the dwarf had gone outside the gate, was soon brought back,

and thrown into prison. In his flight he had forgotten the most valuable

things he had, the blue light and the gold, and had only one ducat in

his pocket. And now loaded with chains, he was standing at the window of

his dungeon, when he chanced to see one of his comrades passing by. The

soldier tapped at the pane of glass, and when this man came up, said to

him: 'Be so kind as to fetch me the small bundle I have left lying in

the inn, and I will give you a ducat for doing it.' His comrade ran

thither and brought him what he wanted. As soon as the soldier was alone

again, he lighted his pipe and summoned the black manikin. 'Have no

fear,' said the latter to his master. 'Go wheresoever they take you, and

let them do what they will, only take the blue light with you.' Next day

the soldier was tried, and though he had done nothing wicked, the judge

condemned him to death. When he was led forth to die, he begged a last

favour of the king. 'What is it?' asked the king. 'That I may smoke one

more pipe on my way.' 'You may smoke three,' answered the king, 'but do

not imagine that I will spare your life.' Then the soldier pulled out

his pipe and lighted it at the blue light, and as soon as a few wreaths

of smoke had ascended, the manikin was there with a small cudgel in his

hand, and said: 'What does my lord command?' 'Strike down to earth that

false judge there, and his constable, and spare not the king who has

treated me so ill.' Then the manikin fell on them like lightning,

darting this way and that way, and whosoever was so much as touched by

his cudgel fell to earth, and did not venture to stir again. The king

was terrified; he threw himself on the soldier's mercy, and merely to

be allowed to live at all, gave him his kingdom for his own, and his

daughter to wife.
